title_en: Robam Electric: Traditional Enterprises Can Explore More New Business Models in the Internet Era
body_en: In 2014, Robam Appliances' Double Eleven sales exceeded 124 million yuan, securing the top spot on the kitchen appliance leaderboard. Currently, e-commerce sales account for 22% of Robam Appliances' total volume, with a year-on-year growth rate of as high as 150%. High growth is expected to continue in 2015. Mobile terminal sales represent over 30% of this, growing rapidly and becoming an important battleground for future e-commerce. Jiang Lingwei, General Manager of Robam Appliances' E-commerce, stated in an interview with Entrepreneur Plus that all traditional enterprises should embrace the internet, and mobile internet is a major trend. Drivers of Scale Growth Three years ago, people said, "Not doing internet is waiting to die, doing internet is seeking death." Today, three years later, everyone should embrace the internet. Online and offline are now integrated and inseparable, with more and more traditional brands moving online, and online brands moving offline. The concern that online sales are impacting offline channel dealers is no longer present. I believe the two are not in conflict, mainly because the consumer groups for online and offline are completely different. Taking kitchen appliances as an example, online buyers are between 25 and 35 years old, younger than offline buyers. Young consumers have fully adapted to and are accustomed to the online shopping lifestyle. The internet is no longer mysterious, and all enterprises are willing to integrate online and offline, and are willing to attempt so-called O2O. Moreover, there is now a very good logic for doing internet business, with a complete ecosystem. This e-commerce ecosystem includes specialized e-commerce talent training bases, logistics and shipping bases, visual design bases, and e-commerce universities, all of which jointly support e-commerce operations. Once a traditional enterprise decides to embark on the internet path, subsequent work can be integrated. Currently, online sales are growing rapidly and have become a driver of brand sales growth. Defender of High-End Brands Of course, for Robam Appliances, we also bear the responsibility of operating as a high-end brand in the e-commerce channel. We have summarized a high-end brand model: one foundation, one core, and three characteristics. The foundation is the necessity to focus on one industry and conduct in-depth research. The core is high value. The three characteristics refer to continuous innovation and leadership in product technology, strengthening brand cultural value in brand connotation, and comprehensively exceeding consumer expectations in consumption experience. As a high-end brand, we must achieve industry leadership in products, services, and technology. In the past, when buying large home appliances, we would call customer service for range hood installation. Nowadays, consumers can easily achieve this through their mobile WeChat. Each of our installers is equipped with a mobile terminal, and an installer can complete all after-sales problem recording work with a smartphone. Through intelligent services and intelligent hardware, we are transforming the consumer service end. Previously, brands couldn't find consumers, but now we can proactively find and interact with consumers. Therefore, the core of the internet's future transformation for traditional enterprises will undoubtedly be the reengineering of internal processes, making a series of innovations centered around the consumer. This is the lifeline for future development. I believe this is what traditional enterprises must do next. Therefore, when traditional enterprises transform, in addition to considering their offline foundations, the more critical aspect is to seize the current internet dividends. This is a core point. Explorer of New Business Models The internet is one of the carriers of new business models. In the internet era, new business models must be continuously explored. From C2B, crowdfunding, to WeChat commerce, the emergence of new business models is constantly accelerating. We have also been making new attempts. This year, we have explored four new business models: First, rebuilding the official shopping platform. In July of this year, we explored and established our own vertical portal website. Without any promotion, it has already achieved a certain scale of sales. We are exploring whether this model is effective, and after trying it, we believe it is a trend to follow. This is because the official website is not just a shopping platform; it is a carrier for all Robam Appliances consumers and a platform for consumer interaction. It has online customer service, an interactive platform, and an after-sales platform, where consumer questions can be answered, service needs can be met, and DIY interactions can occur, allowing us to express the functions we want to convey. Of course, this is not to compete with various platforms but to provide a final carrier for consumers, where they can find us with any issues. We have transitioned from product lifecycle management to user lifecycle management, especially for large home appliances like ours. Because our repurchase rate is very low, unless people are buying a new home, the chance of buying a range hood is very low. The typical lifespan of a range hood is 7 years. We are considering how to maintain customer relationships after purchasing a range hood, ensuring consumers continue to love and trust our brand after the "seven-year itch." Second, we provide value-added services beyond products. Value-added services include disposable filters, oil cups, and safety inspection services. We ensure users have no worries. In addition to warranty services, we also provide one free safety inspection and maintenance service annually, giving consumers peace of mind. Third, the intelligent ROKI system will be launched next year. ROKI, the Robam Appliances Kitchen Intelligent System, not only has intelligent cooking navigation but also maximizes user experience through internet applications. The ROKI intelligent cooking navigation system makes cooking easier for beginners. The range hood interface can display each cooking step and link with smart stoves to automatically adjust heat and cooking time, enabling zero-basis gourmet cooking and making recipes smarter. Fourth, mobile terminal development. The mobile terminal is very important to us. We must seize the major trend of the current internet wave and keep pace with the mobile terminal layouts of Alibaba, JD.com, and Suning. At the same time, we are also using mobile terminals to connect backend systems and interact closely with consumers. As more and more consumers shop on mobile terminals, they also communicate and connect with brands on mobile terminals. Therefore, we are doing more front-end and back-end matching on mobile terminals. First, we are conducting personalized design and development for mobile terminals, considering the small screen size and consumer reading habits. Second, we are building a WeChat mall, allowing consumers to have their own entry point on the mobile terminal and access it anytime. We are also leveraging many platforms and apps for our official shopping website. Third, we are connecting the backend systems of the mobile terminal. We have many WeChat and Weibo service functions, and we may try developing an app in the future. During this year's Double Eleven, we innovated on multiple levels and promoted brand influence through event marketing. Before Double Eleven, we launched a "Stormy Chef" event marketing campaign, which was very effective. It was the only kitchen appliance brand to win a silver award at the China E-commerce Marketing Award - the Golden Peanut Award, and also received the Best Internet Experience Award from Analysys International. New Channel for Consumer Interaction Robam Appliances was among the first home appliance brands to venture into e-commerce in 2008. At that time, traditional brands were offline, and the internet was online. Today, deeply influenced by the internet, Robam Appliances has undergone tremendous changes from the backend to the frontend. In the past, when we developed a product, we would decide to make it and then ask consumers to buy it! Now, when we develop products, the first question we ask is: Do consumers think the same way? Do they want to use such a product? Current product development is consumer-centric, which is a significant change brought about by internet thinking. The key for traditional enterprises to engage in the internet is: they must clearly see that the internet is not just a sales channel, but also a disruptor that influences internal management and processes. Our biggest challenge now is how to interact with consumers through the internet. Consumers are no longer just concerned with sales; they are more concerned with the benefits that kitchen appliances can bring them. Therefore, targeting young women, we launched the "Stormy Chef" event. Young women want to cook a sumptuous dinner for their families on weekends but are particularly resistant to oily fumes. In the "Stormy Chef" event, we told consumers that our range hoods can avoid these problems. Robam Appliances can help many women and office workers enjoy the pleasure of cooking. At the same time, we are also the only user to do a Showcase on Alibaba Mama. We set up a reception at the Robam Appliances flagship store and launched an interactive mini-game. Over 200,000 people participated in half a month, with very good results. After the event, we firmly occupied the top position in the Taobao Index. "Stormy Chef" and "Showcase" have been very helpful for our brand communication because they are both close to consumers. As a leading brand in the kitchen appliance industry, Robam Appliances has consistently focused on high-end products for 36 years, achieving 17 years of sales leadership. Robam Appliances has achieved comprehensive leadership in both online and offline channels. We have many WeChat and Weibo service functions, and we may try developing an app in the future. Before Double Eleven, we launched a "Stormy Chef" event marketing campaign, which was very effective. title_en: Robam Electric as the sole representative of the kitchen appliance industry participating in the 5th China Home Appliance Development Summit Forum
body_en: On March 11th, the 5th China Home Appliance Development Summit Forum was grandly held in Shanghai. As an important supporting event for the China Home Appliance Expo, this event was hosted by the authoritative institution in the home appliance industry, the China Household Electrical Appliances Association, and jointly promoted by CCTV. Entering its fifth year, the China Home Appliance Development Summit Forum focused on the most heated keywords in the home appliance industry and even the entire Chinese economy – "New Normal." As the sole representative of the kitchen appliance industry, Mr. Zhao Jihong, President of Robam Group, discussed the new normal of China's home appliance development with Mr. Fang Hongbo, Chairman of Midea Group, Mr. Lan Ye, CMO of JD.com, Mr. Sun Jingyan, Vice President of Haier Home Appliance Industry Group, and Mr. Xie Hui, Vice President of Samsung China CE Division. The forum was themed "Embracing the New Normal and Unlocking a New Era," and engaged in heated discussions around two high-interest topics: "Channel Transformation and Product Value-Added: Which is the Breakthrough Point for Creating New Demand?" and "Home Appliance Enterprises and Internet Enterprises: Who Will Lead the Future of Smart Home Appliances?" Industry leaders such as Robam Appliances, JD.com, Midea, Haier, Skyworth, LeTV, and AVC (All View Cloud) spoke freely and shared their views, pushing the atmosphere at the venue to a climax. "New Normal" has undoubtedly been one of the hottest buzzwords of 2014. In recent years, with the accelerated deep transformation of the home appliance industry, significant achievements in various model innovations, and rapid development in channel construction, more and more traditional home appliance companies are breaking away from traditional thinking and seeking new development models. Meanwhile, numerous internet companies have also entered the home appliance industry, bringing a zero-distance and networked approach, making innovation, intelligence, and high-end gradually become mainstream terms in the industry. Under this new normal, how to better create consumer demand has triggered a new round of reshuffling and integration for major enterprises in China's home appliance industry. In terms of brand positioning, it is necessary to achieve related diversification, resource synergy, and strengthen specialization. Mr. Fang Hongbo, Chairman and President of Midea Group, believes that any Chinese home appliance enterprise, especially in white goods, still has a certain gap with the global industry. To cultivate new competitiveness and business models, it is necessary to further integrate into the internet era, using its own innovative brand power, value capabilities, and core technological advantages to compete. The future of smart living, building smart homes, and creating a better life are the directions for the home appliance industry's development going forward. Mr. Sun Jingyan, Vice President of Haier Home Appliance Industry Group, in his keynote speech themed "Customizing Smart Home Solutions and Creating the Best User Living Experience," stated that smart homes are facing a critical turning point from "implementation" to "popularization." Haier will form an Internet of Things between user needs and production factories through smart connectivity, from both smart homes externally and interconnected factories internally. Kitchen appliances have always been an important part of the home appliance industry. As a leading brand in the kitchen appliance sector, Robam Appliances has always been at the forefront in terms of both brand and technology. Mr. Zhao Jihong, President of Robam Group, discussed channels and brands, believing that Robam Appliances, focusing on the kitchen appliance field, fully understands consumer needs and market changes, and therefore places greater emphasis on innovation in specialized areas. However, in the face of the development of the internet industry today, whether in the kitchen appliance sector or the entire home appliance industry, it is about shortening the distance between the internet, products, and consumers, thereby dominating the market. Therefore, thoroughly understanding consumer needs and serving them with innovative business models, providing consumers with good value and products is the most important thing. Intelligence was ignited multiple times at the forum. Robam Appliances, a pioneer in the intelligent direction within the industry, officially launched the pre-sale of the world's first smart range hood with a powerful suction and equipped with the ROKI system on the first day of the Home Appliance Expo. Robam Appliances comprehensively showcased the ROKI intelligent cooking system to consumers, recreating the ideal smart kitchen lifestyle scenario of the internet era. This received high recognition from internet companies such as 360, Alibaba, JD.com, and Baidu present, and also demonstrated Robam Appliances' strong capabilities in the field of smart home appliances. Smart kitchen appliances are closely related to our lives. Their development will greatly promote the informatization process of our families and provide people with a more relaxed, comfortable, efficient, and safe modern kitchen lifestyle. As an important component of the home appliance industry, it will further integrate with the internet in the near future, just like smartphones today, becoming within reach. The resulting consumer trends will become increasingly prominent. High-end, intelligent innovative products will also inject new vitality into the market, inevitably unlocking a new era. 1 Previous Article: Robam Appliances Represents the Kitchen Appliance Industry in Discussing the Innovative Development of Smart Home Appliances in China Next Article: The High-End Side-Draft Range Hood JuMu 5900 is Grandly Released, Leading the Era of Powerful Suction with Side-Draft Technology

title_en: Robam Electric Honored as One of China's Top 100 E-commerce Enterprises
body_en: Reporters learned from the 2nd China E-commerce Culture Festival that Hangzhou Robam Appliances Co., Ltd. was honored with the title of "Top 100 Chinese E-commerce Enterprises in 2010." This is the first large-scale evaluation activity covering all upstream and downstream enterprises and elements of the entire e-commerce industry chain in China's 12 years of e-commerce development, and it has produced China's first "Elite Ranking" in e-commerce. The selection of the Top 100 Chinese E-commerce Enterprises was undertaken by the renowned market research firm iResearch, commissioned by the organizing committee of the 2nd China E-commerce Culture Festival. The first selection of the Top 100 Chinese E-commerce Enterprises encompassed three major categories of enterprises: e-commerce operations, applications, and services, comprehensively and multidimensionally reflecting the overall level and landscape of China's e-commerce. After more than a decade of development and transformation, the landscape of China's e-commerce has undergone tremendous changes. The public and the industry are eagerly anticipating numerous emerging and new forces to take the stage of e-commerce, which is dazzling and brilliant, and refresh some of the old faces from memory. Xu Weida, Director of Online Operations at Robam Appliances, said: In response to the YuHang District government's call for enterprise transformation and upgrading, the company launched comprehensive e-commerce activities in 2008, including online shopping, TV direct sales, and catalog sales. In November 2008, Robam Appliances established its professional B2C mall – Robam Official Shopping Network (shop.robam.com). The company's product sales have also entered B2C platforms represented by Tmall and wholesale distribution platforms represented by Alibaba. This has fully covered all types of sales platforms currently available for online wholesale, retail, and distribution, achieving comprehensive sales platforms. Robam Appliances' online marketing revenue has been growing at a rate of 200% annually, and the economic benefits achieved can fully support its own growth. 0 Previous: 9B22 Wins 2010 IF International Design Award Next: Chairman Ren Jianhua Invited to Attend the 2010 Annual Council Enlarged Meeting of the Range Hood Branch

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: To all relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The supply chain security of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently needs to strengthen the technological innovation and industrial support for domestic pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the quality improvement of domestic pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," hosted by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the quality improvement and innovation of excipients. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues with three themes: "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," to promote the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars, and jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows: 1. Conference theme: Promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry 2. Time and location: November 8th Registration Venue: New Ji Hotel, Hefei (2766 Wenzhong Road, Yaohai District, Hefei, Anhui Province) November 9-10 Main venue and sub-venue: Shaoquanhu Campus of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine, Hefei, Anhui Province (350 Longzihu Road, Yaohai District, Hefei, Anhui Province) 3. Conference arrangements: The conference will adopt a format of main venue and sub-venue reports for communication. The conference will invite well-known experts and scholars from domestic universities, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, regulatory agencies, etc., to give keynote speeches and special lectures. Please see the attached schedule for the conference schedule. 4. Participants: Researchers, managers, graduate students, etc., engaged in research and development related to pharmaceutical excipients, pharmaceutical packaging materials, drug delivery devices, formulation quality control, formulation equipment, pharmaceutical services, etc., from higher education institutions, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, drug regulatory agencies, and other related institutions. 5. Conference paper submission: 1. Requirements for paper submission: Chinese and English abstracts and paper format. Papers that have not been published in publicly distributed journals or presented at national academic conferences are the responsibility of the authors; please ensure clear expression and accurate data. Researchers in the pharmaceutical field are welcome to actively submit papers. 2. Paper submission method: Please submit the paper abstract to the conference website https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn before October 20, 2024, click on the "Online Paper Submission" button on the right, follow the process to upload your paper abstract, and you will receive an automatic email confirmation of the online submission. After the paper is reviewed by experts, the organizing committee will select several papers for further communication or publication in the "Drug Analysis" journal. 3. Poster submission method and time: Same as the paper. The conference welcomes poster submissions, which should be in A1 standard size. 6. Registration: (1) Registration method: 1. Please register by clicking on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button on the conference website link https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn; 2. Or scan the QR code below with your mobile phone WeChat, click on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button to fill in the registration information and submit. (2) Registration deadline: The registration deadline is October 30, 2024. (3) Notes on registration: 1. To ensure that participants receive registration confirmation, invoices, etc., please fill in accurate and true email addresses, mobile phone numbers, and other information; 2. This registration website is only for registration, and the payment channel is not yet open; 3. Registered participants can log in to the personal center of the conference website to check and modify their registration information; 4. Participants who do not submit papers can also attend the conference. 7. Conference fees: (1) Conference registration fee: 1. Registration fee standard: The registration fee includes conference materials and lunch during the conference. 2. Payment methods: (1) Telegraphic transfer method: After registering for the conference, participants should pay the registration fee by bank transfer, supporting both corporate and personal transfers to the following account: Payee: Chinese Pharmaceutical Association Bank: Bank of China Head Office Account number: 778350009320 It is recommended to use online banking for personal transfers, or you can also use Alipay transfer (to a bank card, with the name filled in the "Chinese Pharmaceutical Association" column). Please indicate "Pharmaceutical Excipients + Participant's Name + Unit Abbreviation" in the remittance note. After successful payment, please upload the remittance voucher to the conference website in a timely manner for the secretariat to confirm the payment information and issue an invoice; (2) On-site payment: You can pay the registration fee through mobile online banking, or transfer the fee on-site by scanning the payment QR code (Alipay, WeChat); there is no POS machine on-site, and payment methods such as credit card swiping and UnionPay are not supported. (2) Invoice matters: 1. This conference can provide a VAT ordinary invoice for "conference registration fee" (electronic invoice). After uploading the personal remittance voucher (photo, screenshot, etc.) to the conference system, please accurately fill in the invoice information in the billing instructions section of your personal information. 2. In cases where the name of the remitter does not match the participant's name, one unit remits on behalf of multiple participants, or the unit remits collectively but requires separate invoices, please send a detailed explanation by email to the secretariat at z38@cpa.org.cn, providing the remitter's name, participant's name, work unit, contact information, detailed information for issuing the invoice, number and amount of invoices, as well as the person receiving the invoice and mailing address. 3. Representatives who are unable to attend the conference due to special reasons after remittance can apply for a full refund of the registration fee by sending an email to the secretariat. The refund process will be handled collectively after the conference, and the refund will be returned to the original payment method. For accurate refund processing, please indicate the full name and account information (account number, bank) of the original remitter in the refund application email. 8. Other matters: Accommodation and transportation expenses for participants are self-funded. Please refer to Attachment 2 for hotel booking and transportation information. 9. Conference credits: Full-time participants will be awarded 3 continuing education credits from the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association. 10. Contact person and contact information: 1. Contact person: Zhu Yizi (conference paper submission, registration fee payment, etc.) Peng Can, Duan Xiaohui, Lu Jia (conference consultation, accommodation arrangements, etc.) 2. Contact information: 010-67095606, 13956024560, 13956990010, 15212451687 3. Secretariat email: z38@cpa.org.cn Attachment 1. body_en: Editor's note: In order to implement the requirements of the State Council's "Notice on Issuing a Package of Policies and Measures to Stabilize the Economy Solidly", accelerate the promotion of digitalization to assist in the implementation of the "Three Products" strategy in the consumer goods industry, further boost consumer confidence, tap into consumption potential, consolidate and enhance the fundamental role of consumption in economic development, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently organized the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products". China Electronics News has specially opened a column for the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products", reporting on the progress of the event, expert opinions, and policy interpretations. Stay tuned. On July 5th, the "Digitalization to Assist the Consumer Goods Industry in the Implementation of the 'Three Products' Action Plan" was announced and the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products" was launched in Beijing. Luo Li, member of the Party Group and Deputy Director of the Chongqing Economic and Information Commission, stated at the meeting that the consumer goods industry is an important pillar industry in Chongqing. Chongqing will focus on key areas such as research and development design, production manufacturing, and public services, guided by the "Digitalization to Assist the Consumer Goods Industry in the Implementation of the 'Three Products' Action Plan", to promote resource sharing, platform connection, and industry collaboration, improve the quality of Chongqing's consumer goods industry supply system, and promote high-quality development of the entire industry. The consumer goods industry maintains a steady development trend. It was introduced that in recent years, under the guidance of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Chongqing has vigorously implemented an innovation-driven development strategy led by big data intelligence, deepened the integration of digital and real, and achieved an output value of 483.02 billion yuan for the city's above-scale consumer goods industry enterprises in 2021, a year-on-year increase of 10.5%, maintaining a steady development trend. Firstly, focus on the construction of digital platforms to enhance innovation capabilities. Introduce platforms such as Daqian Huiding and Kaiwu Industry for prototype making and high-end mold making services, establish the Chongqing Consumer Goods Industry Innovation Design Research Institute, the Chongqing Industrial Design Industry Alliance, promote the construction of platforms such as Langjian D+M Intelligent Manufacturing Workshop, and the Southwest Center of the China Industrial Design Institute, and use digital means to carry out collaborative innovation. Promote the construction of the industrial Internet platform for the "Hardware Capital of Western China" in Dazu District, Chongqing, which has registered nearly 500 companies, nearly 100 companies have registered on the identification and analysis secondary node platform, with over 500 million codes used and over 200 million data analyses. Promote the "Chengyu Twin City Economic Circle Intelligent Manufacturing Quality Brand Building Project" of Chongqing Saibo Industrial Technology Research Institute was selected for the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's "Industrial Quality Brand Building Enhancement Special Project". Support Zhixiang Jintai to continue the construction of the new crown vaccine production platform project, support key pharmaceutical industrial parks to collaborate with international leading companies such as Cytiva to create a commercial-scale biopharmaceutical contract manufacturing platform through joint construction and other methods. Secondly, focus on the application of big data intelligence to comprehensively improve the capacity and quality of effective supply. Deepen the application of digital technology. Since 2018, the city has created 170 digital workshops and 31 smart factories. A group of key industry enterprises such as Jiulong Paper, Yihai Kerry, and Tianyou Dairy have successfully created national-level green factories, and 31 companies have created municipal-level green factories. Cultivate 4 5G+ industrial Internet integrated innovation application demonstration scenes, promote the implementation of over 1,200 intelligent transformation projects, build 62 industrial Internet pilot demonstration projects, identify 9 "hidden champions", 15 "small giants", and 345 "specialized, refined, new" enterprises; Duanji Clothing relies on big data to build a 3D fitting system, carry out personalized customization and flexible production, and lead innovation and development with intelligent manufacturing; Sumida, Shangshang Clothing and other leading clothing companies deepen the industrial chain synergy, build a "headquarters base + satellite factory" development model, effectively promote rural revitalization. Promote the development of digital medicine, focus on areas such as inspection and testing, sports medicine, chronic disease rehabilitation, and assisted reproduction, build key platforms such as the Chongqing Medical University Laboratory of Translational Medicine, and enhance clinical transformation capabilities. Thirdly, focus on empowering digital marketing to enhance brand cultivation capabilities. Play an effective guiding role of the government, continuously hold the "Yujian Meipin" Chongqing consumer goods brand promotion theme activities on multiple platforms, innovatively combine brand promotion with urban marketing, attract consumer attention through multiple live broadcast activities, continuously promote brand building through online zones and offline activities, promote industry enterprises to accelerate their "online presence". Collaborate with the municipal tourism group to set up online zones using the "Cloud-based Cultural and Tourism Hotel" and "Chongqing Taobao Cultural and Tourism Boutique Pavilion" to help companies expand their marketing channels. Promote deep cooperation between Dadukou District and Feixiang Industrial Internet to deepen C2M new intelligent manufacturing model cooperation, build a Chongqing noodle industrial demonstration park, and promote the slogan "Chongqing Noodles, Made in Chongqing". Promote Alibaba, Kuaishou Technology, Meituan Technology, and other platform companies to establish the Chongqing Consumer Goods Industry Brand Innovation Service Alliance, build a digital marketing "circle of friends". Regularly hold industrial design and digital marketing empowerment training courses to create an industrial ecological atmosphere. Promote high-quality development of the industry from three aspects Regarding the key tasks for the next step, Luo Li stated that Chongqing will focus on key areas such as research and development design, production manufacturing, and public services, guided by the "Digitalization to Assist the Consumer Goods Industry in the Implementation of the 'Three Products' Action Plan", to promote resource sharing, platform connection, and industry collaboration, improve the quality of Chongqing's consumer goods industry supply system, and promote high-quality development of the entire industry. Firstly, use digitalization to promote innovation empowerment. Use digital technology as a link to promote the "Three-Year Doubling Plan for R&D Institutions of Large-scale Industrial Enterprises", encourage large-scale industry enterprises to carry out research and development activities universally, establish research and development institutions universally, comprehensively promote the construction of enterprise research and development institutions, vigorously promote the construction of a group of high-level national or municipal enterprise research and development institutions such as enterprise technology centers and key laboratories of industry and information technology, build a concentrated area for digital economy empowerment, promote collaborative innovation activities between industry, academia, and research, cultivate a group of industry technology innovation benchmarks, and use high-quality supply to promote consumption upgrading. Secondly, use digitalization to promote intelligent manufacturing efficiency. Continue to promote intelligent transformation, support enterprises to build intelligent manufacturing, environmentally friendly processes, and flexible production technology systems, explore the construction of C2M shared factories, enhance product manufacturing capabilities and green development levels. Build industrial Internet platforms around fields such as food and clothing. Plan to build a home design information sharing platform. Enhance the coordinated supporting capacity of green packaging. Cultivate and build a number of R&D and manufacturing projects for AI imaging, "Internet + personal" and household medical testing equipment. Thirdly, use digitalization to unleash brand effectiveness. Combine platform resources, rely on digital scenarios, deepen the application of online platforms, promote the integrated development of agriculture, industry, commerce, culture, and tourism, support the construction of the Chongqing Noodle Industrialization Digital Marketing Service Center, the Prefabricated Vegetable Innovation Service Center, and the Craft Art Propaganda Platform, promote new product development and brand incubation, expand brand influence through multiple channels, further enhance the industrial symbols of "Chongqing flavor", "Chongqing craftsmanship", and "Chongqing taste". Luo Li emphasized that the 2022 National Tour of the "Three Products" organized by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology is an important event to fully demonstrate industry development achievements, exchange development experiences, and enhance regional cooperation. Chongqing will make full preparations and actively participate, especially as a sub-venue of the "Three Products" consumption season activities, it will jointly host the 2022 China (Chengdu-Chongqing) Food Industry Expo with Sichuan, innovate event content, conduct new consumption conferences, brand nights, and other series of theme activities, and organize key districts, counties, and industry enterprises to actively participate and deepen cooperation to ensure the successful, concise, and safe industry event.

title_en: 【Meticulous observation of autumn】Stablecoin legislation sets sail, Hong Kong's virtual asset development is on the rise with a broad future ahead.
body_en: Chen Weiming, Fellow of the Chartered Secretaries Institute, Bachelor of Laws, EMBA, licensed by the Securities and Futures Commission Last month, the Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region officially passed the "Stablecoin Bill", establishing a licensing system for the issuance and operation of fiat-backed stablecoins, laying the regulatory foundation for the development of virtual assets. While this move appears to be a risk control policy on the surface, its deeper significance lies in paving the way for the tokenization of assets and Real World Assets (RWA). This not only solidifies Hong Kong's role as an international financial center in the future but also opens up potential channels for legitimate cross-border financing of mainland assets. Tokenization refers to the digitization and splitting of physical or traditional assets such as real estate, bonds, accounts receivable, private equity, etc., into tradable tokens in blockchain form. These tokens, linked to specific asset values, fall under the category of RWA, significantly enhancing asset liquidity and expanding investment and financing channels. According to estimates by Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the global tokenization market is expected to reach $160 trillion by 2030. International financial institutions such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and UBS have already been actively involved in the on-chain market for physical assets, issuing tokenized bonds, tokenized funds, tokenized real estate equity, etc., and have conducted trials in locations such as Singapore, Switzerland, and Abu Dhabi. Mainland RWAs have transitioned from experimentation to practical application Under the policy framework of "blockchain does not equal virtual currency" in the mainland, blockchain applications that are "regulated, controllable, and serve the real economy" are allowed and encouraged, including pilot projects and practical operations of tokenizing physical assets on the chain. Representative commercial cases include China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (China Securities Depository) collaborating with Ant Chain under Ant Group and China CITIC Bank to register, verify, and transfer accounts receivable between enterprises (supply chain finance) on the platform, tokenize them, and convert accounts receivable from small and micro suppliers to large enterprises into digital certificates, circulating them in real-time for financing by financial institutions. Another case is the cooperation between China Merchants Bank and China Trust Registration (China Trust Registration Co., Ltd.) to jointly develop a private chain system, on-chain signatures, and rent verification mechanisms, converting the future 5-year rental income rights of long-term rental apartments in Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Chengdu, etc., into digital certificates, which investors can subscribe to and obtain income rights. RWA tokenization creates a new bridge for mainland assets to "go global" Another significant aspect of RWA tokenization is creating a new legal bridge for mainland physical assets to go global. For example, through the following three financial structures: 1. Overseas SPV + RWA issuance platform. Chinese companies can set up SPVs in Hong Kong to hold domestic asset income rights, which can be audited and evaluated before being converted into tokenized notes issued to overseas investors. For example, an energy company can convert its power plant rental income into RWA tokens, finance them on the Hong Kong platform, and settle transactions with stablecoins. 2. Cross-border asset fund channel + tokenized fund. If the fund channel is further opened, mainland asset managers can establish tokenized REITs or private equity funds in Hong Kong, raising funds from international institutional investors within a compliant framework, effectively forming a "tokenized fund channel". 3. RWA mortgage loan platform. After converting mainland assets into RWA, companies can mortgage them on a Hong Kong digital asset platform to obtain stablecoin loans in Hong Kong dollars, renminbi, or US dollars, which can then be exchanged for fiat currency to inject into international projects. This model has been tested in Singapore and Switzerland, and Hong Kong has excellent financial and capital market talent with similar conditions. Institutional innovation helps enhance financial competitiveness The passage of the "Stablecoin Bill" signifies a shift in virtual asset policy from "fire prevention" to "city building". If further measures such as guidelines for tokenized bonds, RWA certification systems, and blockchain custody standards are introduced, Hong Kong can not only serve as a global experimental ground for the digitization of physical assets but also become a digital bridge connecting mainland physical assets with global capital. Institutional innovation is the key to future competitiveness in capital markets.

title_en: Chinese brands break through global barriers.
body_en: Huawei store in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Visual China The China Online Consumer Brand Index (CBI) has increased from 59.42 to 63.38 from the first quarter of 2023 to the first quarter of 2025. Xinhua News Agency Read the report The China Online Consumer Brand Index, Global Brand China Online Top 500, and Online Brand Purchasing Power Index reports released by institutions such as the National Development Institute of Peking University have attracted widespread attention from the economic community. The data in the report shows that from the first quarter of 2023 to the first quarter of 2025, the China Online Consumer Brand Index (CBI) increased from 59.42 to 63.38. Compared to the base index in the first quarter of 2025, it increased by 6.7 percentage points, indicating a significant improvement in the quality of consumer goods in China. The China Online Consumer Brand Index CBI report (from the first quarter of 2023 to the first quarter of 2025) believes that with the continuous advancement of high-level opening-up to the outside world, the advantages of China's super-large-scale market are becoming more prominent, making it a core market for global brand layout. This "development report" of global brands in China not only outlines the upgrading trend of the Chinese consumer market but also shows a pleasing fact: both Chinese and foreign brands are shining in the Chinese market. Behind the slogan "Global Brands, Winning in China" reflects the unique development logic of global brands and the local market. This column analyzes this in detail. Looking at China Chinese Brands: Winning the Favor of Global Consumers The research data from institutions such as Peking University's National Development Institute introduced multidimensional evaluation criteria based on internet platforms like Taobao. The report evaluates brand quality comprehensively based on dimensions such as sales, prices, searches, and positive reviews, presenting the current development status of brands from different perspectives. Overall, many Chinese brands have achieved success in the domestic market, entering the consumer market deeply with advanced technology, mature management experience, and strong brand influence, successfully integrating into the lives of Chinese consumers through cutting-edge innovation research and development and high-quality production and marketing. In the wave of high-quality economic development in China, Chinese brands are breaking through from the domestic market to the global stage with unstoppable momentum. From BYD topping the global electric vehicle manufacturers to Heytea "sweetening" Southeast Asia, and DJI drones soaring in the world sky... these remarkable achievements confirm that the rise of Chinese brands is not accidental. In the increasingly competitive global market, the road for Chinese brands to break through is full of challenges. Technological innovation is undoubtedly the key force driving Chinese brands to achieve cross-border development and successful breakthroughs. For example, many brands are investing in high-end equipment, new energy vehicles, and other emerging industries, competing with international giants on the same stage through technological breakthroughs and innovation, winning the favor of global consumers. Based on this, Chinese brands have moved away from the competition model of relying on low prices and low costs in the past, building differentiated competitive barriers with technological advantages, achieving a "gorgeous transformation." At the same time, more and more Chinese brands are exploring traditional cultural elements, integrating them into product design and brand concepts, endowing products with excellent traditional Chinese cultural connotations. In the field of clothing, some brands combine traditional Hanfu elements with modern fashion design to create clothing series that are both Eastern and modern, not only popular in the domestic market but also attracting the attention of many international consumers. From "a few hundred million shirts for a Boeing" to today's new energy vehicles, smartphones, and other high-end products renowned worldwide, Chinese brands and Chinese manufacturing have made remarkable progress, paving a path of astonishing innovative development. Viewing the World International Brands: More and More Choosing China as their "Second Home Field" Walking with China means walking with opportunities; investing in China means investing in the future; choosing China means winning globally. In the current global economy facing uncertainty, the "certainty" of the Chinese consumer market has become the biggest attraction. This certainty comes from the market size of over 1.4 billion people, the consumption potential of a massive middle-income population, and the continuous empowerment at the policy level, providing stable expectations for brand development. China has always maintained an open and inclusive attitude, welcoming international brands to participate in the Chinese market competition. This not only brings more high-quality choices to Chinese consumers but also provides opportunities for learning and reference for Chinese brands. While strengthening the construction of Chinese brands, China actively creates a fair competitive market environment, promoting mutual learning and progress among global brands. Looking at the report, the success of Chinese and foreign brands in China is not accidental but a natural result of China's open genes, innovation vitality, ecological integration, and super-large-scale advantages. As more and more international brands choose China as their "second home field" and local brands accelerate towards the global stage, this vibrant market is writing a new chapter of global business cooperation with open arms. Facing Challenges Brand Building: Requires Persistent Investment and Innovation While we applaud the achievements of Chinese brands in breaking through internationally, we must also realize that the road ahead is still long and full of challenges. For Chinese brands to continue to exert force in the global market, achieve long-term and steady development, the road ahead is still arduous. In the process of brand internationalization, challenges such as cultural differences, trade barriers, and intensified international competition cannot be ignored. At the same time, as consumer demands become increasingly diversified and personalized, how to continuously improve product quality, optimize service experiences, strengthen brand cultural connotations to meet higher-level market demands, becomes the "must-answer question" for the advancement of Chinese brands. Brand building is a long-term project that requires persistent investment and innovation. China has become the only country in the world with all industrial categories, but the "neck-breaking" issue remains prominent in high-end and cutting-edge technology. Faced with a complex and ever-changing international situation, the solution to this problem, as practice has shown, has no shortcuts, and only by persistently taking one step at a time can we see the light. From the perspective of the global value chain, although Chinese brands have moved towards the high end, there are still gaps with international top brands in brand premium capabilities, global market operation experience, and sustainable development system construction. This requires Chinese brands to take big steps in innovative development and solidify their foundation, exploring new growth paths while maintaining traditional advantages. (According to Xinhua News Agency)

title_en: AI empowers Chinese listed companies to go global, with overseas revenue approaching 10 trillion yuan.
body_en: In 2025, going global is no longer an "option," but a "necessity," becoming a significant strategic opportunity for business development. According to statistics from the China Listed Companies Association, in 2024, listed companies maintained a good development trend in their export business, achieving overseas revenue of 9.44 trillion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 7.97%, with the proportion of revenue from overseas markets increasing by 1.06 percentage points compared to the previous year. "China has already achieved technological leadership in areas such as 5G, AI, and smart cars. Chinese companies' technology, supply chain, service, and brand capabilities have already had a spillover effect," said Wu Yongming, CEO of Alibaba Group and Chairman and CEO of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, at the Alibaba Cloud Enterprise Going Global Conference. However, against the backdrop of the accelerated restructuring of the global economic landscape, Chinese companies' global expansion process is facing unprecedented complexity and uncertainty. From regulatory compliance to supply chain management, from market environment to cultural adaptation, the barriers that companies need to overcome in going global far exceed traditional understanding. On one hand, geopolitical conflicts, rising trade protectionism, and technological blockades have intensified external risks; on the other hand, internal capabilities in resource allocation, strategic decision-making, and localization operations within companies are also increasing. Faced with multiple challenges, companies going global are seeking technological breakthroughs. AI, cloud computing, and other digital technologies have evolved from auxiliary tools to core infrastructure, with Chinese tech giants like Alibaba and Huawei playing important roles. In this process, technological empowerment is significantly reducing barriers for companies going global, enhancing their international competitiveness, which may be a key turning point for Chinese companies to transition from "going out" to "going up." The wave of going global has been particularly significant in the past two years, with consumer goods, gaming, manufacturing, and other industries expanding into overseas markets. In addition to large-scale leading companies, many small and medium-sized enterprises are also eyeing the opportunities in overseas markets. However, these companies face diverse challenges when considering expanding into overseas markets. Cultural differences are unavoidable obstacles for Chinese companies going global. Language is the first barrier to overcome, as businesses need to address the issue of language barriers and communicate in the local language at every step, while also understanding the needs and preferences of overseas consumers. Directly selling Chinese products in overseas markets often yields unsatisfactory results. Cultural habit differences can lead to misunderstandings, for example, the Middle East region has many taboos related to dietary, clothing, and advertising content due to religious beliefs. If companies are unaware and blindly promote products, they may offend local people and trigger a public relations crisis. Compliance issues are also relatively complex. There are significant differences in laws and regulations between countries, and companies operating overseas need to comply with local laws and regulations, including taxation, labor laws, environmental protection, and market competition. Companies often need to invest significant resources to ensure compliance, otherwise they may face fines, lawsuits, or even business prohibitions. Moreover, there is a scarcity of relevant professional talents. These fields require specific professional skills and knowledge, as well as a deep understanding of different cultures and market environments. Finding employees with the necessary skills who are willing to work across different time zones is a challenge, especially when covering multiple markets. Language and cultural barriers, complex compliance issues, a shortage of professional talents, high customer acquisition costs... these are the numerous challenges that businesses face on the road to going global. The integration of AI brings a turning point. "When analyzing a company's operational processes and breaking them down into specific tasks, it can be seen that artificial intelligence has potential value in multiple areas," said Zhang Kaifei, Vice President of Alibaba's International Digital Business Group and Head of AI Business, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald. For enterprises going global, AI innovation is no longer just an optional auxiliary tool, but a core driver for business growth and localization. Taking the example of cross-border e-commerce, AI performs excellently in scenarios such as AI customer service and marketing push, bringing double-digit improvements in effectiveness. It is worth noting that such improvements are not only in terms of reducing labor costs and increasing efficiency but in most scenarios, AI can bring a 1% to 30% improvement in conversion rates, click-through rates, and consumer satisfaction. Alibaba International is at the forefront of AI applications. In November 2023, it launched the AI tool "Business Assistant," equipping small and medium-sized enterprises with AI agents. In 2025, Alibaba announced that its AI foreign trade products had been integrated with advanced models such as DeepSeek. Other platform-based companies are also following suit. For example, Dunhuang.com released the large-scale AI model "Feitian" in the early 2024 for the cross-border e-commerce vertical field, introducing various AI applications. TikTok recently announced the launch of the AI-driven "Seller Assistant" on its seller center, providing intelligent support to brands and merchants. Focus Technology's core platform, China Manufacturing Network, also introduced AI assistants such as Maico and Mentarc for sellers and a Sourcing AI procurement assistant for buyers. Zhang Kaifei stated that compared to leading businesses, small and medium-sized businesses usually benefit more, "the smaller the business, the more they can benefit from AI applications." He told reporters that especially when small and micro-enterprises are trying to expand into overseas markets, they find it more difficult to find talent capable of handling relevant tasks. The application of artificial intelligence technology fills the talent gap for these businesses, providing the possibility to improve operational efficiency and quality, thereby gaining a competitive advantage in the market. "I believe that the number of small and micro-enterprises will experience tremendous growth, and the threshold for entrepreneurship will decrease," Zhang Kaifei said. In addition to the empowerment of AI applications, going global requires higher capabilities in digital infrastructure for enterprises. "Currently, many enterprises in the early stages of development, especially in the early stages, focus mainly on how to make the entire system operate quickly," said Han Hongyuan, Vice President of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald. The challenges faced in going global are more complex. For example, on the supply chain side, as businesses expand their operations globally, the stability of the supply chain will face more tests. Companies going global need to build a diverse supply network, establish global supply chain nodes, use digital technology to monitor the supply chain in real-time, and enhance its resilience and risk management capabilities. In multinational operations, geographical spans can lead to delayed service responses, potentially causing fragmented user experiences and damaging the company's brand image. Companies should establish a global integrated service network, rely on digital platforms to allocate and share service resources, and optimize the collaborative processes of cross-regional service teams. It is evident that in the face of diverse challenges, digital and intelligent capabilities have become important means of response, and companies going global need to build a strong, efficient, and flexible digital infrastructure. The "2025 Alibaba Cloud Enterprise Going Global White Paper" points out that the traditional self-built IT infrastructure model is no longer able to meet the needs of companies to quickly respond to changes in overseas markets. Cloud computing services, with their global layout, elastic expansion capabilities, and full-stack service advantages, have become the best solution to this problem. "When a startup wants to use high-level IT capabilities, the cloud is the most direct choice," said Han Hongyuan. "If a self-built approach is adopted, all related affairs need to be managed independently, which undoubtedly adds complexity. From this perspective, cloud services provide powerful support for enterprises in the process of exploring new markets." Leading domestic cloud service providers are strong participants in this field. Han Hongyuan stated that Alibaba Cloud's overseas business has always existed, but it was not given high priority in the past. Since last year, Alibaba Cloud has significantly increased its focus on overseas business. Recently, at the 2025 Alibaba Cloud Enterprise Going Global Conference, Wu Yongming stated that Alibaba Cloud will strategically invest in accelerating the construction of a global cloud computing network, speeding up the internationalization of AI products, enhancing the development of overseas consulting, technology, and service teams, and paving the way for Chinese companies going global. Similarly, Huawei Cloud has also released a series of measures and solutions for Chinese companies going global, launching the Global Business Boosting solution in 2025, covering the four stages of going global: "consulting planning, cloud acceleration, cloud innovation, and ecosystem development," reducing the threshold for companies going global. Although Alibaba Cloud and Huawei Cloud have different focuses in their support for going global, both emphasize the importance of localized services, including deep integration of technology adaptation, talent, culture, and compliance systems. As Han Hongyuan mentioned, the biggest difference between Chinese companies going global today and foreign companies entering China during the early days of reform and opening up is the disappearance of the technological gap. Chinese companies now have the technological strength to compete with their global counterparts, and the global layout of cloud service providers further narrows the operational and ecological gaps. Digital infrastructure is no longer just technical support but has become a key variable determining the global competitiveness of companies going global. In the future, companies going global will enter a stage of "meticulous cultivation." title_en: Looking at the next round of China's economic "opportunity" from the "Private Economy Promotion Law" | Minmao Perspective
body_en: On May 20th, the Private Economy Promotion Law officially came into effect. Since the proposal to formulate this law in December 2024, to its formal promulgation and implementation in less than a year and a half, it is evident how determined the legislators were. A relevant official from the Ministry of Justice stated that the enactment of the Private Economy Promotion Law is an important measure to implement the important instructions of General Secretary Xi Jinping and the decision-making arrangements of the Party Central Committee. It is a landmark event in the construction of a socialist market economy and holds milestone significance in the development of China's private economy. Since the 20th National Congress, the support for the private economy in the country has significantly increased. In July 2023, the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council issued the "Opinions on Promoting the Development and Growth of the Private Economy," proposing 31 specific measures. In July 2024, the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee listed "formulating the Private Economy Promotion Law" as an important reform measure. In the same year in December, the Central Economic Work Conference made clear requirements for the promulgation of this law. In February 2025, General Secretary Xi Jinping attended a symposium of private enterprises and delivered an important speech. The official promulgation of the Private Economy Promotion Law signifies a dense issuance of policies and laws, indicating that China's private economy is about to usher in a new phase of significant development opportunities. The first chapter of the law aims to eliminate the market bottlenecks and institutional obstacles faced by the current development of the private economy. The stability of enterprises leads to economic stability, and strong enterprises lead to a strong economy. Why is the private economy so important? The answer can be found in the data set "56789": as of 2024, private enterprises have contributed more than 50% of tax revenue, over 60% of the national GDP, more than 70% of technological innovation achievements, over 80% of urban employment, with the number of private enterprises accounting for over 90% of the total number of enterprises, and the total import and export value accounting for over 50% of the total foreign trade value. Behind "56789," the private economy has grown into a solid pillar of the national economy, playing a core role in stabilizing the Chinese economy, ensuring people's livelihoods, promoting innovation, and driving development. However, in recent years, the development of the private economy has faced a series of significant challenges, including the impact of the three-year pandemic, the China-US trade war, and the transformation and upgrading of the Chinese economy. Private enterprises are at the forefront of the market, facing the greatest difficulties and pressures. According to statistics, private investment has been negative for two consecutive years, with the proportion falling to 50.1%, a decrease of 15 percentage points from the peak ten years ago. According to the 2024 national survey data from the China Economic System Reform Research Association of the National Development and Reform Commission, the main operational difficulties faced by private entrepreneurs currently are "few orders, few customers, insufficient consumption" (57.8%), "fierce competition, low profits" (42.2%), while the urgent need for government support for private enterprises includes "strengthening talent and employment demand guarantees" (45.2%), "implementing fair competition policy systems" (42.6%), "improving the normalization of prevention and clearance mechanisms for overdue payments" (32.5%), "improving financing support policy systems" (32.2%), "supporting private enterprises to enhance technological innovation capabilities" (31.4%), and "removing market access barriers" (30.6%), among others. High-quality development and common prosperity are the two core goals of China's economic development in the new era. Looking at the two sets of data mentioned above, with private enterprises contributing over 70% of technological innovation and over 80% of employment, it is clear that to achieve the two major goals of high-quality development driven by innovation and common prosperity, there must be a strong determination and effort to continuously promote the development and growth of the private economy, allowing private enterprises to become bigger and stronger. On the other hand, with over 90% of private enterprises contributing only slightly over 50% of tax revenue and just over 60% of GDP, it indicates that private enterprises currently face challenges such as thin profits, operational difficulties, low technological content, and weak development. It is urgent to eliminate the market bottlenecks and institutional obstacles that hinder the further development of private enterprises, promoting high-quality and leapfrog development of the private economy. The promulgation of the Private Economy Promotion Law is timely. The new law consists of 9 chapters and 78 articles, based on the principles of "equal treatment, fair competition, equal protection, and common development." It comprehensively formulates legal provisions to promote the development and growth of the private economy from seven aspects, including fair competition, investment and financing promotion, technological innovation, and rights protection, focusing on key issues encountered in the current development of the private economy. As the first fundamental law specifically addressing the development of the private economy, the new law explicitly defines the legal status of the private economy for the first time, incorporating the "two adherences" into the law. It also includes the statement that "promoting the sustained, healthy, and high-quality development of the private economy is a major long-term policy of the state" into the legal provisions. This marks a historic leap for China's private economy from "policy support" to "legal escort," fully demonstrating the firm determination of the Party Central Committee to promote the development and growth of the private economy. In the new historical period, the private economy bears a new historical mission. The private economy is the source of innovation for China's economic growth, and establishing a fair competition mechanism is the economic and legal foundation for implementing a unified national market. Strengthening and expanding the private economy is the fundamental guarantee for achieving common prosperity. Whether state-owned enterprises or private enterprises, they are the wealth of the country and the people, an important part of the socialist market economy. State-owned enterprises and private enterprises are the two "economic battle regulars" under the leadership of the Party, each bearing their own economic and social responsibilities. The key to reforming state-owned enterprises lies in "focusing on large and letting go of small," while the key to reforming private enterprises lies in "focusing on small and letting go of large." Each private enterprise is like a "seed," and as long as it is placed under the sunlight of the rule of law and in the soil of the market economy, it has the potential to grow into a towering tree. The development and growth of the private economy are the fundamental driving force for sustainable economic growth and high-quality development in China. Under the perspective of the Private Economy Promotion Law, new trends and patterns of economic development are emerging. Those who follow the natural order will succeed, and those who act with determination will achieve success. "In the new era and on the new journey, the prospects for the development of the private economy are broad and promising, and it is the right time for the vast number of private enterprises and entrepreneurs to demonstrate their capabilities." The promulgation of the Private Economy Promotion Law has provided a "reassurance pill" for the 50 million private enterprises nationwide and injected a "heart-strengthening agent." This is a milestone event in the construction of a socialist market economy. Currently, China's economy is at a critical stage of transformation and upgrading. The future trend of China's economic development is shifting from resource-driven to innovation-driven, from export-driven to domestic demand-driven, from coastal areas to inland regions, from urban to rural areas, ultimately aiming to achieve a unified national market and a new development pattern of dual circulation. Recently, Elon Musk predicted that China's economy will be two to three times the size of the United States in the future. To achieve such a grand goal, China's economy must undergo an explosive growth, with the greatest increment coming from the private economy. The global economic order and China's economic landscape are undergoing profound adjustments, and the economic forces at home and abroad are on the verge of a major battle. At this critical juncture, the country hopes that the private economy can quickly grow stronger and assume greater responsibilities and missions in the fight against challenges. The key directions of state support for the development of the private economy will become the "wind vane" for the next round of economic reform and development in China. By analyzing the relevant legal provisions of the Private Economy Promotion Law, we can make an assessment. 1. Fair competition clause: Ensuring equal development rights for private enterprises. The law stipulates: The country implements a nationwide unified market access negative list system, implements a fair competition review system, and follows the principle of "non-prohibition or entry" for private enterprises; public resource transactions such as bidding, government procurement, and monopolistic industries shall not restrict or exclude private enterprises; in the allocation and use of natural resources, public service resources, and human resources, private enterprises shall be treated equally. One of the main reasons hindering the development and growth of the private economy is the deep-rooted discrimination against private enterprises in society. The phenomenon of "glass doors" and "revolving doors" is very common in market access, resource allocation, and policy measures related to talent treatment. To complement the implementation of the Private Economy Promotion Law, the National Development and Reform Commission, together with the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation, promptly issued a notice on carrying out a campaign to clear and rectify market access barriers to promote the construction of a unified national market. This campaign aims to comprehensively clear and rectify various unreasonable provisions and practices that set up market access barriers in violation of regulations, creating a fair market access environment. Except for a few "restricted areas," all industries and markets are open to private enterprises, and the state legally guarantees the equal rights of private enterprises to use various production factors such as funds, technology, human resources, data, and land. If the above legal provisions can be effectively implemented, the market position of private enterprises and state-owned enterprises will be completely equal. This is a basic requirement for implementing a unified national market and an inevitable requirement for realizing a socialist market economy with Chinese characteristics. Only by fully unleashing the enormous potential for the development of private enterprises can the greatest advantages of the "mixed ownership system" be stimulated, and the best results of the socialist market economy of "1+1>2" be achieved. 2. Investment and financing promotion clause: Financial support must tilt towards private enterprises. The law stipulates: Support private enterprises in investing in national major strategic projects, strategic emerging industries, and the construction of modern infrastructure; relax the tolerance for non-performing loans for inclusive small and micro-enterprise loans, support private enterprises in providing accounts receivable, warehouse receipts, equity, intellectual property rights, and other rights for pledge loans, and provide a green channel for chattel mortgage registration; lower the threshold for private enterprises to go public, etc. Difficulty in investment and financing is another important reason hindering the development and growth of private enterprises. To complement the implementation of the Private Economy Promotion Law, the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission has introduced multiple financial support policies to break the capital bottleneck for the development of private enterprises. The state's key support areas are twofold: one is loans for small and micro-enterprises, as it involves employment and people's livelihoods, the tolerance for non-performing loans has been relaxed to 3%, and the risk capital weight has been discounted from 85% to 75%, in order to increase the enthusiasm of banks to lend. The other area is high-tech and emerging industries, which are the two key directions for state support of private enterprise development. Currently, pilot projects for equity investment by financial asset investment companies are being carried out, promoting the construction of a comprehensive experimental zone for intellectual property finance, focusing on improving the service model of technology finance to support investment in technology innovation enterprises. Only by continuously increasing financial support and promoting the continuous development and growth of private enterprises can the fundamental economic challenges of ensuring people's livelihoods and driving innovation be fundamentally addressed. 3. Technological innovation clause: Promoting private enterprises to become the main force of national science and technology and industrial innovation. The law stipulates: Support private enterprises in strengthening basic and cutting-edge research, developing key core technologies, common basic technologies, and cutting-edge cross-disciplinary technologies, promoting the integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation, fostering new industries, new models, and new drivers; support capable private enterprises in taking the lead in undertaking national major technology research tasks, and open national major scientific research infrastructure to private enterprises; the state strengthens the protection of original innovation by private enterprises and their operators. Technology is the primary productive force, and innovation is the primary driving force. Private enterprises account for over 92% of high-tech enterprises in the country, and specialized and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises account for over 95%. Private enterprises have become the mainstay of national science and technology and industrial innovation. However, due to the incomplete reform of the scientific and technological system and the lack of inclination of national scientific and technological resources towards private enterprises, the market has not fully played its decisive role in resource allocation. On May 20th, the Private Economy Promotion Law officially came into effect. Since the proposal to formulate this law in December 2024, to its formal promulgation and implementation in less than a year and a half, it is evident how determined the legislators were. A relevant official from the Ministry of Justice stated that the enactment of the Private Economy Promotion Law is an important measure to implement the important instructions of General Secretary Xi Jinping and the decision-making arrangements of the Party Central Committee. It is a landmark event in the construction of a socialist market economy and holds milestone significance in the development of China's private economy. Since the 20th National Congress, the support for the private economy in the country has significantly increased. In July 2023, the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council issued the "Opinions on Promoting the Development and Growth of the Private Economy," proposing 31 specific measures. In July 2024, the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee listed "formulating the Private Economy Promotion Law" as an important reform measure. In the same year in December, the Central Economic Work Conference made clear requirements for the promulgation of this law. In February 2025, General Secretary Xi Jinping attended a symposium of private enterprises and delivered an important speech.
