title_en: "Double engine" drives this shopping festival (picture)
body_en: The annual mid-year shopping festival, "618," is in full swing, with online and offline promotions battling for over twenty days. When "low prices" become the norm, this year's "618" sees new, attention-grabbing phenomena emerging beyond price wars: "export-to-domestic" goods and "new national brands" are powerfully taking center stage, becoming new engines to drive consumption growth. This annual consumer feast is quietly evolving into an important window to observe China's industrial transformation and domestic demand potential. Pressure Forces Change Foreign Trade Enterprises' "Internal Circulation" Breakthrough Battle The U.S.'s tariff hammer, coupled with the uncertainty of the global trade environment, has sent a chilling wave through many Chinese foreign trade enterprises that have long relied on overseas orders. Returning to the vast domestic demand market has become their inevitable choice to seek survival. ■ Case 1: The "Dual Circulation" Path of "Carpet Town" Cuihuangkou Town in Wuqing District, Tianjin, a small town of less than 100 square kilometers, once accounted for half of the country's carpet production, truly earning its title as "Carpet Town." Over 1,200 carpet enterprises form the industrial cornerstone of the town, with hundreds of large-scale enterprises focusing on overseas markets. However, U.S. tariffs exceeding 30% have put immense pressure on enterprises primarily exporting to the U.S. Liu Mingjun, born in the 1980s and the third-generation head of a family carpet business, deeply understands this: "Exporting to the U.S. is on a 'lifeline,' and foreign trade business is mainly in a wait-and-see mode." Under these circumstances, the "walking on two legs" strategy that the enterprise has adhered to for years has become a key support, providing a solid buffer for the domestic sales team that has been deeply cultivated for many years. At the same time, Liu Mingjun is actively expanding into markets such as the Middle East, Russia, and Southeast Asia, and is responding positively to the government's plan to participate in an exhibition in Russia in September: "We will definitely go, we must break into new markets!" The carpet industry affects the livelihoods of 54,000 people in Cuihuangkou Town, with nearly half of the population directly or indirectly employed. Carpet output value accounts for one-fifth of the town's GDP, with exports contributing nearly half. Under pressure, departments at all levels, from the municipal to the town, have acted swiftly: intensively organizing "export-to-domestic" matchmaking meetings, forming groups to explore emerging markets like Vietnam and Thailand, and establishing centralized procurement companies to reduce raw material costs... Government-enterprise synergy is injecting momentum into the industry. However, "transitioning to domestic sales" is by no means a simple switch of sales channels. Liu Mingjun highlights the key challenge: "Consumer preferences vary greatly across countries. The U.S. favors thick and durable washable carpets, Saudi Arabia prefers vibrant ethnic patterns, while the domestic market favors soft-touch imitation cashmere carpets." The gap in categories, materials, and colors means products need to be deeply reimagined. For this reason, her enterprise firmly implements a "dual circulation" strategy: on one hand, actively expanding domestic demand; on the other hand, never lightly giving up on the overseas markets cultivated for many years. Chen Chenggong, secretary-general of the Cuihuangkou Town Chamber of Commerce, stated that this year the town government has meticulously planned a series of professional sales training sessions for e-commerce platforms, attracting the deep participation of platforms such as Pinduoduo Overseas Edition (TEMU), JD.com, and Taobao. At the same time, export enterprises are accelerating their transformation, shifting to diversified business strategies of "online + offline" and "domestic + international" to enhance their risk resistance. "Resilience is etched in the DNA of Cuihuangkou's carpet industry; through a century of storms, we always find new paths," said Chen Chenggong. ■ Case 2: The "Internal and External Cultivation" Balancing Act of the "Hometown of Silk Flowers" A similar transformation story is unfolding in another characteristic industrial cluster in Wuqing District, Tianjin—the artificial flower industrial cluster in Caolizi Town. Caolizi Town is a well-known "Hometown of Silk Flowers," with an industrial scale accounting for about one-third of the national total and an annual output value of nearly 2 billion yuan. Of the town's 28,000 residents, over 15,000 are engaged in silk flower production. Previously, 90% of silk flowers from Caolizi Town were exported overseas. Today, this flower is writing a new chapter of "internal and external cultivation." Wang Wenlong, manager of Meiyu Craft Flower Co., Ltd. in the town, told reporters: "During '618,' our sales indeed increased significantly compared to usual. The domestic market shows signs of recovery this year, and we actively participated in the major promotions of various platforms." Wang Wenlong's enterprise is deeply involved in the entire artificial flower industry chain, covering raw materials, production, agency, and online sales. He admitted that the company's strategy is to "grasp both hands equally firmly": on one hand, making great efforts to develop the domestic market; on the other hand, never giving up on the export market. He crunched the numbers: the company focused on domestic sales at its inception, then gradually opened up international markets. Currently, the sales ratio of domestic to export has stabilized at 4:6. "'Meiyu Craft Flower' will do its utmost to maintain and develop in both markets," Wang Wenlong emphasized. With advantages such as timely supply and low defect rates, the company's own brands are quite popular on Alibaba International Station and domestic trade platforms, with annual sales stable at around 100 million yuan. However, Wang Wenlong has also keenly observed changes in the domestic e-commerce ecosystem: "The enthusiasm of buyers and sellers on platforms for big promotions seems to be less intense than in previous years. There are online live streams every day, and discounts are available at all times. The 'scarcity' of major promotions is diminishing." This suggests that foreign trade enterprises transitioning to domestic sales need not only adapt to product differences but also profoundly understand the rapidly iterating domestic e-commerce gameplay and consumer psychology. National Subsidies Fuel Fire Some National Brands Explore "All-Time Low Prices" A significant change in this year's "618" is the strong intervention of national-level "trade-in" subsidies (hereinafter referred to as "national subsidies"). Building on last year's coverage of 8 major categories including washing machines, televisions, and air conditioners, the national subsidy categories have been significantly expanded this year, adding more items such as mobile phones and digital products, smartwatches (and bracelets), microwave ovens, water purifiers, and dishwashers, further activating consumers' enthusiasm for upgrades and becoming an accelerator for "new national brands" to "break out." Taobao Tmall stated that the national subsidy categories covered on its platform exceed 1,600, including 12 major categories of home appliances, mobile phones and digital products, smart wearables, as well as smart home, home improvement, and other newly added categories. At the same time, Taobao Tmall has undertaken the online distribution of national subsidies for 29 provinces and cities across the country, becoming one of the platforms with the widest coverage, attracting over 150 million visits to national subsidy products daily. The "national subsidy + platform subsidy" combination has brought consumers unprecedented benefits. In social media feeds, shopping tips like "for the price of a wool coat, you can buy a quite good air conditioner" are widely circulated. With multiple subsidies superimposed, prices of domestic big-brand popular home appliances have collectively "plummeted," with some categories experiencing "all-time low prices." Taking air conditioners as an example, the subsidy intensity has significantly increased: from a limit of one unit per household last year to three units this year, with a maximum subsidy of 6,000 yuan. This has directly stimulated consumption: Haier's energy-saving 1.5 HP split air conditioner: original price 2,799 yuan, now 1,486 yuan (about 5.3 fold); Midea's Cool Gold air conditioner: original price 2,499 yuan, with national subsidy and "618" discounts, the final price is 1,559 yuan; TCL's 1.5 HP new-level heating and cooling air conditioner: original price 2,499 yuan, with national subsidy and "618" discounts, the final price is only 1,199 yuan (about 4.6 fold)... Many consumers in Tianjin took this opportunity to replace all their home air conditioners. Ms. He, a resident of Nankai District, not only replaced her own air conditioner but also successfully persuaded her mother-in-law to do the same: "The new air conditioner not only has a simple and attractive appearance but, more importantly, is more energy-efficient." On the JD.com platform, the effect of national subsidies is equally significant. The transaction amount for categories such as domestic tires, automotive maintenance supplies, and repair and modification parts increased by over 30 times year-on-year, while the transaction amount for electric bicycles increased by 300%. Domestic new energy vehicle-related categories have grown rapidly, with transaction amounts for automotive charging equipment increasing by 10 times year-on-year. Policy dividends are precisely irrigating key areas of green consumption and industrial upgrading. Minor Flaws Remain: Pain Points in Experience Persist Although national subsidies have effectively boosted consumer enthusiasm, the convenience of policy implementation and the user experience of platform functions still have room for improvement, creating some discordant notes amidst the "618" fervor. Ms. Lü, who lives in Hexi District, wanted to buy a Dongling dough mixer during "618." She saw on the Taobao flagship store's main image that the "618 price was about 624 yuan" and added it to her cart in advance. However, when she placed the order after the promotion began, the checkout page consistently showed 714 yuan, no matter how she tried. After consulting customer service, she received a complex operating guide: she needed to claim the subsidy first, place a separate order, and finally use "UnionPay QuickPass" to pay. Ms. Lü, who is not accustomed to using "UnionPay QuickPass," switched to the same product on JD.com and found that it also required "UnionPay QuickPass" and the price remained unchanged. After several unsuccessful communication attempts, Ms. Lü was ultimately dissuaded by the cumbersome process and decisively chose to forgo the national subsidy, purchasing it for 619 yuan from a distributor on Taobao. "The policy is good, but the operation is too troublesome. I hope the process can be simpler and more intuitive," Ms. Lü said helplessly. Ms. Liu, who lives in Hedong District, was troubled by the platform's "intelligent" recommendations. She found that a fish oil product she had browsed was "automatically" added to her shopping cart multiple times without her initiating it. "I just browsed it, I didn't intend to buy it, but the product was forced into my cart. This kind of 'forced addition' feature is too 'rogue'!" Despite multiple complaints to the platform, the problem recurred, severely affecting her shopping mood. This reflects the need for a better balance between platforms pursuing conversion rates and respecting user choice. National Brands Rise Time-Honored Brands Renewed and High-Quality Domestic Products Popular While "high-quality foreign trade products" accelerate domestic sales, a group of "time-honored brands" carrying national memories and new national brands that have risen through their strong capabilities have also shone brightly during this "618," demonstrating strong brand appeal and market competitiveness. As the first national bicycle brand in New China, "Flying Pigeon," a name carrying the memories of generations, is attracting more and more young followers. On JD.com's Flying Pigeon official flagship store, a popular mountain bike has received over 50,000 positive reviews. The platform's "Billion Subsidy" is unprecedented: the daily price of 914 yuan is reduced by 166 yuan, with the final price only 748 yuan. User reviews are filled with praise such as "good quality, low price," "cool appearance is stunning," and "old brand's cost-effectiveness is excellent." Another JD.com self-operated Flying Pigeon smart electric bicycle priced at 999 yuan even became the sales champion in the sub-1000 yuan price segment. The bicycle industry is one of Tianjin's representative industries in its export-oriented economy. Public data shows that in 2024, Tianjin's bicycle export volume and export value both accounted for over 30% of the national share, ranking first in national bicycle exports for 12 consecutive years since 2013. Jinghai, Tianjin, is known as the "Capital of Chinese Bicycles and Electric Bicycles," and Wangqingtuo Town in Wuqing District is a well-known industrial base, with brands like Flying Pigeon and Fujida enjoying fame at home and abroad. A responsible person from an electric bicycle enterprise in Tianjin revealed to reporters that the tariff war has indeed affected the export of domestic bicycles to the U.S. However, fortunately, the company's layout in markets such as Southeast Asia, Europe, and South America is relatively balanced, and the overall pressure is bearable. More encouragingly, with the stabilization of the domestic consumption market and the deepening of the concept of green and low-carbon travel, the domestic bicycle sales market is showing strong growth momentum, thanks to the precise reach of online platforms. Data released by the digital freight platform Yunmanman on World Bicycle Day confirms this: Tianjin is the undisputed "King of Bicycles," with the highest shipping volume nationwide; the top five regions receiving Tianjin bicycles are Shandong, Xinjiang, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Hunan, reflecting the abundant vitality of the internal circulation. The charm of national brands is not limited to nostalgia. In an era of increasingly rational consumption, high cost-performance and high-quality domestic products are becoming consumers' "favorite." In the scorching summer heat, domestic pure silk clothing sales on various e-commerce platforms are exceptionally popular. Multiple brands from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Shanghai have sold out. Consumer reviews are practical and direct: "I used to blindly trust international big brands, with a chemical fiber shirt costing thousands or even tens of thousands of yuan. Now I buy domestic brands, 100% pure silk, with good design and workmanship, for only a few hundred yuan. It's amazing!" This shift from blindly pursuing "foreign brands" to recognizing the "quality-price ratio" of domestic products provides a solid consumption foundation for the rise of national brands. Similarly, Tianjin's "time-honored brands" like Yumaojing Children's Cream, as well as a batch of emerging domestic skincare and cosmetics brands, have become new favorites among beauty enthusiasts with their "conscientious prices" and "high cost-performance." After trying them, consumers exclaimed, "National brands are truly amazing" when comparing them to expensive international brands. More than a dozen leading platforms, including Alibaba, JD.com, Pinduoduo, Douyin, and Kuaishou, have all invested heavily, making "export-to-domestic" goods and new national brands strategic high ground, with unprecedented investment intensity. Platforms are providing resource tilting with real money to build "moats": JD.com has launched a 200 billion yuan special support plan covering traffic, logistics, finance, and services, focusing on supporting foreign trade enterprises, industrial belt merchants, and "time-honored brands." Pinduoduo's "hundred billion yuan support" focuses on cross-border small and medium-sized merchants transitioning to domestic sales, providing special subsidies, traffic support, and operational guidance. Douyin E-commerce has launched a "Special Support Plan for High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" with remarkable results. According to its disclosure, from April 16th to May 9th, the transaction value of domestic brands participating in this plan exceeded 430 million yuan, with live streaming sales contributing over 300 million yuan. Kuaishou E-commerce has established a "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" special assistance team and released multiple measures: opening green channels for entry, tilting exclusive traffic and subsidies, creating hot topics, short video seeding, influencer live streaming sourcing, and setting up "National Brand Category Days" to comprehensively promote the transformation of "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" into "National Brand Bestsellers." In addition, Meituan has launched five measures to pave the way for foreign trade enterprises; Baidu is using AI technology to help millions of enterprises develop domestic sales; Hema has opened a 24-hour green channel; and JD Seven Fresh has launched the "Quality Merchant Plan"... "Direct procurement of orders," "exclusive traffic," and "supply-demand matching" have become standard actions for platforms supporting foreign trade transitions to domestic sales. A "positioning battle" for high-quality foreign trade supply chains has fully escalated. Platforms are not only responding to the national "dual circulation" strategy but also valuing the R&D capabilities and strict quality control standards that foreign trade enterprises have accumulated over many years. Zhuang Shuai, a specially appointed researcher at the E-commerce Research Center of the eNet Research Institute and founder of Bailian Consulting, analyzed: "The manufacturing capabilities that have long served European and American markets can precisely fill the supply gap in China's mid-to-high-end consumption. These high-quality supply chains are core resources for platforms to upgrade their product pools and attract high-end users." Platforms also know well that not all foreign trade enterprises can easily "turn around." "Insufficient e-commerce experience, inventory backlog, and difficulty in acquiring traffic" are the three common pain points faced by foreign trade enterprises. Therefore, platforms are offering "nanny-style" services to solve their transformation challenges. Foreign trade industrial belts in Ningbo, Linhai, and Cixi in Zhejiang have been suffering from a decrease in orders since last year. Deep cooperation with e-commerce platforms during "618" has brought them a turning point. The shipment volume of products such as garment steamers, fans, and vacuum cleaners has significantly increased. Some platform e-commerce teams have even taken on the entire sales and fulfillment chain for some enterprises, including product selection, online operations, marketing promotion, logistics and distribution, and customer service and after-sales, allowing foreign trade enterprises lacking domestic e-commerce experience to "travel light." The case of Yangzhou Shuguang Toothbrush Factory is quite representative. This old enterprise with annual exports exceeding 200 million yuan faced a crisis of three production lines potentially shutting down due to a sharp drop in foreign trade orders under the impact of the tariff storm. After JD.com's Jingxi self-operated team intervened, they developed a new "soft-bristled toothbrush" category based on big data analysis of domestic consumption trends and precisely targeted consumers in third- and fourth-tier cities. The enterprise负责人 remarked: "The platform's data and channel empowerment have allowed us to find a breakthrough in domestic sales. We are now setting a domestic sales target of 100 million yuan and plan to develop more 'Chinese-flavored' products that meet domestic demand in the future." According to data from the Ministry of Commerce, since April, e-commerce platforms have, through eight major measures such as direct procurement of orders and setting up foreign trade zones, attracted over 3,100 foreign trade enterprises, with sales in special zones exceeding 1.1 billion yuan and platform direct procurement reaching tens of billions. The platform's role as a main battlefield in assisting foreign trade to transition to domestic sales is becoming increasingly prominent. Expert Opinion: Deep Cultivation Leads to "Long-Term Popularity" The acceleration of foreign trade enterprises returning to the domestic demand market is a strategic adjustment under multiple pressures and a reflection of China's economic resilience and domestic demand potential. Experts believe that this process is fraught with both opportunities and challenges, posing higher demands on enterprise capabilities. "The return of foreign trade enterprises to the domestic demand market is essentially an inevitable choice under multiple pressures such as rising export costs and shrinking overseas orders caused by Sino-U.S. tariff barriers," Zhuang Shuai pointed out incisively. However, for foreign trade enterprises that have long relied on the large-order overseas model, transitioning to domestic sales means all-around challenges: 1. Production Mode Conflicts: The contradiction between large-scale production for European and American orders and the domestic demand for small-batch, multi-batch, and fast-response flexible production. 2. Channel Cost Pressure: The high traffic costs and payment term pressures on domestic e-commerce platforms may significantly squeeze enterprise profit margins. 3. Standard Conversion Barriers: In fields such as food and home appliances, different domestic and international quality, safety, and certification standards need to be navigated, increasing compliance costs. 4. Brand Recognition and Marketing: Many foreign trade OEM enterprises lack domestic brand recognition and need to build brand image and marketing systems from scratch. Bao Yuezhong, Chairman of Baum Consulting, emphasized: "Platform and policy support and endorsement can play a certain role, but the key is for enterprises to proactively seek change and not 'wait for, rely on, or ask for.' Enterprises familiar with international markets must quickly settle down to study the characteristics of domestic market demand, e-commerce channel rules, and supermarket channel gameplay. Cooperation is two-way, and the cultivation of the enterprise's own internal strengths is crucial." Moreover, the large-scale return of foreign trade enterprises to domestic sales also serves as a "shot in the arm" for local enterprises, creating a significant "catfish effect." Zhuang Shuai analyzed: Foreign trade goods generally adhere to the high-quality standards of exports to Europe and America. At the same quality level, their prices are more competitive, raising the quality benchmark for the domestic market. In addition, the mature after-sales service systems of foreign trade enterprises are being brought into the domestic market, helping to raise the overall consumption service level. At the same time, novel product categories, such as outdoor equipment, smart home appliances, and distinctive small home appliances, which were previously mainly exported, are accelerating their entry into the domestic market, enriching consumer choices. All these factors will force local enterprises to accelerate product iteration and improve service quality, promoting overall industrial upgrading. The smoke of "618" will eventually dissipate. The grand transformation from "high-quality foreign trade goods" to "national brand bestsellers" is by no means achievable in a single promotional event. It tests the enterprises' deep cultivation ability to understand the local market, reshape their product systems, build brand power, and optimize their supply chains; it tests how platforms can more accurately match supply and demand, empower merchants more efficiently, and serve consumers more friendly; it also tests how policies can be implemented more smoothly and more effectively stimulate market vitality. —Whoever can transform "bestsellers" from "618" into sustained "long-term popularity" will win a broader future in the new chapter of China's high-quality economic development. Opportunities and challenges coexist, and deep cultivation leads to far-reaching achievements.

Jinghai, Tianjin, is known as the "Capital of Chinese Bicycles and Electric Bicycles," and Wangqingtuo Town in Wuqing District is a well-known industrial base, with brands like Flying Pigeon and Fujida enjoying fame at home and abroad. A responsible person from an electric bicycle enterprise in Tianjin revealed to reporters that the tariff war has indeed affected the export of domestic bicycles to the U.S. However, fortunately, the company's layout in markets such as Southeast Asia, Europe, and South America is relatively balanced, and the overall pressure is bearable. More encouragingly, with the stabilization of the domestic consumption market and the deepening of the concept of green and low-carbon travel, the domestic bicycle sales market is showing strong growth momentum, thanks to the precise reach of online platforms. Data released by the digital freight platform Yunmanman on World Bicycle Day confirms this: Tianjin is the undisputed "King of Bicycles," with the highest shipping volume nationwide; the top five regions receiving Tianjin bicycles are Shandong, Xinjiang, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Hunan, reflecting the abundant vitality of the internal circulation. The charm of national brands is not limited to nostalgia. In an era of increasingly rational consumption, high cost-performance and high-quality domestic products are becoming consumers' "favorite." In the scorching summer heat, domestic pure silk clothing sales on various e-commerce platforms are exceptionally popular. Multiple brands from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Shanghai have sold out. Consumer reviews are practical and direct: "I used to blindly trust international big brands, with a chemical fiber shirt costing thousands or even tens of thousands of yuan. Now I buy domestic brands, 100% pure silk, with good design and workmanship, for only a few hundred yuan. It's amazing!" This shift from blindly pursuing "foreign brands" to recognizing the "quality-price ratio" of domestic products provides a solid consumption foundation for the rise of national brands. Similarly, Tianjin's "time-honored brands" like Yumaojing Children's Cream, as well as a batch of emerging domestic skincare and cosmetics brands, have become new favorites among beauty enthusiasts with their "conscientious prices" and "high cost-performance." After trying them, consumers exclaimed, "National brands are truly amazing" when comparing them to expensive international brands. Platform Competition From "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" to "National Brand Bestsellers" The accelerated shift of foreign trade enterprises to domestic sales has triggered an unprecedented resource competition among e-commerce platforms. More than a dozen leading platforms, including Alibaba, JD.com, Pinduoduo, Douyin, and Kuaishou, have all invested heavily, making "export-to-domestic" goods and new national brands strategic high ground, with unprecedented investment intensity. Platforms are providing resource tilting with real money to build "moats": JD.com has launched a 200 billion yuan special support plan covering traffic, logistics, finance, and services, focusing on supporting foreign trade enterprises, industrial belt merchants, and "time-honored brands." Pinduoduo's "hundred billion yuan support" focuses on cross-border small and medium-sized merchants transitioning to domestic sales, providing special subsidies, traffic support, and operational guidance. Douyin E-commerce has launched a "Special Support Plan for High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" with remarkable results. According to its disclosure, from April 16th to May 9th, the transaction value of domestic brands participating in this plan exceeded 430 million yuan, with live streaming sales contributing over 300 million yuan. Kuaishou E-commerce has established a "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" special assistance team and released multiple measures: opening green channels for entry, tilting exclusive traffic and subsidies, creating hot topics, short video seeding, influencer live streaming sourcing, and setting up "National Brand Category Days" to comprehensively promote the transformation of "High-Quality Foreign Trade Goods" into "National Brand Bestsellers." In addition, Meituan has launched five measures to pave the way for foreign trade enterprises; Baidu is using AI technology to help millions of enterprises develop domestic sales; Hema has opened a 24-hour green channel; and JD Seven Fresh has launched the "Quality Merchant Plan"... "Direct procurement of orders," "exclusive traffic," and "supply-demand matching" have become standard actions for platforms supporting foreign trade transitions to domestic sales. A "positioning battle" for high-quality foreign trade supply chains has fully escalated. Platforms are not only responding to the national "dual circulation" strategy but also valuing the R&D capabilities and strict quality control standards that foreign trade enterprises have accumulated over many years. Zhuang Shuai, a specially appointed researcher at the E-commerce Research Center of the eNet Research Institute and founder of Bailian Consulting, analyzed: "The manufacturing capabilities that have long served European and American markets can precisely fill the supply gap in China's mid-to-high-end consumption. These high-quality supply chains are core resources for platforms to upgrade their product pools and attract high-end users." Platforms also know well that not all foreign trade enterprises can easily "turn around." "Insufficient e-commerce experience, inventory backlog, and difficulty in acquiring traffic" are the three common pain points faced by foreign trade enterprises. Therefore, platforms are offering "nanny-style" services to solve their transformation challenges. Foreign trade industrial belts in Ningbo, Linhai, and Cixi in Zhejiang have been suffering from a decrease in orders since last year. Deep cooperation with e-commerce platforms during "618" has brought them a turning point. The shipment volume of products such as garment steamers, fans, and vacuum cleaners has significantly increased. Some platform e-commerce teams have even taken on the entire sales and fulfillment chain for some enterprises, including product selection, online operations, marketing promotion, logistics and distribution, and customer service and after-sales, allowing foreign trade enterprises lacking domestic e-commerce experience to "travel light." The case of Yangzhou Shuguang Toothbrush Factory is quite representative. This old enterprise with annual exports exceeding 200 million yuan faced a crisis of three production lines potentially shutting down due to a sharp drop in foreign trade orders under the impact of the tariff storm. After JD.com's Jingxi self-operated team intervened, they developed a new "soft-bristled toothbrush" category based on big data analysis of domestic consumption trends and precisely targeted consumers in third- and fourth-tier cities. The enterprise负责人 remarked: "The platform's data and channel empowerment have allowed us to find a breakthrough in domestic sales. We are now setting a domestic sales target of 100 million yuan and plan to develop more 'Chinese-flavored' products that meet domestic demand in the future." According to data from the Ministry of Commerce, since April, e-commerce platforms have, through eight major measures such as direct procurement of orders and setting up foreign trade zones, attracted over 3,100 foreign trade enterprises, with sales in special zones exceeding 1.1 billion yuan and platform direct procurement reaching tens of billions. The platform's role as a main battlefield in assisting foreign trade to transition to domestic sales is becoming increasingly prominent. Expert Opinion: Deep Cultivation Leads to "Long-Term Popularity" The acceleration of foreign trade enterprises returning to the domestic demand market is a strategic adjustment under multiple pressures and a reflection of China's economic resilience and domestic demand potential. Experts believe that this process is fraught with both opportunities and challenges, posing higher demands on enterprise capabilities. "The return of foreign trade enterprises to the domestic demand market is essentially an inevitable choice under multiple pressures such as rising export costs and shrinking overseas orders caused by Sino-U.S. tariff barriers," Zhuang Shuai pointed out incisively. However, for foreign trade enterprises that have long relied on the large-order overseas model, transitioning to domestic sales means all-around challenges: 1. Production Mode Conflicts: The contradiction between large-scale production for European and American orders and the domestic demand for small-batch, multi-batch, and fast-response flexible production. 2. Channel Cost Pressure: The high traffic costs and payment term pressures on domestic e-commerce platforms may significantly squeeze enterprise profit margins. 3. Standard Conversion Barriers: In fields such as food and home appliances, different domestic and international quality, safety, and certification standards need to be navigated, increasing compliance costs. 4. Brand Recognition and Marketing: Many foreign trade OEM enterprises lack domestic brand recognition and need to build brand image and marketing systems from scratch. Cooperation is two-way, and the cultivation of the enterprise's own internal strengths is crucial." At the same quality level, their prices are more competitive, raising the quality benchmark for the domestic market. At the same time, novel product categories, such as outdoor equipment, smart home appliances, and distinctive small home appliances, which were previously mainly exported, are accelerating their entry into the domestic market, enriching consumer choices. All these factors will force local enterprises to accelerate product iteration and improve service quality, promoting overall industrial upgrading. The smoke of "618" will eventually dissipate. The grand transformation from "high-quality foreign trade goods" to "national brand bestsellers" is by no means achievable in a single promotional event. It tests the enterprises' deep cultivation ability to understand the local market, reshape their product systems, build brand power, and optimize their supply chains; it tests how platforms can more accurately match supply and demand, empower merchants more efficiently, and serve consumers more friendly; it also tests how policies can be implemented more smoothly and more effectively stimulate market vitality. —Whoever can transform "bestsellers" from "618" into sustained "long-term popularity" will win a broader future in the new chapter of China's high-quality economic development. Opportunities and challenges coexist, and deep cultivation leads to far-reaching achievements.

title_en: Farewell to low-price internal competition, 618 can go further · Chongqing Daily Digital Newspaper
body_en: In 2025, the 618 shopping festival arrived earlier than before, kicking off on May 13th. In addition to being labeled as the "longest promotion in history," this year's 618 holds another special significance - it is the first 618 after the country clearly set the tone of "anti-internal competition." Looking back, 618 can be seen as a typical example of internal competition. In the early years, e-commerce platforms used discounts to attract customers and rapidly expand their user base in order to seize market share. As more platforms entered the market, the competition for low prices continued to intensify, with some platforms requiring merchants to offer the "lowest price on the entire network" and even engaging in "either-or" exclusive competition. At the same time, the complex and cumbersome rules of discounts and the endless pre-sale routines not only exhausted consumers' patience but also further exacerbated internal competition within the industry. When the early dividends dried up, 618 finally reached a standstill. Among those most exhausted were the merchants - on one hand, engaging in low-price competition inevitably compressed profit margins; on the other hand, those with high traffic prices won, and the threshold for participating in major promotions continued to rise. In this situation, merchants were making less and less money, either cutting back on quality and service to maintain a low-price advantage, or "raising prices first, then discounting." As a result, consumers' shopping experience was no longer guaranteed, and the attractiveness of major promotion events was greatly reduced. At this stage, 618 has fundamentally relied too much on exchanging growth for low prices, leading the industry into a zero-sum game. In fact, this kind of inefficient and repetitive "internal competition" has become a major obstacle to China's current economic transformation and upgrading. Therefore, last year's Central Political Bureau meeting and other meetings clearly called for the rectification of "internal competition," and this year's National People's Congress even included "comprehensively rectifying 'internal competition'" in the Government Work Report, demonstrating the decision-makers' firm determination to combat internal competition. From a macroeconomic perspective, China is currently in a critical period of transition from old to new driving forces. Against this backdrop, the development model relying on low prices and scale expansion has reached its limit and urgently needs to shift towards innovation-driven and quality improvement. For example, last year's 618, although the promotion period was extended to nearly a month, experienced negative growth for the first time in 16 years. This market feedback is a strong warning against past strategies. If companies invest a large amount of resources in price wars rather than cultivating core competitiveness, it will inevitably lead to the industry lingering in low-level and repetitive competition, hindering the optimization and upgrading of the entire economic structure. When faced with challenges, one must seek change. This year's 618 marks a turning point. In terms of activity rules, Taobao has changed from "cross-store discounts" to "official discounts"; in terms of platform relationships, JD Logistics has integrated with the Taobao system, and Taobao fully supports WeChat Pay... Platforms are no longer simply competing on low prices but are focusing on improving service efficiency and promoting resource sharing, reducing the tense competition and reshaping the ecosystem together. These changes are not only an active exploration of sustainable development models under policy guidance but also reflect the e-commerce industry's positive response to changes in market demand. 618 should serve as a mirror, allowing every industry to see its past and future. Take the food delivery industry, for example - the "money-burning war" between platforms is very similar to what 618 used to be; in addition, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers recently issued a proposal explicitly opposing the disorderly "price war" among car companies. This indicates that the phenomenon of low prices, low quality, and low-level competition still exists, and there is still a long way to go in rectifying "internal competition." This not only requires consensus within the industry but also relies on a combination of loosening and tightening, comprehensive governance, and multi-party efforts to build a new paradigm of healthy competition. By bidding farewell to low-price internal competition, we can go further. In the market, competition will never end, but good competition will elevate the industry rather than drag it down like a vortex. When we call for letting go of the obsession with low prices, we are actually calling for a return to values. Competing on value will inevitably be more challenging than competing on price, but success in this area means technological iteration and industry-wide advancement. Remember, falling downward may be fast in the short term, but it leads to the abyss; climbing higher, no matter how high the mountain, will eventually lead to the summit.

title_en: Build a "bridge" for African youth to start businesses in China.
body_en: Not long ago, energy storage products from a new energy company in Changsha, Hunan, crossed the ocean to the Republic of Mali (hereinafter referred to as "Mali"), bringing light to the local people. In addition to a container of products, the company is also establishing a presence in the capital of Mali, Bamako, and will use its industrial park as a pilot project to build a complete solar power system, gradually expanding to surrounding rural areas. This project, which has attracted the attention of the people of Mali, would not have been possible without the efforts of Aboubacar Garba KONTE, the head of the incubation station of the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base in Mali. On June 13, at an important special event of the 4th China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo, the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Dialogue, Konte was named an expert of the "Hunan Xiangjiang New Area-China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base Think Tank." This is a recognition of his contributions to China-Africa economic and trade cooperation. In 2016, Konte came to Beijing University of Science and Technology to pursue a Ph.D. in management. At that time, he never imagined that this period of study would completely change his life trajectory, and even bring new hope to his homeland in Africa. During his studies, Konte visited a Chinese solar factory. In the factory, rows of solar products were shining brightly in the sunlight, and workers were assembling new energy products. This scene deeply impressed him, "The most abundant resource in Africa is sunlight, but my hometown is plunged into darkness due to a lack of electricity." Only less than 5% of the population in Mali can have stable electricity, and the electrification rate in rural areas is as low as 20%. At night, many children can only do their homework by candlelight, and hospitals sometimes cannot operate normally due to power shortages. Konte realized that solar energy could be one of the key elements to change the lives of African people. In 2022, after graduating with a Ph.D., Konte did not choose to return to his home country for employment, but instead went to Guangzhou and established a technology transfer company, hoping to introduce China's clean energy technology to Africa. However, the road to entrepreneurship was not smooth - policy coordination, fundraising, market promotion, each step was full of challenges. Two years ago, he walked into the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base in Hunan Xiangjiang New Area for the first time, and the atmosphere here impressed him. "This place not only provides office space, but also connects with Chinese companies, applies for policy support, and even helps foreign entrepreneurs solve the problem of their children's education!" In just a few months, he decided to move his company and family from Guangzhou to Changsha. The China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base provided him with an expert apartment, assisted in business registration, and even helped his children contact an international school. With no worries, Konte began to push forward his "African Solar Plan." With the help of the base, he visited more than 10 new energy companies in Changsha and eventually reached a cooperation agreement with a solar technology company in Hunan. "Our goal is not only to sell products, but to empower Africans with technology for sustainable development," Konte said. Today, he frequently travels between China and Mali, coordinating with the Chinese supply chain while negotiating with local governments and chambers of commerce on landing matters. In addition to cooperation in new energy, he has also introduced sesame from his hometown to the Chinese market. Konte's story is a microcosm of the struggles of many African youth in China. Leading the way for these African youth to start their businesses in Hunan is the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base created by the Hunan Xiangjiang New Area. Currently, the base has established contacts with over 200 government agencies, chambers of commerce, and companies from more than 50 African countries, supporting the incubation and cultivation of many African youth entrepreneurship projects. The base team follows up on projects through online and offline research, face-to-face meetings with key project companies, and covers various fields such as economy and trade, agriculture, culture, education, energy, and healthcare; hosting nearly 80 online and offline events related to China-Africa cooperation, including the China (Changsha)-Nigeria Investment and Trade Promotion Conference, with an average of cross-border "business matchmaking meetings" every week. As the results of China-Africa youth innovation and entrepreneurship gradually emerge, the base is attracting more and more attention, becoming a "super hub" for resource connection. "A lot of African agricultural products are very attractive in China, with a sense of mystery, so smooth channels are crucial," said Lei Ting, head of the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base. In the tide of China-Africa cooperation, such "bridges" are becoming increasingly important. During the 2022 "Double 11" period, the base, together with the United Nations International Trade Center and Alibaba Group, launched the "Digital Village" project plan, importing a batch of high-quality coffee beans from countries such as Rwanda and Ethiopia in Africa, roasting them domestically, and then making them into drip coffee. In just two minutes in the live broadcast room, nearly 20,000 boxes of this coffee were sold, making the farmers in the country of origin ecstatic. There is a medical equipment manufacturing company in Hunan Xiangjiang New Area that mainly produces oxygen equipment for hospitals, which has attracted the interest of customers in Algeria. However, due to the long distance between the two parties and the lack of face-to-face meetings, there was some hesitation when it came to discussing orders. In 2023, the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base invited a counselor from the Algerian Embassy to visit Hunan and inspect this company. In the presence of the counselor, the company's head connected via video with a buyer from Algeria, confirming the reliability of the cooperation and facilitating the project. Today, the office of young entrepreneurs from Algeria in the China-Africa Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Base is thriving. It is reported that there are more than 20 young people from 8 countries currently stationed at the base, a considerable number of whom started their businesses after studying in China, as well as some young people recommended by various African embassies and some young people from Africa who have already had economic and trade exchanges with China. After several years of cooperation, the base has successfully landed more than 30 projects. "These (African youth) come to China with dreams, and then bring China's technology, experience, and friendship back to Africa. And Changsha, with its open policies and inclusive environment, has become their first choice," Lei Ting said.

title_en: "Three fees in one" are collected with water in Zunyi City to improve the efficiency of garbage disposal fee collection.
body_en: Report (Correspondents Lu Lihua, Zhang Ji, Xiao Jun) "Before, we had to go to the window to pay the garbage disposal fee, now it is deducted together with the water bill, which is much more convenient." On June 12, Zunyi citizen Ms. Wang opened her phone and found that in addition to the water and sewage treatment fees, there was also a urban garbage disposal fee when she paid her water bill through the "Guizhou Taxation" WeChat public account. Ms. Wang is very satisfied with this convenient payment method. In the past, the urban household garbage disposal fee was collected by multiple departments, with inconsistent standards, making collection difficult and costly. To solve this problem, in January 2024, under the guidance of the Guizhou Provincial Taxation Bureau of the State Administration of Taxation, the Zunyi Taxation Bureau proposed the "collected with water" model - the garbage disposal fee is collected by the water supply enterprise, achieving the combined collection of "water fee + sewage treatment fee + garbage disposal fee". To ensure the smooth implementation of the combined collection of the three fees, the tax department of Zunyi City leveraged its own advantages, provided support in setting the fee standards and data provision, and after extensive consultation and holding public hearings, issued new standards for the urban household garbage disposal fee in the central urban area of Zunyi City. At the same time, the tax department signed a commission collection agreement with the water supply company, clarified the requirements related to the collection process, and carried out policy publicity and interpretation through government websites, news media, community outreach, etc., to ensure that payers understand the policy and know how to operate. title_en: Guangzhou will strengthen policy guidance and capital support in key areas such as AI.
body_en: Guangzhou will strengthen financial support for market entities in the fields of artificial intelligence and low-altitude economy. On June 17, Guangzhou held a press conference for the 11th Guangzhou International Investment Conference. The 11th Guangzhou International Investment Conference will be held from June 26 to 27. As of June 16, more than 800 guests have registered to attend, including senior executives from Fortune 500 companies, central enterprises, and the top 500 Chinese companies, as well as representatives from enterprises in new productive sectors such as artificial intelligence, low-altitude economy, new energy storage, biomedicine, high-end equipment, and clean technology. Currently, Guangzhou is focusing on building a "12218" modern industrial system, including 15 strategic industrial clusters, 6 future industries, and 8 modern service industries, and has established 5 key industrial development offices. Yang Xiaoyan, Deputy Director of the Development and Reform Commission of Guangzhou, stated at the meeting that Guangzhou will introduce a "package" of policies in the field of artificial intelligence and low-altitude economy. In terms of artificial intelligence, Guangzhou will introduce special policies for the development of the artificial intelligence industry, innovatively launch "four vouchers linkage" including computing power vouchers, data vouchers, scenario vouchers, and model vouchers to reduce the research and development operating costs of market entities. At the same time, Guangzhou will establish an artificial intelligence industry investment fund, focusing on algorithm research and development, computing power infrastructure, industry applications, and providing full-cycle financing support to market entities through "angel investment + VC follow-up + Pre-IPO relay". In the low-altitude economy sector, the focus will be on building a "full-cycle service" ecosystem. By constructing a low-altitude industry fund matrix, mobilizing social capital to focus on research and development, manufacturing, and operational services, enterprises will be provided with a full chain of financial support including equity financing, debt financing, and listing incubation. Additionally, Guangzhou will accelerate the issuance and implementation of the "Measures for Promoting the High-Quality Development of the Low-Altitude Economy" to strengthen policy support in areas such as research and development, manufacturing, and airworthiness certification. In terms of infrastructure construction, efforts will be made to accelerate the construction of "1+5+100" low-altitude take-off and landing sites and new infrastructure projects such as low-altitude intelligent networking. Reporters learned that Guangzhou is strengthening policy guidance for key industries, formulating and implementing a batch of special policies for intelligent connected new energy vehicles, specialty semiconductor processes, biomedicine, and other industries. The city is also enhancing carrier support, nurturing and constructing the first batch of 10 characteristic benchmark industrial parks, and is preparing to launch the second batch of parks soon. Furthermore, capital support is being strengthened through the establishment of industrial development funds and the promotion of activities such as the "Gathering Chain in Guangzhou, Setting Sail in the Bay Area" strategic industrial cluster supply and demand docking, and the "One Month, One Chain" investment and financing service for specialized and innovative enterprises. Wang Yuyin, Deputy Director of the Industrial and Information Technology Bureau of Guangzhou, stated that from January to April this year, industrial investment in Guangzhou increased by 15% year-on-year. In terms of attracting leading enterprises and major projects, advanced manufacturing projects such as TCL Huaxing T9, Zengxin, Rongjie Lithium Battery, Gaojing Solar, and Maisheng Medical have been successively constructed and put into operation. In addition, Guangzhou is strengthening the attraction of industrial chains. In recent years, efforts have been made to stabilize, supplement, and strengthen the automotive industry chain, attracting a number of core automotive component companies such as Continental Electronics and Beixin LiDAR. Since 2024, 64 new projects have been connected to the automotive industry chain, with 40 signed contracts and an expected total investment exceeding 18 billion yuan, driving the establishment of the "Huawang Automobile" project in cooperation with Guangzhou Automobile Group and Huawei in Nansha. By relying on leading enterprises such as Guangzhou Pharmaceutical, Lejin, and Yuexin, a group of upstream and downstream enterprises have been gathered, focusing on local high-quality medical resources, attracting a group of high-quality enterprises such as Aoluxin and Dongze Medical to settle in, and building a good ecosystem of close cooperation between upstream and downstream enterprises and the development of large, medium, and small enterprises. From January to April this year, Guangzhou added more than 300 industrial projects with a total planned investment exceeding 76 billion yuan. According to Han Zhenxiang, Deputy Director of the Guangzhou Municipal Bureau of Commerce, from January to April this year, Guangzhou introduced 625 new industrial investment projects with a total expected investment of 161.5 billion yuan, including 70 projects with investments or revenues exceeding 1 billion yuan. The total investment in manufacturing projects in the city accounts for over 50%. The total investment in domestic projects in the city ranks first in the province. There were 2,664 newly established foreign-funded enterprises, an increase of 14.9%, with actual foreign investment of 11.54 billion yuan, showing growth in both the number of new foreign-funded enterprises and the actual use of foreign investment. Strategic cooperation agreements have been reached with large enterprises such as the Investment Promotion Bureau Group, Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China, and Tencent, and investment projects from companies such as Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Pengrui Li, Ant Group, Hikvision, and Douyin have been successively implemented. In the first half of the year, Ant Group's "Dual Centers" and Douyin's South China Innovation Base settled in Haizhu District, Guangzhou, which has already attracted numerous platform companies. Yang Xiao, Deputy District Mayor of the district, mentioned that in addition to Ant's "Dual Centers" and Douyin South China, this year the district also landed a batch of new projects for the first time, including Kuaishou E-commerce, Hellobike Smart Driving, and Shanghai Douyin E-commerce. Starting in 2021, Haizhu District took the lead in establishing the country's first artificial intelligence large-scale model application demonstration zone, with 17 models approved, covering education, transportation, language, and other fields, ranking first in the province. At the same time, Haizhu District has implemented an industrial ecological prosperity plan, nurturing 65 backbone enterprises in the new generation information technology industry with a value of over 100 million yuan, forming a situation of "leading the head, supporting the backbone, and prospering the small and medium-sized enterprises". Chen Chao, Secretary-General of the Guangzhou Development Zone Management Committee, stated that the Guangzhou Development Zone is improving the investment and financing system of "state-owned enterprise investment + industrial fund guidance + social capital", establishing a 5 billion yuan science and technology innovation mother fund. A scene "opportunity list" has been established, relying on the annual construction volume of over 200 billion in the entire region to accelerate the creation of industrial application scenarios for artificial intelligence, unmanned driving, hydrogen energy storage, low-altitude economy, and other industries. From January to May, the Guangzhou Development Zone and Huangpu District signed 170 new high-quality projects; the total investment under agreement reached 93.3 billion yuan, an increase of 13%. This includes the hundred-billion-yuan project of the Tibet-Guangdong DC, as well as six billion-yuan projects such as GAC Flying Car. Manufacturing projects such as the headquarters base of Siyuan Shares and the high-performance composite material base of Jinfahao have successively started construction. The actual utilization of foreign capital in the district was 869 million US dollars, accounting for 47% of the total in Guangzhou. The number of newly registered business entities exceeded 35,700, a significant increase of 73.9%, with the total number of business entities exceeding 300,000 for the first time.

title_en: LC: 800G optical module drives market recovery in Q2 2025.
body_en: Official WeChat Official Weibo Recently, LightCounting released the "June 2025 Quarterly Update Report on the Optical Communication Market." The report predicts that although the market performance was flat in the first quarter, optical module sales in the second quarter will increase by 10% compared to the previous quarter, with the main growth coming from 800G Ethernet optical modules (as shown in the chart). The 1.6T optical modules, not reflected in the chart, will also be shipped for the first time, contributing a small amount of revenue to the market. As Amazon and Meta shift to higher-speed modules, sales of 400G Ethernet modules will decline. Sales of 400G and 800G active optical cables (AOC) also remain strong. In addition, DWDM, FTTx, and wireless front-haul (WFH) optical modules rebounded after a seasonally slow first quarter, driving market growth in the second quarter. However, the telecom market is not expected to significantly recover. In the first quarter of 2025, the top 15 global telecom service providers (TSPs) saw flat revenue, but capital expenditures decreased by 5% year-on-year. The three major Chinese operators - China Mobile, China Telecom, and China Unicom - have all announced cuts in capital spending this year, with the total expenditure of the three companies in 2025 amounting to $39.8 billion, a 10% decrease from 2024. Leading operators in revenue growth in the first quarter of 2025 include Softbank (7% year-on-year growth), Deutsche Telekom (3% growth), and China Unicom (3% growth). In contrast, Telecom Italia saw a 19% year-on-year revenue decline, while Telefonica saw a 12% decline, mainly due to selling businesses to focus on core assets. M&A activity is becoming increasingly active, with U.S. telecom operators acquiring fiber assets, while European operators are optimizing their layouts by divesting non-core businesses. In terms of technology giants, Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle all significantly increased their spending in the first quarter of 2025 compared to the same period last year. Among them, Oracle's spending soared by 233% year-on-year, but it is the smallest in scale among the top five companies - with spending of less than $11 billion for the full year of 2024, while Meta and Amazon were $39 billion and $83 billion respectively. Oracle's first-quarter spending reached $5.6 billion, exceeding 50% of its full-year spending in 2024. Alibaba's first-quarter revenue was $32.5 billion, a 5% year-on-year increase, but a 17% decrease from the previous quarter. The company announced that it will invest over 380 billion yuan (approximately $53 billion) in AI infrastructure construction over the next three years. Baidu's revenue was $4.5 billion, a 3% year-on-year increase, but a 5% decrease from the previous quarter, with spending of $398 million, a 41% year-on-year increase and a 23% quarter-on-quarter increase. Tencent's revenue was $24.7 billion, a 12% year-on-year increase, a 3% quarter-on-quarter increase, with spending of $3.7 billion, an 89% year-on-year increase, but a 36% quarter-on-quarter decrease.

title_en: Notice on holding the 2024 Academic Annual Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association (Second Round)
body_en: Relevant units: Pharmaceutical excipients are an important foundation in China's pharmaceutical industry, and are one of the key factors determining the quality of generic drugs and the high-quality development of innovative formulations. The security of the supply chain of pharmaceutical excipients used in high-end formulations in China urgently requires the strengthening of technical innovation and industrial support for domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. At the same time, ensuring the quality of clinical medication, reducing drug costs, and alleviating the pressure on medical insurance to a large extent also depend on the improvement of the quality of domestically produced pharmaceutical excipients. In line with the principle of "promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry," the "2024 Annual Academic Conference of the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association," organized by the Pharmaceutical Excipients Professional Committee of the Chinese Pharmaceutical Association, is scheduled to be held in Hefei, Anhui Province from November 8th to 10th, 2024. This academic conference will feature conference reports in the fields of materials science related to pharmaceutical excipients, innovative drugs, and innovative formulations, analyzing the development difficulties and innovations of pharmaceutical excipients; inviting authoritative experts to deeply discuss the in vivo processes of pharmaceutical excipients and drug delivery carriers, as well as the improvement and innovation of excipient quality. The conference will set up expert venues and young scholar sub-venues on the themes of "Pharmaceutical Excipients, Packaging Materials, and Drug Delivery Devices," "New Materials, New Carriers, and Innovative Formulations," and "Pharmaceutical Excipients and Innovative Drugs," promoting the wide participation of enterprises, academia, and young scholars to jointly focus on the technological innovation and industrial research and development of pharmaceutical excipients. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows: 1. Conference theme: Promoting technological innovation in pharmaceutical excipients and enhancing the new productive forces of the pharmaceutical industry. 2. Time and place: November 8th Registration location: New Ji Hotel, Hefei (2766 Wenzhong Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province) The main venue and sub-venues on November 9-10 will be held at the Shaoquanhu Campus of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine in Hefei, Anhui Province (350 Longzihu Road, Yaohai District, Hefei City, Anhui Province). 3. Conference arrangements: The conference will adopt a format of reports at the main venue and sub-venues. The conference will invite well-known experts and scholars from domestic universities, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, regulatory agencies, etc., to give keynote speeches and special lectures. Please refer to Annex 1 for the detailed schedule. 4. Participants: Researchers, managers, and graduate students engaged in research and development related to pharmaceutical excipients, pharmaceutical packaging materials, drug delivery devices, formulation quality control, formulation equipment, pharmaceutical services, etc., from universities, research institutes, pharmaceutical companies, research and development units, medical institutions, drug regulatory agencies, and other related institutions. 5. Call for papers: 1. Requirements for submission of papers: Chinese and English abstracts and paper format. Papers that have not been published in publicly distributed journals or presented at national academic conferences are the responsibility of the authors; please ensure clear expression and accurate data. We welcome active submissions from researchers in the pharmaceutical field. 2. Paper submission method: Please submit the abstract of the paper to the conference website https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn before October 20, 2024, click on the "Online Paper Submission" button on the right, and follow the process to upload your paper abstract. After successful upload, you will receive an automatic email confirmation of the online submission. After the paper is reviewed by experts, the organizing committee will select several papers for further communication or publication in the "Drug Analysis" journal. 3. Poster submission method and time: Same as the paper. The conference welcomes poster submissions, which should be in A1 standard size. 6. Registration: (1) Registration method: 1. Please log in to the conference website link https://yyfl2024.sciconf.cn and click on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button to register; 2. Or scan (or long-press to recognize) the QR code below with your mobile phone, click on the "Individual Representative Registration" or "Group Representative Registration" button to fill in the registration information and submit. (2) Registration deadline: The registration deadline is October 30, 2024. (3) Notes on registration: 1. To ensure that participants receive registration confirmation, invoices, etc., please fill in accurate and true email addresses, mobile phone numbers, and other information; 2. This registration website is only for registration, and the payment channel is not yet open; 3. Registered individuals can log in to the personal center of the conference website to check and modify their registration information; 4. Participants who do not submit papers can also attend the conference. 7. Conference fees: (1) Conference registration fee: 1. Registration fee standard: The registration fee includes conference materials and lunch during the conference. 2. Payment methods: (1) Telegraphic transfer: After registering for the conference, participants should pay the registration fee by bank transfer, supporting both corporate and personal transfers to the following account: Payee: Chinese Pharmaceutical Association Bank: Bank of China Head Office Account number: 778350009320 It is recommended to use online banking for personal transfers, or you can also use Alipay transfer (to a bank card, with the name field filled in as "Chinese Pharmaceutical Association"). Please indicate "Pharmaceutical Excipients + Participant's Name + Unit Abbreviation" in the remittance note. After successful payment, please upload the remittance voucher to the conference website in a timely manner for the secretariat to confirm the payment information and issue an invoice; (2) On-site payment: You can pay the registration fee by mobile online banking, or by scanning the payment QR code on-site (Alipay, WeChat) for transfer; there is no POS machine on-site, and payment methods such as card swiping and UnionPay QuickPass are not supported. (2) Invoice matters: 1. This conference can provide a VAT ordinary invoice for "conference registration fees" (electronic invoice). After uploading the personal remittance voucher (photo, screenshot, etc., of the complete order) to the conference system, please accurately fill in the invoice information in the billing instructions section of your personal information. 2. In cases where the name of the remitter does not match the participant's name, one unit remits for multiple attending representatives, or the unit requests separate invoices, please send detailed explanations by email to the secretariat at z38@cpa.org.cn, providing the remitter's name, participant's name, work unit, contact information, detailed information for issuing the invoice, number of invoices and amounts, as well as the person receiving the invoice and the mailing address. 3. Representatives who are unable to attend the conference due to special reasons after remittance can apply for a full refund of the registration fee by sending an email to the secretariat. The refund work will be handled uniformly after the conference, and the refund will be returned along the original payment path. For accurate refunds, please indicate the full name and account information (account number, bank) of the original remitter in the refund application email. 8. Other matters: Accommodation and transportation expenses for attending representatives are self-funded. Please refer to Annex 2 for hotel booking and transportation information. 9. title_en: Zhejiang Yongkang helps foreign trade enterprises reduce costs and burdens.
body_en: In response to the changing global trade market environment this year, the Market Supervision Bureau of Yongkang City, Zhejiang Province, has recently focused on the pain points of foreign trade enterprises, opened up new paths for internal trade, and fully supported enterprises in reducing burdens, increasing efficiency, stabilizing orders, and expanding markets. Proactively building an e-commerce platform for external sales to internal sales, expanding the sales channels for foreign trade enterprises. The bureau relies on the JD platform's billion-yuan special procurement plan to build the "Hardware Foreign Trade Excellent Products for Internal Sales" platform, and has successively held events such as the Tmall Home Yongkang Industrial Belt Selection Conference and the Taobao Flash Sale Special, promoting the launch of a special exhibition area for "Source Factory Excellent Products · Export Quality" on the 1688 platform. Actively constructing a cross-border testing and certification system to facilitate the circulation between domestic and foreign markets. The bureau utilizes the National Hardware Tools and Category Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Center and Quality Station to open a "CCC Certification Testing" green channel for electric tools, and introduces convenient measures such as "institutional errands" and "shared laboratories" to simplify the certification process for products transitioning from export to internal sales, saving operating costs for foreign trade enterprises. Strengthening intellectual property protection to stimulate the transformation momentum of enterprises. The bureau relies on Zhejiang's first Hardware Industry Intellectual Property Fast Maintenance Center to develop a "fast pre-examination" channel for appearance patents, providing one-on-one filing guidance for key foreign trade enterprises to accelerate the transformation of their innovative achievements. Since the beginning of this year, it has helped 67 key foreign trade enterprises to handle patent fast pre-examination filings, with the average authorization time compressed to 5 working days, a 90% reduction compared to the conventional process.

title_en: Zhejiang Consumer Protection Commission interviewed multiple platforms.
body_en: Hangzhou News (Reporter Shi Benyun) In response to the issue of a high piracy rate of 35.8% in platform online book purchases discovered in the previous investigation (see "Some Platform Self-operated Stores Actually Selling Pirated Children's Books" on page 1 of China Consumer News on June 4), the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee held a meeting on June 13 to report the relevant information of the piracy book consumption investigation. Representatives from platforms such as Douyin, JD.com, Taobao, Tmall, Pinduoduo, and WeChat Video attended the meeting and responded to the issues raised in the report. On the eve of this year's Children's Day, the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee, in collaboration with the Zhejiang Children's Publishing House, conducted a special investigation on pirated books, involving multiple platforms such as Douyin, JD.com, Taobao, Tmall, Pinduoduo, and WeChat Video. A total of 478 children's literary books published by the Zhejiang Children's Publishing House were purchased, and after verification by the publishing house, 171 pirated books were found, resulting in a piracy rate of 35.8%. The relevant person in charge of the Zhejiang Children's Publishing House revealed the harm of pirated books to the entire industry at the meeting, calling on major platforms to increase penalties for selling pirated works, establish stricter copyright protection mechanisms, strengthen piracy complaint handling, and curb the circulation of pirated books from the source. The relevant person in charge of the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee proposed three opinions on strengthening the governance of pirated books on platforms: first, to raise awareness. Pirated books seriously disrupt the order of the publishing market and threaten the physical and mental health of minors. Platforms should enhance their awareness, take proactive measures to govern, shift from post-punishment to preventive measures in piracy governance, truly prioritize consumer rights protection, and have a "zero tolerance" policy towards pirated books. Second, to improve platform rules. Platforms should carefully review relevant laws and regulations such as the E-commerce Law, examine whether current platform rules meet regulatory requirements and governance needs, and whether there is a gap with the expectations of the people. They should further refine and improve regulations related to book review, violation handling, etc., and strengthen the responsibility of the platform. Third, to explore long-term mechanisms. It is suggested that relevant platforms work together with publishing houses to explore long-term governance mechanisms for pirated books, establish a "green channel" with publishing houses, promptly respond to and effectively handle complaints related to pirated books, strengthen monitoring and governance of abnormal behaviors such as low-price sales and shell operations, and form a joint force to combat pirated books. Next, the Zhejiang Consumer Rights Protection Committee will continue to monitor the governance of pirated books on platforms and conduct "look-backs" as needed, striving to create a safe and trustworthy online book purchasing environment for consumers. At the same time, it will further unite the forces of publishing houses, platforms, and other parties to promote collaborative governance of pirated books, and build a solid copyright protection barrier to promote the high-quality development of the cultural industry.
