title_en: The situation in the Middle East is deteriorating, but the overall market remains stable.
body_en: Wei Jun The situation in the Middle East has deteriorated, with Asian stock markets generally falling on Tuesday. The Hong Kong stock market rose initially and then fell, opening high in the morning and rising to 24,131 points, an increase of about 71 points. It later dropped to 23,880 points before the close, a decrease of 188 points, closing at 23,980 points, down 80 points or 0.34% for the day, with a reduced turnover of 202.144 billion yuan. However, the Hang Seng Index is still above the 20-day moving average of 23,723 points, and the consolidation at high levels led by institutional investors remains unchanged. Except for the Utilities Index, all sector indices of the Hang Seng Index softened. The recently strong Financials Index also fell by 0.7%, facing greater pressure. In terms of active stocks, the recently strong stock, Meituan (9992), showed a significant pullback, falling by 6% for the day with a turnover of 6.238 billion yuan; Alibaba (9988) rose by 1.68%, performing well with a turnover of 6.875 billion yuan. There was a net inflow of 6.302 billion yuan from Northbound funds, marking the 15th consecutive day of net inflows. China Construction Bank (0939) continued to see a net inflow of 1.122 billion yuan, while Alibaba saw a net inflow of 599 million yuan. In the comprehensive enterprise sector, CITIC (0267), Beijing Enterprises (0392), and Shanghai Industrial (0363) performed well against the market trend, rising by about 1.4% to 1.6%, as Northbound funds continue to favor the value rebound of central and state-owned enterprises. Data shows that Hong Kong's IPO fundraising of 108.7 billion Hong Kong dollars in the first half of the year topped the global rankings, and the market anticipates a continued strong trend in the second half of the year. Sany Heavy Industry (600031.SH), which submitted an application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on May 22, is expected to boost demand from international investors in the engineering machinery sector. Its subsidiary, Sany International (0631), has shown strong performance in recent weeks and can be accumulated in stages during market adjustments. Sany Heavy Industry to be listed in Hong Kong Sany Heavy Industry is a private enterprise (with a market value of 152.8 billion yuan in A-shares as of yesterday's closing), holding a 66.36% stake in Sany International (with a market value of 22 billion yuan as of yesterday's closing). Sany Heavy Industry is the third largest globally and the largest in China in the engineering machinery sector, focusing on the research, development, manufacturing, and sales of machinery products such as excavators, concrete machinery, cranes, piling machinery, and road machinery. Since the beginning of the year, the export of engineering machinery has been in a growth period, with emerging economies in the Middle East, Central Asia, and Latin America vigorously improving infrastructure. Additionally, the demand for infrastructure repair due to geopolitical military conflicts is favorable for the growth of engineering machinery orders. Sany International recently announced that as of the end of March this year, the unaudited attributable profit to the owners of the parent company increased by 23.2% year-on-year to 635 million yuan (RMB, the same below). Revenue increased by 14.6% year-on-year to 5.876 billion yuan. The group stated that the comprehensive implementation of globalization, digitalization, and low-carbon strategies has significantly increased the revenue of the group's port machinery, oil and gas equipment, silicon energy products, and overseas mining truck revenue. In addition, the acquisition of the lithium energy business completed in July last year has brought new sources of income. The group pointed out that the comprehensive implementation of digital operations, the implementation of measures to improve quality and efficiency, reduce costs, and control expenses, have increased the gross profit margin of excavators, port machinery, oil and gas equipment, and silicon energy products. Sany International retraces, suitable for accumulation in stages Sany International closed at 6.81 Hong Kong dollars yesterday, down by 1 cent, with a turnover of 80.2 million yuan. The stock has risen from the 5 yuan level to a recent high of 7.08 yuan in the past two months, a cumulative increase of over 40%. The current price-earnings ratio is 18.6 times, the forecasted price-earnings ratio is 9 times, the dividend yield is 4.2%, the price-to-book ratio is 1.69 times, and the valuation is not considered expensive. It is suitable for accumulation during retracements, with a target price of 7.50 yuan. The opinions expressed in this article are those of the author and do not represent the position of the newspaper.

title_en: The province's campaign to protect minors has been launched.
body_en: This newspaper, Taizhou, June 17th (Reporter Chen Jiuren) On the 17th, the province-wide publicity month for the protection of minors and the promotion of child-friendly activities, "Protecting Minors in Zhejiang and Warming Children's Hearts," was launched in Taizhou. This is the first publicity month event after the implementation of the "Zhejiang Province Regulations on the Protection of Minors," aiming to jointly create a good social environment conducive to the healthy growth of minors. At the event, the top ten "small and warm" public welfare projects for children, such as the Alibaba Youth Cloud Assistance Program and the "Hello Taizhou" mobile children care project, were announced. A cooperation agreement was signed for the construction of a collaborative community for psychological health services for families, schools, communities, and medical institutions under the theme of "Warming Children's Hearts." The Children's Observation Team also issued a proposal for the construction of child-friendly cities. The protection of minors is a systematic project. In order to carry out the publicity and implementation of the regulations, the provincial government's Women and Children's Work Committee has taken the lead in promoting legal publicity through activities such as entering villages (communities), households, schools, hospitals, enterprises, and key locations, forming a working pattern led by the government, with the participation of various groups and the entire society. For five consecutive years, Taizhou has included projects for caring for the growth of young people in the city government's livelihood projects, taking the lead in implementing a system for preventing harm to minors in the province, and issuing the country's first white paper on mandatory parenting education. With the construction of a national child-friendly city as the link, a full-chain, full-cycle, and full-coverage protection scene for minors is being created.

title_en: Bubble Mart AB side: Explosive sales and hidden capital flows.
body_en: Recently, Pop Mart has been taking frequent actions, and the commercialization of IP is accelerating comprehensively. On June 10th, a first-generation collectible mint LABUBU was sold for a high price of 1.08 million yuan at the Yongle 2025 Spring Auction, immediately sparking a market frenzy. From the proliferation of counterfeit goods, scalpers rushing to buy, to the sell-out of the new store in Hangzhou, LABUBU's popularity continues to rise. Against this background, Pop Mart is rapidly advancing its diversification strategy. On June 13th, Pop Mart's independent jewelry brand POPOP opened its first store in the luxury gathering Shanghai Grand Gateway Plaza. On June 14th, POPOP's first store in Beijing officially opened at the China World Trade Center. "We have always hoped to expand more possibilities through different categories, and jewelry is a very important category that we have been trying." Wang Ning, Chairman and CEO of Pop Mart International Group, said at the opening ceremony of POPOP's first store in Shanghai. It is not difficult to see that Pop Mart is trying to explore more diverse IP monetization. On June 16th, Uniqlo announced the launch of a new collaborative series featuring Pop Mart's THE MONSTERS IP as the theme. "The popularity of LABUBU is not only due to luck but also to Pop Mart's operational strategy. From the release of the March financial report to subsequent new product launches, flash events, and a series of actions, there is coherence," said Guo Yulian, General Manager of Mighty Jaxx China, in an interview with 21st Century Business Herald. However, behind the frenzy of Pop Mart, the capital market presents a different picture. Since 2024, major shareholders including founder Wang Ning have started intensive reductions, especially in May this year when Fengqiao Capital cleared its entire pre-listing holdings, triggering a strong market reaction. This capital move contrasts sharply with the company's high-profile market performance. This contrast has led to renewed doubts in the market about Pop Mart's continued innovation capabilities: How long can the heat of LABUBU be sustained? Can the company replicate the next explosive IP? These questions that have existed since the Molly era have been answered by Wang Ning multiple times. However, the market continues to question and inquire. On June 17th, Pop Mart's stock price fell all the way, closing down 6.04% on the Hong Kong stock market, with a market value evaporating by about 22.3 billion Hong Kong dollars (about 20.4 billion yuan). In just one week, Pop Mart continued to dominate social media. On June 10th, the world's only mint LABUBU was sold for 1.08 million yuan at the Shanghai Yongle Spring Auction, while the limited edition brown LABUBU was sold for 820,000 yuan, breaking the record for toy auction prices. On the night of June 12th at 10 o'clock, Pop Mart released a series of new products online on its mini-program and official flagship store. There were queues in many places to buy blind boxes, and videos circulating on social platforms showed disputes over buying Pop Mart blind boxes. On June 15th, the new Pop Mart store in Xixi Tianjie, Hangzhou, opened, and it was reported that due to scalpers "grabbing boxes," the products were sold out within two hours, and the store had to close urgently. However, the issue of scalpers has always been criticized by the public, and behind this is the high premium in the second-hand market. For example, the LABUBU and VANS collaboration released in 2024 for 599 yuan has been speculated to 31,999 yuan in the second-hand market, with a premium of over 52 times. Not only is there a frenzy of buying in the domestic market, but the overseas market is also very lively. The offline Pop Mart store in South Korea also caused disputes due to crowded buyers queuing. In May of this year, due to high demand, there was even a "fight" incident at the Westfield Stratford City shopping center in London, UK. title_en: 21st Dialogue | HKEX CEO Charles Li: "Solving hand in hand", Chinese concept stocks returning to Hong Kong "definitely acceptable"
body_en: Since the reform of the listing system by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018, 33 Chinese concept stocks have listed in Hong Kong, accounting for over 70% of the total market capitalization of all Chinese concept stocks listed in the United States. As 2025 approaches, the Hong Kong IPO market continues to rebound. Against the backdrop of tense Sino-US geopolitical relations, an increasing number of Chinese concept stocks are considering listing in Hong Kong. Concurrently, whether the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will relax the market capitalization threshold and dual-class share structure restrictions for Chinese concept stocks listing in Hong Kong has become a focal point of market attention. Market analysis indicates that among the 27 Chinese concept stocks listed in the US with market capitalizations exceeding US$1 billion, 22 companies have equity structures that do not comply with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's regulations. In April, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po revealed that he had instructed the Securities and Futures Commission and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to be prepared, stating that if Chinese concept stocks listed overseas wish to return, Hong Kong must be made their preferred listing destination. "Our consistent attitude is that we want high-quality companies to list in Hong Kong. Every company has its uniqueness, and if they need some flexibility to overcome certain issues, we will work hand-in-hand with them to resolve them," said Hong Kong Stock Exchange CEO Bonnie Chan Yick-ting in an exclusive interview with a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald. She admitted that to better serve the real economy with finance, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange regularly reviews its listing rules. "As long as there is market demand, we must study it. This is the spirit of 'people, goods, and venue' that we advocate." Bonnie Chan Yick-ting. File photo The return of an increasing number of Chinese "giants" to list in Hong Kong has undoubtedly injected new vitality into Hong Kong's capital market. However, some industry insiders are concerned about whether these large-scale enterprises will face issues such as insufficient trading activity and suppressed stock prices after returning to Hong Kong, thereby affecting the overall market liquidity. In response, Bonnie Chan Yick-ting firmly stated, "Hong Kong is an open market, and there is no need to question whether we can handle it. The answer is 'we can definitely handle it.' As long as the companies are outstanding enough, and as long as they are favored by investors, funds will flow in continuously from all directions." According to statistics, in the first five months of this year, 27 Hong Kong stocks were listed through IPOs, raising a total of HK$77.346 billion, nearing last year's full-year level. Bonnie Chan Yick-ting stated that the liquidity in Hong Kong's new stock market is very ample. Over the past decade, cumulative financing has exceeded US$300 billion (approximately HK$2.35 trillion), ranking first globally. In the first five months of 2025, the average daily trading volume in the Hong Kong securities market was HK$242.3 billion, more than double that of HK$110.2 billion in the same period last year. This year, the Hong Kong market has successfully welcomed the listing of several large new stocks. These companies have shown high trading activity after listing, dispelling market concerns about insufficient liquidity for "giant" enterprises. At the same time, the performance of Hong Kong's refinancing market has also been impressive. As of June 6, 2025, the cumulative refinancing volume this year has reached US$25.9 billion (approximately HK$203.3 billion), more than double the IPO fundraising amount in Hong Kong during the same period. To continuously enhance the attractiveness and competitiveness of the Hong Kong market and thus improve overall liquidity, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has launched a series of innovative initiatives in recent years. Among them, the "FINI" (Fast Interface for New Issuance) system launched in 2023 is a key component. This system aims to shorten the settlement cycle for new shares, significantly reducing it from the traditional "T+5" to "T+2." The shortening of the settlement cycle means an increase in capital turnover efficiency, which can effectively reduce market risk and attract more international investors to participate in new stock subscriptions, thereby further enhancing the liquidity of the new stock market. Since the beginning of this year, Hong Kong stock liquidity has significantly improved, leading to a substantial narrowing of the A-H share price gap. This has also prompted leading A-share companies to more actively consider listing in Hong Kong. The recent listing of CATL, a leading new energy company in mainland China, in Hong Kong has pushed this trend to a climax, setting the record for the largest IPO financing globally this year. "For companies with overseas expansion plans, listing in Hong Kong not only provides a financing platform but also facilitates their overseas mergers and acquisitions, equity incentives, and other activities. By listing in Hong Kong, companies can use Hong Kong stocks as consideration for overseas acquisitions, thus avoiding the pressure of relying solely on cash payments," said Bonnie Chan Yick-ting. "If a company is listed simultaneously in the A-share and Hong Kong markets, the trading activity in the Hong Kong market will also drive the trading volume in the A-share market, achieving a virtuous cycle." In 2024, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) introduced five capital market cooperation measures with Hong Kong and has continued to optimize the filing process for companies listing overseas. These policies provide a more convenient and efficient channel for mainland companies to list in Hong Kong, reducing compliance costs and time for these companies, thereby stimulating more enthusiasm for companies to choose the A+H model. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's own continuously optimized listing mechanism also provides a convenient financing environment for mainland companies. It is reported that last year the Hong Kong Stock Exchange lowered the market capitalization threshold for specialist technology companies and jointly optimized the approval process timetable for new listing applications with the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission. In early May this year, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange officially announced the launch of the "Tech Company Fast Track." According to a report by CICC, since the listing of Midea in Hong Kong in September last year, eight A-share companies have listed in Hong Kong, with IPO financing totaling HK$98.11 billion, including industry leaders like Midea and CATL. According to the CSRC's filing information and listed company disclosures, nearly 50 more A-share companies plan to list in Hong Kong, with 23 having already completed the filing or submitted their materials. On June 10, the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council issued the "Opinions on Deepening the Shenzhen Comprehensive Reform Pilot and Further Deepening Reform and Innovation to Expand Opening-up" (hereinafter referred to as the "Opinions"), which allows companies in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong to list in Shenzhen. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange is expected to welcome "H+A" listed companies. In response, she jokingly said, "The A+H model is not a competitor to A-shares, but a supplement to A-shares. The two can form a virtuous interaction and jointly expand the 'cake' of the capital market. As long as it plays a complementary role, it is a good thing." Since the beginning of the year, with DeepSeek leading the narrative of China's asset revaluation, the Hong Kong stock market has shown a unique performance. With a year-to-date gain of over 20%, Hong Kong stocks have led major global stock markets. Inflows of southbound and international capital into Hong Kong stocks have become the main driving force for the market's upward trend this year. "The emergence of DeepSeek in January this year has allowed the market to re-evaluate Chinese concept stocks," Bonnie Chan Yick-ting said with a smile. "The market is undergoing a 'treasure hunt' process, with investors deeply researching and uncovering high-quality Chinese assets." The stable development of the Chinese economy and the series of economic stimulus policies issued by the state have greatly boosted investor confidence in the Chinese capital market and Chinese assets. At the same time, she believes that the global trend of "de-dollarization" is intensifying, reshaping the capital market. "With the decline in global interest rates and the improvement of market sentiment, funds are seeking new allocation directions. We observe that many international investors are re-evaluating their portfolios, beginning to seek investment targets beyond dollar assets, and considering shifting some funds from more volatile markets to markets with greater growth potential." Bonnie Chan Yick-ting pointed out that global asset reallocation will be a long-term process. Undoubtedly, this will bring new opportunities for non-dollar assets, including Hong Kong stocks. It is worth noting that international capital is also "voting with its feet." Taking CATL's H-share listing as an example, its international placement accounted for 92.5%, including overseas institutions from 15 countries and regions such as the Kuwait Investment Authority (a Middle Eastern sovereign wealth fund), Mirae Asset Global Investments, UBS Asset Management, and Oaktree Capital, with 23 top international cornerstone investors subscribing. "21st Century": Everyone is very concerned about the "Tech Company Fast Track" recently launched by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. What is the overall application situation? Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: "The Tech Company Fast Track" was launched on May 6th, primarily to support the nation's overall strategy of promoting technological innovation. Over the years, from Chapter 18A to Chapter 18C, we have aimed to better serve companies by providing them with tailored listing rules. Some companies, due to their highly innovative nature, may sometimes be uncertain if they can meet our listing requirements. By opening this fast track, we provide them with a channel to engage with us directly at an earlier stage, offering one-on-one pre-listing guidance. This has also opened a confidential submission channel, and the market reaction has been particularly positive. Since its launch, many companies have made inquiries. Our listing department colleagues ensure a preliminary response within five working days, holding meetings with companies. Currently, under Chapters 18A and 18C, over 20 companies have expressed their intention to proceed, which I believe is a good result. "21st Century": Is this reaction in line with or beyond your expectations? Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: Investors are clearly very enthusiastic about technology and tech companies right now. For example, the leading companies that have recently listed saw very high-quality institutional investors place orders during their offerings, including many long-term funds and sovereign funds. Subsequently, funds from the Middle East and Europe have gradually joined. When I recently met with foreign investors, they particularly liked two sectors in China: one is tech companies, and the other is new consumption. New consumption is also very hot right now, with examples like milk tea, Labubu, and the upcoming IPO of Haitain Soy Sauce. In the future, quite a few companies will be coming to the market successively. "21st Century": What were your gains and feelings from your recent trip to the Middle East with the Chief Executive of Hong Kong? Besides opening an office in Riyadh, how will the Hong Kong Stock Exchange further facilitate financial connectivity between Hong Kong and the Middle East in the future? Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: Every time I return from the Middle East, many media outlets ask me the same question – when will Middle Eastern companies list here? I think it will take some time to brew. The Hong Kong Stock Exchange has a longer history and a larger number of listed companies, over two thousand. However, Middle Eastern exchanges are still at the stage of having one to two hundred listed companies, reflecting that some local enterprises still need to go through a development process. Although there are no Middle Eastern companies directly listing yet, both sides have listed each other's assets as underlying assets for ETFs. Hong Kong listed a new ETF in May, with "Sukuk" (Saudi Islamic Bonds) as the underlying asset. The Hong Kong Stock Exchange has listed two ETFs with Saudi assets as the underlying, and correspondingly, the Saudi Stock Exchange has listed two ETFs tracking Hong Kong stocks, with good trading performance. Our work must continue, and we must continue to promote to local companies. However, this time in the Middle East, I spent more time digging for investors. I found that they (Middle Eastern investors) are actually quite knowledgeable. They discussed "Connect" with me and are aware of our latest developments and optimization plans. "21st Century": Is this because the world is facing the same problems? Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: You are absolutely right. Recently, whether it's the Middle East, Europe, or the US, global investors are facing the same task. When people perceive that the US market is highly volatile and unstable, and when the US experienced a "triple kill" of stock, bond, and currency markets for a period, many dollar asset fund managers are re-planning whether to adjust their fund allocations. In this scenario, where can they diversify their investments? Where should they place their assets? This is actually a difficult question. Because the US dollar asset market is a huge entity, their biggest problem is "not being able to fit it all in." Recently, why have our Hong Kong stocks, for example, had such good IPO performance? It is precisely because at the time they were making decisions, we launched these reasonably sized, highly compatible, and excellent IPOs. In addition to the primary market, from the beginning of the year until now, our secondary market rights issues have also been very hot. There have been several rights issues exceeding US$5 billion, such as for Xiaomi and BYD. Recently, China Ping An issued US$1.5 billion in zero-coupon convertible bonds, and all the news I've heard indicates they are sold out. Against this backdrop, with the approval of LME Hong Kong warehouses, what are the future plans for the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in building a commodity ecosystem? Why has this been able to move forward? It's mainly because we are serving offshore users and companies. Why were we so fast? It proves there is indeed demand. Starting with warehouses, we can gradually build an ecosystem. Because warehouses are opened, there will be demand for logistics, trade finance, and transaction-related financial services around them. The next step is to explore products, such as commodity-related financial products, securities products, futures, etc. I think the potential here is quite significant. "21st Century": Do you see any inherent connection between this and the recent hot commodity market? Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: There is a popular saying in mainland China recently called "people, goods, and venue." "People, goods, and venue" can actually be applied to my business. I operate a platform, which is financial infrastructure. So I need "people," meaning "participants." Whether you are a company, an individual, or an investor, you are my "participant." "Goods" are my products. If you go to a supermarket, the shelves must be well-stocked. If we are to get a piece of the pie in the de-dollarization process, we must match and align with what the US has. Finally, "venue" is what we have always talked about: in all transaction processes, whether the procedures, workflows, and platforms can provide users with the ultimate experience is very important. Therefore, we introduced normal trading services during adverse weather last year, and we will soon introduce the minimum price change unit for stock trading, as well as the southbound RMB counter, etc. These are all aimed at providing users with the best experience in our "venue." Bonnie Chan Yick-ting: When we review listing rules, we are essentially following a path of continuous evolution and rule adjustment to keep up with economic changes. I have been in this field for over thirty years, starting in 1993. What do they need? What are their characteristics? What are their funding requirements? Why have we gone from strictly requiring profitable companies to relaxing it to non-profitable enterprises, and then to companies with no revenue? I can create a set of inclusive listing rules, but while being inclusive, we maintain quality. However, their market capitalization was very large, accounting for nearly 70%-80% of the total market capitalization of all Chinese concept stocks listed in the US. If they need flexible handling to overcome their unique problems, we will work hand-in-hand with them to resolve the issues on a case-by-case basis. This wave of Chinese concept stock returns is driven not only by pressure from the US market but also by the inherent attractiveness of the Hong Kong stock market. After Alibaba converted to a dual primary listing and was included in "Stock Connect" in September last year, its stock price and liquidity saw significant improvements. I tell them not to worry. (Their implied meaning is that if you can handle them, I will move my trading venue here.) Because as long as the companies are good enough, and as long as they are transactions and investment targets favored by investors, funds will flow in from all directions at any time. Secondly, in the secondary market, the average daily trading volume in 2023 was HK$100 billion, HK$132 billion last year, and HK$240 billion this year. Since the implementation of measures in September last year, there has been a strong rally. We broke records three times in two weeks, with the highest daily trading volume reaching HK$620 billion. This indicates that we have sufficient depth as a capital market, we can cope, and we have the technical capability to maintain it. "21st Century": The Hong Kong Stock Exchange had very good performance in the first quarter of this year, and its stock price performance was also outstanding. Since the emergence of DeepSeek in January, everyone has begun to re-evaluate Chinese concept stocks. They are truly on a treasure hunt now, so this rally is relatively long-lasting. From January to now, trading volumes have generally remained at historical high levels. In addition to this rally not being policy-driven but fundamentals-driven, there is also the backdrop of de-dollarization. Dollar assets are a behemoth, and this adjustment is ongoing, with considerable incremental flows. As 2025 approaches, the Hong Kong IPO market continues to rebound. Against the backdrop of tense Sino-US geopolitical relations, an increasing number of Chinese concept stocks are considering listing in Hong Kong. Concurrently, whether the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will relax the market capitalization threshold and dual-class share structure restrictions for Chinese concept stocks listing in Hong Kong has become a focal point of market attention. Market analysis indicates that among the 27 Chinese concept stocks listed in the US with market capitalizations exceeding US$1 billion, 22 companies have equity structures that do not comply with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's regulations. In April, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po revealed that he had instructed the Securities and Futures Commission and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to be prepared, stating that if Chinese concept stocks listed overseas wish to return, Hong Kong must be made their preferred listing destination. "Our consistent attitude is that we want high-quality companies to list in Hong Kong. Every company has its uniqueness, and if they need some flexibility to overcome certain issues, we will work hand-in-hand with them to resolve them," said Hong Kong Stock Exchange CEO Bonnie Chan Yick-ting in an exclusive interview with a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald. She admitted that to better serve the real economy with finance, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange regularly reviews its listing rules. "As long as there is market demand, we must study it. This is the spirit of 'people, goods, and venue' that we advocate." Bonnie Chan Yick-ting. File photo The return of an increasing number of Chinese "giants" to list in Hong Kong has undoubtedly injected new vitality into Hong Kong's capital market. In response, Bonnie Chan Yick-ting firmly stated, "Hong Kong is an open market, and there is no need to question whether we can handle it. The answer is 'we can definitely handle it.' At the same time, the performance of Hong Kong's refinancing market has also been impressive. As of June 6, 2025, the cumulative refinancing volume this year has reached US$25.9 billion (approximately HK$203.3 billion), more than double the IPO fundraising amount in Hong Kong during the same period. To continuously enhance the attractiveness and competitiveness of the Hong Kong market and thus improve overall liquidity, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has launched a series of innovative initiatives in recent years. Among them, the "FINI" (Fast Interface for New Issuance) system launched in 2023 is a key component. This system aims to shorten the settlement cycle for new shares, significantly reducing it from the traditional "T+5" to "T+2." The shortening of the settlement cycle means an increase in capital turnover efficiency, which can effectively reduce market risk and attract more international investors to participate in new stock subscriptions, thereby further enhancing the liquidity of the new stock market. Since the beginning of this year, Hong Kong stock liquidity has significantly improved, leading to a substantial narrowing of the A-H share price gap. This has also prompted leading A-share companies to more actively consider listing in Hong Kong. "If a company is listed simultaneously in the A-share and Hong Kong markets, the trading activity in the Hong Kong market will also drive the trading volume in the A-share market, achieving a virtuous cycle." In 2024, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) introduced five capital market cooperation measures with Hong Kong and has continued to optimize the filing process for companies listing overseas. These policies provide a more convenient and efficient channel for mainland companies to list in Hong Kong, reducing compliance costs and time for these companies, thereby stimulating more enthusiasm for companies to choose the A+H model. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's own continuously optimized listing mechanism also provides a convenient financing environment for mainland companies. It is reported that last year the Hong Kong Stock Exchange lowered the market capitalization threshold for specialist technology companies and jointly optimized the approval process timetable for new listing applications with the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission. In early May this year, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange officially announced the launch of the "Tech Company Fast Track." According to a report by CICC, since the listing of Midea in Hong Kong in September last year, eight A-share companies have listed in Hong Kong, with IPO financing totaling HK$98.11 billion, including industry leaders like Midea and CATL. According to the CSRC's filing information and listed company disclosures, nearly 50 more A-share companies plan to list in Hong Kong, with 23 having already completed the filing or submitted their materials. On June 10, the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council issued the "Opinions on Deepening the Shenzhen Comprehensive Reform Pilot and Further Deepening Reform and Innovation to Expand Opening-up" (hereinafter referred to as the "Opinions"), which allows companies in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong to list in Shenzhen. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange is expected to welcome "H+A" listed companies. In response, she jokingly said, "The A+H model is not a competitor to A-shares, but a supplement to A-shares. title_en: 60,000 taxis will increase "online hailing" prompts.
body_en: "Why do taxis keep waving their hands when they haven't picked up any passengers?" This is a question often asked by many citizens, especially elderly passengers, when trying to hail a taxi. In the future, citizens can determine whether these taxis have accepted an online booking or are refusing passengers by looking at the "online booking" indicator light on the vehicle. According to the Municipal Transportation Commission, the city is gradually upgrading the light panels of 60,000 taxis equipped with intelligent terminals, adding an "online booking" display mode, with plans to complete the upgrade by September this year. On June 16, a taxi in Chaoyangmen displayed an "online booking" indicator light. Intern Luo Zengjia photographed. Current situation investigation Passengers complain that taxis keep driving past, drivers have something to say At 11 a.m. on June 12, in front of the Dongdan campus of Peking Union Medical College Hospital, a dozen elderly people stood scattered on both sides of the bus stop and intersection, constantly waving their hands trying to flag down a taxi, but to no avail. During this time, many taxis passing by had no passengers. This scene is not uncommon. Observations by reporters around several hospitals and commercial areas found that when passengers waved for a taxi, some "empty" taxis often drove straight past. Especially for the middle-aged and elderly groups, who are not familiar with online car-hailing platforms, they often find themselves in the embarrassing situation of being unable to hail a taxi on the road. When it comes to this topic, taxi drivers feel very wronged. Many taxis that appear to be "empty" are actually accepting orders from online platforms. With the vigorous development of online car-hailing services, the mode of accepting orders by taxis has undergone significant changes. "If we don't connect to the platform and rely solely on hailing orders, our income will be greatly affected," one taxi driver admitted. "It's not that we don't want to stop, it's that once we accept an online booking, we simply can't stop." It is understood that most drivers are connected to multiple platforms, and platform dispatching has become their main way of getting jobs. During interviews, many drivers stated that compared to picking up passengers on the roadside, the efficiency of "calling a car online" is higher. Of course, if there are no orders from the platform, they are also willing to pick up passengers hailing on the roadside. Transportation Department Displaying "online booking" already has a task According to the Municipal Transportation Commission, the original light panels of cruising taxis (indicating vacant, occupied, or out of service) have been modified. After the modification, the city's taxi management department will integrate data with online taxi-hailing platforms such as Didi and Gaode, taxi dispatch centers, and vehicle-mounted intelligent terminals to automatically display the words "online booking" on the light panel when a cruising taxi accepts an online booking, making it easier for passengers to identify the vehicle's operational status. Currently, some taxis have a small electronic display screen installed on the inside of the front windshield, with the words "online booking." This indicates that the taxi already has a task and is going to pick up passengers who have booked online. The transportation department stated that since June 2024, the city has been gradually upgrading the light panels of 60,000 taxis equipped with intelligent terminals, adding an "online booking" display mode to make it easier for passengers to know the operational status of taxis. Currently, there are still some vehicles that cannot display this status due to not having an intelligent terminal installed, and plans are in place to complete the vehicle updates by September this year to achieve the "online booking" status display. Standardizing operations Taxis displaying "vacant" should stop to pick up passengers It is reported that this light panel upgrade is achieved through real-time data sharing and software upgrades of vehicle-mounted intelligent terminals, without involving hardware modifications or changing light fixtures. The "online booking" mode is automatically controlled by the backend software system, changing automatically based on the status of the vehicle accepting orders from online platforms such as Didi and Gaode, without the need for manual operation by the driver. In addition, the transportation department will standardize driver operating behavior, requiring drivers to actively respond and stop to pick up passengers when they are displaying a "vacant" status on the taxi. This report was written by Sun Hongyang, with contributions from intern Liu Yujie.

title_en: Talent development chain empowers e-commerce value chain.
body_en: The RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement) initiated by the ten ASEAN countries officially took effect in 2023 in the 15 member countries. The agreement aims to promote regional economic development and cultural exchange. With the rapid development of global trade, RCEP has become a major cooperation platform for the "Belt and Road Initiative," playing a positive role in supporting the free trade system of cross-border e-commerce in countries along the route, maintaining the stability of regional industrial chains, and promoting the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce in China. RCEP's strategic drive and the current demand for cross-border e-commerce talent Data shows that the annual growth rate of the cross-border e-commerce market in Southeast Asia among RCEP member countries has exceeded 25%, while markets in Central Asia, Central and Eastern Europe still have huge room for expansion. In this context, cross-border e-commerce language service talents have become a key link connecting Chinese enterprises with overseas markets. These talents need to have bilingual communication skills, cross-border professional skills, cross-cultural understanding, and be able to serve as communicators for economic and trade cooperation and disseminators of Chinese cultural values. However, the current talent development faces multiple challenges. At the level of industry-education integration, cooperation between schools and enterprises remains superficial, teaching content is disconnected from job requirements, and there is a lack of real project practice; at the level of cultural education, the curriculum system generally overlooks cultural differences among RCEP member countries, such as religious customs in ASEAN countries, business etiquette in Japan and South Korea, etc.; at the level of knowledge system, there is a tendency to prioritize language skills over cultural logic, making it difficult for talents to cope with complex cross-border scenarios. For example, some cross-border e-commerce product detail pages have caused local consumers to resist due to cultural taboos not being considered during translation, directly affecting the effectiveness of the company's overseas expansion. Therefore, building a scientific training model has become an urgent need for industry development. Innovative practice of the "Chinese + Cross-border Professional Skills" training model Huzhou Vocational and Technical College integrates language education and vocational education resources based on the theory of situational education and work-based learning theory, constructing a "Chinese + Cross-border Professional Skills" talent training model. It builds a three-dimensional training structure of "structure-function-context" to help students improve their abilities in real work situations. Taking Amazon platform operation teaching as an example, teachers first help students master product description translation skills through language courses (structure), then let students know how to adjust the copy based on the consumption habits of the target country through case analysis (function), and finally apply what they have learned in simulated store operations (context) to help students form a "learn-practice-use" closed loop. Specifically, there are the following training paths. Building a "1+N+X" three-level training framework. This framework is based on the core culture of the enterprise. "1" represents the enterprise's mission, vision, and values, such as Alibaba's mission of "making it easy to do business anywhere in the world," which is the soul of the training framework. "N" refers to personalized training programs based on the "MVV" of different enterprises, such as developing training programs focusing on the Russian-speaking market for enterprises like "AliExpress" and designing special courses for the Southeast Asian market for brands like Lazada. "X" represents a cross-cultural training system that customizes content based on cultural differences among RCEP member countries - emphasizing business etiquette details for the Confucian cultural circle (Japan, South Korea, Singapore), focusing on religious taboo training for the Islamic cultural circle (Malaysia, Indonesia), and emphasizing workplace communication habits for the Christian cultural circle (Australia, New Zealand). A cooperation case between a cross-border e-commerce company and a school shows that this framework has shortened the internship adaptation period from 3 months to 1 month, increased the accuracy of product translation by 40%, and reduced customer complaint rates by 25%. In the specific implementation, companies need to involve senior practitioners in course design, transforming real work processes into teaching modules, such as optimizing the case analysis course "Amazon online product detail page design" into three teaching units: keyword analysis, selling point refinement, and cultural adaptation. Innovative multi-domain collaborative training model. Adopting a three-dimensional training path of "online + offline" and "domestic + overseas." Online, virtual operations are conducted using cross-border e-commerce simulation platforms (such as Eclac), where students can process orders from different countries and the system automatically provides feedback on cultural adaptability scores; offline, joint school-enterprise training bases are established to introduce real projects from companies, such as providing product detail page translation services for small businesses in Southeast Asia. In terms of international cooperation, joint training programs are conducted with schools in each member country, with students studying language and professional knowledge domestically for the first two years and then studying local business culture in the target country for the third year while participating in internships at local companies. Taking the "Cross-border E-commerce English" course as an example, the teaching content is restructured according to the "pre-sale - in-sale - after-sale" process: in the pre-sale stage, students learn market research English, analyzing how Thai consumers prefer to express their preferences for green products; in the in-sale stage, they practice translating product detail pages, meeting the strict requirements of Japanese consumers for detailed descriptions; in the after-sale stage, they simulate dispute resolution, mastering the special requirements of Korean customers for apology etiquette. This scenario-based teaching helps improve students' employment rates and the satisfaction of employing companies. Development and application of a dynamic teaching material system. The school has established a "research - practice - development - evaluation" iterative mechanism for teaching materials. First, the school surveyed 50 "going global" companies, identified 12 typical tasks in cross-border e-commerce language services (such as exhibition negotiations, customs declarations, social media marketing, etc.), and distilled 86 core skill points. Then, teachers integrated these skill points into the curriculum, with each unit including a "cultural tips" module, such as adding details on "Vietnamese taboos" and "Indonesian prayer time arrangements" in the Southeast Asian market chapter. Supplementary online micro-courses have been developed, allowing students to scan QR codes to watch videos of Malaysian business negotiations for situational imitation. In the use of teaching materials, teachers have established a three-dimensional evaluation system: language application abilities are assessed through role-playing in physical classrooms, knowledge mastery is analyzed through correct answer rates in online learning, and skill transfer effects are measured through order conversion rates in cross-border platform practices. After using these teaching materials, a vocational college saw a significant improvement in students' performance in the national cross-border e-commerce skills competition, and companies reported a significant enhancement in interns' cultural adaptation abilities. Value breakthroughs and future optimization directions of the training model This training model fills three major gaps in current talent development: cultural cognitive gap (such as resolving marketing mistakes due to religious differences), skill connection gap (such as shortening the adaptation period from the classroom to the workplace), and value dissemination gap (such as conveying Chinese brand concepts through language services). Data from a certain cross-border e-commerce talent service agency shows that graduates trained in this model have cross-cultural communication ability scores 2.3 levels higher than those trained in traditional models, leading to an 18% increase in overseas customer repurchase rates on the platform. In the future, schools plan to optimize the model in two ways. First, by integrating digital technology, they will develop an AI-based cross-cultural communication training system to enhance adaptability through interactive simulations with virtual clients; second, they will expand into minor language directions, building a diverse training system of "English + minor languages + professional skills" to meet the demands of languages such as Thai and Vietnamese in RCEP member countries. As the markets of RCEP member countries deepen, this model will provide a more solid talent support for building an Asia-Pacific economic community, helping Chinese enterprises achieve higher-quality "going global" in the global value chain. (Author's unit is Huzhou Vocational and Technical College)

title_en: Deeply develop the consumer scene ecosystem to create new support points for consumption growth.
body_en: Building a "trinity" consumption system to stimulate consumption growth momentum The Inner Mongolia Branch of Postal Savings Bank of China has overall built a "policy-oriented + digital empowerment + green consumption" trinity consumption promotion system in the credit card business. In terms of product innovation and consumption scene construction, in line with the digital, green and other consumption trends, the main battlefield is the offline branch micro-business circle standard five-fold activity, with breakthroughs in online mainstream platforms such as Alipay, Meituan, Douyin, and JD, continuously releasing consumption potential, effectively driving up the monthly consumption scale. The year-on-year increase in cumulative consumption transactions is 27.8%, with a cumulative consumption amount of 14.32 billion yuan, an account activation rate of 53%, 3,249 participating merchants with special offers, and over 42,800 participating customers. Responding to the national "trade-in old for new" policy to activate consumption market potential In response to the national "trade-in old for new" policy, the Inner Mongolia Branch of Postal Savings Bank of China actively implemented the "two new" policy in accordance with the requirements of the head office, fully leveraging enthusiasm, initiative, and creativity, and continuously amplifying the effects of the "two new" policy. As one of the first branches of Postal Savings Bank of China to launch the "trade-in old for new" activity for household appliances and digital products nationwide, the Inner Mongolia Branch has built 2,600 digital appliance consumption scenes, collaborated with mainstream online digital retailers, and launched Inner Mongolia's special "trade-in old for new" double surprise marketing activities. By stacking subsidies, it has reduced consumers' purchasing costs, allowing them to replace intelligent, green, and healthy household appliances at a more affordable price, improving their quality of life, guiding users towards green and low-carbon consumption, and more effectively stimulating market vitality. As of April, the special "trade-in old for new" initiative has driven consumption to exceed 108 million yuan, ranking 2nd among 15 peer institutions in Inner Mongolia, and ranking 1st among peer institutions nationwide in the Postal Savings Bank, with over 18,000 customers generating over 30,000 high-frequency transactions. Enhancing brand promotion to enhance the brand influence of Postal Savings Bank credit cards In the future, the Inner Mongolia Branch of Postal Savings Bank of China will continue to optimize product design, innovate consumption scenes, fully implement business district construction, build an "activity publicity cloud window," play the "combination punch" of digital marketing, continuously improve service quality, optimize customer consumption experience, continuously enhance the brand influence of Postal Savings Bank credit cards, and support the high-quality economic development of Inner Mongolia. (Yu Shan)

title_en: Some regions cancel "national subsidy"? There is no hot spot for consumer goods to be replaced with old ones.
body_en: During the "618" period, online and offline promotional activities continued for several days, and consumers' enthusiasm for trading in old items for new ones remained high. However, there were discussions on social media about some regions temporarily unable to apply for the "national subsidy." In response to these hot topics, reporters conducted interviews in various locations. Since the end of May, discussions about Chongqing, Jiangsu, Hubei, and other regions temporarily unable to receive the "national subsidy" have attracted attention on social media. When reporters checked the Yunshanfu App's Chongqing consumer goods trade-in page, an announcement mentioned that the subsidy funds for 27 small categories of green smart home appliances and home improvement kitchen and bathroom "renewal" had been used up. Recently, when logging into the national subsidy section on Taobao, reporters also saw a notice on the Jiangsu page stating, "Jiangsu national subsidy activity is being upgraded, and you will not be able to receive it during the upgrade." The Hubei page on the JD national subsidy section also had reminders such as "Hubei smart home national subsidy activity is being upgraded." Based on these statements, some netizens began to speculate whether the "national subsidy" in some areas would be stopped. Through interviews with relevant departments and officials in various locations, reporters learned that there is no situation of canceling the "national subsidy." Reporters contacted the Market Operation and Consumer Promotion Department of the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Commerce and learned that the consumer goods trade-in policy in Jiangsu has not been suspended. Jiangsu's previous announcement clearly stated the regulations for the management of the consumer goods trade-in funds, which includes the implementation of quota management for the "national subsidy." At the end of May, the Chongqing Municipal Commerce Commission replied in its "Public Mailbox" section on its official website that the city is actively expanding the implementation of the consumer goods trade-in subsidy policy, and the enthusiasm of the citizens is high. The first phase of subsidy funds is about to be used up. Currently, relevant departments are drafting the second phase of the trade-in subsidy policy. The Hubei Provincial Department of Commerce explicitly told reporters that the Hubei national subsidy activity will run throughout the year 2025, until December 31. "Currently, daily quotas are issued for home appliances and digital 3C products, and it is first-come, first-served," said Dong Wei, a staff member of the circulation department of the Hubei Provincial Department of Commerce. Industry insiders stated that some regions have temporarily improved the pace of implementing the "national subsidy" policy. In fact, the consumer goods trade-in work will continue throughout the year, and consumers will have the opportunity to apply for the "national subsidy" every month and every week. Recently, some companies, platforms, and self-media have taken advantage of the situation to create panic and consumers should be particularly careful in discerning. In fact, apart from the few regions mentioned above, most provinces' national subsidy activities are progressing normally. The consumer goods trade-in policy is an important policy promoted at the national level. Why is the usage of the "national subsidy" different in various regions after its implementation? Through research, reporters found that based on the national subsidy rules, each region has a certain degree of autonomy to determine the "small details" of the implementation of the national subsidy, such as how to apply for and use the subsidy. He Daixin, director and researcher of the Financial Research Office of the Financial Strategy Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, believes that the progress of policy implementation in some regions is related to the local consumption structure and consumer enthusiasm. "This also indicates that the market demand for the 'national subsidy' is strong, and the policy has stimulated consumption vitality." Since the beginning of this year, the consumer goods trade-in policy has been "strengthened" and "expanded," not only adding new categories such as mobile phones, tablets, dishwashers, but also doubling the scale of the long-term special national bonds arranged, from 150 billion yuan last year to 300 billion yuan this year. This 300 billion yuan of long-term special national bonds, combined with local matching and self-arranged funds, constitute the source of the "national subsidy." Reporters learned that this 300 billion yuan is distributed to local governments in "chunks." title_en: The highest three years of zero commission, JD enters the wine and travel industry, and once again stages a "Three Kingdoms Kill" with Alibaba and Meituan.
body_en: On June 18th, JD Travel released an open letter to all hotel operators, officially entering the hotel and travel industry. JD stated that in recent years, the tourism market has been thriving, giving rise to more diverse demands. JD hopes to provide supply chain services to the hotel industry through new channels, optimize supply chain costs, and promote the healthy and sustainable development of the hotel industry. Compared to the food delivery industry, the competition in the hotel and travel market is more intense, adding a sense of tension to the industry with JD's move. JD's Entry Similar to entering the food delivery industry, JD first showed "sincerity" to merchants. JD proposed that hotel merchants participating in the "JD Hotel PLUS Membership Program" would enjoy up to three years of 0 commission. JD stated that its advantage lies in having over 800 million high-spending users nationwide, deep cooperation with over 30,000 large enterprises and over 8 million small and medium-sized enterprise customers nationwide. JD users and partners highly overlap with the main customer base of four-star or higher hotels. At the same time, JD is the platform of the first camp in domestic local life traffic, and the high-frequency consumption of massive users has also given rise to more consumption demands such as travel. At a sharing session on June 17th, JD's founder, Liu Qiangdong, discussed entering the hotel and travel business, stating that the goal is to reduce the costs of these industries by 1/3 through the supply chain and provide a new channel for hotel catering. Regarding JD's launch of the hotel and travel business, analysts believe it is related to JD's previous accumulations. Chen Liteng, a digital life analyst at the E-commerce Research Center of NetEase, told Yicai that JD's hotel and travel business is currently in the investment period, optimizing the entrance and integrating resources in parallel. JD launched flight booking in 2011, established the JD Travel channel in 2014, and accumulated supply chain resources through investments in Tuniu and strategic cooperation with Ctrip. The current move can be seen as a strategic upgrade of existing businesses rather than starting from scratch. Why does JD aim at hotel and travel for innovation? In terms of profit, the profit of the hotel and travel business is higher than that of the food delivery business. Before Meituan adjusted its financial report disclosure method in the second quarter of 2022, the financial report showed that the hotel and travel business was the most profitable business for Meituan. In the first quarter of 2022, Meituan's revenue from catering and food delivery business was 24.2 billion yuan, with an operating profit of 1.6 billion yuan. The revenue from the hotel and travel business in the first quarter was 7.6 billion yuan, with an operating profit of 3.5 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 26.4% to 35 billion yuan, and an operating profit margin of 45.6%. Although the revenue of the hotel and travel business is only one-third of the revenue from catering and food delivery, it contributes more than twice the profit. Ctrip's financial report for the first quarter of this year showed revenue of 13.8 billion yuan and a net profit of 4.3 billion yuan, with an adjusted EBITDA profit margin of 31%. At the same time, looking at the development path of Douyin Local Life, which is also a latecomer in the hotel and travel industry, there is still room for growth in the current market. In addition, after entering the hotel and travel business, the platform can also drive group buying for catering, tickets, photography, and other in-store services, with even greater potential. For example, the "2025 May Day Consumption Data Report" released by Douyin Local Life shows that offline in-store consumption during the May Day holiday was strong, with orders for accommodation, family meals, and Douyin group purchases increasing by over 70%, and hotel and scenic spot package group purchase orders increasing by 116%. The in-store verification volume of chain clothing store group purchases increased by 462%. Regarding JD's entry into hotel and travel, Chen Liteng believes that JD's core advantage lies in its mature supply chain management system. According to public information, JD plans to replicate its industrial supply chain experience in the hotel and travel industry, compressing hotel operating costs through direct procurement. In addition, relying on the precipitation of JD's retail business and the breakthrough of the food delivery business, its hotel and travel sector has a natural flow entry. Data for the first quarter of 2025 shows that JD's daily food delivery orders reached 25 million, with high-net-worth males accounting for 72% of the over 30 million users in the PLUS membership system, which is highly compatible with corporate travel demand. If airport VIP lounges and hotel benefits are integrated into the membership ecosystem, it can leverage the B-side market. Intense Market Competition Compared to the food delivery business, the current competition in the hotel and travel industry is more intense, with major platforms each having their own advantages. Chen Liteng believes that the leading platform Ctrip has been deeply cultivating the hotel and travel industry for 20 years, with its core competitiveness lying in high-star hotel resources, a well-established business travel service chain, and leading AI technology applications, and is shifting its focus to the global market. In addition, Tongcheng Travel has obvious advantages in the sinking market. Meituan, through the "Local Life + Hotel and Travel" closed-loop, has a high penetration rate of homestays and chain hotels; Fliggy relies on the Alibaba ecosystem and has advantages in resource acquisition and user traffic. Mafengwo mainly provides destination strategies and services, while Qunar's strengths lie in flight price comparison and booking. In addition, social platforms such as Douyin and Xiaohongshu are accelerating their entry into hotel and travel content marketing. This also means that JD will face fierce challenges. Considering JD's mention of reducing supply chain costs, a new round of "price wars" in the local life field may also emerge. In 2023, Douyin and Kuaishou aggressively entered the local life field, with Douyin announcing in October of that year that it would invest 500 million yuan over the next year to encourage and support influencers to explore stores and facilitate transactions between businesses and influencers. Later, Meituan countered by reducing commissions and launching live streaming. In the OTA market, years ago, there were price wars among various companies, and in the end, through acquisitions, Ctrip "eliminated opponents," with eLong and Qunar both falling under the Ctrip umbrella. With the "extinguishing" of Lvmama, there are still active players in the market such as Tongcheng Travel, Tuniu, Mafengwo, and Fliggy, with Meituan also focusing on the hotel and travel business. In the OTA field, JD still faces its old rivals Alibaba and Meituan, who are fiercely competing in the food delivery market. Zhao Huanyan, a senior economist and veteran tourism industry analyst, believes that behind Fliggy is Alibaba. With JD's "invasion" of the hotel and travel market, along with Meituan, the competition in the entire online travel market has become more intense, especially since Alibaba, JD, and Meituan are internet e-commerce companies that do not only focus on the hotel and travel business, thus having a large user base with many highly sticky users. However, Ctrip, Tongcheng Travel, Tuniu, and others have higher levels of expertise in various aspects of hotels, attractions, and travel services, and have a deeper market presence. Therefore, who will have the advantage in the tourism market will depend on the specific services provided to tourists in the future, and which platform consumers are more willing to pay on.

title_en: Chinese brands are accelerating their rise by upgrading quality through "trade-in" programs. Online and offline interactions are both active, reflecting a new landscape of e-commerce consumption in China during the "618" shopping festival.
body_en: Reporter Sun Qiru The annual "618" e-commerce promotion has begun, with the rise of emotional interest-based new consumer trends, Chinese brands accelerating their rise, "trade-in for new" leading quality upgrades, and online and offline interactions in all fields... The highlights of the "618" promotion have become a powerful booster for unleashing consumer potential and driving industrial upgrades. "Supplementing and enhancing" boosts quality consumption upgrades Following last year's purchase of many household appliances during "Double 11," Ms. Yao placed another order during "618" for a domestic smartphone priced at over 6000 yuan and an ultra-thin refrigerator. "With platform subsidies and national subsidies, the price is really affordable." Many platforms started their "618" promotions a month ago. This year, many platforms have simplified their promotional strategies by eliminating complex methods such as full reductions and stacking coupons, instead opting for direct discounts to facilitate transactions, making it easier for consumers to shop. At the same time, with the addition of national subsidies, many products have very attractive prices during the "618" period, further stimulating people's enthusiasm for consumption. Mr. Sun, who loves travel and photography and is approaching retirement age, recently purchased a DJI drone, saving 900 yuan with just the national subsidy, and over a thousand yuan with platform subsidies. With the dual benefits of national subsidies and e-commerce promotions, the enthusiasm for quality upgrades in consumption continues to rise. A responsible person from JD Retail revealed yesterday that this year's "618" platform unprecedented subsidy intensity and multiple subsidy stacking have driven explosive sales in multiple categories, with sales of mobile communications, household appliances, and food and seasoning increasing by 88%, 161%, and 138% respectively compared to the previous year. Among them, the sales volume of smartphones in the 4000 to 6000 yuan price range increased by 50% year-on-year, AI notebooks increased by 151% year-on-year, and sales of 100-inch TVs increased by 260% year-on-year. The rise of emotional interest-based new consumer trends "Many people don't understand why such a small hardware item can be sold for hundreds or even thousands of yuan. Being able to play with it anytime, anywhere is very interesting," said white-collar worker Mr. Liu, showing the two fingertip gyroscopes he just bought during "618." From fingertip gyroscopes to push cards and titanium fans, some metal gadgets known as EDC (Everyday Carry) are gradually entering the urban male vision of pursuing a refined lifestyle and stress relief from being niche geek toys. According to Taobao, the transaction volume of EDC toys on the platform has exceeded 150 million yuan, with consumers ranging in age from 18 to 60, and a rapid increase in young consumers aged 18 to 24. As of June 12, six merchants in the Taobao toy trend industry had sales exceeding 100 million yuan, nearly a hundred merchants exceeding tens of millions of yuan, 16 single products exceeding tens of millions of yuan, and over 2400 Taobao toy stores achieving triple-digit year-on-year growth, leading to explosive growth in the entire industry. The Labubu craze that has swept the world from China in the past year also staged a "reverse cargo" during "618." On June 18, the special live broadcast of Pinduoduo Mart on AliExpress went live, attracting 240,000 people from countries such as the UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand to the live broadcast room, with more than 10 popular IP products including Labubu being instantly sold out as soon as they were listed. Derivative products of copyrighted works such as comics, animations, games, idols, and special effects are driving the rapid growth of the "Guizi" economy. The person in charge of the Taobao toy industry told reporters that during this year's "618," the number of overseas orders for "Guizi" products increased by triple digits year-on-year, and it is particularly gratifying that the vast majority of transactions came from derivative products of domestic IPs. The bustling instant retail track Not only is online sales hot, but this year's "618" has achieved full-channel linkage between online and offline, driving growth in orders for physical stores. "Since the food delivery market has new players, I have been drinking unlimited 5.9 yuan coffee for the past two weeks. If the takeaway doesn't arrive on time, the platform even gives it for free," said freelancer Mr. Yang. According to JD data, during "618," the platform's instant retail business achieved explosive growth. The person in charge of JD's food delivery service introduced at the "618" media open day that although the food delivery business was officially launched in March this year, the daily order volume has exceeded 25 million, with over 1.5 million high-quality dining establishments joining, and the number of full-time delivery riders exceeding 120,000, showing strong growth momentum. At the same time, JD's food delivery service has also generated significant synergies with existing retail businesses, with over 400,000 new registered PLUS members driven by the food delivery business in April alone, and the food delivery repurchase rate of PLUS members being twice that of non-members. Li Mingtao, an expert from the National E-commerce Demonstration City Expert Committee, stated that the "618" e-commerce promotion, from simplified rules to the introduction of instant retail, reflects the platforms' grasp of changes in consumer demand. Consumers have higher requirements for product quality, cost-effectiveness, and experiential value, and only by starting from demand orientation can the promotion effectively stimulate consumer enthusiasm.

title_en: Police issue urgent warning about summer flight ticket refund and change fraud.
body_en: This newspaper (Reporter Sun Ying) The summer tourist season is approaching, and scammers are targeting tourists and students with airline tickets again. The "refund and change" fraud is on the rise. The Beijing police issued an emergency warning yesterday to beware of the "refund and change" scam. Scammers first let the victim log in to Alipay or other legitimate platforms to process the refund, in order to gain the victim's trust, and then guide the victim to log in to a fake website or app to complete the scam. Recently, Mr. Wang, a resident, purchased a plane ticket in preparation for a trip. The day before departure, he suddenly received a call from a stranger, who claimed that the plane Mr. Wang was about to board could not take off due to landing gear damage, and offered to handle the refund or change for him. Without verifying the situation, Mr. Wang followed the instructions to log in to the Alipay interface for the payment operation, filled in the Civil Aviation Administration Alipay account, refund amount, and reason for refund, and clicked to confirm the payment. However, the Alipay interface prompted "the other party is an enterprise account, unable to create a payment." Although the refund failed on the legitimate platform, after this series of operations, Mr. Wang became deeply convinced of the refund matter, not knowing that the real trap was just beginning. The other party claimed that Mr. Wang's failure to open a corporate account caused the refund to fail, and step by step guided Mr. Wang to visit a fake Civil Aviation Administration website, download an app called "Timely Service," input his bank account and password, and open a so-called corporate account. During this process, the other party claimed that the account needed to be verified before the refund, and asked Mr. Wang to transfer 440,000 yuan and 260,000 yuan to the account. After the transfers were completed, Mr. Wang did not receive the promised refund. Anti-fraud police detailed the scam tactics of this "refund and change" fraud. First, scammers usually contact the victim by phone the day before the plane takes off, falsely claiming that the flight has been canceled due to unforeseen circumstances, and promising compensation and rebooking services. Then, scammers instruct the victim to log in to a legitimate payment platform for a refund, making the victim believe it is true. When the refund fails, they guide the victim to log in to a fake website or unofficial app, and then trick the victim into transferring money to complete the scam. The police remind the public that when purchasing or changing airline tickets, it is important to do so through legitimate channels and not to trust any low-priced tickets or refund/change information from unofficial platforms. If receiving notifications of flight cancellations, delays, or changes, do not click on links directly or call the phone number provided in the notification. Verify with the official channels of the airline first. For any ticket refunds or changes, there is no need to transfer money to the other party first, and do not provide bank account numbers or passwords to strangers or on unofficial websites or platforms.
