title_en: After Qianling Mountain Park waived the entrance fee, the number of visitors increased by 30%, and revenue exceeded ten million - with no tickets, business is booming.
body_en: Guizhou Daily Tianyan News reporter Gao Wei At 10 a.m. on June 14th, the non-legacy snack "Wangji Crispy Duck" in the Qianyun Hui non-legacy market in Guizhou Qianlingshan Park wafted with a tempting oil fragrance. This small shop, which is only 16 square meters, sells over 100 ducks on average per day on weekends, becoming one of the most popular consumption points in Qianlingshan Park after the admission fee was waived. In January 2024, Qianlingshan Park announced the complete cancellation of admission fees. This decision, which seemed to be "cutting off a source of income," unexpectedly opened up new profit space. After the admission fee was waived, the park's visitor flow increased by 30% year-on-year, and the operating income from commercial assets and project operations that have been contracted exceeded 13 million yuan, creating a new development path in the cultural tourism industry of "waiving admission fees without reducing revenue." "After the admission fee was waived, visitors are more willing to pay for unique experiences, and the per capita consumption has increased instead of decreased," said a person in charge of Qianlingshan Park management. In the market, the owner of "Qian Tea Official," Jiang Zhijie, enthusiastically recommends the original drink "Wood Ginger Lemon Tea" to visitors: "The main ingredient of this drink, wood ginger, is a specialty ingredient in Guizhou." The store incorporates local ingredients such as prickly pear and hairy fruit into new tea drinks, selling 200 cups in a single day on weekends, and with the addition of independently designed "Qianling Monkey" cultural and creative products, the daily revenue reaches 14,000 yuan. "In August, we will launch online stores on platforms such as Xiaohongshu, Pinduoduo, Taobao, etc., so that more out-of-town customers can buy Guizhou cultural and creative products," Jiang Zhijie revealed. Not far away, "Shrub Coffee" was filled with tourists taking photos in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the "window with Qianlingshan water" as a check-in wall made the store's weekend daily turnover easily exceed ten thousand yuan, with 70% of repeat customers being female. "For the summer season, the store plans to launch a 'Afternoon Tea + Lake Tour' package in collaboration with the cruise ship, expecting to extend the visitor's stay by more than 4 hours," said Yao Suzhi, the person in charge of Shrub Coffee (Qianlingshan Park store). In the "Qianlai Culture" cultural and creative store, the "Hip-hop Monkey" doll wearing a Miao silver collar was eagerly sought after by tourists. The host Zhang Feie introduced, "Inspired by the 'Qianling Monkey' IP and Guizhou ethnic culture, the store currently has more than 30 products in ethnic and animal series, with 90% of purchases made by out-of-town tourists." The popularity of the internet-famous golden snub-nosed monkey "Xiaolaofei" has further boosted cultural and creative sales, and "Qianlai Culture" has taken advantage of this trend to launch related derivative products, which are expected to be sold by the end of July. These lively consumption scenes are all concentrated in the Qianyun Hui non-legacy market, which was transformed from a disused warehouse. In March of this year, the market completed its transformation with significant results. It revitalized 4,100 square meters of inefficient space, built a 1-kilometer lakeside promenade, and added public activity spaces and a music dock. Since its operation, 15 non-legacy shops have settled in, with a 40% increase in visitor flow compared to before the transformation. Last year, the operating rights of Qianlingshan Park were transferred to a district-owned cultural tourism company, following the logic of asset marketization, re-inviting investment from outside, and introducing high-quality operating companies for market-oriented operations. Currently, the commercial area within the park has expanded to 10,200 square meters, the number of merchants has increased to 35, and the number of formats has increased to 62, with traditional projects such as cable cars and cruise ships also undergoing upgrades. From "relying on admission tickets" to "scene revolution," Qianlingshan Park has achieved a breakthrough reconstruction of consumption formats; from "single sightseeing" to "immersive experience," it has deeply satisfied the needs of visitors. "Waiving admission fees is not the end, but a new starting point for development," said a person in charge of the park management, stating that the park will deepen the integration of "culture + tourism + commerce" development, create a more attractive urban leisure space, and provide a replicable "Guiyang solution" for the transformation of national scenic spots.

title_en: Discharged from the hospital and immediately receiving compensation, "Hui Min Bao" truly benefits the people.
body_en: [Shenzhen Commercial Daily] (Reporter Qiu Qingyue) 57-year-old Wang Cuicui (pseudonym) sat in front of the hospital bed, tightly holding the examination report, with a furrowed brow. When she was diagnosed with ovarian malignant tumor, the high cost of surgery, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy once almost made her collapse. But now, she has a sense of relief: "The doctor told me that the hospitalization expenses this time can be directly deducted from the reimbursement of 'Shenzhen Huimin Bao', so I don't have to scramble to raise money anymore." Wang Cuicui's experience is one of the epitomes of many insured patients under "Shenzhen Huimin Bao". In 2023, the first release of "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" introduced a one-stop settlement service, breaking through the data barriers between Shenzhen medical insurance, hospitals, and commercial insurance systems, achieving "reimbursement upon discharge". This not only reduces the pressure on the masses to advance funds but also transforms the reimbursement process from "running around" to "no running at all". Wang Cuicui's medical bills record the bitterness and hope of an ordinary family in Shenzhen. In 2024, her total treatment cost exceeded 1.21 million yuan. To raise money, she planned to mortgage her house and borrow money from relatives and friends. The turning point came in 2023. Under the joint guidance of the Shenzhen Medical Security Bureau, the Shenzhen Local Financial Management Bureau, and the Shenzhen Regulatory Bureau of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" was first introduced. The conditions for participating in "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" are lenient, not limited by age, occupation, or health condition, as long as one is covered by Shenzhen medical insurance. In addition, as long as the insured person seeks treatment at a total of more than 9,600 designated medical institutions in Shenzhen and hospitals connected to the Guangdong provincial network settlement platform, when discharged, the system automatically deducts the reimbursement portion of Shenzhen medical insurance and "Shenzhen Huimin Bao", and the patient only needs to pay the amount they are responsible for, effectively reducing the problems of insured persons needing to advance funds, taking a long time, and requiring a lot of documentation. As of June 6, 2025, "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" has provided one-stop settlement services for 320,000 person-times, accounting for 99%, truly achieving "more data running, less legwork for the masses". "In the past, reimbursement required submitting identification, medical records, invoices, and other materials, now all of these are automatically captured by the system." The person in charge of the underwriting institution of "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" introduced that through data processing technology, hospitals, medical insurance, and commercial insurance parties achieve real-time data verification, eliminating false claims; AI algorithms automatically match reimbursement rules, compressing the lengthy traditional commercial insurance claims process to "instant settlement". Feng Yonghua (pseudonym), a medical assistance recipient being treated for liver cell carcinoma at a tertiary hospital in Shenzhen, calculated a bill: the total medical expenses during the last hospitalization amounted to 213,500.95 yuan, after reimbursement by Shenzhen medical insurance, "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" compensated 62,640.92 yuan. "I used to think that commercial insurance was a luxury, but now with the 88 yuan 'Shenzhen Huimin Bao', I can be insured for up to 4 million yuan, and the government fully subsidizes our participation." This "universal" aspect is the core of the design of "Shenzhen Huimin Bao". For special difficult groups such as medical assistance recipients in this city, registered disabled residents, difficult workers, and preferential treatment objects, relevant government functional departments also provide unified assistance for participation. It is worth noting that the 2025 annual "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" is currently in the centralized enrollment period, with enrollment ending at the end of the month. Normal participants who pay Shenzhen medical insurance and Shenzhen residents covered by non-local medical insurance can all participate. Participants can conveniently enroll and pay through various channels, such as following the official designated participation platform "Shenzhen Huimin Bao" WeChat public account, or through "Shenzhen Medical Insurance" "Micro Insurance" WeChat public account, "Alipay" "UnionPay QuickPass" "i Shenzhen" "Bank of Communications" "Yue Sheng Shi" APP and "Yue Sheng Shi" mini-program, or visit offline service windows for consultation and processing. Please handle it in a timely manner, as missing the deadline will not allow for retroactive payment.

title_en: Enter "a door", allowing "little brother" to have higher efficiency in safeguarding rights and lower costs.
body_en: What do new forms of employment such as couriers and delivery drivers care most about when running orders? The answer is efficiency, speed, and time. When disputes arise, such as in the settlement of compensation, can there be a mediation model that matches the efficiency of these "delivery guys"? It is reported that in June 2024, the Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security, together with multiple departments, jointly issued the implementation opinions on the one-stop mediation of labor disputes in new forms of employment. One year later, the city completed the construction layout of the first batch of one-stop mediation centers for labor disputes in new forms of employment, achieving full coverage at the district level. More than 40 different levels of one-stop mediation organizations were established in districts, streets, and towns across the city, handling over 1,100 labor disputes by the end of 2024. Multi-departmental coordination plays a role in dispute prevention, resolution, and source governance. From the perspective of the "delivery guys," all they need to do is enter "one door," or apply online and mediate online to efficiently protect their rights and reduce running around. Aggregated linkage speeds up conflict resolution In half a day, Xiao He and Xiao Zhang, who came to Shanghai to work and decided to return to their hometown after delivering food for a week on a certain platform, finally received their hard-earned money. They walked into the Hongkou District one-stop mediation center for labor disputes in new forms of employment. Based on the preliminary investigation of new business formats in the district, the mediator quickly found the company involved from the list of companies and contacted the company's responsible person, Ms. Ji. Ms. Ji stated that due to the consolidation and settlement of order information, the relevant compensation would be paid on the 25th of the following month. Learning that they had to wait for more than a month, Xiao He and Xiao Zhang became emotional. Through the mediator's coordination from multiple dimensions of emotions, reason, and law, the company paid 1,400 yuan in compensation that same afternoon. Behind the speed-up of conflict resolution is aggregated linkage, creating a new model of one-stop mediation. The Shanghai Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Department, courts, judicial authorities, and trade unions strengthen cooperation to explore a working pattern of "human resources leading, departmental coordination, and industry participation." Each district actively explores increasing joint mediation functions in labor dispute arbitration institutions or related mediation organizations, establishing one-stop mediation centers for labor disputes in new forms of employment based on existing human resources, judicial, and trade union mediation organizations. It is reported that when handling a collective dispute involving a domestic service platform in Jiangpu Road Street, Yangpu District, the street judicial office, police station, law firm, and mediation center worked together. The mediation center was responsible for overall coordination and data verification, the judicial office provided legal support and participated in mediation, and the police station was responsible for maintaining order and risk prevention. Through efforts in "enterprise negotiation - data verification - employee communication," they successfully resolved a collective dispute involving more than 100 workers from 12 districts in the city, with a total amount of over 900,000 yuan. Integrated mediation reduces the cost of safeguarding rights During an online mediation session, the mediator, "delivery guy" Yang, the site involved, and the staff of the food delivery platform all logged on promptly and entered the mediation process. Yang admitted that he had worked for several platforms before, earning 6 to 7 yuan per order. When he joined, the site's management informed him of the payment standards, but Yang did not pay attention to the specific pricing range, so he hoped to increase the amount appropriately. The site manager and related personnel stated that the site where Yang worked implemented a refined calculation system for order volume, with different settlement standards for different order volume ranges. Upon review, it was found that there were indeed flaws in the notification of the settlement policy, leading to Yang misunderstanding the unit price standard. They agreed to partially reduce the accommodation and equipment costs that Yang should have borne. Real-time communication and repeated discussions greatly reduced the cost. The two sides quickly reached an agreement, with Yang agreeing to be paid at a standard rate of 5 yuan per order by the platform and site, while the platform and site agreed to waive a total of 1,030 yuan in related expenses for Yang. Multi-party coordination is one of the most time-consuming and labor-intensive aspects of mediating disputes. One-stop mediation conducts full-process online mediation activities for labor disputes that meet the conditions for online mediation; for cases where online mediation applications are submitted but offline mediation is required, or where mediation applications have been submitted on-site but meet the conditions for online mediation, one-stop mediation organizations strive to integrate online and offline services to provide high-quality, low-cost, and diverse dispute resolution services for new forms of employment. Promoting substantive resolution and ensuring follow-up connections It is understood that the platform company "Ele.me" in Putuo District has undergone two "upgrades" in its dispute mediation mechanism. In October 2021, the Putuo District Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security guided "Ele.me" to establish the "Blue Knights" dispute mediation committee pilot work and set up an online mediation platform. In October 2024, in collaboration with the Municipal Labor Dispute Arbitration Institute, the district people's court, judicial bureau, and general trade union, they jointly established a one-stop city-district joint mediation center for labor disputes in new forms of employment with "Ele.me." It is reported that Shanghai is focusing on areas or industries with active platform economies and more labor disputes, strengthening labor dispute negotiation and mediation work to promote the substantive resolution of conflicts. While vigorously promoting mediation, efforts are made to ensure compliance and connect mediation with arbitration and litigation. On the one hand, the results of mediation are confirmed. If a mediation agreement is reached, the parties must promptly and fully implement the agreement. On the other hand, legal guidance is provided for arbitration and adjudication. For new forms of employment disputes where the parties do not agree to mediation or mediation is unsuccessful, if it falls within the scope of labor dispute acceptance, the parties can apply for arbitration, and the mediation organization can accept the arbitration application. Next, the Shanghai Human Resources and Social Security Department will actively cooperate with relevant departments to continue promoting the establishment of one-stop mediation organizations for labor disputes in new forms of employment as needed, continuously improving the capacity of mediation organizations. Strengthening organizational support and personnel deployment to ensure more efficient and convenient resolution of labor disputes in new forms of employment.

title_en: Chain Talk / Hong Kong digital asset market steadily advancing \ Fu Rao, Shi Jianzheng
body_en: In terms of the current situation, the dual drive of stabilizing the currency system and digitizing real-world assets (RWA) is pushing the Hong Kong digital asset market into a new stage. Among them, green bonds, as a representative asset type, have taken the lead in tokenization trials, becoming an effective lever to promote the integration of sustainable finance and digital finance. It not only provides a concrete scenario for asset digitization but also offers technical tools for green transformation, serving as an institutional intersection to achieve the dual goals of "fintech + green development." As an international financial and innovation center, Hong Kong is actively promoting a series of measures including stablecoin regulatory frameworks, RWA standard formulation, and trial platform construction. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's draft Stablecoin Regulations clearly stipulate that stablecoins must be 100% backed by physical assets and be regulated under a licensing system, providing an institutional foundation for asset clearing and value anchoring. At the same time, Hong Kong Cyberport and Science Park have launched RWA technology sandbox construction, encouraging institutions to design on-chain assets for green scenarios such as energy, construction, and transportation. With the joint efforts of the SAR government and various market forces, Hong Kong is expected to build a digital asset institutional foundation centered on "stable value intermediaries" and "on-chain asset representation," providing a compliant, secure, and efficient reference template for digital assetization in the Greater Bay Area, Asia, and global markets. Moving towards "real scenario applications" Among many trial scenarios, green bond tokenization has shown the strongest potential for implementation. Green bonds, due to their clear asset structure and specific use, have demonstrated high feasibility in tokenization practices. Recently, Fosun Wealth and Ant Group have collaborated to layout green energy RWA tokenization, in conjunction with the HKMA-supported "Green FinTech Pilot Program," focusing on on-chain confirmation, standard splitting, and intelligent management of carbon assets, renewable energy rights, marking a shift where RWA is no longer just a financial innovation concept but a practical exploration closely integrated with physical industries and sustainable development. This trend also provides insights to the market: RWA should move from "on-chain value representation" towards "real scenario applications," relying on stablecoins as a clearing medium to address past issues of asset illiquidity and lack of transparent evaluation mechanisms. In the future, green electricity, carbon emission quotas, agricultural revenue rights, marine resource usage rights, etc., are also expected to be included in the on-chain asset system, further enriching asset structures and expanding investment targets. Although trial projects are gradually being implemented, to achieve scalable development, RWA still faces multiple challenges such as compliance verification, cross-chain settlement, information disclosure, valuation standards, etc. The global market still lacks a unified language and standard system for "on-chain finance." Currently, licensed platforms in Hong Kong such as OSL are actively building infrastructure covering KYC, data custody, AML anti-money laundering, smart contract auditing, etc., to provide underlying trust guarantees for RWA circulation. On the other hand, stablecoins themselves as a new payment tool also need to form institutional consensus in terms of legal status, clearing risks, and value stability. Jurisdictions such as Singapore and New Zealand have classified stablecoins under the "Payment Services Act," requiring issuing institutions to undergo reserve asset audits and have mandatory redemption mechanisms. In comparison, Hong Kong's legislative process and institutional sophistication are gradually benchmarking international standards, paving the way for market development. Furthermore, at the technical level, to achieve sustainable development of RWA, a series of underlying protocol and cross-chain interface compatibility issues still need to be addressed. Currently, most RWA trials are built on Ethereum or EVM-compatible chains, lacking modular deployment capabilities tailored for financial institutions. In the future, there should be accelerated construction of dedicated chain systems supporting multiple asset classes, privacy protection, and high-frequency clearing, interfacing with existing financial core systems (such as SWIFT, CHATS) to form a complete closed-loop system of "off-chain confirmation - on-chain trading - on-chain clearing." Only with the triple drive of institutions, industry, and technology can RWA truly move out of the trial phase and towards the mainstream capital market. It is worth emphasizing that the true value of RWA tokenization lies not only in improving asset efficiency but also in endowing traditional assets with new combinability, traceability, and social responsibility attributes. In the context of green finance, through on-chain technology, the use of funds can be visualized, project effects quantitatively evaluated, forming a "data foundation" for sustainable finance. This "visible, calculable, traceable" financial trust mechanism not only helps improve fund allocation efficiency but also assists companies in fulfilling environmental, social, and governance (ESG) responsibilities, achieving policy transformation supporting sustainable development goals (SDGs) with digital tools. From a broader perspective, this is also the important mission of Hong Kong as an Asian financial technology hub: not only promoting asset digitization but also supporting industry decarbonization, greening, and responsibility, driving "trusted assets" to become the institutional unit of a "trusted society." Building a "institutional pivot" When stablecoins serve as the institutional anchor for payment clearing and RWA as the product carrier for asset mapping, the coupling of "anchoring + circulation" will increasingly highlight Hong Kong's position in the global financial restructuring. In the future, stablecoins and RWA tokenization will undoubtedly establish the institutional foundation of Hong Kong's future digital asset market. With the three-way promotion of SAR government regulation guidance, technological innovation, and industry demand, Hong Kong is expected to become the "institutional pivot" for regional asset tokenization and green financial innovation. Whoever can establish governance standards, audit mechanisms, and cross-border recognition systems for on-chain assets first will occupy the upstream discourse power in the global financial landscape. Hong Kong, positioned at the core of this transformation, is actively laying out and steadily advancing. (The author, Fu Rao, is the Executive Director of the Hong Kong International Institute of New Economy, and Shi Jianzheng is a visiting lecturer at the Singapore University of Social Sciences and a Chartered Financial Analyst.)

title_en: The large-scale financial application has entered a new stage, and the 16th session of the Lujiazui Financial Salon has successfully concluded.
body_en: On June 19th, the 16th session of the "Lujiazui Financial Salon" was successfully held in Pudong, Shanghai, with the theme "Large-scale Financial Applications and Innovation - Smart Finance, Large-scale Model Driving New Quality Productivity Leap". Many guests from the financial and technology sectors shared insightful views. Currently, the application of large-scale models in the financial industry has moved from simple applications to a new stage of value creation, facing various bottlenecks in the practical process, all parties are working together to promote the deep integration of large-scale models with the financial industry. Challenges such as illusions still exist in the core scenes of AI and large-scale models in the financial industry. Pan Runhong, Vice President of China Financial Electronic Technology Group, stated in his speech that the application of large-scale model technology in financial scenarios has achieved phased results. Currently, the financial industry is at a key point in the transformation to intelligence, and applications have moved from initial scenario exploration to a new stage of value excavation. "This is not only an important opportunity for the reconstruction of financial service processes and the transformation and upgrading of the financial industry, but also poses higher requirements for the mastery of new technologies," Pan Runhong said. Xu Tong, Chief Information Officer of Hengfeng Bank, shared his experience in exploring AI+ financial applications in his speech. He stated that the application of AI in financial institutions can be divided into three stages: the first stage solves the problem from 0 to 1 in the scenario, forming a systematic scenario from a local scenario, with the core being the construction of an intelligent body of prompt word knowledge base. The second stage focuses on fine-tuning the scenario model, forming basic application capabilities and general capabilities through the intelligent body platform. The third stage, in the case of limited resources, transforms the consensus formed by business value creation within the bank into comprehensive applications. According to Xu Tong's experience, the construction of AI can be broken down into five parts: application engineering, model engineering, knowledge engineering, computing power engineering, and organizational engineering. By building a knowledge middle platform under the background of AI, banks can form differentiated points of effort and main attack points. As AI applications mature, the overall work organization structure and workflow of financial institutions will undergo progressive changes. "Financial institutions should always adhere to the value orientation of 'application as the core, scenario as the king', create an intelligent engine that empowers business, and the core is still value creation," said Cheng Long, Chief Information Officer of CICC. It is possible to quickly integrate intelligent technology into existing scenarios around three types of scenarios: user experience product innovation and competitiveness enhancement, key risk prevention and control, and operational efficiency improvement and cost reduction, in order to achieve good application effects. Cheng Long pointed out that the key to competition in the AI era lies in innovation, not just efficiency improvement. With the widespread application of large-scale model technology, in addition to using new technologies to empower auxiliary scenarios such as knowledge Q&A, intelligent customers, and virtual assistants, the real value lies in applying them to scenarios that traditional technologies find difficult or impossible to solve, enabling deep integration of AI capabilities with core business scenarios and professional processes. By using AI to strengthen risk control, develop new products, create new models and new revenue, and then enhance the company's innovation capabilities and market competitiveness. From the perspective of foreign banks, Zhang Fangchang, General Manager of the Information Technology Architecture Platform Department of Bank of East Asia, introduced that foreign banks have more cross-border businesses, and when facing multiple regulations, AI can greatly improve efficiency in areas such as data acquisition for cross-border lending, document review, and ledger organization. With limited human and computing resources, maximizing scenarios is the core theory of large-scale model applications, with customer growth, risk control, and cost efficiency as the primary goals. Wei Jiaohua, General Manager of Taibao Technology, believes that in the process of focusing on core financial business scenarios, large-scale models and AI still face some challenges. For example, the illusion problem, that is, large-scale models cannot guarantee accuracy, lack of data foundation and unstructured knowledge. If the issue of personal private domain is not resolved well, no one will be willing to contribute their own experience. In addition, in the popularization of large-scale models, the relevant technological literacy of business personnel also needs to be improved. In Wei Jiaohua's view, large-scale models are "students" and should learn from people. When large-scale models assist in decision-making, they can provide an answer, but people are responsible for making decisions. When using large-scale models, they can also be seen as a member of the team, and people can solve problems that have been replaced by AI by working harder and being better than the large-scale model. From the perspective of small and medium-sized banks, Zhao Weixing, President of Chongqing Fumin Bank, pointed out that the application of financial large-scale models needs to reconstruct cognitive logic from a strategic level. He emphasized that the synergy between general large-scale models and vertical domain expertise is far superior to the isolated development of professional models. Small and medium-sized banks should focus on "real value scenarios" that reduce costs and increase efficiency, be wary of technical application misconceptions, and build a new paradigm of an "algorithmic bank". Zhao Weixing proposed that in the future, banks need to shift from being "product-driven" to "customer demand-driven intelligent body ecology", using a combination of general large-scale model base + industry knowledge base + dynamic data flow to truly adapt financial products to enterprise operational needs, rather than being constrained by traditional risk preferences. The financial industry should avoid getting caught up in a "technological arms race" and should seek breakthroughs in the balance between computing power economy and green development. "Financial large-scale models are crucial, but financial large-scale models alone are not enough" In the process of deep integration of AI large-scale models with the financial industry, the assistance of technology companies also plays an important role. Several guests from technology companies shared insights on overcoming application bottlenecks with new technology breakthroughs based on their practical experience. Li Chao, General Manager and Chief Scientist of Tencent Cloud Tianyu, believes that the digital development of the financial industry has three main lines: transformation of data elements circulation, deepening of intelligent applications, and upgrading of inclusive finance, with financial risk control being the intersection of the three main lines. Data elements have non-competitive and high-speed cross-temporal and spatial flow characteristics, and financial institutions need to reconstruct their risk management systems to activate the potential of data elements. Intelligent technology has also brought about new types of attacks, requiring traditional risk control systems to upgrade to a more refined model confrontation mode. At the level of inclusive finance, financial risk control can reduce marginal costs and obtain better business flow by restructuring the underlying logic of business. Wang Wei, Chief Technology Officer of Ant Financial Services Group, believes that the development of financial business and AI technology go hand in hand. The financial industry has the characteristics of large business scale, high data quality, and rich scenarios, and the continuous development of AI technology brings continuous mode changes and reshaping to the financial business. Today, AI has been widely used in hot areas of finance such as services, risk control, marketing, investment research, and investment advisory, and financial institutions are the industry that has embraced the AI technology revolution most thoroughly. Wang Wei pointed out that the challenges of applying AI in financial business can be summarized into three main aspects: computing power input, data trustworthiness, and vertical pressure. In order to solidly implement the capabilities of AI and intelligent bodies in the financial industry, there are still many technological dividends to be explored in vertical domain fine-tuning, knowledge injection, model lightweighting, and algorithm architecture optimization. Large-scale models are crucial in the financial industry, but they are not enough on their own, so the landing of intelligent bodies in the financial industry is more like a jigsaw puzzle, requiring a combination of a series of capabilities to complement each other. Through sharing practical experience in the implementation of generative AI applications, Kuang Wenchuan, Chief Scientist of China Electronics and Director of the China Electronics Golden Information Research Institute, pointed out that although large-scale models and intelligent bodies demonstrate powerful capabilities, they are not universal solutions and require evaluation of their applicability in different scenarios. The deep integration of data, models, and computing power is crucial, and it is necessary to continuously explore the potential of large-scale models through scenario-oriented engineering paths, using enterprise-level knowledge engineering and other means. Faced with challenges such as industrialization in the process of building a digital intelligence infrastructure, highly customized requirements from various enterprises, and long-term stable operation, Kuang Wenchuan called for increased collaboration between the industry and the industrial side, opening up scenarios, and exploring ways to share industry datasets through a hierarchical classification approach, sharing the practical results of "from 0 to 1", and jointly promoting the scale and modernization of the application of digital intelligence infrastructure. Zhang Yande, General Manager of the Industry Project Group of Huawei's Computing Power Platform Vanguard Team, explained the importance of a solid computing power base for AI financial applications. The application of industry + AI is a systematic engineering process, and Zhang Yande summarized the engineering as "architecture first, easy first, difficult later, holistic decomposition, gradual advancement, and urgent battle" in 16 words. The engineering architecture starts from the computing power base, and customers need not only chips and servers, but also upper-level operator libraries and AI toolchains, requiring service providers to establish unified service capabilities with partners to promote the overall value of AI in the financial industry. Zheng Miao, Deputy General Manager of the New Financial Industry of Alibaba Cloud's Public Cloud Business Unit, believes that the financial industry is not lacking in scenarios, but in blockbuster scenarios. All traditional application scenarios are worth reconstructing with AI, leading to a paradigm shift in application scenarios. The construction of AI scenarios can be divided into five major projects: application engineering, model engineering, knowledge engineering, computing power engineering, and security engineering. Wu Yijun, General Manager of the Product Overall Department of Qi Anxin, focused on the security of large-scale model applications. Currently, large-scale model technology is accelerating the empowerment of thousands of industries, but its complex application architecture and development process have brought new security challenges, such as jailbreak attacks, prompt word injections, denial of service attacks, component vulnerabilities, and data leaks. Wu Yijun suggested that in the deployment and use of open-source large-scale models, a four-tier security barrier should be established in network security, permission control, content compliance, and data security, managing external access, internal services, and operations and maintenance management through three data channels. Sun Hongjun, CTO of SoftBank Financial Business Group, introduced the experience of DeepSeek driving the transformation of old and new architectures in bank systems. The system architecture of financial institutions is very complex, and updates and replacements are common requirements. Past technology stack transitions were carried out through interactions between people from requirements to design to development. AI tools replace human-to-human interactions at each node, allowing outdated systems to quickly transition to new systems, with cost, time, and quality all guaranteed. Jing Shaofei, Director of the Product Department of Boland, pointed out that financial institutions frequently encounter difficulties in obtaining computing power, managing models, developing agents, and controlling security in AI landing practices. A one-stop model construction, training, and deployment platform should emphasize security, controllability, and flexible scalability, support rapid integration with various business scenarios, and provide enterprises with full-process AI empowerment capabilities from data governance, model development to the landing of intelligent applications, helping financial customers efficiently build an autonomous and controllable intelligent business system. "AI Agent is the 'last mile' of large-scale model landing" In the roundtable discussion session on the theme of "The Landing Practice of AI Agents in the Financial Industry", representatives from several financial institutions further introduced their insights on the application of AI intelligent bodies in financial industry scenarios. Li Jiabin, Director of the Software Development Center of China Postal Savings Bank, believes that there is still a lot of work to be done in the evaluation of AI tools. AI landing scenarios are easy, but how to implement them well requires a lot of evaluation. Doing a good job of evaluation can improve the efficiency of AI Agents' landing and reduce development costs. He Peng, Director of the Data Management Department of China Minsheng Bank, pointed out that the core of AI Agents is to solve the "last mile" problem. Most of the work of a large institution revolves around the mainstream processes that have been designed, but there are many details that may not be effectively expressed and implemented in terms of technological needs. However, these parts can greatly improve the work efficiency of a large number of employees, which is why institutions pay close attention to relevant technology layouts. At the same time, the construction of the AI Agent system also requires follow-up changes in organizational systems. Chen Longqiang, Chief Digital Officer of Zhongxin Baixin Bank, suggested that the layout of AI Agents should "get on the bus quickly". Developing intelligent bodies based on MCP will bring out true intelligence, but attention should be paid to issues such as data security, model security, and ethics, "it may be very enjoyable to run after getting on the bus, but safety must be taken into account". Jia Jianguo, Executive Director and Director of the Information Technology Department of China-Europe Fund, believes that the era of multiple intelligent bodies will come quickly, and the collaborative governance of multiple intelligent bodies will become the primary task. The collaboration of multiple intelligent bodies needs to solve the problem of division of rights and responsibilities, and clarify who bears the consequences of business decisions. If there are illusions, multiple checks of multiple intelligent bodies can be attempted. Li Shuanghong, Head of the Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at Guojin Securities, believes that large-scale models are still far from using a universal interface, but now that the flow has developed, it is difficult to completely disappear like a bubble. The specific development of large-scale models in the future cannot be predicted, and it depends on the joint efforts of the industrial, technological, and AI sectors to see what results will be produced. Tan Ke, Head of the New Technology Application Product Team at China Life Research Center, stated that as the coverage of intelligent bodies becomes wider, with the continuous improvement of various capabilities, the gradual clarification of various industry standards, and the joint efforts of the entire ecosystem of vendors, the industry is confident in the future of intelligent bodies. This event was guided by the Shanghai Municipal Committee Financial Office and the Pudong New Area People's Government, co-organized by the Lujiazui Financial Salon Secretariat and China Financial Electronic Technology Group Co., Ltd., with media support from First Financial and Cailian Society. This series of events will build a regular exchange platform in response to the "Lujiazui Forum", and through mechanized, scenarized, and internationalized operations, continue to output the "Pudong Wisdom" of financial reform to empower the high-quality development of Pudong's economy, and fully promote the construction of the core area of Shanghai International Financial Center to new heights.

Zhao Weixing proposed that in the future, banks need to shift from being "product-driven" to "customer demand-driven intelligent body ecology", using a combination of general large-scale model base + industry knowledge base + dynamic data flow to truly adapt financial products to enterprise operational needs, rather than being constrained by traditional risk preferences. The financial industry should avoid getting caught up in a "technological arms race" and should seek breakthroughs in the balance between computing power economy and green development. "Financial large-scale models are crucial, but financial large-scale models alone are not enough" In the process of deep integration of AI large-scale models with the financial industry, the assistance of technology companies also plays an important role. Several guests from technology companies shared insights on overcoming application bottlenecks with new technology breakthroughs based on their practical experience. Li Chao, General Manager and Chief Scientist of Tencent Cloud Tianyu, believes that the digital development of the financial industry has three main lines: transformation of data elements circulation, deepening of intelligent applications, and upgrading of inclusive finance, with financial risk control being the intersection of the three main lines. Data elements have non-competitive and high-speed cross-temporal and spatial flow characteristics, and financial institutions need to reconstruct their risk management systems to activate the potential of data elements. Intelligent technology has also brought about new types of attacks, requiring traditional risk control systems to upgrade to a more refined model confrontation mode. At the level of inclusive finance, financial risk control can reduce marginal costs and obtain better business flow by restructuring the underlying logic of business. Wang Wei, Chief Technology Officer of Ant Financial Services Group, believes that the development of financial business and AI technology go hand in hand. The financial industry has the characteristics of large business scale, high data quality, and rich scenarios, and the continuous development of AI technology brings continuous mode changes and reshaping to the financial business. Today, AI has been widely used in hot areas of finance such as services, risk control, marketing, investment research, and investment advisory, and financial institutions are the industry that has embraced the AI technology revolution most thoroughly. Wang Wei pointed out that the challenges of applying AI in financial business can be summarized into three main aspects: computing power input, data trustworthiness, and vertical pressure. In order to solidly implement the capabilities of AI and intelligent bodies in the financial industry, there are still many technological dividends to be explored in vertical domain fine-tuning, knowledge injection, model lightweighting, and algorithm architecture optimization. Large-scale models are crucial in the financial industry, but they are not enough on their own, so the landing of intelligent bodies in the financial industry is more like a jigsaw puzzle, requiring a combination of a series of capabilities to complement each other. Through sharing practical experience in the implementation of generative AI applications, Kuang Wenchuan, Chief Scientist of China Electronics and Director of the China Electronics Golden Information Research Institute, pointed out that although large-scale models and intelligent bodies demonstrate powerful capabilities, they are not universal solutions and require evaluation of their applicability in different scenarios. The deep integration of data, models, and computing power is crucial, and it is necessary to continuously explore the potential of large-scale models through scenario-oriented engineering paths, using enterprise-level knowledge engineering and other means. Faced with challenges such as industrialization in the process of building a digital intelligence infrastructure, highly customized requirements from various enterprises, and long-term stable operation, Kuang Wenchuan called for increased collaboration between the industry and the industrial side, opening up scenarios, and exploring ways to share industry datasets through a hierarchical classification approach, sharing the practical results of "from 0 to 1", and jointly promoting the scale and modernization of the application of digital intelligence infrastructure. Zhang Yande, General Manager of the Industry Project Group of Huawei's Computing Power Platform Vanguard Team, explained the importance of a solid computing power base for AI financial applications. The application of industry + AI is a systematic engineering process, and Zhang Yande summarized the engineering as "architecture first, easy first, difficult later, holistic decomposition, gradual advancement, and urgent battle" in 16 words. The engineering architecture starts from the computing power base, and customers need not only chips and servers, but also upper-level operator libraries and AI toolchains, requiring service providers to establish unified service capabilities with partners to promote the overall value of AI in the financial industry. Zheng Miao, Deputy General Manager of the New Financial Industry of Alibaba Cloud's Public Cloud Business Unit, believes that the financial industry is not lacking in scenarios, but in blockbuster scenarios. All traditional application scenarios are worth reconstructing with AI, leading to a paradigm shift in application scenarios. The construction of AI scenarios can be divided into five major projects: application engineering, model engineering, knowledge engineering, computing power engineering, and security engineering. Wu Yijun, General Manager of the Product Overall Department of Qi Anxin, focused on the security of large-scale model applications. Currently, large-scale model technology is accelerating the empowerment of thousands of industries, but its complex application architecture and development process have brought new security challenges, such as jailbreak attacks, prompt word injections, denial of service attacks, component vulnerabilities, and data leaks. Wu Yijun suggested that in the deployment and use of open-source large-scale models, a four-tier security barrier should be established in network security, permission control, content compliance, and data security, managing external access, internal services, and operations and maintenance management through three data channels. Sun Hongjun, CTO of SoftBank Financial Business Group, introduced the experience of DeepSeek driving the transformation of old and new architectures in bank systems. The system architecture of financial institutions is very complex, and updates and replacements are common requirements. Past technology stack transitions were carried out through interactions between people from requirements to design to development. AI tools replace human-to-human interactions at each node, allowing outdated systems to quickly transition to new systems, with cost, time, and quality all guaranteed. Jing Shaofei, Director of the Product Department of Boland, pointed out that financial institutions frequently encounter difficulties in obtaining computing power, managing models, developing agents, and controlling security in AI landing practices. A one-stop model construction, training, and deployment platform should emphasize security, controllability, and flexible scalability, support rapid integration with various business scenarios, and provide enterprises with full-process AI empowerment capabilities from data governance, model development to the landing of intelligent applications, helping financial customers efficiently build an autonomous and controllable intelligent business system. "AI Agent is the 'last mile' of large-scale model landing" In the roundtable discussion session on the theme of "The Landing Practice of AI Agents in the Financial Industry", representatives from several financial institutions further introduced their insights on the application of AI intelligent bodies in financial industry scenarios. Li Jiabin, Director of the Software Development Center of China Postal Savings Bank, believes that there is still a lot of work to be done in the evaluation of AI tools. AI landing scenarios are easy, but how to implement them well requires a lot of evaluation. Doing a good job of evaluation can improve the efficiency of AI Agents' landing and reduce development costs. He Peng, Director of the Data Management Department of China Minsheng Bank, pointed out that the core of AI Agents is to solve the "last mile" problem. Most of the work of a large institution revolves around the mainstream processes that have been designed, but there are many details that may not be effectively expressed and implemented in terms of technological needs. However, these parts can greatly improve the work efficiency of a large number of employees, which is why institutions pay close attention to relevant technology layouts. At the same time, the construction of the AI Agent system also requires follow-up changes in organizational systems. Chen Longqiang, Chief Digital Officer of Zhongxin Baixin Bank, suggested that the layout of AI Agents should "get on the bus quickly". Developing intelligent bodies based on MCP will bring out true intelligence, but attention should be paid to issues such as data security, model security, and ethics, "it may be very enjoyable to run after getting on the bus, but safety must be taken into account". The specific development of large-scale models in the future cannot be predicted, and it depends on the joint efforts of the industrial, technological, and AI sectors to see what results will be produced. This series of events will build a regular exchange platform in response to the "Lujiazui Forum", and through mechanized, scenarized, and internationalized operations, continue to output the "Pudong Wisdom" of financial reform to empower the high-quality development of Pudong's economy, and fully promote the construction of the core area of Shanghai International Financial Center to new heights.

title_en: Neue Klasse aims to be game-changer for BMW
body_en: BMW is pinning high hopes on its forthcoming Neue Klasse models, especially in China, where the German carmaker hopes they refresh its brand image and revive its fortunes in the world's largest and most competitive auto market. The first China-made Neue Klasse model, the iX3, is scheduled to hit the Chinese market in 2026. But Jochen Goller, BMW's board member responsible for customer, brand, and sales, insists that the Neue Klasse is "much more than just new cars". Unlike the incremental updates BMW has traditionally favored, the Neue Klasse represents a comprehensive reset, involving synchronized innovation across multiple core dimensions. Among other things, it combines a new design philosophy, cutting-edge human-machine interfaces, sixth-generation electric drive technology, and the "superbrains" that act as central control units. More importantly, it represents a complete decoupling of vehicle architecture and core innovations. This modular approach allows for greater flexibility in development and application. For the Chinese market, BMW is integrating features co-developed with tech giants including Alibaba, Huawei, and ByteDance in an effort to tailor the Neue Klasse to the preferences of Chinese consumers. "We believe the Neue Klasse should redefine BMW's brand image in China," Goller said. "Many people see BMW as delivering an exceptional driving experience, but slightly trailing in smart technology. We want to change that." Goller said he has personally test-driven two Neue Klasse models and is confident they will impress. "With the launch of these models, we hope people will say: 'It drives beautifully and leads in intelligence.'" Like other global premium brands, BMW is seeing sales shrink in China, its largest market around the world. Tech-savvy and open-to-innovation car buyers are being wooed away by Chinese NEV startups. Statistics show that its first-quarter sales fell 17.2 percent year-on-year in the country, although it saw decent growth in all other major markets. "But China is growing as a market, and that is good news for us," said Goller. China's automobile market, with annual sales surpassing 24 million vehicles, presents a complex landscape of consumer preferences and fierce competition between domestic and foreign automakers. Goller has highlighted a focused strategy targeting 3-4 percent of the market — buyers who seek a blend of driving enjoyment and advanced technology, rather than competing head-on for mass volume. "If consumers are simply looking for a 'smartphone on wheels', there are other brands they can choose. But for those who seek pure driving passion, a spirit of exploration, and the solid engineering that underpins it all, BMW is the ideal choice. "BMW must be sharply focused on what it stands for — pure driving pleasure and a spirit of adventure — and avoid diluting its identity," said Goller. The German carmaker also stresses the importance of localization as a pillar of its China strategy. Its production base in Shenyang, Liaoning province, is one of the most advanced of its global manufacturing network. Its R&D network in China is second only to the one in Germany. Sean Green, president and CEO of BMW Group Region China, highlights the company's significant software engineering operations in Nanjing, Jiangsu province, employing more than 600 engineers dedicated to rapid innovation cycles. This local talent pool enables BMW to tailor its offerings to Chinese consumers by integrating partnerships with tech giants such as Alibaba, Huawei, and ByteDance. These collaborations have brought advanced AI driver assistance, entertainment features, and digital services into the Neue Klasse lineup, allowing BMW to compete with emerging Chinese EV startups on their own turf. One example is the new operating system, of which more than 70 percent of the features were developed in China. Despite these technical advances, BMW remains committed to preserving its traditional strengths: combining superior driving dynamics with leading-edge digital capabilities, rather than chasing every technological fad, said Goller. While BMW continues to refine its technical offerings, it is also rethinking how it communicates with the new generation of Chinese consumers. Goller pointed to the IMAX-style panoramic iDrive showcased at the Shanghai auto show as an example of "bold, disruptive" marketing that resonated with local audiences. He said that more of such engagement is required. "We know what pieces are needed for success in China (in the new era)," said Goller, "And now we are putting them together." lifusheng@chinadaily.com.cn

title_en: Borrowing the "expanding domestic demand" momentum, food and beverage companies in the Shanghai market are steadily advancing and seeking development.
body_en: In 2025, under the policy of "expanding domestic demand", food and beverage companies represented by companies listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange have consolidated their foundation and achieved breakthroughs through innovation. The Economic Reference News reporter noticed that 31 companies that have disclosed their 2024 financial reports have cumulatively distributed dividends exceeding 80 billion yuan, with 18 companies having a cash dividend ratio of over 50%. Companies such as Kuaijishan, Babifood, and Youyou Food have seen their dividend amounts nearly double. Stability: Driven by domestic demand, demonstrating the resilience of basic needs. From the perspective of "stability", the essential attributes and high-frequency consumption characteristics of the food and beverage industry will continue to provide companies with stable cash flow and risk resistance. Shanghai-listed food and beverage companies that have disclosed their 2024 financial reports have a total net operating cash flow of 124.5 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 32%. In terms of performance, industry leader Maotai is as stable as a rock. Under the promotion of the policy of "expanding domestic demand and promoting consumption", measures such as the distribution of consumer vouchers directly stimulate domestic demand growth. Maotai's revenue reached 174.1 billion yuan, with a net profit attributable to the parent company of 86.2 billion yuan, and both revenue and net profit growth rates exceeding 15% year-on-year. Leading sports beverage company Dongpeng Beverage achieved a total operating income of 15.8 billion yuan in 2024, a year-on-year increase of 41%, and achieved a net profit attributable to the parent company of 3.3 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 63%. The performance of its core products was outstanding, with Dongpeng Special Drink's market share in the national energy drink market increasing from 43% in 2023 to 48%, making it the best-selling energy drink in the country for four consecutive years. Faced with uncertainties such as the United States imposing tariffs, food and beverage companies quickly adjusted their strategies and accelerated their layout in the domestic market. E-commerce platforms such as Hema and JD.com have helped food and beverage companies shift to domestic sales through traffic support, further expanding their sales channels. Wufangzhai's online sales network covers major e-commerce platforms such as Tmall, JD.com, Douyin, and Pinduoduo, with 37 self-operated stores and more than 300 cooperative stores. During the reporting period, the company continued to adapt and optimize its operational strategies, solidifying the operating benefits of each platform, and achieving a year-on-year increase in gross profit margin of 8.05%. Babifood Chairman Liu Huiping said, "Our retail business is also growing rapidly, and cooperation with some core customers is deepening, with sales continuously increasing. For example, cooperation with Hema, a representative customer, is deepening, with monthly sales increasing by more than three times, and sales through Meituan channels have also achieved good results, exceeding tens of millions of yuan for the whole year." Progress: Innovation leads, opening up multiple growth paths. From the perspective of "progress", innovation-driven will become the core driving force for enterprise development. Whether it is the rise of emerging categories or the dividend of emerging channels, they will provide new growth points for companies. At the same time, trends such as the "rise of Chinese brands" and the "silver economy" will also bring more market opportunities to companies. Shanghai-listed food and beverage companies continue to deepen their multi-category strategic layout, achieve scene breakthroughs through differentiated product innovation, and seize the opportunity of consumption upgrade. For example, sugar-free tea and functional beverages are in the stage of increasing penetration. Dongpeng Beverage's electrolyte drink "Dongpeng Rehydration" exploded in the market since its launch last year, with a year-on-year increase in sales of 280.37% in 2024, successfully extending the consumption scene from the traditional "tired" scene to the "sweat point" scene of sports rehydration with its precise positioning of "rapid electrolyte replenishment". The organic integration of bulk snacks and channel innovation helps companies break through. Many Shanghai-listed companies have seized the growth dividend of emerging high-potential channels. Youyou Food, which mainly sells pickled chicken feet, stated in its 2024 annual report that in the industry's changing landscape of continuous shrinkage of traditional retail channels, the company achieved structural breakthroughs, pioneered the establishment of a membership-based retail system, and established cooperation with top channels. In 2024, the company cooperated with Sam's Club, Costco, and other companies to enter the membership-based hypermarket channel, and the new product, deboned duck feet, launched for Sam's Club became a hit. The company made a profit of 157 million yuan for the whole year, a year-on-year increase of 35.44%. Looking ahead to 2025, Youyou Food stated that after a careful evaluation by the company, it is expected that revenue growth will not be less than 20%. According to industry professionals, emerging channels such as bulk snack channels, content e-commerce channels, and membership-based hypermarket channels are growing significantly faster than traditional channels (distribution/comprehensive e-commerce, etc.), and companies embracing omni-channel are expected to achieve product volume. The "rise of Chinese brands" and the "silver economy" have also become highlights of the industry. Time-honored brands such as Yuengzufeng have launched low-sugar pastries to cater to the health trend. The company stated that low-sugar, low-fat, high-fiber, additive-free, and other healthy baked products have become market hotspots, and functional baked goods (such as those with added probiotics and dietary fiber) are also favored by consumers. The growth of these demands has driven innovation in product research and development and raw material selection for companies. The company continues to optimize its product process technology, use healthy cooking methods, streamline ingredients, select high-quality raw materials, and ensure that products meet modern consumers' demand for healthy eating. "Chinese time-honored brand" Guangzhou Restaurant closely follows hot topics such as the silver economy and the concept of food and medicine sharing the same origin, opening up new tracks such as "Cantonese-style light nourishment" and "Cantonese-style leisure sugar water", and launching products such as ginseng intelligence chicken soup and tangerine peel lotus seed red bean paste. The company continues to delve into research and development to cultivate product items, launching a series of meat products such as squab and chicken cutlets, further enriching the product matrix. This combination of tradition and innovation not only meets the diverse needs of consumers but also injects new vitality into the brand. (Reporter Zhang Wen, Shanghai) (This article is reprinted from Economic Reference News)

title_en: Chinese Translation Association 2022 Work Summary
body_en: Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping as the core has attached great importance to the development of the translation cause, making a series of important instructions and directives. Superior departments, including the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, have made a series of important deployments to implement the requirements of the Party Central Committee. The Translators Association of China (TAC) has always taken the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's important instructions and the deployments and requirements of the Party Central Committee as its fundamental follow-up and action guide. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, TAC has comprehensively implemented the Party Central Committee's series of major deployments on building international communication capabilities and constructing a discourse system. With the aim of serving the country, society, the industry, and its members, and with the mission of connecting China and foreign countries and communicating with the world, TAC adheres to the development concepts of demand-driven, talent-based, technology-empowered, and serving the overall situation. It fully leverages the organizational advantages and industry-leading role of a national social organization, emancipates the mind, seeks truth from facts, forges ahead with determination, and pioneers innovation. New breakthroughs, progress, and achievements have been made in serving the overall situation of the Party and the country, strengthening the construction of the discourse system, promoting the development of the language service industry, expanding international exchange and cooperation, and strengthening its own organizational and institutional development. I. Deeply Studying and Implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, Promoting New Progress in Building International Communication Capabilities In accordance with the spirit of central documents and implementing the general requirement to "innovate foreign propaganda methods, strengthen the construction of the discourse system, and strive to create new concepts, new categories, and new expressions that integrate China and foreign countries," TAC has integrated industry resources and established work mechanisms, actively participating in the construction of national projects such as "China Keywords" and the "International Communication Translation Talent Pool." It has actively engaged in the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic, timely launching standardized achievements in foreign translation, and making pioneering explorations from the professional perspective of a national translation organization to strengthen international communication capabilities and the construction of the discourse system, playing a demonstrative role in improving national translation capabilities and the quality and level of foreign translation work. (I) Undertaking Major National Projects and Important Translation Tasks, Assisting in the Construction of the Discourse System for Foreign Communication in the New Era Since 2015, the Association has participated in the implementation of the national key project "China Keywords Multilingual Foreign Communication Platform" for many consecutive years, innovatively carrying out multilingual, multimedia, multi-channel, and multi-format foreign discourse translation and communication work. Keywords have been released to the outside world in 19 languages including Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, German, Portuguese, Italian, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Lao, Kazakh, Brazilian Portuguese, and Cyrillic Mongolian, totaling over 10,000. A series of 12 thematic books and over 160 types of foreign translation and dissemination products, including books, e-books, and short videos, have been compiled and released. These have been featured multiple times at important domestic and international conferences and events such as the Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation, the Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations, and the BRICS Meeting on Governance. They have also been promoted and showcased at large international exhibitions and events such as the China International Import Expo, the China International Fair for Trade in Services, and the China-ASEAN Expo. Relying on its branches such as the Committee for Foreign Discourse System Research, the Committee for Foreign Communication Translation, and the Committee for Foreign Affairs Translation, the Association has conducted joint research on the standardization of foreign translation. title_en: Notice of Online Training on Quality Control for Procurement and Outsourcing (Including External Collaboration) Processes
body_en: Industry Association [2021] No. 2 Notice on Organizing an Online Training Course on Quality Control of Procurement and Outsourcing (Including External Collaboration) Processes To All Concerned Units: Procurement and outsourcing (including external collaboration, hereinafter omitted) processes/products hold a very important position in the product operation of an organization, as they directly affect the quality management level and delivery progress of projects/products. Failure to control them effectively can lead to significant or severe quality issues in projects/products, or failure to fulfill contracts on time, ultimately causing customer dissatisfaction and even loss of customer trust. Therefore, it is a crucial component of the quality management system. Both the GB/T19001—2016 standard and the GJB9001C-2017 standard stipulate strict control requirements that must be implemented in the operational processes of enterprises and project/model management processes. Therefore, to standardize the control level of model procurement and outsourcing processes/products and enhance the development capabilities of projects/models, our association is organizing this online training. The relevant matters are hereby notified as follows: I. Training Content (I) Identifying Procurement and Outsourcing Needs (including definitions, distinctions, inputs for procurement and outsourcing, and case studies) (II) Establishing Entry and Continued Entry Criteria (including principles, methods, and case studies) (III) Determining Control Types and Degrees (methods for product and supplier classification) (IV) Evaluating and Selecting Suppliers (including exceptions to the normal process for special procurement, and case studies) (V) Communicating General and Specific Requirements (including contract and technical agreement management, and case studies) (VI) Implementing Verification and Other Assurance Measures (including acceptance methods and special control methods for outsourced products, and case studies) (VII) Performance Monitoring and Re-evaluation (including methods for developing and evaluating supplier performance indicators, and case studies) (VIII) Retaining Records of Activities (including types of records and case studies) II. Lecturing Expert Hou Xiaokang: Research-level Senior Engineer, National Registered Auditor, GE Company Customer Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, Member of the China Aviation Industry Quality Expert Database, Senior Quality Management Expert, with over 240 teaching experiences. III. Training Audience Project leaders for equipment development, personnel engaged in project management, quality management, plan management, contract management, outsourcing/external collaboration management, as well as related design, manufacturing, testing, and process personnel. IV. Training Method Due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, this training will be conducted via online live broadcast. The specific training time will be notified to registered participants after the registration deadline. To ensure training quality, the entire lecture session will be 4 hours long (online), with one training session providing lifelong Q&A. The specific training time will be notified to registered representatives 5 days in advance. V. Training Certificate Upon successful completion of the training, a course hour certificate will be issued. VI. Meeting Arrangements (I) Online training fee (conference fee): 1000 Yuan per person. Payment can be made via the designated Alipay or bank transfer. (Please indicate "Training, Unit, Name" when transferring payment.) Bank Information: Account Name: China Aviation and Aerospace Tooling Association Opening Bank: China Guangfa Bank Co., Ltd. Beijing Exhibition Center Branch Bank Account: 137 081 516 010 000 264 (II) Registration Deadline: April 16, 2021 (III) Training Time and Website: To be notified separately after registration and payment. VII. Notes (I) Please accurately fill in the unit name on the reply form for invoicing purposes. Please provide a detailed mailing address. (II) Please submit the reply form to the organizing committee (via phone, fax, email, or WeChat). (III) Contact Information: Tel: 010-64622010 010-84380548 Mobile: 13811051374 13521306899 Fax: 010-64621970 E-mail: cata@cata1990.com WeChat Official Account: Search "中国航空航天工具协会" or "CATA1981" on WeChat. After following, you can register and obtain authoritative industry release information!
