title_en: The consumer appeal behind "valley rice"
body_en: During the Dragon Boat Festival holiday, a "Gu Zi" flash mob event in Wangfujing, Beijing attracted a large number of young people to queue up for check-ins, and limited edition badges and action figures were sold out within hours. Anime IPs have already jumped out of the screen, transforming into "Gu Zi" merchandise, social content, and offline traffic entrances, attracting young consumer groups in the commercial district. In today's constantly evolving urban commercial landscape, "second dimension" culture is reshaping the offline consumption ecology with astonishing mobilization power. A flash mob of anime IPs, a distinctive "Gu Zi store," a set of limited edition trading cards or action figures can often trigger a queue frenzy, injecting vitality into deserted shopping malls. Transitioning from "self-cultivation" to "affecting regional foot traffic," "second dimension" is no longer a niche label, but an important commercial variable that integrates content, social interaction, and experiential scenes. The term "Gu Zi" comes from the English word "Goods," referring to peripheral products derived from IPs. According to iMedia Research, by 2029, the market size of China's "Gu Zi economy" will exceed 300 billion yuan, becoming a new driving force for regional consumption, cultural tourism integration, and urban renewal. The related trends have become increasingly prominent in recent consumer trends. For example, after the release of the animated film "Ne Zha 2" during the Spring Festival, its peripheral products sold over 300 million yuan on Taobao platforms in less than a month, driving sales in multiple stores to the tens of millions level; during holidays such as May Day and the Dragon Boat Festival, anime flash mobs and "Gu Zi" sales events frequently took place in major cities across the country. In places like Wangfujing in Beijing, Nanjing East Road in Shanghai, Beijing Road in Guangzhou, and Jianghan Road in Wuhan, many "Gu Zi stores" and IP flash mob events have seen long queues, with products selling out in seconds and resale at a premium becoming the norm. The appeal of "Gu Zi" lies not in its functional attributes, but as an emotional medium and cultural label. For the "Z generation," queuing for hours for a limited edition badge or a co-branded drink is a spirit of "expressing love through possession." IPs are no longer just visual content but have become a medium for identity, community belonging, and social interaction. The peripherals stuffed in "pain bags" have also become new "traffic nodes" in urban consumption scenes. This high stickiness of cultural consumption is reshaping the operational logic of offline commercial districts. The Joy City in Wangfujing, Beijing, uses popular IP combinations to guide the gathering of foot traffic; Hangzhou Hubin Intime introduces "dimensional" stores and flash installations, driving an increase in foot traffic on the entire floor; Chengdu Taikoo Li creates a "Gu Zi block," where anime peripheral sales also drive growth in dining, beverages, and accommodation. According to some property management companies, after the introduction of "Gu Zi stores," overall foot traffic on weekends increased by nearly 20%, and holidays are showing a "full house" trend. The downward trend of the "Gu Zi economy" is also evident. In many university areas and subway commercial districts, collective "Gu Zi" stores have quickly become gathering places for trendsetters. Third and fourth-tier cities activate local consumption through anime exhibitions, Cosplay festivals, and other activities. For example, in Zhejiang Jiande, the anime carnival revitalized the old street night market economy, while in Wuhan, the combination of "cherry blossoms + second dimension" created a popular scene in the university area, indicating a quiet transformation in cultural tourism consumption structure. More importantly, the "Gu Zi economy" has significant repurchase capability and scene extensibility. Brands continuously create "freshness" through limited releases, selection mechanisms, cross-border collaborations, etc., extending consumers' paths to stores and their stay time. Deep integration with online communities blurs the boundaries between "shopping" and "participation," and from murder mystery games, themed cafes to immersive exhibitions, the experiential formats derived from "Gu Zi" are constructing a set of three-dimensional consumption scenes. Behind "Gu Zi" is also a reflection of urban cultural vitality. In recent years, many local governments have attempted to link local cultural and tourism resources with IPs to achieve a win-win situation of cultural revitalization and consumption transformation. For example, the Henan Museum developed action figures based on traditional jade pendants and linked them to exhibitions and sales, while Guangxi collaborated with the game "Light and Night Love" to promote district renewal. By aggregating the interests of the "Z generation" through the "Gu Zi economy," the expression of urban youthfulness is gradually emerging. Of course, the "Gu Zi craze" is not without worries. Currently, some "Gu Zi stores" rely heavily on a single IP, lack content updates, and experience a sharp decline in foot traffic once the hype fades; flash projects struggle to retain regular customers, quickly losing momentum after holidays; scalping, false blind boxes, and other irregularities also damage consumer trust. Moving from a traffic economy to sustainable development, the "Gu Zi economy" still needs to overcome many obstacles. In the future, to truly unleash the long-term value of the "Gu Zi economy," cities and enterprises need to shift from "grabbing hotspots" to "building platforms." This includes promoting local IP originality, creating youth brands with greater local cultural recognition, and deep operational management of offline commercial space content, transitioning from "selling goods" to "selling experiences," "selling emotions," and "selling communities," constructing reusable and immersive consumer experiences. (Wang Qichen)

title_en: Involved in 126 million yuan case, hundreds of people were deceived: Victims tell the story of the scam of "proxy for affordable housing" in Haikou.
body_en: With both hands leaning on a shiny cane, Wu Xiaofen, who has physical disabilities, appeared trembling in front of the reporter. It was a normal morning in late June, with the sunlight shining on the glass of a tea restaurant on Jinpan Road in Haikou. Wu Xiaofen struggled to climb a step and sat down, placing the cane in the corner to the left of her seat. The backpack she carried was filled with a thick stack of materials, the most prominent of which was a criminal ruling made by the Higher People's Court of Hainan Province, as well as a long list of victims. Wu Xiaofen was one of the victims in this criminal ruling. Three years ago, she entrusted someone to help her purchase affordable housing in Haikou, only to be cheated out of 300,000 yuan. For an ordinary worker, this 300,000 yuan was almost all of Wu Xiaofen's savings. According to the criminal ruling in Wu Xiaofen's hands, 291 victims (as of February 29, 2024) were cheated through various channels to purchase policy-based housing in Haikou (mainly affordable housing), involving a total amount of up to 126 million yuan. This housing fraud case, directed and orchestrated by three people and involving numerous "extras" driven by interests, lasted for a staggering six years in Haikou, leaving people bewildered. On February 5 of this year, the mastermind of the case - Gan Xiaoyan, an unemployed person in Haikou, the legal representative of a real estate agency Li Yechun, and the former traffic assistant police officer in Haikou, Qiu Wenqin, were sentenced to life imprisonment, 13 years, and 10 years respectively for fraud, and their personal property was confiscated or fined. On April 17, the Higher People's Court of Hainan Province made a final ruling on the case, upholding the original verdict. How were the 291 victims deceived, how did the total amount of 126 million yuan become the basis of this fraud case, and what thoughts did this case leave people with? By opening the relevant criminal rulings and judgments, perhaps the answers can be found. "Hooked" by real estate short videos "Although the three scammers have been sentenced, our money, the victims, has not been recovered." On the morning of June 24, Chen Shiyong, a victim of the "Haikou 1.26 billion yuan real estate fraud case," told China Real Estate News that he was cheated out of 400,000 yuan when buying a house. Since being cheated out of buying affordable housing in 2022, Chen Shiyong has become particularly vigilant. When communicating with reporters via WeChat or being interviewed face-to-face, he always looked suspicious at first, spoke very little, and appeared extremely cautious. In Chen Shiyong's intermittent narration, the reporter learned that his purchase of the house was purely accidental. Chen Shiyong, who does renovations in Haikou, likes to watch short videos in his spare time. "I was watching videos and came across a real estate agent selling affordable housing, saying 'interested, private chat'." Chen Shiyong told the reporter that he and his family were crowded in a small rental house, "thinking of buying an affordable house in Haikou to settle down." Following the "interested, private chat," Chen Shiyong contacted the real estate agent through a video account, who then introduced him to a person named "Li Yechun." According to the relevant criminal judgment, Li Yechun, born in 1991, was one of the main criminals in the "Haikou 1.26 billion yuan real estate fraud case." At the time of the crime, Li Yechun's identity was the legal representative of a real estate agency in Haikou and the actual controller of a real estate agency office in Haikou for a company in Sanya. The relevant information provided by Chen Shiyong shows that on February 16, 2022, he signed a "House Purchase Agency Agreement" with Li Yechun's company, intending to purchase a 110-square-meter house in the Meishe Shijia community in Haikou. Li Yechun was responsible for helping Chen Shiyong obtain the qualifications to purchase the house, with a unit price not exceeding 9,000 yuan per square meter. The Meishe Shijia project in Haikou was one of the first affordable housing projects in Haikou to be piloted. Although the project had a small land area and only two high-rise buildings with a total of over 200 units, its location on the "golden" section of Guoxing Avenue and Wazao Road in Haikou naturally attracted the attention of homebuyers. According to the housing policy at the time, the affordable housing in Haikou was sold through a lottery system, and the Meishe Shijia project had only 217 units available for sale, attracting over 2,000 applicants. Additionally, the affordable housing project implemented a government-mandated sales price, with a unit price of 15,000 yuan per square meter. Chen Shiyong also did some calculations and realized that if he could get a house for less than 9,000 yuan per square meter, it would be a good deal. After signing the agreement, Chen Shiyong paid Li Yechun a total of 400,000 yuan for "agency service fees" and "down payment" in multiple installments. Behind the house purchase is the word "fraud" Wu Xiaofen, who was interviewed with a cane, had a different experience in purchasing a house compared to Chen Shiyong and other victims. Wu Xiaofen told the reporter that she was introduced by a classmate's classmate to purchase affordable housing from one of the main criminals in the case, Gan Xiaoyan. Who is Gan Xiaoyan? According to the aforementioned criminal judgment, Gan Xiaoyan, born in 1982, is a Haikou native with a junior high school education and unemployed. "The classmate's classmate said that Gan Xiaoyan had connections and could help with the purchase of affordable housing qualifications; the other party also said 'don't ask too many questions,' which seemed very mysterious." Wu Xiaofen told the reporter that based on her trust in her classmate, she did not inquire too much and paid Gan Xiaoyan 300,000 yuan for "housing quota fees" and other expenses. In the aforementioned judgment, a witness with the surname Wang stated that Gan Xiaoyan had indeed helped someone apply for public rental housing before and succeeded in less than two months. After that, Gan Xiaoyan's claim of having connections spread within a certain range, becoming the most powerful "trust tool" for her later fraud. "At that time, everyone around believed in her 'supernatural powers,' and few people doubted her at first." Wu Xiaofen said that whether it was Li Yechun, Gan Xiaoyan, or Qiu Wenqin, they not only played the role of "accomplice" to each other but also deceived each other. The judgment recorded that Gan Xiaoyan once had someone photoshop the official announcement information from the housing department's website and send it to Li Yechun's side, claiming that Li's client had obtained the affordable housing lottery qualification, but the traces of the photoshop were too obvious and were discovered. Driven by interests, an invisible and vast "network of interests" was formed, including various personnel such as real estate agents, social individuals, etc. Friends introduced friends, relatives introduced relatives, classmates introduced classmates, and successfully introducing clients could earn a "tea fee" of 20,000 to 50,000 yuan per unit. In addition, Gan Xiaoyan and others provided a "base price," allowing intermediaries to arbitrarily increase the price above this "base price," for example, a "base price" of 350,000 yuan per unit, with some people raising it to 600,000 yuan per unit. The reporter learned that to gain the trust of homebuyers, the fraudsters arranged for personnel to play different roles as "accomplices," taking buyers to the sales center of the affordable housing project in batches to sign contracts on-site. "The sales center staff warmly served us tea, and the purchase agreement was signed at the project site. You had no reason not to believe it." Wu Xiaofen said. Finding ways to delay time is a common trick used by Gan Xiaoyan and others to stabilize homebuyers. The judgment stated that if the victims did not receive the house as requested and asked for a refund, Gan Xiaoyan would delay by changing the community, paying a small amount of liquidated damages, making fake "pre-purchase notification letters," and fake screenshots of official website information, then continue to deceive the victims by gradually asking for money under the guise of paying for parking spaces, verification fees, etc. Another important "role" in this case, Qiu Wenqin, used his position as a traffic assistant police officer (resigned around August 2021) from January 2020 to fabricate his acquaintance with relevant department leaders, falsely claiming that he could help victims obtain qualifications to purchase affordable housing through internal connections. During this time, Qiu Wenqin used private seals and forged materials such as a fake "Haikou Affordable Housing Subscription Letter" to delay the handover time agreed upon with the victims, continuing to deceive them by asking for money under the pretext of paying the down payment, locking the house, etc. The judgment stated that by the time of the crime, Gan Xiaoyan had collected a total of 71,117,873.11 yuan from the victims, refunded 7,522,278 yuan before the crime. Except for a small portion used to repay previous debts, she spent the rest on buying private lotteries, cross-border gambling, and personal extravagance. Li Yechun collected 37,825,830 yuan from the victims, refunded 1,510,000 yuan before the crime. Except for a small portion used to repay previous debts, he spent the rest on gambling, repaying personal debts, paying intermediary fees, etc. Qiu Wenqin collected 5,791,566 yuan from the victims, refunded 90,000 yuan before the crime. Except for a small portion used to repay previous debts, he spent the rest on gambling, daily expenses, and personal extravagance. According to audits by relevant agencies, a total of 291 victims paid a total of 126,345,670.68 yuan to Gan Xiaoyan, Li Yechun, Qiu Wenqin, and other intermediaries through bank transfers, WeChat, Alipay, cash, etc. The amount involved in the case has not been refunded to the victims, with 109,624,658.68 yuan still outstanding. Reflections on the real estate fraud case The truth will eventually come to light. This real estate scam in Haikou lasted for six years, growing more and more inflated. On February 22, 2023, the Haikou police arrested Gan Xiaoyan at the Qunshang Square in Meilan District; on February 27, Li Yechun had a dispute with homebuyers at his residence and reported it to the police, leading to the discovery of his involvement with Gan Xiaoyan and others in the fraud case; on March 13, Qiu Wenqin voluntarily surrendered to the police. Qiu Wenqin's statement to the police after surrendering is quite meaningful: from early 2020 to around May 2021, when Haikou officially introduced the policy for applying to purchase affordable housing, he, relying on his position as a traffic assistant police officer, falsely claimed to have the ability to purchase affordable housing in Haikou's Daok He and Yuefang and Meishe Jiayuan Phase II projects, collecting 80,000 to 150,000 yuan from multiple clients. He later tried to seek help from relevant leaders, but the response was "not possible." It is understood that local policy-based housing includes low-rent housing, public rental housing, economically affordable housing, limited-price commercial housing, and affordable commercial housing. These types of housing have specific conditions and restrictions for application and purchase. In fact, after checking the identities of the 270 victims in this case, it was found that 106 individuals had obtained pre-purchase qualifications, but there was no evidence to show that these victims' housing qualifications were related to Gan Xiaoyan and others. It is understood that in Hainan, such real estate fraud cases are not isolated incidents. Through each case, we are forced to reflect on whether these incidents have occurred too frequently: why do such things happen repeatedly? Around 2021, the heads of two real estate agencies in Sanya City used the pretext of selling internal resettlement housing at low prices to defraud 165 homebuyers of a total of 140 million yuan, creating a major fraud case that shocked the entire country. In 2023, Zhao Mouwen, a labor dispatch worker at the Haikou Xiuying District Housing Acquisition Service Center, helped others purchase houses in the Rongjin Huayuan community, resulting in dozens of homebuyers being defrauded of up to 10 million yuan... Many homebuyers initially chose to trust Gan Xiaoyan and others for several reasons: First, information asymmetry. The victims were not very familiar with the policies and measures regarding affordable housing and other security housing. Although they were eligible to apply, they chose to use the services of scammers for convenience; it was difficult for them to distinguish between truth and falsehood regarding the scammers' carefully crafted lies and staged signing scenes. Second, greed. The government's set price for affordable housing was 15,000 yuan per square meter, but the scammers claimed that they could get a house for 6,000 to 7,000 yuan per square meter. The victims did some calculations and thought that even if they paid tens of thousands of yuan, it would still be a good deal. Third, a sense of luck. Government-subsidized housing is mainly aimed at urban low-income groups, teachers, doctors, and other special groups, and their applications require certain qualifications. Some people who did not meet the conditions held a "pick up" mentality. Fourth, driven by interests. In this case, if it were just Gan Xiaoyan and a few others "running the business," they would not have been able to create such a fraud case. Under the direction and temptation of Gan Xiaoyan and others, a carefully woven "network of interests" spread to innocent homebuyers. This network included real estate agents, social individuals, etc., who could freely increase the price above the "base price" and charge 20,000 to 50,000 yuan per unit as a "tea fee," leading some people to take risks. Gan Xiaoyan and others have paid the price for their illegal activities, but for the 291 victims, recovering their losses and healing their emotional wounds may be difficult in the short term. After Chen Shiyong and other victims finished telling their stories to the reporter, it was close to noon, and the bright sunlight was scorching the city's streets and buildings. Chen Shiyong rolled up his materials into a tube-shaped bundle and told the reporter that although he later obtained the qualifications to purchase affordable housing, he "no longer has the money to buy a house." Wu Xiaofen put the materials back in her backpack, picked up the shiny wooden cane from the corner to the left of the seat, struggled to stand up, then walked down the steps and towards the door. She skillfully started the light three-wheeled electric vehicle parked on the side of the road, passing through the dappled sunlight on the street, disappearing into the bustling crowd... (The victims in this article are all pseudonyms)

title_en: When the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail meets Jiangxi
body_en: Open the map of China's high-speed rail lines, the dense high-speed rail lines in the central region indicate the vitality and potential of this area's development. On June 28, 2015, the opening and operation of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail line, one of the main channels of the "Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal" high-speed rail network in China, broke through the long-standing geographical barriers and temporal barriers in areas such as southern Anhui, northeastern Jiangxi, and northern Fujian. It also outlined the "cross skeleton" of Jiangxi's high-speed rail in northeastern Jiangxi, highlighting Jiangxi's locational advantages. In the past ten years, the Fuzhou-Ganzhou section of the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail has accumulated 140 million passenger trips. Recently, reporters visited areas along the Hefei-Fuzhou high-speed rail line to experience the vitality and pulsation that high-speed rail has brought to Jiangxi's economic and social development. "The activation of 'cool resources' leads to 'hot industries'" At noon on June 18, Li Dongqin, a villager from Beishan Village in Sishiba Town, Guangxin District, Shangrao City, was hosting her sister who had come back from Zhejiang to visit. "In the past, when they came from Hangzhou to Shangrao, they still had to take a bus to the village after arriving in Shangrao, which took one to two hours on the road. After the Wufu Mountain Station opened, it only takes a little over ten minutes to come from Shangrao by high-speed rail, and you arrive at the doorstep when you get off the train," Li Dongqin said. title_en: 8 Chinese companies listed in "Time" magazine's top 100, the rise of innovative forces in cultural and technological creativity.
body_en: Bubble Mart, DeepSeek, and Meixue Group from mainland China have been listed on the 2025 TIME100 Most Influential Companies list, showcasing the economic strength of the mainland. The list includes disruptors like Bubble Mart, DeepSeek, and Yushu Technology; innovators like Alibaba and BYD; and titans like Meixue Group, ByteDance, and Huawei. This recognition of multiple mainland companies in TIME magazine is seen as a significant symbol, indicating that these companies have significant influence in their respective fields and are globally recognized, reflecting the increasing economic strength of the mainland. Bubble Mart has gained global popularity due to its exclusive licensing of the popular toy Labubu. By selling various Labubu plush toy products in blind boxes and featuring Labubu in numerous TikTok unboxing videos, Bubble Mart has experienced rapid business growth. In 2024, Bubble Mart's revenue and profits more than doubled compared to 2023. Additionally, Bubble Mart is known not only for selling toys but also for creating immersive in-store experiences, such as a store in Vietnam designed like a medieval castle accessible by cable car, attracting global attention. DeepSeek, on the other hand, gained international attention with its R1 reasoning model released in January, which was claimed to be on par with OpenAI's latest model but at a lower training cost. This led to DeepSeek's free chatbot application briefly surpassing OpenAI's ChatGPT and topping the Apple App Store rankings, shaking investors' confidence in other leading global artificial intelligence companies and causing a $1 trillion market cap loss in the US stock market. DeepSeek's rise has become a significant "wake-up call" for the US, making it one of the tech companies globally watched by the public. BYD, which continued to be listed in 2025, has become the undisputed leader in electric vehicles, surpassing Tesla in global sales for the second consecutive quarter. BYD's focus on developing new technologies has allowed it to occupy the market-leading position, with innovations like the "God's Eye" advanced driver assistance system and a battery that can be fully charged in just 5 minutes, capable of driving 249 miles. Market opinions suggest that the recognition of multiple mainland companies in TIME magazine holds significant symbolic meaning, indicating that these companies have significant influence in their respective fields and are globally recognized, reflecting the strong economic power of the mainland. In fact, the stock performance of these listed mainland companies that are already publicly traded has been quite impressive this year, with Bubble Mart rising 188%, Meixue Group rising over 150%, Alibaba rising 37%, and BYD rising 40% since the beginning of the year.

title_en: Gravity Media Co., Ltd. Reply Announcement Regarding the Shanghai Stock Exchange's Inquiry Letter on Information Disclosure of the Company's 2024 Annual Report (Continued on Page C91)
body_en: Stock Code: 603598 Stock Abbreviation: Gravity Media Announcement No.: 2025-022 The board of directors and all directors of the company guarantee that the content of this announcement does not contain any false records, misleading statements, or major omissions, and they shall bear individual and joint responsibility for the truthfulness, accuracy, and completeness of its content. Gravity Media Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "the Company" or "Gravity Media") recently received the "Information Disclosure Regulatory Inquiry Letter Regarding Gravity Media Co., Ltd.'s 2024 Annual Report" (Shangzheng Gonghan [2025] No. 0648) (hereinafter referred to as the "Inquiry Letter") issued by the Shanghai Stock Exchange. In accordance with the requirements of the "Inquiry Letter," the Company, together with Yongzhonghe Certified Public Accountants (Special General Partnership), has diligently reviewed and implemented each question raised in the "Inquiry Letter." The relevant questions and their responses are as follows: 1. Regarding Business Model and Revenue Recognition. The annual report shows that the company's main business is brand marketing, social marketing, e-commerce marketing and operation services, etc., and its profit comes mainly from customer service fees and media platform channel incentives. In 2024, the company achieved a total operating income of 6.29 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 32.7%; the net profit attributable to the parent company before and after deducting non-recurring items was -18.105 million yuan and -17.281 million yuan respectively, turning from profit to loss; among which, the operating income in the fourth quarter was significantly higher than in other quarters, but the net profit declined sharply and incurred losses. The company failed to disclose its 2024 performance by the end of January 2025 as required, which the company stated was due to significant changes in domestic media platform channel policies in 2024, leading to a large deviation in the company's forecast for its 2024 performance. Please supplement and disclose: (1) Detailed breakdown of the main business models, including the company's service content and processes, key performance indicators, pricing methods, major customers, suppliers, and settlement policies, etc.; [Company Reply] Gravity Media's main business is mainly composed of three different business models: brand marketing, e-commerce marketing and operation services, and social marketing. 1. Brand Marketing Service Content: The company provides clients with brand strategy and creative design, integrated communication, market research, and data services. Among these, brand strategy and creative design services mainly provide clients with brand positioning, content creative design, content marketing, IP customization, and other services; integrated communication services mainly provide clients with media resource purchasing plans and services for online video media, social marketing media, television media, offline advertising, and other media resources; market research and data services rely on the company's data research and application capabilities to provide consulting services such as market analysis and consumer insights for clients. Service Process: The company participates in the client's bidding process, wins bids after rounds of comparison, and then signs an annual framework service contract or a single project service contract with the client. In the annual framework service contract model, the company recommends media advertising resources to the client and agrees on the prices of different advertising resources for various media with the client. Within the time limit specified in the annual framework service contract, the company designs a media placement plan with the client based on marketing goals, and then produces advertising materials (e.g., creative copy, image materials, video materials, etc.) according to the client's needs and places them on the media. In the single project service contract model, the company recommends media advertising resources to the client and provides services for single advertising material production and media placement. Performance Indicators: Performance indicators for brand services and content creative services include brand awareness index, content engagement rate, etc.; integrated communication services are measured by metrics such as CPM (Cost Per Mille) and ROI (Return on Investment). Major Customers: The company's major customers include Yili, etc. Customer Pricing Method: The company charges fees based on the actual advertising placement after the advertisement is placed on the media. The price charged by the company to the client = Media advertising resource list price * Media discount * Agency discount rate. The company calculates the agency discount rate offered to clients based on the rebate rate of different media, taking into account the company's operating costs. Customer Settlement Method: The company settles with clients and issues invoices after the advertisement is placed on the media. Generally, clients pay within 45 days after the company issues the invoice. Major Suppliers: The company's major suppliers include media such as Tencent. Supplier Settlement Method: After the advertisement is placed on the media, the company settles with the media based on the media advertising resource list price * media discount as the price benchmark, and pays the supplier after a certain settlement period. The settlement period varies for different media and different advertising resources. Media offer rebates to the company after a certain period based on indicators such as the company's advertising placement volume during the period. The settlement period for rebates and the rebate ratio vary for different media (for rebate settlement period and ratio, see the table below). E-commerce Marketing and Operation Services Service Content: The company provides services for traffic procurement both on and off platforms for clients' online stores or live streaming rooms. Meanwhile, the company drives traffic through big data of internet users, guiding internet users to the client's applications, mini-programs, online stores, live streams, etc. Service Process: The company participates in the client's bidding process, wins bids after rounds of comparison, and signs a service contract with the client after winning the bid. Subsequently, based on the client's marketing goals, the company designs customized advertising placement plans by combining internet user demographics and content preferences. title_en: The good expo opens with explosive products! Xiaomi YU7, Yushu robot are here, decoding the new password of Chinese consumption.
body_en: On June 27th, the grand opening of the "2025 First Good Life Expo" (hereinafter referred to as the "Good Expo") took place. The exhibition area covered 15,000 square meters, with six exhibition halls and various interactive sections. It attracted over 400 companies to participate, promoting the upgrading of national consumption and helping "Made in China" to ascend to a global brand strategy. The Good Expo was organized by Sina Finance, with four major e-commerce platforms - Alibaba, JD, Pinduoduo, and Douyin E-commerce - as joint organizers. Weibo and Meituan served as strategic partners, while the China Economic Media Association, China Chamber of Commerce for Import and Export of Foodstuffs, Native Produce and Animal By-Products, China Chamber of Commerce for Import and Export of Chemicals, and China United Nations Procurement Promotion Association supported the event, creating a consumer experience event that integrates display, trade, and communication. During the opening ceremony, four exhibitors were invited to share their thoughts, interpreting the true meaning of "good life." They included Liu Fangxin, who safeguarded the Tangshan bone china tradition, Zhao Hui from Zhi Feng Tang who believed in the happiness of bees, Wang Yang from Meikosen Technology who emphasized the importance of creativity in China, and Li Gengxu, the "Agricultural AI Promoter," who displayed hope for remote Chinese villages on his computer screen. Additionally, the President of Guiren Bird, Lv Xiulan, and the CEO of Sina Finance, Deng Qingxu, jointly launched the "Weight Management Year Good Life Run" initiative, emphasizing the importance of enjoying exercise and returning to the essence of health through running. At the expo, Ma Liujin showcased their food products, with founder Wang Xiaofei sharing his growth experience and entrepreneurial insights. Wang Xiaofei discussed the origins of Ma Liujin in the competitive Chinese catering industry and their unique brand positioning and business model. He emphasized the importance of traditional Sichuan cuisine and the fusion of tradition and modernity in their offerings. The expo also featured exhibitors from various sectors, showcasing the vibrancy of the Chinese consumer market. The event aimed to connect supply and demand, promote the integration of digital platforms with offline scenes, and demonstrate the infinite possibilities of Chinese business innovation. The expo highlighted the resilience and innovative vitality of the Chinese consumer market, signaling high-quality economic development to the world. The expo featured a wide range of exhibitors, offering a glimpse into new consumer experience scenarios. Traditional and future elements coexisted, showcasing craftsmanship and innovation. The expo covered various fields, including specialty agricultural products, consumer electronics, beauty and personal care, food and beverages, pet products, outdoor travel, and subculture trends. The expo also provided opportunities for consumers to interact with cutting-edge technology and cultural heritage. From top-quality cashmere products to smart wearable devices, the expo catered to all aspects of a quality lifestyle. The event also included interactive experiences and exclusive discounts for attendees to enjoy. Overall, the expo aimed to redefine the concept of a good life by integrating technology, tradition, and innovation. It provided a platform for consumers to explore and experience the latest products and services while promoting the values of quality living in modern society.

title_en: 【Stable Employment Enterprises in Action】Alibaba increases efforts to introduce and cultivate AI talents.
body_en: This report (Reporter Zou Tirang) "From delivery to receiving the offer, the whole process was successfully completed in less than two weeks." Luo, a student from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, said that he has been paying attention to the internship recruitment dynamics since the beginning of this year. On the second day of the Alibaba Group's 2026 Spring Internship Recruitment in February, he applied for a position at Alibaba Cloud. Fortunately, he quickly received the first offer letter from the group. Currently, many companies are actively taking measures to create more diversified job opportunities by increasing research and development investment, innovating business models, and other means. As one of the leading companies in the Internet industry, Alibaba Group is relying on its own technological advantages and platform resources to continue to focus on the AI field, continuously strengthening the recruitment and training of talents in the field of artificial intelligence. As of now, the Alibaba Group's 2026 Spring Internship Recruitment has been completed. This recruitment activity is different from the past, as in addition to continuing to focus on positions in the technical field, there has been a significant increase in the emphasis on the field of artificial intelligence. It is reported that this internship recruitment provided more than 3,000 positions, with AI-related positions accounting for nearly half, and some AI business departments having even higher proportions, with around 65% for Alibaba Cloud's AI positions and over 80% for some AI positions. Taotian Group under Alibaba issued over 1,000 offers for this internship recruitment, adding a large number of AI positions covering various fields such as AI algorithms, AI engineering, AI products, AI operations, and AI design. At the same time, the "Top Talent T-Star Program" has launched a special internship recruitment, marking the first time the T-Star Program has recruited interns. Previously, this talent program mainly targeted top talents in global cutting-edge technology competitions, academia, and practical experience. It is reported that students who participate in the internship and perform well will be provided with a full-time offer under the T-Star Program by Taotian. Wen Dao, a doctoral graduate from the Computer Department of Beihang University, joined Taotian through the T-Star project in 2024. He is currently working on training a large model for video generation at Taotian, responsible for the "Taobao Xingchen - Image Video Model." "When I was looking for a job, I mainly applied to the talent programs of major companies. T-Star has a lot of value in terms of interview difficulty and salary level. Taotian has stable business and cash flow, which can guarantee the application of the business, as well as a lot of computing resources. For me, I can focus on long-term research and development in a certain direction, working on influential projects in the industry," Wen Dao said. The recruitment official website shows that the positions open at Taotian are closely related to the research of new technologies in the AI field, covering algorithm engineers (large model training direction), multimodal, 3D reconstruction and generation, AIGC direction, digital human image generation and driving, natural language processing, machine learning, video coding and decoding, computer vision, basic platform development, etc. "As a technology company that has always been committed to exploration and innovation, Alibaba is increasing its efforts to recruit and train talents in the AI field. We hope to provide a broad development space for more outstanding young talents and jointly embrace the huge development opportunities of the AI era," said Jiang Fang, Chief Talent Officer of Alibaba Group.

title_en: Promote food culture and open up the value chain.
body_en: Traditional advantageous food production areas and local specialty food industries are important development carriers and key growth engines of China's food industry. In recent years, under a series of policy guidance, various regions have been cultivating characteristic advantageous food production areas and industries according to local conditions, turning small specialties into large industries, effectively driving farmers' income growth and the high-quality development of the food industry. A Variety of Specialty Foods Blossoming In recent years, various regions have fully considered the development foundation and growth potential of the local food industry, taking into account factors such as local customs, dietary habits, and cultural heritage, to determine key industries for cultivation and priority development of characteristic food industries, promoting the gradual formation of a pattern of diversified development. In Liuzhou City, Guangxi, the history of "suo" snails dates back 20,000 years, while the consumption of rice noodles can be traced back to the Qin Dynasty. In the late 1970s, in the bustling streets of Liuzhou, the clever combination of the two gave birth to the specialty snack known as snail rice noodles. Through industrial concepts, industry chain thinking, and internet marketing, Liuzhou City has transformed snail rice noodles from a street-side "small rice noodle" into a large industry with global reach. By the end of 2020, the snail rice noodle industry in Liuzhou had surpassed three hundred million yuan. By 2024, the total sales revenue of the snail rice noodle industry chain in Liuzhou reached 75.964 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 13.4%. Also growing into a billion-yuan industry is the Chinese prickly ash in Guizhou. Originally a "wild fruit" mainly found in Guizhou, Chinese prickly ash has been valued for its high vitamin C content compared to most fruits. Since the beginning of this century, it has been gradually developed into one of the key agricultural specialty industries in Guizhou Province. The former Chief Engineer of the State Forestry Administration, Feng Jiaping, believes that Chinese prickly ash is an industry unique to Guizhou, which can avoid industrial homogenization and is conducive to continuously expanding the market. In recent years, Guizhou Province has strongly supported the Chinese prickly ash industry in creating high-quality products, nurturing leading enterprises, and expanding the scale of the industry. Currently, the planting area of Chinese prickly ash in Guizhou has exceeded 2 million mu, with an annual comprehensive output value exceeding one hundred billion yuan. In Qinxian County, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, the golden-colored and pearl-shaped Qinzhou yellow millet, as a key cultivation target of Shanxi's traditional advantageous food production areas and local specialty food industries, is becoming the "golden engine" driving local economic development and farmers' income growth. Qinxian's yellow millet has a long history of cultivation, and the local area has now formed a pattern of large-scale, standardized, and industrialized development. There are more than 30 professional cooperatives engaged in the cultivation of "Qinzhou yellow" in Qinxian, with over 30,000 households involved. The planting area has reached 100,000 mu, with an annual millet production in Qinxian exceeding 30,000 tons. Traditional Industries Moving towards Modern Cluster Development The growth of small specialties into large industries relies on regions breaking away from traditional development thinking, continuously extending the industrial chain, and nurturing and expanding modern industrial clusters. "Liuzhou City adheres to the concept of the entire industry chain, promotes the aggregation of elements in various links of the industrial chain and supply chain, and has created a modern industrial cluster centered around Liuzhou snail rice noodles, integrating 'production + processing + technology + cultural tourism,'" said Yang Zhigang, Director of the Liuzhou Municipal Bureau of Commerce. Liuzhou City has vigorously developed customized agriculture, fully implemented standardized production, identified 20 demonstration bases for the production of raw materials for snail rice noodles, and the scale of core raw material planting and breeding has exceeded 200,000 mu; it has established the Liuzhou snail rice noodle industrial park, Liuzhou snail rice noodle production aggregation area, and Liuzhou snail rice noodle e-commerce industrial park, attracting more than 100 upstream and downstream enterprises such as raw material supply, product processing, e-commerce, and logistics distribution to settle in the park; deepened technical cooperation with more than 10 scientific research institutions, established the country's first "Snail Rice Noodle Industry College," created a number of research and development platforms, and carried out key research on the core common technologies of the snail rice noodle industry. Guizhou Province is focusing on enhancing the influence and visibility of the "Guizhou Chinese prickly ash" public brand, promoting the modernization of the industrial cluster by leveraging the core advantages of the Chinese prickly ash production area. Currently, various regions in Guizhou are exploring models such as "planting enterprises + cooperatives + farmers" and "processing enterprises + integrated industries + farmers" to promote large-scale planting of Chinese prickly ash. At the same time, they are strengthening the integration of production and research, creating an integrated platform covering the entire industry chain of "management, learning, research, production, processing, and sales." Guizhou Province has collaborated with research institutions such as Sun Yat-sen University, Beijing Technology and Business University, and Guizhou University to complete 44 research projects. The Guizhou Provincial Department of Science and Technology has implemented 15 Chinese prickly ash research projects, achieving certain results in the utilization of Chinese prickly ash functional components, optimization of deep processing, and quality control improvement. From the field to the table, Shanxi's Qinzhou yellow millet has established a green development system covering the entire industry chain of planting, processing, warehousing, logistics, sales, and services. Qinxian has introduced special support policies, investing a total of 67.31 million yuan in the past three years to support key agricultural enterprises. At the same time, it is vigorously promoting the "winter sowing millet" technology, implementing "organic dry farming," and encouraging farmers to adopt new technologies and models through policy subsidies. Qinxian has cooperated with the national millet and sorghum industry technology system to establish a system of "technology system + leading enterprises + breeding base," creating 19 standardized green and organic breeding bases covering 3,205 mu, and cultivating excellent varieties such as "Qinhuang No. 2." Brand Leading the Exploration of Domestic and International Markets In the process of cultivating industrial clusters, regions focus on brand leadership to accelerate the entry of local famous products into domestic and international markets. Leveraging the influence of the snail rice noodle brand, Liuzhou City is vigorously promoting the integration of culture and tourism. Liuzhou has created a boutique cultural experience route for snail rice noodles, launching special routes for "snail rice noodle tours" and "snail rice noodle study tours"; it has deeply explored the unique street culture of snail rice noodles nationwide, creating snail rice noodle experiential destinations for intangible cultural heritage. "Next, Liuzhou will continue to promote the internationalization and high-quality development of the snail rice noodle industry, transforming Liuzhou snail rice noodles from a local traditional specialty product into a global 'internet-famous food,'" said Yang Zhigang. Guizhou is relying on the core advantages of the Chinese prickly ash production area to continuously enhance the influence and visibility of the "Guizhou Chinese prickly ash" public brand, creating flagship brands such as "Cinengji," empowering Chinese prickly ash to expand into the national market. At the same time, Guizhou is advancing the sales and brand promotion of Chinese prickly ash in accordance with the strategy of coordinated online and offline development, implementing the "three-step advancement" strategy of sales and brand promotion for Chinese prickly ash in the province, the country, and globally. It is cooperating with e-commerce platforms such as JD.com and Taobao, and actively participating in offline exhibition and promotion activities to help Chinese prickly ash products "set sail overseas." The relevant person in charge of the Guizhou Industry and Information Technology Department stated that Guizhou will take the "Guizhou Chinese prickly ash" public brand as a guide, fully implement the brand strengthening enterprise strategy, and create well-known Chinese prickly ash enterprise brands and product brands. Qinxian County, Shanxi Province, also focuses on the brand building and market expansion of Qinzhou yellow millet. On the one hand, it enhances brand visibility through geographical indication protection, organic certification, etc., and "Qinzhou yellow" has successively obtained national green and organic food certifications; on the other hand, it actively builds sales platforms, with online sales accounting for 30% of total sales. In the future, Qinxian will strengthen brand protection, publicity, and promotion, enhance brand reputation, and make Qinzhou yellow millet, the "golden pearl of the Taihang Mountains," more popular among consumers.

title_en: Old German companies talk about "Investing in China" Drum Tower篇
body_en: □ Reporter Dong Xiang Correspondent Gu Xuan "In the first five months of this year, the continuous implementation of the old-for-new policy has significantly boosted our retail sales." On June 20th, at the Gu Lou Innovation Square in Nanjing, Song Linbing, the President of Bosch Home Appliances Group in Greater China, revealed the company's latest performance. This foreign-funded enterprise, rooted in China for over 30 years, remains optimistic about the Chinese market and is committed to developing in the Chinese market. Looking back to 1994, when China's market economy had just opened its doors, Bosch Home Appliances from Germany crossed the oceans and entered the Chinese market. Three years later, the company established Bosch China Sales Company in the Zhongnan International Building in the Gulou District of Nanjing, building a sales and service network in China. Based in Nanjing and radiating across the country, over the past nearly 30 years, Bosch Home Appliances' industrial layout has accelerated continuously - in 2004, a home appliance park was established in Nanjing, with three factories for washing machines, kitchen appliances, and motors; in 2011, a research and development center was established in Nanjing; in 2021, the new headquarters building in China was put into use at the Gu Lou Innovation Square; last year, the China Research and Development Center was upgraded to a global research and development center, and the Home Appliance Talent Center was simultaneously unveiled. Today, among the 7 companies Bosch Home Appliances has invested in in China, 4 are located in Nanjing, including investment companies, sales, customer service companies, and the full value chain of the home appliance park and research and development center, which have successively been recognized as the first regional headquarters of multinational companies in Nanjing and the first batch in our province. It has become the largest foreign-funded home appliance manufacturer in the Chinese market. The advantage of talent from China has provided the company with a continuous source of innovation. The global research and development center, built with an investment of 400 million yuan, has a team of 700 engineers. Washing and drying sets complete clothing wrinkle removal in 19 minutes, refrigerators thaw deep-frozen meat in 10 minutes, embedded drinking machines achieve direct drinking and separate routes for living water, dishwashers combine sterilization and energy saving... In China for 30 years, closely following the Chinese market, carrying out localized innovation, a series of innovative products tailored to Chinese consumers have become Bosch Home Appliances' winning strategy in China. "We are particularly grateful for the series of stable foreign investment policies continuously introduced by the Chinese government in recent years, which have strengthened our confidence and determination in investment and development in China." Song Linbing said. In August last year, the Ministry of Commerce and four other departments launched the "old-for-new" policy for home appliances. Upon hearing the news, Bosch Home Appliances immediately formed a team, participated in the enterprise selection conducted by the provincial Department of Commerce, and successfully boarded the first train at the end of September. "Thanks to the incentive of the old-for-new policy, our retail sales achieved double-digit growth from September to December last year, especially with a significant increase in the sales proportion of emerging categories and high-efficiency products." Song Linbing introduced that the company seized the opportunity to showcase its "self-selected actions", cooperated with Suning to create a brand festival, and upgraded online stores in cooperation with Tmall and JD. A new high-performance range hood product launched for the Chinese market this year made it to the best-selling list on a certain e-commerce platform during the "6.18" period. New market opportunities have arrived. Currently, China's demand for home appliances is shifting from new house matching to old house renovation and transformation. Residences delivered 10-15 years ago have entered a period of renovation for their kitchens and home appliances. Bosch Home Appliances, which has long been familiar with China, deeply understands this trend and actively connects with local retailers to provide a one-stop solution covering decoration design, home appliance selection, and installation services as a breakthrough in opening up new markets. "China is one of the world's largest and most dynamic home appliance markets, and also one of Bosch Home Appliances' most important markets." Song Linbing stated that they will firmly uphold the development concept of "in China, for China, and also for the world", and tell the story of "investing in China" with practical actions.

title_en: Business travel and cultural integration, consumer scenarios "refreshed"
body_en: This newspaper (Reporter Ma Xiaodong) reported that the fifth Haihe International Consumer Season launch event was held at the V1 Auto World in Wuqing District over the past weekend. As an important activity of the Ministry of Commerce's "Buy in China" Tianjin Station, this consumer season is jointly organized by the Municipal Bureau of Commerce, the Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism, the Municipal Sports Bureau, and the Municipal Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security. It will launch 10 benchmark activities including the Boutique Shopping Festival, the 6th Tianjin Nightlife Festival, and the 2025 Tianjin Better Life Festival, which will continue until the end of September. On the day of the launch event of the Consumer Season, the V1 Racing Sports Carnival kicked off simultaneously, with over 100 modified cars on display in a spectacular and eye-catching parade. Traditional classic cars, brand car displays, and parent-child amusement projects also provided unique experiences for the citizens. Located in the new commercial district of Wuqing, Florence Town will actively attract inbound consumption during the consumer season. Foreign tourists who spend over 200 yuan on shopping can enjoy the "buy now, refund immediately" service for departure tax refunds. During the Boutique Shopping Festival, our city's key commercial districts will showcase their charm. Among them, more than 10 large commercial shopping centers in the Jinstreet Commercial District in Heping District are focusing on "first release economy" to tap potential, continuously launching first releases, first shows, and first exhibitions. For example, Tianhe City has introduced the first stores of dining brands such as Youhe, Meiguo, and Jiuseyun this year alone, continuously enhancing the richness of the mall's brand. "Tianjin Tianhe City adjusts over 100 brands every year, with more than half of them being first stores and flagship stores. Most brands enter in the form of the latest image stores and specialty stores," said the person in charge of the mall. Taking advantage of the 8th anniversary, Tianhe City recently launched shopping discounts, points deductions, and set up indoor and outdoor garden decorations to create a romantic summer atmosphere for customers, creating a new type of urban commercial space that combines life and social functions. In addition, Hema Fresh's first store in Tianjin opened in Nankai Joy City, introducing over 7,000 specialty products. Yonghui Supermarket's second self-adjusted store in Tianjin, the Tianjin Binhai Wanda Store, has been renovated and reopened, bringing more shopping choices to consumers in Tianjin. To promote integration in multiple fields, new scenes in culture, tourism, sports, and other aspects will also be unveiled during this consumer season. The Municipal Cultural and Tourism Department will use "Haihe Night" as the city's cultural and tourism brand, launching eight series of cultural and tourism activities such as "rippling water" and "cool summer." The Municipal Sports Bureau will focus on creating the "Enjoy Tianjin · Football Carnival" series of activities, and will host professional events such as the National Judo Points Competition, the National Baseball Championship, as well as the Nezha Cultural and Sports Carnival and other mass sports and cultural activities, deeply integrating sports with consumption. It is worth mentioning that the Municipal Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security has launched the "Warm-hearted Benefits for the People, Smooth Travel in Tianjin" social security card special activity in conjunction with this consumer season. Users who bind their physical social security card to Alipay can receive discounts when shopping at designated merchants, and enjoy special consumption discounts in supermarkets, sports facilities, and elderly care facilities.

title_en: The automotive industry is exploring new models for going global.
body_en: At the LanTu Automobile Digital Assembly Workshop in the Wuhan Economic Development Zone in Hubei Province, the 200,000th complete vehicle of LanTu Automobile rolled off the production line. Xinhua News Agency reporter Wu Zhizun The picture shows the new energy vehicle production line of NIO's second factory in the Anhui Hefei Xinqiao Intelligent Electric Vehicle Industrial Park. Xinhua News Agency reporter Zhang Duan Currently, the global automotive industry is undergoing accelerated transformation, and international trade relations are becoming increasingly complex, bringing many uncertainties to the supply chain structure of the automotive industry. China's new energy vehicle industry is actively participating in global cooperation with an open and innovative attitude. Strengthening the connection between China's automotive industry and the world, promoting supply chain collaboration, is crucial for the green transformation and innovative development of the global automotive industry. Strengthening localization operations Under the drive of electrification and intelligence, the regional pattern of the global automotive industry is undergoing profound changes. China's new energy vehicle industry is rising and has established a relatively complete industrial chain system. The latest data shows that from January to May this year, China exported 2.49 million complete vehicles, a year-on-year increase of 7.9%; and exported 855,000 new energy vehicles, a year-on-year increase of 64.6%. At the 2025 Global New Energy Vehicle Cooperation Development (Shanghai) Forum held recently, Zhang Yongwei, Vice Chairman and Secretary-General of the China Electric Vehicle Hundred People's Association, stated that China's automotive industry needs to explore new development paths based on the new global automotive situation. The traditional globalization cooperation model is facing bottlenecks. On the one hand, barriers to complete vehicle sales are increasing and extending to the supply chain; on the other hand, the supply chain of new energy vehicles is highly complex and may be affected by geopolitical, technological barriers, and cross-industry integration, facing potential risks. "In this context, the previous 'brand going global + complete vehicle investment' model is difficult to work, and it is necessary to restructure the cooperation logic and path." Zhang Yongwei suggested promoting deep links between Chinese complete vehicle enterprises and supply chains with the world automotive market. Relying on China's rich variety of models and a relatively complete incremental supply chain mainly based on new energy and intelligence, empower the global automotive industry development, help other countries develop local automotive industries, and even create local brands, achieve industrial complementarity, resource sharing. At the same time, export digital, intelligent, standardized service systems, and accelerate integration into the global market. Globalization of brands and localization of operations are gradually becoming a new model for Chinese automotive companies to expand cooperation globally. Tang Zhikun, General Manager of the International Business Center of Guangdong Xiaopeng Automobile Technology Group Co., Ltd., introduced that Xiaopeng has explored four market models in Europe, including direct sales agents, agency system, "subsidiary + dealers," and general agents, basically achieving full coverage of the European market. In terms of brand building, they have tried cross-border marketing to help the brand penetrate local communities and cultures. For example, Norwegian consumers prefer outdoor sports, Xiaopeng Automobile has sponsored local cycling events for three consecutive years, deepening consumer recognition of the brand. According to the latest plan of LanTu Automobile, by 2026, LanTu Automobile will cover the mainstream new energy vehicle market, enter 60 countries' markets by 2030, and establish more than 500 stores. Gao Yuan, Senior Director of Overseas Business of LanTu Automobile Technology Co., Ltd., said: "LanTu Zhiyin Global Edition is developed adaptively for overseas markets, integrating local service resources and financial supply chains to achieve win-win results by serving local users with local resources." Collaborative layout of the entire chain ecosystem As Chinese new energy vehicle companies go international, battery export has become an important part of the coordinated development of the industry chain. "Global development must adhere to long-termism and drive industrial development with technology." Xiong Yonghua, Vice President of Strategy and Operations of Guoxuan High-tech, said that the company's passenger car product line has developed to the fourth generation of battery cells, establishing 8 research and development centers and 20 production bases globally, with more than 10,000 global patent technologies applied. Many countries in Europe, America, and Southeast Asia have introduced policies related to battery localization production, carbon footprint, etc., imposing higher requirements on enterprises. For example, the EU's "New Battery Act" requires battery producers to take extended responsibility, including collection, processing, recycling, and disposal of batteries. "We plan to build 99 recycling points this year through two modes: self-built recycling supply chain and co-construction of recycling system with overseas strategic partners." Xiong Yonghua said the company has built a vertically integrated industrial chain from mineral extraction of battery raw materials, material production, battery manufacturing, product application to battery recycling and utilization. The supply chain of traditional automotive industry includes car companies, parts suppliers, and service providers, while the new energy vehicle industry requires hardware manufacturers, energy service providers, and data service providers to build the entire value network together. Cheng Dandan, Deputy General Manager of the European subsidiary of Ruipulan Jun Energy Co., Ltd., believes that China is breaking technological monopolies through innovation in core new energy technologies such as batteries, intelligent driving, and electronic control, achieving a strategic shift from "OEM manufacturing" to "rule-making." For new energy vehicles to truly go green overseas, it is essential to have a complete charging and swapping infrastructure, as well as a coordinated layout of vehicles, piles, networks, and storage throughout the entire chain. Sun Maojian, Vice Chairman of Hunan Jingneng New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., believes that with the current penetration rate of electrification exceeding 40%, the supply chain is shifting from cost-driven to ecology-driven. New global collaborative demands are driving the entire supply chain to break boundaries and reconstruct. Sun Maojian stated that during the company's overseas practice, they found that the global supercharging standards are fragmented, and the rate of repeated testing for supercharging certification is high. He called for the establishment of a global high-quality intelligent supercharging network, promoting mutual recognition of testing results between China, Europe, and ASEAN, eliminating digital barriers to repeated certification, and creating a technology-sharing platform. "For Chinese companies to successfully enter markets such as Europe, they need to pay attention not only to product competitiveness but also to a deep understanding and adaptation to local markets, regulations, culture, and user habits." Luca Ford, Director and Executive Vice President of Eldo Group, stated that establishing charging infrastructure in Europe faces multiple obstacles such as urban land constraints and complex policies, requiring Chinese supply chain companies to strengthen cooperation with local governments and enterprises to create infrastructure solutions suitable for local conditions. Building an overseas service system China has become the world's largest exporter of automobiles, undergoing a transformation from selling products to providing services, and then to deepening cultivation of the local market. From "going out" to "integrating in," this poses higher requirements for local operations and innovation capabilities, requiring multiple parties to work together to build a comprehensive service system for the automotive industry to go global. In the era of digital transformation and going global, automotive companies are facing new challenges. "Safety and compliance are the first steps in the overseas plan. We cannot rush out, sell products, fail, and then retreat." Shen Tao, General Manager of the Industry Cluster of Amazon Web Services (China), analyzed that the automotive industry not only has regional compliance requirements but also needs to meet new requirements including generative AI applications, data privacy protection, etc. Bai Hua, General Manager of the Solution and Delivery Department of China Unicom Smart Internet Technology, suggested that referring to the internationalization experience of German and Japanese car companies, Chinese car companies should design a global compliance management platform that is risk-identifiable, process-controllable, and responsibility-traceable when establishing overseas subsidiaries, to ensure alignment with local companies and laws and regulations. "Chinese automotive going global is not just about exporting products but also about the overall breakthrough of the global layout of the industrial chain." Bai Hua believes that this requires integration with local culture, market, and industrial chain, achieving a "one country, one strategy" approach. Relying on the support of the full industry chain digital base, China Unicom Smart Internet has rooted in local operations, deploying local vehicle networking service platforms and service teams in Frankfurt, Riyadh, Singapore, and Mexico City. Next, the company will expand its digital services from vehicle networking to industry digitalization, integrating compliance solutions, overseas smart computing center solutions, digital manufacturing systems, and marketing systems. Driven by intelligence and globalization, the automotive industry is transitioning from "electrification going global" to "intelligence going global," promoting the continuous improvement of China's international competitiveness in the automotive industry. Xing Di, Deputy General Manager of the AI Automotive Industry of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, introduced that Alibaba Cloud Tongyi Large Model has full-size, full-modal, and wide-open-source capabilities. The application of large models on vehicles will further improve the experience of intelligent assisted driving and intelligent cabins. Alibaba Cloud will continue to invest, accelerate the construction of a global cloud computing network, deploy full-stack AI capabilities at every node globally, and serve enterprises going global. The automotive industry chain is long, with a long usage cycle. As the global stock of new energy vehicles increases, related companies' value overseas needs to extend from research, development, production, and sales to usage and service. Jiang Yongxing, Founder and CEO of Open Thinking Era Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., pointed out that new energy vehicle models iterate quickly, have many components, and require complex technical support. Overseas car owners may face problems such as a lack of authorized repair shops nearby and different operating system ecosystems. Jiang Yongxing suggested that in the aftermarket of new energy vehicles going global, suppliers should jointly build a digital network, connect information such as mainframe authorization, parts maintenance, and warranty traceability, to provide better services to car owners of global car manufacturers. (Reporter Jia Jiao)

Collaborative layout of the entire chain ecosystem As Chinese new energy vehicle companies go international, battery export has become an important part of the coordinated development of the industry chain. "Global development must adhere to long-termism and drive industrial development with technology." Xiong Yonghua, Vice President of Strategy and Operations of Guoxuan High-tech, said that the company's passenger car product line has developed to the fourth generation of battery cells, establishing 8 research and development centers and 20 production bases globally, with more than 10,000 global patent technologies applied. Many countries in Europe, America, and Southeast Asia have introduced policies related to battery localization production, carbon footprint, etc., imposing higher requirements on enterprises. For example, the EU's "New Battery Act" requires battery producers to take extended responsibility, including collection, processing, recycling, and disposal of batteries. "We plan to build 99 recycling points this year through two modes: self-built recycling supply chain and co-construction of recycling system with overseas strategic partners." Xiong Yonghua said the company has built a vertically integrated industrial chain from mineral extraction of battery raw materials, material production, battery manufacturing, product application to battery recycling and utilization. The supply chain of traditional automotive industry includes car companies, parts suppliers, and service providers, while the new energy vehicle industry requires hardware manufacturers, energy service providers, and data service providers to build the entire value network together. Cheng Dandan, Deputy General Manager of the European subsidiary of Ruipulan Jun Energy Co., Ltd., believes that China is breaking technological monopolies through innovation in core new energy technologies such as batteries, intelligent driving, and electronic control, achieving a strategic shift from "OEM manufacturing" to "rule-making." For new energy vehicles to truly go green overseas, it is essential to have a complete charging and swapping infrastructure, as well as a coordinated layout of vehicles, piles, networks, and storage throughout the entire chain. Sun Maojian, Vice Chairman of Hunan Jingneng New Energy Technology Co., Ltd., believes that with the current penetration rate of electrification exceeding 40%, the supply chain is shifting from cost-driven to ecology-driven. New global collaborative demands are driving the entire supply chain to break boundaries and reconstruct. Sun Maojian stated that during the company's overseas practice, they found that the global supercharging standards are fragmented, and the rate of repeated testing for supercharging certification is high. He called for the establishment of a global high-quality intelligent supercharging network, promoting mutual recognition of testing results between China, Europe, and ASEAN, eliminating digital barriers to repeated certification, and creating a technology-sharing platform. "For Chinese companies to successfully enter markets such as Europe, they need to pay attention not only to product competitiveness but also to a deep understanding and adaptation to local markets, regulations, culture, and user habits." Luca Ford, Director and Executive Vice President of Eldo Group, stated that establishing charging infrastructure in Europe faces multiple obstacles such as urban land constraints and complex policies, requiring Chinese supply chain companies to strengthen cooperation with local governments and enterprises to create infrastructure solutions suitable for local conditions. Building an overseas service system China has become the world's largest exporter of automobiles, undergoing a transformation from selling products to providing services, and then to deepening cultivation of the local market. From "going out" to "integrating in," this poses higher requirements for local operations and innovation capabilities, requiring multiple parties to work together to build a comprehensive service system for the automotive industry to go global. In the era of digital transformation and going global, automotive companies are facing new challenges. "Safety and compliance are the first steps in the overseas plan. We cannot rush out, sell products, fail, and then retreat." Shen Tao, General Manager of the Industry Cluster of Amazon Web Services (China), analyzed that the automotive industry not only has regional compliance requirements but also needs to meet new requirements including generative AI applications, data privacy protection, etc. Bai Hua, General Manager of the Solution and Delivery Department of China Unicom Smart Internet Technology, suggested that referring to the internationalization experience of German and Japanese car companies, Chinese car companies should design a global compliance management platform that is risk-identifiable, process-controllable, and responsibility-traceable when establishing overseas subsidiaries, to ensure alignment with local companies and laws and regulations. "Chinese automotive going global is not just about exporting products but also about the overall breakthrough of the global layout of the industrial chain." Bai Hua believes that this requires integration with local culture, market, and industrial chain, achieving a "one country, one strategy" approach. Relying on the support of the full industry chain digital base, China Unicom Smart Internet has rooted in local operations, deploying local vehicle networking service platforms and service teams in Frankfurt, Riyadh, Singapore, and Mexico City. Next, the company will expand its digital services from vehicle networking to industry digitalization, integrating compliance solutions, overseas smart computing center solutions, digital manufacturing systems, and marketing systems. Driven by intelligence and globalization, the automotive industry is transitioning from "electrification going global" to "intelligence going global," promoting the continuous improvement of China's international competitiveness in the automotive industry. Xing Di, Deputy General Manager of the AI Automotive Industry of Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, introduced that Alibaba Cloud Tongyi Large Model has full-size, full-modal, and wide-open-source capabilities. The application of large models on vehicles will further improve the experience of intelligent assisted driving and intelligent cabins. Alibaba Cloud will continue to invest, accelerate the construction of a global cloud computing network, deploy full-stack AI capabilities at every node globally, and serve enterprises going global. The automotive industry chain is long, with a long usage cycle. As the global stock of new energy vehicles increases, related companies' value overseas needs to extend from research, development, production, and sales to usage and service. Jiang Yongxing, Founder and CEO of Open Thinking Era Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., pointed out that new energy vehicle models iterate quickly, have many components, and require complex technical support. Overseas car owners may face problems such as a lack of authorized repair shops nearby and different operating system ecosystems. Jiang Yongxing suggested that in the aftermarket of new energy vehicles going global, suppliers should jointly build a digital network, connect information such as mainframe authorization, parts maintenance, and warranty traceability, to provide better services to car owners of global car manufacturers. (Reporter Jia Jiao)
