title_en: E-commerce giants are stepping up their efforts in instant retail, leading to explosive growth.
body_en: Currently, with the increased investment from internet giants such as JD.com, Taobao, and Meituan, instant retail is experiencing explosive growth. The continuous efforts of internet platforms have also driven the rapid development of the third-party instant delivery industry. Industry insiders believe that the current "takeout war" is in the first half of the competition stage in the catering industry, and the second half will expand to department stores, groceries, supermarkets, pharmacies, and other fields, ushering in an industry tipping point. With the investment from various platforms to collectively increase industry penetration, it is expected that in 3 years, the daily volume of takeout plus instant retail will exceed that of e-commerce. By Jiang Yongxia, a reporter from this newspaper This year, instant retail has undoubtedly become the focus within the retail industry. With JD.com, Taobao, and other e-commerce giants intensifying their efforts in instant retail business, market competition is becoming increasingly fierce. In this instant retail market battle, whether third-party instant delivery platforms such as SF Express and Shansong can get a piece of the pie remains to be seen and will require time to test. Intense competition in instant retail Currently, with the increased investment from internet giants such as JD.com, Taobao, and Meituan, instant retail is experiencing explosive growth. It is understood that JD.com's takeout business has been online for only 4 months, with a daily order volume exceeding 25 million, over 1.5 million high-quality dining establishments have joined, and the number of full-time delivery riders has exceeded 120,000. Currently, the daily order volume of Taobao Flash Sale has exceeded 60 million. Furthermore, not long ago, Alibaba announced the merger of Ele.me into Alibaba's China e-commerce business group, focusing on unified goals and operations to promote the rapid development of instant retail. Recently, Meituan announced that it will comprehensively expand instant retail. For example, Xiaoxiang Supermarket will gradually expand to all first and second-tier cities and gradually cover 200 high-quality county-level agricultural areas nationwide in the supply chain. Meituan Flash Sale will continue to expand its categories, such as 3C electronics, fresh food, alcoholic beverages, fast-moving daily necessities, etc., to optimize the consumer shopping experience. The strategic adjustments made by e-commerce giants around instant retail business all reveal their emphasis on instant retail. Shortly after the launch of JD.com's takeout service, Liu Qiangdong, the founder and chairman of JD.com, not only personally experienced delivering takeout but also invited delivery riders to dine together to promote JD.com's takeout service. On June 24th, there were reports that Alibaba's founder Jack Ma and Alibaba Group CEO Daniel Zhang appeared at the Ele.me office to participate in Taobao Flash Sale's weekly meeting. The high level of attention and direct participation from giants have further accelerated the intense competition in the instant retail market. JD Logistics enters the battlefield The instant retail competition sparked by the takeout war is further evolving. Recently, JD Logistics announced in a statement on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange that with the rapid development of JD.com's takeout business, JD Logistics has started recruiting full-time delivery riders to participate in JD.com's delivery service. In addition to recruiting full-time delivery riders, JD Logistics has also established the position of deputy station manager in its branches to manage full-time delivery riders on a daily basis, but there will be no changes in the order and dispatch logic for full-time delivery riders. It is understood that JD Logistics, as a mature logistics brand, has the most abundant courier management experience in the industry, and its logistics advantages, which Liu Qiangdong considers as JD's "moat," are something to be proud of. Now, JD Logistics has announced the recruitment of full-time delivery riders and the establishment of the position of deputy station manager for professional management, which will undoubtedly help further professionalize full-time delivery riders, improve their service levels, and optimize consumers' experience of using JD.com's takeout service. Moreover, recently, JD Logistics launched the industry's first "Instant Delivery Warehouse" integrated service. As the first nationwide open instant retail warehouse and distribution integrated solution provider, JD Logistics uses a "shared front warehouse + self-operated delivery" model to lower the entry barriers for merchants in the instant retail sector. Specifically, the "Instant Delivery Warehouse" can pre-position goods to the "nearest location to consumers," relying on JD Logistics' service level and self-operated delivery capabilities to achieve an average delivery time of 30 minutes in core areas. More importantly, through the shared warehouse model, it helps merchants break free from the constraints of high investment and high operating costs of self-built warehouses. With the efforts of JD Logistics, a new round of "timeliness war" in instant delivery may be staged. Third-party companies actively layout With e-commerce giants entering the instant retail and instant delivery sectors, their order volumes are soaring, and the number of full-time delivery riders is increasing. So, do third-party instant delivery companies still have a chance? At the beginning of the development of instant retail, in the delivery process, platforms and merchants mainly relied on social transportation resources, which also drove the rapid development of the third-party instant delivery industry. Companies such as Dada, Shansong, and SF Express have grown rapidly in this wave of dividends, and while expanding in scale, they have also successively entered the capital market. These third-party instant delivery companies not only promote industry development but also witness the industry evolution under market changes. Recently, a person in charge of SF Express mentioned the current competitive landscape and the future development space of their own company at a shareholder meeting. The person in charge believes that the "takeout war" has driven the development of instant retail and instant delivery, leading the industry to a major outbreak. The person in charge further stated that the current "takeout war" is in the first half of the competition stage in the catering industry, and the second half will expand to department stores, groceries, supermarkets, pharmacies, and other fields, ushering in an industry tipping point. The current takeout industry is at a high point, with various platforms investing funds to collectively increase industry penetration. It is expected that in 3 years, the daily volume of takeout plus instant retail will exceed that of e-commerce. This trend is also evident in the data from Taobao Flash Sale. According to information released by Taobao Flash Sale, the number of non-catering orders has increased by as much as 179% year-on-year. Consumer purchasing habits have shown a significant shift under the influence of "6.18," no longer limited to catering but starting to use instant delivery for various items. With the continuous expansion of non-catering scenes in instant retail, SF Express will also have more opportunities to shine. It is reported that SF Express focuses on customized capacity for all scenarios, covering various long-distance, heavy-weight non-standard deliveries, and providing differentiated solutions for vertical categories such as supermarkets, pharmacies, and digital products. At the same time, through synergy with the SF Express ecosystem, they are creating an integrated supply chain of "warehousing + transfer + same-city instant delivery," providing one-stop fulfillment services from warehouse to warehouse, warehouse/store to consumer, to help more e-commerce brands transform and improve efficiency. In addition, with the continued efforts of e-commerce giants, SF Express believes that they have unique advantages. "Large customers are concerned about the sustainability of dividends, unwilling to be strongly tied to platforms, and more willing to use third-party cooperation to build product brands and develop private domains. We can solve the problem of service integrity in multi-platform operations. Middle-tier merchants can leverage platform traffic to increase exposure. The company will continue to accept orders from small and medium-sized merchants, forming a diverse order ecosystem, which is beneficial for the stability and activity of delivery riders." The person in charge mentioned, "The backend also provides delivery riders with a better running environment and choices. Through technological scheduling combined with human management, dispersed delivery riders can become an efficient system, and this 'knight culture' system is solidly implemented."

title_en: Zhao Baofeng lets the old taste stay on more people's taste buds (picture)
body_en: "Red Soil Braised Pork" is a long-standing Tianjin delicacy that takes 24 hours to prepare. It is described as "rich in sauce, fatty but not greasy, melts in the mouth, and leaves a lasting aftertaste." Zhao Baofeng, the fourth-generation inheritor of this dish who has dedicated 13 years to perfecting the craft, had his own dreams and profession before focusing on "Red Soil Braised Pork." He was not only a hot air balloon pilot in China but also a sailor. In 2012, he officially joined the production of "Red Soil Braised Pork," assisting his father Zhao Chenglin in expanding the production from a workshop to a factory, allowing this delicious Tianjin dish to reach beyond Tianjin. Behind the traditional flavor are the cultural memories of generations Reporter: Please introduce the historical origin of "Red Soil Braised Pork." Zhao Baofeng: My father, Zhao Chenglin, learned the craft from the second-generation inheritor Wei Shaoqi. According to Wei Shaoqi, "Red Soil Braised Pork" originated from a grand dish served at the 60th birthday banquet of Empress Dowager Cixi in the late Qing Dynasty. A chef in the imperial kitchen created this dish by meticulously cutting a piece of pork belly into the shape of the Chinese character "万" (meaning longevity) and steaming it until tender. The dish was then served with the skin side down and flipped onto a plate, presenting a vibrant color and a clear "万" character. Empress Dowager Cixi was delighted by the dish, praising its taste. After the fall of the Qing Dynasty, the chefs from the imperial kitchen scattered, and Wei Shaoqi's master, Zhang Youlin, learned the art of braised pork from a former imperial chef who had fled. Reporter: How did "Red Soil Braised Pork" develop? Zhao Baofeng: My father, Zhao Chenglin, started learning to make "Red Soil Braised Pork" at the age of 13 and has been in this profession for 60 years. In the 1990s, as society progressed and living standards improved, my father gained recognition for his skill in making "Red Soil Braised Pork." He boldly transformed and updated the traditional techniques, creating a unique flavor profile to cater to modern tastes, especially those of Tianjin locals. He developed a 18-step production process and insisted on using traditional methods like steaming with wood fire. Making a bowl of "Red Soil Braised Pork" takes 24 hours. The perfect dish should have a bright red color and a pure meaty aroma. My father adhered to the concept of green food production, packaging the product in vacuum-sealed frozen form to meet the demand for traditional flavors. The stylish gift box of "Red Soil Braised Pork" is convenient, affordable, and symbolizes auspiciousness, attracting a constant stream of buyers during traditional festivals. Reporter: How did "Red Soil Braised Pork" transition from a manual workshop to a modern factory? Zhao Baofeng: With the continuous development of the economy, my father's workshop "Zhaoji Braised Pork" could no longer meet the growing market demand, often facing shortages, especially during the Chinese New Year. Additionally, there was a need to improve food safety and hygiene standards. Therefore, my father and I established the "Zhao Chenglin (Tianjin) Food Co., Ltd." to produce "Red Soil Braised Pork" in a factory that meets national standards. We also registered the trademark "Zhao Chenglin Red Soil Braised Pork." It was during this time that I was officially recognized as the fourth-generation inheritor of "Red Soil Braised Pork." To upgrade the production of "Red Soil Braised Pork" from a workshop to a modern factory, my father and I went through hardships. The traditional techniques of making "Red Soil Braised Pork" and the technical standards of modern food production enterprises are quite different, sometimes conflicting. For example, the traditional method requires steaming with wood fire, but for environmental reasons, modern production processes cannot use wood fire. This difference in production methods affects the taste of the final product. This dilemma troubled my father, but with his years of experience and expertise, he devised a set of production equipment that met the requirements. We then collaborated with renowned food machinery manufacturers in Tianjin and Beijing to develop custom equipment. Using this equipment and new processes, we were able to produce a product that met modern food safety standards while preserving the original flavor. Staying true to the original intention Craftsmen should focus on their craft Reporter: After more than a decade of practice and exploration, what are your thoughts on the development of this intangible cultural heritage? Zhao Baofeng: Whether it tastes good and retains the traditional flavor, customers can tell with just one bite. We cannot be careless in production, ensuring that the ingredients are clean and using the best quality materials to interpret the traditional craftsmanship with ingenuity. While preserving traditional techniques, we must also keep up with the times in terms of promotion, market structure, and sales. In my opinion, the key is to focus on the product itself. Regardless of changing circumstances, we have certain rules, and the quality of the product speaks for itself. Ultimately, the core of braised pork lies in its fragrance. In our inheritance, we adhere to a return to nature and staying true to our original intentions, emphasizing that craftsmen should focus on their craft. Reporter: What are the biggest challenges encountered in the inheritance and development of this intangible cultural heritage? Zhao Baofeng: The most challenging part is preserving the original taste of the intangible cultural heritage. title_en: The world's attention/Hong Kong IPO gathers 5 trillion, ranking among the top in the world for 28 years.
body_en: In the past 28 years since Hong Kong's return to the motherland, the IPO market has also experienced 28 years of vigorous development. Data shows that in the past 28 years, the cumulative fundraising amount in the Hong Kong new stock market is about 5 trillion yuan, and the fundraising scale has long been among the top in the world, injecting strong vitality into the financial market. Chen Liang, Chairman of CICC, told Ta Kung Pao reporters that Hong Kong's significant achievements are not only due to the rapid rise of the mainland economy, but also to Hong Kong's active integration into the overall development of the country. He emphasized that in the long run, Hong Kong will still be the preferred platform for mainland companies to list overseas, and will continue to play an important role as a link between international capital and mainland assets. Ta Kung Pao reporter Jiang Quqiao "In the past 28 years, the fundraising scale of Hong Kong IPOs has always maintained a leading position in the global market, which is a remarkable achievement." Chen Liang evaluated the progress made by the Hong Kong IPO market. CICC has been deeply cultivating the Hong Kong market for many years and found that the hot development trend of the new stock market is inseparable from the combined effects of "institutional innovation," "international positioning," and "mainland economic dividends." In recent years, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange has successively introduced a number of reforms favorable to the IPO market, including allowing companies with a dual-class share structure to list in 2018. After the implementation of the reform, well-known companies such as Alibaba (09988), JD.com (09618), and Meituan (03690) have come to Hong Kong. In addition, the introduction of the Chapter 18A system allows biotechnology companies without profits to list, and the new Chapter 18C system targeting special technology companies in 2023. At the same time, the launch of the mutual market access mechanism has broken down barriers to the flow of funds between the mainland and Hong Kong, significantly improving market liquidity. Listing reforms facilitate innovative corporate financing Chen Liang concluded that the Hong Kong capital market, through continuous institutional innovation, has continuously expanded the inclusiveness of listings, becoming the preferred listing place for Chinese innovative companies. He pointed out that with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange continuously launching mechanisms such as Chapter 18C and "Science and Technology Enterprise Line" from 2023, the new stock market has entered a new development period, with not only a significant increase in the number of listed companies, but also continuous optimization of the structure. In addition to institutional reforms, Chen Liang believes that Hong Kong's deep international background has successfully attracted mainland companies and global capital to converge, which is also an important driving force for the development of the IPO market. He continued to say that Hong Kong's legal system is based on common law, and the regulatory rules of regulatory agencies follow international standards, highly aligning with global financial markets, making the Hong Kong market the preferred platform for mainland companies to go international and for global capital to invest in China. This year's fundraising data is 200 billion, returning to the top of the world "Among the approximately 2,600 listed companies in Hong Kong, 57% are mainland companies, and their total market value accounts for over 90%." Chen Liang frankly stated that the rapid growth of the mainland economy has nurtured a large number of strong and rapidly developing excellent companies, which are the important pillars of the Hong Kong capital market. He also mentioned that the listing of leading mainland companies in Hong Kong has attracted the attention of global investors, significantly enhancing the influence of the Hong Kong stock market. Looking back on the 28 years of development, the Hong Kong new stock market has experienced wind and rain, but has become more resilient. After experiencing the impact of the epidemic, the market has shown strong recovery momentum, and the fundraising scale has continued to improve since 2023. This year, the fundraising amount is expected to reach 200 billion yuan, returning to the top of the global fundraising rankings. Chen Liang believes that Hong Kong should fully leverage its own advantages in the future, continuously optimize the listing system, attract more high-quality companies from the mainland and overseas to list, and quickly fill in the current gaps to further enhance competitiveness.

title_en: Langfang Telecom escorts the silver-haired digital life.
body_en: Recently, Hebei Langfang Telecom went to the local elderly care center to carry out activities to assist and respect the elderly, bringing thoughtful services and heartfelt care to the elderly. At the event, the staff of the Langfang Telecom Love Wing Station quickly got involved in the service work. They provided free mobile phone screen protectors and cleaning services for the elderly, with every action being meticulous in order to provide the best user experience for the elderly. Faced with various problems encountered by the elderly in using their phones, the staff remained patient, answering and solving each one. Considering that the elderly generally have difficulty operating smartphones, the staff adopted a one-on-one software guidance approach, teaching the elderly how to use apps step by step. From WeChat video calls, sharing moments, to Alipay online payments, and utility bill payments, the staff provided detailed explanations and demonstrations, allowing the elderly to better enjoy the convenience brought by the smart era and bridge the "digital divide." While providing practical mobile phone services, anti-fraud education was also a key focus of this activity. The staff carefully selected classic anti-fraud videos, combined with real and common fraud cases in life, and used easy-to-understand language to explain common fraud methods and prevention techniques to the elderly. In order to deepen the understanding of anti-fraud knowledge, the love ambassadors also innovated in their approach, using scenario simulations and interactive quizzes to encourage active participation and discussion among the elderly. The successful organization of this event not only effectively improved the digital life skills of the elderly, enabling them to use smartphones more freely and enjoy the convenience of smart living, but also built a solid anti-fraud "firewall" within the elderly community, enhancing their awareness and self-protection abilities. Langfang Telecom will continue to deepen its services for the elderly, closely focusing on the actual needs of the elderly to carry out more diverse and content-rich activities, allowing the convenience of smart living to benefit more elderly people, and ensuring that the traditional virtues of respecting and caring for the elderly are passed down and promoted throughout society.

title_en: New Regulations Target Big Data "Price Discrimination"
body_en: Recently, the State Administration for Market Regulation and the Cyberspace Administration of China jointly issued the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Rules for Online Trading Platforms" (hereinafter referred to as the "Measures"). These Measures explicitly prohibit algorithmic abuse behaviors such as "data discrimination against old customers," a new regulatory policy that not only strengthens the institutional defense line for consumer rights protection but also fundamentally reshapes the profit logic that e-commerce platforms have long relied on from the ground up. Consumers have long suffered from "data discrimination against old customers"! Ms. Hu from Shaoxing, Zhejiang, booked a hotel using her Ctrip Diamond membership for 2889 yuan, while the hotel's actual listed price was only 1377.63 yuan. Ultimately, the People's Court of Keqiao District, Shaoxing City, ruled in judgment document (2021) Zhe0603 Minchu No. 10347 that Ctrip should "refund three times the price." In the typical cases of consumer rights protection published by the Jiangsu Provincial Higher People's Court in 2024, Ms. Zhu from Jiangsu found that when purchasing a four-piece bedding set on an e-commerce platform, the price for old users was 20% higher than for new users. These cases, judicially or officially recognized, are precisely the core pain points targeted by the "Measures." For a long time, "data discrimination against old customers" has become an important means for some e-commerce platforms to increase profits without incurring additional operating costs, relying on the obscurity of algorithms. Platforms analyze multi-dimensional data such as users' consumption habits, payment capacity, and device information to implement differentiated pricing for different users. Old users, often having higher trust and lower price sensitivity, become targets for "harvesting." This pricing model is essentially a disguised price fraud that exploits information asymmetry, yet it was once considered a low-cost, high-return profit shortcut by many platforms. At the same time, the issue of shrinking benefits in platform membership systems has become increasingly prominent. For example, some platforms unilaterally modify membership rules, leading to significant shrinkage of user rights and causing user dissatisfaction. Such unilateral modification of rules is one of the key aspects regulated by the "Measures." The implementation of the "Measures" directly cuts off this grey profit path, explicitly requiring platforms to disclose the basic logic of their algorithmic pricing, prohibit the use of data advantages to implement price discrimination, and stipulate that modifications to platform rules must be publicly announced 15 days in advance and user opinions solicited. Users who do not accept the changes can receive a full refund unconditionally. This means that profit models reliant on dynamic pricing algorithms and non-compliant adjustments to membership rules will become unsustainable. In the short term, the excess profits of OTAs and comprehensive e-commerce platforms that rely on price discrimination will be significantly reduced. However, from a regulatory practice perspective, this pressure is not unbearable. For instance, in platform-specific rectifications in some regions, the involved platforms not only did not experience a large-scale profit collapse after compliance rectification but also improved user retention rates due to improved reputation. This indicates that compliance is not the opposite of profitability. Under the pressure of the new regulations, a clear direction for the profit reconstruction of e-commerce platforms has emerged, focusing on shifting from "traffic harvesting" to "deep cultivation of value." On the one hand, platforms are forced to reduce their reliance on differentiated pricing and instead compress costs by optimizing supply chains and improving operational efficiency. For example, some platforms reduce merchant costs by integrating upstream supply chains and building digital logistics systems, achieving a win-win for platforms and merchants. On the other hand, standardized operation of membership systems is becoming a new profit breakthrough. The strict restrictions on membership rule adjustments in the "Measures" are driving platforms to shift from "profit through shrinking benefits" to "profit through value-added services." For instance, some platforms are driving the growth of paid user numbers by adding exclusive discounts, free door-to-door returns, and other benefits, confirming the pulling effect of high-quality value-added services on user willingness to pay. The new regulations bring not only adjustments to profit models but also the reshaping of the industry ecosystem. In the past, some platforms, leveraging their traffic monopoly, squeezed profits from upstream and downstream by forcing merchants into "exclusive choice" and setting unreasonable commissions. For example, a judicial ruling found that a certain platform penalized cross-platform merchants through technical means and was ultimately ordered to compensate for losses. The "Measures" explicitly prohibit such unfair competition behaviors, easing the burden on small and medium-sized merchants while also forcing platforms to abandon "monopolistic profits" and instead build core competitiveness through technological innovation and service optimization. It is worth noting that the increase in compliance costs will accelerate industry reshuffling. Leading platforms, with their technological and capital advantages, can complete algorithmic compliance modifications and business model upgrades more quickly. Small and medium-sized platforms that cannot adjust in time may face the risk of user loss and market elimination. In the long run, the new regulations against "data discrimination" are not a restriction on e-commerce platforms but an opportunity to promote high-quality industry development. The essence of the platform economy is a service-oriented economy that connects supply and demand, and its core profit should be based on improving transaction efficiency and creating consumer value. Platforms that respect consumer choice and adhere to compliance bottom lines will achieve more sustainable development. With the continuous upgrading of regulatory technology, the algorithm monitoring platform built by the State Administration for Market Regulation has achieved real-time monitoring of the pricing behavior of mainstream e-commerce platforms, and the "algorithm black box" will gradually be broken. This will prompt the entire industry to abandon low-price competition and routine competition, shifting towards benign competition centered on product quality, service experience, and technological innovation. For e-commerce platforms, actively embracing regulation and reconstructing profit logic is an inevitable choice. On the day the "Measures" were implemented, leading platforms such as Ctrip and Taobao issued algorithmic compliance statements, vowing to disclose pricing logic and establish channels for soliciting user opinions. These measures are both a response to the new regulations and a consideration for their own sustainable development. In the future, only by truly prioritizing user rights, creating core value through supply chain upgrades, service optimization, and technological innovation, can e-commerce platforms establish a firm foothold in the new industry landscape, and this is precisely the core essence of the new regulations in promoting the high-quality development of the platform economy. (Dong Run)

This pricing model is essentially a disguised price fraud that exploits information asymmetry, yet it was once considered a low-cost, high-return profit shortcut by many platforms. At the same time, the issue of shrinking benefits in platform membership systems has become increasingly prominent. For example, some platforms unilaterally modify membership rules, leading to significant shrinkage of user rights and causing user dissatisfaction. Such unilateral modification of rules is one of the key aspects regulated by the "Measures." The implementation of the "Measures" directly cuts off this grey profit path, explicitly requiring platforms to disclose the basic logic of their algorithmic pricing, prohibit the use of data advantages to implement price discrimination, and stipulate that modifications to platform rules must be publicly announced 15 days in advance and user opinions solicited. Users who do not accept the changes can receive a full refund unconditionally. This means that profit models reliant on dynamic pricing algorithms and non-compliant adjustments to membership rules will become unsustainable. In the short term, the excess profits of OTAs and comprehensive e-commerce platforms that rely on price discrimination will be significantly reduced. However, from a regulatory practice perspective, this pressure is not unbearable. For instance, in platform-specific rectifications in some regions, the involved platforms not only did not experience a large-scale profit collapse after compliance rectification but also improved user retention rates due to improved reputation. This indicates that compliance is not the opposite of profitability. Under the pressure of the new regulations, a clear direction for the profit reconstruction of e-commerce platforms has emerged, focusing on shifting from "traffic harvesting" to "deep cultivation of value." On the one hand, platforms are forced to reduce their reliance on differentiated pricing and instead compress costs by optimizing supply chains and improving operational efficiency. For example, some platforms reduce merchant costs by integrating upstream supply chains and building digital logistics systems, achieving a win-win for platforms and merchants. On the other hand, standardized operation of membership systems is becoming a new profit breakthrough. The strict restrictions on membership rule adjustments in the "Measures" are driving platforms to shift from "profit through shrinking benefits" to "profit through value-added services." For instance, some platforms are driving the growth of paid user numbers by adding exclusive discounts, free door-to-door returns, and other benefits, confirming the pulling effect of high-quality value-added services on user willingness to pay. The new regulations bring not only adjustments to profit models but also the reshaping of the industry ecosystem. In the past, some platforms, leveraging their traffic monopoly, squeezed profits from upstream and downstream by forcing merchants into "exclusive choice" and setting unreasonable commissions. For example, a judicial ruling found that a certain platform penalized cross-platform merchants through technical means and was ultimately ordered to compensate for losses. The "Measures" explicitly prohibit such unfair competition behaviors, easing the burden on small and medium-sized merchants while also forcing platforms to abandon "monopolistic profits" and instead build core competitiveness through technological innovation and service optimization. It is worth noting that the increase in compliance costs will accelerate industry reshuffling. Leading platforms, with their technological and capital advantages, can complete algorithmic compliance modifications and business model upgrades more quickly. Small and medium-sized platforms that cannot adjust in time may face the risk of user loss and market elimination. In the long run, the new regulations against "data discrimination" are not a restriction on e-commerce platforms but an opportunity to promote high-quality industry development. The essence of the platform economy is a service-oriented economy that connects supply and demand, and its core profit should be based on improving transaction efficiency and creating consumer value. Platforms that respect consumer choice and adhere to compliance bottom lines will achieve more sustainable development. With the continuous upgrading of regulatory technology, the algorithm monitoring platform built by the State Administration for Market Regulation has achieved real-time monitoring of the pricing behavior of mainstream e-commerce platforms, and the "algorithm black box" will gradually be broken. This will prompt the entire industry to abandon low-price competition and routine competition, shifting towards benign competition centered on product quality, service experience, and technological innovation. For e-commerce platforms, actively embracing regulation and reconstructing profit logic is an inevitable choice. On the day the "Measures" were implemented, leading platforms such as Ctrip and Taobao issued algorithmic compliance statements, vowing to disclose pricing logic and establish channels for soliciting user opinions. These measures are both a response to the new regulations and a consideration for their own sustainable development. In the future, only by truly prioritizing user rights, creating core value through supply chain upgrades, service optimization, and technological innovation, can e-commerce platforms establish a firm foothold in the new industry landscape, and this is precisely the core essence of the new regulations in promoting the high-quality development of the platform economy. (Dong Run)
sentiment_reason: New regulations have been introduced, cutting off profitable shortcuts for e-commerce platforms like Taobao and reducing their profits.

title_en: Meituan Buys Dingdong Maicai, Defense or Attack?
body_en: On February 5th, Meituan announced in a filing with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange that it has completed the acquisition of 100% of the equity in Dingdong Maicai's China business for an initial consideration of approximately US$717 million (approximately RMB 4.98 billion). Regarding the reasons for the acquisition, Meituan stated in its announcement that the company attaches great importance to the grocery retail business, and this transaction aligns with the company's long-term development plan in the grocery retail sector. As of September 2025, Dingdong Maicai operates over 1,000 front-end warehouses in China, with monthly active users exceeding 7 million. Dingdong Maicai's founder, Liang Changlin, also stated in an internal letter that for future development, he has chosen to let go of competition and transition to working shoulder-to-shoulder in cooperation. Regarding this acquisition, Ai Media Consulting CEO Zhang Yi told a reporter from Yicai Global that Dingdong Maicai's mature front-end warehouse model, its layout in the East China region, and its stable profitability have strategic value in complementing Meituan's shortcomings. Zhang Yi believes that fresh produce is the most essential and highest-frequency entry point for Meituan's instant retail strategy. Meituan's competitors, Alibaba and JD.com, are aggressively and forcefully expanding their presence in fresh produce instant retail through Hema and JD.com's 7Fresh respectively. This acquisition will enable Meituan to further integrate resources, create synergies with businesses like Xiaoxiang Supermarket and Meituan Shan Gou, and consolidate its fundamental position in the local lifestyle ecosystem. While all three are increasing their investment in fresh produce instant retail, JD.com, Alibaba, and Meituan each have different focuses in their business models. Zhuang Shuai, founder of Bailian Consulting, stated that JD.com's 7Fresh focuses on the supermarket format, Hema Supermarket and Julian are pursuing both discount and regular pricing strategies, and Meituan Xiaoxiang primarily focuses on front-end warehouses and is gradually developing into the supermarket format. Last year, all three companies made significant progress in the fresh produce instant retail sector. JD.com developed its front-end warehouse business through its 7Fresh stores. In 2023, JD.com integrated its 7Fresh physical stores and front-end warehouses. JD.com confirmed in March 2025 that it would open several new 7Fresh warehouse stores. As of January 2026, JD.com's 7Fresh had over 70 stores nationwide. The Alibaba group is developing its fresh produce instant retail business through the Hema brand. In August 2025, Hema officially announced plans to open nearly 100 Hema Fresh stores within the fiscal year, entering over 50 new cities, at which point the number of Hema Fresh stores would exceed 500. Hema announced in January 2026 that it entered 40 new cities last year. In terms of discount offerings, its discount store Hema NB was officially renamed "Chao Hesuan NB" in August last year, and as of December 31, 2025, it had over 400 stores nationwide. Meituan's Xiaoxiang Supermarket has been primarily based on the front-end warehouse model, until December 2025, when Xiaoxiang Supermarket opened its first offline store in Beijing. In terms of competitiveness, private labels and pricing remain key. Zhuang Shuai stated that differentiation in front-end warehouses is ongoing, with each company strengthening its private label and single-item advantages. For example, Hema has its private labels and Ri Ri Xian series, JD.com 7Fresh has its private labels and 24-hour series, and Meituan Xiaoxiang has its Xiang Da Chu series. In terms of pricing, 7Fresh frequently promotes products with "price-beating" campaigns, while Alibaba and Meituan have opened several offline discount stores. Therefore, despite Dingdong Maicai achieving profitability for several consecutive quarters, the pressure remains significant. In the previous fierce competition in fresh produce retail, Missfresh experienced a collapse. Although Dingdong survived and emerged victorious, achieving profitability for multiple quarters, its profits remain marginal, and the capital market has not been optimistic, with the company's market capitalization staying low, between US$500 million and US$700 million. In response, Chen Liteng, an analyst at the E-commerce Research Center of NetEase, believes this is a decision driven by multiple factors: the high fulfillment costs of the front-end warehouse model, difficulty in reducing fresh produce spoilage, and growth bottlenecks. At the same time, the fresh produce instant retail track has become a battleground for giants like Meituan and Hema, making it difficult for vertical platforms to compete, and their survival space is continuously being squeezed. Coupled with a sluggish capital market valuation and the demand for early investors to exit, the sale allows shareholders and the team to realize value. Furthermore, the high synergy with Meituan allows its business to be integrated into a larger ecosystem, maximizing resource utilization. title_en: State Council Information Office Holds Press Conference to Introduce the Situation of Market Regulation Serving High-Quality Economic Development
body_en: The State Council Information Office held a press conference at 10:00 AM on February 5, 2026 (Thursday). Deng Zhiyong, Deputy Director of the State Administration for Market Regulation and Director of the Standardization Administration of China, Yao Lei, Director of the Price Supervision and Anti-Unfair Competition Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation, Zhu Jianqiao, Director of the Network Transaction Supervision and Administration Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation, and Liu Hongsheng, Director of the Standards and Technology Management Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation, introduced the situation of market regulation serving high-quality economic development and answered questions from reporters. Jia Huili, Deputy Director of the Information Office of the State Council and spokesperson: Ladies and gentlemen, good morning. Welcome to the press conference of the State Council Information Office. Today, we have invited Mr. Deng Zhiyong, Deputy Director of the State Administration for Market Regulation and Director of the Standardization Administration of China, to introduce the situation of market regulation serving high-quality economic development and answer questions of public concern. Also attending today's press conference are Mr. Yao Lei, Director of the Price Supervision and Anti-Unfair Competition Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation, Mr. Zhu Jianqiao, Director of the Network Transaction Supervision and Administration Department, and Mr. Liu Hongsheng, Director of the Standards and Technology Management Department. Now, I invite Mr. Deng Zhiyong to make his introduction. Deng Zhiyong, Deputy Director of the State Administration for Market Regulation and Director of the Standardization Administration of China: Thank you, host. Friends from the media, good morning. I am very pleased to attend today's press conference with my colleagues. First of all, I would like to thank you for your long-term care and support for market regulation work. In 2025, under the strong leadership of the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping as the core, the national market regulation system adhered to the principles of "upholding political integrity, strengthening regulation, promoting development, and ensuring safety," made efforts to improve comprehensive market regulation capabilities, effectively maintained and promoted the formation of a strong domestic market, and achieved remarkable results in supporting economic growth and promoting high-quality development. First, the quality of business entity development has been continuously improved. Business entities are an important micro-foundation for economic recovery and upward trend. In recent years, we have always regarded serving the development of business entities as an important responsibility, continuously improved the market entry and exit mechanisms, deepened the reform of the subscribed capital registration system, vigorously promoted the reform of "efficiently accomplishing one thing" for enterprise relocation and transformation of individual industrial and commercial households into enterprises, optimized the processing procedures for high-frequency matters involving enterprises such as enterprise deregistration and credit repair, vigorously rectified prominent issues of arbitrary charges, strengthened the protection of intellectual property rights and trade secrets, and timely introduced a package of policies and measures to help and alleviate difficulties, helping business entities reduce burdens and increase efficiency. In 2025, 25.745 million new business entities were established nationwide, and the number of active enterprises in operation increased by 9.8% year-on-year, with their proportion of all enterprises increasing by 4.7 percentage points. Second, consumer rights and interests protection has become more robust. Creating a good market order for confident consumption is conducive to smoothing the circulation of supply and demand and releasing consumption potential. In recent years, we have resolutely investigated and punished prominent issues that infringe upon consumers' rights and interests in accordance with the law, focused on strengthening the capacity building for consumer rights protection, smoothed complaint and reporting channels, deeply implemented the three-year action plan to optimize the consumption environment, cultivated scenarios for confident consumption, and created a good consumption atmosphere. In 2025, the "Measures for Handling Complaints and Reports of Market Regulation" were revised. The market regulation system received a total of 26.46 million complaints and reports, recovered 4.35 billion yuan in economic losses for consumers, recalled 8.236 million consumer products throughout the year, and uniformly destroyed 3,683 tons of infringing, counterfeit, and shoddy goods. Third, the fair competition market environment has been continuously optimized. Fair competition is the basic principle of a market economy and an objective requirement for building a unified national market. In recent years, we have focused on strengthening the enforcement of anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition laws, promoted the breaking of local protectionism and market segmentation, and resolutely rectified behaviors such as using market dominance to squeeze the development space of other business entities. In 2025, we organized spot checks for fair competition reviews and urged relevant policy-making bodies to rectify policies and measures that hinder a unified market and fair competition; we investigated and dealt with a series of monopoly cases in the pharmaceutical field, promoting significant price reductions for the involved drugs; and we investigated and dealt with 14,600 cases of various types of unfair competition. Comprehensive rectification of "involutionary" competition, strengthening cost surveys, price inspections, and interviews and guidance for key enterprises, effectively promoted the timely cooling down of "price wars" and "subsidy wars." Fourth, the construction of quality infrastructure is more adapted to industrial needs. High standards lead to high quality, and accurate measurement leads to exquisite manufacturing. Metrology, standards, inspection and testing, and certification and accreditation are important foundations for building a modern industrial system. In recent years, we have fully leveraged the supporting role of quality and the guiding role of standards, vigorously promoted the construction of quality-strong enterprises, quality-strong industrial chains, and quality-strong counties, and continuously carried out quality and technology research and development. In 2025, 21 key technical bottlenecks in industrial chains were broken through, and 71 quality and technical gaps urgently needed by industries were filled; 14 national metrology bases and 1,139 types of national standard materials were newly established; 4,929 national standards were issued, an increase of 56% year-on-year; and 20 key projects for inspection and testing to promote industrial optimization and upgrading were completed, effectively supporting the improvement of the resilience and safety of industrial and supply chains. Fifth, important progress has been made in the governance of the platform economy ecosystem. China has been the world's largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years. The quality of the platform economy ecosystem directly affects the income of businesses, the interests of practitioners, and the rights and interests of consumers. In recent years, we have continuously improved the institutionalized regulation of the platform economy and focused on promoting win-win development among all parties. In 2025, in conjunction with the Cyberspace Administration of China, we issued the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Network Transaction Platform Rules" and the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Live E-commerce," focusing on creating a fairer, more transparent, and trustworthy online trading ecosystem. In conjunction with relevant departments, we carried out special rectifications of prominent problems in the platform economy, effectively rectifying issues such as abuse of rules, unreasonable fees, false marketing, and lack of algorithmic transparency. Sixth, the overall safety situation in the market regulation field is stable. Ensuring the safety of people's lives and property is the top priority of market regulation. In recent years, we have adhered to coordinating development and security, continuously increased the intensity of supervision over food, drug, industrial product, and special equipment safety, and focused on preventing and resolving risks and hidden dangers. In 2025, the non-compliance rate of national food safety spot checks was 2.74%, and the number of enterprises with non-compliant batches of samples decreased by 57% year-on-year; the pass rate of national drug spot checks remained above 99%; in the national supervision and spot checks of industrial product quality, the non-compliance rate of 16 products decreased by more than 10 percentage points. In the next step, we will conscientiously implement the decisions and deployments of the Party Central Committee and the State Council, deeply promote the construction of a unified national market, vigorously stimulate the vitality of various market entities, accelerate the improvement of quality and technology infrastructure capabilities, effectively prevent and resolve safety risks in key areas, and strive to promote effective qualitative improvement and reasonable quantitative growth of the economy, contributing market regulation strength to achieve a good start for the "15th Five-Year Plan." I have briefly introduced the above situation. Next, my colleagues and I will have further exchanges with you. Thank you. Jia Huili: Thank you for your introduction. Now we enter the question-and-answer session. Before asking questions, please announce the news agency you represent. Please raise your hands. Reporter from Jiemu News: Currently, China is continuously increasing its efforts to boost consumption. We have noticed that the State Administration for Market Regulation led the three-year action to optimize the consumption environment in 2025. May I ask about the progress of this action? Thank you. Deng Zhiyong: Thank you for your question. I will answer it. The Central Economic Work Conference emphasized adhering to domestic demand as the primary driver and building a strong domestic market. The State Administration for Market Regulation has always regarded optimizing the consumption environment as an important initiative to boost consumption. The three-year action to optimize the consumption environment was launched in 2025 and has achieved phased results. In terms of stimulating consumption potential, we have released over 210 national standards for major consumer goods such as home appliances, furniture, and clothing, as well as service consumption such as sports fitness, cultural tourism, and catering. We have formulated and promoted a standard system for elderly care services, a quality evaluation system for tourism services, a quality evaluation model for automobile maintenance services, and a credit system for domestic services, continuously improving service quality. Relevant departments have built 19.325 million charging infrastructure facilities, 30,000 commercial logistics and distribution outlets in counties, townships, and villages, and 8,132 "15-minute convenient living circles," constantly enriching consumption scenarios. In terms of addressing consumption pain points, we have deployed the "Iron Fist" action to protect consumers, focusing on investigating and punishing illegal acts such as the quality and safety of children's toys, illegal modification of electric bicycles, trademark infringement in e-commerce, "overlord clauses," and "ghost takeout" that have aroused strong public phản hồi. We have vigorously investigated cases of inferior down jackets being sold as superior ones, the production and sale of counterfeit and shoddy fuel appliances, and conducted concentrated law enforcement actions on measurement cheating at gas stations, investigating and dealing with 72,000 related cases. Focusing on reducing consumption risks, we recalled 8.236 million consumer products and 1.398 million power banks. We investigated and dealt with 1,932 cases of online unfair competition, with fines totaling 71.529 million yuan. In terms of improving the consumption experience, we jointly launched the "Return and Exchange Initiative for Different Stores in Different Locations," publicly posted 214,000 offline units that offer unconditional returns on consumption inquiry platforms, revised and issued the "Measures for Handling Complaints and Reports of Market Regulation," improved administrative mediation procedures, enhanced the effectiveness of consumer rights protection, and regulated malicious claims and abuse of systems. We formulated the "Guiding Opinions on Deeply Promoting the Resolution of Consumption Disputes" to promote diversified resolution of consumption disputes. The national 12315 complaint and public announcement platform's disclosure rate rose to 98.4%. Many places are exploring the public disclosure of complaint information on public electronic screens in consumption gathering areas, reducing consumption disputes at the source. In the next step, the State Administration for Market Regulation will use the construction of confident consumption clusters as a carrier, issue policy documents such as confident consumption standards and the cultivation of confident consumption entities, and cultivate a large number of confident business districts, confident markets, and confident scenic spots with broad influence and high visibility, making them tangible and accessible to consumers. We welcome all sectors of society to participate in the construction of the consumption environment and work together to build confident consumption brands. Thank you. Reporter from China Media Group: Currently, the unified national market still faces problems of local protectionism and administrative monopolies. How will you precisely address these issues in the next step? Thank you. Yao Lei, Director of the Price Supervision and Anti-Unfair Competition Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation: Thank you for your question. I will answer it. The Central Economic Work Conference emphasized the need to deeply promote the construction of a unified national market. We deeply recognize that transforming China's super-large market advantage into a driving force for high-quality development requires not only establishing sound institutional rules but also vigorously breaking down local protectionism and promptly correcting improper market competition interventions, thereby breaking through the bottlenecks and blockages that restrict economic circulation. In the past year, the State Administration for Market Regulation carried out a special campaign to rectify the abuse of power to eliminate and restrict competition, with a year-on-year increase of 34% in cases filed for investigation and 32% in concluded cases. Market regulation departments at all levels have reviewed important policy measures intended to be issued by their respective local governments, modifying and adjusting over 12,000 items, effectively ensuring that relevant major policy measures comply with the requirements of a unified national market and fair competition, and making government behavior more standardized. By dismantling the "fence," we can build "expressways." This year, in breaking down local protectionism and administrative monopolies, we will focus on three aspects: In terms of strict law enforcement and case handling, we will organize special campaigns to concentrate on investigating a batch of key cases, promote the abolition of a batch of regulations and practices that hinder a unified national market and fair competition, and comprehensively improve the quality and efficiency of anti-monopoly law enforcement against the abuse of administrative power to eliminate and restrict competition. We will accurately identify prominent problems and urge rectification, strengthen punishment and deterrence for serious violations, and maintain a high-pressure stance. We will strengthen inter-regional collaboration and professional support, solidify local case-handling responsibilities, and further enhance the accuracy and effectiveness of law enforcement. In terms of strengthening source governance, we will deeply implement the "Regulations on Fair Competition Review," study and revise supporting implementation measures, improve the review mechanism for important policy measures, strictly limit the application of exceptions, and resolutely prevent the issuance of policies and measures that eliminate or restrict competition. We will increase personnel training and accelerate the empowerment of digital technology to further improve the standardization and normalization of review. We will continue to conduct spot checks of policies and measures, properly handle fair competition review complaints, strengthen supervision and constraints, and promote the deep implementation of the system. In terms of emphasizing compliance construction, we will fully leverage the role of the State Council's Anti-Monopoly and Anti-Unfair Competition Commission Office, strengthen cross-departmental risk consultation and information sharing, and enhance policy synergy. We will focus on key areas to proactively strengthen compliance guidance, provide regular risk warnings, and timely disseminate enforcement cases, issue work suggestions, and provide compliance reminders. We will continue to increase the exposure of fair competition enforcement cases, clarify red lines and bottom lines, and use cases to explain the law and promote governance. Recently, we have launched the China Anti-Monopoly New Media Platform, which regularly publishes important activities, policy interpretations, and case information in the anti-monopoly field. We welcome media friends to pay attention. Let us consolidate the consensus and synergy of the whole society in maintaining fair competition, and create a healthy market ecosystem of shared opportunities and common growth. Thank you. Reporter from China Business News: Optimizing the implementation of policies related to "two new" (new industries, new business models) is an important task. How does the State Administration for Market Regulation assist in the implementation of these "two new" policies? What are the next steps? Thank you. Liu Hongsheng, Director of the Standards and Technology Management Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation: Thank you for your question. I will answer it. In 2025, the State Administration for Market Regulation deeply implemented the "National Standardization Development Outline" and effectively carried out the task deployment of the "two new" actions, accelerating the construction of a standard system supporting high-quality development, and achieving positive results. First, accelerate the upgrading of production-side standards. Focusing on the integrated application of emerging technologies and the upgrading of traditional industries, we have issued 174 standards, contributing to the improvement of quality and efficiency in industries and enterprises. Second, iterate and update consumption-side standards. Focusing on consumer goods trade-in, expanding service consumption, and housing renovation, we have issued 230 standards, promoting the improvement of product, service, and engineering quality, and accelerating the expansion of personal and household consumption upgrades. Third, expand the supply of mandatory standards. In standardization work, for standards involving key areas such as health, safety, and environmental protection, we strive to increase the implementation and application of mandatory standards, which we call "strengthen where possible, and strengthen where it should be strengthened." According to this principle, we have accelerated the issuance of 113 mandatory national standards by newly formulating a batch, upgrading a batch, and converting some recommended standards to mandatory ones, continuously strengthening the rigid constraints of standards. Fourth, accelerate the improvement of recycling and utilization standards. Focusing on the entire chain of the circular economy industry, including the trading of second-hand products, product recycling and utilization, and the use of recycled materials, we have issued 66 national standards, accelerating the establishment of a standard system for circular utilization and promoting the high-quality development of the resource recycling industry. The Central Economic Work Conference has made new deployments for the optimized implementation of "two new" policies in 2026. The State Administration for Market Regulation will focus on optimizing and upgrading traditional industries, promoting high-quality and efficient development of the service industry, and vigorously boosting consumption, and will plan and carry out a series of new special actions: First, promote the upgrading of traditional industry standards. Focusing on the high-quality development needs of ten major traditional industries such as petrochemicals, machinery, light industry, steel, non-ferrous metals, building materials, textiles, shipbuilding, automobiles, and electricity, we will adhere to the direction of intelligence, greening, and integration, promote the revision of standards, and assist in the transformation and development of industries. Second, promote the upgrading of consumer goods standards. Focusing on consumers' new demands for safety, quality, greenness, intelligence, and health, we will formulate a work plan for accelerating the upgrading of national standards for consumer goods, and strive to build a new consumer goods standard system that is compatible with high-quality development, providing strong fundamental support for increasing the supply-demand adaptability of consumer goods and stimulating consumption potential. Third, strengthen the construction of service standards. We will research and issue guiding opinions on strengthening the construction of service standards, focusing on the urgent needs of key areas such as producer services, lifestyle services, and public services, strengthening the construction of standards in traditional and emerging service fields, and promoting the high-quality and efficient development of the service industry. Fourth, increase the efforts in developing mandatory standards. We will promote a special action for the implementation and upgrading of mandatory national standards, increase the supply of mandatory standards related to life and property safety, and promptly convert recommended standards in important fields into mandatory national standards, effectively building a defense line for safety-related standards. Thank you. Reporter from 21st Century Business Herald: In recent years, the platform economy has developed rapidly. New business formats such as live e-commerce and food delivery have greatly facilitated people's lives, but there are also problems such as selling inferior goods as superior ones, passing off fakes as genuine, and irrational competition. Could you introduce the key work in platform economy governance and how you will focus on governance in the next step? Thank you. Zhu Jianqiao, Director of the Network Transaction Supervision and Administration Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation: I will answer this question. First, thank you for your attention to platform economy governance. The State Council Information Office held a press conference at 10:00 AM on February 5, 2026 (Thursday). Welcome to the press conference of the State Council Information Office. Today, we have invited Mr. Deng Zhiyong, Deputy Director of the State Administration for Market Regulation and Director of the Standardization Administration of China, to introduce the situation of market regulation serving high-quality economic development and answer questions of public concern. Now, I invite Mr. Deng Zhiyong to make his introduction. In 2025, 25.745 million new business entities were established nationwide, and the number of active enterprises in operation increased by 9.8% year-on-year, with their proportion of all enterprises increasing by 4.7 percentage points. In conjunction with relevant departments, we carried out special rectifications of prominent problems in the platform economy, effectively rectifying issues such as abuse of rules, unreasonable fees, false marketing, and lack of algorithmic transparency. title_en: International Olympic Committee Officially Announced in Milan! Olympic Games "Solely" Selects Alibaba Cloud's Qwen
body_en: Original Title: IOC Officially Announces at Milan Event! Olympic Games "Solely" Selects Tongyi Qianwen February 5, 2026, Milan. On the eve of the Winter Olympics opening, IOC President Coventry officially announced the organization's decision: to build the first "Official Large Model" in Olympic history based on China's Tongyi Qianwen large model. Photo: IOC President Kirsty Coventry announces the creation of the first official large model in Olympic history based on the Tongyi Qianwen large model. The significance of this matter lies not in who is "stamping" whom, but in the fact that China's AI, after years of engineering refinement, has achieved the capability to support cross-lingual, cross-time zone, and highly reliable global services, and can now undergo rigorous testing in extreme scenarios like the Olympic Games. For some time now, Alibaba's Tongyi Qianwen large model has been continuously "in demand" globally. Domestically, Tongyi Qianwen has served over 1 million clients, including major enterprises and institutions such as the Chinese Academy of Sciences, China Construction Bank, and XPeng. Internationally, Meta and Fei-Fei Li's team have chosen to "distill" Alibaba's open-source Tongyi Qianwen model to aid in the development of their own large models. This time, Alibaba's Tongyi Qianwen delving into Olympic scenarios represents an expansion and validation of its capabilities under a higher standard system. "Chinese Technology" Behind a Century of Olympics This selection is not accidental, but a "mutual embrace" born from foresight. As early as last November, when Coventry visited China for the first time as the newly appointed IOC President, he visited Alibaba and met with CEO Eddie Wu. title_en: From "Data Governance" to "Data Intelligence"
body_en: With the advent of the large model democratization trend sparked by DeepSeek, base models with converging functionalities are finding it difficult to establish differentiated advantages. High-quality data is replacing model selection as the core competitiveness in AI. Against this backdrop, data management is no longer merely an IT infrastructure tool but a critical hub for AI value creation. Successful data enterprises must deeply integrate into the AI value chain, transitioning from "data governance" to "data intelligence." Since the rise of generative AI in 2023, the valuations of U.S. data companies Scale AI and Databricks have increased by 98.0% and 109.3% respectively over two years, and Palantir's stock price has surged by 912.2%, attracting significant attention from data industry participants and investors. Leading overseas data enterprises, represented by these companies, are building new competitive advantages in the AI era by extending to full-stack AI services based on industry pain points, reshaping product forms with AI-native workflows, and expanding industry value boundaries through new business models. Development Paths of Three Leading Data Enterprises Despite divergent technical paths, leading companies such as Scale AI, Databricks, and Palantir have all achieved deep integration of AI and data, successfully translating their technological advantages into commercial success. Scale AI has transformed from data labeling services to providing AI infrastructure. Founded in 2016, Scale AI aims to provide more refined and efficient services and high-quality data for companies in areas like autonomous driving, using its proprietary toolchain and machine learning-assisted pre-labeling, which is superior to traditional manual labeling. For instance, as early as 2021, Scale AI increased Toyota's labeling efficiency tenfold within weeks through AI-assisted labeling. Around 2022, Scale AI gradually expanded from data labeling services to full-stack AI services based on enterprise data platforms, serving government and enterprise clients throughout the entire process from AI data governance to the deployment and commercial closed-loop of generative AI applications. For example, its large model decision-making platform, Donovan, integrates multi-source intelligence to generate combat recommendations and has been adopted by the U.S. Department of Defense, elevating the company from a data supplier to an AI infrastructure provider. After receiving investment from Meta in June 2025, its valuation exceeded $29 billion. Databricks has upgraded from a data storage platform to an intelligent data governance platform. Founded in 2013, Databricks aims to address data silos and redundant migration issues in traditional architectures, helping clients tackle challenges such as multimodal data processing, real-time capabilities, and governance. For example, in 2020, it launched the innovative Lakehouse data technology architecture, combining the openness of data lakes with the structured functionality of data warehouses, and applied it to its native execution engine product, Delta Engine. At its launch, it significantly reduced query execution time by 91.1% and costs by 63.4% to 90.2% compared to mainstream cloud data warehouses on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud at the time. By the end of 2023, Databricks revolutionized data management by using AI models to deeply understand the semantics of enterprise data, building the Data Intelligence Platform on its data lakehouse. At that time, it was the only company in the industry with a unified governance layer across data and AI, and a unified query engine covering ETL, SQL, machine learning, and business intelligence. In 2024, its annual recurring revenue reached $3.04 billion. In early 2024, its data intelligence communication platform, launched for telecommunications operators, unified over 60 data sources for U.S. wireless operator T-Mobile, including supply chain fraud detection, order tracking, and expenditure management, reducing business analysis failure rates from 40% to nearly 0%, becoming the foundation of the company's technical architecture. Palantir has extended from data analysis and decision-making tools to a "Data + AI" one-stop solution. Founded in 2003, Palantir initially provided government and enterprises with its correlation analysis and decision-making platforms, Gotham and Foundry, which map complex data into business relationship networks, excelling in ontology modeling as its core technology. For instance, Pacific Gas and Electric Company used Foundry to build a comprehensive operational picture of its power grid, enabling the prediction and identification of wildfire risks within a 25,000-mile power line network, reducing the area burned by wildfires by 99%. In 2023, Palantir officially launched its "Data + AI" one-stop solution, AIP, allowing users to leverage large language models for various tasks and ad-hoc analysis, interacting with documents and intelligent assistants equipped with enterprise-specific information and tools without complex setup or technical expertise. In 2024, its annual recurring revenue reached $2.87 billion. For example, U.S. restaurant chain Wendy's utilized AIP's capabilities to automate inventory management and resource allocation decision-making processes, tracking orders and inventory in real-time for 6,500 restaurants and resolving issues that previously took weeks in just five minutes. Common Secrets to Success and Industry Implications While the development trajectories of Scale AI, Databricks, and Palantir appear different, they share three underlying logics that point the way forward for data enterprises in the AI era. First, they focus on core industry pain points and gradually extend to full-stack AI services. Leading companies do not stop at the tool level. While addressing fundamental issues in AI implementation such as the difficulty of acquiring high-quality data, the separation of data and AI processes, and the challenge of integrating AI applications with business knowledge, they have progressively enhanced their full-stack AI development capabilities. For example, Scale AI addresses data scarcity in high-value scenarios like autonomous driving through AI-assisted labeling and crowdsourcing. Databricks enables seamless collaboration between data and AI teams by unifying storage and computation with its Lakehouse architecture and connecting experimentation and deployment with its data intelligence platform. Palantir encodes industry rules into machine-readable logic through ontology modeling, ensuring AI outputs provide action recommendations that align with business context. Currently, all three have developed multifunctional tools and services around the entire AI development process. Second, they actively embrace AI-native workflows and reshape product forms. Traditional data management tools are mostly "passively responsive" to demands, whereas the AI era requires platforms to proactively empower intelligent applications. For instance, Scale AI's synthetic data generation, Databricks' natively integrated AI/BI GENIE natural language conversational business analysis tool on its platform, and Palantir's natural language question-answering capabilities all embody an "AI-first" design philosophy. They not only manage data but also allow data to directly drive intelligent behavior, achieving a leap from "support systems" to "value creation engines." Third, they explore new business models and expand industry value boundaries. Breaking free from the limitations of traditional one-time licensing or simple resource tool sales, leading data enterprises have experimented with revenue mechanisms that better align with customers' continuous value creation needs in the AI era, focusing on business outcomes and long-term partnerships. For example, Scale AI pioneered a subscription model of "Data as a Service + AI Infrastructure," charging based on data volume and call frequency, fostering long-term customer relationships. Databricks implements an "open core + cloud service revenue sharing" model, building an ecosystem through open source, with cloud revenue feeding back into R&D. Palantir adopts a "high-stickiness customization + results-based payment" approach, achieving high gross margins in high-value scenarios such as government and finance. These models transcend traditional software licensing, align more closely with customer success, and open up avenues for growth. (Author's affiliation: China Telecom Research Institute)
