title_en: Promote the innovative and healthy development of the platform economy
body_en: [Learning, Thinking, Practicing, and Comprehending] The platform economy, as a vital component of the digital economy, serves as a crucial engine for developing new quality productive forces and a key hub for facilitating both domestic and international dual circulation. The innovation capabilities and governance levels of the platform economy significantly influence China's voice in the global digital competition landscape. Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Party Central Committee, with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, has attached great importance to the development of the platform economy, making a series of major decisions and deployments. The "Proposals of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Formulating the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development and the Long-Range Objectives Through to 2035," deliberated and adopted at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee, proposed to "promote the innovative and healthy development of the platform economy." The Central Economic Work Conference held in December 2025 emphasized "promoting the win-win development of platform enterprises, operators within platforms, and laborers." This series of top-level designs and strategic arrangements clarifies the development positioning of the platform economy on the new journey and points the way forward for enhancing its development level and improving its ecosystem governance. I In recent years, China's platform economy has flourished, with its status and role in the overall economic and social development becoming increasingly prominent. China has ranked as the world's largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years. According to data from the National Bureau of Statistics, in 2025, online retail sales of physical goods nationwide grew by 5.2%, contributing 36.2% to the total retail sales of consumer goods. However, it is worth noting that with the rapid penetration of artificial intelligence technology into various industries, the platform economy, while demonstrating immense development potential, is also facing a series of new challenges in terms of innovation capabilities and governance levels. From an innovation perspective, China's platform economy has led the world in business model innovation and the expansion of application scenarios. In areas such as e-commerce, mobile payments, and instant delivery, a number of platform enterprises with global influence have emerged. However, breakthroughs in key technological fields such as underlying algorithms and high-performance chips are still needed. Furthermore, the innovation ecosystem of the platform economy needs to be improved, particularly as the threshold for participation by small and medium-sized enterprise developers is high, which to some extent limits the breadth and depth of platform economy innovation. Therefore, it is imperative to guide platform enterprises to increase investment in "hard technology" fields, strengthen the construction of the platform innovation ecosystem, and enhance the independent controllability of core technologies, thereby comprehensively improving the innovation capacity and global competitiveness of China's platform economy. From a governance perspective, the platform economy has played an important supporting role in stabilizing employment and promoting consumption. However, there are also issues such as the tendency towards "involution" in market competition and the lag of platform governance systems behind the iteration of new business formats. For example, some platform enterprises are trapped in homogeneous competition, relying excessively on "price wars" to compete for existing users rather than creating incremental value through technological innovation. This vicious "involution" can easily lead to an imbalance in profit distribution within the industrial chain and severely squeeze the survival space of small, medium, and micro businesses. In addition, new business formats such as AI digital human live streaming e-commerce and autonomous driving are emerging one after another, often falling into a "grey area" of regulation. At the same time, issues such as "information cocoons" caused by algorithm black boxes and "algorithmic control" over laborers also occur from time to time, posing risks to social ethics and data security. Therefore, it is imperative to build a governance system that is compatible with the development of the platform economy in the era of artificial intelligence. While leaving sufficient room for the development of new business formats and models, it is necessary to create an open, fair, and healthy platform economy ecosystem by improving laws and regulations and innovating regulatory means. II In the face of new situations and challenges, accelerating the innovative and healthy development of the platform economy requires grasping the dynamic relationship between stimulating innovation vitality and establishing a regulated order. It necessitates coordinated efforts from multiple dimensions, including technological capabilities, regulatory mechanisms, and international cooperation, to guide the development focus of the platform economy towards "value co-creation" and build a new pattern of platform economy development that is more resilient and competitive. Leveraging the primary role of platform enterprises in tackling key core technologies to unleash the innovation vitality of the platform economy. On the one hand, focusing on cutting-edge fields, support platform enterprises in forming innovation consortia with universities and research institutes. Through joint establishment of laboratories and pilot bases, concentrate efforts on "bottleneck" areas such as artificial intelligence chips, underlying algorithms, and operating systems to achieve major breakthroughs in key common technologies and frontier leading technologies. On this basis, optimize the incentive mechanism for technological innovation, encourage leading platform enterprises to increase investment in basic research and original innovation through forms such as "innovation vouchers" and "computing power vouchers," so that the platform economy becomes a "source" and "testing ground" for key core technologies. On the other hand, deepen the "integration of physical and digital," and promote the radiation of high-tech achievements to small, medium, and micro enterprises. By guiding platform enterprises and manufacturing enterprises to jointly build an innovation ecosystem, construct an open-source repository of data, models, and tools, and promote the improvement of mechanisms for the transformation of open-source achievements and intellectual property protection, stimulate the enthusiasm of all parties to participate in technological innovation. At the same time, develop a multi-level industrial Internet platform system of "professional + industry + collaborative" type, encourage platform enterprises to open technical interfaces and data resources, develop "small, light, fast, and accurate" digital and intelligent solutions for small and medium-sized enterprises, and promote integrated innovation among upstream and downstream of the industrial chain and large, medium, and small enterprises. Improving the normalized regulatory mechanism to enhance the governance capacity of the platform economy. On the one hand, establish and improve a dynamic and agile ex-ante prevention mechanism. Continuously improve relevant laws and regulations for the platform economy, clarify the primary responsibilities of platform enterprises in data security, consumer rights protection, and market competition, and strengthen compliance review of key aspects such as market access, data collection and use, and algorithm recommendation for platform enterprises. Focusing on key issues such as monopolistic behavior and unfair competition, establish a real-time risk assessment model to achieve dynamic monitoring and risk early warning of platform enterprises' business operations, data security, and market competition, thereby improving the accuracy and foresight of regulation. Leverage the role of the National Technical Committee for Standardization of Platform Economy Governance, accelerate the formulation and improvement of industry standards for platform compliance, product quality, and service safety, guide platform enterprises to establish internal compliance review systems, and unblock channels for consumers and laborers to protect their rights, forming a governance closed loop of "government sets rules, platforms adhere to bottom lines, and society jointly supervises." On the other hand, strengthen the penetrative regulatory mechanism empowered by technology. Relying on technological means such as big data, artificial intelligence, and blockchain, build a regulatory data sharing platform that spans departments, levels, and regions. Through in-depth mining and penetrative analysis of platform enterprises' transaction data, user behavior data, and algorithm model operation data, accurately identify hidden illegal behaviors such as abnormal transactions, data abuse, and algorithmic discrimination in the operation of the platform economy. At the same time, for new intelligent technology industries such as intelligent connected vehicles and robots, explore the establishment of regulatory mechanisms such as "sandbox regulation" and "trigger-based regulation," and provide platform enterprises with sufficient innovation space and necessary trial-and-error space while strictly adhering to the safety bottom line. Supporting platform enterprises to "go global" at a high level to enhance the international competitiveness of the platform economy. On the one hand, encourage platform enterprises to actively expand overseas markets by leveraging their technological R&D advantages and model innovation experience. By deeply participating in the construction of digital infrastructure and digital economy cooperation projects in countries along the Belt and Road Initiative, export mature technical solutions and service standards in areas such as cross-border e-commerce, cloud services, online payments, and digital content, and cultivate a number of multinational platform enterprises with global influence. On the other hand, encourage platform enterprises to participate in the formulation of international digital rules on cross-border data flow, digital economy taxation, and data ownership, and contribute wisdom and solutions to global issues such as digital taxation, artificial intelligence governance, and anti-monopoly. At the same time, support domestic platform enterprises in conducting in-depth cooperation with top global research institutions and technology companies. Through technology licensing, patent sharing, and joint R&D, promote domestic platform enterprises to actively integrate into the global innovation network, continuously expand a mutually beneficial digital development ecosystem, and enhance the position and voice of China's platform economy in the global industrial chain and innovation chain. (Authors: Hu Qing and Wang Jiexian, researchers at the Zhejiang Provincial Academy of Governance and the "Eight-Eight Strategy" Innovation and Development Research Institute of the Zhejiang Provincial Party School, and Vice Dean of the School of Business Administration of Zhejiang Gongshang University, respectively.)

title_en: Business Record
body_en: AI Marketing Investment Exceeds 10 Billion Yuan During Spring Festival Event: Around the Spring Festival of the Year of the Horse, AI products such as Tencent Yuanbao, ByteDance Doubao, and Alibaba Qianwen collectively launched marketing campaigns, with an estimated total investment exceeding 10 billion yuan. Specifically, Tencent Yuanbao launched a 1 billion yuan cash red envelope event and a "Yuanbao Pai" AI social feature. Alibaba Qianwen launched the "Spring Festival Treat Plan" centered around "free meals, drinks, and entertainment." ByteDance Doubao secured exclusive cooperation with CCTV's Spring Festival Gala and gave away over 100,000 tech gifts and cash red envelopes. Commentary: During the Spring Festival, companies' substantial marketing investments quickly translated into traffic. Driven by various strategies, Yuanbao, Doubao, and Qianwen all set new records for daily and monthly active users, entering the "AI Native App Billion-User Club." As the marketing campaigns concluded, the active user numbers and rankings of AI products generally declined. Industry insiders believe that the value of large-scale marketing during the Spring Festival lies in popularizing AI applications to a wider audience, rather than fundamentally changing the landscape of the AI application market. However, with mobile internet traffic reaching its peak, manufacturers have had to engage in this marketing war to gain an advantage in the future competition for AI entry points. As the marketing war subsides and user needs return to real-world scenarios, retaining users has become a challenge for AI manufacturers. In fact, to make users accustomed to and continuously use AI, it is essential to accurately identify their real needs and provide targeted services. This means that in the next phase, the ability to achieve more outstanding performance in terms of functional iteration and experience optimization will largely determine whether the investments made by AI manufacturers during the Spring Festival can translate into higher "cost-effectiveness." Multiple Innovative Drug Companies Achieve Profitability in 2025 Event: According to statistics from securities institutions, as of February 27th, among the 24 innovative drug companies that have released their performance forecasts, 19 achieved positive year-on-year growth in net profit attributable to the parent company. Among them, BeiGene, Ltd. achieved full-year profitability for the first time in 2025, with a net profit attributable to the parent company of 1.422 billion yuan. Shenzhen Chipscreen Biosciences Co., Ltd. achieved a net profit attributable to the parent company of 51.0757 million yuan in 2025, turning losses into profits. Shanghai Yizhong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. achieved a net profit attributable to the parent company of 64.132 million yuan in 2025, a year-on-year increase of 819.42%. Commentary: Domestic innovative drug companies are reaching a turning point in profitability, driven in large part by the continuous release of benefits from medical insurance policies. Last year, 114 new drugs were added to the National Medical Insurance Catalog, 50 of which were Class 1 innovative drugs. The cycle from approval to inclusion in medical insurance for innovative drugs has significantly shortened, accelerating the commercialization of pharmaceutical companies' products. On the other hand, the continuous warming of overseas business development (BD) collaborations by domestic innovative drug companies also contributes to performance realization. Data shows that in 2025, the total value of China's innovative drug overseas licensing transactions exceeded 130 billion US dollars, with over 150 licensing transactions, setting a new historical record. High-quality BD collaborations can not only significantly boost the short-term performance of innovative drug companies but also promote the international development of domestic new drugs, significantly enhancing their long-term value. It is worth noting that while leading companies have strong certainty of profitability, some pharmaceutical companies still experienced declining profits or continued losses last year. The innovative drug industry as a whole is in a stage of overall improvement but with a fragile foundation. Facing the uncertainty of R&D costs and risks, as well as intensifying market competition, only by continuously improving the entire innovation ecosystem can more pharmaceutical companies realize their potential and transition from "following" to "leading." Skyworth Takes Over Panasonic TV Production and Sales Business Event: Recently, Skyworth Group Co., Ltd. announced the establishment of a deep strategic partnership with Panasonic, jointly launching a new global development strategy for high-end televisions. According to the cooperation agreement, Skyworth will be fully responsible for the production, sales, marketing, and channel expansion of Panasonic brand televisions in the European market. Panasonic will continue to focus on core imaging technology research and development, product definition, and quality control, maintaining its consistent high-end audio-visual standards. The two parties will also jointly develop high-end OLED models and promote product technology innovation together. Commentary: For many years, Panasonic has maintained high brand value in the high-end television sector, which Skyworth aims to leverage to further upgrade its globalization strategy, moving from simply "product export" to "brand ecosystem export." For Panasonic, handing over related businesses to Skyworth is an important step in its structural reform, helping the company consolidate resources for technological and product innovation and maintain competitiveness. In the past decade, relying on its advantages in production, supply chain management, logistics, and cost control of sales expenses, Chinese color TV companies have vigorously promoted globalization. In addition to Skyworth, brands like TCL and Hisense have also gradually increased their market share overseas. Overall, the global TV market is experiencing sluggish growth and intensifying competition, with a trend towards consolidation. In this context, only by continuously developing a full industry chain model and innovating can Chinese TV brands remain competitive in international markets. (Reporter Luo Xiaoxiao)

This means that in the next phase, the ability to achieve more outstanding performance in terms of functional iteration and experience optimization will largely determine whether the investments made by AI manufacturers during the Spring Festival can translate into higher "cost-effectiveness." Multiple Innovative Drug Companies Achieve Profitability in 2025 Event: According to statistics from securities institutions, as of February 27th, among the 24 innovative drug companies that have released their performance forecasts, 19 achieved positive year-on-year growth in net profit attributable to the parent company. Among them, BeiGene, Ltd. achieved full-year profitability for the first time in 2025, with a net profit attributable to the parent company of 1.422 billion yuan. Shenzhen Chipscreen Biosciences Co., Ltd. achieved a net profit attributable to the parent company of 51.0757 million yuan in 2025, turning losses into profits. Shanghai Yizhong Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. achieved a net profit attributable to the parent company of 64.132 million yuan in 2025, a year-on-year increase of 819.42%. Commentary: Domestic innovative drug companies are reaching a turning point in profitability, driven in large part by the continuous release of benefits from medical insurance policies. Last year, 114 new drugs were added to the National Medical Insurance Catalog, 50 of which were Class 1 innovative drugs. The cycle from approval to inclusion in medical insurance for innovative drugs has significantly shortened, accelerating the commercialization of pharmaceutical companies' products. On the other hand, the continuous warming of overseas business development (BD) collaborations by domestic innovative drug companies also contributes to performance realization. Data shows that in 2025, the total value of China's innovative drug overseas licensing transactions exceeded 130 billion US dollars, with over 150 licensing transactions, setting a new historical record. High-quality BD collaborations can not only significantly boost the short-term performance of innovative drug companies but also promote the international development of domestic new drugs, significantly enhancing their long-term value. It is worth noting that while leading companies have strong certainty of profitability, some pharmaceutical companies still experienced declining profits or continued losses last year. The innovative drug industry as a whole is in a stage of overall improvement but with a fragile foundation. Facing the uncertainty of R&D costs and risks, as well as intensifying market competition, only by continuously improving the entire innovation ecosystem can more pharmaceutical companies realize their potential and transition from "following" to "leading." According to the cooperation agreement, Skyworth will be fully responsible for the production, sales, marketing, and channel expansion of Panasonic brand televisions in the European market. Panasonic will continue to focus on core imaging technology research and development, product definition, and quality control, maintaining its consistent high-end audio-visual standards. The two parties will also jointly develop high-end OLED models and promote product technology innovation together. Commentary: For many years, Panasonic has maintained high brand value in the high-end television sector, which Skyworth aims to leverage to further upgrade its globalization strategy, moving from simply "product export" to "brand ecosystem export." For Panasonic, handing over related businesses to Skyworth is an important step in its structural reform, helping the company consolidate resources for technological and product innovation and maintain competitiveness. In the past decade, relying on its advantages in production, supply chain management, logistics, and cost control of sales expenses, Chinese color TV companies have vigorously promoted globalization. In addition to Skyworth, brands like TCL and Hisense have also gradually increased their market share overseas. Overall, the global TV market is experiencing sluggish growth and intensifying competition, with a trend towards consolidation. In this context, only by continuously developing a full industry chain model and innovating can Chinese TV brands remain competitive in international markets. (Reporter Luo Xiaoxiao)

title_en: Jack Ma appears! Alibaba's first stop of the new year discusses AI
body_en: On the evening of March 3rd, the official WeChat platform of YunGu Education announced that on the first working day of the new year, Jack Ma visited Hangzhou YunGu School with the core management of Alibaba and Ant Group. He engaged in discussions with the principal and teachers about the challenges and opportunities brought by AI. According to public information from YunGu, Alibaba Group Chairman Daniel Zhang, CEO Eddie Wu, Risk Committee Chairman Joe Tsai, and E-commerce Business Group CEO Jiang Fan, along with Ant Group Chairman Eric Jing and CEO Han Xinyin, participated in the exchange. The rare full gathering of core management highlights the high importance Alibaba Group and Ant Group place on AI development. (Image source: YunGu Education WeChat Public Platform) Jack Ma stated that the AI era has arrived rapidly, with societal impacts exceeding imagination. "None of us are fully prepared, but for teenagers, they have the greatest hope and opportunity for change. Therefore, the purpose of visiting YunGu School this time is to share Alibaba's increasingly clear insights on AI with the teachers." Alibaba Executives Discuss AI on the Same Day During the discussion, the Alibaba management team mentioned that AI iteration is now measured in weeks, and its capabilities are continuously growing. This technological revolution will bring about historic changes to productivity and all aspects of society. In the future, people might not need to work 8 hours a day, societal wealth will be greatly enriched, but many types of jobs will disappear. Jack Ma said, "The reason we all came to YunGu is to tell everyone that this change will come very quickly, and we need to make changes rapidly to help children learn to coexist with AI from now on and adapt to this huge transformation." Alibaba Chairman Daniel Zhang pointed out that in the AI era, critical thinking is very important. Critical thinking is not about asking questions, but about asking the right questions. In the future, machines will be able to do many things, but communication between humans and machines, and communication skills between people, may become one of the most important abilities. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu believes that the difference between humans and machines in the future will lie in three things: curiosity, empathy, and physical strength. Curiosity drives people to do things spontaneously, while machines are passive. Empathy is the understanding of others. When intellectual work is replaced by AI, physical strength becomes very important, so sports will become increasingly important in the future. Ant Group Chairman Eric Jing stated that AI should be used to help people with trivial and frequent tasks, allowing them more time to develop their unique qualities, aesthetics, creativity, and imagination. While using AI effectively, we must avoid it becoming an indispensable crutch and retain the ability to think independently. AI Brings Both Impact and Opportunity During the discussion, Jack Ma expressed that AI brings immense impact but also great opportunities, offering a chance for education to return to its essence. The time spent on rote memorization and endless practice can be freed up to cultivate creativity and imagination. "Children can have more time to play, learn music, painting, sports, and other activities, learning to share, feel, experience, listen, and understand." "Whether a school belongs to the AI era is not determined by the number of AI servers or its AI capabilities. AI possesses 'chips,' while humans possess hearts. The biggest change AI brings to education is that teachers can now fully become 'soul engineers' rather than knowledge disseminators," Jack Ma believes. In the future, children will not compete with AI in calculation and memory, but rather maintain curiosity, learn empathy and responsibility, and possess a sense of experience. Curiosity, imagination, creativity, judgment, and aesthetic ability are the true capabilities that education in the AI era needs to impart to children. Public information shows that YunGu School is a non-profit private school jointly funded by Alibaba partners, with Jack Ma serving as the "Valley Master." Founded in 2017, YunGu School has gradually evolved into a 15-year system covering kindergarten, primary school, middle school, and high school, with its main campus located in Hangzhou. Editor: Zhan Cehngheng Typesetting: Wang Lulu Proofreading: Zhao Yan

title_en: China's online consumption continues its positive and innovative trend.
body_en: Currently, digital technologies such as the internet are deeply integrated into people's lives, and smart products are emerging in an endless stream. Digital consumption is becoming an important engine for economic growth. Data released by the Ministry of Commerce shows that since the "14th Five-Year Plan," China's digital consumption has expanded in scale and improved in quality, with an overall scale exceeding 23.8 trillion yuan. China has been the world's largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years. China's online consumption continues to maintain a positive and innovative trend. In 2025, online retail sales reached 15.97 trillion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 8.6%, which is 1.4 percentage points faster than the full year of the previous year. Among them, online retail sales of physical goods reached 13.09 trillion yuan, an increase of 5.2%, contributing 1.3 percentage points to the total retail sales of consumer goods during the same period. New consumption formats and models such as live-streaming e-commerce and instant retail are growing rapidly. The live-streaming e-commerce industry maintains a good development trend, with a year-on-year increase of 11.3% in live-streaming transaction volume in 2025. Instant delivery is developing rapidly, meeting consumer needs faster and better. This impressive performance of online retail is a vivid epitome of the dual leap in the scale and quality of China's digital consumption. Online retail leads consumption upgrading and enriches the foundation of people's happiness. According to monitoring by the Ministry of Commerce's big data, online retail sales of digital products such as mobile phones and smart robots increased by 20.5% and 18% respectively in 2025. Online retail injects new momentum into the rapid rise of smart consumption, quality consumption, and green consumption, making the convenient life of "ordering with fingertips and delivery to the door" within reach and benefiting thousands of households. Online retail assists industrial transformation and activates the momentum of high-quality development. E-commerce promotes better matching of supply and demand and better stimulates the endogenous driving force of China's industrial development. In 2025, online retail sales of agricultural products nationwide and agricultural products increased by 6.7% and 9.9% respectively, and e-commerce transaction volume in the textile and pharmaceutical industries increased by 6.6% and 3.8% respectively. At the same time, e-commerce has driven the rapid development of logistics and express delivery, communication software, artificial intelligence, and other industries. Online retail connects domestic and overseas markets, painting a new picture of mutual benefit and win-win results. China's online retail "circle of friends" is expanding. In 2025, China's "Silk Road E-commerce" partner countries expanded to 36. The Shanghai "Silk Road E-commerce" Cooperation Pilot Zone has formed and promoted 12 institutional innovation achievements, such as cross-border mutual recognition of digital identities. According to monitoring by the Ministry of Commerce's big data, retail sales of key cross-border e-commerce import platforms increased by 5.6% in 2025. The 4th Global Digital Trade Expo attracted 1812 enterprises from 154 countries and regions, reaching a new scale. 382 items were launched for the first time, showcased for the first time, or exhibited for the first time, an increase of nearly 90%, contributing to the promotion of inclusive and win-win economic globalization through e-commerce. (Comprehensive)

title_en: AI sweeps MWC: Computing power takes over communication, terminal manufacturers compete for entry points
body_en: On March 2nd, local time, the annual Mobile World Congress (MWC) opened in Barcelona, Spain, with the theme "The IQ Era." MWC is the world's most important event in the communications industry, bringing together representatives from mobile phone manufacturers, software vendors, and telecommunications operators from various countries, as well as experts in the field of communications, to showcase and promote the latest products and technologies, guide industry development, and build consensus. In recent years, MWC's themes have focused on next-generation communication technologies and artificial intelligence, with some agendas also touching upon topics such as digital security and data privacy. Notably, 2026 will mark the 20th anniversary of MWC in Barcelona. Over the past two decades, the evolution of communication technology has been clearly visible: from the single connection of the voice era to the interconnectedness of everything in the data era, the rise and iteration of the smartphone industry, and breakthroughs from terrestrial communication to space and air domains. Image source: Xinhua News Agency Looking at this year's exhibition, AI is ubiquitous and deeply integrated into the core architecture of networks and terminals. The communication industry has transformed from infrastructure construction to intelligent platforms, entering an era of network scheduling, fault handling, customer operations, edge computing, and even the architecture of next-generation 6G itself. This transformation is precisely the story that giants like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Intel are collectively telling at this MWC. However, challenges remain. "Relevant research shows that current artificial intelligence models cannot meet the specific needs of the telecommunications industry. If we want to fully leverage the potential of artificial intelligence in the telecommunications field, we need telecom-grade artificial intelligence," said Mats Granryd, Director General of the GSMA (Global System for Mobile Communications Association). With 6G on the horizon, how to use AI to reshape the industry and drive business growth has become an important topic for all participating manufacturers at MWC. As the undisputed leader in AI computing power, Nvidia has revealed its ambition to drive the construction of next-generation communication network architectures at this MWC. During the exhibition, Nvidia announced collaborations with SoftBank, Nokia, Ericsson, and other manufacturers to jointly build AI-native next-generation 6G infrastructure. Nvidia defines 6G as the infrastructure that drives "Physical AI," the core infrastructure supporting large-scale robot collaboration and L4/L5 autonomous driving. "The design of traditional wireless architectures cannot meet these needs, and facing increasingly complex network environments, the original system is facing immense challenges," Nvidia stated. Nvidia believes that 6G will be open, software-defined, and AI-native. In this regard, Nvidia announced that it will jointly build "AI-RAN" (AI Radio Access Network) with its partners. This architecture attempts to break the traditional boundaries between computing power and communication, transforming global telecommunications networks into ubiquitous AI infrastructure. By running base station protocols and large AI models simultaneously on the same computing platform, it aims to achieve efficient operation of 6G communication networks. At the MWC exhibition, Nvidia and Nokia jointly demonstrated a "Universal Computing Platform" solution. This solution, based on a GPU universal platform, achieves hybrid orchestration of traditional radio access network workloads and high-real-time AI applications, breaking the monopoly of dedicated hardware on underlying communication protocols. According to Nokia, in response to the increased traffic fluctuations and high concurrent uplink demands brought about by the "AI super cycle," Nokia is well-prepared for continuous network upgrades in the mobile infrastructure sector by upgrading hardware capabilities and reshaping the AI-RAN architecture, ensuring business experience while supporting a smooth evolution to 6G. Compared to Nvidia's strong focus on developing AI-RAN, another chip giant, Intel, offers a more pragmatic AI transformation path. At this MWC, Intel showcased its new generation Xeon processor platform, covering core network, RAN, and enterprise edge scenarios. Kevork Kechichian, Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Data Center Group at Intel, stated that by deeply integrating AI acceleration engines into general-purpose processors, most inference tasks can be processed locally on existing infrastructure, reducing reliance on independent dedicated hardware. This upgrade solution significantly lowers the financial threshold and technical complexity of applying AI technology to telecommunications networks, making it more attractive to operators who are still digesting 5G capital expenditures and are unwilling to quickly initiate a new round of infrastructure investment. As a global cloud computing giant, Microsoft emphasizes that AI will significantly improve the return on investment in the telecommunications industry. It cited the latest IDC data, which shows that operators can achieve a return on investment of up to 2.8 times in generative and agent AI, with many leading companies reaching as high as 5 times. Microsoft's latest telecommunications industry solutions released during MWC indicate that as AI technology matures, the telecommunications industry is undergoing a qualitative change from point-to-point trials to full-process embedding. Microsoft believes that by deeply integrating artificial intelligence into daily operational systems, operators can automate decision-making and execution, driving continuous improvement in company performance. It is worth noting that leveraging the momentum of AI application expansion, domestic cloud vendors are also accelerating their overseas expansion. During MWC, Tencent Cloud announced the addition of a new cloud availability zone in Frankfurt, Germany. According to Tencent Cloud, with the accelerated application of Tencent's Hunyuan 3D large model and Tencent Cloud's audio and video, palm vein recognition, and other technologies overseas, the new cloud availability zone will also meet the growing demand for AI and cloud services in Europe, laying the foundation for larger-scale international development. Sun Chang, General Manager of Tencent Cloud Europe, stated that they see strong growth in demand for cloud and AI in Europe, and further increasing digital infrastructure construction will give customers the confidence to achieve growth through products and technologies. The MWC exhibition is a stage for domestic terminal manufacturers to launch new products for the European market. Xiaomi, Honor, Lenovo, and other terminal manufacturers held press conferences during MWC to showcase new products for overseas markets. Among them, Honor released its first humanoid robot, targeting shopping assistance, work scene inspection, and companionship scenarios. However, Honor did not disclose detailed information such as the price and specifications of the robot. In addition to robot products, Honor also simultaneously released the RobotPhone, calling it the "world's first robot phone." According to the introduction, with the support of Honor's AI intelligent agent, the RobotPhone adds micro-motors and a movable gimbal structure to the traditional smartphone form factor, supporting physical rotation of the camera and automatic follow-up shooting, possessing multimodal interaction capabilities, and equipped with a 200-megapixel sensor. Regarding the RobotPhone, Honor CEO George Zhao frankly stated that terminal devices should not be confined to the traditional form of "touchscreen black boxes." Fang Fei, President of Honor's Terminal Product Line, stated in an interview with the media that the RobotPhone is Honor's exploration of the boundaries of mobile phones and a decisive factor in anticipating the next stage of intelligent terminals. Wang Jiping, Vice President of IDC China, expressed "excitement" about this press conference, calling it a breakthrough strategic move by Honor in recent years. He pointed out that although IDC's latest forecast shows that the global smartphone market will experience a negative growth of about 13% due to the impact of memory chip shortages, "in this prospect, more manufacturers have shifted their focus to robots and AIoT products." On February 26th, IDC released a report stating that driven by soaring memory chip prices leading to increased device costs, the global smartphone market will experience its largest decline in history in 2026, with shipments falling to their lowest level in over a decade, marking a structural reset for the industry. Under the dual pressure of a saturated existing market and high costs, terminal manufacturers will move beyond the red ocean market of single mobile phones and shift their strategic focus to AI-native hardware with greater imaginative potential. In this context, the booming AI glasses are expected to become an important intelligent device entry point in the AI era. Market research firm Counterpoint data shows that driven by the strong pull of Meta's smart glasses and the robust follow-up of Chinese manufacturers such as Rokid, Xiaomi, and TCL, global smart glasses shipments have doubled year-on-year. IDC predicts that by 2029, global smart glasses market shipments will exceed 40 million units, with China's market share steadily increasing, and a compound annual growth rate (2024-2029) of 55.6%, ranking first globally in terms of growth rate. The reporter noted that Meta, a global leading AI glasses manufacturer, has scheduled multiple events related to AI glasses and wearable devices at this MWC exhibition, including demonstrations of devices and application cases, as well as discussion agendas related to AI glasses. Meta pointed out that AI wearable devices will reshape how we connect, and an open ecosystem is crucial for operators, developers, and users. Concurrently, Alibaba's Qwen presented a stark contrast to Meta. At the MWC exhibition, Qwen erected a giant brand logo, and Alibaba's Qwen AI glasses engaged in a head-to-head competition with Meta's AI glasses. Qwen AI glasses not only secured a larger booth than Meta but also erected a 5-meter-high Qwen brand logo, attempting to convey its ambition in the AI hardware field to the global market. In terms of integrated hardware and software layout, Qwen is extending the boundaries of its AI assistant from mobile phone screens to the physical world. On March 2nd, Qwen's first AI hardware, "Qwen AI Glasses," began pre-orders through all online and offline channels, will be available for immediate purchase on March 8th, and will be launched globally within the year. This product is fully integrated with the Qwen large model, and functions such as ordering takeout, booking taxis, and reserving hotels will be available to users by the end of March. title_en: Interview with Supreme People's Court Vice President Tao Kaiyuan: Judicial Rules for Intellectual Property Related to Artificial Intelligence Need Continuous Exploration
body_en: As artificial intelligence models are iterated and updated, and application scenarios continue to expand, related intellectual property disputes are increasing. The dense release of models such as Seedance 2.0 in early 2026 brought the copyright legality of training data sources into public view; the film and television industry's questions about whether "AI's replication of classic films constitutes infringement" are incessant. Leading AI companies abroad such as Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, and Google are all involved in copyright lawsuits, with plaintiffs including news media, book authors, and film production giants. Related copyright disputes in China have also entered the judicial field. During the 2026 National Two Sessions, the Business Order Studio of 21st Century Business Herald interviewed Tao Kaiyuan, Vice President of the Supreme People's Court. Facing the challenges that generative artificial intelligence brings to intellectual property judicial judgments, she frankly admitted that judges often find it difficult to make judgments by simply "matching" existing laws, but they must answer the "judicial questions" brought about by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology. Tao Kaiyuan believes that a balance must be struck between the development of the artificial intelligence industry and the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of copyright holders. She revealed that the drafting and formulation of judicial policy documents related to artificial intelligence and data property rights are actively being promoted, striving to provide relatively clear judicial boundaries for the application of new technologies. At the same time, she also called for the complex issues in the new field of judicial protection of intellectual property rights involving artificial intelligence, and that relevant judgment rules need to be gradually clarified through continuous exploration. As a senior judge who has long been deeply involved in intellectual property trials, Tao Kaiyuan has noticed that with China's technological rise and the continuous prosperity of the cultural industry, foreign-related intellectual property disputes involving domestic enterprises are increasing. She mentioned that efforts will be made to align with high-standard international economic and trade rules, promote the legislation of special procedures for intellectual property rights, and revise substantive laws and relevant judicial policy documents. Through the adjudication of specific cases, the judgment rules for foreign-related intellectual property rights will be continuously improved, providing institutional support for enterprises to protect their rights across borders. Tao Kaiyuan. Photo courtesy of the source. "21st Century": The Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China proposed to "resolutely break through the bottlenecks and obstacles hindering the construction of a unified national market" and "comprehensively rectify 'involutionary' competition." What work have the People's Courts done in these areas? What are the next arrangements? Tao Kaiyuan: Fair competition is the basic principle of a market economy and an important foundation for the efficient operation of the market mechanism. The "15th Five-Year Plan" proposal clearly states the need to "strengthen anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition enforcement and judiciary, and form a market order of high quality and good price, and benign competition." The judiciary is a key link in ensuring and realizing the rule of law in fair competition and promoting the construction of a unified national market. In recent years, the People's Courts have fully utilized their judicial functions in anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition, lawfully and forcefully regulated various "involutionary" competitive behaviors, and contributed to accelerating the construction of an efficient, standardized, fair, and fully open unified national market. First, focus on building a unified national market and convey a clear policy orientation. Based on the guiding, regulating, and safeguarding role of the judiciary, the Supreme People's Court has issued opinions on serving and safeguarding technological innovation with high-quality trials, clearly proposing to regulate unfair competition and monopolistic behavior in the field of technological innovation according to law, and promote the construction of a unified national market. Second, focus on key areas and resolutely curb "involutionary" competition. Strengthen judicial efforts in anti-unfair competition in key areas such as the platform economy and new energy vehicles. Strengthen the coordinated guidance of batch intellectual property cases, and forcefully regulate involutionary competition behaviors such as false litigation, malicious litigation, and abuse of litigation rights in intellectual property. Third, focus on developing new quality productive forces, and lawfully protect technological innovation and fair competition in emerging fields. Since 2022, the Supreme People's Court has released typical cases of anti-unfair competition and anti-monopoly during the China Fair Competition Policy Publicity Week, and has successively published a total of 51 typical cases of anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition, widely covering new technologies and new business formats such as artificial intelligence and the digital economy, guiding the whole society to advocate, protect, and promote fair competition. With the continuous development of new technologies, new fields, and new business formats, the judicial trial work of anti-unfair competition and anti-monopoly in the People's Courts is also facing more new challenges. In the next step, the People's Courts will thoroughly implement the decisions and arrangements of the Party Central Committee and continue to strengthen intellectual property trial work: First, lawfully, justly, and efficiently try various monopoly and unfair competition cases, focusing on strengthening judicial regulation of "involutionary" competitive behaviors such as predatory pricing and unfair pricing, continuously purifying the market competition ecosystem, and providing clear and definite judicial guidance for fair competition and standardized development of various market entities. Second, deepen the research on the application of the newly revised Anti-Unfair Competition Law, especially strengthen the research on the application of provisions such as platform forced low-price sales and large enterprises abusing their dominant position to delay payments to small and medium-sized enterprises, and continuously improve relevant judgment rules to ensure the accurate implementation of the law. Third, strengthen the judicial protection of intellectual property rights, adhere to both standardized competition and incentive innovation, guide market entities to transform from "price competition" to "innovation competition," and promote the formation of a market environment of high quality and good price, and benign competition. "21st Century": In 2025, the trend of Chinese IPs such as Labubu going global is heating up, and intellectual property disputes involving Chinese enterprises in overseas markets have significantly increased. Regarding "China becoming a preferred jurisdiction for global intellectual property disputes," what efforts will the People's Courts make in terms of procedural convenience, rule衔接, and judicial credibility? Tao Kaiyuan: In recent years, with the leap from "going global" in products to "going global" in technology, services, and supply chains, especially with the vigorous development of cross-border e-commerce, overseas intellectual property disputes and cross-border rights protection litigation initiated by Chinese outbound enterprises or encountered by them have been increasing. On the one hand, this reflects the continuous enhancement of the influence of Chinese enterprises in the global business landscape; on the other hand, it also indicates that enterprises going global need to strengthen their foresight and response to intellectual property risks. In response to new situations and new problems, the People's Courts are working from four aspects to build "preferred litigation destinations": First, lawfully exercise jurisdiction and facilitate rights relief. Adhere to the "convenience" principle of litigation, fully respect the parties' agreement to choose Chinese courts, and exercise jurisdiction according to law. Adhere to strict protection according to law, increase the intensity of infringement damages, and ensure that rights holders receive full compensation. Flexibly use systems such as preliminary judgments and behavior preservation to provide timely relief for Chinese and foreign rights holders and enhance the international influence of Chinese judiciary. Second, adhere to equal protection and stabilize market expectations. Properly try foreign-related intellectual property cases, and lawfully and equally protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties and all types of market entities. Through trademark infringement cases such as "Siemens," "Michelin," and "Lafite," we lawfully crack down on behaviors of imitating famous brands and free-riding, which not only effectively protects foreign famous trademarks but also sets a benchmark for Chinese outbound enterprises in rights protection. Continuously strengthen the publicity of foreign-related intellectual property trials, edit and publish case collections, give full play to their exemplary role, demonstrate the principle and work achievements of Chinese courts in treating all types of market entities equally and providing the same protection, and actively build a first-class business environment that is market-oriented, law-based, and internationalized, so as to serve and guarantee high-level opening up with high-quality trials. Third, deepen institutional衔接 and align with international rules. Accelerate the inclusion of special procedures for intellectual property litigation into the legislative plan, and improve litigation norms that conform to the characteristics of intellectual property cases. Actively promote the reform of the national intellectual property case appellate review mechanism and improve the specialized system of intellectual property trials. Proactively align with high-standard international economic and trade rules, and promote the revision of laws such as the Copyright Law and the Trademark Law, as well as relevant judicial interpretations. Through the adjudication of specific cases, continuously improve the judgment rules for foreign-related intellectual property rights, and provide solid institutional support for enterprises to protect their rights across borders. Fourth, expand diversified dispute resolution and improve resolution efficiency. Deepen the connection between arbitration and mediation with the Arbitration and Mediation Center of the World Intellectual Property Organization, and promote the convenient, fair, and efficient resolution of foreign-related intellectual property disputes. Strengthen the informatization construction of foreign-related trials, explore convenient and beneficial measures such as cross-border electronic service and online trials, so that Chinese and foreign parties can truly feel the efficiency and warmth of Chinese judiciary. Expand foreign publicity channels, build media promotion platforms, promote the publication of "Collection of Classic Intellectual Property Cases of Chinese Courts" (Chinese and English versions), tell the story of China's intellectual property judicial protection, and continuously enhance the dissemination and international influence of China's intellectual property judiciary. "21st Century": In recent years, copyright disputes related to generative artificial intelligence have been fermenting, and there have been many judicial cases at home and abroad. What is your view on the balance between "technological development" and "copyright protection" in such cases? Will the People's Courts issue judicial interpretations or guiding cases to provide clearer legal expectations? Tao Kaiyuan: Indeed, generative artificial intelligence poses significant challenges to copyright judicial practice. Currently, disputes involving generative artificial intelligence accepted by the People's Courts can be specifically divided into three categories: First, whether artificial intelligence-generated content, i.e., AIGC, can be recognized as a work in the sense of copyright law. Second, whether the training of large model service providers by feeding others' works into large models infringes on others' copyrights. Third, if AIGC infringes on others' copyrights, how should the infringement liability be determined, especially whether the liability of large model service providers can be determined by referring to the "safe harbor" principle. These three legal issues are highly controversial in theory and practice, and judges often find it difficult to make judgments by simply "matching" existing laws, but they must answer the "judicial questions" brought about by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology. Intellectual property rights are an important institutional arrangement for stimulating innovation, and they are also social resources that affect public welfare. Excessive protection will stifle subsequent innovation, while insufficient protection will weaken the motivation for creation. We must uphold the legislative purpose of the Copyright Law to protect the rights and interests of creators and encourage the creation of works, adhere to the protection of human intellectual achievements, and seek a balance between the development of the artificial intelligence industry and the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of copyright holders. We should not only show a moderate tolerance for data training behavior but also play the role of copyright law in stimulating innovation. We must adhere to the principle of case-by-case handling, reasonably interpret and apply existing laws, and continuously explore and summarize to gradually improve judicial rules. It must be pointed out that the judicial protection of intellectual property rights involving artificial intelligence is a brand new field, and the relevant issues are extremely complex. The Supreme People's Court attaches great importance to the trial of cases involving artificial intelligence disputes, and is currently actively promoting the drafting of judicial policy documents related to artificial intelligence and data property rights, striving to delineate relatively clear judicial boundaries for the application of new technologies. In the next step, we will continue to strengthen research, widely solicit opinions from all sectors of society, explore and summarize judgment rules for disputes involving artificial intelligence, and promote the healthy development of the artificial intelligence industry. title_en: AI sweeps MWC, computing power takes over communications, terminal manufacturers compete for entry points
body_en: On March 2nd, local time, the annual Mobile World Congress (MWC) opened in Barcelona, Spain, with the theme "The IQ Era." MWC is the world's most important event in the communications industry, bringing together representatives from mobile phone manufacturers, software vendors, and telecommunications operators from various countries, as well as experts in the field of communications, to showcase and promote the latest products and technologies, guide industry development, and build consensus. In recent years, MWC's themes have focused on next-generation communication technologies and artificial intelligence, with some agendas also touching upon topics such as digital security and data privacy. Notably, 2026 will mark the 20th anniversary of MWC in Barcelona. Over the past two decades, the evolution of communication technology has been clearly visible: from the single connection of the voice era to the interconnectedness of everything in the data era, the rise and iteration of the smartphone industry, and breakthroughs from terrestrial communication to space and air domains. Image source: Xinhua News Agency Looking at this year's exhibition, AI is ubiquitous and deeply integrated into the core architecture of networks and terminals. The communication industry has transformed from infrastructure construction to intelligent platforms, entering an era of network scheduling, fault handling, customer operations, edge computing, and even the architecture of next-generation 6G itself. This transformation is precisely the story that giants like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Intel are collectively telling at this MWC. However, challenges remain. "Relevant research shows that current artificial intelligence models cannot meet the specific needs of the telecommunications industry. If we want to fully leverage the potential of artificial intelligence in the telecommunications field, we need telecom-grade artificial intelligence," said Mats Granryd, Director General of the GSMA (Global System for Mobile Communications Association). With 6G on the horizon, how to use AI to reshape the industry and drive business growth has become an important topic for all participating manufacturers at MWC. As the undisputed leader in AI computing power, Nvidia has revealed its ambition to drive the construction of next-generation communication network architectures at this MWC. During the exhibition, Nvidia announced collaborations with SoftBank, Nokia, Ericsson, and other manufacturers to jointly build AI-native next-generation 6G infrastructure. Nvidia defines 6G as the infrastructure that drives "Physical AI," the core infrastructure supporting large-scale robot collaboration and L4/L5 autonomous driving. "The design of traditional wireless architectures cannot meet these needs, and facing increasingly complex network environments, the original system is facing immense challenges," Nvidia stated. Nvidia believes that 6G will be open, software-defined, and AI-native. In this regard, Nvidia announced that it will jointly build "AI-RAN" (AI Radio Access Network) with its partners. This architecture attempts to break the traditional boundaries between computing power and communication, transforming global telecommunications networks into ubiquitous AI infrastructure. By running base station protocols and large AI models simultaneously on the same computing platform, it aims to achieve efficient operation of 6G communication networks. At the MWC exhibition, Nvidia and Nokia jointly demonstrated a "Universal Computing Platform" solution. This solution, based on a GPU universal platform, achieves hybrid orchestration of traditional radio access network workloads and high-real-time AI applications, breaking the monopoly of dedicated hardware on underlying communication protocols. According to Nokia, in response to the increased traffic fluctuations and high concurrent uplink demands brought about by the "AI super cycle," Nokia is well-prepared for continuous network upgrades in the mobile infrastructure sector by upgrading hardware capabilities and reshaping the AI-RAN architecture, ensuring business experience while supporting a smooth evolution to 6G. Compared to Nvidia's strong focus on developing AI-RAN, another chip giant, Intel, offers a more pragmatic AI transformation path. At this MWC, Intel showcased its new generation Xeon processor platform, covering core network, RAN, and enterprise edge scenarios. Kevork Kechichian, Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Data Center Group at Intel, stated that by deeply integrating AI acceleration engines into general-purpose processors, most inference tasks can be processed locally on existing infrastructure, reducing reliance on independent dedicated hardware. This upgrade solution significantly lowers the financial threshold and technical complexity of applying AI technology to telecommunications networks, making it more attractive to operators who are still digesting 5G capital expenditures and are unwilling to quickly initiate a new round of infrastructure investment. As a global cloud computing giant, Microsoft emphasizes that AI will significantly improve the return on investment in the telecommunications industry. It cited the latest IDC data, which shows that operators can achieve a return on investment of up to 2.8 times in generative and agent AI, with many leading companies reaching as high as 5 times. Microsoft's latest telecommunications industry solutions released during MWC indicate that as AI technology matures, the telecommunications industry is undergoing a qualitative change from point-to-point trials to full-process embedding. Microsoft believes that by deeply integrating artificial intelligence into daily operational systems, operators can automate decision-making and execution, driving continuous improvement in company performance. It is worth noting that leveraging the momentum of AI application expansion, domestic cloud vendors are also accelerating their overseas expansion. During MWC, Tencent Cloud announced the addition of a new cloud availability zone in Frankfurt, Germany. According to Tencent Cloud, with the accelerated application of Tencent's Hunyuan 3D large model and Tencent Cloud's audio and video, palm vein recognition, and other technologies overseas, the new cloud availability zone will also meet the growing demand for AI and cloud services in Europe, laying the foundation for larger-scale international development. Sun Chang, General Manager of Tencent Cloud Europe, stated that they see strong growth in demand for cloud and AI in Europe, and further increasing digital infrastructure construction will give customers the confidence to achieve growth through products and technologies. The MWC exhibition is a stage for domestic terminal manufacturers to launch new products for the European market. Xiaomi, Honor, Lenovo, and other terminal manufacturers held press conferences during MWC to showcase new products for overseas markets. Among them, Honor released its first humanoid robot, targeting shopping assistance, work scene inspection, and companionship scenarios. However, Honor did not disclose detailed information such as the price and specifications of the robot. In addition to robot products, Honor also simultaneously released the RobotPhone, calling it the "world's first robot phone." title_en: Exclusive Interview with Supreme People's Court Vice President Tao Kaiyuan: Rules for Intellectual Property Judgments Involving Artificial Intelligence Require Continuous Exploration
body_en: As artificial intelligence models are iterated and updated, and application scenarios continue to expand, related intellectual property disputes are increasing. The dense release of models such as Seedance 2.0 in early 2026 brought the copyright legality of training data sources into public view; the film and television industry's questions about whether "AI's replication of classic films constitutes infringement" are incessant. Leading AI companies abroad such as Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, and Google are all involved in copyright lawsuits, with plaintiffs including news media, book authors, and film production giants. Related copyright disputes in China have also entered the judicial field. During the 2026 National Two Sessions, the Business Order Studio of 21st Century Business Herald interviewed Tao Kaiyuan, Vice President of the Supreme People's Court. Facing the challenges that generative artificial intelligence brings to intellectual property judicial judgments, she frankly admitted that judges often find it difficult to make judgments by simply "matching" existing laws, but they must answer the "judicial questions" brought about by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology. Tao Kaiyuan believes that a balance must be struck between the development of the artificial intelligence industry and the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of copyright holders. She revealed that the drafting and formulation of judicial policy documents related to artificial intelligence and data property rights are actively being promoted, striving to provide relatively clear judicial boundaries for the application of new technologies. At the same time, she also called for the complex issues in the new field of judicial protection of intellectual property rights involving artificial intelligence, and that relevant judgment rules need to be gradually clarified through continuous exploration. As a senior judge who has long been deeply involved in intellectual property trials, Tao Kaiyuan has noticed that with China's technological rise and the continuous prosperity of the cultural industry, foreign-related intellectual property disputes involving domestic enterprises are increasing. She mentioned that efforts will be made to align with high-standard international economic and trade rules, promote the legislation of special procedures for intellectual property rights, and revise substantive laws and relevant judicial policy documents. Through the adjudication of specific cases, the judgment rules for foreign-related intellectual property rights will be continuously improved, providing institutional support for enterprises to protect their rights across borders. Tao Kaiyuan. Photo courtesy of the source. "21st Century": The Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China proposed to "resolutely break through the bottlenecks and obstacles hindering the construction of a unified national market" and "comprehensively rectify 'involutionary' competition." What work have the People's Courts done in these areas? What are the next arrangements? Tao Kaiyuan: Fair competition is the basic principle of a market economy and an important foundation for the efficient operation of the market mechanism. The "15th Five-Year Plan" proposal clearly states the need to "strengthen anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition enforcement and judiciary, and form a market order of high quality and good price, and benign competition." The judiciary is a key link in ensuring and realizing the rule of law in fair competition and promoting the construction of a unified national market. In recent years, the People's Courts have fully utilized their judicial functions in anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition, lawfully and forcefully regulated various "involutionary" competitive behaviors, and contributed to accelerating the construction of an efficient, standardized, fair, and fully open unified national market. First, focus on building a unified national market and convey a clear policy orientation. Based on the guiding, regulating, and safeguarding role of the judiciary, the Supreme People's Court has issued opinions on serving and safeguarding technological innovation with high-quality trials, clearly proposing to regulate unfair competition and monopolistic behavior in the field of technological innovation according to law, and promote the construction of a unified national market. Second, focus on key areas and resolutely curb "involutionary" competition. Strengthen judicial efforts in anti-unfair competition in key areas such as the platform economy and new energy vehicles. Strengthen the coordinated guidance of batch intellectual property cases, and forcefully regulate involutionary competition behaviors such as false litigation, malicious litigation, and abuse of litigation rights in intellectual property. Third, focus on developing new quality productive forces, and lawfully protect technological innovation and fair competition in emerging fields. Since 2022, the Supreme People's Court has released typical cases of anti-unfair competition and anti-monopoly during the China Fair Competition Policy Publicity Week, and has successively published a total of 51 typical cases of anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition, widely covering new technologies and new business formats such as artificial intelligence and the digital economy, guiding the whole society to advocate, protect, and promote fair competition. With the continuous development of new technologies, new fields, and new business formats, the judicial trial work of anti-unfair competition and anti-monopoly in the People's Courts is also facing more new challenges. In the next step, the People's Courts will thoroughly implement the decisions and arrangements of the Party Central Committee and continue to strengthen intellectual property trial work: First, lawfully, justly, and efficiently try various monopoly and unfair competition cases, focusing on strengthening judicial regulation of "involutionary" competitive behaviors such as predatory pricing and unfair pricing, continuously purifying the market competition ecosystem, and providing clear and definite judicial guidance for fair competition and standardized development of various market entities. Second, deepen the research on the application of the newly revised Anti-Unfair Competition Law, especially strengthen the research on the application of provisions such as platform forced low-price sales and large enterprises abusing their dominant position to delay payments to small and medium-sized enterprises, and continuously improve relevant judgment rules to ensure the accurate implementation of the law. Third, strengthen the judicial protection of intellectual property rights, adhere to both standardized competition and incentive innovation, guide market entities to transform from "price competition" to "innovation competition," and promote the formation of a market environment of high quality and good price, and benign competition. "21st Century": In 2025, the trend of Chinese IPs such as Labubu going global is heating up, and intellectual property disputes involving Chinese enterprises in overseas markets have significantly increased. Regarding "China becoming a preferred jurisdiction for global intellectual property disputes," what efforts will the People's Courts make in terms of procedural convenience, rule衔接, and judicial credibility? Tao Kaiyuan: In recent years, with the leap from "going global" in products to "going global" in technology, services, and supply chains, especially with the vigorous development of cross-border e-commerce, overseas intellectual property disputes and cross-border rights protection litigation initiated by Chinese outbound enterprises or encountered by them have been increasing. On the one hand, this reflects the continuous enhancement of the influence of Chinese enterprises in the global business landscape; on the other hand, it also indicates that enterprises going global need to strengthen their foresight and response to intellectual property risks. In response to new situations and new problems, the People's Courts are working from four aspects to build "preferred litigation destinations": First, lawfully exercise jurisdiction and facilitate rights relief. Adhere to the "convenience" principle of litigation, fully respect the parties' agreement to choose Chinese courts, and exercise jurisdiction according to law. Adhere to strict protection according to law, increase the intensity of infringement damages, and ensure that rights holders receive full compensation. Flexibly use systems such as preliminary judgments and behavior preservation to provide timely relief for Chinese and foreign rights holders and enhance the international influence of Chinese judiciary. Second, adhere to equal protection and stabilize market expectations. Properly try foreign-related intellectual property cases, and lawfully and equally protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties and all types of market entities. Through trademark infringement cases such as "Siemens," "Michelin," and "Lafite," we lawfully crack down on behaviors of imitating famous brands and free-riding, which not only effectively protects foreign famous trademarks but also sets a benchmark for Chinese outbound enterprises in rights protection. Continuously strengthen the publicity of foreign-related intellectual property trials, edit and publish case collections, give full play to their exemplary role, demonstrate the principle and work achievements of Chinese courts in treating all types of market entities equally and providing the same protection, and actively build a first-class business environment that is market-oriented, law-based, and internationalized, so as to serve and guarantee high-level opening up with high-quality trials. Third, deepen institutional衔接 and align with international rules. Accelerate the inclusion of special procedures for intellectual property litigation into the legislative plan, and improve litigation norms that conform to the characteristics of intellectual property cases. Actively promote the reform of the national intellectual property case appellate review mechanism and improve the specialized system of intellectual property trials. Proactively align with high-standard international economic and trade rules, and promote the revision of laws such as the Copyright Law and the Trademark Law, as well as relevant judicial interpretations. Through the adjudication of specific cases, continuously improve the judgment rules for foreign-related intellectual property rights, and provide solid institutional support for enterprises to protect their rights across borders. Fourth, expand diversified dispute resolution and improve resolution efficiency. Deepen the connection between arbitration and mediation with the Arbitration and Mediation Center of the World Intellectual Property Organization, and promote the convenient, fair, and efficient resolution of foreign-related intellectual property disputes. Strengthen the informatization construction of foreign-related trials, explore convenient and beneficial measures such as cross-border electronic service and online trials, so that Chinese and foreign parties can truly feel the efficiency and warmth of Chinese judiciary. Expand foreign publicity channels, build media promotion platforms, promote the publication of "Collection of Classic Intellectual Property Cases of Chinese Courts" (Chinese and English versions), tell the story of China's intellectual property judicial protection, and continuously enhance the dissemination and international influence of China's intellectual property judiciary. "21st Century": In recent years, copyright disputes related to generative artificial intelligence have been fermenting, and there have been many judicial cases at home and abroad. What is your view on the balance between "technological development" and "copyright protection" in such cases? Will the People's Courts issue judicial interpretations or guiding cases to provide clearer legal expectations? Tao Kaiyuan: Indeed, generative artificial intelligence poses significant challenges to copyright judicial practice. Currently, disputes involving generative artificial intelligence accepted by the People's Courts can be specifically divided into three categories: First, whether artificial intelligence-generated content, i.e., AIGC, can be recognized as a work in the sense of copyright law. Second, whether the training of large model service providers by feeding others' works into large models infringes on others' copyrights. Third, if AIGC infringes on others' copyrights, how should the infringement liability be determined, especially whether the liability of large model service providers can be determined by referring to the "safe harbor" principle. These three legal issues are highly controversial in theory and practice, and judges often find it difficult to make judgments by simply "matching" existing laws, but they must answer the "judicial questions" brought about by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology. Intellectual property rights are an important institutional arrangement for stimulating innovation, and they are also social resources that affect public welfare. Excessive protection will stifle subsequent innovation, while insufficient protection will weaken the motivation for creation. We must uphold the legislative purpose of the Copyright Law to protect the rights and interests of creators and encourage the creation of works, adhere to the protection of human intellectual achievements, and seek a balance between the development of the artificial intelligence industry and the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of copyright holders. We should not only show a moderate tolerance for data training behavior but also play the role of copyright law in stimulating innovation. We must adhere to the principle of case-by-case handling, reasonably interpret and apply existing laws, and continuously explore and summarize to gradually improve judicial rules. It must be pointed out that the judicial protection of intellectual property rights involving artificial intelligence is a brand new field, and the relevant issues are extremely complex. The Supreme People's Court attaches great importance to the trial of cases involving artificial intelligence disputes, and is currently actively promoting the drafting of judicial policy documents related to artificial intelligence and data property rights, striving to delineate relatively clear judicial boundaries for the application of new technologies. In the next step, we will continue to strengthen research, widely solicit opinions from all sectors of society, explore and summarize judgment rules for disputes involving artificial intelligence, and promote the healthy development of the artificial intelligence industry.
