Expand foreign publicity channels, build media promotion platforms, promote the publication of "Collection of Classic Intellectual Property Cases of Chinese Courts" (Chinese and English versions), tell the story of China's intellectual property judicial protection, and continuously enhance the dissemination and international influence of China's intellectual property judiciary. "21st Century": In recent years, copyright disputes related to generative artificial intelligence have been fermenting, and there have been many judicial cases at home and abroad. What is your view on the balance between "technological development" and "copyright protection" in such cases? Will the People's Courts issue judicial interpretations or guiding cases to provide clearer legal expectations? Tao Kaiyuan: Indeed, generative artificial intelligence poses significant challenges to copyright judicial practice. Currently, disputes involving generative artificial intelligence accepted by the People's Courts can be specifically divided into three categories: First, whether artificial intelligence-generated content, i.e., AIGC, can be recognized as a work in the sense of copyright law. Second, whether the training of large model service providers by feeding others' works into large models infringes on others' copyrights. Third, if AIGC infringes on others' copyrights, how should the infringement liability be determined, especially whether the liability of large model service providers can be determined by referring to the "safe harbor" principle. These three legal issues are highly controversial in theory and practice, and judges often find it difficult to make judgments by simply "matching" existing laws, but they must answer the "judicial questions" brought about by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology. Intellectual property rights are an important institutional arrangement for stimulating innovation, and they are also social resources that affect public welfare. Excessive protection will stifle subsequent innovation, while insufficient protection will weaken the motivation for creation. We must uphold the legislative purpose of the Copyright Law to protect the rights and interests of creators and encourage the creation of works, adhere to the protection of human intellectual achievements, and seek a balance between the development of the artificial intelligence industry and the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of copyright holders. We should not only show a moderate tolerance for data training behavior but also play the role of copyright law in stimulating innovation. We must adhere to the principle of case-by-case handling, reasonably interpret and apply existing laws, and continuously explore and summarize to gradually improve judicial rules. It must be pointed out that the judicial protection of intellectual property rights involving artificial intelligence is a brand new field, and the relevant issues are extremely complex. The Supreme People's Court attaches great importance to the trial of cases involving artificial intelligence disputes, and is currently actively promoting the drafting of judicial policy documents related to artificial intelligence and data property rights, striving to delineate relatively clear judicial boundaries for the application of new technologies. In the next step, we will continue to strengthen research, widely solicit opinions from all sectors of society, explore and summarize judgment rules for disputes involving artificial intelligence, and promote the healthy development of the artificial intelligence industry. In core industries such as manufacturing, agriculture, and trade circulation, logistics costs have shifted from being an "optimizable item" to a core consideration for industrial upgrading. Recently, Wanlian Yida Group launched a new logistics matching trading platform, Yidabao, which innovatively implements a "dual zero" model of "0 membership fee for shippers, 0 commission for drivers." Through an open mechanism, it achieves cost reduction for shippers and increased income for drivers, providing a new practical sample for cost reduction and efficiency improvement in the logistics industry. From traditional heavy-asset physical freight to algorithm-driven network freight, and now to new logistics matching trading platforms, the logistics industry is entering a critical period of deepening digital and intelligent transformation and iterative innovation of business models, reflecting the profound transformation of China's logistics industry from scale expansion to quality improvement. Business Model Innovation: From Optimizing Experience to Building Trust As the "veins" of the real economy, modern logistics connects production on one end and consumption on the other, playing an important foundational role in the national economic cycle. Matching transactions, as a core link in the logistics industry chain, directly affect the cost and vitality of the entire industry through their efficiency and fairness. For a long time, traditional logistics matching models have suffered from ambiguous definition of responsibilities and insufficient protection of the rights and interests of both supply and demand sides. Yidabao innovatively launched the "0 membership fee for shippers, 0 commission for drivers" profit-sharing model, allowing shippers and drivers to eliminate information acquisition costs and returning the platform's value to the essence of matching services. "At present, all compliant enterprises and drivers can register on the Yidabao platform for free," said the head of Wanlian Yida Logistics. Only by providing more open and inclusive services, and effectively reducing costs for shippers and increasing income for drivers, can the long-term value of the platform be truly realized. At the same time, Yidabao integrates multi-dimensional information such as historical transaction data, performance records, and vehicle trajectories to conduct two-way credit evaluation and dynamic profiling of shippers and drivers, building a quantifiable and traceable intelligent credit system with full dimensions. Based on algorithms, it matches "reliable shippers" with "high-quality capacity," ensuring transaction security and optimizing the transaction experience from the source. For shippers, for example, they can quickly match high-quality capacity by publishing their needs with one click, and manage the entire transportation process visually. The logistics manager of a food processing enterprise stated: "In the past, finding a truck required making more than a dozen phone calls, and I also had to worry about whether the driver was reliable. Now, with Yidabao, I can check the transportation trajectory at any time, online payment is convenient, and there is no membership fee, which effectively helps our small and micro enterprises reduce costs and increase efficiency." For drivers, Yidabao pushes real and reliable corporate cargo sources and high-yield transportation orders, and provides intelligent dispatching and route planning services, helping drivers reduce empty mileage and increase income, allowing them to "drive with peace of mind and earn with confidence." It is worth mentioning that Yidabao's intelligent credit system has achieved data interconnection with the digital financial services of Wanlian Yida's industrial Internet ecosystem. The excellent performance records of compliant enterprises and drivers can be directly converted into financing credit, providing financial support for both parties. The positive cycle of "performance - credit - re-performance" makes "credit" a truly usable asset for logistics professionals. Digital and Intelligent Empowerment: From Supply-Demand Matching to Algorithm Optimization In November 2025, the National Development and Reform Commission and other departments issued the "Implementation Plan for Promoting the Open and Interconnected Logistics Data to Effectively Reduce the Overall Logistics Costs of Society," promoting the integrated application of logistics data with industrial data and other multi-source data. Today, the comprehensive development of digital and intelligent technologies has driven the logistics industry to transform from manual matching to algorithm optimization, and from experience-based decision-making to data-driven deep transformation. In the freight sector, many platform companies are accelerating their digital and intelligent layout. Manbang Group relies on digital technologies such as artificial intelligence to build a smart logistics chain covering vehicle-freight matching, capacity dispatching, and transportation management. Huolala has upgraded its "smart brain" to achieve real-time intelligent matching of logistics orders with hundreds of thousands of drivers. Chengfeng Freight focuses on bulk whole-vehicle transportation scenarios such as coal, coke, and steel, focusing on core businesses such as order statistics, vehicle management, and user management, and establishing a materialized view covering all elements. The launch of Yidabao has become a representative of the deep application of digital and intelligent technologies in all scenarios of logistics matching, committed to building a smart logistics new ecosystem covering the entire industry and connecting all scenarios. Data shows that relying on the Wanlian Yida industrial Internet ecosystem, Yidabao has built a national offline professional service team of 15,000 people, connecting over 30,000 certified shippers and over 4 million high-quality capacities, and has built a three-dimensional matching mechanism of "intelligent matching + dedicated dispatching + selected familiar vehicles," completing the entire process from shipper order release to vehicle confirmation in as fast as 10 minutes. According to the relevant technical负责人 of Wanlian Yida, Yidabao, with the Wanlian Yida industrial Internet ecosystem as the foundation, deeply integrates AI technology and trusted data capabilities, enabling logistics data and industrial data to truly "dialogue": through multi-dimensional data streams such as historical transactions, real-time road conditions, and supply-demand fluctuations, it builds a credit evaluation system and dynamic pricing mechanism, forming a high-quality capacity pool and a benign transaction ecosystem, achieving efficient and accurate matching of shipper needs and carrier resources. Ecological Synergy: From Efficient Matching to Industrial Integration In January 2026, the "Action Plan to Accelerate the Cultivation of Leading Transportation and Logistics Enterprises and Enhance the Service and Guarantee Capabilities of Industrial and Supply Chains," jointly issued by the Ministry of Transport and other 8 ministries, proposed to accelerate the digital and intelligent empowerment of transportation and logistics... accelerate the integrated application of new-generation information technologies such as big data, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence, promote the application of new technology models such as electronic waybills, capacity matching, route optimization, and online settlement, and collaboratively promote the development and application of enterprise large models based on various transportation and logistics scenarios. It is understood that Yidabao has integrated different production factors such as manufacturing, trade, and logistics during its trial operation phase, and has successfully provided differentiated solutions for hundreds of leading enterprises in fields such as intelligent manufacturing, modern agriculture, and trade circulation. It has also formed differentiated advantages in segmented tracks such as energy and bulk commodities, and has initially built a complete business closed loop of "transaction + logistics." Industry insiders believe that at a time when industrial digital transformation is entering deep water, these innovative practices are integrating and promoting each other, jointly promoting the transformation of China's logistics industry from "decentralized and extensive" development to "intensive and high-quality" development, making the logistics industry a solid support for the high-quality development of the real economy. The launch of Yidabao is not only an innovation of a platform, but also an upgrade of the development concept of the logistics industry: from pursuing its own development to empowering industrial development, from focusing on efficiency improvement to achieving value symbiosis, and from single business model innovation to ecosystem restructuring. title_en: Use concrete and decisive measures to solve the problem of "involutionary" competition.
body_en: The State Council Information Office recently held a State Council policy briefing to introduce the work of State Council departments in handling suggestions from National People's Congress deputies and proposals from members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in 2025. In response to opinions from deputies and members on strengthening regulatory enforcement and consolidating the primary responsibility of platforms, the State Administration for Market Regulation has attached great importance to this issue. By systematically planning and focusing on investigating and punishing illegal acts, supporting industrial optimization and upgrading, and improving systems and rules, it has innovatively introduced multiple work measures to solve the problem of "involutionary" competition with practical and strong actions, and to help build a unified national market. In terms of investigating and punishing illegal acts, the administration has intensified regulatory enforcement, conducted cost investigations and enforcement inspections in key industries, deployed nine special rectification actions, investigated typical cases of live-streaming e-commerce, interviewed major platform enterprises to urge them to take down "lowest price on the whole network" activities, halted controversial rules such as "refund only," investigated a series of cases of "phantom takeout" and "phantom online stores," and increased the exposure of typical cases to form a strong deterrent, achieving the governance effect of "investigating one case, warning a batch of enterprises, and regulating an industry." In terms of supporting industrial optimization and upgrading, it has promoted the construction of quality-strengthening industrial chains, implemented 1,856 quality-strengthening industrial chain projects, and solved 25,000 quality bottlenecks and blocking points. It has recalled defective mobile power products 10 times, involving nearly 1.4 million units. For the first time, it conducted a special supervision and random inspection of complete vehicles in the new energy vehicle sector, urging enterprises to build a strong defense line for quality and safety. In terms of improving systems and rules, it has promoted the revision and issuance of the "Anti-Unfair Competition Law," and released institutional documents such as the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Rules for Online Trading Platforms" and the "Guidelines for Anti-Monopoly Compliance of Internet Platforms," setting "red lines" and clarifying "bottom lines" for platform enterprises to operate legally and compliantly. It has issued the "Implementation Measures for the Regulations on Fair Competition Review," and market regulation departments nationwide have completed the review of over 60,000 important policies and measures, effectively regulating the economic promotion behavior of local governments.

title_en: Alibaba AI restructures, focusing on Qwen.
body_en: March 2026 has been a period of duality for Alibaba. On one hand, there's a surge in business progress: Jack Ma, along with core management like Joe Tsai, Eddie Wu, and Jiang Fan, made a rare collective appearance to discuss "the unimaginable impact of AI on society" at the Yunqi Academy. Alibaba has swiftly consolidated its scattered AI brands under "Qwen," making a high-profile debut of the Qwen AI glasses at MWC, directly challenging Meta. On the other hand, the AI team is undergoing significant adjustments: Lin Junyang, the technical soul behind the Qwen large model, has chosen to leave for personal career planning. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu responded in an internal email, stating the company will continue to adhere to its open-source model strategy and persistently increase investment in AI research and development, as well as talent acquisition. Jack Ma's words at Yunqi Academy, "The impact of AI is beyond imagination, and no one is fully prepared," also apply to Alibaba itself. As AI development enters a phase of rapid practical application in 2026, Alibaba's internal AI strategy and organizational structure are both evolving. Over the past decade, Alibaba has seemed to operate on two main tracks, giving the impression of "two Alibabas." One is highly traffic-oriented and commercialized, exemplified by the e-commerce systems of Taobao and Tmall, which possess strong profitability. The other is more technology-oriented, encompassing Alibaba Cloud, DAMO Academy, and the Yunqi Conference, investing in technology on a scale and with a dedication that surpasses even typically tech-focused internet companies. While there have been attempts to integrate these two Alibabas organizationally, they have presented distinct impressions to users. The key to Alibaba's potential return to user-centricity in the next decade may lie in its ability to reinvent itself, or to create a larger platform and a new ecosystem that merges these two facets. During the Spring Festival, Qwen, a technology-oriented AI app, was integrated with the e-commerce retail system through an AI-powered milk tea ordering feature. This suggests that Alibaba's top-level design has recognized this issue and made strategic arrangements. However, this is insufficient; the scenarios are too limited. The original e-commerce system is vast, and this single entry point is not enough to unleash AI's full potential. For Alibaba, Qwen can no longer be a "laboratory project" pursued in isolation, driven by technical idealism. It must emerge from its ivory tower, integrate into Alibaba's entire business ecosystem, and become a crucial part of the group's strategy. This is an "coming-of-age" moment for Alibaba's AI, and the direction has been set. Image source: IC photo Alibaba's approach to AI in the past was characterized by a "scattered like a starry sky" extravagance. From Tongyi Laboratory to the Qwen app and Quark, various business lines had their own "prodigal sons," leading to a proliferation of brands, akin to "feudal lords carving up territory." This was common during the pioneering phase of AI and even an advantage, allowing for internal experimentation and encouraging multi-pronged development. However, the benefits of this "adolescent" phase are diminishing. Since last year, Alibaba Group CEO Eddie Wu has clearly defined "user-first" and "AI-driven" as two strategic priorities, announcing an investment of over 380 billion yuan in cloud and AI hardware infrastructure over the next three years, exceeding the total investment of the past decade. This is Alibaba's "gamble" on AI. But with the money invested, has the return followed? Firstly, the open-source path that Alibaba has consistently pursued has an inherent conflict with commercialization. Jia Yangqing, former Vice President of Technology at Alibaba and founder of Lepton AI, commented that balancing open-source and commercial interests is indeed very difficult for a company. However, we cannot deny the influence of Alibaba's Qwen model in the global open-source community. By 2025, its downloads on the Hugging Face community exceeded 600 million, with over 170,000 derivative models. The Stanford "2025 AI Index Report" ranked Qwen third globally in terms of important model contributions. Nevertheless, as AI becomes a "total war" that giants cannot afford to lose, Alibaba faces the challenge of a strategic shift. It needs to leverage the technical influence gained from open-sourcing to serve its commercial goals, such as its AI cloud and super-entry points. The question remains: what is the conversion rate from open-source to commercialization? This has always been an unresolved problem. On the other hand, Alibaba's strong push of the Qwen app during the Spring Festival, leveraging its entire ecosystem, is also a testament to its commitment to commercialization. title_en: Alibaba steps up focus on Qwen LLM
body_en: Chinese tech heavyweight Alibaba Group is reorganizing leadership and stepping up resources around its Qwen large language model following the departure of a key technical leader, as competition intensifies among China's major tech companies in the fast-growing AI application market. In an internal e-mail to employees, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu responded to the resignation of Lin Junyang, a core leader of the Qwen model, on Thursday. According to the e-mail, Alibaba Cloud's chief technology officer Zhou Jingren would continue to lead the Tongyi Lab. The company will also establish a foundation model support group to mobilize group-wide resources for large model development. Wu stressed that building foundational large models is a key long-term strategy for the company, and Alibaba will continue to adhere to its open-source model strategy while further increasing investment in artificial intelligence research and development and stepping up efforts to attract top talent.

title_en: Tech Weekly: Government Work Report Mentions New Breakthroughs in Chip Self-Research; Jack Ma Unusually Gathers with Alibaba and Ant Core Management to Discuss AI
body_en: Jack Ma and Core Management of Alibaba and Ant Group Convene to Discuss AI On March 3rd, the first workday of the new year for Alibaba, founder Jack Ma and the core management of Alibaba and Ant Group gathered at Hangzhou Yunqi School to discuss the challenges and opportunities brought by AI. According to the Yunqi School's official WeChat account, Alibaba Group Chairman Daniel Zhang, CEO Eddie Wu, Risk Committee Chairman Shao Xiaofeng, and E-commerce Business Group CEO Jiang Fan, along with Ant Group Chairman Eric Jing and CEO Han Xinyi, participated in the discussion. This marks a rare occasion where the core management of both Alibaba and Ant Group were all present. [Commentary] Although the meeting took place at a school, Jack Ma's high focus on AI within an educational context is a rare public move for him in the past two years. The rare gathering of the core management of Alibaba and Ant Group underscores the high importance placed on AI by the Alibaba ecosystem. During the discussions, executives mentioned that AI iteration is now measured in weeks, with capabilities continuously growing. They emphasized that this technological revolution will bring about historic changes to productivity and all aspects of society. Both Jack Ma and Daniel Zhang spoke about the immense impact AI could have, and their shared proposition was to adapt quickly, change rapidly, and maintain human thinking. Meituan's AI Browser Responds to Code Controversy On March 2nd, Meituan's Guangnian Zhiwai (GN06) team announced that their product, Tabbit AI Browser, had entered public beta. On March 3rd, "Mengxi Shui Le Ma," the original author of "Peidu Wa" (Read Frog), posted that Tabbit had used code from "Peidu Wa." According to "Peidu Wa's" GPL license, any product using this code must be open-sourced. Subsequently, the Tabbit team communicated directly with the user "Mengxi Shui Le Ma," and an agreement was reached. [Commentary] The dispute between the two parties essentially stemmed from Tabbit's oversight in open-source compliance. The outcome shows that rectifications can be made through rapid settlement. Similar disputes or non-standard practices may emerge in the industry in the future, and this incident can serve as a cautionary case for industry open-source compliance. Government Work Report Mentions New Breakthroughs in Chip Self-Research On the morning of March 5th, the Fourth Session of the 14th National People's Congress opened in Beijing, where Premier Li Qiang delivered the Government Work Report. Regarding the development of the chip industry, the report stated that China's development has been new and improved over the past year, demonstrating vigorous vitality. New quality productive forces have developed steadily, technological innovation has yielded fruitful results, and breakthroughs have been made in chip self-research. The Government Work Report also mentioned that the output of integrated circuits increased by 10.9%. Additionally, the first "Ministers' Corridor" press conference of the Fourth Session of the 14th National People's Congress was held on the same day in the North Hall of the Great Hall of the People. Minister of Science and Technology Yin Hejun stated that new breakthroughs have been achieved in chip research and development. [Commentary] Over the past year, several AI chip companies have made new progress. Hygon has continued to advance the iteration and ecosystem construction of its AI accelerator cards (DCU), promoting the large-scale application of domestic computing power in large model training and inference scenarios. In December last year, Moore Threads launched its new chip architecture, Huagang, which boasts a 50% increase in computing power density compared to the previous generation. In terms of semiconductor equipment, Xinkailai debuted at the Shanghai Semiconductor Equipment Exhibition in March last year, showcasing 31 types of semiconductor process and testing equipment across 6 major categories, including etching, diffusion, thin-film, and physical measurement products. Google Cuts App Commission to 20% Recently, Google announced structural updates to its Google Play business model, including reducing in-app purchase (IAP) commission rates, opening up more payment methods, and introducing a third-party app store registration program. The most notable change is the reduction in app commission rates. Google has adjusted its previous uniform 30% commission model to a new structure of "in-app service fee + payment processing fee." The in-app service fee has been reduced to 20%, with payment processing fees charged separately, at a rate of 5% in some regions. The opening up of third-party payments and app stores means that the commission developers need to pay to Google has been reduced by at least 5%. [Commentary] The industry believes that Google Play accounts for about 40% of overseas mobile game market revenue, which is a significant benefit for game manufacturers and developers going overseas. CICC released a research report stating that in the short term, due to the reduced commission rates under the new regulations, the profits of overseas game products are expected to gradually increase. In the medium to long term, the reduction in commission rates essentially signifies a shift in pricing power within the gaming industry from channels to content creators. 250 Billion Yuan in National Bonds to Support Trade-ins On March 5th, the Government Work Report proposed that 250 billion yuan in ultra-long-term special national bonds will be issued this year to support the trade-in of consumer goods, optimize policy implementation mechanisms, and promote the expansion and upgrading of consumption. Wu Xianjian, Executive Deputy Secretary-General of the China Household Electrical Appliances Commercial Association, analyzed for Yicai Global that the home appliance consumption market still has potential for quality improvement and expansion this year. With national subsidies streamlined to focus on three major areas: automobiles, home appliances, and digital smart products, it is expected that national subsidies this year will avoid the situation of subsidy gaps that occurred in some areas at the end of last year, and will be implemented in an orderly manner, continuing until the end of the year. [Commentary] The implementation of the new round of national subsidies has entered its third year and will continue to be an important catalyst for activating consumer market demand in 2026. Green and intelligent home appliances are becoming the main trend. The digital industry will see a significant recovery in the mid-to-low-end and replacement markets, especially in smart wearable categories such as smart glasses, and in lower-tier markets, which will become new growth points. Beyond policy, companies need to focus on long-term internal transformation, be user-centric, and embrace AI evolution. The core contradiction in the current market remains the mismatch between supply and demand. Matching supply and demand requires refined operations to activate users and create more user value. Operations of Several Autonomous Driving Companies Suspended in UAE On March 1st, Pony.ai responded to inquiries from Yicai Global, stating that it had temporarily suspended its driverless testing and commercial operation services in the UAE. On the same day, WeRide responded to Yicai Global, stating that after communication with local regulatory authorities, WeRide's Robotaxi fleets in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE, and Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, continue normal public commercial operations. The Robotaxi fleet in Dubai, UAE, has been temporarily suspended and is awaiting notification for resumption. On March 5th, Chinese unmanned delivery company Neolix temporarily suspended the daily operations of its unmanned vehicles in Abu Dhabi, UAE. [Commentary] The Middle East is considered a preferred destination for Chinese autonomous driving companies going overseas. This suspension of services is to cooperate with the unified deployment of relevant UAE authorities and effectively ensure travel safety and operational order. Several companies have made proper arrangements for their local teams to fully ensure the safety and stability of employees and are currently maintaining close communication with local regulatory agencies and partners. Relevant business operations will be resumed in a timely manner in strict accordance with official guidelines. Orca Entertainment Group Undergoes Organizational Adjustment Alibaba's Orca Entertainment Group has undergone a new round of major organizational adjustments. It is reported that Fan Luyuan, Chairman and CEO of Orca Entertainment Group, recently sent an internal email to the company's core management announcing an organizational upgrade to actively embrace AI and accelerate the integration of an "online + offline" all-scenario entertainment ecosystem. The email indicates that Du Yanlong has been appointed CTO of Orca Entertainment Group, and Wu Qian (Guangying) will serve as President of Youku. He Mi (Yifeng) and Shen Yan (Zuiweng) will rotate positions, serving as Vice President of Orca Entertainment Group and President of Damai Live respectively. title_en: J.P. Morgan Chase Bank (China) Co., Ltd. Vice President Gu Wei: Leadership is Not Defined by Gender | Her Interview
body_en: In the vast landscape of the financial industry, "she power" is flourishing. Having been deeply involved in global corporate payments and treasury management for many years, Wei Gu, Vice President of JPMorgan Chase Bank (China) Co., Ltd., Head of Global Corporate Payments Greater China, and Product Director Greater China, has witnessed and deeply participated in the key process of China's financial market opening up to the outside world. On the occasion of International Women's Day on March 8th, Wei Gu was interviewed by a reporter from "International Finance News." Juggling multiple roles, she leads her team in continuous innovation in global corporate payments while also connecting the market from a broader perspective, making greater contributions to the development of JPMorgan Chase's corporate banking in China. **Being a Good "Bridge"** Innovation is an unchanging footnote etched in Wei Gu's career trajectory. She recalls that when she first entered the field of global corporate payments, online banking had just been introduced in China, and foreign banks were still in the exploratory stage of conducting RMB business. This track itself was full of possibilities for pioneering and innovation. Seizing the opportunity of the times and her personal aspirations, Wei Gu embarked on her own career journey. Throughout her career, she has always played the role of a "bridge," leveraging policy tailwinds to introduce mature overseas business models into China, and then combining them with technological iteration and innovation to promote the sustained and healthy development of global corporate payments. Reflecting on this experience, she sincerely remarked, "I am quite fortunate." Today, amidst the reshaping of the global trade landscape and the wave of digital transformation, cross-border e-commerce, as a new form of foreign trade, is developing rapidly, posing new challenges to Wei Gu's work. In her view, the scale of the e-commerce industry will continue to accelerate. "At the same time, e-commerce businesses are mostly small-value, high-frequency transactions. The core needs of small and medium-sized sellers are concentrated in fund arrival efficiency, exchange rate risk hedging, simplified payment processes, and cost and risk control, which are also the future development directions for the industry," Wei Gu stated. As the first foreign bank to launch a series of cross-border electronic payment solutions in the market, JPMorgan Chase has always been committed to empowering cross-border e-commerce with professional services and solutions. According to Wei Gu, the company has been deeply involved in cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain, achieving real-time, efficient, and low-cost transactions, significantly improving the efficiency of corporate fund circulation. Relying on its global network covering over 100 markets and localized experience, it helps enterprises deeply integrate into local payment and clearing environments, reduce exchange rate risks and exposures, and achieve efficient treasury management and risk hedging. Furthermore, JPMorgan Chase maintains close communication with regulatory authorities, actively providing feedback on the changes and core needs of small and medium-sized e-commerce business models, and calling for more facilitation measures for them. Wei Gu admitted that small and medium-sized e-commerce businesses have relatively limited resources in terms of manpower and material resources, and may not be able to adapt to the regulatory models of traditional large-scale B2B (business-to-business) trade. Consideration can be given to easing their burdens under strict risk control to support the stable development of small and medium-sized e-commerce, thereby better supporting the real economy. **Embarking on the "Mandatory Question"** In today's era where artificial intelligence is rapidly integrating into all industries, "AI+" is no longer an option but a mandatory question posed by the times, and the field of global corporate payments is also at the forefront of this wave of change. Wei Gu believes that the core value of artificial intelligence lies in significantly improving operational efficiency. JPMorgan Chase invests as much as $18 billion annually in technology, and this year it is expected to increase to $19.8 billion, which includes continuous investment in artificial intelligence. "Whether in overseas or Chinese markets, we will do our best to promote the in-depth application of artificial intelligence technology, driving business processes towards automation and intelligence," Wei Gu said. The reporter learned that in 2025, JPMorgan Chase Bank (China) Co., Ltd. announced the completion of its foreign exchange business reform, becoming the first foreign bank to implement the policy after the State Administration of Foreign Exchange introduced the "1+6" supporting policies for foreign exchange business reform. This innovative practice not only marks the acceleration of digital transformation in China's cross-border financial services but also outlines a new blueprint for global cross-border trade and investment and financing with the concept of "integrity empowering efficiency." Wei Gu explained that the core purpose of the foreign exchange business reform is to promote greater convenience in cross-border transactions. In the past, enterprises needed to provide a large number of supporting documents for cross-border transactions, which was cumbersome and time-consuming. After the reform, the bank conducts a one-time pre-investigation of the enterprise, not only to fully understand its business model and operating data but also to integrate relevant information into its internal intelligent system. Subsequently, the system will track the enterprise's historical transaction data and monitor new businesses in real-time, dynamically updating customer profiles to build a three-in-one business system of "intelligent customer profiling, differentiated risk control engine, and real-time transaction monitoring." For compliant and risk-controlled transactions, they can be processed directly through electronic instructions, replacing traditional document review. Through this model, the processing time for cross-border business has been reduced by an average of 50%-75%. Today, foreign currency payments or cross-border transactions can be as efficient and convenient as domestic RMB real-time transfers, greatly optimizing the corporate experience and truly realizing "letting data run, letting trust grow." "The policy dividends of 'the more integrity, the more convenience' are being transformed into tangible benefits for enterprises through technological innovation," Wei Gu emphasized. **"Focusing on the Most Critical"** It is not difficult to see that global corporate payments business highly relies on attention to detail, compliance awareness, and communication skills. Currently, women account for more than half of the team led by Wei Gu. "Payments are a systematic job connected by countless small details," Wei Gu said. Relatively speaking, women are often more meticulous and patient, possessing natural advantages in relevant positions. At the same time, many women can play a unique role in team cohesion and empathy, injecting positive energy into team collaboration. However, she also emphasized that excellent professional qualities are not gender-specific, and many ability differences are essentially individual differences, not gender differences. "Frankly speaking, in management positions, both men and women must have the ability to face problems directly, make decisive decisions, and promote efficiently. This is a basic requirement of leadership and has nothing to do with gender." When discussing how women can achieve breakthroughs in the workplace, Wei Gu also shared her thoughts. She pointed out that in traditional social expectations, women are often given multiple roles—wife, mother, daughter. Each identity requires time and energy, and coupled with career pursuits, it is easy to fall into a dilemma of scattered energy and difficulty in balancing. In Wei Gu's opinion, for women to go further, the key is not to "want this, want that, and want more," but to learn to make choices, prioritize, and allocate time and energy reasonably. In limited time, focusing on the most critical and essential tasks can achieve a higher quality of balance. She cited her own experience as an example: after returning to work from maternity leave, she had to shoulder the heavy responsibility of team management while also taking care of her young child, once falling into a state of double anxiety of "not doing work well and not taking good care of the child," and her mood was very low. Later, after actively adjusting, Wei Gu set clear boundaries for herself: ensure focus and efficiency during work hours, and leave on time to accompany her family. "I no longer dwell on doing everything myself, but learned to grasp the key points and delegate some work to the team. This not only solved my problem but also promoted the growth of the team." It was this clear choice that allowed Wei Gu to quickly emerge from a temporary state of imbalance and achieve a balance between work and family. Of course, as a manager, Wei Gu's concept of balance is not only about herself but also extends to the entire team. Reasonably allocating team resources, paying attention to the status of team members, and helping everyone find a balance between work and family to maintain the team's efficient, healthy, and sustainable combat effectiveness are important management topics for her. "True empowerment is to allow everyone to work with peace of mind and live with composure," Wei Gu said. For women in the financial industry who have just entered the workplace, Wei Gu finally shared two pieces of advice: First, have enough courage, especially the courage to make mistakes. The cost of making mistakes is very low when you are young; do not hesitate to try or hold back because of the fear of making mistakes. Second, attach importance to the cultivation of communication skills. Women often have strong empathy, which can help them step out of their own perspectives, better understand others, and make communication more efficient and smooth. "For newcomers entering the workplace, communication skills are a crucial skill, and women's advantages can make communication more warm and effective." title_en: China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises Holds Closed-door Seminar on "Accurately Analyzing New Tax Policies and Jointly Promoting High-Quality Development of Small and Medium Enterprises"
body_en: China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises Holds Closed-door Seminar on "Accurately Interpreting New Tax Policies and Jointly Promoting High-Quality Development of SMEs" Release Date: 2026-03-10 To assist SMEs and internet platform enterprises in accurately grasping policy trends after the implementation of the "Regulations on Tax Information Reporting by Internet Platform Enterprises," enhance tax management compliance, and prevent tax risks, the China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises held a closed-door seminar in Beijing on March 8, 2026, titled "Accurately Interpreting New Platform Tax Policies and Promoting High-Quality Development of SMEs." The seminar brought together the wisdom of experts, scholars, and enterprise representatives to jointly explore compliant development paths for the platform economy's taxation and promote high-quality development for SMEs through standardized management. Through cross-industry exchanges and in-depth dialogues among various guests from academia and the business community, the seminar further helped SMEs accurately understand the implications of the new tax policies, enhance their tax compliance management capabilities, and simultaneously promoted internet platform enterprises to conduct platform services more efficiently and in a standardized manner, thereby building a fairer and more orderly market environment. Concurrently, representatives of merchants and platforms discussed and proposed suggestions for further improving the new tax policies. Experts and scholars advised that the new platform tax policies should follow the scientific judgment of the "15th Five-Year Plan" on the macroeconomy, manage expectations effectively, maintain consistency in macroeconomic policy orientation, and avoid negative impacts of policies on business operations. The China Association of Small and Medium Enterprises will also take this seminar as an opportunity to continuously collect the development needs of SMEs, play its role as a bridge and link, offer suggestions for the improvement of national fiscal and tax policies, and help SMEs and the platform economy achieve stable and long-term development on the path of compliant growth.

body_en: [Financial Calendar] China January-February Trade Balance Earnings Release: NIO ►►According to CCTV Finance, the domestic refined oil retail price adjustment window will open upwards at 24:00 on March 9th. According to monitoring by the Price Monitoring Center of the National Development and Reform Commission, during this refined oil price adjustment period, international oil prices rose sharply due to the continuous escalation of the US-Iran conflict. Starting from 24:00 on March 9th, the domestic retail prices of gasoline and diesel will be increased by 695 yuan and 670 yuan per ton, respectively. On average nationwide: 92 octane gasoline, 95 octane gasoline, and 0 octane diesel will be increased by 0.55 yuan, 0.58 yuan, and 0.57 yuan, respectively. According to this calculation, filling a 50-liter fuel tank with 92 octane gasoline will cost an additional 27.5 yuan. ►►On March 9th, companies such as *ST Jinglun and *ST Haiyuan issued announcements warning investors of delisting risks. Among them, *ST Jinglun has already "booked" delisting after releasing its performance forecast. On the same day, *ST Dasheng, *ST Dongyi, and *ST Jinke all issued their third risk warning announcements regarding possible termination of listing. However, due to improved performance or the implementation of restructuring, the above three companies may temporarily lift the delisting alert. ►►Tencent announced the launch of its all-scenario AI intelligent agent WorkBuddy. This product has capabilities similar to "Lobster" OpenClaw and is compatible with "Lobster." WorkBuddy is built with over 20 types of Skills skill packages and the MCP protocol. The intelligent agent was widely used within Tencent before its official release. Users can "remote control" Tencent's version of "Lobster" via their mobile phones. Currently, it supports controlling the intelligent agent to perform tasks through communication tools such as WeChat Work, QQ, Feishu, and DingTalk. ►►According to Xinhua News Agency, US President Trump said at a press conference on the 9th that due to market volatility caused by US and Israeli attacks on Iran, he would cancel some oil-related sanctions to stabilize oil prices. Trump also said that the war with Iran would end "soon," but "not" this week. ►►According to reports, a G7 official revealed that G7 finance ministers reached a broad consensus on Monday regarding whether to immediately release strategic petroleum reserves, deciding not to take this action for now. G7 finance ministers held a conference call on Monday morning to discuss how to respond to the surge in oil prices caused by the US and Israeli war on Iran. They stated in a statement that they are prepared to take "necessary measures" to support global energy supply, including releasing inventories, but no decision has been made to implement it yet. ►►On Monday, the three major US stock indices opened lower and rose higher. As of the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.50%, the Nasdaq Composite Index rose 1.38%, and the S&P 500 Index rose 0.83%. The chip sector strengthened, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rising 3.93%, AMD up 5.33%, Broadcom up 4.62%, TSMC up 2.89%, and Nvidia up 2.72%. The storage sector performed well, with Seagate Technology and Western Digital rising more than 6%, and Micron Technology up 5.14%. Star tech stocks generally rose, with Google up 2.66%, Apple up 0.94%, Tesla up 0.49%, Meta up 0.39%, and Amazon and Microsoft up more than 0.1%. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index rose 1.76%, with Baidu up 2.88%, JD.com up 1.63%, Alibaba up 1.41%, Pinduoduo up 0.66%, and NetEase down 0.11%. WTI crude oil near-month contracts rose 4.26% to $94.77 per barrel, and Brent crude oil near-month contracts rose 6.76% to $98.96 per barrel. Tinci Materials: Net profit in 2025 increased by 181% year-on-year, plans to distribute 3 yuan per 10 shares. Chengdu Huawu: Released a high-speed 10-bit 128GSPS A/D converter chip. Qiangyi Co., Ltd.: Plans to invest 1 billion yuan to build a semiconductor probe card manufacturing base project. Zhuhai CosMX: Plans to raise no more than 3.3 billion yuan for projects including the construction of lithium batteries for smartphone steel casings. Hexin Instruments: The company's stock trading is experiencing abnormal fluctuations and may be subject to delisting risk warning. *ST Jinglun: The company's stock may be delisted due to a market capitalization below 500 million yuan. *ST Haiyuan: If the relevant indicators after audit in 2025 meet the prescribed circumstances, the company's stock will be delisted. COFCO Engineering & Technology: Shengliang Investment and its concerted parties plan to jointly reduce their holdings by no more than 3% of shares. Zhongbei Communication: Signed a service procurement contract worth 429 million yuan to provide computing resource services and related resources. Guotai Huitong: The market has been volatile recently, focusing on the recovery of value stocks and emerging technology sectors. title_en: Two Sessions | Leaders of Ten Top Brokerages Speak Out! Discussing the Development Direction of the Securities Industry
body_en: 2026 marks the beginning of the "15th Five-Year Plan" and a crucial year for China's economy to gather momentum on the track of high-quality development. Recently, the chairmen and CEOs of 10 leading securities firms, including CITIC Securities, Guotai Junan Securities, Huatai Securities, GF Securities, China Galaxy Securities, Guosen Securities, China Merchants Securities, Shenwan Hongyuan Securities, CICC, and CITIC Securities, published signed articles or accepted media interviews to share their profound insights on the reform and development of the capital market, focusing on the study of the Government Work Report and the "15th Five-Year Plan." Overall, the leaders of these securities firms share similar sentiments, believing that the Government Work Report signals a policy of "seeking progress while maintaining stability and improving quality and efficiency," makes clear deployments for the reform and development of the capital market, and provides specific guidance for the high-quality development of securities companies. So, how can policy deployments be translated into practical actions? Through their sharing, the mission and path of the securities industry in the new journey are becoming clear. **Technological Finance will become a key direction for the capability building of securities companies.** This year's Government Work Report places significant emphasis on the capital market. In the section on government work tasks for 2026, it states: "Strengthen financial services for the entire chain and lifecycle of technological innovation. For technology-based enterprises in key core technology fields, implement a normalized 'green channel' mechanism for listing and financing, and mergers and acquisitions, to support innovation and creation with technological finance." "This statement sends a very clear policy signal: the capital market will play a more important role in supporting technological innovation," said Chen Liang, Chairman of CICC. Wang Sheng, Chairman of China Galaxy Securities, also believes that the Government Work Report clarifies the development direction of the capital market, with the primary focus being to strengthen financial support for technological innovation and accelerate the formation of new quality productive forces. He believes that the capital market needs to focus on strategic emerging industries and future industries such as integrated circuits, quantum technology, artificial intelligence, and the low-altitude economy, improve the full-chain financing service system, guide capital to accelerate its aggregation in key core technology fields, and promote the faster industrialization of technological achievements. Securities companies, as important intermediaries and bridges in the capital market, have a significant role to play. Zhang Youjun, Chairman of CITIC Securities, stated that technological finance will become a key direction for the capability building of securities companies. They need to enhance their research and pricing capabilities for new industries and new tracks, as well as their services for mergers, acquisitions, and capital operations, thereby enhancing their own value in supporting innovation and creation. Lin Chuanhui, Chairman of GF Securities, believes that securities companies need to continuously improve their capabilities in value discovery, value cultivation, and value realization. They should work with government investment funds, long-term institutional capital, and social capital to form synergy, promote the formation of innovation capital through multiple channels, accompany innovative enterprises through the "valley of death" in R&D, and guide the aggregation of factor resources towards new quality productive forces. Liu Jian, Chairman of Shenwan Hongyuan, also emphasized the need for securities companies to enhance their value discovery capabilities. In his view, securities companies should strengthen their substantive judgment on the feasibility of technological routes, the innovation and sustainability of core technologies, and deeply mine and cultivate high-quality enterprises with innovative capabilities and development potential. On the other hand, he mentioned that securities companies need to continuously innovate investment banking service models. They should build a "technology expert + industry expert + investment banking expert" model to solve the problem of divergent investment logic among different investors and enhance their service capabilities for technology innovation industries. They should also build an integrated "data assets + large models + scenario landing" model to enhance their service capabilities for new forms of intelligent economy. Furthermore, they should build a "strategic consulting + mergers and acquisitions + industrial going global" transformation service model to address the insufficient supply of transformation financial services faced by traditional industries, and enhance their service capabilities for traditional industries by leveraging integrated services from strategic consulting, financial optimization, capital operations, industrial integration, to cross-border financing. **Further leverage the role of the most important link connecting investors and financers.** The Government Work Report also proposes to "continuously deepen the comprehensive reform of investment and financing in the capital market, further improve the mechanism for long-term capital to enter the market, perfect the investor protection system, expand exit channels for private equity and venture capital funds, and increase the proportion of direct financing and equity financing." The leaders of various securities firms have meticulously analyzed and interpreted these proposals, with "deepening comprehensive reform of investment and financing" receiving the most attention. "Comprehensive reform of investment and financing is the 'key' for the current capital market to shift from scale expansion to quality and efficiency improvement. Reforms on the investment side optimize policies for long-term capital to enter the market, reforms on the financing side improve the functions of multi-level market segments, and reforms on the institutional side build a safety net for investor protection," said Zhang Nasha, Chairman of Guosen Securities. So, what should securities companies do? Zhu Jian, Chairman of Guotai Junan Securities, stated that securities companies should focus on the key task of improving the coordinated functions of investment and financing in the capital market, and further leverage their role as the most important bridge and link connecting investors and financers, to help enhance the inclusiveness and adaptability of the capital market system. Lin Chuanhui further pointed out that on the financing side, securities companies should deeply cultivate industry research, accurately serve technology innovation enterprises, make good use of equity financing and mergers and acquisitions tools, and help more excellent enterprises representing new quality productive forces to land in the capital market. On the investment side, they should strengthen product innovation, provide professional and diversified allocation channels for long-term capital to enter the market, help "long-term flowing water" to precisely irrigate high-quality assets, guide the concepts of rational investment, value investment, and long-term investment, and effectively improve the sense of security and gain for investors. Regarding "further improving the mechanism for long-term capital to enter the market and perfecting the investor protection system," Liu Cheng, Chairman of CITIC Securities, believes that the combination of these two points essentially aims to further solidify the foundation of the "investment market" at the institutional level, allowing the capital market to better balance financing functions, investment functions, and wealth management functions. "Investor protection" has been explicitly written into the Government Work Report again after 14 years. Chen Liang stated that investor protection is an important foundation for the stable operation of the capital market. By improving institutional construction and strengthening investor protection, market confidence can be further enhanced, the credibility of the capital market can be improved, and a more solid foundation can be laid for the long-term healthy development of the capital market. "Investor protection is the concentrated embodiment of the 'people-centered' nature of the capital market, and the capital market should make greater contributions to the preservation and appreciation of people's wealth," said Huo Da, Chairman of China Merchants Securities. He believes that by increasing residents' property income, the capital market can also make its due contribution to expanding domestic demand. Based on this, Huo Da stated that the capital market should strengthen ex-ante prevention and in-process supervision, strictly control unqualified investors from participating in high-risk transactions through differentiated risk assessment standards. At the same time, it should improve ex-post relief and accountability mechanisms, consolidate the responsibility of operating institutions for protecting small and medium investors, and strengthen investor protection education and publicity. Regarding the improvement of the mechanism for long-term capital to enter the market, Zhou Yi, CEO of Huatai Securities, believes that securities companies should, on the one hand, enhance their wealth management capabilities and innovate long-term, stable asset management products, guiding residents' wealth to be allocated to the capital market through compliant channels for the long term, promoting both domestic demand expansion and wealth appreciation. On the other hand, they should strengthen institutional service capabilities, providing customized asset allocation, research consulting, and transaction custody services for long-term funds such as social security and insurance, to help long-term funds precisely invest in high-quality industries and technology innovation enterprises. In addition, they should improve the asset management business system and promote the transformation of investment concepts from short-term speculation to long-term value investment. **The service logic will emphasize specialization, comprehensiveness, and long-term orientation.** "Expanding exit channels for private equity and venture capital funds, and increasing the proportion of direct financing and equity financing" has also sparked heated discussions among securities firm leaders. Liu Cheng believes that the above statement in the Government Work Report is connected with deployments such as "strengthening financial services for the entire chain and lifecycle of technological innovation," which means that the focus of the capital market's support for technological innovation is further extending from single financing support to a more complete capital formation chain, including listing, mergers and acquisitions, and exits, with a greater emphasis on improving resource allocation efficiency and promoting the optimization and upgrading of industrial and supply chains through market-oriented means. Specifically, he believes that venture capital exits are the most incremental and structurally significant part of this year's capital market deployments. Judging from the changes in the Government Work Report from 2024 to 2026, the policy logic has shifted from encouraging development to facilitating circulation. Venture capital investment is essentially a complete chain of "fundraising, investment, management, and exit." Facilitating fund circulation and improving exit mechanisms is not only an urgent demand for venture capital funds but also provides more opportunities for listed companies to expand through mergers and acquisitions and optimize their industrial layout. Zhang Youjun shares a similar view and also proposed that for securities companies, the service logic will emphasize specialization, comprehensiveness, and long-term orientation, enhancing the quality and efficiency of the capital market's service to the real economy with stronger pricing capabilities, industrial understanding, and resource integration capabilities. The statement "increasing the proportion of equity financing" also carries significant weight. Chen Liang pointed out that the Government Work Report explicitly proposes for the first time to increase the proportion of equity financing, reflecting an important direction for further optimizing China's financial structure. Regarding how securities companies can implement policy requirements, Zhou Yi proposed specific ideas from both the financing and investment sides, combining them with business practices. On the financing side, investment banking businesses of securities companies need to closely align with the needs of technological self-reliance and industrial upgrading, further enhance their adaptability to serving the real economy, play the role of investment banks as value discoverers, and strictly control the quality of listed companies. On the investment side, they need to deepen the reform of public funds, optimize the "fundraising, investment, management, and exit" mechanism for venture capital, promote various types of long-term capital to enter the market, and optimize the allocation of financial resources. Securities companies need to strengthen investor education and suitability management, enrich diversified investment products, guide capital to gather in "hard technology" sectors such as artificial intelligence, high-end manufacturing, and biomedicine, and contribute to the development of new quality productive forces. **Building differentiated and specialized operating models.** The Government Work Report also sets requirements for the development of financial institutions, proposing to "regulate the competitive order of financial institutions and deeply promote the reduction and quality improvement of local small and medium-sized financial institutions." Zhu Jian stated that the relevant deployments effectively carry forward the requirements of the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China regarding financial institutions "focusing on their main business, improving governance, and developing in a differentiated manner," pointing the way for the high-quality development of securities companies. In his view, securities companies should adhere to their main responsibilities, focus on their main business, leverage their own resource endowments, deepen institutional reforms, play to their comparative advantages, build differentiated and specialized operating models, firmly hold the bottom line of not having systemic risks, and steadily build first-class investment banks. Zhang Youjun stated that this will prompt securities companies to further emphasize the importance of compliant operations, corporate governance, and risk management, promoting a pattern of "standardized development, characteristic development, and differentiated development." Leading institutions should continue to improve their comprehensive services and international capabilities, while small and medium-sized institutions should strengthen and specialize in regional focus and segmented sectors. Liu Jian shared specific insights on how securities companies can enhance their risk management capabilities. He mentioned that securities companies should, on the one hand, enhance their ability to judge technological risks, energy risks, and innovation risks based on the risk-return characteristics of new elements, new materials, and new energy. They should provide more risk management tools for enterprises and investors by offering structured risk hedging products and optimizing market-making transactions, and engage in proactive risk management. On the other hand, they should tell the story of China's stock market well, and leverage the role of key opinion leaders such as chief economists and industry analysts to actively speak out during critical periods, telling the story of China's economy, Chinese enterprises, and the A-share market with objective and professional voices, enhancing investors' long-term investment confidence, and responding to external market fluctuations objectively and rationally to ensure the stable and healthy operation of the capital market. In addition to the above, securities firm leaders also shared in-depth thoughts on topics such as how to do wealth management well and how to serve high-level opening up. Furthermore, the leaders of these 10 securities firms unanimously stated that they will aim to become first-class investment banks and achieve their own high-quality development by serving national strategies.
