title_en: National People's Congress Deputy Zhao Wanping: Anchoring the Value Leap of Supply Chains, Integrating Digital and Real Economies to Activate Industrial Momentum
body_en: During the 2026 Two Sessions, Zhao Wanping, a National People's Congress deputy and vice president of the Anhui Academy of Agricultural Sciences, was interviewed by 21st Century Business Herald. In his view, China's traditional industries are currently at a critical window for value chain upgrading. The integration of digital and real economies, along with new business models like cross-border e-commerce, are the core drivers for overcoming industrial development pain points and activating new growth momentum. Based on his extensive frontline industry research, Zhao Wanping systematically analyzed the phased characteristics of China's manufacturing and foreign trade development. He pointed out that the industry is currently undergoing a profound transformation from "scale expansion" to "quality and efficiency improvement." Accordingly, he proposed three targeted recommendations aimed at providing more practical and actionable pathways for the upgrading of traditional industries and the expansion of "Made in China" into global markets. Zhao Wanping. Photo courtesy of the source. Zhao Wanping noted that in 2025, China's economy will move forward under pressure, developing towards new and high-quality growth, with the continuous advancement of modern industrial system construction. Traditional industries remain the fundamental base of China's industrial system, continuing to play a "ballast stone" role in economic development. According to data from the National Bureau of Statistics, the added value of China's secondary industry increased by 4.9% year-on-year in the first three quarters of 2025, cumulatively contributing 35.9% to the GDP in the first three quarters, solidifying the core foundation of the real economy's development. As of 2023, China has developed over 1,100 industrial clusters. Zhao Wanping pointed out that some large industrial clusters have over 5,000 merchants and factories, and even some small and medium-sized industrial clusters have two to three thousand market entities, an irreplaceable scale advantage. Focusing domestically, Zhao Wanping observed that the scale development of domestic supply chains has approached the industrial margin, and the problems and drawbacks accumulated during development are also gradually emerging. For example, intensified price competition due to product homogenization and insufficient branding leading to weak innovation are becoming core bottlenecks restricting high-quality industrial development. "China's current consumer groups are undergoing a generational transition, with diversified demands and personalized consumption emerging. The traditional production capacity advantage and OEM model can no longer match the current rapidly changing consumption trends. The product capabilities, manufacturing capabilities, and industrial systems of front-end merchants and back-end factories urgently need to be reshaped," he told reporters. Particularly noteworthy are the continuous changes in international geopolitics and tariff policies, the acceleration of a new round of technological revolution, and the new challenges and opportunities facing economic and trade growth. Traditional industrial clusters are entering a critical window for supply chain value upgrading. The deep integration of digital technology and the real economy is reshaping the operation of industrial and supply chains. Zhao Wanping believes that the emergence of new e-commerce and cross-border e-commerce business models has significantly shortened the supply and demand chain, greatly improved market efficiency, and brought new opportunities for the development of upstream and downstream supply chains. He observed that the downward diffusion of digital capabilities is having a profound impact. Taking new e-commerce platforms like Pinduoduo as an example, through initiatives such as the "Go West" strategy and express delivery to villages, they have extended digital supply chain capabilities to remote areas, opening up two-way circulation channels between urban and rural areas and creating broader conditions for county-level industrial clusters to integrate into the digital system. He pointed out that this deep penetration not only solves the logistics pain points in remote areas but also, through data empowerment, enables production factors at the end of the chain to quickly respond to market demand. At the national strategic level, the positioning of cross-border e-commerce has also become clearer. The "15th Five-Year Plan" proposal explicitly calls for adhering to high-quality development, leading the development of new quality productive forces, and supporting the development of new business models such as cross-border e-commerce. In this context, Zhao Wanping pointed out that leveraging the digital technology capabilities of new business models such as new e-commerce and cross-border e-commerce, and focusing on high-quality supply chain development, is an effective way to promote industrial upgrading and achieve industrial value upgrading. Deep integration between industrial cluster merchants and new market entities like e-commerce platforms will facilitate the use of digital technology to promote product upgrades, technological iteration, and brand transformation of the supply chain. Zhao Wanping pointed out that China's e-commerce currently has a leading advantage in some areas due to its high efficiency and innovation capabilities formed by its super-large market. Domestic platforms, represented by Pinduoduo's cross-border e-commerce, are expanding Chinese models and standards overseas and continuously feeding back into domestic supply chains in practice, promoting business iteration and upgrading. This "feedback" effect is an important driving force for supply chain evolution. He believes that such digital capabilities based on a global perspective can improve overall risk resistance. Promoting the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy is not only a key measure for China to reshape the resilience of its industrial and supply chains and cope with external environmental challenges but also a strategic support for enhancing China's ability to respond to external challenges. Photo courtesy of the source. Based on in-depth research on the current state of the industry, Zhao Wanping proposed specific recommendations from three dimensions: deepening digital-real economy integration, expanding cross-border e-commerce, and upgrading new quality supply, providing clear implementation paths for the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries. First, comprehensively deepen the integration of digital and real economies to help enhance the value of industrial and supply chains. He pointed out that the large-scale construction of China's manufacturing industry over the years has led to the explosive development of supporting supply chain systems, laying the foundation for China's industrial chains to hold an irreplaceable position in global competition. The digital transformation of traditional advantageous manufacturing industries can not only improve the intelligence level and collaborative efficiency of supply chains but also enhance the flexibility and stability of industrial chains in responding to external shocks. Taking Shenzhen's digital products as an example, there are hundreds of suppliers for a single component like a car camera, and the upstream and downstream suppliers for the entire product can reach thousands. He believes that to achieve high-quality development of China's industrial and supply chains, it is necessary to rely on digital technologies such as big data, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence, and to link with the e-commerce platform ecosystem directly facing consumers to achieve efficient coordination of information flow, logistics, and capital flow. Especially when digital capabilities fully penetrate all aspects of the supply chain, it can drive upstream and downstream "cumulative innovation" with new quality merchants as the link and product innovation as the handle, thereby optimizing the structure and improving profits. Second, vigorously encourage cross-border e-commerce to set sail and go global, promoting "Made in China" to the global market. Zhao Wanping pointed out that after more than 20 years of development, new platforms such as social e-commerce and live-streaming e-commerce have become strong engines driving the development of new quality industries, while cross-border e-commerce is still in its pioneering stage of high-speed development. In the past decade, the growth rate of China's cross-border e-commerce imports and exports has consistently exceeded the overall growth rate of trade, and its proportion in the total trade volume has been increasing, becoming a core new driving force for foreign trade growth. Zhao Wanping mentioned that Pinduoduo's cross-border e-commerce platform, for example, has covered more than 90 countries and regions worldwide within three years of its establishment in 2022, and has achieved considerable market scale in most countries globally. Relying on China's complete supply chain system, the platform is exploring sustainable operating models in different markets with a long-term development orientation. He believes that the vigorous development of China's cross-border e-commerce has created new opportunities for the transformation and upgrading of China's industrial and supply chains. The innovative models such as "full custody" and "half custody" introduced by the platform have allowed a large number of industrial cluster factories to move from behind the scenes to the forefront for the first time. Compared with the traditional foreign trade order-taking model, OEM factories can directly connect with global consumers, innovate products according to the needs of different markets, explore brand operations, drive industrial increment, and promote high-quality supply chain development. Third, accelerate the upgrading of "new quality supply" on e-commerce platforms to help industrial clusters develop brands. According to data from the Ministry of Commerce, since the "14th Five-Year Plan," the overall scale of China's digital consumption has exceeded 23.8 trillion yuan, making it the world's largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years, with the leading role of digital consumption continuing to be prominent. He suggested encouraging e-commerce platforms to leverage their digital advantages to assist industrial clusters in accelerating the cultivation of a group of "new quality merchants" who, in addition to production capacity, possess product, technology, and marketing capabilities to match diversified market demands, play a leading role, and drive small and medium-sized merchants in industrial clusters to complete new quality transformation, thereby promoting the brand-oriented, high-quality development of industrial clusters. Currently, this development path has been effectively validated in numerous practices. Taking the Yiwu small commodity industrial cluster in Zhejiang as an example, e-commerce platforms use their data advantages to help merchants select products with potential for explosive sales, assisting them in product innovation. After local merchants developed and upgraded small commodities such as microwave oven covers and press-type ice cube trays, many single products achieved multi-fold profit growth, fully verifying the practical value of new quality supply upgrades. title_en: Hangzhou Innovates with "Credit Accounts"
body_en: To address pain points such as unclear enterprise credit fundamentals and insufficient application and transformation, in recent years, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, has seized the opportunity to undertake the national innovative pilot for the credit system construction of market entities. It has innovatively launched the enterprise "Credit Account," establishing a comprehensive mobile credit file for over 1.1 million enterprises in the city, transforming abstract credit into quantifiable and usable development capital for businesses. Credit construction is data-driven. Hangzhou's "Credit Account" establishes a data-sharing mechanism among government, enterprises, and third-party platforms, forming multi-dimensional and three-dimensional data support to create a "credit portrait" of enterprises throughout their entire lifecycle. Currently, 1.04 billion government department data points and 1.25 billion voluntarily disclosed enterprise information have been collected, and third-party platforms have been introduced to evaluate the credit information of over a million enterprises. A quantitative credit evaluation model covering 6 major dimensions and 37 indicators has been built, enabling daily dynamic assessment of credit status. Enterprises can intuitively and clearly understand their credit status through the "Zhejiang Enterprise Online" mobile app, similar to checking a bank account. In terms of credit compliance improvement, Hangzhou has innovatively launched the "AI Credit Steward," utilizing artificial intelligence technology to provide enterprises with "credit health check" services, issuing "one enterprise, one policy" credit diagnostic reports, and offering easy-to-understand and actionable improvement suggestions. A credit expert team has been assembled to provide hands-on, supportive, and scheduled guidance services to enterprises through online consultations, on-site visits, and centralized training. Since the pilot program, 2,585 enterprises have been guided and assisted, and 118 high-quality credit management enterprises have been cultivated. Furthermore, Hangzhou has issued the nation's first quantitative evaluation standard for the credit management process of market entities – the "Evaluation Standards for Credit Management of Market Entities," covering multiple dimensions such as system construction, process execution, personnel capabilities, and risk response, guiding enterprises to implement credit compliance requirements throughout their entire operational management process. The value of credit lies in its application. In terms of financing and loans, Hangzhou has launched a "Credit + Financial Services" pilot program, using credit account information as an important reference for financial institutions' credit granting decisions. Currently, credit products have been launched, and loans totaling 104 million yuan have been issued. In terms of business cooperation, "Credit Account" information is incorporated into third-party platform evaluation systems, helping trustworthy enterprises obtain more business opportunities. Meanwhile, Xiaoshan District has launched a "Credit + Transportation" pilot program, providing exclusive benefits such as VIP waiting areas, fast lanes, and air ticket discounts for 460 enterprises with excellent credit. Qiantang District has launched a "Credit + Park Development" pilot program, issuing special credit development reports for over 100 industrial parks, serving as an important decision-making reference for government departments to optimize industrial layout, for park management to identify and cultivate high-quality enterprises, and for entrepreneurs to efficiently select locations. In the next step, Hangzhou will continue to focus on expanding the scope of information collection, opening public query channels, establishing "Credit Accounts" for individual industrial and commercial households, and deepening multi-field scenario-driven applications. This will further promote the construction and application of "Credit Accounts," injecting strong "credit momentum" into the high-quality economic and social development of Hangzhou.
full_text: Hangzhou Innovates with "Credit Accounts". To address pain points such as unclear enterprise credit fundamentals and insufficient application and transformation, in recent years, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, has seized the opportunity to undertake the national innovative pilot for the credit system construction of market entities. It has innovatively launched the enterprise "Credit Account," establishing a comprehensive mobile credit file for over 1.1 million enterprises in the city, transforming abstract credit into quantifiable and usable development capital for businesses. Credit construction is data-driven. Hangzhou's "Credit Account" establishes a data-sharing mechanism among government, enterprises, and third-party platforms, forming multi-dimensional and three-dimensional data support to create a "credit portrait" of enterprises throughout their entire lifecycle. Currently, 1.04 billion government department data points and 1.25 billion voluntarily disclosed enterprise information have been collected, and third-party platforms have been introduced to evaluate the credit information of over a million enterprises. A quantitative credit evaluation model covering 6 major dimensions and 37 indicators has been built, enabling daily dynamic assessment of credit status. Enterprises can intuitively and clearly understand their credit status through the "Zhejiang Enterprise Online" mobile app, similar to checking a bank account. In terms of credit compliance improvement, Hangzhou has innovatively launched the "AI Credit Steward," utilizing artificial intelligence technology to provide enterprises with "credit health check" services, issuing "one enterprise, one policy" credit diagnostic reports, and offering easy-to-understand and actionable improvement suggestions. Furthermore, Hangzhou has issued the nation's first quantitative evaluation standard for the credit management process of market entities – the "Evaluation Standards for Credit Management of Market Entities," covering multiple dimensions such as system construction, process execution, personnel capabilities, and risk response, guiding enterprises to implement credit compliance requirements throughout their entire operational management process. title_en: National Bureau of Statistics: National economy started strongly and got off to a good start in January-February
body_en: (March 16, 2026) In January-February, under the strong leadership of the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, all regions and departments conscientiously implemented the decisions and deployments of the Party Central Committee and the State Council, adhered to the general principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability, implemented a more proactive and effective macro policy, increased counter-cyclical and cross-cyclical adjustments, continuously expanded domestic demand, optimized supply, improved incremental growth, and revitalized existing stock. Production and supply growth accelerated, market demand showed steady growth, employment and prices remained generally stable, new quality productive forces grew stronger, and the economy got off to a strong start with a good beginning. I. Industrial Production Accelerated, with Good Momentum in Equipment Manufacturing and High-Tech Manufacturing In January-February, the value-added of industrial enterprises above the designated size nationwide increased by 6.3% year-on-year, a 1.1 percentage point acceleration from December of the previous year. By sector, the value-added of the mining industry increased by 6.1% year-on-year, manufacturing by 6.6%, and production and supply of electricity, heat, gas, and water by 4.7%. The value-added of equipment manufacturing increased by 9.3% year-on-year, and that of high-tech manufacturing increased by 13.1%, both faster than the overall industrial growth by 3.0 and 6.8 percentage points, respectively. By ownership, the value-added of state-controlled enterprises increased by 4.2% year-on-year; joint-stock enterprises by 6.9%, foreign-funded and Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan-funded enterprises by 4.0%; and private enterprises by 7.4%. By product, the output of 3D printing equipment, lithium-ion batteries, and industrial robots increased by 54.1%, 42.6%, and 31.1% year-on-year, respectively. In terms of month-on-month changes, the value-added of industrial enterprises above the designated size in February increased by 0.83% compared to the previous month. In February, the Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index was 49.0%; the Business Activity Expectation Index was 53.2%, up 0.6 percentage points from the previous month. II. Services Sector Grew Relatively Fast, with Rapid Development of Modern Services In January-February, the national service production index increased by 5.2% year-on-year, a 0.2 percentage point acceleration from December of the previous year. By sector, the production indices for information transmission, software and information technology services, leasing and business services, finance, transportation, warehousing and postal services, and accommodation and catering increased by 10.1%, 8.2%, 7.0%, 6.3%, and 5.4%, respectively. In February, the Services Business Activity Index was 49.7%, up 0.2 percentage points from the previous month; the Services Business Activity Expectation Index was 55.8%. Among them, the business activity indices for accommodation, catering, and culture, sports, and entertainment were in a high prosperity range above 60.0%. III. Market Sales Growth Recovered, with Relatively Fast Growth in Service Retail In January-February, the total retail sales of consumer goods reached 8,607.9 billion yuan, an increase of 2.8% year-on-year, a 1.9 percentage point acceleration from December of the previous year. By location of operating units, retail sales of consumer goods in urban areas reached 7,444.9 billion yuan, an increase of 2.7%; retail sales of consumer goods in rural areas reached 1,163.0 billion yuan, an increase of 3.2%. By type of consumption, retail sales of goods reached 7,581.5 billion yuan, an increase of 2.5%; catering revenue reached 1,026.4 billion yuan, an increase of 4.8%. Sales of basic living necessities and some upgraded goods grew relatively fast. Retail sales of clothing, shoes, hats, and textiles, grain, oil, and food, communication equipment, and gold, silver, and jewelry above the designated size increased by 10.4%, 10.2%, 17.8%, and 13.0% year-on-year, respectively. In terms of month-on-month changes, total retail sales of consumer goods in February increased by 0.81% compared to the previous month. In January-February, service retail sales increased by 5.6% year-on-year, a 0.1 percentage point acceleration from the whole previous year. Among them, retail sales of communication and information services, tourism consulting and leasing services, and cultural, sports, and leisure services grew relatively fast. In January-February, online retail sales of goods and services nationwide reached 3,254.6 billion yuan, an increase of 9.2% year-on-year. Among them, online retail sales of goods reached 2,081.2 billion yuan, an increase of 10.3%, accounting for 24.2% of the total retail sales of consumer goods; online retail sales of services reached 1,173.4 billion yuan, an increase of 7.3%. IV. Fixed Asset Investment Turned from Decline to Growth, with Relatively Fast Growth in Infrastructure Investment In January-February, national fixed asset investment (excluding rural households) reached 5,272.1 billion yuan, an increase of 1.8% year-on-year, compared to a decrease of 3.8% for the whole previous year; excluding real estate development investment, national fixed asset investment increased by 5.2%. By sector, infrastructure investment increased by 11.4% year-on-year, manufacturing investment by 3.1%, and real estate development investment decreased by 11.1%. The sales area of new commercial residential buildings nationwide was 92.93 million square meters, a year-on-year decrease of 13.5%; the sales value of new commercial residential buildings was 818.6 billion yuan, a decrease of 20.2%. By industry, investment in the primary industry increased by 17.4% year-on-year, investment in the secondary industry by 5.4%, and investment in the tertiary industry decreased by 0.4%. Private investment decreased by 2.6% year-on-year, with the decline narrowing by 3.8 percentage points compared to the whole previous year; excluding real estate development investment, private investment increased by 1.0%. Investment in high-tech industries increased by 5.1% year-on-year, with investment in the aerospace manufacturing industry, research and development and design services, and information services increasing by 20.2%, 20.6%, and 16.5%, respectively. In terms of month-on-month changes, fixed asset investment (excluding rural households) in February increased by 0.39% compared to the previous month. V. Imports and Exports of Goods Grew Rapidly, with Continued Optimization of Trade Structure In January-February, the total value of goods imports and exports reached 7,732.1 billion yuan, an increase of 18.3% year-on-year, a 13.4 percentage point acceleration from December of the previous year. Among them, exports reached 4,617.8 billion yuan, an increase of 19.2%; imports reached 3,114.3 billion yuan, an increase of 17.1%. Imports and exports of general trade increased by 13.5% year-on-year. Imports and exports to countries jointly building the "Belt and Road" increased by 20.0%. Imports and exports of private enterprises increased by 22.8%. Exports of mechanical and electrical products increased by 24.3%. VI. Employment Situation Remained Generally Stable, with Urban Surveyed Unemployment Rate Remaining Flat Year-on-Year In January-February, the average urban surveyed unemployment rate nationwide was 5.3%, flat year-on-year. In February, the urban surveyed unemployment rate nationwide was 5.3%, up 0.1 percentage points from the previous month. The surveyed unemployment rate for local registered laborers was 5.4%; for migrant laborers, it was 5.0%, of which the surveyed unemployment rate for migrant agricultural laborers was 5.2%. The urban surveyed unemployment rate in 31 large cities was 5.1%. The average weekly working hours for employed personnel in enterprises nationwide was 48.1 hours. VII. Consumer Price Index Increased, while Producer Price Index Decline Narrowed In January-February, the national Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 0.8% year-on-year, with a 0.2% increase in January and a 1.3% increase in February. By category, in January-February, prices of food, tobacco, and beverages and dining out increased by 0.6% year-on-year, clothing by 1.9%, housing by -0.1%, household goods and services by 2.7%, transportation and communication by -2.1%, education, culture, and entertainment by 1.0%, medical and healthcare by 1.8%, and other goods and services by 14.3%. Among food, tobacco, and beverages and dining out prices, pork prices decreased by 11.2%, grain prices by 0.2%, fresh fruit prices increased by 4.5%, and fresh vegetable prices increased by 8.8%. The core CPI, excluding food and energy prices, rose by 1.3% year-on-year. In terms of month-on-month changes, the national CPI increased by 0.2% in January and 1.0% in February. In January-February, the national industrial producer ex-factory price index decreased by 1.2% year-on-year. By month, it decreased by 1.4% year-on-year in January and increased by 0.4% month-on-month; it decreased by 0.9% year-on-year in February and increased by 0.4% month-on-month. In January-February, the national industrial producer purchase price index decreased by 1.1% year-on-year. Overall, in January-February, major economic indicators showed a significant rebound, and the national economy got off to a good start. However, it should also be noted that the impact of changes in the external environment is deepening, geopolitical risks continue to rise, and there are still many old and new challenges facing domestic economic development and transformation, with some enterprises experiencing operational difficulties. In the next stage, we must adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly implement the spirit of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and its plenary sessions, conscientiously implement the deployments of the Central Economic Work Conference and the National Two Sessions, fully, accurately, and comprehensively implement the new development concept, accelerate the construction of a new development pattern, focus on promoting high-quality development, adhere to the general principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability, implement a more proactive and effective macro policy, develop new quality productive forces based on local conditions, focus on stabilizing employment, enterprises, markets, and expectations, and promote the effective improvement of the quality and reasonable growth of the economy. (2) The statistical scope of industrial enterprises above the designated size refers to industrial enterprises with an annual main business income of 20 million yuan and above. Due to the annual changes in the scope of industrial enterprises above the designated size, to ensure the comparability of this year's data with the previous year, the period used for calculating the year-on-year growth rate of indicators such as product output is as consistent as possible with the statistical scope of enterprises in the current period, and there are differences in caliber compared to the data published in the previous year. The main reasons are: first, changes in the scope of statistical units. Each year, some enterprises are included in the survey scope due to their scale, while others are excluded due to a decrease in scale, as well as the impact of newly established and put into operation enterprises, bankruptcies, and deregistered (revoked) enterprises. Second, there are instances of repeated statistical reporting of product output data by some enterprise groups (companies) across regions. Based on special surveys, the repeated output across regions by enterprise groups (companies) has been deduplicated. (3) The service production index refers to the change in output of the service sector in the reporting period relative to the base period, after excluding price factors. (4) The statistical scope of total retail sales of consumer goods includes legal entities, industrial activity units, and individual businesses engaged in commodity retail activities or providing catering services. Among them, units above the designated size refer to wholesale enterprises (units and individual businesses) with an annual main business income of 20 million yuan and above, retail enterprises (units and individual businesses) with 5 million yuan and above, and accommodation and catering enterprises (units and individual businesses) with 2 million yuan and above. Due to the annual changes in the scope of wholesale and retail enterprises, and accommodation and catering enterprises (units and individual businesses) above the designated size, to ensure the comparability of this year's data with the previous year, the period used for calculating the year-on-year growth rate of indicators such as retail sales of consumer goods by units above the designated size is consistent with the statistical scope of enterprises (units and individual businesses) in the current period, and there are differences in caliber compared to the data published in the previous year. The main reasons are that each year some enterprises (units and individual businesses) reach the designated size and are included in the survey scope, while some enterprises (units and individual businesses) fall below the designated size and are excluded from the survey scope, as well as the impact of newly opened, bankrupt, and deregistered (revoked) enterprises (units and individual businesses). (5) Service retail sales refer to the total value of services directly provided by enterprises (industrial activity units, individual businesses) to individuals and other units in the form of transactions for non-production and non-business purposes. It aims to reflect the value of services sold by service providers in monetary form, including retail sales of services in transportation, accommodation, catering, education, health, sports, and entertainment. (6) To more comprehensively reflect the development of the online consumption market, the statistical indicators for online consumption have been improved. Based on the trend of online consumption development, the scope of statistical platforms for online network services has been expanded, and the calculation of online service retail sales has been strengthened. Therefore, the original "online retail sales" has been adjusted to "online retail sales of goods and services," with unchanged indicator connotation and expanded statistical scope; "online retail sales of physical goods" has been adjusted to "online retail sales of goods," with unchanged indicator connotation and statistical scope; and "online retail sales of services" has been added. Data for online retail sales of goods and services are not comparable with online retail sales data. Due to the annual changes in the scope of key platforms included in the statistics of online retail sales of goods and services, to ensure the comparability of this year's data with the previous year, the period used for calculating the year-on-year growth rate of online retail sales of goods and services is consistent with the statistical scope of platforms in the current period, and there are differences in caliber compared to the data published in the previous year. The main reasons are that new platforms are added to the survey scope each year, and some platforms that do not meet the statistical system requirements are removed from the survey scope. (7) Fixed asset investment (excluding rural households) refers to the total amount of work completed and expenses incurred in the construction and purchase of fixed assets in a certain period, expressed in monetary terms. Infrastructure investment: According to the current statistical system, infrastructure investment includes fixed asset investment in electricity, heat production and supply, gas production and supply, water production and supply, railway transportation, road transportation, water transportation, air transportation, pipeline transportation, multimodal transport and transport agencies, loading and unloading, postal services, telecommunications, radio, television and satellite transmission services, internet and related services, water conservancy management, ecological protection and environmental governance, and public facilities management. The growth rate of infrastructure investment is calculated on a comparable basis. Due to reforms in investment statistical system methods, statistical law enforcement inspections, and other regulations, the fixed asset investment data for the same period of the previous year have been revised, and the growth rate of fixed asset investment is calculated on a comparable basis. (8) Import and export data are from the General Administration of Customs. (9) Due to rounding, there may be discrepancies between the total and the sum of sub-items for some data.

title_en: How far are we from "trust and let go" as AI agents accelerate their implementation?
body_en: From the launch of Manus, a general AI agent that ignited the market, to the continued popularity of the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, commonly known as "Lobster," and then to the intensive deployment of desktop Agent tools by internet companies like Alibaba and Baidu, AI agents are entering work and life scenarios at an unprecedented speed, moving from the realm of code. As visions such as "24/7 digital employees" and "one-person companies" accelerate towards reality, cities like Shenzhen and Wuxi have recently introduced policies to support the implementation of open-source agent projects like OpenClaw in fields such as manufacturing and government affairs. However, challenges related to technological maturity, security governance, and the industrial ecosystem are also surfacing. Industry experts believe that AI agents are in a critical "transition period" from technological exploration to large-scale application. "Currently More Like a 'Junior Intern' Requiring Meticulous Debugging" Unlike conversational AIs familiar to users, such as ChatGPT and Doubao, execution-oriented agents like the recently popular OpenClaw have fundamental differences in their technical positioning. "AI agents can be understood as digital employees that can both think and execute," said Zheng Jichang, Dean of the China Institute for Innovation Services at Tsinghua University, in an interview with Economic Information Daily. The core difference between the two lies in whether they possess "closed-loop execution capabilities." AI agents can connect with various large models like ChatGPT for deep thinking and content generation. Unlike traditional AI assistants, they also possess "hands-on ability." Zheng Jichang pointed out that AI agents can directly translate instructions into actual operations. By invoking system permissions and automation tools, they can perform specific operations on a computer like humans. Zheng Jichang gave an example: when a user gives the task "organize this week's work, generate a weekly report, and send it to the department's Feishu group," an AI agent can automatically read relevant files, generate the document, open Feishu, and complete the sending, achieving a complete process from understanding the task to completing the execution. However, from a technical perspective, the statement "AI is starting to act on its own" still needs to be viewed more rationally. Zheng Jichang pointed out that currently, AI agents are more like "junior interns" that require meticulous debugging. While they can efficiently complete tasks in specific scenarios, they often exhibit misunderstandings or operational errors. They are still a considerable distance from the stable and reliable autonomous intelligence that the public expects. Cloud Empowerment Opens Commercial Exploration Since their launch, AI agents have seen accelerated deployment from various industry players. Domestic "cloud" vendors, including Tencent Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, and Baidu Intelligent Cloud, have integrated them, helping users lower the barrier to entry by simplifying deployment processes and providing cloud-based operating environments. Institutions predict that the market size of AI agents in China will exceed 3.3 trillion yuan by 2028, with rapid penetration of enterprise-level applications. Taking CoPaw, an open-source desktop Agent tool launched by Alibaba on February 28th, as an example, users can deploy it locally and in the cloud with one click. They can also perform secondary development based on CoPaw, freely connect local models, write Skills, and access exclusive messaging applications to meet more customized scenario needs. According to the CoPaw team, the tool supports connection to multiple communication platforms such as DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, and Discord, and has built-in functional modules for document editing, news reading, and file management. The system can also use task scheduling mechanisms to enable agents to automatically organize emails, generate weekly reports, or manage to-do lists. The Copaw team stated, "In the future, we will further explore the collaborative mechanism of large and small models, allowing lighter local models to process private data and more powerful cloud models to handle planning and code writing, thus balancing security and performance." Industry insiders believe that the emergence of such tools is lowering the usage threshold for AI agents, providing a foundational condition for more developers and enterprises to explore application scenarios. According to Zhu Keli, founding dean of the Research Institute of the New Economy, AI agents are currently in a stage where the concept is clear, the direction is defined, the focus is concentrated, and the potential is huge, but maturity still needs to be improved. On the technical level, planning capabilities, tool invocation capabilities, and multi-step task execution capabilities are rapidly advancing, but there is still significant room for improvement in the stability of complex tasks, the reliability of long-chain logic, and cross-scenario generalizability. On the industrial level, large-scale commercial applications are mainly concentrated in automation tasks with relatively simple structures and low risks. Regarding the next steps in the development of AI agents, Zheng Jichang believes that AI agents should follow a steady path from single-point applications to system collaboration, and from efficiency improvement to decision-making penetration. In 2026, AI agents will enter a period of large-scale implementation and governance exploration. He also emphasized that enterprises need to realize as soon as possible that they must prioritize building an "AI-ready" data foundation and governance framework. From "Usable" to "Reliable": Large-Scale Application Still Needs a Breakthrough The popularity of OpenClaw is both an inevitable result of technological evolution and a stress test of the current industry status. How to bridge the gap from "usable" to "reliable" is crucial for determining whether AI agents can truly achieve large-scale application. As AI agents begin to access critical business environments such as email systems, code repositories, and databases, their potential risks are gradually becoming apparent. A security expert from 360 Digital Security Group pointed out that some typical security risks have already emerged due to improper configuration during the installation, deployment, and use of OpenClaw agents. For example, attackers may embed hidden instructions in web content through "prompt injection." Once the agent reads the relevant web page, it may be induced to leak sensitive information such as system keys. In practical applications, if the agent misunderstands user instructions, it may also lead to operational errors, such as accidentally deleting emails or core business data. Zheng Jichang believes that there is a key bottleneck in the transition of agents from "usable" to "reliable," and breaking through this bottleneck requires efforts in three directions. The first is infrastructure innovation. He stated that a high-performance and high-security "operating base" must be built for agents. The second is architectural evolution, which requires promoting the evolution of agents from single models to a closed loop of "perception-reasoning-execution-self-evolution." The last is governance and protocols. He suggested establishing "safety rules" for agents and building a unified security and responsibility framework, such as requiring agents to inherit user permission boundaries (identity propagation) in any operation, achieving full-chain traceability. "Only when infrastructure, architectural design, and governance rules break through simultaneously can agents truly win user trust and become reliable executors in the digital world," said Zheng Jichang. Zhu Keli also emphasized the need for efforts in multiple aspects, including technical architecture, task design, and verification mechanisms. Strengthen planning and reflection capabilities to enable agents to have self-checking, error correction, and dynamic adjustment capabilities during execution; establish human-computer collaboration mechanisms, retaining manual confirmation and supervision at key operational nodes; and improve industry standards and testing systems to form quantifiable and verifiable reliability indicators. (Intern Lin Chenxuan also contributed to this article)

title_en: March 16th Important News Overview
body_en: 1. Li Chenggang, China's International Trade Representative and Vice Minister of Commerce, stated on the 16th that over the past day and a half, Chinese and US teams have engaged in in-depth, candid, and constructive consultations. During these consultations, both sides have reached preliminary consensus on some issues, and the consultation process will continue. 2. Li Chenggang said on the 16th that China's stance on the US's unilateral Section 301 investigation is consistent, and we oppose such unilateral investigations. We are concerned about the potential disruption and damage that the possible outcomes of these investigations could cause to the hard-won stable economic and trade relationship between China and the US. 3. The Party Committee of the National Financial Regulatory Administration held an expanded meeting on March 16th. The meeting emphasized the prudent resolution of risks in key areas. It called for forceful, orderly, and effective efforts to resolve risks in small and medium-sized financial institutions, firmly adhering to the bottom line of preventing defaults. It further stressed leveraging the role of the "whitelist" system for ensuring housing delivery and accelerating the establishment of a financing system compatible with the new model of real estate development. It also called for legally and compliantly supporting the resolution of financing platform debt risks and strictly preventing, cracking down on, and punishing illegal financial activities to safeguard the public's "money bags." 4. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology held a cadre meeting. The meeting emphasized the need to promote the optimization and upgrading of the industrial system. It called for implementing actions to revitalize traditional industries, deploying major technological transformation and upgrading projects, carrying out pilot work for urban technological transformation, and strengthening standard guidance, quality improvement, and brand building. It also stressed fostering and expanding emerging and future industries, building pillar industries such as integrated circuits, aerospace, and biomedicine, and promoting the establishment of investment growth and risk-sharing mechanisms for future industries. The meeting further called for vigorously developing intelligent manufacturing, green manufacturing, and service-oriented manufacturing, and promoting the deep integration of informatization and industrialization. It also emphasized moderately advanced planning and construction of new information infrastructure such as 5G and intelligent computing, and upgrading the "5G+Industrial Internet" initiative. Actions for digital transformation of manufacturing will be carried out, the "Artificial Intelligence + Manufacturing" action will be deeply implemented, and a batch of characteristic intelligent bodies will be cultivated. The development of satellite internet will be accelerated. 5. The Shanghai Branch of the People's Bank of China, in conjunction with the Shanghai Regulatory Bureau of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, issued the "Notice on Adjusting the Minimum Down Payment Ratio Policy for Commercial Property Loans in Shanghai." The notice makes the following adjustments to the commercial property loan policy in Shanghai: Starting from March 16, 2026, the minimum down payment ratio for commercial property loans (including "commercial-residential dual-use properties") in Shanghai will be adjusted to not less than 30%. 6. Meta plans to invest up to $27 billion in the artificial intelligence company Nebius over the next five years. title_en: Recovered losses of 4.35 billion yuan! State Administration for Market Regulation releases 2025 consumer rights protection data
body_en: On the 15th, the State Administration for Market Regulation announced that in 2025, market regulation departments nationwide handled a total of 43.866 million consumer complaints, reports, and inquiries through channels such as the National 12315 Platform and telephone, recovering 4.35 billion yuan in economic losses for consumers and effectively protecting their legitimate rights and interests. The State Administration for Market Regulation stated that consumer complaints and reports in 2025 exhibited the following characteristics: **Consumer Complaints Exceed 20 Million for the First Time, with After-Sales Service and Contract Issues Being Prominent** In 2025, market regulation departments nationwide handled a total of 20.366 million complaints, a year-on-year increase of 9.3%. The total number of complaints surpassed 20 million for the first time, indicating a continuous enhancement of consumer rights awareness. After-sales service complaints have ranked first for three consecutive years, highlighting the insufficient attention some businesses pay to after-sales support and their failure to meet consumers' basic service demands. In terms of growth rate, contract issues saw a year-on-year increase of 40.3%, making it the core issue with the fastest growth in complaints. Consumers' reported problems mainly focused on difficulties in refunds, unclear contract terms, "unfair clauses" hidden in standard contracts, businesses failing to fulfill their obligations as agreed, and discrepancies between promotional promises and contract content. **Online Shopping Demands Show New Characteristics, Recovering Over 1 Billion Yuan in Economic Losses** In 2025, the National 12315 Platform received 15.067 million online shopping complaints and reports, a year-on-year increase of 14.3%, accounting for 56.9% of the total complaints and reports. Among these, there were 11.447 million complaints and 3.62 million reports, recovering 1.07 billion yuan in economic losses for consumers, which accounted for 24.6% of the total recovered economic losses. In terms of issues, after-sales service and quality problems in online shopping were the two areas with the most concentrated consumer feedback, with complaint and report volumes of 3.486 million and 2.886 million respectively, accounting for a combined 42.3%. Furthermore, price disputes during e-commerce shopping festivals were prominent, with the core conflict being that consumers, after paying a deposit during the pre-sale period, found that the product price was actually lower during the final payment stage or the peak of the event. Although platforms offered price protection services, consumers often had their price protection applications rejected due to reasons such as changes in product links or different types of coupons. **Food Delivery Demands Show Significant Fluctuations, Industry Competition Needs to Return to Rationality** In 2025, the platform received 505,000 food delivery complaints and reports, a year-on-year increase of 14.1%. Among the main issues, food safety (262,000 cases), after-sales service (63,000 cases), contract issues (24,000 cases), unfair competition (23,000 cases), and quality issues (19,000 cases) ranked high, accounting for nearly 80% of the total. In the third quarter, major platforms continued to attract users through "subsidy wars." While order volume surged, service and support capabilities did not keep pace, leading to a rise in demands. The platform received a 23.8% year-on-year increase and a 19.2% quarter-on-quarter increase in complaints and reports, marking the period with the largest increase in demands for the year. However, in the fourth quarter, as subsidy policies receded and the market gradually "cooled down," demand also declined accordingly, with a 22.8% quarter-on-quarter decrease compared to the third quarter. The State Administration for Market Regulation stated that overall, the volume of consumer demands in the food delivery industry shows phased changes with market fluctuations, and industry competition needs to shift towards a more rational and sustainable direction. **"Charging Anxiety" Demands Surge, Service Experience Urgently Needs Upgrading** In 2025, the platform received 156,000 complaints and reports related to power banks, a year-on-year increase of 62.5%. Specific issues were concentrated in product quality problems, return disputes, difficulties in borrowing and returning shared power banks, and abnormal billing. Meanwhile, with the rapid increase in the ownership of new energy vehicles and the continuous expansion of charging infrastructure, the shortcomings in charging facility service quality have become increasingly prominent. In 2025, the platform received 61,000 complaints and reports related to new energy vehicle charging facilities, a year-on-year increase of 47.8%. Specific issues were concentrated in difficulties in refunding prepaid balances, some charging pile operating companies going out of business and becoming unreachable, non-transparent charging standards, and ineffective human customer service. **Jewelry Consumption Upgrades, Gold and Jade Become Core Areas of Demand** In 2025, the platform received 380,000 jewelry complaints and reports, a year-on-year increase of 16.4%. Among these, gold jewelry (142,000 cases) and natural jade (102,000 cases) became the core areas of demand. Together with silver jewelry (45,000 cases), alloy jewelry (28,000 cases), and natural gemstones (17,000 cases), they accounted for 87.9% of the total jewelry complaints and reports. According to consumer feedback, the problems mainly focused on three aspects: First, some products had insufficient precious metal purity, jade of inferior quality passed off as superior, and excessive harmful substances in ornaments. Second, "fixed-price" gold jewelry did not clearly indicate the weight, with the actual unit price far exceeding the market gold price, and hidden conditions for exchanges. Third, problems in e-commerce channels were prominent, with related demands accounting for 60% of the total jewelry complaints and reports, involving false advertising, goods not matching descriptions, and issues with "customized items being non-refundable." **Smart Consumption Rapidly Rises, Functional Claims Disconnect with User Perception** In 2025, the National 12315 Platform received 152,000 complaints and reports related to smart devices, a year-on-year increase of 26.6%. Among these, smartwatches (50,000 cases), smart home devices (29,000 cases), drones (19,000 cases), smart accessories (18,000 cases), and smart robots (17,000 cases) ranked high in complaint and report volumes, accounting for 87.5% of the total. In terms of growth rate, drones, smart bracelets (10,000 cases), and smart glasses (3,235 cases) saw significant increases, with year-on-year growth of 45.5%, 39.4%, and 37.7% respectively. Consumer complaints mainly focused on: First, some products over-promoted their "smart" labels, while their actual functions were limited to basic networking or simple remote control, failing to address real pain points, leading to a significant gap between consumer expectations and reality. Second, software issues such as failed system upgrades, app crashes, poor compatibility, and data synchronization failures were intertwined with hardware malfunctions. Third, the emerging smart device sector lacks unified technical specifications and quality standards, with an incomplete after-sales system and high thresholds for returns and exchanges being prominent issues.

The State Administration for Market Regulation stated that consumer complaints and reports in 2025 exhibited the following characteristics: **Consumer Complaints Exceed 20 Million for the First Time, with After-Sales Service and Contract Issues Being Prominent** In 2025, market regulation departments nationwide handled a total of 20.366 million complaints, a year-on-year increase of 9.3%. The total number of complaints surpassed 20 million for the first time, indicating a continuous enhancement of consumer rights awareness. After-sales service complaints have ranked first for three consecutive years, highlighting the insufficient attention some businesses pay to after-sales support and their failure to meet consumers' basic service demands. In terms of growth rate, contract issues saw a year-on-year increase of 40.3%, making it the core issue with the fastest growth in complaints. Consumers' reported problems mainly focused on difficulties in refunds, unclear contract terms, "unfair clauses" hidden in standard contracts, businesses failing to fulfill their obligations as agreed, and discrepancies between promotional promises and contract content. **Online Shopping Demands Show New Characteristics, Recovering Over 1 Billion Yuan in Economic Losses** In 2025, the National 12315 Platform received 15.067 million online shopping complaints and reports, a year-on-year increase of 14.3%, accounting for 56.9% of the total complaints and reports. Among these, there were 11.447 million complaints and 3.62 million reports, recovering 1.07 billion yuan in economic losses for consumers, which accounted for 24.6% of the total recovered economic losses. In terms of issues, after-sales service and quality problems in online shopping were the two areas with the most concentrated consumer feedback, with complaint and report volumes of 3.486 million and 2.886 million respectively, accounting for a combined 42.3%. Furthermore, price disputes during e-commerce shopping festivals were prominent, with the core conflict being that consumers, after paying a deposit during the pre-sale period, found that the product price was actually lower during the final payment stage or the peak of the event. Although platforms offered price protection services, consumers often had their price protection applications rejected due to reasons such as changes in product links or different types of coupons. **Food Delivery Demands Show Significant Fluctuations, Industry Competition Needs to Return to Rationality** In 2025, the platform received 505,000 food delivery complaints and reports, a year-on-year increase of 14.1%. Among the main issues, food safety (262,000 cases), after-sales service (63,000 cases), contract issues (24,000 cases), unfair competition (23,000 cases), and quality issues (19,000 cases) ranked high, accounting for nearly 80% of the total. In the third quarter, major platforms continued to attract users through "subsidy wars." While order volume surged, service and support capabilities did not keep pace, leading to a rise in demands. The platform received a 23.8% year-on-year increase and a 19.2% quarter-on-quarter increase in complaints and reports, marking the period with the largest increase in demands for the year. However, in the fourth quarter, as subsidy policies receded and the market gradually "cooled down," demand also declined accordingly, with a 22.8% quarter-on-quarter decrease compared to the third quarter. The State Administration for Market Regulation stated that overall, the volume of consumer demands in the food delivery industry shows phased changes with market fluctuations, and industry competition needs to shift towards a more rational and sustainable direction. **"Charging Anxiety" Demands Surge, Service Experience Urgently Needs Upgrading** In 2025, the platform received 156,000 complaints and reports related to power banks, a year-on-year increase of 62.5%. Specific issues were concentrated in product quality problems, return disputes, difficulties in borrowing and returning shared power banks, and abnormal billing. Meanwhile, with the rapid increase in the ownership of new energy vehicles and the continuous expansion of charging infrastructure, the shortcomings in charging facility service quality have become increasingly prominent. In 2025, the platform received 61,000 complaints and reports related to new energy vehicle charging facilities, a year-on-year increase of 47.8%. Specific issues were concentrated in difficulties in refunding prepaid balances, some charging pile operating companies going out of business and becoming unreachable, non-transparent charging standards, and ineffective human customer service. **Jewelry Consumption Upgrades, Gold and Jade Become Core Areas of Demand** In 2025, the platform received 380,000 jewelry complaints and reports, a year-on-year increase of 16.4%. Among these, gold jewelry (142,000 cases) and natural jade (102,000 cases) became the core areas of demand. Together with silver jewelry (45,000 cases), alloy jewelry (28,000 cases), and natural gemstones (17,000 cases), they accounted for 87.9% of the total jewelry complaints and reports. According to consumer feedback, the problems mainly focused on three aspects: First, some products had insufficient precious metal purity, jade of inferior quality passed off as superior, and excessive harmful substances in ornaments. Second, "fixed-price" gold jewelry did not clearly indicate the weight, with the actual unit price far exceeding the market gold price, and hidden conditions for exchanges. Third, problems in e-commerce channels were prominent, with related demands accounting for 60% of the total jewelry complaints and reports, involving false advertising, goods not matching descriptions, and issues with "customized items being non-refundable." **Smart Consumption Rapidly Rises, Functional Claims Disconnect with User Perception** In 2025, the National 12315 Platform received 152,000 complaints and reports related to smart devices, a year-on-year increase of 26.6%. Among these, smartwatches (50,000 cases), smart home devices (29,000 cases), drones (19,000 cases), smart accessories (18,000 cases), and smart robots (17,000 cases) ranked high in complaint and report volumes, accounting for 87.5% of the total. In terms of growth rate, drones, smart bracelets (10,000 cases), and smart glasses (3,235 cases) saw significant increases, with year-on-year growth of 45.5%, 39.4%, and 37.7% respectively. Consumer complaints mainly focused on: First, some products over-promoted their "smart" labels, while their actual functions were limited to basic networking or simple remote control, failing to address real pain points, leading to a significant gap between consumer expectations and reality. Second, software issues such as failed system upgrades, app crashes, poor compatibility, and data synchronization failures were intertwined with hardware malfunctions. Third, the emerging smart device sector lacks unified technical specifications and quality standards, with an incomplete after-sales system and high thresholds for returns and exchanges being prominent issues.

title_en: Alibaba Launches Enterprise-Grade "Dragonfly" App Wukong: Considering Performance-Based Pricing
body_en: "Lobster" became popular for only a few days before quickly moving into the phase of enterprise vulnerability prevention. In the wave of AIAgent implementation, how to meet the security usage needs of customers, especially enterprise-level customers, is becoming a key point in the competition for major players' "new AI products." On March 17th, DingTalk released its enterprise-level AI-native work platform "Wukong," which will begin its invite-only testing immediately and will be directly integrated into DingTalk for over 20 million enterprises. DingTalk CEO Chen Hang (alias Wuzhao) stated that the release of Wukong marks DingTalk's official evolution from a collaborative office tool to an AI-native work platform. With the release of Wukong, DingTalk is rewriting its underlying code and undergoing a comprehensive CLI (Command Line Interface) transformation, allowing Wukong Agents to natively operate thousands of DingTalk capabilities rather than simulating human clicks on a graphical interface. In other words, DingTalk is evolving to be more AI-friendly than human-friendly. Furthermore, Wukong will fully support connecting users' DingTalk accounts, security access permissions, and application systems within the enterprise. Simultaneously, Alibaba's ToB capabilities across its ecosystem will be gradually embedded into the platform as skills, serving as a unified exit for Alibaba's AI capabilities in enterprise work scenarios. For enterprise customers, Wukong has also launched the first batch of OPT (One Person Team) ten industry solutions, covering ten scenarios including e-commerce, cross-border e-commerce, and knowledge-based bloggers. The plan is to transform AI Skills from a technical concept into industry-level, out-of-the-box solutions, where one person can have an "Agent team" proficient in industry skills to work for them, which is becoming a new vision for the Agent era. However, the reality of "Lobster's" overnight popularity and subsequent rapid explosion of security issues stands in the way of the imagination of "letting Agents finish the work." In the past period, cases of Lobster leaking company and personal information, breaking through permissions to "cause trouble," and even leading to users' computers being remotely controlled by attackers and poisoned by malicious plugins have been endless. How to defend against "shrimp farming security" has become a new focus of competition for major manufacturers recently. "The freedom in 'shrimp farming' on the C-end is greater, but freedom can also bring greater destruction. Enterprises are serious scenarios and cannot tolerate these destructive risks," said DingTalk CTO Zhu Hong in an interview with media including Yicai. He added that in the process of Agent implementation, compared to the C-end's potential competition on capability limits, the B-end market competition must first ensure the security bottom line. Zhu Hong introduced that a potential differentiated competitive advantage of Wukong comes from the integration of enterprise data, organizational structure, knowledge, and permissions originally loaded in DingTalk. For example, AI Agents will automatically inherit enterprise permission rules. At the same time, Wukong strengthens localized security execution, full-link auditing capabilities to ensure AI behavior is traceable and regulable, and enterprise cluster deployment and unified scheduling, allowing IT departments to centrally manage the operating status, resource consumption, and security policies of all AI Agents. On March 16th, Alibaba announced the establishment of the Alibaba Token Hub (ATH) business group, incorporating the Qianwen business unit, Wukong business unit, and others into the ATH business group. The Wukong business unit is positioned to "build the B-end AI application entrance and deeply integrate model capabilities into enterprise workflows." It is understood that in terms of organizational structure, DingTalk belongs to the Wukong business unit, and the DingTalk brand will continue to operate independently. Under Alibaba's new AI strategy centered around "Token," Zhu Hong mentioned that as enterprise workflows become more automated, the traditional commercial model of software has been primarily subscription-based. He believes that in the future, the interface called by a workflow will become an API call mode, where software companies call capabilities and pay as they go. In the future, Wukong will also consider commercial models such as pay-as-you-go and pay-for-performance. In addition, Wuzhao revealed in his speech that Wukong will also enter the global market and will subsequently support connections to mainstream global IM platforms such as WeChat and Slack.
