title_en: Consumer spending rebounded significantly in the first two months.
body_en: On March 16th, the State Council Information Office held a press conference where Fu Linghui, spokesperson for the National Bureau of Statistics, chief economist, and director of the Department of Comprehensive Statistics of National Economy, introduced the national economic performance from January to February. In terms of consumption, from January to February, the total retail sales of consumer goods reached 8,607.9 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 2.8%, which was 1.9 percentage points faster than in December of the previous year. During the same period, service retail sales increased by 5.6% year-on-year, 0.1 percentage points faster than the full year of the previous year. Among these, retail sales in communication and information services, tourism consulting and leasing services, and cultural, sports, and leisure services grew rapidly. Regarding these data, Wang Qing, chief macro analyst at Oriental Jincheng, told a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald that firstly, the funds for trade-in programs were allocated in advance this year, and the policy mechanisms were optimized. Various regions implemented the trade-in of consumer goods from January 1st, achieving a smooth transition and orderly connection of policies, which concentrated the effect of promoting consumption in the first two months of the year. Secondly, the Spring Festival holiday was extended by one day this year, leading to a concentrated release of public consumption demand, which strongly boosted the growth of related goods and services consumption. The 9-day Spring Festival holiday in 2026 was called the "longest Spring Festival holiday in history," with active cultural tourism and leisure entertainment market activities, leading to rapid growth in service consumption. Data from the National Bureau of Statistics shows that from January to February, service retail sales grew by 5.6%, significantly faster than the growth of commodity retail sales. Driven by the Spring Festival holiday, residents' cultural and tourism consumption increased significantly, driving the expansion of related service sales. In the first two months, retail sales in tourism consulting and leasing services and cultural, sports, and leisure services maintained a growth rate of over 10%. During the 2026 National Spring Festival Cultural and Tourism Consumption Month, approximately 35,000 cultural and tourism consumption activities were held across the country, with consumption vouchers and subsidies totaling about 420 million yuan issued. During the Consumption Month, night tours such as drone shows, immersive performances, and cultural and creative markets were also rich and colorful, promoting the growth of night-time cultural and tourism consumption. Intangible cultural heritage experiences, cultural performances, and festival temple fairs held across the country attracted tourists. In Jingdezhen, Jiangxi, tourists directly experienced the transformation from "a handful of mud to exquisite porcelain" by participating in the entire process of ceramic firing. Intangible cultural heritage projects such as paper-cutting and lion dances in Guangdong attracted tourists to slow down and experience them in depth. In Quanzhou, Fujian, tourists wearing "Zan Hua Wei" (a type of headdress) walked through ancient streets and alleys of thousands of years to capture moments. Fu Linghui stated that during the Spring Festival, domestic travel reached nearly 600 million person-times, with total travel expenses exceeding 800 billion yuan, reaching a historical high. At the same time, the expansion of visa-free policies for inbound travel led to an increase in inbound tourists, which also promoted the expansion of domestic market sales. During the Spring Festival, residents' social gatherings increased, and dining out consumption expanded significantly. In the first two months, catering revenue increased by 4.8% year-on-year, a growth rate 2.6 percentage points faster than in December of the previous year. In recent years, China has expanded high-level opening-up and optimized visa-free policies for inbound travel. This Spring Festival, many regions in China welcomed an increase in inbound tourists. During the Spring Festival holiday, Beijing received 142,000 inbound tourists, with inbound tourist spending reaching 1.48 billion yuan, both increasing by more than 40% year-on-year. Guangdong received 34.8% more inbound tourists year-on-year, accounting for an increase of 1.5 percentage points in the proportion of tourists in the province. At the same time, the way of celebrating Spring Festival has also undergone new changes, with "reverse Spring Festival" and "traveling for Spring Festival" becoming new trends, promoting the growth of service consumption. Jiang Han, a senior researcher at the Pangu Think Tank, told a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald that reverse Spring Festival has significantly optimized the allocation of transportation resources, effectively filling the capacity gap in traditional off-peak seasons, and improving the overall operational efficiency of aviation and railways, driving the growth of urban accommodation, catering, and offline retail. In terms of consumption, reverse Spring Festival has activated the potential of "silver consumption" and promoted the upgrading of the consumption structure. "Reverse Spring Festival often combines with traveling for Spring Festival, prompting family consumption to shift from traditional gift-giving to experiential services, such as micro-trips in cities and cultural exhibitions, increasing the added value of Spring Festival consumption," Jiang Han said. In the first two months of this year, commodity consumption showed a clear trend of upgrading and improving quality. Fu Linghui introduced that residents' consumption quality has steadily improved, coupled with the boost from Spring Festival holiday consumption, sales of some basic living goods have expanded significantly. In the first two months, retail sales of goods in the grain, oil, and food category, and the clothing, shoes, hats, textiles, and accessories category above the designated size increased by 10.2% and 10.4% respectively. The main reason is the improvement in residents' requirements for the quality and grade of commodity consumption. At the same time, driven by the upgrading of residents' consumption, sales of goods related to developmental and improvement-oriented demand have grown rapidly. In the first two months, retail sales of gold, silver, and jewelry above the designated size increased by 13% year-on-year. In addition, China continues to implement the consumer goods trade-in policy this year, and the policy's pulling effect is significant. The first batch of 62.5 billion yuan in ultra-long-term special treasury bonds has been allocated in advance, and the gradual removal of unreasonable restrictions in the consumption field will support consumption growth. From January to February this year, retail sales of communication equipment above the designated size increased by 17.8%, maintaining relatively rapid growth; retail sales of household appliances and audio-visual equipment increased by 3.3%, a significant rebound from December of last year. Among household appliances and audio-visual equipment, goods with high energy efficiency ratings achieved double-digit growth, and demand for green products is expanding. The Ministry of Commerce learned that since the beginning of this year, the consumer goods trade-in policy has been steadily and orderly promoted. As of now, the cumulative sales of related goods under the 2026 consumer goods trade-in program have reached 47.623 million units, a year-on-year increase of 15.3%, driving sales of 323.26 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 3.2%. Among them, the trade-in of automobiles received a total of 1.008 million subsidy applications, driving new car sales of 164.43 billion yuan. The trade-in of home appliances sold 17.13 million units, driving sales of 69.44 billion yuan. The purchase of new digital and smart products sold 29.485 million units, driving sales of 89.39 billion yuan. In 2026, smart glasses were included in the scope of new purchase subsidies for the first time, becoming a new favorite for Spring Festival consumption. Digital product consultation and purchase volume in Tianjin, Chongqing, Sichuan, and other places increased significantly. At the same time, the trend of optimizing and upgrading the consumption structure is obvious. Data from the Ministry of Commerce shows that the proportion of mid-to-high-end mobile phone products accounted for 65.0%. Data from China UnionPay shows that the average transaction amount for computers, air conditioners, and televisions also increased significantly compared to the same period last year. From the reporter's observations during the Spring Festival, the trade-in policy has become an important booster for people to purchase products such as mobile phones and cars. The reporter saw a continuous stream of customers looking at and ordering cars at the YuBei Auto Market in Anyang. According to the sales director, the extension of national subsidies, coupled with the traditional consumption peak before the festival, has led to a rapid warming of the automotive market during Spring Festival. At the same time, services in Beijing, Shanxi, Jiangxi, Chongqing, and other places were "not closed" during the Spring Festival holiday, with subsidy application channels open 24/7 and sufficient reserves of eligibility coupons. Tianjin, Zhejiang, Hubei, Gansu, and other regions provided consumers with "real money" policy dividends through the "national subsidy + local red envelopes + merchant discounts" model. Yu Fenghui, a specially invited researcher at the China Financial Think Tank, told a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald that preferential measures such as strengthening trade-in programs and consumption red envelopes can reduce consumers' actual payment costs and increase their willingness to purchase. "These policy measures, working together, can effectively stimulate domestic demand, promote consumption upgrading, and also create more sales opportunities for enterprises, helping the real economy to recover and develop. Especially in the current economic situation, such a combination of policies is of positive significance for stabilizing economic growth." It is worth noting that there is an important change in the consumption-related indicators released this year: the indicator of "online retail sales of goods and services" was released for the first time, while the indicator of "online retail sales" was discontinued. Fu Linghui explained that the "online retail sales of goods and services" indicator is an optimized and improved version of the original "online retail sales" indicator. The main difference is that the "online retail sales of goods and services" indicator has expanded the statistical scope of online service platforms and strengthened the calculation of online service retail sales. Data shows that with the strengthening momentum of online consumption and digital consumption, online retail sales have continued to expand. In the first two months, online retail sales of goods and services increased by 9.2% year-on-year, significantly faster than the growth rate of total retail sales of consumer goods. Among them, online retail sales of goods increased by 10.3%, faster than the growth of total retail sales of goods, and its driving effect on consumption continued to strengthen. The popularity of online service consumption continued to rise. From January to February, online service retail sales increased by 7.3% year-on-year, also faster than the growth of total service retail sales. Guo Tao, an angel investor and special researcher at the E-commerce Research Center of the E-commerce Association of China, told a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald that the growth of online retail sales of goods and services in January-February this year demonstrates the vitality of the online consumption market, benefiting from the combined effect of multiple factors. "At the policy level, national policies to promote consumption have created a favorable environment for online consumption, effectively stimulating potential; the holiday effect is significant, with the ultra-long Spring Festival holiday driving up online demand for New Year's goods purchases and cultural tourism; consumption upgrading has promoted the growth of quality-oriented and developmental demand, with expanded demand for green and healthy goods and services such as communication and tourism; digital technology has given rise to emerging formats such as online short dramas, injecting new momentum into growth," Guo Tao said. The Outline of the 14th Five-Year Plan also proposes to cultivate and strengthen rural characteristic industries and new industries and business formats such as rural leisure tourism, cultural experience, and rural e-commerce. In Guo Tao's view, during the "15th Five-Year Plan" period, online consumption will show a multi-dimensional upgrading trend: rural e-commerce will accelerate quality improvement, achieving a transformation from scale expansion to quality improvement with policy support and facility improvement; service consumption will become the main driver of growth, with online services in fields such as cultural tourism and health and wellness continuing to gain momentum; online and offline integration will deepen, providing more convenient and personalized consumption experiences through the creation of diverse scenarios; green and intelligent consumption will increase its proportion, and sales of related goods and supporting services will grow steadily under policy promotion. Regarding the trend of consumption this year, Fu Linghui pointed out that from January to February, market sales showed positive changes and growth momentum strengthened, which is the result of the combined effect of policies to promote consumption, consumption upgrading, and the growth of new consumption drivers. Looking ahead, the upgrading of residents' consumption structure and the growth of new consumption drivers will continue to be important factors influencing consumption growth. The implementation of a series of policies to promote consumption will further boost consumption growth, and consumption is expected to continue to grow steadily. He also emphasized that building a strong domestic market and stimulating the endogenous动力 of residents' consumption still requires sustained efforts. Regarding how to promote consumption in the next stage, Fu Linghui stated: "We must leverage China's advantage of a super-large market, deeply implement special actions to boost consumption, formulate and implement plans to increase the income of urban and rural residents, promote the expansion and upgrading of commodity consumption, implement actions to improve the quality and benefit of service consumption, continuously optimize the consumption environment, unleash the consumption potential in fields such as culture and tourism, sports events, and health and wellness, stimulate consumption vitality, and better promote economic circulation and continuously improve people's livelihoods." The implementation of a series of policies to promote consumption will further boost consumption growth, and consumption is expected to continue to grow steadily. title_en: From the reduction of the "Apple Tax" to the protection of the digital economy through anti-monopoly.
body_en: On March 15th, Apple adjusted its App Store commission policy in mainland China, stating it will always maintain an overall rate no higher than in other countries and regions. This not only means that the discriminatory treatment previously imposed on Chinese developers by Apple will be effectively eliminated, but also indicates that Apple will establish a long-term mechanism to ensure that Chinese developers can continue to innovate in a fair and reasonable business environment. This is the first time Apple has lowered the "Apple Tax" on its App Store in China since its official entry into the market 16 years ago. Apple's official statement revealed a key piece of information: the adjustment was made "based on communication with Chinese regulatory authorities." Apple's adjustment in China did not involve any other fees or "hidden increases" disguised as "lower prices," unlike in Japan where a payment processing fee is charged in addition to commission, or in the EU where a core technology fee is levied, resulting in higher overall rates for local developers. Industry developers estimate that this adjustment essentially brings the overall rate to the lowest level globally. Considering the magnitude and attitude of Apple's adjustment, it is not difficult to infer that Chinese regulatory authorities exerted effective pressure, reflecting the continuous improvement of digital market rules and enhanced regulatory influence by Chinese authorities in their ongoing efforts to normalize anti-monopoly regulation. In fact, the alleged monopoly of Apple's App Store has long been criticized by the market. Apple operates a closed ecosystem where its App Store is the sole platform for users to install applications, leaving them with no other choice. In contrast, the Android system is highly open, supporting not only the Google Play Store but also stores from manufacturers like Huawei and Xiaomi, as well as third-party app stores, giving Android users multiple options for app installation. Globally, strengthening anti-monopoly regulation for large technology companies is an inevitable trend. From Google being ordered to divest its advertising technology business in the United States, to Apple being forced to open up "sideloading" (third-party distribution channels) in the EU, Japan, and other countries and regions, and Amazon facing anti-monopoly investigations in digital markets, the "walled gardens" of tech giants are being dismantled by the sword of anti-monopoly. Especially in the era of artificial intelligence, large technology companies' penetration into people's lives is becoming deeper, and the potential threats are greater, necessitating strengthened anti-monopoly regulation to maintain a fair competitive market order, stimulate market innovation, protect the legitimate rights and interests of consumers, and safeguard the development of the digital economy. China has been continuously strengthening its enforcement and judicial efforts in anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition, treating both domestic and foreign enterprises equally. In recent years, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) has investigated and dealt with monopoly cases such as Alibaba Group's "choose one of two" case and Meituan's "choose one of two" case, initiated investigations into Google and Ctrip, and conducted further investigations into Nvidia. At the same time, SAMR has innovated its regulatory methods, promptly identifying problems, transmitting pressure, and urging rectification through market investigations, reminders, and administrative interviews for companies with potential risks. Under high-pressure anti-monopoly enforcement, the reduction of the "Apple Tax" in China will lead to a win-win situation for multiple parties. China's 5 million developers will reduce their annual cost expenditures by over 6 billion yuan, prices for consumer subscriptions, game top-ups, and live-streaming rewards are expected to decrease, and the entire industry is likely to break old interest patterns. However, it is worth noting that Apple has not yet opened up "sideloading" in China, and Chinese users still lack multiple payment path options such as third-party payments and external link payments. The market highly anticipates that under continuous regulatory pressure, Apple will also dismantle its "fences" in China as soon as possible. In today's world, the market is the most scarce resource. China possesses the advantage of a super-large market and has shifted from "using the market to exchange for technology" to "using the market to create technology." China has a superior innovation environment and talent pool, continuously iterating commercial application scenarios, a rapidly developing digital economy, and active market competition, which can bring unique growth opportunities to multinational technology companies. It is believed that with the in-depth advancement of the construction of a unified national market and the continuous improvement of the digital governance system, the digital economy will usher in greater development opportunities. (Lin Lili)

title_en: Detailed Analysis of Alibaba's Latest Earnings Report: Alibaba Cloud Revenue Grows 36%, "Model + Cloud + Chip" Integration Accelerates AI Commercialization
body_en: On March 19, Alibaba Group released its Q3 financial report for fiscal year 2026, ending December 31, 2025. The report showed that Alibaba Cloud's revenue accelerated by 36%, and revenue from AI-related products achieved triple-digit growth for the tenth consecutive quarter. With continued high investment in instant retail, user experience, and AI technology, China E-commerce Group achieved adjusted EBITA of RMB 34.613 billion, and instant retail revenue grew by 56%. "This quarter, Alibaba continued to invest in its two core areas of AI and consumption. AI is one of our main growth engines," said Wu Yongming, CEO of Alibaba Group. Behind this new financial report, the growth of Alibaba Cloud validates Alibaba's heavy bet on AI, and Alibaba will continue to increase its investment in AI. Alibaba Cloud accelerates growth In terms of core business, Alibaba Cloud continues to maintain rapid growth. Financial data reveals that in this quarter, the Cloud Intelligence Group's revenue reached RMB 43.284 billion, a year-on-year increase of 36%, with external commercialization revenue growing by 35%. The report states that this momentum was primarily driven by the growth in public cloud revenue, including the increasing popularity of AI-related products. Meanwhile, revenue from AI-related products continued its strong momentum, achieving triple-digit year-on-year growth for the tenth consecutive quarter. Over the past few months, Alibaba Cloud has achieved significant breakthroughs at the model layer, application layer, and chip level. In February of this year, Alibaba Cloud released its new generation of large-scale model, Qwen3.5-Plus, which has made progress in inference, programming, and agent capabilities. Notably, Pingtouge Semiconductor Co., Ltd. ("Pingtouge") appeared in Alibaba's financial report for the first time. The report disclosed that the company has achieved mass production of its self-developed Pingtouge GPUs, supporting end-to-end AI workloads from training and fine-tuning to inference. This product is compatible with mainstream AI frameworks, enhancing Alibaba's long-term computing power supply capabilities. Combined with the Qianwen model and cloud computing, it provides cost-effective AI services to external clients. This business has rapidly expanded and is now making a substantial contribution to Alibaba's cloud infrastructure supply. The earnings call revealed that Pingtouge's annualized revenue has reached tens of billions of yuan. As of February 2026, Pingtouge had cumulatively delivered 470,000 self-developed GPU chips. Pingtouge does not rule out the possibility of an IPO in the future. Alibaba Cloud's globalization business continues to expand. As of December 31, 2025, Alibaba Cloud operates 92 availability zones in 29 regions worldwide. In terms of open source, Alibaba has open-sourced over 400 of its 1000 Questions models to date, with global downloads exceeding 1 billion and over 200,000 derived models. Full-stack AI capabilities are becoming Alibaba's core competitive advantage. A research report released by Morgan Stanley on March 12 stated that Alibaba has achieved "four-layer vertical integration" in the field of AI: possessing highly competitive self-developed GPU chips, powerful cloud infrastructure, open-source models, and a wealth of application scenarios. "In the future, relying on the full-stack AI capabilities of 'large-scale models + cloud + chips,' and the comprehensive integration with Alibaba's business ecosystem, we will continue to exert our efforts in both AI to B and to C directions," said Wu Yongming, CEO of Alibaba Group. He added that the construction and continuous growth of Alibaba Cloud's basic capabilities are pushing Alibaba's AI strategy to a new climax. He predicts that within five years, Alibaba Cloud and AI commercialization revenue will increase significantly from over 100 billion yuan this year to 100 billion US dollars (approximately 690 billion yuan), with a compound annual growth rate of approximately 47%. The battle for AI gateways erupts on two fronts. Amid the industry trend of accelerated agent deployment, it is worth noting that Alibaba AI has recently experienced explosive growth in both the B2B and B2C sectors. Financial reports show that in February, the monthly active users of Alibaba's AI-to-C flagship application, Qianwen, exceeded 300 million. Qianwen's Spring Festival activities drove nearly 140 million users to experience AI shopping, covering multiple sectors including catering, daily necessities, ticketing services, and travel booking. In January of this year, Alibaba upgraded Tongyi Qianwen, achieving deep integration between Qianwen and Alibaba's ecosystem businesses such as Taobao, Tmall, Taobao Flash Sale, Gaode Maps, Fliggy, and Alipay. Through the integration of AI with the Alibaba ecosystem, Alibaba is gaining a differentiated advantage in the competition for AI-to-C entry points. Alibaba's recently released enterprise-level AI-native work platform "Wukong" is also regarded by the industry as an important weapon for AI in the B2B sector. While ensuring a "lower limit" of security, Wukong Agent will be able to natively operate thousands of DingTalk capabilities through a complete CLI (command line interface) transformation of DingTalk, bringing imaginative B2B productivity. On March 16, Alibaba announced the official establishment of the Alibaba Token Hub (ATH) business group, including the Qianwen Business Unit and the Wukong Business Unit, to provide organizational support for the dual-track development of AI to B and to C and improve business strategic synergy. While upgrading from selling resources to selling intelligent capabilities with "token" as the main theme, Wu Yongming observed that many companies, when using tokens, do not treat them as part of their IT budget, but rather as part of the company's overall production or R&D costs and means of production. "This is the most fundamental intrinsic factor that Alibaba sees as the long-term growth potential of AI in the future." Alibaba is fostering synergy among various businesses within the Alibaba Token Hub to jointly seize future opportunities in AI agents. Wu Yongming stated that Alibaba clearly sees AI agents as an ecosystem at the application layer, with numerous innovations and a rich variety of applications. The market value and potential of Qianwen+Wukong and the Maas business connecting the model and application layers will be enormous. AI applications may become the largest distribution channel for AI tokens in the future. However, Wu Yongming emphasized that from the perspective of models and applications, Alibaba's priority is undoubtedly to build the most intelligent model. Only by building the most powerful model can Alibaba attract various industries to use its B-end, C-end applications and Maas business. More applications, scenarios and data will also iterate Alibaba's model capabilities, gradually connecting this data flywheel and business closed loop. Wu Yongming predicts that within five years, the annual revenue from cloud and AI commercialization will increase significantly from more than 100 billion RMB this year to 100 billion USD (approximately 690 billion RMB), with a compound annual growth rate of approximately 47%. Instant Retail expects to generate profit in fiscal year 2029 In China's e-commerce sector, the financial report shows that Alibaba's instant retail revenue, including Taobao Flash Sale, increased by 56% year-on-year during the reporting period, driving double-digit growth in both active buyers and 88VIP users on the Taobao App. The report states that thanks to improved fulfillment and logistics efficiency, improved order structure, and high customer retention rates, the unit economics and average order value of the instant retail business continued to improve sequentially. It is worth mentioning that Jiang Fan, CEO of Alibaba's e-commerce business group, said in the earnings call that the company will maintain its goal of achieving a total GMV of over 1 trillion yuan in fiscal year 2028 for instant retail and expects to achieve overall profitability in fiscal year 2029. title_en: Wu Yongming on Alibaba's AI ambitions: $100 billion in annual commercial revenue, T-Head does not rule out an IPO
body_en: On March 19, during the earnings call following the release of the financial report, Alibaba CEO Wu Yongming announced the commercial goals of Alibaba Group's AI strategy: within five years, the annual commercial revenue from cloud and AI will grow significantly from over 100 billion yuan this year to 100 billion US dollars (approximately 690 billion yuan), with a compound annual growth rate of about 47%. As of the end of February in fiscal year 2026, Alibaba Cloud's external commercial revenue has exceeded 100 billion yuan. "The continuous growth of Alibaba's AI and cloud revenue and profit is foreseeable," Wu Yongming stated. With the continuous growth of the company's revenue scale, the upgrade of the AI business from selling resources to selling intelligent capabilities, and the cost reduction and efficiency improvement brought by T-Head's self-developed chips, the company is fully confident in its five-year goal. At the same time, he emphasized that growth is related to the scale effect of products, and during the process of R&D investment and market growth, it will not be a linear growth; today's investment may take one or two years to generate greater growth. Alibaba is forming a full-stack AI layout: with chips and cloud computing as the AI infrastructure layer, Token Hub as the main thread, and an AI model and application layer composed of large models, the MaaS business, and "to-B + to-C" applications, together constituting complete capabilities from AI Infra to applications. In his speech, Wu Yongming mentioned that when a large number of enterprises consume tokens, they do not treat tokens as an IT budget, but rather as part of the entire company's production or R&D costs and means of production. This is the most fundamental intrinsic factor for Alibaba to see the long-term nature of future AI growth. He expects that in the future, commercial MaaS revenue will become Alibaba Cloud's largest revenue-generating product. Alibaba Cloud is accelerating the construction of its MaaS platform. Over the past three months, the token consumption scale of the public model service market on the Bailian MaaS platform has increased by 6 times. In terms of models, Alibaba stated that it will soon launch the next version of the model optimized for coding and agentic scenarios based on Qwen3.5. T-Head, appearing in Alibaba's financial report for the first time, became the focus of this earnings call. The financial report shows that T-Head's self-developed GPU chips have achieved large-scale mass production. Wu Yongming revealed that as of February 2026, the product has achieved a cumulative large-scale delivery of 470,000 units. In Alibaba Cloud's actual business scenarios, over 60% of T-Head chips serve external commercial customers. It has completed AI task adaptation for large-scale external customers and supported the AI tasks of more than 400 enterprise customers, covering multiple industries such as the Internet, financial services, and autonomous driving. "In the next 3-5 years, global AI computing power will be in a very tight state, especially in the Chinese market where it will be even tighter." Based on his optimism about the continuous growth in demand for AI computing power, Wu Yongming stated that T-Head, with its self-developed chip capabilities, is crucial to Alibaba. It can provide more AI computing power to Alibaba's cloud and AI businesses, and also enable the MaaS business to gain higher growth momentum. Currently, T-Head's annualized revenue scale has reached 10 billion yuan. He stated that in the future, T-Head does not rule out the possibility of an IPO. In addition, regarding on-demand retail, Jiang Fan, CEO of Alibaba's E-commerce Business Group, stated that Alibaba will maintain its goal of exceeding 1 trillion yuan in overall GMV for on-demand retail in fiscal year 2028, and expects to achieve overall profitability in fiscal year 2029. Over the next two years, it will firmly invest towards this goal while achieving a leading market position. title_en: How is the comprehensive rectification of "involutionary" competition progressing? (New Economic Landscape)
body_en: The more "involutionary" products become, the lower their quality. A power bank manufacturer was investigated for violating mandatory product certification regulations and false advertising; the more "involutionary" platforms become, the greater the pressure on merchants. Several food delivery platforms were summoned for a "subsidy war"... "Involutionary" competition is low-price, low-quality, and low-level competition. It not only disrupts the market, reduces the efficiency of market resource allocation, and erodes the long-term competitiveness of enterprises, but also affects industrial structure optimization and high-quality development. In response to typical "involutionary" behaviors in market competition, a series of measures have been introduced since last year. What is the progress of comprehensive rectification of "involutionary" competition? Reporters conducted interviews. Strengthen regulation of "involutionary" competition such as mandatory promotion and commercial defamation. "The platform requires hotels to enable 'price adjustment assistant.' Once it detects that our prices are higher than other platforms, it automatically lowers the room rates without notifying us." A hotel operator recounted their experience of being forced to have their pricing interfered with by a certain platform. Recently, under regulatory pressure, the platform has taken down the "price adjustment assistant" function, which is of positive significance in alleviating price "involution" in the hotel industry. Early this year, the State Administration for Market Regulation issued the "Guidelines for Anti-Monopoly Compliance of Internet Platforms," listing eight risk examples such as "lowest price on the whole network" and platform sales below cost, clarifying the content and specific requirements for the compliance of internet platform enterprises, which helps to raise market expectations, guide enterprises to operate legally, and prevent problems before they occur. The revised Anti-Unfair Competition Law in June 2025 strengthens the regulation of new and typical "involutionary" competition. For example, regarding platform behaviors that force merchants on the platform to reduce prices, or even require them to be the "lowest price on the whole network," against their will, it is explicitly stipulated that merchants shall not be forced or implicitly forced to sell goods at prices below cost according to the platform's pricing rules, disrupting the market competition order. Regarding the behavior of some operators hiring "internet trolls" to maliciously slander other operators, it fills legal loopholes and expands the scope of commercial defamation targets from "competitors" to "other operators," thereby more comprehensively regulating relevant defamation behaviors. A series of institutional rules are continuously improved, aiming to solve the problem of "involutionary" competition with practical and strong measures. Strengthen certification supervision of products clearly priced below cost. Some media reported that a consumer's power bank caught fire while charging on the sofa. When they left home, they forgot to unplug it, and a tragedy occurred within just three hours, destroying almost everything in the house and causing heavy losses. Inferior power banks are a typical example of "the more the market is involved, the lower the quality of products," ultimately infringing on consumer rights. How to prevent the risk of product quality decline caused by "involutionary" competition in production enterprises? Yang Dong, deputy director of the Certification Supervision Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation, believes that mandatory product certification is an important means to reduce institutional transaction costs and guard the bottom line of product quality and safety. Under the pressure of "involutionary" competition, the impulse of enterprises to reduce costs increases, and the potential risks to product quality further increase. Strengthening product consistency management has become a fundamental element in effectively leveraging the mandatory product certification system. Regulatory authorities will deeply carry out a special action to "guard the bottom line" of the mandatory product certification system. Strengthen the daily supervision of designated certification bodies for mandatory product certification, conduct continuous compliance checks on the capacity and conditions of these bodies, and establish a bimonthly scheduling mechanism for designated bodies of key products. Improve the level of refined management, requiring certification bodies to strengthen risk identification, use "cost accounting" methods, and strengthen certification supervision of products clearly priced below cost. Formulate management regulations for certification bodies to establish certification quality directors and certification project quality managers, strengthening responsibility to individuals. Strengthen the inspection of raw materials and important components during certification implementation, and promote the improvement of enterprises' quality assurance capabilities and product consistency levels. Reduce disorderly competition in key industries and regulate the behavior of local governments. What policy measures have been introduced since last year to address "involutionary" behaviors? In response to phenomena such as "subsidy wars" on internet platforms, the "Basic Requirements for Service Management of Food Delivery Platforms" have been implemented, stipulating the overall requirements for service management of food delivery platforms, including merchant management, pricing behavior, protection of delivery personnel's rights and interests, protection of consumers' rights and interests, and complaint and appeal handling, etc., to improve service quality and reduce disorderly competition. In response to phenomena such as "emphasis on marketing over quality" and "low price and low quality" in online sales, the "Guiding Opinions on Improving the Quality of Products and Services of Online Transaction Platforms" provide institutional guarantees for promoting a virtuous cycle of "high quality and reasonable price." To promote the high-quality development of new energy vehicles, lithium batteries, and photovoltaic industries, the State Administration for Market Regulation deployed the development of 167 national standards in the "new three items" field in 2025. Through standards for quality and safety, energy efficiency and consumption, and classification, it promotes the governance of "involutionary" competition in "new three items" enterprises. Zhu Meina, deputy director of the Standards and Technical Management Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation, introduced that as of the end of 2025, China has cumulatively issued 57 related national standards. In the next step, the development of relevant national standards will be further accelerated to drive the high-quality development of the "new three items" with standard leadership. Zhao Chunlei, deputy director of the Competition Policy Coordination Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation, introduced that the in-depth implementation of the fair competition review system and strengthening the enforcement against abuse of administrative power to exclude or restrict competition are important measures to regulate improper government intervention in market competition. In 2025, market regulation departments at all levels have carried out a series of work in implementing the fair competition review system and strengthening the enforcement against administrative monopolies. Improve the fair competition review system to further clarify the boundaries of government behavior. The "Implementation Measures for the Regulations on Fair Competition Review" have been published, refining the four aspects and nineteen standards stipulated in the regulations into sixty-six prohibited situations. The "Regulations on Prohibiting and Punishing Abuse of Administrative Power to Exclude or Restrict Competition" have been revised to increase the types of behavioral manifestations, strengthen punishment for violations and accountability, and solidify the institutional foundation for breaking local protectionism and administrative monopolies. In the next step, the State Administration for Market Regulation will promote regions and departments at all levels to thoroughly implement the "Regulations on Fair Competition Review," continuously break down local protectionism and market segmentation, promote the better combination of an effective market and a capable government, deeply rectify "involutionary" competition, and contribute to the in-depth promotion of the construction of a unified national market.

title_en: How is the comprehensive rectification of "involutionary" competition progressing?
body_en: The more "involutionary" products become, the lower their quality. A power bank manufacturer was investigated and punished for violating mandatory product certification regulations and false advertising; the more "involutionary" platforms become, the greater the pressure on merchants. Several food delivery platforms were summoned for "subsidy wars"... "Involutionary" competition is low-price, low-quality, and low-level competition. It not only disrupts the market, reduces the efficiency of market resource allocation, and erodes the long-term competitiveness of enterprises, but also affects industrial structure optimization and upgrading, as well as high-quality development. In response to typical "involutionary" behaviors in market competition, a series of measures have been introduced since last year. What is the progress of comprehensive rectification of "involutionary" competition? Reporters conducted interviews. Strengthening regulation of "involutionary" competition such as mandatory promotion and commercial defamation. "The platform requires hotels to enable the 'Price Adjustment Assistant.' Once it detects that our prices are higher than other platforms, it automatically lowers the room rates without notifying us." A hotel operator recounted their experience of being forced to have their pricing interfered with by a certain platform. Recently, under regulatory pressure, the platform has taken down the "Price Adjustment Assistant" function, which is of positive significance in alleviating price "involution" in the hotel industry. Early this year, the State Administration for Market Regulation issued the "Guidelines for Anti-Monopoly Compliance of Internet Platforms," which lists eight risk examples such as "lowest price on the whole network" and selling at a loss, and clarifies the content and specific requirements for the compliance of internet platform enterprises. This helps to raise market expectations, guide enterprises to operate legally, and prevent problems before they occur. The revised Anti-Unfair Competition Law in June 2025 strengthens the regulation of new and typical "involutionary" competition. For example, for behaviors where platforms, against the will of platform operators, forcibly require price reductions or even demand the "lowest price on the whole network," it is explicitly stipulated that platform operators shall not be forced or implicitly forced to sell goods at prices below cost according to the platform's pricing rules, disrupting the market competition order. For behaviors where some operators hire "internet trolls" to maliciously slander other operators, it fills legal loopholes and expands the scope of commercial defamation targets from "competitors" to "other operators," thereby more comprehensively regulating relevant defamation behaviors. A series of institutional rules are continuously improved, aiming to solve the problem of "involutionary" competition with practical and strong measures. Strengthening certification supervision of products with prices significantly below cost. According to media reports, a consumer placed a power bank on the sofa to charge, and forgot to unplug it when leaving home. In just 3 hours, a tragedy occurred, with almost all household items destroyed and heavy losses incurred. Inferior power banks are a typical example of "the more the market is involuted, the lower the quality of products," ultimately infringing upon consumer rights. How to prevent the risk of declining product quality that may arise from "involutionary" competition by manufacturers? Yang Dong, Deputy Director of the Department of Certification and Supervision of the State Administration for Market Regulation, believes that mandatory product certification is an important means to reduce institutional transaction costs and guard the bottom line of product quality and safety. Under the pressure of "involutionary" competition, the impulse for enterprises to reduce costs increases, and the potential risks to product quality further increase. Strengthening product consistency management has become a fundamental element in leveraging the role of the mandatory product certification system. Regulatory departments will deeply carry out a special campaign to "guard the bottom line" of the mandatory product certification system. Strengthen the daily supervision of mandatory product certification designated bodies, conduct continuous verification of the compliance of their capabilities and conditions, and establish a bimonthly scheduling mechanism for designated bodies of key products. Improve the level of refined management, requiring certification bodies to strengthen risk identification, make good use of "cost accounting" methods, and strengthen certification supervision of products with prices significantly below cost. Formulate management regulations for certification bodies to establish certification quality directors and certification project quality managers, and strengthen the implementation of responsibilities to individuals. Strengthen the inspection of raw materials and important components during certification implementation, and promote the improvement of enterprises' quality assurance capabilities and product consistency. Reducing disorderly competition in key industries and regulating the behavior of local governments. What policy measures have been introduced since last year to address "involutionary" behaviors? In response to phenomena such as "subsidy wars" on internet platforms, the "Basic Requirements for Service Management of Food Delivery Platforms" have been implemented, stipulating the overall requirements for service management of food delivery platforms, including merchant management, pricing behavior, protection of delivery personnel's rights and interests, protection of consumers' rights and interests, and complaint and appeal handling, to improve service quality and reduce disorderly competition. In response to phenomena such as "emphasis on marketing over quality" and "low price and low quality" in online sales, the "Guiding Opinions on Improving the Quality of Products and Services of Online Trading Platforms" provide institutional guarantees for promoting a virtuous cycle of "high quality and good prices." To promote the high-quality development of new energy vehicles, lithium batteries, and photovoltaic industries, the State Administration for Market Regulation has deployed the development of 167 national standards in the "new three items" fields in 2025. Through the development of standards for quality and safety, energy efficiency and consumption, and grading and classification, it aims to govern the "involutionary" competition of "new three items" enterprises. Zhu Meina, Deputy Director of the Department of Standards and Technical Management of the State Administration for Market Regulation, introduced that as of the end of 2025, China has cumulatively issued 57 related national standards. In the next step, the development of relevant national standards will be further accelerated to drive the high-quality development of the "new three items" with standard leadership. Zhao Chunlei, Deputy Director of the Department of Fair Competition Policy Coordination of the State Administration for Market Regulation, introduced that the in-depth implementation of the fair competition review system and strengthening the enforcement against abuse of administrative power to exclude or restrict competition are important measures to regulate improper government intervention in market competition. In 2025, market regulatory departments at all levels have carried out a series of work in implementing the fair competition review system and strengthening the enforcement against administrative monopolies. Improve the fair competition review system to further clarify the boundaries of government behavior. The "Implementation Measures for the Regulations on Fair Competition Review" have been published, refining the four aspects and nineteen standards stipulated in the regulations into sixty-six prohibited situations. The "Regulations on Prohibiting Abuse of Administrative Power to Exclude or Restrict Competition" have been revised to add types of behavioral manifestations, strengthen punishment for violations and accountability, and solidify the institutional foundation for breaking local protectionism and administrative monopolies. In the next step, the State Administration for Market Regulation will promote all regions and departments to deeply implement the "Regulations on Fair Competition Review," continuously break down local protectionism and market segmentation, promote the better combination of an effective market and a capable government, deeply rectify "involutionary" competition, and contribute to the in-depth promotion of the construction of a unified national market.

title_en: State Administration for Market Regulation 2026 First Quarter Regular Press Conference Transcript
body_en: On the morning of March 20th, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) held its first quarterly press conference of 2026. The following is a transcript of the conference: Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Ladies and gentlemen, friends from the media, good morning! Spring breezes bring warmth, and swift horses gallop. We have just entered the Year of the Horse in the lunar calendar and are ushering in the spring of the "15th Five-Year Plan." It is a pleasure to gather with you all again at this hopeful time. We have made a quarterly commitment to jointly open the curtain on this year's first regular press conference. Market regulation work concerns development vitality and the well-being of the people. Over the past year, we have tackled challenges through reform and provided support through service, striving to create a unified, open, and orderly market environment. In the new year, we will continue to uphold our original intention of "regulation for the people" and shoulder the mission of "serving development," striving to write a new chapter on our new journey. Now, I will brief you on the progress of recent key work. Further practical measures to optimize the business environment. Recently, SAMR officially released two new standards: the "Norms for Business Entity Registration Documents (2026 Edition)" and the "Norms for Business Entity Registration Submission Materials (2026 Edition)." The new standards will be fully implemented on May 1st, further improving the efficiency of registration services by strengthening precise information collection, preventing risks of false impersonation, and enhancing the application of technologies such as electronic signatures. Significant achievements in the "Credit Repair Service Year." Since the launch of the "Credit Repair Service Year" in March last year, market regulation departments at all levels have cumulatively repaired the credit of 13.9048 million business entities. Repairing corporate credit rebuilds market confidence. In the next step, SAMR will continue to consolidate the achievements of the campaign, optimize and upgrade the national unified platform for credit repair, issue service guidelines, deepen innovative pilot programs, and provide more standardized, efficient, and convenient credit repair services. In-depth advancement of anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition work. In the first quarter, we intensively issued a series of new regulations. The newly revised "Regulations on Prohibiting Abuse of Administrative Power to Exclude or Restrict Competition" targets administrative monopolies. The "Guidelines on Anti-Monopoly in Public Utilities" and the "Guidelines on Anti-Monopoly Compliance for Internet Platforms" focus on key areas and guide standardized development. The "Regulations on Trade Secret Protection" have been formulated to strengthen the protection of corporate trade secrets and severely crack down on unfair competition practices that infringe upon trade secrets. The "Guidelines on Price Behavior Compliance in the Automotive Industry" have been released to stabilize market expectations and regulate price competition in the automotive market. The "Announcement on Further Improving the Entrusted Review System for Business Operator Concentration" released today will further enhance review efficiency and elevate business operator concentration review work to a new level. Standard-setting leads development in emerging fields. Since the beginning of this year, we have led with high standards and built a foundation with precise measurement, releasing 798 national standards in emerging fields, transportation and logistics, production safety, and people's livelihood security. In areas such as intelligent connected vehicles, life and health, smart meters, and physical chemistry, we have released 32 national metrology technical specifications, effectively supporting industrial technological iteration and upgrading. Continued strengthening of regulation on industrial products sold online. In response to persistent problems of online sales of counterfeit goods and product quality safety, we will formulate the "List of Key Industrial Products Sold Online," which will be an important component of the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Quality and Safety of Key Industrial Products Sold Online." The "List" will effectively promote the implementation of the "Regulations." Public comments will be solicited soon. Upgraded safety governance for special equipment. The 2026 edition of the "Rules for the Use and Management of Special Equipment" was officially released on the SAMR website today and will take effect on May 1st. The issuance of the new rules will further standardize the use and management of special equipment, effectively implement the primary responsibility for safety, build a strong safety defense line for special equipment, and effectively ensure the safety of people's lives and property. Precise efforts in special rectification campaigns. Recently, SAMR has deployed several special rectification campaigns: first, a six-month cleanup and rectification of the misuse of suggestive language in relevant advertisements to restore a clear and truthful market; second, a joint law enforcement action to "crack down on counterfeiting and clear up sources" in traditional craft markets, targeting issues such as "fake certificates, fake institutions, fake products, and fake websites" in areas like jewelry, precious metal ornaments, and rosewood products, to protect the integrity of the industry; third, a series of actions to improve compliance and quality in online food safety, with special rectification focusing on prominent issues such as food sold through live streaming, health foods, and internet-famous foods; fourth, comprehensive governance of prominent issues in alcoholic beverage products, severely cracking down on illegal and irregular acts related to alcoholic beverages to safeguard the bottom line of food safety. In addition, we would like to highlight two points: first, the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Food Business Operators Implementing Primary Food Safety Responsibility in Live E-commerce" and the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Food Sales Chain Enterprises Implementing Primary Food Safety Responsibility" officially take effect today. Please pay attention. Second, the "Draft Amendments to the Implementation Measures of the Regulations on Fair Competition Review" will be open for public comment soon. We sincerely invite all sectors of society to offer their suggestions. The above is the full content of this briefing. Market regulation, with its mission on its shoulders, never stops. We will, with firmer resolve and more solid work, guard a clear market and escort a better life. Next, we will enter the question-and-answer session. Please raise your hands to signal, and state your affiliated institution. Question from a reporter from China Consumer News: You just mentioned that SAMR has deployed a joint law enforcement action to "crack down on counterfeiting and clear up sources" in traditional craft markets. What specific measures are being taken in this action to address the chaos of "fake certificates" and "fake products" in online marketing channels such as e-commerce platforms and live streams? If consumers suspect that a merchant's inspection report is fake, what channels can they use to quickly verify or report it? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: The online space is not beyond the law. In response to the chaos of "fake certificates" and "fake products" appearing on e-commerce platforms and in live streams, this action will strike hard and use sharp tools, bringing platform operators, live stream operators, and anchors within the scope of key supervision. We will guide and urge online trading platforms to use technological means to build early warning and monitoring models, enhance intelligent identification capabilities, and promptly discover and remove counterfeit goods. At the same time, we will focus on investigating and punishing online false marketing and false review activities, and severely crack down on behaviors of setting up fake websites or links to provide false certificate information. We will clean up and investigate and deal with business activities that mislead consumers by operating without verified qualifications, forging or misusing inspection reports, or illegally using keywords such as "inspection and testing" in accordance with the law. If you suspect that an inspection report is forged, you can take the following measures: First, verify the identity. You can log in to the official website of the market regulation department to check the qualifications of the institution. If the institution cannot be found or the information does not match, the authenticity of the report is questionable. Second, check the information. Verify whether the product name, model, and batch number in the report match the information of the physical object. If they do not match, be vigilant. Third, inquire about authenticity. Directly contact the inspection agency through official channels to find out if it is genuine or fake. Fourth, seek redress early. If a false report is found, report it immediately to the local market regulation department through the 12315 platform. We would like to remind everyone that an inspection report is not a "universal pass," and rational consumption is the "amulet." Consumers are advised to pay more attention to reputation, compare credibility, and not be blinded by "a piece of paper" or pay for "impulse purchases." Let us work together to build a strong defense line for quality and safety, making every live stream shopping experience a pleasant one of confident consumption and happy ordering. Question from a reporter from Guangming Daily: You just mentioned that the 2026 edition of the "Rules for the Use and Management of Special Equipment" will be released. Could you please introduce the characteristics of the new rules? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Special equipment is ubiquitous across all industries and involved in all aspects of production and life. The total number of special equipment nationwide has exceeded 24.4 million units, with pressure pipelines exceeding one million kilometers and gas cylinders exceeding 300 million. These types of equipment have complex usage scenarios and high safety risks, so we must adhere to prevention first and advance the front line, building a safety defense line from the source to avoid casualties and property losses. As a core safety technical specification, the new "Rules for the Use and Management of Special Equipment" can be summarized by four core characteristics: First, responsibilities are clearer. The new rules refine the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Special Equipment Use Units Implementing Primary Safety Responsibility," unify the requirements for the establishment and staffing of safety management personnel in special equipment use units, and clarify the responsibilities of key positions such as safety directors and safety officers, ensuring "clear powers and responsibilities, and accountability to individuals." Second, management is more in place. The risk control and hidden danger investigation and treatment mechanisms of special equipment use units are organically integrated, forming a closed-loop management of daily control, weekly investigation, and monthly scheduling, allowing for early detection and early treatment of hidden dangers. Third, supervision is more precise. Based on the scale, quantity, and risk characteristics of special equipment, differentiated and precise measures are implemented. Instead of a "one-size-fits-all" approach, we adopt a "tailored" approach for precise supervision and targeted efforts. Fourth, services are more optimized. Online declaration and online verification are promoted, allowing data to travel more and businesses to run less. The registration process is simplified, and processing efficiency is greatly improved, truly achieving benefits for businesses and convenience for the public, with speed and efficiency. In the next step, we will strictly enforce supervision and rigidly promote implementation. We will promote the full implementation of the new rules, strengthen supervision, and strictly enforce the law. We will ensure that safety responsibilities are carried through from beginning to end, that risk investigation never stops, and that the lives and property of the people are protected. Question from a reporter from People's Daily: Could you introduce the background for the issuance of the "Regulations on Trade Secret Protection" and what new features and requirements the regulations have? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: The issuance of the "Regulations on Trade Secret Protection" is a call of the times and a direction of reform, with great significance and far-reaching impact. It is an important step in building a trade secret protection system and an important part of promoting the implementation of the law. On the one hand, it refines legal provisions, making protection clear and tangible. The "Anti-Unfair Competition Law" has undergone three revisions, continuously strengthening the foundation of trade secret protection. This "Regulation" further refines these provisions with a clear objective: to make legal provisions operable and rights protection perceivable, providing a clear "roadmap" and "instruction manual" for market operators and regulators. On the other hand, it aligns with international rules and escorts opening-up with high standards. High-level protection is high-level opening-up. Perfect trade secret protection is the "ballast stone" for aligning with high-standard international economic and trade rules and a "booster" for creating a fair competitive environment and serving global business entities. The characteristics of the "Regulations" can be summarized in three points: First, it responds to the new needs of trade secret protection in the digital age. The forms of trade secrets are changing, and data algorithms are becoming core assets. The "Regulations" actively respond to the wave of digital information, clearly including "data" and "algorithms" within the scope of technical information protected by trade secrets, listing technical confidentiality measures for scenarios such as remote office and cross-border collaboration, and clarifying digital situations among "improper means" of infringing trade secrets. Second, it constructs a systematic administrative law enforcement and supervision system. It defines and refines the constituent elements of trade secrets and clarifies case jurisdiction, filing standards, the burden of proof for rights holders and suspected infringers, circumstances that do not constitute infringement of trade secrets, supervision and law enforcement means, legal responsibilities, and administrative penalty discretion. Third, it comprehensively enhances the governance effectiveness of trade secret protection. It promotes the shift of focus forward, strengthening operators' awareness and capacity for trade secret protection through training and other means; encourages the establishment of modern management systems, strengthening trade secret protection through innovative forms such as certification and evidence preservation; and fully leverages the role of industry self-regulation to build a comprehensive trade secret protection framework. Question from a reporter from Xinhua News Agency: On March 1st, the pilot reform of the CCC mark deployment by SAMR officially began. Could you please introduce the relevant situation of this reform? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Previously, SAMR launched a pilot reform of the CCC mark for three major categories and 11 types of products, including power banks, electric bicycles and safety accessories, and gas appliances and safety accessories. This reform aims to improve the compulsory product certification system, consolidate the primary responsibility of enterprises for product quality and safety, and effectively prevent illegal acts such as the counterfeiting of certification marks and false certification. This reform focuses on problems and emphasizes practical results. On the basis of the original CCC mark, it integrates a CCC traceability QR code to build a data chain of certification information linking "certified products—manufacturing enterprises—certification certificates—issuing bodies." With just "one-click scanning," one can verify in real-time whether a product has obtained valid CCC certification and clearly obtain key information such as the producer, product specifications, and issuing body, achieving "traceability from the source, verification of authenticity, and accountability." We adhere to the principle that reform should not add burdens and services should not increase costs. The pilot reform clearly requires certification bodies to provide CCC traceability QR code labels free of charge to certified enterprises when issuing certificates, for printing or embossing on products. A 12-month preparation and transition period has been set to allow enterprises sufficient time to adjust and adapt. After the transition period ends, i.e., from March 1, 2027, all certified products manufactured and sold within the pilot scope will be required to "carry the code" to be standardized for market entry. Currently, the pilot reform work has been fully launched and is progressing in an orderly manner. The first batch of 11 pilot products with CCC traceability QR codes have been put into production and are being launched successively. In the next step, we will continue to deepen the pilot program, summarize our experience, make regulation smarter, make quality more reliable, and ensure that the dividends of reform truly benefit thousands of households. Question from a reporter from Economic Daily: You just mentioned that SAMR released the "Announcement on Further Improving the Entrusted Review System for Business Operator Concentration" today. Could you please briefly introduce the relevant situation? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Improving the entrusted review system for business operator concentration is another measure to deepen reform taken by SAMR, following the pilot entrusted review transitioning to formal entrusted review on August 1, 2025. The purpose is to further improve quality and efficiency, and to accelerate the review of business operator concentration. This is mainly reflected in two aspects: First, "full coverage" of entrusted case types. In addition to entrusting some simple cases, we have added entrusted review for some non-simple cases, achieving full coverage of entrusted review for business operator concentration case types and further improving review efficiency. Second, "expansion" of the entrusted review team. Based on the original 5 entrusted provincial market regulation departments, we have added 3 more provincial market regulation departments to review simple cases, meeting the local demand for investment and mergers and acquisitions growth, and better serving regional development strategies such as the great development of the western regions and the comprehensive revitalization of the northeast. Looking back, on August 1, 2022, SAMR officially launched a three-year pilot program for entrusted review of business operator concentration. Three years later, we have transitioned the pilot entrusted review to a normalized and standardized formal entrusted review system. Since the implementation of entrusted review, review efficiency has significantly increased, regulatory capacity has steadily strengthened, and synergy between central and local authorities has continued to grow. As of the end of 2025, SAMR has entrusted the market regulation departments of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Chongqing, and Shaanxi to review 1,550 cases of business operator concentration, accounting for 56% of the total number of applications received by SAMR during the same period. Of these, 1,376 cases have been concluded, accounting for 57% of the total number of cases concluded by SAMR during the same period. The total transaction value of these cases was approximately 4.26 trillion yuan, accounting for 39% of the total transaction value of all cases concluded by SAMR during the same period. From 2023 to 2025, the number of cases concluded by entrusted provincial market regulation departments increased from 358 to 436, and then to 491, with an average annual growth rate of 17%. In the next step, we will strengthen supervision and guidance of the entrusted provincial market regulation departments to ensure that review work is unified, standardized, and efficient, continuously stimulate market vitality, and better serve the overall situation of high-quality development. Question from a reporter from Phoenix TV: You mentioned earlier that the "List of Key Industrial Products Sold Online (2026 Edition)" will be open for public comment soon. What are the main considerations for formulating this "List"? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: At the end of last year, SAMR released the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Quality and Safety of Key Industrial Products Sold Online," which clarifies the quality and safety responsibilities and obligations of e-commerce operators for key industrial products sold online. The "List of Key Industrial Products Sold Online" is a key supporting document for the "Regulations," defining the specific scope of key industrial products sold online. The compilation of this "List" primarily considers the following factors: First, it focuses on products with high online sales volume, prioritizing industrial products with large sales volumes, wide audiences, and frequent consumer use, such as electric water heaters and toys. Second, it targets pain points in product quality and safety, focusing on products with potential safety hazards, high non-compliance rates in supervision and spot checks, and those that are prone to causing personal injury or property damage, such as electric bicycles and household gas stoves. Third, it focuses on operability and effectiveness, fully considering the technical capabilities of e-commerce platforms in quality control aspects such as review and inspection, to ensure that requirements can be implemented and are feasible, such as products requiring code verification like safety helmets and mobile power supplies. The "List" will provide clear and explicit guidance for e-commerce operators selling key industrial products, which will further promote the innovation and healthy development of the platform economy. Question from a reporter from China News Service: On January 9th, SAMR announced the launch of an investigation and assessment of market competition in the food delivery platform service industry. What is the latest progress? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: At the beginning of the year, the Office of the Anti-Monopoly Commission of the State Council announced the launch of an investigation and assessment of market competition in the food delivery platform service industry in accordance with the "Anti-Monopoly Law." The purpose is to express competition concerns, assess monopoly risks, and regulate market order in response to issues such as "subsidies, price wars, and traffic control" in the industry. We are proceeding with the investigation and assessment according to the established plan. Currently, in conjunction with the members of the Anti-Monopoly Commission of the State Council, we have conducted on-site investigations at relevant food delivery platforms to collect comprehensive information; organized merchant symposiums to communicate with industry associations and platform operators; and conducted face-to-face interviews to widely understand the concerns and demands of merchants, delivery riders, and consumers on the platforms. In the next step, we will continue to conduct on-site inspections, interviews, and surveys to gain an in-depth understanding of the competitive behavior of food delivery platforms, fully solicit opinions from platform operators, new employment groups, and consumers, systematically analyze market competition, organize analysis and argumentation, transmit regulatory pressure, and propose corresponding disposal measures. Question from a reporter from CCTV Finance Program Center: What follow-up enforcement actions has SAMR taken regarding the issues exposed in this year's "3.15" Gala? Can you disclose the latest progress? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: This question you've raised is of great concern to everyone, I believe. Regarding the violations of laws and regulations in the market regulation field exposed by the "3.15" Gala, SAMR has quickly deployed efforts to investigate and deal with them strictly and swiftly in accordance with the law. We have also held talks and assigned special supervision to relevant local governments and market regulation departments to resolutely protect the legitimate rights and interests of consumers. The enforcement actions have achieved the following phased progress. Regarding the issue of "bleached chicken feet," SAMR organized a special task force to conduct surprise enforcement on the involved enterprises, seizing 27 barrels of hydrogen peroxide (commonly known as "double oxygen water") and 551 boxes of chicken feet products on site. Regarding the issue of "all-purpose exosomes," the local drug administration departments, in conjunction with health, market regulation, and public security departments, formed an inspection team and seized "exosome" related products on site. Currently, relevant departments have filed investigations against 4 involved companies and 3 medical aesthetic institutions and medical institutions in accordance with the law. Regarding the issue of "growth-boosting marketing scams," local market regulation departments, in conjunction with public security and health departments, have conducted investigations and disposed of the cases, filing investigations against 11 business entities. Relevant products are being sampled and sent for testing. Regarding the issue of "mystery experts in private domain marketing," local market regulation departments, in conjunction with public security departments, have conducted on-site inspections and extracted electronic data and key evidence from the involved companies, including the production of false course lectures. Regarding the issue of "who is poisoning AI," local market regulation departments, in conjunction with public security departments, have conducted on-site inspections of the involved enterprises, and the public security department has launched an investigation.
