Our attitude is: we will not let go until the problems are thoroughly investigated, and we will not let go until rectification is in place. Market regulation departments will take practical actions to respond to social concerns and build a strong defense line for consumer safety. Question from a reporter from the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection News Center: I noticed that SAMR recently deployed the "Clear Wind Iron Discipline" education and rectification work for law enforcement teams. Can you introduce the relevant situation? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: In order to build a market regulation team that enforces the law for the people and has a strong work style, on the basis of three years of work style construction, SAMR has recently deployed a year-long "Clear Wind Iron Discipline" special education and rectification action. The purpose is to further establish and practice a correct view of development achievements, improve the level of standardized and civilized law enforcement, and effectively maintain a fair and orderly market environment. This action focuses on three main tasks: First, consolidate the ideological foundation and adhere to "regulation for the people." We will conduct in-depth discussions on "Why enforce the law and for whom," launch an online warning education base, and report negative cases. The sole purpose is to let the concept of "regulation for the people" penetrate the hearts of every law enforcement officer and translate into conscious action, making law enforcement more forceful and service warmer. Second, temper excellent skills and achieve "precise striking." We will organize all-staff training, conduct skill competitions, and strengthen practical training. The goal is to improve the regulatory capabilities of frontline personnel from clue discovery to case investigation. We will establish a talent pool of skilled case handlers and cultivate law enforcement and case handling experts, protecting fairness with professionalism and winning public trust with competence. Third, adhere to introspection and strictly rectify discipline. We will adopt a "zero tolerance" attitude towards issues such as uncivilized law enforcement, irregular procedures, and unfair case handling, and resolutely self-examine, strictly examine, and deeply examine them. Specific measures include comprehensive self-examination and self-correction, extensive clue collection, strict investigation and punishment in accordance with the law, and deepening reform through cases. For prominent issues, we will announce a batch, deal with a batch, and transfer a batch, with no cover-ups and no leniency. At the same time, we will adhere to both root causes and symptomatic treatment, improve normalized measures for work style and discipline construction, improve the mechanism for supervising law enforcement discipline, and actively introduce social supervision to fundamentally enforce discipline and improve work style. To facilitate supervision channels, we will soon open a "Clear Wind Iron Discipline" reporting platform on the homepage of the SAMR website. We welcome all sectors of society and friends from the media to actively provide clues and strengthen supervision. The market regulation team is the main force for maintaining market order and the service team that interacts most with the public. We will, with the determination of self-revolution, strictly, deeply, and practically carry out this education and rectification, striving to forge an iron army of law enforcement that the Party can trust and the people are satisfied with. Thank you for your continued support and companionship, friends from the media. Every bit of progress in market regulation work is inseparable from your recording, witnessing, and promotion. On the road ahead, let us continue to work side by side, respond to concerns with facts, guard trust with actions, and jointly maintain a fair and orderly market environment. Today's press conference ends here. Thank you all again!

On the morning of March 20th, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) held its first quarterly press conference of 2026. The following is a transcript of the conference: Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Ladies and gentlemen, friends from the media, good morning! Spring breezes bring warmth, and swift horses gallop. We have just entered the Year of the Horse in the lunar calendar and are ushering in the spring of the "15th Five-Year Plan." It is a pleasure to gather with you all again at this hopeful time. We have made a quarterly commitment to jointly open the curtain on this year's first regular press conference. Market regulation work concerns development vitality and the well-being of the people. Over the past year, we have tackled challenges through reform and provided support through service, striving to create a unified, open, and orderly market environment. In the new year, we will continue to uphold our original intention of "regulation for the people" and shoulder the mission of "serving development," striving to write a new chapter on our new journey. Now, I will brief you on the progress of recent key work. Further practical measures to optimize the business environment. Recently, SAMR officially released two new standards: the "Norms for Business Entity Registration Documents (2026 Edition)" and the "Norms for Business Entity Registration Submission Materials (2026 Edition)." The new standards will be fully implemented on May 1st, further improving the efficiency of registration services by strengthening precise information collection, preventing risks of false impersonation, and enhancing the application of technologies such as electronic signatures. Significant achievements in the "Credit Repair Service Year." Since the launch of the "Credit Repair Service Year" in March last year, market regulation departments at all levels have cumulatively repaired the credit of 13.9048 million business entities. Repairing corporate credit rebuilds market confidence. In the next step, SAMR will continue to consolidate the achievements of the campaign, optimize and upgrade the national unified platform for credit repair, issue service guidelines, deepen innovative pilot programs, and provide more standardized, efficient, and convenient credit repair services. In-depth advancement of anti-monopoly and anti-unfair competition work. In the first quarter, we intensively issued a series of new regulations. The newly revised "Regulations on Prohibiting Abuse of Administrative Power to Exclude or Restrict Competition" targets administrative monopolies. The "Guidelines on Anti-Monopoly in Public Utilities" and the "Guidelines on Anti-Monopoly Compliance for Internet Platforms" focus on key areas and guide standardized development. The "Regulations on Trade Secret Protection" have been formulated to strengthen the protection of corporate trade secrets and severely crack down on unfair competition practices that infringe upon trade secrets. The "Guidelines on Price Behavior Compliance in the Automotive Industry" have been released to stabilize market expectations and regulate price competition in the automotive market. The "Announcement on Further Improving the Entrusted Review System for Business Operator Concentration" released today will further enhance review efficiency and elevate business operator concentration review work to a new level. Standard-setting leads development in emerging fields. Since the beginning of this year, we have led with high standards and built a foundation with precise measurement, releasing 798 national standards in emerging fields, transportation and logistics, production safety, and people's livelihood security. In areas such as intelligent connected vehicles, life and health, smart meters, and physical chemistry, we have released 32 national metrology technical specifications, effectively supporting industrial technological iteration and upgrading. Continued strengthening of regulation on industrial products sold online. In response to persistent problems of online sales of counterfeit goods and product quality safety, we will formulate the "List of Key Industrial Products Sold Online," which will be an important component of the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Quality and Safety of Key Industrial Products Sold Online." The "List" will effectively promote the implementation of the "Regulations." Public comments will be solicited soon. Upgraded safety governance for special equipment. The 2026 edition of the "Rules for the Use and Management of Special Equipment" was officially released on the SAMR website today and will take effect on May 1st. The issuance of the new rules will further standardize the use and management of special equipment, effectively implement the primary responsibility for safety, build a strong safety defense line for special equipment, and effectively ensure the safety of people's lives and property. Precise efforts in special rectification campaigns. Recently, SAMR has deployed several special rectification campaigns: first, a six-month cleanup and rectification of the misuse of suggestive language in relevant advertisements to restore a clear and truthful market; second, a joint law enforcement action to "crack down on counterfeiting and clear up sources" in traditional craft markets, targeting issues such as "fake certificates, fake institutions, fake products, and fake websites" in areas like jewelry, precious metal ornaments, and rosewood products, to protect the integrity of the industry; third, a series of actions to improve compliance and quality in online food safety, with special rectification focusing on prominent issues such as food sold through live streaming, health foods, and internet-famous foods; fourth, comprehensive governance of prominent issues in alcoholic beverage products, severely cracking down on illegal and irregular acts related to alcoholic beverages to safeguard the bottom line of food safety. In addition, we would like to highlight two points: first, the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Food Business Operators Implementing Primary Food Safety Responsibility in Live E-commerce" and the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Food Sales Chain Enterprises Implementing Primary Food Safety Responsibility" officially take effect today. Please pay attention. Second, the "Draft Amendments to the Implementation Measures of the Regulations on Fair Competition Review" will be open for public comment soon. We sincerely invite all sectors of society to offer their suggestions. The above is the full content of this briefing. Market regulation, with its mission on its shoulders, never stops. We will, with firmer resolve and more solid work, guard a clear market and escort a better life. Next, we will enter the question-and-answer session. Please raise your hands to signal, and state your affiliated institution. Question from a reporter from China Consumer News: You just mentioned that SAMR has deployed a joint law enforcement action to "crack down on counterfeiting and clear up sources" in traditional craft markets. What specific measures are being taken in this action to address the chaos of "fake certificates" and "fake products" in online marketing channels such as e-commerce platforms and live streams? If consumers suspect that a merchant's inspection report is fake, what channels can they use to quickly verify or report it? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: The online space is not beyond the law. In response to the chaos of "fake certificates" and "fake products" appearing on e-commerce platforms and in live streams, this action will strike hard and use sharp tools, bringing platform operators, live stream operators, and anchors within the scope of key supervision. We will guide and urge online trading platforms to use technological means to build early warning and monitoring models, enhance intelligent identification capabilities, and promptly discover and remove counterfeit goods. At the same time, we will focus on investigating and punishing online false marketing and false review activities, and severely crack down on behaviors of setting up fake websites or links to provide false certificate information. We will clean up and investigate and deal with business activities that mislead consumers by operating without verified qualifications, forging or misusing inspection reports, or illegally using keywords such as "inspection and testing" in accordance with the law. If you suspect that an inspection report is forged, you can take the following measures: First, verify the identity. You can log in to the official website of the market regulation department to check the qualifications of the institution. If the institution cannot be found or the information does not match, the authenticity of the report is questionable. Second, check the information. Verify whether the product name, model, and batch number in the report match the information of the physical object. If they do not match, be vigilant. Third, inquire about authenticity. Directly contact the inspection agency through official channels to find out if it is genuine or fake. Fourth, seek redress early. If a false report is found, report it immediately to the local market regulation department through the 12315 platform. We would like to remind everyone that an inspection report is not a "universal pass," and rational consumption is the "amulet." Consumers are advised to pay more attention to reputation, compare credibility, and not be blinded by "a piece of paper" or pay for "impulse purchases." Let us work together to build a strong defense line for quality and safety, making every live stream shopping experience a pleasant one of confident consumption and happy ordering. Question from a reporter from Guangming Daily: You just mentioned that the 2026 edition of the "Rules for the Use and Management of Special Equipment" will be released. Could you please introduce the characteristics of the new rules? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Special equipment is ubiquitous across all industries and involved in all aspects of production and life. The total number of special equipment nationwide has exceeded 24.4 million units, with pressure pipelines exceeding one million kilometers and gas cylinders exceeding 300 million. These types of equipment have complex usage scenarios and high safety risks, so we must adhere to prevention first and advance the front line, building a safety defense line from the source to avoid casualties and property losses. As a core safety technical specification, the new "Rules for the Use and Management of Special Equipment" can be summarized by four core characteristics: First, responsibilities are clearer. The new rules refine the "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Special Equipment Use Units Implementing Primary Safety Responsibility," unify the requirements for the establishment and staffing of safety management personnel in special equipment use units, and clarify the responsibilities of key positions such as safety directors and safety officers, ensuring "clear powers and responsibilities, and accountability to individuals." Second, management is more in place. The risk control and hidden danger investigation and treatment mechanisms of special equipment use units are organically integrated, forming a closed-loop management of daily control, weekly investigation, and monthly scheduling, allowing for early detection and early treatment of hidden dangers. Third, supervision is more precise. Based on the scale, quantity, and risk characteristics of special equipment, differentiated and precise measures are implemented. Instead of a "one-size-fits-all" approach, we adopt a "tailored" approach for precise supervision and targeted efforts. Fourth, services are more optimized. Online declaration and online verification are promoted, allowing data to travel more and businesses to run less. The registration process is simplified, and processing efficiency is greatly improved, truly achieving benefits for businesses and convenience for the public, with speed and efficiency. In the next step, we will strictly enforce supervision and rigidly promote implementation. We will promote the full implementation of the new rules, strengthen supervision, and strictly enforce the law. We will ensure that safety responsibilities are carried through from beginning to end, that risk investigation never stops, and that the lives and property of the people are protected. Question from a reporter from People's Daily: Could you introduce the background for the issuance of the "Regulations on Trade Secret Protection" and what new features and requirements the regulations have? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: The issuance of the "Regulations on Trade Secret Protection" is a call of the times and a direction of reform, with great significance and far-reaching impact. It is an important step in building a trade secret protection system and an important part of promoting the implementation of the law. On the one hand, it refines legal provisions, making protection clear and tangible. The "Anti-Unfair Competition Law" has undergone three revisions, continuously strengthening the foundation of trade secret protection. This "Regulation" further refines these provisions with a clear objective: to make legal provisions operable and rights protection perceivable, providing a clear "roadmap" and "instruction manual" for market operators and regulators. On the other hand, it aligns with international rules and escorts opening-up with high standards. High-level protection is high-level opening-up. Perfect trade secret protection is the "ballast stone" for aligning with high-standard international economic and trade rules and a "booster" for creating a fair competitive environment and serving global business entities. The characteristics of the "Regulations" can be summarized in three points: First, it responds to the new needs of trade secret protection in the digital age. The forms of trade secrets are changing, and data algorithms are becoming core assets. The "Regulations" actively respond to the wave of digital information, clearly including "data" and "algorithms" within the scope of technical information protected by trade secrets, listing technical confidentiality measures for scenarios such as remote office and cross-border collaboration, and clarifying digital situations among "improper means" of infringing trade secrets. Second, it constructs a systematic administrative law enforcement and supervision system. It defines and refines the constituent elements of trade secrets and clarifies case jurisdiction, filing standards, the burden of proof for rights holders and suspected infringers, circumstances that do not constitute infringement of trade secrets, supervision and law enforcement means, legal responsibilities, and administrative penalty discretion. Third, it comprehensively enhances the governance effectiveness of trade secret protection. It promotes the shift of focus forward, strengthening operators' awareness and capacity for trade secret protection through training and other means; encourages the establishment of modern management systems, strengthening trade secret protection through innovative forms such as certification and evidence preservation; and fully leverages the role of industry self-regulation to build a comprehensive trade secret protection framework. Question from a reporter from Xinhua News Agency: On March 1st, the pilot reform of the CCC mark deployment by SAMR officially began. Could you please introduce the relevant situation of this reform? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Previously, SAMR launched a pilot reform of the CCC mark for three major categories and 11 types of products, including power banks, electric bicycles and safety accessories, and gas appliances and safety accessories. This reform aims to improve the compulsory product certification system, consolidate the primary responsibility of enterprises for product quality and safety, and effectively prevent illegal acts such as the counterfeiting of certification marks and false certification. This reform focuses on problems and emphasizes practical results. On the basis of the original CCC mark, it integrates a CCC traceability QR code to build a data chain of certification information linking "certified products—manufacturing enterprises—certification certificates—issuing bodies." With just "one-click scanning," one can verify in real-time whether a product has obtained valid CCC certification and clearly obtain key information such as the producer, product specifications, and issuing body, achieving "traceability from the source, verification of authenticity, and accountability." We adhere to the principle that reform should not add burdens and services should not increase costs. The pilot reform clearly requires certification bodies to provide CCC traceability QR code labels free of charge to certified enterprises when issuing certificates, for printing or embossing on products. A 12-month preparation and transition period has been set to allow enterprises sufficient time to adjust and adapt. After the transition period ends, i.e., from March 1, 2027, all certified products manufactured and sold within the pilot scope will be required to "carry the code" to be standardized for market entry. Currently, the pilot reform work has been fully launched and is progressing in an orderly manner. The first batch of 11 pilot products with CCC traceability QR codes have been put into production and are being launched successively. In the next step, we will continue to deepen the pilot program, summarize our experience, make regulation smarter, make quality more reliable, and ensure that the dividends of reform truly benefit thousands of households. Question from a reporter from Economic Daily: You just mentioned that SAMR released the "Announcement on Further Improving the Entrusted Review System for Business Operator Concentration" today. Could you please briefly introduce the relevant situation? Wang Qiuping, Spokesperson for SAMR and Director of the Department of Publicity: Improving the entrusted review system for business operator concentration is another measure to deepen reform taken by SAMR, following the pilot entrusted review transitioning to formal entrusted review on August 1, 2025. The purpose is to further improve quality and efficiency, and to accelerate the review of business operator concentration. This is mainly reflected in two aspects: First, "full coverage" of entrusted case types. In addition to entrusting some simple cases, we have added entrusted review for some non-simple cases, achieving full coverage of entrusted review for business operator concentration case types and further improving review efficiency. Second, "expansion" of the entrusted review team. Based on the original 5 entrusted provincial market regulation departments, we have added 3 more provincial market regulation departments to review simple cases, meeting the local demand for investment and mergers and acquisitions growth, and better serving regional development strategies such as the great development of the western regions and the comprehensive revitalization of the northeast. Looking back, on August 1, 2022, SAMR officially launched a three-year pilot program for entrusted review of business operator concentration. Three years later, we have transitioned the pilot entrusted review to a normalized and standardized formal entrusted review system. Since the implementation of entrusted review, review efficiency has significantly increased, regulatory capacity has steadily strengthened, and synergy between central and local authorities has continued to grow. As of the end of 2025, SAMR has entrusted the market regulation departments of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Chongqing, and Shaanxi to review 1,550 cases of business operator concentration, accounting for 56% of the total number of applications received by SAMR during the same period. Of these, 1,376 cases have been concluded, accounting for 57% of the total number of cases concluded by SAMR during the same period. The total transaction value of these cases was approximately 4.26 trillion yuan, accounting for 39% of the total transaction value of all cases concluded by SAMR during the same period. From 2023 to 2025, the number of cases concluded by entrusted provincial market regulation departments increased from 358 to 436, and then to 491, with an average annual growth rate of 17%. In the next step, we will strengthen supervision and guidance of the entrusted provincial market regulation departments to ensure that review work is unified, standardized, and efficient, continuously stimulate market vitality, and better serve the overall situation of high-quality development. title_en: Master Lecture Series | Issue 19: Policy Interpretation Meeting on "Rules for Pricing Behavior on Internet Platforms" Held in Beijing
body_en: On March 20th, the Internet Society of China held its 19th "Master Forum" in Beijing, focusing on a policy interpretation session for the "Rules on Pricing Behavior of Internet Platforms." The meeting was presided over by Pei Wei, Deputy Secretary-General of the Internet Society of China. Han Wei, a member of the Expert Advisory Group of the State Council's Anti-Monopoly and Anti-Unfair Competition Commission and Executive Director of the Competition Law Research Center at the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, served as the main expert. He provided an in-depth interpretation of the "Rules on Pricing Behavior of Internet Platforms" (hereinafter referred to as the "Rules"), jointly issued by the National Development and Reform Commission, the State Administration for Market Regulation, and the Cyberspace Administration of China, to help internet companies accurately understand the spirit of the rules and grasp key compliance points. In his opening remarks, Deputy Secretary-General Pei Wei stated that the platform economy is currently at a critical juncture, transitioning from high-speed growth to high-quality development. Price, as a market signal and the most direct touchpoint for user perception, has its behavioral norms that not only concern consumer rights but also directly impact the healthy development of the platform ecosystem. The introduction of the "Rules" is an important opportunity to guide enterprises from passively responding to regulation to actively building compliance systems, and from price competition to value competition. Director Han Wei systematically reviewed and practically analyzed the background, core provisions, and compliance key points of the "Rules." He also elaborated on the compliance risks and response strategies for platform companies in areas such as pricing strategies, promotional activities, price disclosure, and price comparisons, using typical case studies. Representatives from 45 internet companies attended the meeting and exchanged views with the expert on practical issues they encountered. This policy interpretation session provided important guidance for internet companies to accurately understand and effectively implement the "Rules on Pricing Behavior of Internet Platforms." The association will subsequently promote the formulation of the "Self-Discipline Convention on Pricing Behavior of Internet Platforms" and organize the development and promotion of relevant industry standards to help enterprises enhance their compliance capabilities and jointly create a fair, orderly, transparent, and honest market environment for the platform economy.

title_en: Tech Weekly | WeChat Integrates Openclaw; Alibaba's T-Head Does Not Rule Out IPO Possibility
body_en: WeChat officially launches the WeChat "ClawBot" plugin, supporting OpenClaw integration. On the 22nd, WeChat officially launched the WeChat "ClawBot" plugin, which supports OpenClaw integration. Users can connect OpenClaw to WeChat by scanning a QR code or copying a command. After connecting, users can quickly interact with their own "lobsters" through WeChat chat. [Comment]: Considering WeChat's universal user coverage, it's not surprising that this move is expected to ignite a nationwide "lobster farming" craze. Tencent Cloud also reposted the relevant news immediately, and selling tokens through "lobster farming" is expected to become a new high-growth category for future revenue. Alibaba's T-Head Not Ruling Out IPO Possibility On March 19th, during an earnings call, Alibaba stated that T-Head's self-developed GPU chips have achieved mass production, with cumulative mass deliveries reaching 470,000 units as of February 2026. In Alibaba Cloud's actual business scenarios, over 60% of T-Head chips serve external commercial customers, having completed mass AI task adaptation for external clients and supporting AI tasks for over 400 enterprise customers. Currently, T-Head's annualized revenue scale has reached tens of billions, and Alibaba stated that T-Head does not rule out the possibility of an IPO in the future. [Comment]: Alibaba's ambition for AI commercialization is erupting. During the earnings call, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu announced the commercial goals of Alibaba Group's AI strategy: within five years, annual revenue from cloud and AI commercialization will significantly increase from over 100 billion yuan this year to 100 billion US dollars (approximately 690 billion yuan), with a compound annual growth rate of about 47%. In the future, how to seize the market opportunity of tight AI computing power demand and occupy the token entry point will be a major challenge for Alibaba. ByteDance Sells Moonton On March 20th, an internal letter from Moonton was exposed, announcing that Saudi Arabia's Savvy Games Group will acquire Moonton, and the transaction will be completed in the near future. After the transaction, Moonton will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Savvy. Currently, ByteDance and Moonton have not responded to this. According to the internal letter, after the transaction, Moonton's management structure will remain unchanged, and it will still be a Shanghai-headquartered company. Zhang Yunfan, head of ByteDance's gaming business, will continue to serve as Moonton's CEO. The internal letter did not disclose the specific transaction amount, but it is reported that the acquisition price exceeds 6 billion US dollars. [Comment]: ByteDance acquired Moonton Technology in 2021, with reports at the time stating the transaction amount exceeded 4 billion US dollars. If the transaction amount is accurate, this investment has appreciated by 50% in five years. Zhang Shule, an analyst in the gaming industry, told Yicai-First Business Daily that for the seller, ByteDance has resolved a "chicken rib" asset that made money but had weak relevance to its overall strategy, and at a price higher than expected. For the buyer, Saudi Arabia now has its own hit esports game, and with esports and its derivative chains, it has a real foundation for building a second economic pillar besides oil. Alibaba and Baidu Announce on the Same Day, Cloud Vendors Usher in a Price Hike Wave On March 18th, Alibaba Cloud and Baidu AI Cloud announced price increases on the same day. The core reasons for both price increases are based on the explosive global AI demand, the mismatch between supply and demand for computing power, and the significant increase in costs of core hardware such as chips and servers. The price adjustments are made to ensure stable and non-degraded service. [Comment]: The characteristic of this round of price increases by cloud vendors is structural, mainly concentrated in areas such as GPU cloud computing, high-performance storage, and AI networks, rather than a comprehensive increase in general computing power. The core reason for the price increase is the accelerated landing of Agentic AI driven by recent model capability improvements, the phenomenal adoption of OpenClaw, and other factors, leading to a rapid surge in demand for large model training and inference, coupled with phased pressure on high-end chips, HBM, energy consumption, and delivery resources. Microsoft May Sue OpenAI On March 18th, local time, it was reported that Microsoft is considering suing Amazon and OpenAI because Amazon's plan to offer OpenAI's new product Frontier may violate a long-term agreement previously reached between Microsoft and OpenAI. [Comment]: Behind this news is Microsoft's AI anxiety. In addition to disputes in external cooperation, Microsoft is also making internal adjustments. Microsoft announced on March 17th that it will integrate the commercial and consumer versions of Copilot teams to improve user experience. Jacob Andreou, formerly Vice President of AI Products and Growth at Microsoft, will serve as Executive Vice President of Copilot. Microsoft has been under continuous pressure for some time. Especially in terms of stock performance, Microsoft's stock price has been declining since November last year and is currently at a low point. Tiertime and Pop Mart Reach Settlement in IP Dispute On March 16th, 3D printer manufacturer Tiertime released a statement on its Weibo account stating that the company has reached a friendly consultation and settlement with Pop Mart, and the relevant content has been completely removed. The previous dispute between the two parties stemmed from multiple models involving Pop Mart's IPs appearing on Tiertime's MakerWorld platform. These IPs were uploaded by users of the platform, and other users could download the models and print them using Tiertime's 3D printers. Previously, Pop Mart sued Tiertime and its affiliated companies on grounds of copyright ownership and infringement disputes. [Comment]: In China, the popularity of toys and figurines like Labubu in recent years has been a driving force for 3D printer consumption. At the same time, the declining price of 3D printers has also led to this product form moving from the geek community to the mass consumer market. However, how to solve IP copyright issues remains a challenge for the industry. Overseas Star Company Exposed for "Shelling" Kimi Recently, Cursor, an AI programming tool with an overseas valuation of nearly 30 billion US dollars, released its new model Composer 2, claiming it was self-developed without disclosing the base model. Developers confirmed through API model IDs that it is based on the domestically developed open-source Kimi K2.5, which was subsequently confirmed by Musk and the Kimi team. Cursor is facing controversy for "shelling" due to not disclosing its source according to open-source protocols, highlighting that domestic open-source models have become a global AI backbone. [Comment]: The fact that Cursor's base model is based on Kimi proves that open source is the biggest competitive force in the industry and once again validates that Chinese open-source models will become the biggest force in global AI development. In the future, the industry frontier will no longer be about who trains from scratch, but who can adapt, fine-tune, and productize the fastest. Home Appliance Exports to the Middle East Encounter "Growing Pains" As of March 20th, the war between the US and Israel in Iran has entered its 21st day. Chinese home appliance exports are encountering "growing pains." On one hand, exports to the Middle East market are facing obstacles, and logistics costs have doubled. On the other hand, raw material costs have risen sharply. According to a research report from the research institution Industry Online, since the Middle East conflict has continued to escalate, the production volume of Chinese household air conditioners exported has significantly decreased compared to the initial plan. Overseas customers have canceled or postponed orders due to increased shipping costs or additional war surcharges from shipping companies. A decrease of over 500,000 units is expected in March. [Comment]: According to NIQ GfK retail monitoring, the Middle East & Africa major home appliance market has maintained positive growth for the past two years and is a strong performing region globally. Due to the Middle East conflict, shipping and logistics costs have increased in the short term, and exports to the Middle East market are facing obstacles. The European market will also be indirectly impacted. Home appliance exports will face increased pressure in the short term, potentially leading to order losses. If the situation does not ease in the short term, continued war and rising prices will dampen consumer confidence in the region, and the Middle East and Europe may drag down the global major home appliance market, leading to a year-on-year decline in overall major home appliance consumption. Panasonic to Implement New System in China on April 1st Masaharu Nakayama, CSO of Panasonic Corporation and President of China and Northeast Asia Business, recently revealed in an exclusive interview with Yicai-First Business Daily that he will officially take over the responsibility for Panasonic's China and Northeast Asia business from Tetsuro Homma starting April 1st this year. Under the new system, Panasonic's air conditioning and lighting businesses in China will be transferred to sister companies, and after the transfer of 80% equity of Panasonic Home Technology (Hangzhou) Co., Ltd. to YKK Corporation, Panasonic will implement "synergistic sales" in China. Starting April 1st, the new Panasonic Corporation will be officially established, with business divisions for major appliances, small appliances, and AVC products. The China and Northeast Asia business will be the only regionally-focused organization with cross-business coordination functions under the new Panasonic Corporation. [Comment]: Panasonic's move aims to streamline its organization and improve operational efficiency and profitability. The Panasonic China and Northeast Asia Company, established in April 2019, will have its business segmented on April 1st: air quality (fresh air) air conditioning and EW (electrical materials and lighting) businesses will be transferred to Panasonic Air Conditioner Fresh Air Cold Chain Group and Panasonic Electric Works Co., Ltd., respectively. Other white goods and related businesses will be transferred to the new Panasonic Corporation. Panasonic China's business will still have a high degree of autonomous decision-making power. Within the home appliance revenue of Panasonic China and Northeast Asia business, the proportion of revenue from the Asian market (excluding Japan and China) will double to 20% within the next three years. title_en: AI Weekly | Jensen Huang Throws Out Nvidia's Trillion-Dollar Revenue Expectation; Samsung Faces Threat of Largest Strike in History
body_en: Jensen Huang projects Nvidia's revenue to reach one trillion dollars. On March 16th, local time, Nvidia's GTC conference was held at the SAP Center in San Jose. The Groq 3 LPU made its debut, bringing the Rubin platform's chip count to seven, along with five racks, forming an AI supercomputer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also made a prediction about Nvidia's revenue. "A year ago, I saw $500 billion in order revenue from Blackwell and Rubin for 2025-2026, which was a huge amount," Huang said. Now, a year later, he sees that revenue reaching $1 trillion for 2025-2027. [Commentary]: Jensen Huang released information about Nvidia's revenue growth. The next day, in an interview, he reiterated this revenue projection, emphasizing that it does not include revenue from diversified businesses such as CPUs, Groq, storage systems, and Feynman architecture products. Judging by the products released at this GTC, Nvidia's product portfolio has become increasingly rich, showcasing collaborative design and vertical integration, while also releasing information about businesses like space computing and autonomous driving. Jensen Huang: AI will make people busier. On the second day of the GTC keynote, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was interviewed by the media at a hotel near the GTC venue. With the increasing use of AI products like OpenClaw, Huang made a statement in the interview: AI will not make people jobless, but rather will make them busier. "I'm busier every day now than I was six months ago," he said. He noted that the advent of computers, the internet, and mobile devices previously made people busier, and AI completes tasks very quickly. Soon, people will only need to write instructions and definitions, then use agents, and the results will be fed back within 30 minutes, with everything returning to human hands. [Commentary]: Technological advancements will increase efficiency, but not necessarily make people idle. There are many historical examples of this. Before AI completely replaces human jobs, those who use AI will not necessarily become leisurely. Jensen Huang offers a perspective: While people become busier, technological progress will bring many changes to the world, and productivity gains will create new jobs. From this perspective, people need not be overly fearful of the changes brought about by new technologies. Alibaba Establishes Alibaba TokenHub Business Group. News on March 16th: Alibaba is forming a new business unit to integrate its vast AI services and R&D operations. According to reports, the company will house the research team developing the flagship Qwen large model, the consumer-facing application division, and consolidate major AI-related products into a business unit led by CEO Eddie Wu. An internal memo from Eddie Wu to employees shows that the new department, named Alibaba TokenHub, will also oversee the management of DingTalk, Alibaba's Slack-like office application, and devices such as smart glasses under the Quark brand. The mysterious Wukong business unit was revealed for the first time in this adjustment, aiming to build an AI-native work platform for B-end clients. [Commentary]: Prior to this organizational adjustment, Lin Junyang, the core R&D lead for Qwen, suddenly resigned, leading to many questions about Alibaba's AI strategy. This adjustment aims to accelerate collaboration between teams supporting Alibaba's overall AI layout, covering research, product development, and design. It also clearly signals the company's intention to commercialize AI: the department's name directly points to a unit of measurement (Token) for charging users. Baidu Promotes Integration of Large Models and Search/Recommendation Business. On March 18th, Baidu appointed He Jingzhou from the Large Model Algorithm Department to rotate to the Mobile Ecosystem Group (MEG) from the Foundation Model Research Department (BMU), serving as the head of the Baidu App R&D Center, reporting to Luo Rong. This rotation will promote the integration of large models with the search and recommendation business, strengthening the application of cutting-edge technologies like large models in core scenarios such as search and recommendation. The former head, Zhao Shiqi, resigned due to personal reasons. [Commentary]: Previously, Baidu MEG underwent organizational adjustments, merging all search businesses for PC and mobile. This personnel adjustment is a crucial step towards the deep integration of large models and the search/recommendation business. He Jingzhou's rotation from the Foundation Model Department to lead Baidu App R&D aims to break down technical and scenario barriers, directly implementing the capabilities of the Wenxin large model into core search and recommendation segments, and accelerating the upgrade of AI-native search experiences. This is both a strategic implementation of technology-driven business and highlights Baidu's determination to reconstruct core products with AI and enhance competitiveness. Samsung Faces Threat of Largest Strike in History. Amidst the global AI surge and a "super cycle" of tight supply for memory chips, semiconductor giant Samsung Electronics is facing internal turmoil. According to Yonhap News Agency and other media reports, on March 18th, the "Joint Struggle Headquarters," composed of multiple unions of Samsung Electronics, announced that the strike vote, which began on March 9th, received overwhelming support with a 93.1% approval rate. The unions plan to commence an 18-day general strike in late May. [Commentary]: With the global data center construction boom continuously driving up semiconductor demand, market concerns are rising that the strike will disrupt production and exacerbate the global semiconductor supply shortage. Industry estimates suggest that if a general strike is launched, Samsung Electronics could face total losses ranging from 5 trillion to 9 trillion Korean won (approximately RMB 23 billion to 41.4 billion). This includes wafer scrap due to production line shutdowns, penalties for delayed delivery, and maintenance costs for key equipment due to downtime. Kioxia Issues Notice of Discontinuation for TSOP Packaged Products. First Financial reporter learned that storage manufacturer Kioxia recently issued a notice to customers regarding the discontinuation of TSOP (Thin Small Outline Package) products. "Due to the end of the lifecycle of related substrates, market demand, and production limitations, Kioxia needs to stop producing our TSOP packaged products," the notice stated. The reporter learned that the discontinuation affects some SLC (Single-Level Cell) and MLC (Multi-Level Cell or Double-Level Cell) storage products. [Commentary]: Storage manufacturers are shifting their production capacity towards high-performance storage products suitable for AI data centers. QLC technology is gradually gaining attention from NAND flash memory manufacturers. SLC and MLC are considered to have no significant advantage in storage density. Kioxia's previous business focus has shifted to high-speed interface solutions like PCIe 5.0 and QLC SSDs with greater storage density. Some storage manufacturers have also discontinued older production capacity to allocate more to high-performance products in response to strong demand from data centers. Tencent to at Least Double Investment in New AI Products This Year. On March 18th, Tencent Holdings released its fourth-quarter 2025 financial report. In the fourth quarter, Tencent's revenue was 194.37 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 13%, and its Non-IFRS operating profit was 69.52 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 17%. In this financial report, AI was undoubtedly the protagonist. The report mentioned that AI deployment in games accelerated content production and improved marketing efficiency; in advertising, the upgrade of foundation models drove marketing service revenue growth higher than the industry; and Tencent Cloud's scaled profitability benefited from the rising demand for enterprise AI. In an interview, Tencent executives stated that Tencent invested 18 billion yuan in new AI product development last year, with investments in new AI products exceeding 7 billion yuan in the fourth quarter. This year's investment will at least double. [Commentary]: Tencent is using profits generated from its core businesses to support AI investments. Tencent has signaled its intention to continue increasing AI investment. Management mentioned that Tencent's capital expenditure did not grow much last year, and they hope for a significant increase in capital expenditure this year. title_en: The National Market Supervision System's Online Transaction Supervision Work Symposium was held.
body_en: Reported by Peng Xie and intern Jiang Hanyu. From March 19th to 20th, the National Market Supervision System's Online Transaction Supervision Work Symposium was held in Hefei, Anhui. The meeting deeply studied and implemented the spirit of the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the Central Economic Work Conference, conscientiously implemented the deployment requirements of the National Market Supervision Work Conference, summarized and reviewed the work in 2025 and the achievements in online transaction supervision since the "14th Five-Year Plan" period, deeply analyzed the current situation, and deployed key tasks for 2026. The meeting pointed out that in 2025, market supervision departments adhered to the people-centered development philosophy, conscientiously implemented the decisions and deployments of the Party Central Committee and the State Council, took responsibility, and fulfilled their duties. Positive results were achieved in deepening the rectification of prominent problems in the platform economy, improving regulatory systems, rules, and standards, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of all parties, and stimulating the vitality of online business entities. The development environment of the platform economy continued to be optimized, the order of the online market was effectively regulated, and the capacity building of the online supervision team was further strengthened. The meeting emphasized that to do a good job in online transaction supervision in 2026, it is necessary to promote development and security simultaneously, follow the general work idea of "emphasizing politics, strengthening supervision, promoting development, and ensuring security," strengthen regulatory law enforcement in key areas, innovate online transaction supervision methods, improve the ability of penetrative supervision, improve and perfect regulatory systems and rules, continuously enhance the level of normalized supervision, and promote the innovation and healthy development of the platform economy. At the meeting, responsible comrades from the market supervision departments of 10 provinces and municipalities directly under the Central Government, including Beijing, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Shandong, Henan, Guangdong, Sichuan, and Shaanxi, made exchange speeches. Responsible comrades in charge from the market supervision departments of provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, as well as responsible comrades from relevant departments and directly affiliated units of the General Administration, attended the meeting.

title_en: Severing the Black and Gray Industry Chain of "Poisoned" AI
body_en: Recently, China Media Group's 3.15 Gala exposed a shocking black and gray industry chain of "poisoning" AI large models. The essence of AI "poisoning" is to exploit the characteristics of large models that rely on online search for real-time information and learn from massive data, by artificially creating "false consensus" to manipulate algorithm outputs. Illicit businesses use GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) tools to mass-produce fake reviews, forge user evaluations, and fabricate industry rankings, publishing them extensively on online platforms through self-media accounts. When users ask AI for product recommendations, these meticulously designed false information, due to their sheer volume and diverse angles, are more likely to be judged by the AI as "high-weight information" and adopted, ultimately becoming the "standard answer" provided by the AI. Through the "food" for AI "poisoning" data, fictitious products are packaged as authoritative recommendations, and malicious smears are disguised as objective evaluations, forming a complete black and gray chain of "software supply—content generation—network-wide feeding—model manipulation—profit realization." The root cause of this chaos lies in the rapid pace of technological iteration outpacing institutional development, creating a regulatory vacuum. Currently, GEO services operate on the fringes of the law. Although they may violate advertising laws, anti-unfair competition laws, and consumer rights protection laws, the responsible parties are unclear, evidence is difficult to obtain, penalties are light, and the cost of violation is low. At the same time, websites and AI large models, in their pursuit of user coverage, have relaxed source verification, objectively providing opportunities for "poisoning." Furthermore, some businesses, driven by short-term gains, view "AI ranking" as a low-cost shortcut to acquire customers, fueling the spread of black and gray industries. Governing AI "poisoning" requires a systematic approach, building a multi-stakeholder governance framework encompassing legal regulation, technical defense, platform accountability, and public participation. Improve legal provisions and define red lines for behavior. "Malicious data feeding" should be explicitly included within the scope of anti-unfair competition regulations, clarifying the responsibilities of AI service providers, content publishing platforms, and GEO service providers. The distinction between "data poisoning" and legitimate GEO optimization should be clarified, and acts of forging information to manipulate AI should be severely punished, increasing the cost of violation. Platforms and accounts dedicated to publishing false content should be shut down and rectified according to law, eradicating the breeding ground for black and gray industries. Strengthen technical defenses and enhance model "immunity." AI platforms should establish data traceability mechanisms, assess the credibility of training and retrieval content, and introduce a "whitelist" source system to improve the ability to identify mass, homogenized content. For sensitive fields such as healthcare and finance, mandatory cross-verification from multiple sources should be implemented, and information sources should be clearly marked in responses. Algorithms should be used to counter algorithms, establishing dynamic monitoring and cleaning mechanisms to promptly detect and block "poisoning" activities. Consolidate platform responsibilities and build governance synergy. Information publishing platforms should strengthen monitoring and handling of abnormal behaviors such as mass publishing and marketing soft articles, cutting off the channels for the spread of false information. AI large model manufacturers should prioritize the use of official information from authoritative media, academic journals, and licensed institutions, enhance model transparency, and provide links to the sources of answers, allowing users to verify them and breaking the "black box recommendation." Simultaneously, efforts should be made to establish industry standards for AI data security and a data governance ecosystem, standardizing the processes for data collection, cleaning, and auditing. Enhance public literacy and build a social defense line. Users should cultivate the understanding that "AI is not authoritative" and rationally verify information obtained through AI, especially for important issues such as investment and consumption decisions or medical treatment choices, where cross-verification through official channels is essential. Regulatory authorities should strengthen the popularization of AI safety knowledge to help the public identify AI hallucinations and false information. The "poisoning" of AI not only pollutes the "food" of large models but also the foundation of trust in the digital society. Only by letting the sunshine of the rule of law illuminate the black box of algorithms and the power of regulation penetrate the mist of data can we thoroughly sever the black and gray industry chain and truly make AI an intelligent assistant that serves the public and benefits society.

The essence of AI "poisoning" is to exploit the characteristics of large models that rely on online search for real-time information and learn from massive data, by artificially creating "false consensus" to manipulate algorithm outputs. Illicit businesses use GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) tools to mass-produce fake reviews, forge user evaluations, and fabricate industry rankings, publishing them extensively on online platforms through self-media accounts. When users ask AI for product recommendations, these meticulously designed false information, due to their sheer volume and diverse angles, are more likely to be judged by the AI as "high-weight information" and adopted, ultimately becoming the "standard answer" provided by the AI. Through the "food" for AI "poisoning" data, fictitious products are packaged as authoritative recommendations, and malicious smears are disguised as objective evaluations, forming a complete black and gray chain of "software supply—content generation—network-wide feeding—model manipulation—profit realization." The root cause of this chaos lies in the rapid pace of technological iteration outpacing institutional development, creating a regulatory vacuum. Currently, GEO services operate on the fringes of the law. Although they may violate advertising laws, anti-unfair competition laws, and consumer rights protection laws, the responsible parties are unclear, evidence is difficult to obtain, penalties are light, and the cost of violation is low. At the same time, websites and AI large models, in their pursuit of user coverage, have relaxed source verification, objectively providing opportunities for "poisoning." Furthermore, some businesses, driven by short-term gains, view "AI ranking" as a low-cost shortcut to acquire customers, fueling the spread of black and gray industries. Governing AI "poisoning" requires a systematic approach, building a multi-stakeholder governance framework encompassing legal regulation, technical defense, platform accountability, and public participation. Improve legal provisions and define red lines for behavior. "Malicious data feeding" should be explicitly included within the scope of anti-unfair competition regulations, clarifying the responsibilities of AI service providers, content publishing platforms, and GEO service providers. The distinction between "data poisoning" and legitimate GEO optimization should be clarified, and acts of forging information to manipulate AI should be severely punished, increasing the cost of violation. Platforms and accounts dedicated to publishing false content should be shut down and rectified according to law, eradicating the breeding ground for black and gray industries. Strengthen technical defenses and enhance model "immunity." AI platforms should establish data traceability mechanisms, assess the credibility of training and retrieval content, and introduce a "whitelist" source system to improve the ability to identify mass, homogenized content. For sensitive fields such as healthcare and finance, mandatory cross-verification from multiple sources should be implemented, and information sources should be clearly marked in responses. Algorithms should be used to counter algorithms, establishing dynamic monitoring and cleaning mechanisms to promptly detect and block "poisoning" activities. Consolidate platform responsibilities and build governance synergy. Information publishing platforms should strengthen monitoring and handling of abnormal behaviors such as mass publishing and marketing soft articles, cutting off the channels for the spread of false information. AI large model manufacturers should prioritize the use of official information from authoritative media, academic journals, and licensed institutions, enhance model transparency, and provide links to the sources of answers, allowing users to verify them and breaking the "black box recommendation." Simultaneously, efforts should be made to establish industry standards for AI data security and a data governance ecosystem, standardizing the processes for data collection, cleaning, and auditing. Enhance public literacy and build a social defense line. Users should cultivate the understanding that "AI is not authoritative" and rationally verify information obtained through AI, especially for important issues such as investment and consumption decisions or medical treatment choices, where cross-verification through official channels is essential. Regulatory authorities should strengthen the popularization of AI safety knowledge to help the public identify AI hallucinations and false information. The "poisoning" of AI not only pollutes the "food" of large models but also the foundation of trust in the digital society. Only by letting the sunshine of the rule of law illuminate the black box of algorithms and the power of regulation penetrate the mist of data can we thoroughly sever the black and gray industry chain and truly make AI an intelligent assistant that serves the public and benefits society.

title_en: The China Advertising Association, in collaboration with Alimama, has released new industry evaluation standards.
body_en: On March 20th, at the "AI Myriad Forms · Intelligent Leadership of the Future" Alibaba Mama Future Business Awards Annual Ceremony, Alibaba Mama officially announced the launch of its super business intelligence agent engine, "AI Myriad Forms," marking the official end of the single-point tool era in e-commerce operations and reconstructing an operational paradigm centered on "multi-agent collaboration." Under the new paradigm, an industry standard deeply integrated with it has emerged. At the ceremony, Zhang Guohua, President of the China Advertising Association and Global Vice President of the International Advertising Association, officially released the group standard "Evaluation Index System for Brand Power Improvement Effect Driven by Artificial Intelligence." This standard was jointly formulated by the China Advertising Association and Alibaba Mama, in collaboration with numerous academic and industry institutions such as the National Advertising Research Institute, the School of Advertising and Brand Management at Communication University of China, the Peking University New Media Marketing and Communication Research Center, the School of Journalism at Renmin University of China, the School of Journalism and Communication at South China University of Technology, the School of Culture and Communication at Capital University of Economics and Business, Beijing Zhimeng Consulting Co., Ltd., Beijing Guoxin Brand Evaluation Scientific Research Institute, and Miaozhen Information Technology Co., Ltd. It aims to provide a scientific, unified, and operable "measuring stick" for brand power in the new era of marketing deeply involved with AI. President Zhang Guohua stated at the release: "AI is reshaping the underlying paradigm of advertising efficiency and brand value. AI's assistance in setting industry standards and discerning quality is already a top priority for the industry." At the same time, he highly recognized the value of Alibaba Mama's AI Myriad Forms in strengthening brand mindshare and optimizing advertising efficiency, and expressed his expectations for its contribution to industry progress. Today, the logic of brand power construction is undergoing a fundamental reversal. Driven by AI technology, consumers have transformed from silent audiences into active searchers, enthusiastic participants, and keen experience feedback providers. Traditional brand evaluation systems, which rely heavily on static exposure and post-event research, struggle to capture the value recognition hidden behind active behaviors and even more so to systematically measure the process of brand mindshare solidifying into long-term assets. The group standard "Evaluation Index System for Brand Power Improvement Effect Driven by Artificial Intelligence" is precisely based on the deep application of AI technology in brand marketing, closely following the market trend of "the rise of consumer proactivity," and possesses three major innovations: "Full-Domain Data Attribution," "Business Value Enhancement," and "Measurement Paradigm Innovation." Specifically, it can accurately track the proactive behaviors of consumers in various stages such as search, interaction, and conversion, closing the evaluation loop and making every brand touchpoint traceable and attributable. It can also elevate the evaluation perspective from "short-term traffic monetization" to "full-domain business operations" by quantifying the synergistic effects of "short-term ROI" and "long-term brand assets." Most importantly, the new standard abandons the limitations of traditional traffic indicators centered on PV and ROI, as well as subjective qualitative judgments, and upgrades to a new measurement paradigm represented by "Widespread Reach," "Interaction," and "Navigate," achieving a leap from "vague estimation" to "objective insight." • Widespread Reach: Includes the breadth of brand exposure, the accuracy of target audience coverage, and the frequency of brand advertising reach, measuring the brand's precise coverage capability of target audiences across multiple platforms and scenarios with AI assistance, serving as the cornerstone of brand existence. • Interaction: Measures the volume of brand interactions, brand association, and purchase intention, evaluating the depth and breadth of two-way communication between the brand and consumers, and serving as an important link in building connections. • Navigate: Focuses on measuring the brand's mindshare in the consumer's active information acquisition and decision-making stages, including brand search volume, search conversion rate, and search user assets. It directly reflects whether consumers actively search for the brand when they have a need, serving as key proof of the brand moving from "market existence" to "active consumer choice," and signifying the deep solidification of brand mindshare. This standard not only provides an index system but also offers clear definitions and calculation explanations for each indicator, along with corresponding application guidelines. It provides evaluation focus and ideas for different scenarios such as brand health diagnosis, marketing campaign evaluation, industry benchmarking, and long-term asset building, possessing both foresight and practicality. President Zhang Guohua emphasized that Chinese brands must not only create high-quality products but also continuously enhance their brand power in international competition, which is inseparable from more precise consumer reach, higher quality creative expression, and more compelling brand stories. The release of this industry standard is precisely to help brands deepen consumer communication and capture user mindshare, enabling consumers to recognize, choose, repurchase, and like the brand. Alibaba Mama's AI Myriad Forms also provides strong momentum for this, helping brands efficiently reach target audiences and improve communication accuracy and brand influence. The new advertising standards in the AI era jointly promoted by Alibaba Mama and the China Advertising Association, for brands, help build a quantifiable, optimizable, and sustainable brand asset management system, making the long-term value of brand building investments "visible and measurable." For the marketing ecosystem, it guides the industry from short-term traffic competition to deep brand value operation and long-term business management. For industry research, it provides a standardized methodology, making cross-platform and cross-period brand power comparisons possible. The future is here, and only change is constant. With the consolidation of industry consensus and the improvement of evaluation tools, brand building is moving towards an unprecedented new era. The China Advertising Association will work hand in hand with Alibaba Mama to jointly promote the high-quality and sustainable development of the industry.

body_en: [Financial Calendar] Boao Forum for Asia 2026 Annual Conference (3/24-3/27) Earnings Release: Xiaomi Group ►► On March 23rd, at the China Development Forum 2026 Annual Conference, Liu Liehong, Director of the National Data Administration, stated that in the next step, they will work with relevant departments to vigorously promote the "Computing-Electricity Coordination" project, ensuring that new computing power facilities at hub nodes achieve a green electricity application ratio of over 80% and maximize the supporting role of green electricity. Liu Liehong explained that Computing-Electricity Coordination refers to a new infrastructure project that deeply integrates computing power infrastructure with the power system through digital technology, intelligent algorithms, and information networks, promoting dynamic resource matching and optimized allocation, and achieving a virtuous cycle of "strengthening computing with electricity, and promoting electricity with computing." Key aspects include promoting direct supply of green electricity and aggregated green electricity supply to enhance the support capacity of green electricity for computing power, and promoting waste heat recovery and utilization to enhance green and low-carbon circular benefits. In October 2024, the National Data Administration, in conjunction with relevant departments, organized pilot programs in hub nodes such as Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, the Yangtze River Delta, and Inner Mongolia, as well as clean energy-rich regions like Qinghai and Xinjiang, focusing on direct green electricity supply, multi-source complementary energy, and source-load interaction to explore Computing-Electricity Coordination models. ►► The National Development and Reform Commission stated that since the domestic refined oil product price adjustment on March 9th, international crude oil prices have risen sharply due to the escalating US-Iran conflict, with crude oil prices in the Middle East reaching historical highs. To mitigate the impact of abnormal international oil price increases, reduce the burden on downstream users, and ensure stable economic operation and social well-being, temporary control measures have been implemented for domestic refined oil product prices while maintaining the existing price mechanism framework. According to the current price mechanism calculation, domestic retail prices for gasoline and diesel (standard products) should have increased by 2205 yuan and 2120 yuan per ton, respectively, starting from 24:00 on March 23rd. To alleviate the burden on downstream users, the state has implemented temporary control measures, resulting in an actual increase of 1160 yuan and 1115 yuan per ton for domestic gasoline and diesel, respectively, which is 1045 yuan and 1005 yuan less than the calculated increase, equivalent to an average reduction of about 0.85 yuan per liter for gasoline and diesel nationwide. For private car owners, assuming a fuel tank capacity of 50-60 liters, filling up a tank of 92 octane gasoline will cost 40-50 yuan less. For large truck drivers, assuming a fuel tank capacity of 400-600 liters, filling up a tank will cost 300-500 yuan less. ►► According to CCTV News, on March 23rd, the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, in conjunction with the Municipal Commission of Commerce and the Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism, legally summoned and provided administrative guidance to twelve platform companies including Ctrip, Qunar, Gaode, JD.com, Taobao Flash Sale, Meituan, Fliggy, Tongcheng Travel, Tujia, Xiaozhu.com, Douyin, and Kuaishou. The first batch of issues discovered since the comprehensive rectification of platform "involution-style" competition was centrally communicated, and rectification requirements were proposed. The issues communicated this time mainly focused on four aspects: infringement of merchants' independent operating rights; setting unreasonable rules; false advertising; and shortcomings in the compliance management systems of some platforms. During the meeting, market regulation authorities issued an "Administrative Warning Letter" to the relevant platforms, requiring them to strictly implement their principal responsibilities and rectify the relevant issues within a specified period. They were also required to protect the legitimate rights and interests of platform operators and consumers, prohibiting the mandatory or disguised mandatory sale of goods by platform operators at prices below cost according to their pricing rules, which disrupts market competition order. For suspected violations, relevant departments will conduct in-depth investigations and handle them according to law. For platform companies outside Beijing, the cases will be transferred to the market regulation authorities in their respective jurisdictions for investigation. All platforms stated that they attach great importance to the issues pointed out during the meeting, will earnestly reflect, rectify immediately, and draw inferences from one instance to generalize, thoroughly identify and promptly rectify "involution-style" competition risks and hidden dangers, and promote win-win development for platforms and platform operators and laborers. ►► According to Xinhua News Agency, US media reported that US President Trump said on the 23rd that the US had a "strong" dialogue with Iran and had reached an agreement in principle. Trump said that the US had dialogue with the Iranian leadership, but not with the Iranian Supreme Leader. The dialogue was conducted by US Special Envoy Witcoff and his son-in-law Kushner with the Iranian side. Trump said that the US and Iran might have a phone conversation on the 23rd. If an agreement is reached, it would be a "great start" for Iran and the entire region. Regarding Iran's denial of dialogue with the US, Trump said that the US had destroyed a large amount of Iranian infrastructure, and it was difficult to obtain information there. He also said that he had just spoken with the Israeli side, and Israel was very satisfied with the current situation. ►► On Monday, US stocks ended a three-day losing streak, with all three major indices rising by more than 1%. Major technology stocks rose across the board, with Tesla up 3.5%, Amazon up more than 2%, and Meta, Nvidia, and Apple up more than 1%. Boosted by falling oil prices, airline stocks, which are highly sensitive to fuel costs, surged. Cruise line operators' stocks soared, with Norwegian Cruise Line up more than 6%, and Carnival Corporation and Viking Holdings both up more than 5%. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index rose 0.86%. title_en: Token's Chinese name is decided: Ciyuan
body_en: On the 24th, Liu Liehong, Director of the National Data Administration, stated at a press conference held by the State Council Information Office that by March of this year, China's average daily token usage had exceeded 140 trillion, a more than 1,000-fold increase from 100 billion at the beginning of 2024. Compared to the target of 100 trillion by the end of 2025, it has grown by over 40% in just three months. "The substantial increase in average daily token usage fully demonstrates that China's artificial intelligence development has entered a phase of rapid growth," Liu Liehong said. He added that AI application scenarios are continuously deepening, evolving from conversational abilities to intelligent agents capable of decision-making and execution. China's AI industry competitiveness is significantly strengthening, and the currently highly anticipated "Token export" is a symbol of this enhanced industrial competitiveness. According to Liu Liehong, with the joint efforts of all parties, the construction of high-quality datasets in China has achieved phased results. By the end of 2025, over 100,000 high-quality datasets had been built nationwide, with a total volume exceeding 890 PB, which is approximately 310 times the total digital resources of the National Library of China. In the next step, the National Data Administration will continue to promote data empowerment for AI innovation and development, coordinate all parties to deeply implement a new round of action plans for building high-quality datasets, and accelerate pilot initiatives driven by scenario demands. The aim is to create AI-Ready high-quality datasets that are technically feasible, practical, convenient, and quality-assured, thereby achieving both quantitative and qualitative improvements in the supply of high-quality datasets.

title_en: The State Administration for Market Regulation held the 2026 Anti-Monopoly Work Conference.
body_en: Reported by He Ke On March 19, the 2026 Anti-Monopoly Work Conference was held in Xiamen, Fujian. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the conference deeply studied and implemented the spirit of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and its plenary sessions, conscientiously implemented the deployment requirements of the National Market Regulation Work Conference, summarized the anti-monopoly work in 2025, analyzed the current situation, and studied and deployed key tasks for 2026. Wang Tiehan, Director of the Anti-Monopoly Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation, attended the conference and delivered a speech. The conference pointed out that since 2025, market regulation departments at all levels have conscientiously implemented the decisions and deployments of the Party Central Committee and the State Council, strengthened anti-monopoly supervision and law enforcement, handled 22 monopoly cases throughout the year, reviewed 706 cases of operator concentration, promoted the continuous optimization of the market competition environment, and effectively supported the sustained economic recovery and improvement. The fair competition review system has been deeply implemented, and source control has been strengthened; 96 cases of abuse of administrative power to exclude or restrict competition have been filed and investigated, effectively regulating government economic promotion behavior and creating a favorable competition ecosystem. The conference emphasized that 2026 is the first year of the "15th Five-Year Plan." To do a good job in anti-monopoly work, it is necessary to focus on promoting the construction of a unified national market in depth, continuously deepening fair competition governance, intensifying efforts to break down local protectionism and market segmentation, regulate market competition order, thoroughly address "involutionary" competition, deepen international exchanges, improve systems and mechanisms, continuously enhance regulatory effectiveness, demonstrate new responsibilities in serving national strategies, and achieve new accomplishments in seizing the initiative in international competition, making positive contributions to promoting high-quality development and serving a good start to the "15th Five-Year Plan." Comrades in charge of market regulation departments from Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Shandong, Guangdong, and Chongqing made exchange speeches. Comrades in charge of market regulation departments from provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, comrades in charge of relevant divisions and offices, and comrades in charge of relevant bureaus and directly affiliated units of the State Administration for Market Regulation attended the conference.
