title_en: The policy toolbox is gradually becoming more complete, and the market-oriented development of data elements will be intensified.
body_en: The policy toolkit for the market-oriented allocation reform of data elements in China is gradually becoming more complete. Relevant departments will further promote the marketization and valorization of data elements in the next steps, including accelerating the establishment of a unified national data property registration system and promptly issuing policy documents for building a national integrated data market, to further promote the development and utilization of data resources. Since its establishment, the National Data Administration has explored and formed a "5+3+1" working system for the market-oriented allocation reform of data elements. The "5" refers to five aspects: improving fundamental data systems, building and operating data infrastructure, cultivating scenarios and integrating data applications, building a national integrated data market, and strengthening the data industry. The "3" refers to three foundations: solidifying breakthroughs in core technologies in the data field, data standardization, and digital talent cultivation. The "1" refers to one key focus: empowering artificial intelligence innovation and development with data. "Overall, the policy toolkit for the market-oriented allocation reform of data elements is gradually becoming more complete, the work roadmap is becoming clearer, and the value of data elements is being promoted with 'accelerated speed'," said Liu Liehong, Director of the National Data Administration. This year is the year for releasing the value of data elements, and efforts will be intensified to promote the marketization and valorization of data elements, focusing on the implementation of systems, scenario cultivation, and data supply. Specifically, the National Data Administration will accelerate the establishment of a unified national data property registration system, promptly issue policy documents for building a national integrated data market, and promote the construction of fundamental data systems and data infrastructure in an integrated manner, to solve the "impossible triangle" problem of secure, compliant, and efficient data circulation, providing strong guarantees for the release of data element value. In conjunction with relevant departments, efforts will be intensified to cultivate high-value scenarios and better leverage the multiplier effect of data elements. In addition, this year, in collaboration with more than 10 departments rich in public data resources, more public data will be made available, with public data leading the way to better empower the high-quality development of the economy and society with data elements. Zhao Gang, President of SaiZhi Industry Research Institute, told the Economic Information Daily that the relevant deployment measures will further address the problem of "difficulty in rights confirmation" in data circulation and utilization, helping all parties clarify specific allocation plans for data "ownership, usage rights, and operating rights," encouraging all types of entities to supply data and use it with confidence, and promoting the circulation, utilization, value release, and income distribution of data resources. In addition, it will promote the construction of an open, shared, and secure national integrated data market, breaking down data barriers between regions, industries, and departments, realizing the free circulation and efficient allocation of data elements nationwide, and promoting the deep empowerment of data resources across all industries. It is worth noting that data is also a key factor of production in the intelligent economy. This year's government work report proposed to "create a new form of intelligent economy" and clearly stated to "deepen the development and utilization of data resources, improve the fundamental systems of data elements, and build high-quality datasets." It is learned that by the end of 2025, China will have built over 100,000 high-quality datasets, with a total volume exceeding 890 PB. By March of this year, China's average daily token (word element) call volume has exceeded 140 trillion, an increase of more than 1,000 times compared to 100 billion at the beginning of 2024, and an increase of more than 40% in three months compared to 100 trillion at the end of 2025. "The substantial increase in average daily token call volume fully demonstrates that China's artificial intelligence development has entered a stage of rapid growth, and application scenarios are continuously deepening. From the perspective of data, this signifies a large increase in the supply of datasets, the continuous release of the value of data elements, and the entry of data elements empowering artificial intelligence innovation and development into a stage of virtuous interaction," said Liu Liehong. In the next step, the National Data Administration will continue to promote data empowerment for artificial intelligence innovation and development, coordinate with all parties to deeply implement the new round of high-quality dataset construction action plan, including six special actions: strengthening the foundation and expanding capacity, tackling annotation challenges, improving quality and efficiency, empowering applications, managing services, and releasing value. Guided by scenario needs, efforts will be made to accelerate pilot initiatives, creating AI-Ready high-quality datasets that are technically feasible, practical, convenient, and quality-assured, achieving quantitative and qualitative improvements in the supply of high-quality datasets. In the manufacturing sector, as new-generation information technologies represented by artificial intelligence are deeply integrated into all processes and links of manufacturing, data is increasingly becoming an important factor of production and a valuable strategic resource for industry. By the end of 2025, the numerical control rate of key processes in key industry enterprises in China will reach 68.6%. Recently, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology launched the Industrial Data Foundation Building Action, carrying out pilot initiatives for the construction of high-quality industry datasets for AI empowerment. "Through pilot initiatives, we will focus on breaking through the bottlenecks in industrial data collection, acquisition, and utilization," said Wang Yanqing, Director of the Information Technology Development Department of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. In the next step, support and guarantees will be strengthened, policy guidance will be reinforced, and a favorable ecosystem will be cultivated. This will include promoting the issuance of policy documents on data elements empowering new industrialization, releasing reference guidelines for the application of data elements in industrial scenarios, and strengthening development guidance and model promotion. Efforts will be made to accelerate the research and development of industrial data standards, develop and strengthen data service enterprises such as data consulting, data governance, and data annotation, and strengthen and optimize artificial intelligence open-source communities, creating a highland for the aggregation of high-quality open-source data resources. "In the future, we will continue to promote the application and empowerment of high-quality datasets in industry large models and intelligent agent application scenarios," said Zhao Gang, emphasizing the need to promote the creation of "data-model-application" or "token-intelligent agent-skills" closed loops, especially in key areas such as industrial manufacturing, autonomous driving, low-altitude economy, healthcare, and scientific research, to accelerate the release of data value in AI applications. (Reporter Guo Qian)

title_en: The food delivery war should end.
body_en: The food delivery war affects not only the ledgers of restaurant owners but also the livelihoods of ordinary people. When catering consumption, the "ballast stone" of the economy, falters due to price wars, the chill felt by the overall economy will eventually be transmitted to every micro-individual. Healthy competition should be a virtuous contest of technological innovation, efficiency improvement, and service optimization. In the past few days, have you received any free order coupons from food delivery platforms? At a recent press conference, the State Administration for Market Regulation disclosed the latest progress in its anti-monopoly investigation into food delivery platforms, stating that regulatory authorities have entered relevant platforms to conduct on-site investigations. In the next step, they will further exert regulatory pressure through questionnaires and audits, and study disposal measures. This sends a clear message to the market about the regulatory stance: the frenzied food delivery war must be extinguished! The food delivery war, while seemingly beneficial to the public, is actually a form of involution. For consumers, the food delivery war is indeed "appealing." Who doesn't like a 1-yuan milk tea or a 3-yuan coffee? However, what is free is often the most expensive. When we shift our focus from the free order coupons on our phones to the overall economy, we will find that the cost of this war is ultimately borne by us ordinary people, and far exceeds expectations. The most direct impact is reflected in macroeconomic data. From the end of the second quarter to the third quarter of 2025, the CPI, which reflects China's resident consumption price, continued to fall, and the consumer market felt a chill. Strangely, if food and energy are excluded, the core CPI has actually been rising. This indicates that consumption should have been recovering but was somehow "pulled down." What "pulled" it down was catering. In China's CPI basket, food, tobacco, alcohol, and dining out account for nearly 30%, the highest among all categories. This means that when catering prices rise, CPI may follow suit; when catering prices fall, CPI may also dip. With this background, looking at the data reveals that from the end of the second quarter to the third quarter of 2025, the growth rate of China's catering revenue slowed down. The timing and trend of its decline highly overlap with the overall CPI's downward curve. During the same period, housing and transportation and communication, which also have high weights, did not experience similar declines. This period precisely coincided with the white-hot food delivery war and the most aggressive platform subsidies. Financial reports show that during the food delivery war, Alibaba, JD.com, and Meituan collectively subsidized between 80 billion and 100 billion yuan. The China Hotel Association pointed out that the price decline caused by large subsidies between platforms has become a significant factor constraining the growth of the catering industry since June 2025. According to Meituan's observations, this war has directly pushed the average price of dine-in catering back to 10 years ago. On the surface, the food delivery war appears to be platforms making concessions, but from a macroeconomic perspective, it is a fierce blow to the pricing system of the catering industry. To survive the subsidy war, catering enterprises have had to sacrifice quality and compress profits, leading the entire industry into a vicious cycle of losing money to gain attention. This ultimately drags down the overall trend of consumption recovery, which is precisely contrary to the central government's deployment to boost consumption and adds unnecessary resistance to macroeconomic regulation. The food delivery war affects not only the ledgers of restaurant owners but also the livelihoods of ordinary people. Consumption is the main engine driving economic growth. When catering consumption, the "ballast stone" of the economy, falters due to vicious price wars, the chill felt by the overall economy will eventually be transmitted to every micro-individual. When corporate profits are paper-thin or even result in losses from the outset, where will employment opportunities come from? And how can salary growth be discussed? Precisely because of this, the timely intervention by regulators to halt the food delivery war is actually an act of maintaining normal economic operations, preventing vicious competition from disrupting the rhythm of economic recovery, and allowing businesses and workers to have normal lives and incomes. Healthy competition should be a virtuous contest of technological innovation, efficiency improvement, and service optimization, not a money-burning game built on capital, nor a zero-sum game that exploits monopolistic positions to control traffic and force allegiances. Allowing food delivery prices to return to a reasonable range, freeing the catering industry from the dilemma of "die without subsidies, chaos with subsidies," and shifting market competition from price wars to service competition is the true way to benefit businesses and the public. Price wars cannot go far; involutionary competition has no winners. The food delivery war must end. (She Ying)

title_en: Beijing summons 12 platform companies to address "involutionary" competition.
body_en: On March 23rd, the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, in conjunction with the Municipal Commerce Bureau and the Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism, jointly summoned and provided administrative guidance to 12 platform enterprises including Ctrip, Qunar, Gaode, JD.com, Taobao Flash Sale, Meituan, Fliggy Travel, Tujia Homestay, and Douyin. The meeting centrally communicated the first batch of issues discovered since the comprehensive rectification of platform "involutionary" competition and put forward rectification requirements. Starting from October 2025, Beijing has been carrying out comprehensive rectification of platform "involutionary" competition, using the accommodation and catering industries as a starting point. Documents such as the "Negative List of Platform 'Involutionary' Competitive Behaviors" have been successively issued. Through a "four-pronged" approach of platform self-inspection, undercover investigations, surprise inspections, and experience surveys, risks of "involutionary" competition are systematically identified and addressed. It is understood that the first batch of issues mainly manifest in four aspects: infringement of merchants' independent operating rights, setting unreasonable rules, false advertising, and shortcomings in the compliance management systems of some platforms. Regarding infringement of merchants' independent operating rights, some platforms, without merchants' consent, have modified backend settings to unilaterally register merchants for promotional activities. They also monitor prices through technical means and require merchants to sell at the lowest prices across the entire network, stripping merchants of their pricing autonomy. These actions not only cause operational losses for merchants but also lead to risks in product and service quality. In terms of setting unreasonable rules, some platforms exploit their dominant position to establish unfair rules, increasing the operational burden on merchants through penalties such as fines and traffic restrictions. In terms of false advertising, some platforms use deceptive advertising to induce consumers to purchase goods, infringing upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests. Regarding compliance management systems, some platforms have nominal compliance management organizations, unclear responsibilities, and compliance mechanisms that fail to function effectively. During the meeting, market regulation departments issued administrative admonitions to the relevant platforms, requiring them to strictly fulfill their primary responsibilities, rectify the identified issues within a specified period, protect the legitimate rights and interests of platform operators and consumers, and prohibit the mandatory or disguised mandatory sale of goods by platform operators at prices below cost according to their pricing rules. For suspected violations, relevant departments will conduct in-depth investigations and deal with them according to law. For platform enterprises outside Beijing, the cases will be transferred to the market regulation departments in their respective jurisdictions for investigation according to law. Responsible persons from each platform stated that they will seriously reflect on the issues raised during the meeting, make immediate corrections, thoroughly identify and promptly rectify hidden risks of "involutionary" competition, and promote the win-win development of platforms, platform operators, and workers.

title_en: The food delivery war should end.
body_en: The food delivery war affects not only the ledgers of restaurant owners but also the livelihoods of ordinary people. When catering consumption, the "ballast stone" of the economy, falters due to price wars, the chill felt by the overall economy will eventually be transmitted to every micro-individual. Healthy competition should be a virtuous contest of technological innovation, efficiency improvement, and service optimization. In the past few days, have you received any free order coupons from food delivery platforms? At a recent press conference, the State Administration for Market Regulation disclosed the latest progress of its anti-monopoly investigation into food delivery platforms, stating that regulatory authorities have entered relevant platforms to conduct on-site investigations. In the next step, they will further transmit regulatory pressure through questionnaires and verifications, and study disposal measures. This sends a clear message to the market about the regulatory stance: the frenzied food delivery war must be extinguished! The food delivery war, while seemingly beneficial to the public, is actually a form of involution. For consumers, the food delivery war is indeed "appealing." Who doesn't like a 1-yuan milk tea or a 3-yuan coffee? However, what is free is often the most expensive. When we shift our focus from the free order coupons on our phones to the overall economic landscape, we realize that the cost of this war is ultimately borne by us ordinary people, and far exceeds expectations. The most direct impact is reflected in macroeconomic data. From the end of the second quarter to the third quarter of 2025, the CPI, which reflects China's consumer price index, continued to fall, and the consumer market felt a chill. Strangely, if food and energy are excluded, the core CPI has actually been rising. This indicates that consumption should have been recovering but was somehow "pulled down." What "pulled" it down was catering. In China's CPI basket, food, tobacco, and alcohol, along with dining out, account for nearly 30%, the highest proportion among all categories. This means that when catering prices rise, the CPI is likely to follow suit; when catering prices fall, the CPI is likely to dip. With this background, looking at the data reveals that from the end of the second quarter to the third quarter of 2025, the growth rate of China's catering revenue slowed down. The timing and trend of this decline highly overlap with the overall CPI downward curve; during the same period, housing and transportation and communication, which also have high weights, did not experience similar declines. And this period precisely coincided with the white-hot food delivery war and the most frenzied platform subsidies. Financial reports show that during the food delivery war, Alibaba, JD.com, and Meituan collectively subsidized between 80 billion and 100 billion yuan. The China Hotel Association pointed out that the price decline caused by large subsidies between platforms has become a significant factor constraining the growth of the catering industry since June 2025. According to Meituan's observations, this war has directly pushed the average price of dine-in catering back to 10 years ago. On the surface, the food delivery war appears to be platforms making concessions, but from a macroeconomic perspective, it is a fierce blow to the pricing system of the catering industry. To survive the subsidy war, catering enterprises have had to sacrifice quality and compress profits, leading the entire industry into a vicious cycle of losing money to gain attention. This ultimately drags down the overall trend of consumption recovery, which runs counter to the central government's deployment to boost consumption and adds unnecessary resistance to macroeconomic regulation. The food delivery war affects not only the ledgers of restaurant owners but also the livelihoods of ordinary people. Consumption is the main engine driving economic growth. When catering consumption, the "ballast stone" of the economy, falters due to vicious price wars, the chill felt by the overall economy will eventually be transmitted to every micro-individual. When corporate profits are paper-thin or even result in losses from the outset, where will employment opportunities come from? And how can salary growth be discussed? Precisely because of this, the timely halt of the food delivery war by regulators is actually an act of maintaining normal economic operations, preventing vicious competition from disrupting the rhythm of economic recovery, and allowing businesses and workers to have normal lives and incomes. Healthy competition should be a virtuous contest of technological innovation, efficiency improvement, and service optimization, not a money-burning game built on capital, nor a zero-sum game that exploits monopolistic positions to control traffic and force allegiances. Allowing food delivery prices to return to a reasonable range, freeing the catering industry from the dilemma of "dying without subsidies and chaos with subsidies," and shifting market competition from price wars to service competition is the true way to benefit businesses and the public. Price wars cannot go far; involutionary competition has no winners. The food delivery war must end.

title_en: No one wins in involution; improving quality leads to long-term success.
body_en: Huang Weixin Recently, the State Administration for Market Regulation disclosed the latest progress of its anti-monopoly investigation into food delivery platforms and forwarded an article from the Economic Daily titled "The Food Delivery War Should End." This move sends a clear signal: the overheated price war in food delivery must be extinguished. While the food delivery war appears to benefit consumers through subsidies, it distorts the valuation logic of the capital market and severely drags down consumption recovery, running counter to the directive of boosting domestic demand and stabilizing the overall economy. The food delivery war is essentially a zero-sum game driven by capital. The three major platforms have cumulatively invested hundreds of billions in subsidies to burn cash and grab market share. While orders have surged, restaurants are "making a profit by losing money," and corporate profits have been significantly depleted. The capital market has voted with its feet, with the market value of related platforms shrinking considerably, dragging down the Hang Seng Tech Index. Funds that should have been invested in technological innovation and industrial upgrading have been reduced to subsidies for milk tea and coffee, worth mere cents or dollars. This not only damages long-term investment value but also leads to the misallocation of social resources. Following the strong statement from regulators, technology and internet stocks in the Hong Kong stock market immediately saw a turnaround. On March 25, Meituan's stock price surged intraday, at one point rising by over 14%, Alibaba rose by over 5%, and JD.com rose by over 4%. The market's reaction reflects a strong desire for healthy competition. This indicates that the capital market is optimistic about the positive impact of regulators halting the food delivery war on the real economy. Catering is the cornerstone of consumption recovery. While short-term low prices may appear to benefit consumers, they distort normal consumption expectations and create obstacles for macroeconomic regulation. There are no winners in involution; quality improvement is the long-term strategy. Healthy market competition should focus on technological innovation, efficiency improvement, and service optimization, rather than capital burning and traffic monopolies. Timely cessation of the vicious price war is not only about repairing the catering ecosystem, stabilizing merchant operations, and the income of practitioners, but also about guiding platforms to return to value creation. Allowing the consumer market to escape the low-price trap and return to a sustainable recovery track is of great significance for promoting economic growth and stimulating domestic demand.

title_en: OpenAI's Strategic Retreat: Sora Exits, AI Enters the "Value War" Era
body_en: OpenAI is starting to simplify. On March 24th local time, two years after the release of the "world simulator" that shocked the tech industry, OpenAI suddenly put an end to its AI video generation application, Sora. This also means the termination of Disney's strategic investment of up to $1 billion in OpenAI and its IP licensing agreement. Previously, the two parties had planned to feature Mickey Mouse, Marvel heroes, and Star Wars characters in Sora. The "cause of death" for Sora is not complicated: too high costs, too much controversy, and too much internal friction. As the IPO window approaches, a video experimental product with high investment and low returns appears out of place. After two years of multi-pronged attacks and widespread blooming, OpenAI has finally admitted that it can no longer "have it all." Beyond Sora, OpenAI is successively shrinking its computing power collaborations, adjusting non-core businesses, and consolidating resources into enterprise services with greater commercial prospects. However, the path to commercialization ahead of it is not easy. Image source: Photographed by our reporter Liang Yuanhao OpenAI announced that it will gradually shut down its AI video generation application, Sora. This decision means that Sora and related API services for consumers and developers will be terminated, and OpenAI will also stop its plan to integrate video functions into ChatGPT. The Sora team officially released a farewell message on social media: "We are saying goodbye to the Sora application. Thank you to everyone who has created, shared, and built communities around Sora... We know this news is disappointing. We will share more soon, including timelines for the application and API, and details on how to save your work." An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed that the iOS app, API interface, and Sora website services will be shut down, but a specific timeline for the shutdown has not yet been announced. However, the company clearly stated that ChatGPT's AI image generation function will continue to be retained. This decision appears quite sudden. According to reports, just the night before the shutdown was announced, OpenAI's team was still in a collaboration meeting with Disney regarding Sora-related projects. Only 30 minutes after the meeting ended, the Disney team learned of Sora's discontinuation, with one insider describing the move as a "rug-pull." In early 2024, when OpenAI first showcased Sora's realistic video generation capabilities, the industry widely believed it would be the beginning of another content creation revolution after ChatGPT. In September 2025, Sora 2 was launched as a standalone application and quickly topped the Apple App Store charts, reaching over a million downloads even faster than ChatGPT. At the time, OpenAI stated that Sora 2 might represent the "GPT-3.5 moment" in the video domain. However, the application's moment of glory did not last long. Data from third-party data platform Appfigures shows that in December 2025, its downloads decreased by 32% month-on-month; by January 2026, downloads plummeted by another 45%, and the app's ranking fell out of the top 100. At the same time, Sora has been accompanied by significant controversy. While AI video applications showcase their video generation capabilities, they have also been criticized for making it harder to distinguish between real and fake images. The large volume of videos generated by Sora and other AI software has exacerbated concerns about intentional AI-generated fake videos on the internet. Although OpenAI announced a licensing agreement with Disney in December 2025, allowing users to create videos using hundreds of characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar, and Star Wars, this collaboration has also fallen through with Sora's shutdown. Insiders revealed that the $1 billion deal never involved any fund transfer. Internal friction is more severe than external pressure. According to multiple sources, Sora has been controversial since its inception, with many employees questioning why "expensive and scarce massive computing resources were invested in this business," which directly squeezed the computing power allocation for ChatGPT and other core products. The computational intensity required to generate high-quality video is on a completely different scale compared to traditional text generation, and Sora's operation has placed continuous pressure on OpenAI's cost structure. Goldman Sachs estimates that for every $1 of revenue OpenAI earns, it loses $0.69. In 2025, its annual revenue exceeded $20 billion, but losses are expected to be between $14 billion and $17 billion. Computing power costs account for over 60% of total expenses, and positive cash flow is not expected until 2030. For OpenAI, Sora was more of a technological exploration. As the IPO window approaches, the capital market's demand for revenue realization capabilities has become urgent. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar admitted, "We must build a company that is ready to go public." Faced with profitability pressure, Sora, a video experiment with high investment and low returns, appears out of place. Sora's shutdown is not an isolated incident. In the past month, OpenAI has also scaled back some of its computing power collaborations with Nvidia and re-evaluated its data center expansion plans. The in-app shopping feature for ChatGPT, promoted last year, has been adjusted to a lighter "shopping assistant" role due to a user conversion rate of less than 1%. The underlying logic of these adjustments is consistent: the company is withdrawing dispersed resources and concentrating them on a few core products with proven market demand. Fidji Simo, CEO of OpenAI's Applications business, previously mentioned that the company's past simultaneous investments in multiple applications and technology stacks have slowed down development speed, and the quality standards of some products have not met expectations. She emphasized that when certain business directions begin to show results, concentrating resources and avoiding dispersion is a necessary choice. This direction of "showing results" refers to OpenAI's upcoming integrated desktop "super application." According to the plan, ChatGPT, the AI programming tool Codex, and the self-developed browser Atlas will be integrated into a unified agent scheduling framework. The goal of this product is to build an Agentic AI platform capable of autonomously completing tasks such as programming, price comparison, and local operations. The direct driver of this strategic shift comes from competitor Anthropic. With its products Claude Code and Claude Cowork, Anthropic has rapidly expanded its user base among developers and enterprise clients. According to reports, Claude Code is used by 500,000 developers worldwide, with an annualized revenue of $2.5 billion, while OpenAI's Codex generates about $1 billion. This gap has even triggered a "Code Red" status within OpenAI. While shrinking its product line, OpenAI is still expanding its workforce, with a more pronounced focus on the B-end. According to reports, OpenAI plans to increase its total employee count from 4,500 to 8,000 by the end of 2026, adding approximately 3,500 positions, with a focus on recruiting engineering, product development, and sales talent, and even creating "technical ambassador" roles to help enterprise clients deploy AI tools. OpenAI seems to have realized that there is more than one path to AGI, but the path to commercialization must become narrower. In this blueprint, the C-end video entertainment attribute represented by Sora is significantly diluted. In its response to the closure of Sora, an OpenAI spokesperson explicitly stated: "The Sora research team will transition to world simulator research to support robotics in handling real-world physical tasks." This means that Sora's underlying technology has not disappeared but has been "downgraded" or "restructured" into the more strategically significant field of embodied intelligence, serving hardware devices that can directly generate industrial value. Looking back at Sora's rise and fall over the past year, it reflects a certain illusion of the AI frenzy period, which is that as long as there is enough computing power, all industries can be reshaped. However, in the face of the triple ceilings of business logic, legal ethics, and physical computing power, even the top technology companies must learn to make trade-offs between ideals and reality. From an industry perspective, Sora's exit also signifies that the AI industry is bidding farewell to unconstrained expansion and entering a period of meticulous commercialization. At the GTC conference, Nvidia elevated Tokens to the fundamental unit of the AI era, shifting the industry's focus from training to inference and emphasizing the continuous invocation of models in real business scenarios. Within this framework, Agent systems are seen by the market as the next-generation computing entry point, where model usage shifts from one-off question-and-answer to continuous task execution, significantly increasing Token consumption and transforming Tokens from a technical indicator into a measurable and priceable commercial unit. Chinese technology companies are also accelerating their deployment along this logic. Alibaba Cloud's latest financial report shows that its AI-related product revenue has achieved triple-digit growth for 10 consecutive quarters, with external commercialization revenue increasing by 35% year-on-year. Alibaba has established Alibaba Token Hub internally to integrate related businesses, launched the enterprise-level Agent platform Wukong, and integrated Qwen into core scenarios such as Taobao and Alipay. Tencent has launched Agent products such as QClaw and WorkBuddy and is promoting the implementation of AI in WeChat, QQ, and enterprise tools. Meanwhile, leading manufacturers such as Alibaba Cloud and Baidu announced price increases for AI computing power and storage in March, with high-performance computing card prices rising by 5% to 34%. Users are willing to pay a premium for stable and reliable performance. The price war is receding, and the value war is quietly emerging. In the capital markets, investor tolerance for tech stocks has significantly decreased. In an environment of low risk appetite, investors are paying more attention to profit and cash flow performance, putting continuous selling pressure on tech heavyweights that are increasing AI capital expenditures. Both Tencent and Alibaba have seen their stock prices pressured after disclosing earnings due to the squeeze on short-term profits from AI investments. Returning to OpenAI, the company still possesses significant structural advantages: over 800 million weekly active users, the highest global consumer AI brand recognition, and a newly acquired $110 billion in ammunition. The new model Spud is about to be released, and Codex already has over 2 million weekly active users. Daniel Newman, CEO of Futurum Group, previously stated, "The market wants to see OpenAI's revenue growth match its expenditure scale." Sora's shutdown indicates that OpenAI's management has recognized the problem. However, the competition in the AI industry is far from over. With its founding team almost entirely dispersed, unprecedented capital obligations, and competitors already gaining ground, OpenAI faces greater challenges. In the era of "value war," it is no longer the definer but a participant being defined. As the control over technological direction shifts from model vendors to downstream infrastructure and upper-layer applications, OpenAI's moat needs to be re-examined. Thank you to everyone who has created, shared, and built communities around Sora... We know this news is disappointing. We will share more soon, including timelines for the application and API, and details on how to save your work." An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed that the iOS app, API interface, and Sora website services will be shut down, but a specific timeline for the shutdown has not yet been announced. However, the company clearly stated that ChatGPT's AI image generation function will continue to be retained. This decision appears quite sudden. According to reports, just the night before the shutdown was announced, OpenAI's team was still in a collaboration meeting with Disney regarding Sora-related projects. Only 30 minutes after the meeting ended, the Disney team learned of Sora's discontinuation, with one insider describing the move as a "rug-pull." In early 2024, when OpenAI first showcased Sora's realistic video generation capabilities, the industry widely believed it would be the beginning of another content creation revolution after ChatGPT. In September 2025, Sora 2 was launched as a standalone application and quickly topped the Apple App Store charts, reaching over a million downloads even faster than ChatGPT. At the time, OpenAI stated that Sora 2 might represent the "GPT-3.5 moment" in the video domain. However, the application's moment of glory did not last long. Data from third-party data platform Appfigures shows that in December 2025, its downloads decreased by 32% month-on-month; by January 2026, downloads plummeted by another 45%, and the app's ranking fell out of the top 100. At the same time, Sora has been accompanied by significant controversy. While AI video applications showcase their video generation capabilities, they have also been criticized for making it harder to distinguish between real and fake images. The large volume of videos generated by Sora and other AI software has exacerbated concerns about intentional AI-generated fake videos on the internet. Although OpenAI announced a licensing agreement with Disney in December 2025, allowing users to create videos using hundreds of characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar, and Star Wars, this collaboration has also fallen through with Sora's shutdown. Insiders revealed that the $1 billion deal never involved any fund transfer. Internal friction is more severe than external pressure. According to multiple sources, Sora has been controversial since its inception, with many employees questioning why "expensive and scarce massive computing resources were invested in this business," which directly squeezed the computing power allocation for ChatGPT and other core products. The computational intensity required to generate high-quality video is on a completely different scale compared to traditional text generation, and Sora's operation has placed continuous pressure on OpenAI's cost structure. Goldman Sachs estimates that for every $1 of revenue OpenAI earns, it loses $0.69. In 2025, its annual revenue exceeded $20 billion, but losses are expected to be between $14 billion and $17 billion. Computing power costs account for over 60% of total expenses, and positive cash flow is not expected until 2030. For OpenAI, Sora was more of a technological exploration. As the IPO window approaches, the capital market's demand for revenue realization capabilities has become urgent. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar admitted, "We must build a company that is ready to go public." Faced with profitability pressure, Sora, a video experiment with high investment and low returns, appears out of place. Sora's shutdown is not an isolated incident. In the past month, OpenAI has also scaled back some of its computing power collaborations with Nvidia and re-evaluated its data center expansion plans. The in-app shopping feature for ChatGPT, promoted last year, has been adjusted to a lighter "shopping assistant" role due to a user conversion rate of less than 1%. The underlying logic of these adjustments is consistent: the company is withdrawing dispersed resources and concentrating them on a few core products with proven market demand. Fidji Simo, CEO of OpenAI's Applications business, previously mentioned that the company's past simultaneous investments in multiple applications and technology stacks have slowed down development speed, and the quality standards of some products have not met expectations. She emphasized that when certain business directions begin to show results, concentrating resources and avoiding dispersion is a necessary choice. This direction of "showing results" refers to OpenAI's upcoming integrated desktop "super application." According to the plan, ChatGPT, the AI programming tool Codex, and the self-developed browser Atlas will be integrated into a unified agent scheduling framework. The goal of this product is to build an Agentic AI platform capable of autonomously completing tasks such as programming, price comparison, and local operations. The direct driver of this strategic shift comes from competitor Anthropic. With its products Claude Code and Claude Cowork, Anthropic has rapidly expanded its user base among developers and enterprise clients. According to reports, Claude Code is used by 500,000 developers worldwide, with an annualized revenue of $2.5 billion, while OpenAI's Codex generates about $1 billion. This gap has even triggered a "Code Red" status within OpenAI. While shrinking its product line, OpenAI is still expanding its workforce, with a more pronounced focus on the B-end. According to reports, OpenAI plans to increase its total employee count from 4,500 to 8,000 by the end of 2026, adding approximately 3,500 positions, with a focus on recruiting engineering, product development, and sales talent, and even creating "technical ambassador" roles to help enterprise clients deploy AI tools. OpenAI seems to have realized that there is more than one path to AGI, but the path to commercialization must become narrower. In this blueprint, the C-end video entertainment attribute represented by Sora is significantly diluted. In its response to the closure of Sora, an OpenAI spokesperson explicitly stated: "The Sora research team will transition to world simulator research to support robotics in handling real-world physical tasks." This means that Sora's underlying technology has not disappeared but has been "downgraded" or "restructured" into the more strategically significant field of embodied intelligence, serving hardware devices that can directly generate industrial value. Looking back at Sora's rise and fall over the past year, it reflects a certain illusion of the AI frenzy period, which is that as long as there is enough computing power, all industries can be reshaped. However, in the face of the triple ceilings of business logic, legal ethics, and physical computing power, even the top technology companies must learn to make trade-offs between ideals and reality. From an industry perspective, Sora's exit also signifies that the AI industry is bidding farewell to unconstrained expansion and entering a period of meticulous commercialization. At the GTC conference, Nvidia elevated Tokens to the fundamental unit of the AI era, shifting the industry's focus from training to inference and emphasizing the continuous invocation of models in real business scenarios. Within this framework, Agent systems are seen by the market as the next-generation computing entry point, where model usage shifts from one-off question-and-answer to continuous task execution, significantly increasing Token consumption and transforming Tokens from a technical indicator into a measurable and priceable commercial unit. Chinese technology companies are also accelerating their deployment along this logic. Alibaba Cloud's latest financial report shows that its AI-related product revenue has achieved triple-digit growth for 10 consecutive quarters, with external commercialization revenue increasing by 35% year-on-year. Alibaba has established Alibaba Token Hub internally to integrate related businesses, launched the enterprise-level Agent platform Wukong, and integrated Qwen into core scenarios such as Taobao and Alipay. Tencent has launched Agent products such as QClaw and WorkBuddy and is promoting the implementation of AI in WeChat, QQ, and enterprise tools. Meanwhile, leading manufacturers such as Alibaba Cloud and Baidu announced price increases for AI computing power and storage in March, with high-performance computing card prices rising by 5% to 34%. Users are willing to pay a premium for stable and reliable performance. The price war is receding, and the value war is quietly emerging. In the capital markets, investor tolerance for tech stocks has significantly decreased. In an environment of low risk appetite, investors are paying more attention to profit and cash flow performance, putting continuous selling pressure on tech heavyweights that are increasing AI capital expenditures. Both Tencent and Alibaba have seen their stock prices pressured after disclosing earnings due to the squeeze on short-term profits from AI investments. Returning to OpenAI, the company still possesses significant structural advantages: over 800 million weekly active users, the highest global consumer AI brand recognition, and a newly acquired $110 billion in ammunition. The new model Spud is about to be released, and Codex already has over 2 million weekly active users. Daniel Newman, CEO of Futurum Group, previously stated, "The market wants to see OpenAI's revenue growth match its expenditure scale." Sora's shutdown indicates that OpenAI's management has recognized the problem. However, the competition in the AI industry is far from over. With its founding team almost entirely dispersed, unprecedented capital obligations, and competitors already gaining ground, OpenAI faces greater challenges. In the era of "value war," it is no longer the definer but a participant being defined. As the control over technological direction shifts from model vendors to downstream infrastructure and upper-layer applications, OpenAI's moat needs to be re-examined. title_en: Daily average token calls reach 140 trillion
body_en: Recently, a set of data on token call volume has been continuously circulating in the tech community, attracting widespread attention and heated discussion from all sectors. At the China Development Forum 2026 Annual Meeting held on March 23rd, it was revealed that in March of this year, China's average daily token call volume exceeded 140 trillion, a more than thousandfold increase compared to 100 billion at the beginning of 2024, over two years. In the same month, China's weekly token call volume for AI large models surpassed that of the United States for three consecutive weeks, making it one of the countries with the highest AI application activity globally. The latest data from OpenRouter, the world's largest AI model API aggregation platform, shows that from March 16th to 22nd, the global total token call volume for AI large models was 20.4 trillion, with China alone accounting for 7.359 trillion, or 36% of the global total. Tokens, as the smallest unit of measurement for information processed by AI models, are a key indicator of AI model activity and industrial value. The explosive growth in China's token call volume directly reflects the development speed of China's AI industry and also mirrors profound changes in the global AI application landscape. China's leading achievement is by no means accidental but the result of the synergistic effect of multiple factors. Policy guidance continues to intensify. In August 2025, the State Council issued the "Opinions on Deepening the Implementation of the 'Artificial Intelligence+' Action," clearly outlining phased goals for 2027, 2030, and 2035. In January 2026, eight departments, including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, jointly issued the "Implementation Opinions on the Special Action of 'Artificial Intelligence+ Manufacturing'," clearly proposing the core goal of launching 1,000 high-level industrial intelligent agents by 2027. Immediately following, at the Two Sessions in March, the Government Work Report for the first time proposed "creating a new form of intelligent economy," clearly stating the need to "accelerate the promotion of new-generation intelligent terminals and intelligent agents." A series of policies are closely linked and progressively advancing, providing clear and continuous institutional guarantees for technological innovation, computing power construction, and scenario implementation. Technological innovation continues to break through. Domestic large models are gradually narrowing the gap with global leading technologies through optimization of underlying architectures, and are continuously improving in inference costs and response speeds, capable of completing the same complex tasks with fewer tokens. A series of domestic models, represented by DeepSeek and MiniMax M2.5, have not only reduced API usage costs to low levels but have also continuously approached or even surpassed overseas closed-source models in some niche scenarios. This dual advantage of "high performance and low cost" directly lowers the entry barrier for developers and enterprises, providing the core driving force for the exponential growth of token call volume. Computing power infrastructure is continuously improving. Computing power is the fundamental resource supporting the training and inference of large models. With the large-scale application of domestic chips in some scenarios and the continuous increase in the proportion of intelligent computing power, the CCID Consulting predicts that China's intelligent computing power will exceed 35% by 2026, and China's AI industry is moving away from its reliance on a single computing power path. A more autonomous, diversified, and cost-controllable computing power supply system enables large-scale, high-frequency token calls, providing a stable underlying support for the daily average call volume exceeding 140 trillion tokens. Application scenarios are accelerating their outbreak. The leap in token call volume is essentially a reflection of AI applications deeply integrating into social and economic activities. On one hand, tools like the open-source AI agent OpenClaw consume 10 to 100 times more tokens per interaction than traditional AI. Liu Xingliang, president of DCCI Internet Research Institute, stated that the core value of such tools is to push AI from "being able to chat" to "being able to execute," truly making AI a "digital employee." The enthusiasm of Chinese users for these "capable" AI tools is essentially a pressing demand for personal productivity upgrades. On the other hand, emerging scenarios like video generation have become an important growth driver for token consumption. Pan Helin, a member of the Expert Committee of the Information and Communication Economic Commission of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, pointed out that after the launch of models like Ji Meng AI's Seedance 2.0, a creative wave has quickly emerged on short video platforms, with social dissemination and content production mutually reinforcing each other, continuously driving up the scale of calls. From intelligent assistants to multimodal generation, the large-scale implementation of diverse scenarios constitutes a strong engine for token consumption. The industrial ecosystem is diversified and collaborative. Unlike the US AI industry's reliance on breakthroughs from a few leading companies, China has built a multi-level, broadly participatory ecosystem structure of "open-source communities + technology enterprises + massive creators." Open-source projects like OpenHarmony and OpenEuler continue to make breakthroughs in fundamental software, demonstrating vibrant community vitality. Technology enterprises such as ByteDance, Baidu, Alibaba, and Tencent continue to increase R&D investment, promoting the iteration and upgrading of domestic large models and their overseas expansion. Massive individual creators and small and medium-sized enterprises leverage foundational models to quickly transform AI into actual productivity. A closed-loop system of "R&D - Application - Feedback - Iteration" is formed among these three, and through platforms reaching billions of users such as WeChat, DingTalk, and Feishu, AI capabilities are democratized and implemented, ultimately achieving a virtuous cycle of "technological iteration - cost optimization - application popularization," driving China's AI industry from quantitative accumulation to systemic leadership through ecological collaboration. Looking ahead from the beginning of the "15th Five-Year Plan" period, the prospects are even more magnificent. The outline of the "15th Five-Year Plan" clearly proposes the comprehensive implementation of the "Artificial Intelligence+" action, empowering thousands of industries in an all-round way. It is estimated that by the end of the "15th Five-Year Plan" period, the scale of China's artificial intelligence-related industries could exceed 10 trillion yuan, entering a broader growth space. JPMorgan Chase predicts that China's AI inference token consumption will grow from approximately 10 quadrillion in 2025 to about 3900 quadrillion in 2030, a nearly 370-fold increase in five years. While the potential is huge, challenges cannot be ignored: how to achieve qualitative improvement on the basis of quantitative growth, how to resolve copyright issues related to AI-generated content, and how to build an integrated security governance system covering data, technology, and networks are all issues that China's AI industry needs to continuously address. From the open-source craze of everyone "raising shrimp" to the creative explosion of AI videos on social media, from the thousandfold growth in token call volume over two years to the increasingly完善 industrial ecosystem, China's artificial intelligence development has long moved beyond the stage of purely technological catch-up and entered a stage of systemic breakthroughs based on the domestic market and a complete industrial system. The average daily token call volume exceeding 140 trillion is not only a key turning point for artificial intelligence from technological accumulation to application outbreak but also a microcosm of the synchronized resonance between open-source innovation and scenario implementation, and the deep integration of data elements and AI technology, becoming a distinct mark of the high-quality development of China's digital economy. We are experiencing and witnessing the "Chinese moment" of artificial intelligence, and all of this is just the beginning. (Reporter Wu Shuang)

title_en: Tackling e-commerce counterfeit and shoddy goods requires a serious approach.
body_en: The "AB goods" chaos in e-commerce is not an isolated problem in a specific sector, but rather an industry-wide persistent issue under platform traffic rules. Only when traffic is no longer solely driven by low prices can quality truly return to its rightful meaning of "good products at reasonable prices." The long-criticized chaos of "AB goods" in e-commerce has recently resurfaced. A consumer recently posted on social media, showing two identical down jackets purchased from the same store, with significant differences in color, style, and filling weight. On a complaint platform, there are over 2,600 related complaints about "goods not matching the description," exposing this chaos not as an isolated problem in a specific sector, but as an industry-wide persistent issue under platform traffic rules. "AB goods" refers to merchants displaying high-quality A-grade products but actually shipping B-grade products that are similar in appearance but inferior in quality. Common tactics include: the version displayed on the platform and in live streams differing from the version actually shipped, and seemingly promotional price reductions actually involving reduced specifications and quality. The occurrence of this chaos is related to the traffic rules of e-commerce platforms. In particular, the "automatic price following" tool puts merchants in a dilemma: platforms allocate traffic based on low prices, and merchants are pressured to lower prices due to traffic demands. After lowering prices, profit margins become thin, forcing them to reduce costs and quality. After all, for many small and medium-sized merchants, there is a cruel choice: either sell genuine products at a loss, potentially leading to bankruptcy due to poor management; or use B-grade products to survive, cutting costs in areas where consumers are less likely to notice. Consumers are not unaware of the principle that "you get what you pay for"; low prices and low quality are understandable. However, the problem lies in merchants not clearly indicating the differences between the actual product and the sample, and even employing deceptive sales methods, which constitutes an infringement of consumers' right to know and is suspected of fraud. From another perspective, if merchants openly labeled products as "value version" or "online exclusive," consumers would naturally weigh their options. In reality, legal identification of "AB goods" faces numerous obstacles: first, the similarity in appearance makes identification difficult, and subtle differences are hard to document, leading to a high threshold for identification and difficulty in obtaining evidence. This makes it difficult for legal provisions to be truly implemented, and sometimes the cost of testing even exceeds the cost of the product itself, making it difficult for consumers to protect their rights. Second, even if a complaint is successful, the penalties are insufficient and lack deterrent effect. The low cost of violation and high potential returns make merchants flock to it, not hesitating to take risks. The good news is that the "Rules on Price Behavior of Internet Platforms," jointly issued by the National Development and Reform Commission, the State Administration for Market Regulation, and the Cyberspace Administration of China, will officially take effect on April 10th. The rules explicitly prohibit platforms from forcing or implicitly forcing merchants to "automatically follow prices" and to sell at prices below cost, aiming to curb "involutionary" price wars and promote platforms to shift from "grabbing traffic" to "emphasizing quality." Under the guidance of these rules, the path of using A-grade products for traffic and B-grade products for profit is likely to become unfeasible. However, the implementation of the rules is only the first step in breaking the deadlock. Their effectiveness will take time and requires the joint protection of all parties in the market. On the one hand, regulatory authorities should refine relevant standards, streamline complaint and reporting channels, and form a long-term restraint mechanism and strong deterrence. On the other hand, platforms should also position themselves correctly, proactively adjust their traffic allocation mechanisms, incorporate quality, service, and user reputation into core weights, and strengthen their review and supervision responsibilities for merchants. Only when traffic is no longer solely driven by low prices can quality truly return to its rightful meaning of "good products at reasonable prices."

title_en: Japanese media: Chinese internet giants are betting on intelligent agents
body_en: According to a March 24 report by The Nikkei, several Chinese internet giants are increasing their capital expenditures, including on data centers, aiming to rapidly improve infrastructure and respond to the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI). However, there are also concerns that aggressive investment could lead to a deterioration in profitability. The report states that at an earnings call on March 19, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu emphasized the rapid development of AI in China, noting that it is quickly integrating into various industries. Alibaba's fourth-quarter earnings for fiscal year 2025, announced on the same day, showed a significant year-on-year drop in net profit, although revenue from its cloud computing business increased. In addition to cloud services, Alibaba is also independently developing its generative AI platform model, "Tongyi Qianwen," and semiconductor products for AI to better meet growing demand. Wu stated that the company plans to achieve $100 billion in revenue from Alibaba Cloud and AI-related businesses within five years. The report indicates that strengthening AI-related businesses is inseparable from investment in data centers, as they are the foundation of these services. Goldman Sachs predicts that by 2027, the capital expenditures of four major internet companies – Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and Baidu – are expected to reach $84 billion, a 60% increase from 2025. "Intelligent agents" capable of autonomous operation are particularly attracting industry attention. This is attributed to China's policies encouraging the application of intelligent agents and the rapid popularization of the open-source service OpenClaw in China. The report notes that while Chinese internet companies are introducing "OpenClaw," they are also deploying their own intelligent agents to compete in terms of user-friendliness. Alibaba has already begun offering intelligent agents to consumers and released its enterprise-grade AI-native work platform, "Wukong," on March 17. Similar to the 72 transformations of Sun Wukong in "Journey to the West," "Wukong" can perform various tasks, such as document editing and transcribing meeting recordings. Tencent will also deploy intelligent agents on its social platform WeChat, which has over a billion users. Upon receiving instructions, these agents will utilize in-app programs (such as ride-hailing services) to fulfill user requests. The goal is to use intelligent agents as an entry point to guide users to utilize more of Tencent's services. Tencent CEO Pony Ma stated at an earnings call on March 18 that by focusing on intelligent agents, Tencent can expand its areas of strength and better leverage its advantages as a diversified internet service provider. However, the continuous expansion of investment in AI infrastructure and technological research and development may also impact corporate profitability. The report points out that Tencent Cloud achieved profitability for the first time in fiscal year 2025, while Alibaba's cloud services still contribute limitedly to overall profitability. title_en: "Hundred Shrimp War" begins, cloud vendors re-evaluate token value
body_en: The "OpenClaw" wave has sparked a global surge in shrimp farming. In interviews with media outlets like Yicai Global, Li Qiang, Tencent Group's Vice President and President of Enterprise Business, jokingly remarked that just as there was a "battle of a hundred models" before, there is now a "battle of a hundred shrimps." This March, tech giants such as Tencent, Alibaba, Baidu, JD.com, NetEase Youdao, Xiaomi, and 360 have entered the market, expanding the number of shrimp-related products to dozens. Reporters have learned that some shrimp products have been launched very quickly. Taking Tencent WorkBuddy as an example, Wang Shengjie, the product lead, told reporters that the product prototype was iterated in January. After he and a few colleagues worked through two nights, it was launched on January 17th. With the popularity of OpenClaw, remote control capabilities were added after the Spring Festival, along with integration with WeChat Work and QQ. The entire infrastructure of Tencent CodeBuddy is the foundation for the rapid launch of this product. More supporting products are also being launched. On March 27th, Tencent Cloud released a panoramic view of its Agent products at a summit in Shanghai, covering infrastructure, models and ecosystem, scenarios and applications, and security dimensions. It also opened up its self-developed Skills, the open-source SkillsHub, and skill ecosystems like WeChat and WeChat Work. The Agent market is booming, and for cloud vendors, the most significant change is the increase in token consumption. "Token consumption has driven a substantial increase in computing power usage," Li Qiang told reporters. Tencent Cloud expects its overall revenue growth this year to be higher than last year, with AI being a major growth engine. JD.com recently announced usage data for its JD Cloud shrimp products, stating that token call volume increased by 455% week-on-week within a week. IDC predicts that the usage of Agents by the world's largest 2,000 listed companies will increase tenfold by 2027, with token and API call volumes growing a thousandfold. Reporters have learned that cloud vendors are already evaluating the deep impact of these Agents. Li Qiang's judgment is that AI for Business (AI to B) has become the largest incremental market for all cloud vendors, and the industry is now at the cusp of an explosion in industrial-grade AI. In the past, Tencent Cloud primarily sold large models and related computing power to leading large model companies, embodied intelligence, and other highly internet-related enterprises. However, as OpenClaw drives AI from the conversational layer to the execution layer, the reduced barrier to AI usage will boost the willingness of B-end users to adopt large models. These Agent capabilities can be used in multiple scenarios. Li Qiang gave an example to reporters, stating that WorkBuddy extends beyond code writing to application scenarios such as daily business collaboration and office task processing. Agents will be able to replace manual labor in more core areas such as contract review, bid writing and review, video material reading, and internal audits. Additionally, Agents can review the quality of responses from human customer service representatives in the customer service domain. For photos taken during drone inspections, Agents can also quickly read and provide insights, replacing manual effort. The industry believes that the impact of OpenClaw will be even more profound. Various shrimp products call upon cloud-based large model capabilities and require payment for tokens. Cloud vendors' related businesses include MaaS (Model as a Service). For a period, cloud vendors engaged in price wars around large model calls, leading some market participants to believe that token consumption alone was a game of endlessly driving down prices. However, with the increase in token consumption brought about by shrimp products, how to re-evaluate the token consumption model has become a question for cloud vendors. In response to the opportunities presented by increased token consumption, several domestic cloud vendors have made moves recently. Alibaba recently established the Alibaba Token Hub business group, with the core objectives of "creating tokens, delivering tokens, and applying tokens," personally led by CEO Wu Yongming. Wu Yongming predicts that future commercial MaaS revenue will become Alibaba Cloud's most profitable product. Market news also suggests that ByteDance's Volcano Engine has seen a daily increase of over 60% in cloud-based large model calls in less than two months. With the continued popularity of OpenClaw, Volcano Engine has raised its MaaS annual business revenue target to over 10 billion yuan. Previously, Tencent emphasized that simply consuming tokens is not a healthy business, and highlighted the importance of SaaS (Software as a Service) business and the demands for training and databases brought about by AI, in addition to tokens. In this wave of shrimp fever, Tencent's emphasis on tokens has also increased. Tencent Cloud announced today that it has upgraded its MaaS platform to TokenHub. However, there is still some "cold thinking" in the industry regarding the opportunities brought about by increased token consumption. "Assuming tokens are like fuel consumption, if we only focus on fuel consumption and not on the economics of building the engine, the user-side costs might be very high, and customers will eventually abandon it," Li Qiang gave an example to reporters. Tokens are not a sticky business; if customers are acquired through low prices, they can easily be lost if "red envelopes and eggs" are no longer given. Tokens are one of Tencent Cloud's important management metrics, but they are not prioritized above all else. Instead of focusing on tokens, it is more important to focus on whether we can create Agents that are as easy to use and safer than OpenClaw. Cloud vendors will continue to adjust their strategies in this wave of opportunities, and industry insiders predict that the impact of shrimp will continue. Wang Shengjie told reporters that shrimp is not a transitional product, but a concept with demands and scenarios, capable of completing tasks in a non-intrusive, automated, and secure, controllable manner. Shrimp products are essentially Agents, and which one performs better depends on its information extraction and contextual understanding capabilities. Due to the diversity of user profiles, there will also be diversity in Agents.

title_en: 21 Commentary | How will "Word Elements" Reshape the Competitive Logic of the AI Industry?
body_en: Gao Tingfan (Associate Professor, School of Economics, University of International Business and Economics; Director, China Association for Commercial Economy) Recently, at the China Development Forum 2026 Annual Meeting, Liu Liehong, Director of the National Data Administration, stated that "Token" is not only the value anchor of the intelligent era but also the "settlement unit" connecting technological supply and commercial demand, providing quantifiable possibilities for the implementation of business models. He also provided an official translation for Token: "词元" (ci yuan). According to the latest data from the National Data Administration, the daily average "ci yuan" call volume in China has surged from 100 billion at the beginning of 2024 to 1.4 million trillion in March of this year, an increase of over a thousandfold in two years. The capital market reacted swiftly, with "ci yuan concept" stocks in A-shares experiencing a widespread surge, and many individual stocks hitting their daily limit or rising significantly. This is not just a pursuit of these growth figures, but rather an indication of a deeper industrial signal: "ci yuan" is transforming from a technical parameter into the core unit of account and resource allocation signal in the AI era. For a general-purpose technology to move from the laboratory to widespread adoption, it needs to cross a critical threshold: from "technically feasible" to "economically feasible." Crossing this threshold often depends on something seemingly insignificant: finding a basic unit that can be measured, priced, and settled. In 1881, when Edison built the first commercial power station on Pearl Street in New York, his biggest challenge was not generating electricity, but measuring it. His invention of the electric meter turned electricity into a commodity that could be charged for by volume. It was this metering tool, not the generator itself, that more profoundly changed the course of industrial history – electricity transformed from a laboratory marvel into a public utility. Today, "ci yuan" is playing the role of "kilowatt-hour" in the AI era. Once intelligence can be standardized, tiered in pricing, and settled by volume, the entire industry can truly shift from discussing capital stories to calculating operating profits. The thousandfold increase in "ci yuan" call volume is less about describing the scale of AI usage and more about announcing something more fundamental: intelligence finally has its own "electric meter." Looking back at the past few years, major manufacturers have continuously competed on the parameter scale, evaluation rankings, and open-source buzz of their AI large models. This is typical supply-side competition in the early stages of innovative industry development, with core breakthroughs in technological capabilities. The thousandfold growth in "ci yuan" call volume signifies a shift in the industry's focus – from how good the models are to how much they are used, from technological breakthroughs to commercial implementation and empowering the real economy. In fact, this transition process – the diffusion and application of innovation – is not smooth. Between 2024 and 2025, the API call prices for mainstream AI models in China were primarily low-priced or free, following the classic path of internet platform economics: first acquire users and a developer ecosystem with low prices, then find monetization channels. The explosive growth in "ci yuan" demand is fundamentally rewriting this landscape. It is understood that Alibaba Cloud's Model-as-a-Service platform achieved its highest growth rate in the first quarter of this year, and computing resources have begun to be tilted towards "ci yuan" business. Almost simultaneously, Alibaba announced the establishment of a new business group named Alibaba Token Hub, integrating capabilities across the entire chain from foundational models to application layers, led directly by the CEO. This is not merely a departmental reorganization, but a strategic shift by China's leading technology companies centered around "ci yuan." For the race in the "ci yuan" economy, the thousandfold growth in two years marks not an endpoint, but a new starting line. It is not about who has the highest model benchmark scores, but about who can first build a complete infrastructure system from computing power production, intelligent scheduling, to terminal accessibility. China is the world's largest market for artificial intelligence applications, which also means it will have the most vigorous demand for "ci yuan" globally. This is a very significant trump card. Therefore, it is necessary to further promote demand to drive self-controlled computing power supply, a reasonable and transparent pricing mechanism, and an inclusive architecture that allows small and medium-sized enterprises and ordinary entrepreneurs to "afford to use intelligence," thereby truly transforming the demand advantage into China's industrial competitiveness advantage in the AI era.
