title_en: AI Era Cloud Competition Diverges: Telecom Operators Slow Down, Internet Giants Return to Growth
body_en: The financial reports of the three major telecom operators have been released, revealing the performance of their cloud businesses. According to the financial reports, operator clouds, which once surged with the advantage of "cloud-network integration," have seen their growth slow down again in 2025, following a slowdown in 2024. China Telecom's Tianyi Cloud revenue reached 120.7 billion yuan (RMB, same below), still showing growth, but its growth rate has fallen from 17.1% in the previous year to 5.44%. Unicom Cloud's growth rate dropped from 17.1% to 5.2%, with an estimated annual revenue of 72.2 billion yuan. China Mobile, for the first time, no longer separately disclosed "Mobile Cloud" revenue in its annual report, instead presenting it under the categories of "computing services + AI services." Among these, computing services revenue was 89.832 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 11.1%; AI services revenue was 90.833 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 5.3%. In stark contrast, internet cloud vendors staged a strong comeback in 2025. Companies like Alibaba, Tencent, and Baidu not only achieved profitability or significant profit growth but also saw exponential growth in AI-related revenue, driven by large models. Looking back, 2021-2023 were the "golden years" for operator clouds. During that period, Tianyi Cloud, Mobile Cloud, and Unicom Cloud all maintained triple-digit year-on-year growth rates, steadily increasing their market share in the public cloud market, and once appeared poised to push the "predecessors" – internet cloud vendors – out of the top tier. In just two years, the situation has dramatically reversed. Zhou Guijun, a telecommunications industry analyst, believes that AI may be the key determinant of success or failure behind this shift. As AI becomes the new generation of digital infrastructure, the cloud market is transitioning from a rough "IT resource leasing" model to a more refined era of "token and computing power billing," allowing internet vendors to regain their advantage. Facing these challenges, finding a way out for cloud businesses under the new growth logic has become a new imperative for operators. The Logic of Change: Saying Goodbye to "Rapid Growth" Operators are no longer willing to undertake a large volume of loss-making, low-margin integration projects for the sake of book growth, which has increased the difficulty of cloud business growth. Why did operator cloud businesses collectively hit a bottleneck in 2025? Industry insiders believe this trend is not accidental but a result of the superposition of multiple internal and external factors. "The onboarding of government and enterprise clients has basically peaked," said Li Jun, a department head at China Telecom in East China. In the early stages of cloud adoption in 2021, operators had a clear advantage in driving government and enterprise projects and resource deployment. Coupled with a large market gap at the time, large-scale deployments by major clients directly boosted the profitability of their cloud businesses. However, by 2025, most government departments and large central state-owned enterprises had completed their basic cloud migration. As the market approached saturation, the number of new projects significantly decreased. The market has moved from a "pioneering period" to an "operational period." With tightening budgets, government and enterprise clients are demanding deeper business transformation solutions from cloud vendors. Zhou Guijun believes that compared to internet cloud vendors, operators have long focused on providing underlying resources such as bandwidth and storage (IaaS), with weak accumulation in PaaS (Platform as a Service) and SaaS (Software as a Service). As the growth logic of the cloud market shifts to basic computing power supply, operators lack sufficient "stickiness" when facing complex business scenarios. In contrast, the service model of internet cloud providers is not project-based. Their products are standardized and segmented, with a rich ecosystem. With the advent of the AI era, operators' shortcomings in technical reserves and market-oriented operational capabilities have become apparent. Facing the small and medium-sized enterprise market and general AI application scenarios, operators' product flexibility and service response speed are inferior to internet cloud vendors, making it difficult to expand new incremental customer groups, thus further exacerbating the slowdown in growth. In addition, some operators have begun to shift from "focusing on scale" to "focusing on quality," voluntarily abandoning some low-profit integration projects, which has also affected the growth rate of their cloud businesses to some extent. According to reports, in order to seize market share, operators frequently bid for large government and enterprise projects at low prices between 2022 and 2024. Although this strategy boosted revenue scale in the short term, it also laid the groundwork for profitability issues. By 2025, as the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) shifted the assessment criteria for central state-owned enterprises from "revenue scale orientation" to "quality and value orientation," operators were no longer willing to undertake a large volume of loss-making, low-margin integration projects for the sake of book growth, which increased the difficulty of cloud business growth. Yang Guang, an analyst at Omida Telecom Strategy, believes that operator clouds have historically relied heavily on government and enterprise clients. The first wave of cloud adoption demand in this market has been gradually released. Relying solely on traditional government and enterprise orders can no longer support high-speed growth in cloud businesses, while the expansion into the small and medium-sized enterprise market has not achieved effective breakthroughs. These issues have led to the current predicament. Wang Qinglin, manager of Ruidaheng Research Institute, previously pointed out to reporters that the high growth of operator clouds was largely due to the rapid development of the government and enterprise market and a low base. As the scale reaches a certain level, a return to rational growth is a normal industry development trend. Internet Cloud Camp's Counter-Trend Return The explosive growth of AI-related businesses is considered the main reason behind the return to high growth for internet cloud giants. In stark contrast to operator clouds, internet cloud giants have seen their performance accelerate again, driven by this round of AI. Among them, Alibaba Cloud's revenue in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 reached 30.127 billion yuan, an increase of 18% year-on-year. Looking at a longer period, Alibaba further positioned AI+Cloud as its core growth engine in 2025, with AI-related product revenue maintaining triple-digit growth for seven consecutive quarters. In fiscal year 2025, Alibaba Cloud's adjusted EBITA margin was approximately 8.8%, a significant improvement from previous fiscal years, achieving both scale and profitability growth. Tencent Cloud also achieved "improving growth" in external cloud services in 2025. Tencent explicitly stated that driven by AI demand, overseas expansion, and tight supply of memory and CPUs, cloud service revenue growth and pricing environment have improved. In addition, Baidu Smart Cloud's infrastructure revenue in 2025 was approximately 20 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 34%. In the fourth quarter, AI cloud infrastructure revenue was 5.8 billion yuan, and subscription-based AI accelerator infrastructure revenue increased by 143% year-on-year. The explosive growth of AI-related businesses is considered the main reason behind the return to high growth for internet cloud giants. Alibaba explicitly stated that strong AI demand drove the growth of its Cloud Intelligence Group. Wu Yongming, CEO of Alibaba Cloud, said at the earnings call that demand for AI-related products is exploding across the board, with both large internet companies and small and medium-sized enterprises exceeding expectations in their demand for AI computing power and model services. Public data shows that the average daily token call volume of Alibaba Cloud's external customers has surged from less than 1 trillion at the beginning of 2025 to nearly 5 trillion, reflecting the exponential growth in the actual usage of its AI applications. Previously, Alibaba announced that its investment in cloud computing and AI infrastructure over the next three years would exceed the total investment of the past decade. Zhou Guijun believes that this shift from "selling servers" to "selling tokens" has boosted the return of internet cloud vendors' growth. The former provides easy-to-use APIs, allowing thousands of small and medium-sized developers to access large model capabilities through the cloud. This model has extremely low marginal costs and strong economies of scale. Internet cloud vendors not only provide computing power but also offer industry-optimized pre-trained models. For enterprise clients, it is more convenient to directly call existing business logic on Alibaba Cloud or Tencent Cloud than to rent a bunch of bare metal servers from operators. Tencent also emphasized that the acceleration of cloud service revenue is due to increased demand and an improved pricing environment. This means that the core of Tencent Cloud's growth is not just "selling more computing power," but the combined efficiency improvement of cloud resource utilization driven by AI, video, advertising, and international business. At the same time, Tencent expressed positive outlook for the growth of external cloud service revenue in 2026, citing similar reasons as in 2025, including AI demand, overseas expansion, and a more favorable pricing environment due to tight supply of memory and CPUs. Baidu, in addition to achieving 5.8 billion yuan in smart cloud revenue in the fourth quarter and a 143% year-on-year increase in subscription-based AI accelerator infrastructure revenue, also saw its AI application revenue exceed 10 billion yuan for the full year. This means that Baidu Cloud is no longer just traditional IaaS, but an AI infrastructure that directly embeds models, chips, application platforms, and industry solutions, and recovers investment through AI applications and AI-native marketing services. Price Hikes Reshape Cloud Competition Strategy The successive price increases by multiple internet cloud vendors have put the operator cloud camp, which had previously gained market share by pursuing cost-effectiveness and economies of scale, in a more passive position. At this critical juncture of shifting fortunes, in early 2026, internet cloud vendors quickly seized the opportunity, shifting from "market grabbing" to "monetizing through price increases." On March 18, Alibaba Cloud announced price increases of 5%-34% for some AI computing products and a 30% increase for its cloud parallel file storage service, citing surging global AI demand, rising supply chain costs, and increasing prices for core hardware procurement. During the same period, Baidu AI Cloud quickly followed suit, announcing price increases of 5%-30% for AI computing products and services, and simultaneously raising prices for parallel file storage. While Tencent did not implement such direct price increases, its management clearly stated a "better pricing environment," and had already adjusted the billing strategy for some large model services in March. The successive price increases by multiple internet cloud vendors have put the operator cloud camp, which had previously gained market share by pursuing cost-effectiveness and economies of scale, in a more passive position. In response, the industry believes that adapting to industry trends and changing business models is the fundamental way to break through. Yang Guang believes that the price hike wave is driven by changes in the supply and demand of AI computing power. Data from the National Data Administration shows that China's average daily token call volume has surged from about 100 billion at the beginning of 2024 to about 140 trillion in March 2026, an increase of more than a thousandfold in two years. Against this backdrop, the explosive growth in demand has led to a rapid scarcity of computing power resources. Meanwhile, the significant increase in procurement costs for hardware such as computing power and storage chips has further exacerbated the cost pressure on cloud vendors. This change in situation also forces operators to change their current cloud business operating strategies to adapt to the trend. This is precisely why China Telecom emphasized at a recent earnings call that it will link its "intelligent cloud system" with "token value operation"; China Mobile also emphasizes that in the future, it will promote the coordinated development of AI services, data algorithms, industry large models, and computing power networks. In this regard, Zhou Guijun interprets that in the past, government and enterprise clients purchased cloud services based on factors such as data centers, bandwidth, price, and delivery capabilities. Now, clients are increasingly focusing on model effectiveness, inference costs, agent efficiency, and data governance capabilities. If operators continue to position themselves as "cloud resource providers" in the future, they are likely to fall into a dilemma of price sensitivity and profit margin compression. Therefore, they must upgrade their cloud products to industry solutions, AI middle platforms, and inference platforms. After changing their business models, the advantage of "cloud-network integration" for operators may become apparent. Zhou Guijun stated that operators possess nationwide network resources, data centers, and energy advantages, and still have significant advantages in network coverage, edge access, dedicated lines, low-latency connections, government and enterprise reach, and localized delivery, which are core competitiveness that internet cloud vendors cannot match. If these advantages can be transformed into overall solutions, they have the opportunity to create barriers in many government and enterprise application scenarios. Especially in the era of AI inference and agent applications, computing power is not always located in massive central cloud data centers. The importance of edge computing and distributed scheduling will continue to increase, which is precisely the area where operators have the greatest potential to deepen their expertise. Therefore, he stated that this is also why operators are firmly shifting towards computing-network integration and de-emphasizing cloud business expansion. As the era of competing for scale and market share in the cloud market comes to an end, the key to the next stage will be to truly integrate networks, computing power, data, and industry scenarios, which will also be a major highlight for observing the performance of operator clouds in the industry.

Tencent explicitly stated that driven by AI demand, overseas expansion, and tight supply of memory and CPUs, cloud service revenue growth and pricing environment have improved. In addition, Baidu Smart Cloud's infrastructure revenue in 2025 was approximately 20 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 34%. In the fourth quarter, AI cloud infrastructure revenue was 5.8 billion yuan, and subscription-based AI accelerator infrastructure revenue increased by 143% year-on-year. The explosive growth of AI-related businesses is considered the main reason behind the return to high growth for internet cloud giants. Alibaba explicitly stated that strong AI demand drove the growth of its Cloud Intelligence Group. Wu Yongming, CEO of Alibaba Cloud, said at the earnings call that demand for AI-related products is exploding across the board, with both large internet companies and small and medium-sized enterprises exceeding expectations in their demand for AI computing power and model services. Public data shows that the average daily token call volume of Alibaba Cloud's external customers has surged from less than 1 trillion at the beginning of 2025 to nearly 5 trillion, reflecting the exponential growth in the actual usage of its AI applications. Previously, Alibaba announced that its investment in cloud computing and AI infrastructure over the next three years would exceed the total investment of the past decade. Zhou Guijun believes that this shift from "selling servers" to "selling tokens" has boosted the return of internet cloud vendors' growth. The former provides easy-to-use APIs, allowing thousands of small and medium-sized developers to access large model capabilities through the cloud. This model has extremely low marginal costs and strong economies of scale. Internet cloud vendors not only provide computing power but also offer industry-optimized pre-trained models. For enterprise clients, it is more convenient to directly call existing business logic on Alibaba Cloud or Tencent Cloud than to rent a bunch of bare metal servers from operators. Tencent also emphasized that the acceleration of cloud service revenue is due to increased demand and an improved pricing environment. This means that the core of Tencent Cloud's growth is not just "selling more computing power," but the combined efficiency improvement of cloud resource utilization driven by AI, video, advertising, and international business. At the same time, Tencent expressed positive outlook for the growth of external cloud service revenue in 2026, citing similar reasons as in 2025, including AI demand, overseas expansion, and a more favorable pricing environment due to tight supply of memory and CPUs. Baidu, in addition to achieving 5.8 billion yuan in smart cloud revenue in the fourth quarter and a 143% year-on-year increase in subscription-based AI accelerator infrastructure revenue, also saw its AI application revenue exceed 10 billion yuan for the full year. This means that Baidu Cloud is no longer just traditional IaaS, but an AI infrastructure that directly embeds models, chips, application platforms, and industry solutions, and recovers investment through AI applications and AI-native marketing services. Price Hikes Reshape Cloud Competition Strategy The successive price increases by multiple internet cloud vendors have put the operator cloud camp, which had previously gained market share by pursuing cost-effectiveness and economies of scale, in a more passive position. At this critical juncture of shifting fortunes, in early 2026, internet cloud vendors quickly seized the opportunity, shifting from "market grabbing" to "monetizing through price increases." On March 18, Alibaba Cloud announced price increases of 5%-34% for some AI computing products and a 30% increase for its cloud parallel file storage service, citing surging global AI demand, rising supply chain costs, and increasing prices for core hardware procurement. During the same period, Baidu AI Cloud quickly followed suit, announcing price increases of 5%-30% for AI computing products and services, and simultaneously raising prices for parallel file storage. While Tencent did not implement such direct price increases, its management clearly stated a "better pricing environment," and had already adjusted the billing strategy for some large model services in March. The successive price increases by multiple internet cloud vendors have put the operator cloud camp, which had previously gained market share by pursuing cost-effectiveness and economies of scale, in a more passive position. In response, the industry believes that adapting to industry trends and changing business models is the fundamental way to break through. Yang Guang believes that the price hike wave is driven by changes in the supply and demand of AI computing power. Data from the National Data Administration shows that China's average daily token call volume has surged from about 100 billion at the beginning of 2024 to about 140 trillion in March 2026, an increase of more than a thousandfold in two years. Against this backdrop, the explosive growth in demand has led to a rapid scarcity of computing power resources. Meanwhile, the significant increase in procurement costs for hardware such as computing power and storage chips has further exacerbated the cost pressure on cloud vendors. This change in situation also forces operators to change their current cloud business operating strategies to adapt to the trend. This is precisely why China Telecom emphasized at a recent earnings call that it will link its "intelligent cloud system" with "token value operation"; China Mobile also emphasizes that in the future, it will promote the coordinated development of AI services, data algorithms, industry large models, and computing power networks. In this regard, Zhou Guijun interprets that in the past, government and enterprise clients purchased cloud services based on factors such as data centers, bandwidth, price, and delivery capabilities. Now, clients are increasingly focusing on model effectiveness, inference costs, agent efficiency, and data governance capabilities. If operators continue to position themselves as "cloud resource providers" in the future, they are likely to fall into a dilemma of price sensitivity and profit margin compression. Therefore, they must upgrade their cloud products to industry solutions, AI middle platforms, and inference platforms. After changing their business models, the advantage of "cloud-network integration" for operators may become apparent. Zhou Guijun stated that operators possess nationwide network resources, data centers, and energy advantages, and still have significant advantages in network coverage, edge access, dedicated lines, low-latency connections, government and enterprise reach, and localized delivery, which are core competitiveness that internet cloud vendors cannot match. If these advantages can be transformed into overall solutions, they have the opportunity to create barriers in many government and enterprise application scenarios. Especially in the era of AI inference and agent applications, computing power is not always located in massive central cloud data centers. The importance of edge computing and distributed scheduling will continue to increase, which is precisely the area where operators have the greatest potential to deepen their expertise. Therefore, he stated that this is also why operators are firmly shifting towards computing-network integration and de-emphasizing cloud business expansion. As the era of competing for scale and market share in the cloud market comes to an end, the key to the next stage will be to truly integrate networks, computing power, data, and industry scenarios, which will also be a major highlight for observing the performance of operator clouds in the industry.

title_en: Industrial ecosystem upgrade and reconstruction, continuing to heavily invest in supply chain layout in 2026
body_en: Qingdao's century-old enamelware is winning over the younger generation on Pinduoduo. Meizhou pomelos have been upgraded from being sold "cheap by the pound" to "boutique by the piece." Benefiting from Pinduoduo's "10 Billion Subsidy" program, many agricultural product merchants save hundreds of thousands of yuan annually in fees. Small home appliances like blenders from Zhongshan, Guangdong, have found a growing market in western regions. In April 2025, building upon merchant-friendly initiatives such as the "10 Billion Subsidy," Pinduoduo accelerated its high-quality development strategy upgrade, launching a groundbreaking merchant-empowerment strategy of "100 Billion Yuan" in the e-commerce industry. Over three years, the platform plans to invest 100 billion yuan in resources to continuously benefit both supply and demand sides, driving merchant and industry upgrades and transformations, and actively building a win-win ecosystem for users, merchants, industries, and the platform. Over the past year, leveraging the "100 Billion Yuan Support" strategy, Pinduoduo has increased investment in special initiatives like "Good Local Specialties on Pinduoduo," "New Quality Supply," and "E-commerce Westward Expansion." The platform has entered hundreds of agricultural production areas and industrial belts, delving into every link of the supply chain to promote the refinement and standardization of agricultural products and foster brand development and high-quality growth in industrial belts. Furthermore, by the end of 2025, Pinduoduo will further promote consumption inclusivity by including more remote villages in the "free shipping zone," thereby stimulating rural economic vitality through "free delivery to villages." Building on the supply chain foundation laid by the "100 Billion Yuan Support," Pinduoduo recently announced the establishment of "New Pinduoduo," signaling a continued heavy investment in China's supply chain and the launch of brand self-operation, driving high-quality and branded development of domestic industries. This is the first strategic move following Pinduoduo's release of its new phase strategy: "Focus, Heavy Investment in Supply Chain Upgrades, and High-Quality Development." Currently, New Pinduoduo has established a new special company in Shanghai, with an initial cash injection of 15 billion yuan. Over the next three years, a total of 100 billion yuan in capital is planned to integrate the supply chain resources of "Pinduoduo + Temu," focusing on the global market. The company will systematically operate its own brands and incubate brands for different markets and categories. "We have anchored China's supply chain as the core of our future business development. The company will continue to practice high-quality development, deeply cultivate the high quality and branding of China's supply chain, achieve platform re-creation, and drive value leapfrogging of the ecosystem," stated Group Co-Chairman and Co-CEO Zhao Jiazhen. Entering Hundreds of Agricultural Production Areas and Industrial Belts Supply Chain Achieves Transformation and Upgrading In April 2025, following the launch of "100 Billion Yuan Support," Pinduoduo officially initiated the "2025 Good Local Specialties on Pinduoduo" agricultural special action. By the end of 2025, the "Good Local Specialties on Pinduoduo" special team had entered over a hundred agricultural production areas, including Lianjiang abalone, Meizhou pomelos, Yunnan coffee, Guizhou刺梨, and Zhaotong potatoes. Leveraging the platform's digital capabilities, they implemented customized support based on the characteristics and industrial advantages of each region. By enriching product offerings and store matrices, they addressed issues such as insufficient seasonal supply and low standardization of fresh produce, promoting refined and deep processing development in agricultural production areas, effectively increasing the added value of agricultural products, boosting farmers' production and income, and achieving long-term development. In Lianjiang, Fujian, local merchants had long been limited to selling primary processed products like live and frozen abalone, resulting in limited profits and scale. With Pinduoduo's support, Lianjiang merchants engaged in deep processing of seafood, innovating and developing black truffle abalone. This single product achieved monthly sales exceeding 10 million yuan, sparking a new wave of industrial upgrading in the region. In Meizhou, Guangdong, local fruit farmers brought their pomelos to Pinduoduo, breaking the pricing and grading power previously held by distributors. This transformed Meizhou pomelos from being sold "cheap by the pound" to "boutique by the piece," accelerating their path to refined development. In March of this year, Pinduoduo announced the official upgrade of the "2026 Good Local Specialties on Pinduoduo" special initiative, focusing on empowering the entire agricultural industry, increasing investment in agricultural product supply chains, and promoting the comprehensive development and upgrading of agricultural specialty industries to achieve long-term development. "Moving forward, we will continue to delve into major agricultural production areas, focusing on empowering merchants to develop various deep and finely processed agricultural and sideline products, leaving more profit and pricing power within the agricultural production areas, and assisting them in achieving high-quality development of quality agriculture and branded agriculture," stated a representative from "2026 Good Local Specialties on Pinduoduo." In industrial belts, Pinduoduo's "100 Billion Yuan Support" initiative continues to bolster "New Quality Supply," accelerating its cultivation and upward flow, promoting merchant quality and efficiency, and driving the upgrading of industrial belts. To date, the "New Quality Supply" special team has visited over a hundred high-quality manufacturing clusters, including Yiwu cosmetics, Shenzhen digital products, Shandong accessories, Shaodong luggage, Pinghu down products, and Weihai fishing gear. They have also delved into various links of the supply chain, including raw materials and accessories, to achieve transformation and upgrading in each segment and actively address the industrial challenge of homogeneous competition. Qingdao, Shandong, is the largest "city of accessories" in the north. Local merchants have improved accessories using intangible cultural heritage enamel craftsmanship, giving rise to differentiated accessory brands that blend oriental aesthetics with original genes. Leveraging Pinduoduo's insights into new consumption, local merchants have further refined the traditional bright color style of enamel accessories, incorporating contemporary youth preferences to develop styles like the "Chinese Zodiac" and "Zodiac Signs." They have also introduced commuter-friendly enamel accessories, truly bringing intangible cultural heritage enamel craftsmanship into daily life. In Yiwu, Zhejiang, many "invisible champions" who previously manufactured overseas cosmetic brands are struggling with declining profits. With Pinduoduo's backing, these "invisible champions" have found a new path, offering cost-effective products like blushes and hand creams for twenty to thirty yuan, precisely targeting new customer groups such as junior high and university students, and successfully embarking on their brand journey. "Fee Reduction + Subsidy" Dual Approach Tens of Millions of Merchants Achieve Quality and Efficiency Improvement Over the past year, Pinduoduo's "100 Billion Yuan Support" has continued to provide fee reductions and refunds to platform merchants, in addition to the "10 Billion Subsidy." Following a series of refund policies for fees such as "technical service fees" and "promotion service fees," Pinduoduo has also significantly reduced the technical service fees for the "10 Billion Subsidy," security deposits for specific category stores, and offered substantial platform subsidies like "10 Billion Consumer Vouchers," enabling tens of millions of merchants to reduce costs and increase efficiency. In Chengdu, Sichuan, a flower merchant has deeply experienced the platform's fee reduction efforts. According to the merchant, nearly half of their agricultural product orders are on a "pay-after-use" basis. "The platform's 'pay-after-use' technical service fee has been uniformly reduced to 0.6%, and combined with previous resource placement technical fee refunds, we save an average of 50,000 to 60,000 yuan per month, allowing us to invest more funds into the agricultural product supply chain." In industrial belts, Pinduoduo's fee reductions have also created new space for merchants' product research and development and industrial upgrading. A mid-tier children's shoe merchant stated that after the implementation of policies like "promotion service fee refunds," they save hundreds of thousands of yuan annually. These savings are fully reinvested in the research and development of new products, enhancing product competitiveness and allowing the merchant to operate more confidently in a market crowded with giants. Beyond fee reductions, Pinduoduo also reinvests in merchants and industries through substantial subsidies, continuously releasing the platform's consumption potential and driving accelerated industrial transformation and upgrading. In Wuhan, Hubei, several products from a sunflower seed company were included in subsidy lists for programs like the "10 Billion Subsidy" and "Ten Thousand People Group." Daily orders for the store increased by 40%, repurchase rates grew by over 30%, and the company climbed to the top 5 in sales within its category on the platform, becoming an invisible champion in its niche market. In the industrial clusters of Jinjiang, Fujian, a number of old factories in the sports, apparel, and snack industries have also benefited from the platform's reduction policies. A long-standing brand of outdoor jackets, established for 30 years, used the reduced funds to develop new outdoor jacket products. Combined with platform activities like "10 Billion Consumer Vouchers," they successfully entered the youth market, injecting new momentum into the local apparel industry. "The most significant impact was Pinduoduo's 100 Billion Yuan Support initiative launched in April last year. They personally issued discount coupons to consumers, which not only boosted sales but also increased merchant profits." According to merchants, Pinduoduo might give consumers coupons of 10 or 20 yuan at a time, but the merchant's net price remains unchanged. The improvement brought by direct financial subsidies is significant, with store sales doubling, reaching 3 to 4 million yuan in monthly sales. "From Half a Month to Three Days" Remote Villages Included in "Free Shipping Zone" In 2025, Pinduoduo's "100 Billion Yuan Support" continued to accelerate "E-commerce Westward Expansion." In addition to waiving logistics transit fees in western regions, the platform has continuously broken down logistics barriers in counties and towns, helping to extend the "free shipping zone" to remote administrative villages. This allows high-quality goods from eastern regions to be shipped to western and other remote areas, improving the quality of life for local consumers and stimulating economic vitality in western and other remote regions. During the 2026 Spring Festival, Yu Shengmin in a small village in Ankang, Shaanxi, experienced a lively holiday. According to Yu Shengmin, in the past, most villagers had to travel over 20 kilometers to the nearest town to purchase goods. Since Pinduoduo's "free delivery to villages" service arrived, his Pinduoduo station has opened. Villagers' express packages filled Yu Shengmin's shelves, with daily parcel volume exceeding a hundred before Spring Festival. Villagers purchased a wide variety of New Year goods, and the constant flow of packages has completely revitalized Yu Shengmin's small shop. In Purang Village, Qamdo, Tibet, surrounded by mountains, express deliveries previously had to be sent to Lhasa and then transferred to Qamdo, taking half a month. Local villagers also had to travel to the county town to pick up their packages. The "100 Billion Yuan Support" initiative, while maintaining the second-stage freight fee reduction for goods shipped west, has continuously improved last-mile delivery networks, tackling the challenges of "the last mile." This has transformed express delivery in Purang Village from "half a month to pick up" to "three-day delivery," and from "picking up in town" to "collecting at the village entrance." From the perspective of Guangdong merchant Jiang Youjun, the Inner Mongolia region in 2025 is no longer a blank market. After the launch of "E-commerce Westward Expansion," logistics time from Zhongshan to Inner Mongolia was shortened to three days, enabling Jiang Youjun's large-capacity blenders to successfully enter the local market, with monthly sales reaching hundreds of units. In fact, small and large home appliances like blenders are becoming best-selling products in western regions with Pinduoduo's promotion. Data shows that pet supplies, sunscreens, trendy merchandise, and home appliances are rapidly entering the western market, with significant order growth. "E-commerce Westward Expansion" has also accelerated the process of "Western Goods Going East." In Min County, Gansu, local astragalus products were historically only circulated within Ningxia and Gansu. After the implementation of the "100 Billion Yuan Support" in 2025, astragalus is now available in various forms, such as sliced astragalus and astragalus powder. It has also traveled over two thousand kilometers to appear in the soups and teas of people in Guangdong, sparking a new wave of health and wellness trends. Benefiting from the inclusivity brought by "E-commerce Westward Expansion," economic vitality in both eastern and western regions has been further stimulated. Many industry insiders point out that by waiving logistics transit fees, Pinduoduo has expanded the sales radius for platform merchants, and previously overlooked western and other remote areas are becoming new growth markets. Establishment of New Pinduoduo Continued Heavy Investment in Supply Chain in 2026 In December 2025, at the annual shareholder meeting, Pinduoduo announced the upgrade of its corporate governance structure, implementing a co-chairman system and appointing Zhao Jiazhen as Co-Chairman, who will serve alongside Chen Lei as Group Co-Chairman and Co-CEO. Since Zhao Jiazhen took on the role of Co-CEO, Pinduoduo has fully transitioned to a new phase of high-quality development for the platform and ecosystem, successively launching major merchant-friendly policies such as "100 Billion Yuan Support" and "10 Billion Subsidy," assisting the industry ecosystem in leaping from scale to quality. At the shareholder meeting, Pinduoduo's management repeatedly emphasized the continued heavy investment in China's supply chain. Pinduoduo Co-Chairman and Co-CEO Chen Lei stated that Pinduoduo will continue to adhere to a long-term perspective, rooted in China's supply chain, and is committed to achieving sustainable development in all markets, creating real value for consumers. Zhao Jiazhen also stated that Pinduoduo's next phase will not be about diversification, but about greater focus – focusing on the high-quality development of China's supply chain. "We will invest more energy, financial resources, and material resources to accelerate the upgrade and re-creation of China's supply chain, promote the high-quality and branded development of the industry ecosystem, and drive the overall upgrade of the supply chain operating model. I believe that in the next three years, we will have the opportunity to re-create a Pinduoduo," Zhao Jiazhen said. Under the new phase strategy of "Focus, Heavy Investment in Supply Chain Upgrades, and High-Quality Development," Pinduoduo has established "New Pinduoduo" to fully launch its brand self-operation model. Through this model, the company will continue to heavily invest in China's supply chain, establish higher manufacturing standards, and incubate a batch of internationally influential brands. Currently, New Pinduoduo has established a special company and will form a dedicated team to provide comprehensive overseas solutions for industrial belts, comprehensively promoting the high-quality and branded "going global" for merchants in China's industrial belts. "From the practical experience of the '100 Billion Yuan Support' initiative in the early stages, branded development has become a new engine for China's industrial development. In the next three years, through the 'New Pinduoduo' self-operation model, we will continue to heavily invest in China's supply chain, injecting another 100 billion yuan in cash. More self-operated brands from China's industrial belts will go global through 'New Pinduoduo,' driving the overall transformation and upgrading of China's supply chain," Zhao Jiazhen stated. title_en: Internet companies' annual reports are being released intensively – AI becomes the key driving force for performance growth
body_en: AI-driven profit hits new highs, instant retail grows strongly, and international development opens new prospects... Recently, the annual reports of internet companies for 2025 have entered a period of intensive disclosure, and the performance of major internet companies such as Tencent, Alibaba, Baidu, JD.com, and Pinduoduo has attracted much attention. The annual reports show that the overall operations of large internet companies in 2025 were stable. Technology breakthroughs, deep cultivation of supply chains, and ecological synergy are increasingly becoming key variables reshaping the competitive landscape. The industry competition has moved from traffic competition to a new stage driven by innovation and competition in the industrial chain. Overall revenue grew steadily Overall, the fundamentals of large internet companies are stable. In terms of revenue, in 2025, JD.com's revenue was 1,309.1 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 13%; Tencent's revenue was 751.77 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 14%; Pinduoduo's revenue was 431.8 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 9.65%; Meituan's revenue was 364.9 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 8%; Baidu's revenue was 129.1 billion yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 3%; Alibaba's revenue in the fourth quarter of 2025 was 284.843 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 2%. In terms of net profit, the performance varied. In 2025, Tencent achieved an operating profit of 280.66 billion yuan under non-IFRS standards, a year-on-year increase of 18%; Pinduoduo's net profit was 99.4 billion yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 11.62%; JD.com's net profit under non-GAAP standards was 27 billion yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 43.5%; Meituan turned from profit to loss, with a net loss of 23.4 billion yuan for the full year; Baidu achieved a net profit attributable to Baidu of 5.589 billion yuan, a year-on-year decrease of 76%; Alibaba's net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders in the fourth quarter of 2025 was 16.322 billion yuan. Inertia in the main business supports growth. Pony Ma, Chairman and CEO of Tencent, said: "We maintained healthy growth in 2025, benefiting from AI technology's improved ad targeting capabilities and player interaction in games, as well as accelerated growth and profitability in cloud business revenue." JD Retail remains the pillar of JD.com Group, with annual retail revenue reaching 1,126.4 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 10.9%. In particular, daily necessities categories showed strong growth momentum. Xu Ran, CEO of JD.com Group, said at a conference call that daily necessities categories have achieved double-digit growth for five consecutive quarters, significantly outperforming the overall market, thanks to the substantial improvement in the company's supply chain capabilities and operational efficiency. Meituan, focusing on the "Retail + Technology" strategy, consolidated its advantages in instant retail and firmly pursued international development, with strong growth in grocery retail and overseas businesses. "In 2025, Meituan demonstrated business resilience in a complex environment," said Chen Shaohui, CFO of Meituan. "We will focus on improving operational efficiency and high-quality growth, increasing investment in technology and ecology, and striving to create more value for ecosystem participants." Li Mingtao, Chief E-commerce Expert at the China International Electronic Commerce Center, believes that overall, large internet companies maintained a stable growth trend in 2025. However, substantial investments by some internet companies in R&D, supply chain layout, and food delivery subsidies have also led to the pain of "increasing revenue but not profit," with a decline in operating profit or even annual losses for some companies. Instant retail competition is fierce In the past year, the instant retail market has been turbulent. Internet companies have either entered the food delivery track with billions in subsidies or increased investment to defend their market share, fiercely competing for order volume and market share. JD.com made a high-profile entry into the food delivery market. In February 2025, JD.com's food delivery service was officially launched, and in one year, it gained over 240 million users and captured over 15% of the food delivery market share. Xu Ran stated that 2025 is the starting year for JD.com's food delivery business, with significant investments made in both operations and R&D. In the long term, food delivery and instant retail are important strategic directions for JD.com. Alibaba's instant retail business has undergone significant adjustments, with the "Ele.me" brand being rebranded as "Taobao Flash Purchase" and more closely integrated with the Taobao app. In the fourth quarter of 2025, Alibaba's instant retail business further expanded its scale, with revenue growing strongly by 56%. Alibaba stated that this was due to improved fulfillment logistics efficiency, better order structure, and high customer retention rates, with continuous improvements in unit economics and average order value. To cope with intense industry competition, Meituan has continued to increase direct subsidies to the catering industry and innovated offerings such as "Brand Satellite Stores" and "Group Meal" to meet consumer demand in collaboration with catering brands. Additionally, through innovative models such as brand flagship lightning warehouses and self-operated front-end warehouses, it has expanded the "30-minute delivery of everything" from catering delivery to various categories such as daily necessities and 3C digital products. In 2025, Meituan maintained a stable market share of over 60% in GTV (Gross Transaction Value). "The intensified competition in the food delivery market, from a positive perspective, offers more choices for consumers and food delivery merchants, and better protection for the rights and interests of merchants and riders. The scenario of 'everything can be delivered' is accelerating its penetration into physical goods, creating new consumption scenarios and incremental consumption," said Li Mingtao. At the same time, continuous "burning money to grab orders" has distorted the market price system, lowered product quality and services, and is detrimental to the healthy development of the industry in the long run, reflected in the significant erosion of profits and increased losses in the companies' annual reports. Recently, the State Administration for Market Regulation revealed that regulatory authorities have conducted on-site investigations at relevant food delivery platforms. Several internet companies have stated at earnings calls that they oppose involution and will tighten subsidies. "Under the strong guidance of regulatory authorities, continuing to compete for users and market share through 'burning money subsidies' is unsustainable. Platforms should shift from subsidy wars and price wars to service wars and value wars based on their own endowments, resource advantages, and user differentiation, promoting the industry towards a healthier and higher-quality direction," said Li Mingtao. Increased investment in AI Upon reviewing the financial reports of internet companies, AI has become a frequently used term, beginning to contribute tangible revenue and profits, and becoming a key driver of performance growth. In 2025, AI has generated substantial benefits in Tencent's core businesses, driving the growth of core businesses to outperform the industry average. The three major segments achieved steady growth in the fourth quarter: value-added services revenue increased by 14% year-on-year to 89.92 billion yuan; marketing services revenue increased by 17% year-on-year to 41.12 billion yuan; and financial technology and enterprise services revenue increased by 8% year-on-year to 60.82 billion yuan. At the same time, Tencent is increasing its investment in AI and exploring new growth opportunities. Its AI product matrix continues to advance: Hunyuan 3.0 will be released in April this year, and "crayfish" series Agents such as WorkBuddy and QClaw are being launched one after another, with increased user activity in AI applications such as Yuanbao, QQ Browser, and Sogou Input Method. "AI is one of our main growth engines," said Daniel Zhang, CEO of Alibaba Group. In the fourth quarter of 2025, Alibaba Cloud's revenue grew strongly by 36%, with AI-related product revenue achieving triple-digit growth for 10 consecutive quarters, and MaaS platform business also showing high-speed growth. In an analyst conference call, Daniel Zhang announced Alibaba Group's AI strategy's commercial goal: to achieve an annual commercialized revenue of over 100 billion US dollars for cloud and AI, including MaaS, in the next five years. Baidu's AI business is also gradually moving from the technology investment stage to the commercial realization stage. In 2025, Baidu's AI business revenue reached 40 billion yuan, of which AI business revenue accounted for 43% of Baidu's general business revenue in the fourth quarter. AI Cloud is showing strong momentum, with Baidu AI Cloud revenue increasing by 34% year-on-year in 2025, AI-native marketing service revenue increasing by 301% year-on-year, and AI application revenue exceeding 10 billion yuan. Meituan continues to increase its investment in AI, with R&D investment reaching 26 billion yuan for the full year, a year-on-year increase of 23%. On the one hand, it is making substantial investments in R&D related to drones, autonomous vehicles, and robots. On the other hand, it is leveraging its years of accumulated service scenario advantages and data advantages to improve user experience through AI technology innovation and help merchants use AI assistants. "The rapid development of AI, especially its widespread penetration among users, will have a disruptive impact on the traffic thinking of internet companies, and the commercial landscape of the internet will undergo significant changes," said Li Mingtao. Major internet companies are increasing their AI investments, striving to build new entry points, new scenarios, new applications, and new ecosystems based on AI as the foundation, rapidly forming a new closed loop of 'AI + Business'." The industry is comprehensively shifting to a new cycle of high-quality competition centered on AI, with efficiency as the fundamental principle, and compliance as the bottom line. (Reporter Li Hualin)

title_en: National Data Bureau: Proposes to explore new transaction models such as tokenized data trading
body_en: April 15th, People's Finance News. The National Data Administration is soliciting public feedback on the "Implementation Plan for Promoting the Construction of High-Quality Industry Datasets (Draft for Comments)". The draft proposes innovating commercial models for high-quality industry datasets. It aims to improve long-term operational mechanisms for datasets, encourage datasets to be listed and traded on data circulation service institutions such as data exchanges, and develop diversified service forms like "subscription models," "marketplace models," and "customization models." This will drive a tiered advancement of commercial models from basic data package sales to Application Programming Interface (API) calls, model-based solutions, and full-stack services. It also explores new trading models such as tokenized transactions, building a quantifiable and priceable dataset value system based on tokens.

title_en: Exploration of the Difficulties and Solutions for "Three-ization" Supervision of Cross-border E-commerce
body_en: The deep integration of digital technology into global value chains has made cross-border e-commerce a significant engine for stabilizing foreign trade and promoting growth. However, its characteristics of being cross-regional, decentralized, and easily concealed pose challenges to traditional tax collection and administration systems based on local management and physical locations. Balancing support for business model innovation with strengthening compliance management is crucial for tax base security, long-term industrial development, and the enhancement of digital economy governance capabilities. The author believes that current cross-border e-commerce tax collection and administration face three main difficulties. First is the "concealment" of taxpayers. Some small and medium-sized cross-border e-commerce businesses, lacking import-export rights or facing unfavorable cost-benefit ratios, often use service providers to "nominally" export and then settle payments through third-party payments, private accounts, or foreign exchange swaps, further severing the link between fund flows and the actual taxpayers. Some service providers, in order to obtain export subsidies, inflate financing performance, or even engage in "bill purchasing and matching" to defraud tax refunds, actively provide "invisible" channels. For example, in 2024, HD Import and Export Trade Company in Quanzhou, Fujian Province, defrauded export tax refunds by purchasing fraudulent customs declarations, involving 1,360 special VAT invoices with a total value of 144 million yuan. The essence of this problem is the failure of the traditional "customs declaration form - taxpayer" correspondence in the new business model, making it difficult to identify the true taxable entity. Second is the "fragmentation" of business structures. To comply with Amazon's platform rules of "one legal entity, one business license, one store," some cross-border e-commerce businesses control multiple shell companies through equity proxy or operational proxy, forming "store matrices" to gain traffic. These shell companies do not participate in actual operations, and there is significant room for manipulation in revenue and cost accounting, posing risks in adjusting taxable income, exploiting tax incentives, and issuing invoices within tax-exempt limits. The lack of transparency in related party information and the difficulty in tracing beneficial owners challenge the tax authorities' ability to conduct penetrative supervision. The underlying contradiction reflected in this problem is that tax collection and administration rely on legal forms such as company law, while the commercial substance has been fragmented by multiple legal entities, and the divergence between form and substance makes traditional collection and administration difficult to apply. Third is the "offshoring" of profit distribution. Some cross-border e-commerce businesses establish "domestic-overseas dual entity" structures, where domestic companies undertake core functions such as R&D and operations and consistently show low profits or losses; overseas companies in low-tax jurisdictions accumulate significant profits through transfer pricing, evading domestic income tax. Research also confirms this, with some "overseas warehouse" businesses reporting export prices on customs declarations that are a low proportion of the actual retail price. In response to the above issues, the author suggests taking the "strengthening the foundation project" of tax and fee collection and administration under digital transformation as a guide, and promoting collaborative governance from three dimensions. First, improve the data exchange mechanism to identify "nominal export" risks. Implement the requirements of the "Announcement of the State Administration of Taxation on Matters Concerning the Prepayment of Corporate Income Tax" (State Administration of Taxation Announcement [2025] No. 17), improve the regular data exchange mechanism between tax, customs, foreign exchange, and market supervision departments, integrate information on orders, logistics, and foreign exchange collection, and deepen the construction of risk identification models for "nominal exports." For enterprises with a sharp increase in export volume in a short period, implement sensitive commodity indicators and temporary blocking measures; for "nominal" enterprises that refuse to pay overdue taxes, implement nationwide customs export interception; and include frequently associated personnel in a joint punishment "blacklist." At the same time, encourage local governments to adjust subsidy policies that are solely export-volume-oriented, formulate compliance standards for cross-border e-commerce, and implement differentiated incentive measures such as precise policy push, accelerated review of export tax refunds, and convenient cross-border fund settlement for cross-border e-commerce enterprises that achieve "real invoice procurement, actual owner customs declaration, public account foreign exchange collection, and compliant operation." Through "data penetration + behavioral constraints + incentive restructuring," promote cross-border e-commerce from passive supervision to active compliance. Second, penetrate complex structures with substantive taxation to solve the regulatory challenges of multi-entity shell companies. Implement the "Regulations on Tax Information Reporting by Internet Platform Companies," strengthen the platform's primary responsibility for cross-border e-commerce platforms, and tax authorities may, in accordance with Article 7 of these regulations, require platforms to provide tax-related information such as contracts, transaction details, fund accounts, and logistics of platform operators and practitioners when tax risks are identified, thereby blocking information blind spots of "one control, multiple stores" at the source. Establish a recognition map of shell company matrices, promptly mark shell companies controlled through equity proxy, operational proxy agreements, etc., to prevent tax arbitrage through entity dispersion. Increase the management of the application of tax preferential policies such as for small-scale VAT taxpayers, prevent enterprises from splitting revenue through multiple shell companies to obtain tax benefits, and for enterprises with significant risks, conduct tax assessments and audits in accordance with the law. Third, distribute profits based on value contribution to curb tax base erosion and profit transfer. Implement cross-border tax source monitoring for key cross-border e-commerce businesses, dynamically collect information on group equity structures, value chain distribution, and related-party transactions, increase reminders and self-inspection guidance, and encourage enterprises with large-scale related-party transactions and high compliance levels to lock in profit attribution through advance pricing arrangements; for enterprises with risks of special tax adjustments, explore the use of the profit split method to reasonably divide domestic and foreign contributions, especially to quantify domestic R&D and operational contributions (such as algorithm development, supply chain management, brand operations) separately, ensuring that profit distribution matches value creation. At the same time, fully utilize controlled foreign corporation rules, strengthen the collection and administration practice of treating profits accumulated in low-tax jurisdictions as domestic profits subject to taxation, and maintain tax base security and market fairness. (Author's affiliation: Ningbo Municipal Tax Service, State Administration of Taxation)

title_en: The release ceremony for the group standard "Guidelines for the Construction of Enterprise Supply Chain Control Towers" was held in Haikou.
body_en: The Release Ceremony for the Group Standard "Guidelines for the Construction of Enterprise Supply Chain Control Towers" was Held in Haikou. Release Time: 2026-04-15 11:33:25 China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing Procurement Committee Follow China Federation of Logistics WeChat Qzone Sina Weibo Copy Link On April 15, 2026, the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing held the release ceremony for the group standard "Guidelines for the Construction of Enterprise Supply Chain Control Towers (T/CFLP0092—2026)" at the 2026 Global Procurement and Supply Chain Exchange Conference. The issuance of this standard comes at a critical time when the country is deeply implementing the "Artificial Intelligence Plus" initiative and accelerating the development of a new intelligent economy. It will provide systematic technical support and implementation guidance for various enterprises to build intelligent and integrated supply chain management hubs. Supply chain control towers are intelligent hub systems for integrated supply chain management, built on technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data, the Internet of Things, cloud computing, and digital twins. The newly released "Guidelines for the Construction of Enterprise Supply Chain Control Towers" provide comprehensive and systematic construction guidance from aspects such as construction principles, basic conditions, system architecture, application scenarios, data management, and security management. It is applicable to various enterprises for the planning and construction of supply chain control towers. The standard clarifies five major construction principles: strategic synergy, unified management, scenario-driven, data-driven, and secure and controllable. It proposes a three-layer system architecture design: data layer, capability layer, and application layer. It standardizes core functional modules such as intelligent analysis, intelligent control, intelligent supervision, intelligent prediction, intelligent decision-making, knowledge management, intelligent autonomy, and human-computer interaction. It also provides construction recommendations for data management and security management. This standard was proposed and overseen by the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, and compiled by the Professional Committee of Procurement and Supply Chain Management of the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing. Forty central enterprises, universities, and technology companies, including China Resources Holdings Company Limited, China Minmetals Corporation, Sinochem Holdings Corporation Ltd., China Southern Power Grid Corporation Limited, China Energy Engineering Group Co., Ltd., and Suzhou Institute for Advanced Studies of Artificial Intelligence, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, jointly participated in its drafting, pooling the wisdom and practical experience of various parties in China's supply chain management field. With the increasing complexity of the global supply chain environment, enterprises have an urgent need for supply chain visibility, manageability, controllability, and optimization. As an important means to enhance supply chain resilience and intelligence, supply chain control towers urgently require unified technical and management standards. The release of this standard will provide a scientific and feasible construction path for a wide range of enterprises, promoting the development of China's supply chain management system towards digitalization, intelligence, and standardization. In the next step, the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing will organize standard promotion and training, pilot applications, and implementation to promote the effective implementation of the standard in more industries and enterprises, contributing standard power to the cultivation of a new intelligent economy and the construction of a modern industrial system. title_en: Full cycle, all channels, all fields – multiple departments detail new drug pricing regulations
body_en: Xinhua News Agency, Beijing, April 15th. By Xu Pengcheng and Peng Yunjia, Xinhua News Agency. How drug prices are set is related to the development of the pharmaceutical industry and, more importantly, to the cost of medical treatment and medication for the public. Recently, the General Office of the State Council issued the "Several Opinions on Improving the Drug Price Formation Mechanism," providing a "compass" for drug pricing. On April 15th, the State Council Information Office held a regular press briefing on State Council policies to provide an in-depth interpretation of the drug price formation mechanism. Classified Policies for Drug Prices Throughout the Lifecycle— "Throughout the lifecycle means improving drug pricing policies based on different stages after a drug is launched on the market," said Shi Zihai, deputy director of the National Healthcare Security Administration. The opinions implement classified policies for drug prices throughout their lifecycle, leaving ample room for high-level innovative drugs and encouraging enterprises to continue their research and development efforts. At the same time, they set rules for autonomous pricing for other drugs, guiding enterprises to price fairly and reasonably. Specifically, for newly launched drugs, a drug launch price mechanism will be introduced, differentiating between high-level innovative drugs, improved new drugs, and generic drugs, and providing policy support and guidance. For drugs included in the medical insurance catalog, the guiding role of medical insurance payment standards on drug prices will be leveraged. For drugs with diversified supply, launched for many years, and included in centralized procurement, procurement rules will be optimized based on the characteristics of different types of drugs, and the drug price formation mechanism for centralized procurement will be improved. For routine drugs listed online, the management and dynamic adjustment system for online drug listing prices will be improved. Wang Xiaoning, director of the Department of Pharmaceutical Price and Tender Procurement of the National Healthcare Security Administration, introduced that 199 innovative drugs have been included in the medical insurance drug catalog through negotiations over the past eight years. As of February this year, the medical insurance fund has cumulatively spent 504.8 billion yuan on negotiated drugs within their agreement periods, benefiting 1.17 billion person-times. More Transparent Drug Price Information Through All Channels— Transparent drug price information aims to enable the public to "shop around," understand clearly, and purchase with confidence. The opinions clarify that pharmacies will be guided to set retail prices reasonably, and price comparisons for medical insurance drugs in designated pharmacies will be promoted. The characteristics of online pharmacies, such as transparent information, convenient price comparison, and sufficient competition, will be utilized to conduct regular online and offline price comparisons, identify abnormal prices, and promote fair and reasonable pricing for drugs through different channels. "Drugs in public hospitals are procured through provincial pharmaceutical procurement platforms and sold at zero markup, except for traditional Chinese medicine decoction pieces," said Wang Xiaoning. "It is normal for prices in physical pharmacies and online pharmacies to fluctuate to some extent due to factors such as business models and procurement channels, but these fluctuations must be within a reasonable range." Wang Xiaoning introduced that the retail prices of drugs in designated medical insurance pharmacies should not be significantly higher than those in other channels, nor should there be unfair "yin-yang" pricing for medical insurance and non-medical insurance patients. In addition, various regions have developed mini-programs for designated pharmacies to publicly compare prices, achieving full coverage monitoring of prices in physical pharmacies and making it convenient for the public to find more affordable pharmacies. More Reasonable Drug Prices Across All Sectors— Shi Zihai introduced that the opinions standardize the pricing, supply, and payment of drugs in key areas, making medication more accessible and prices more reasonable for the public. For innovative drugs, emphasis is placed on promoting diversified payment and reasonable price formation, and accelerating the implementation of commercial health insurance innovative drug catalogs. He Yaqiong, director of the Consumer Goods Industry Department of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, introduced that during the "14th Five-Year Plan" period, over 200 innovative drugs and nearly 300 innovative medical devices were approved for market launch. By 2025, the total value of overseas licensing transactions for innovative drugs in China will exceed 130 billion U.S. dollars. "Another 14 innovative drugs have been approved for market launch this year, and China's pharmaceutical innovation continues to maintain good momentum," said Li Jiangning, director of the Drug Registration and Administration Department of the National Medical Products Administration. For drugs in short supply, the focus is on ensuring supply and stabilizing prices, and optimizing the rules for direct online listing of drugs in short supply. "We are closely monitoring joint ventures for the production and supply of small-volume drugs, which has effectively alleviated the tight supply of over 130 clinically essential drugs," said He Yaqiong. Gong Xianguang, director of the Department of Drug Policy and Essential Drug System of the National Health Commission, introduced that China is strengthening the dynamic adjustment and management of the list of drugs in short supply. At the same time, it is conducting studies on the temporary import of 48 drugs, such as defibrotide and gefitinib tablets, which are available overseas but not supplied in China, to ensure urgent clinical treatment needs. In addition, according to the opinions, government-guided prices will be implemented for anesthetic drugs and Class I psychotropic drugs in accordance with the law. For drug excipients and raw materials, measures will be taken to prevent monopolies of raw materials and disorderly price increases for pharmaceutical excipients and packaging materials, and guidance will be strengthened for the prices of traditional Chinese medicine materials. "We have always prioritized combating monopolistic behavior in the pharmaceutical sector and maintained a high-pressure stance," said Yao Lei, director of the Price Supervision and Anti-Unfair Competition Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation. He stated that close attention will be paid to key drugs related to the public's medication rights, such as drugs in short supply, emergency rescue drugs, and commonly used drugs, and that clues will be investigated promptly, cases will be filed quickly, and investigations and punishments will be expedited.

For drugs with diversified supply, launched for many years, and included in centralized procurement, procurement rules will be optimized based on the characteristics of different types of drugs, and the drug price formation mechanism for centralized procurement will be improved. For routine drugs listed online, the management and dynamic adjustment system for online drug listing prices will be improved. Wang Xiaoning, director of the Department of Pharmaceutical Price and Tender Procurement of the National Healthcare Security Administration, introduced that 199 innovative drugs have been included in the medical insurance drug catalog through negotiations over the past eight years. As of February this year, the medical insurance fund has cumulatively spent 504.8 billion yuan on negotiated drugs within their agreement periods, benefiting 1.17 billion person-times. More Transparent Drug Price Information Through All Channels— Transparent drug price information aims to enable the public to "shop around," understand clearly, and purchase with confidence. The opinions clarify that pharmacies will be guided to set retail prices reasonably, and price comparisons for medical insurance drugs in designated pharmacies will be promoted. The characteristics of online pharmacies, such as transparent information, convenient price comparison, and sufficient competition, will be utilized to conduct regular online and offline price comparisons, identify abnormal prices, and promote fair and reasonable pricing for drugs through different channels. "Drugs in public hospitals are procured through provincial pharmaceutical procurement platforms and sold at zero markup, except for traditional Chinese medicine decoction pieces," said Wang Xiaoning. "It is normal for prices in physical pharmacies and online pharmacies to fluctuate to some extent due to factors such as business models and procurement channels, but these fluctuations must be within a reasonable range." Wang Xiaoning introduced that the retail prices of drugs in designated medical insurance pharmacies should not be significantly higher than those in other channels, nor should there be unfair "yin-yang" pricing for medical insurance and non-medical insurance patients. In addition, various regions have developed mini-programs for designated pharmacies to publicly compare prices, achieving full coverage monitoring of prices in physical pharmacies and making it convenient for the public to find more affordable pharmacies. More Reasonable Drug Prices Across All Sectors— Shi Zihai introduced that the opinions standardize the pricing, supply, and payment of drugs in key areas, making medication more accessible and prices more reasonable for the public. For innovative drugs, emphasis is placed on promoting diversified payment and reasonable price formation, and accelerating the implementation of commercial health insurance innovative drug catalogs. He Yaqiong, director of the Consumer Goods Industry Department of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, introduced that during the "14th Five-Year Plan" period, over 200 innovative drugs and nearly 300 innovative medical devices were approved for market launch. By 2025, the total value of overseas licensing transactions for innovative drugs in China will exceed 130 billion U.S. dollars. "Another 14 innovative drugs have been approved for market launch this year, and China's pharmaceutical innovation continues to maintain good momentum," said Li Jiangning, director of the Drug Registration and Administration Department of the National Medical Products Administration. For drugs in short supply, the focus is on ensuring supply and stabilizing prices, and optimizing the rules for direct online listing of drugs in short supply. "We are closely monitoring joint ventures for the production and supply of small-volume drugs, which has effectively alleviated the tight supply of over 130 clinically essential drugs," said He Yaqiong. Gong Xianguang, director of the Department of Drug Policy and Essential Drug System of the National Health Commission, introduced that China is strengthening the dynamic adjustment and management of the list of drugs in short supply. At the same time, it is conducting studies on the temporary import of 48 drugs, such as defibrotide and gefitinib tablets, which are available overseas but not supplied in China, to ensure urgent clinical treatment needs. In addition, according to the opinions, government-guided prices will be implemented for anesthetic drugs and Class I psychotropic drugs in accordance with the law. For drug excipients and raw materials, measures will be taken to prevent monopolies of raw materials and disorderly price increases for pharmaceutical excipients and packaging materials, and guidance will be strengthened for the prices of traditional Chinese medicine materials. "We have always prioritized combating monopolistic behavior in the pharmaceutical sector and maintained a high-pressure stance," said Yao Lei, director of the Price Supervision and Anti-Unfair Competition Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation. He stated that close attention will be paid to key drugs related to the public's medication rights, such as drugs in short supply, emergency rescue drugs, and commonly used drugs, and that clues will be investigated promptly, cases will be filed quickly, and investigations and punishments will be expedited.
