title_en: Unleashing New Vitality in the Smart Economy by Rooting in the Real Economy
body_en: Like a surge, the core term "token" in the AI field has recently swept across the internet. By March of this year, China's daily token calls exceeded 140 trillion, a 40% increase from the end of 2025. Behind this lies the rapid growth phase of China's artificial intelligence development; it further indicates that only by being rooted in the real economy and responding to people's needs can the intelligent economy unleash new vitality. Recently, the accelerated implementation of intelligent agent applications, such as "lobster farming," has enabled AI to move from conversational interaction to autonomously executing tasks, driving explosive growth in token demand. From domestic large models like Doubao continuously refreshing their capabilities, to intelligent agents empowering factory production scenarios, and solo businesses receiving a continuous stream of overseas orders, China's artificial intelligence industry is striding forward in areas such as tackling large model research and development and implementing intelligent agent applications, making the intelligent economy a new blue ocean for digital economy growth. In the opening year of the "15th Five-Year Plan," "creating a new form of intelligent economy" and "intelligent agents" were written into the government work report for the first time. As concepts like computing power and tokens become more widespread with the popularization of AI applications, the artificial intelligence industry and the development of the intelligent economy are ushering in broader application scenarios and market opportunities. As a key variable influencing future development, the development of artificial intelligence must aim for industrial application, take practical measures to promote cross-industry integration and transformation and upgrading, and create more tangible value. The explosion in computing power demand is driving the accelerated upgrading of cloud services and domestic semiconductor industries; the continuous prosperity of the ecosystem is leading to numerous new software applications covering office, finance, industry, and other scenarios; applications are blooming in multiple areas, achieving leaps in efficiency in government services, enterprise management, and personal productivity. Artificial intelligence is continuously "adding" potential to the development of traditional industries, stimulating innovation in emerging and future industries. The intelligent economy has a wide coverage and a long empowerment chain. When artificial intelligence is deeply integrated with the real economy, its rich data resources, diverse application scenarios, and massive user base will be transformed into unique advantages and powerful momentum for China to build a modern industrial system and achieve high-quality development. Better benefiting people is the fundamental purpose of the development of the intelligent economy. From "technological leadership" to "usable by everyone," making intelligent services readily accessible and benefiting thousands of households is the original intention and ultimate goal of the intelligent economy's development. Adhering to "people-centered and intelligent for good," accelerating intelligent applications in production and life, especially in areas such as elder care, childcare, and assistance for the disabled, will continuously meet people's needs for a better life and enhance their sense of gain, happiness, and security. (Xinhua News Agency, Beijing, April 15)

title_en: 21 Interview | Lu Chuncong, President of the China Academy of Industrial Internet: Promoting Industrial Intelligent Applications, "Seven Parts in Data, Three Parts in Models"
body_en: Since the beginning of this year, the intelligent economy has become a hot topic of development. In early March, the 2026 Government Work Report for the first time proposed to build a new form of intelligent economy and deepen and expand "Artificial Intelligence+". Subsequently, the "Fifteenth Five-Year Plan" Outline, which was fully released, also made it clear to cultivate new intelligent-native models and new business formats, and comprehensively implement the "Artificial Intelligence+" action. How to understand the intelligent economy? What role will manufacturing play in it? With the continuous emergence of new intelligent economy models and new business formats, what are the key points worth paying attention to in the future of "Artificial Intelligence + Manufacturing"? Regarding the above topics, a reporter from 21st Century Business Herald recently interviewed Lu Chuncong, president of the China Industrial Internet Research Institute. In his view, manufacturing is the main battlefield of the intelligent economy, and promoting industrial intelligent applications is "70% in data, 30% in models." Faced with the characteristics of industrial data being diverse and heterogeneous, multi-level distribution, and deep coupling, systematic solutions of "1 set of intelligent infrastructure + 3 types of high-quality datasets" can be explored. At the same time, Lu Chuncong emphasized that industrial large models and intelligent agents play a role in a hierarchical and integrated collaborative manner. They are reshaping every link from equipment to the industrial ecosystem. Promoting "AI + Manufacturing" must not be a "one-size-fits-all" approach, and must adhere to "promoting by industry and promoting by level." Lu Chuncong. Photo courtesy of the source "21st Century": What role will manufacturing play in the intelligent economy? In the context of the continuous promotion of the "AI + Manufacturing" action, how to understand the synergistic relationship between "intelligent industrialization" and "industrial intelligentization"? Lu Chuncong: Manufacturing is the foundation of a country and the basis of a strong nation, and it is also the main battlefield of the intelligent economy. In 2025, China's manufacturing added value will reach 34.7 trillion yuan, maintaining the global first for 16 consecutive years. China has more than 6 million manufacturing enterprises and the world's most complete and comprehensive industrial system, which constitutes the most valuable "full-scenario" application soil for artificial intelligence technology and a vast "blue ocean" for digital and intelligent transformation. Regarding the synergistic relationship between "intelligent industrialization" and "industrial intelligentization," I believe it is a two-way embrace. We promote "AI + Manufacturing," which is to use artificial intelligence technology to transform manufacturing in an all-round, whole-chain manner. 80% of China's manufacturing belongs to traditional industries, which have urgent needs for cost reduction, quality improvement, efficiency enhancement, green development, and safety. This process, also known as "industrial intelligentization," provides AI technology with the most valuable real-world data and complex industrial scenarios that no web crawler or synthetic data can replicate. Second, "emphasize security." Many enterprises worry about data leakage. In terms of technical routes, the principle of "data physically not leaving the domain" should be strictly adhered to, and privacy computing technologies such as edge computing and federated learning should be adopted. Raw data should not be uploaded to the cloud to effectively protect commercial secrets. Third, "calculate for the long term." Evaluating ROI (Return on Investment) should not only consider short-term hardware and software procurement costs but also the improvement in yield, reduction in energy consumption, shortening of R&D cycles brought about by AI, as well as the "resilience" and "response speed" of the supply chain when facing market fluctuations. Zhejiang has nurtured a large number of digital and intelligent transformation service providers (data merchants) who understand industry, algorithms, and data. As "industry problem solvers," they are closely integrated with manufacturing enterprises as "industry problem setters," forming a highly dynamic collaborative innovation ecosystem of supply and demand. Second, it deeply binds "hardcore scenarios" with "data assets." Zhejiang enterprises are very pragmatic. They not only deploy industrial intelligent applications on a large scale in workshops but also take the lead in exploring the registration, evaluation, and entry into the books of industrial data assets. They have truly transformed massive production scenarios into high-quality datasets, turning data elements from "sleeping resources" into "core assets." title_en: Token Boom: AI Computing Power Prices Rise Across the Chain, Ushering in an Era of "Energy Efficiency Competition"
body_en: Computing power is becoming the most scarce "hard currency" in the AI era, with prices across the entire chain continuously rising. The annual lease price of overseas Nvidia H100 has increased by nearly 40%; domestic cloud vendors have collectively adjusted prices – Tencent Cloud's Tencent HY 2.0 Instruct model input price increased by 463% and then by another 5% overall, Alibaba Cloud's Pingtouge Zhenwu 810E and other computing power card products have increased by 5% to 34%, Baidu AI Cloud related services have increased by 5% to 30%, iFlytek's Smart Computing Platform AI inference service has increased by 8%, SenseTime's SenseCore large model training costs have increased by an average of 12%, and Zhipu has raised prices 3 times since February... Recently, computing power products across the entire chain have seen price increases, marking a sharp reversal of the AI "price war" that has lasted for more than two years. Is this a cyclical fluctuation due to short-term supply-demand mismatch, or a trend-driven increase driven by AI? Where will the future focus of industry competition lie? Recently, reporters interviewed Pan Helin, a member of the Expert Committee of the Information and Communication Economic Commission of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and Guo Liang, Chief Engineer of the Cloud Computing and Digitalization Research Institute of the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, to deeply explore the industry transformation trends behind the surge in computing power prices. The surge in Tokens is the "core engine" of the computing power price hike. "The root cause of the price increase is the demand-driven nature of artificial intelligence," Pan Helin believes. This includes both the computing power consumption brought about by AI training and the demand for inference computing power stimulated by the explosion of AI applications. Guo Liang analyzes that the price increase includes four factors: First, the "reverse" surge in hardware costs. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) storage and high-end chips are in an absolute seller's market, with storage prices doubling in the first quarter of 2026, leading to high hardware procurement and operation and maintenance costs. Second, the demand structure has shifted from training to inference. With the explosion of AI agents, the number of Token calls in the inference stage has surged. Inference is a continuous operational expenditure, and the electricity and bandwidth costs brought about by massive concurrency have exceeded the subsidy limits of cloud vendors. Third, the business model has shifted from "land grabbing" to "profitability." The early computing power price war has completed initial ecosystem binding, and under financial pressure, vendors must increase prices to cover expensive computing power depreciation. Fourth, the strategic scarcity of computing power resources. Global high-end computing power leasing capacity is in short supply, and electricity quotas are tight, leading to extreme supply-demand imbalance, leaving no room for price decreases. For more than two years, cloud vendors have continuously lowered prices with the logic of "burning money for market share," compressing Token costs to less than one yuan per million Tokens. However, currently, complex inference can lead to daily call costs of hundreds of yuan, and prices are continuously rising. The free public beta of large models has also ended simultaneously. "The collective price increase in the industry is an inevitable result of shifting from 'burning money to expand scale' to 'commercial sustainability'," Guo Liang stated. This marks the end of the era of cheap computing power and the entry into a stage of "value revaluation" oriented towards profit. Regarding price competition, Pan Helin believes that cloud computing vendors have not yet discovered AI application scenarios with large-scale user stickiness. Most vendors' purchased computing power servers are mainly used for AI model training, rather than directly providing computing power services to enterprise or individual users. Since the beginning of this year, open-source AI works such as "Lobster Hot" and "Happy Horse" have emerged. Their innovation and ease of use have greatly stimulated ordinary users' enthusiasm for cloud computing products, not only significantly promoting the explosive growth of Token sales but also further driving the overall demand for computing power resources and storage services. Storage and chips are the "cost drivers" of the computing power price increase. Currently, the price increase trend in the computing power industry chain has spread from upstream hardware to downstream services. Dozens of companies, including major domestic and international cloud vendors, have successively increased prices for AI computing power and related services. So, in the computing power industry chain, which links are the root cause of the price increase? Guo Liang believes that "from the perspective of the computing power industry chain structure, storage supply, advanced packaging, chip manufacturing, and wafer production have all contributed to the increase in computing power prices." Specifically, in terms of storage supply, especially for HBM and high-capacity flash memory, as model parameter scales continue to expand and multimodal interaction becomes increasingly popular, inference tasks require memory bandwidth that surpasses the demand for computing power itself. For example, the HBM production capacity of manufacturers like Samsung and SK Hynix has been locked in by long-term orders before the first quarter of 2026. In advanced packaging technologies such as CoWoS, although wafer manufacturing capacity is expanding, the expansion cycle of advanced packaging processes that integrate computing chips with HBM is long and the technical threshold is high. Even if wafer supply is sufficient, if packaging and shipment cannot be completed, computing power resources in the market will remain in short supply. In the wafer production stage, compared to storage and packaging, although advanced process wafer capacity is also tight, its release rhythm is relatively predictable with the large-scale expansion of major global foundries, and it is no longer the main driver of current price fluctuations. "The price increase is mainly concentrated in two links," Pan Helin analyzed. "First, the price increase of computing power servers themselves, such as AI computing power servers from manufacturers like Nvidia. Second, the price increase of computing power and storage leasing services provided by cloud computing vendors." Among these, the price increase of computing power servers is mainly due to two factors: on the one hand, chip manufacturing capacity is limited, with the core bottleneck being that lithography machine capacity cannot meet the rapid development needs of the AI industry. On the other hand, there is a shortage of storage chips. Memory chips themselves have inherent production cycles, and the explosive growth of AI demand has further exacerbated the supply-demand imbalance. The expansion of storage chip production capacity usually takes about 3 years. Even considering that manufacturers have made advance arrangements, it will take at least 1-2 years to effectively alleviate the supply pressure. The surge in computing power prices is a stress test that accelerates industrial consolidation. "This round of price increases is a 'stress test'," Guo Liang vividly described. It will accelerate industrial consolidation, moving away from a period of extensive development towards a "deep water zone" of high-threshold, high-efficiency Token production and usage. This round of computing power price increases is profoundly reshaping the competitive landscape of the entire AI industry chain, with different impacts on leading manufacturers and small and medium-sized enterprises. For leading manufacturers, Guo Liang believes that the price increase will help restore profits and ecosystems. On the one hand, price increases alleviate the huge computing power depreciation pressure on cloud vendors, shifting them from "acquiring customers at a loss" to "quality growth." On the other hand, leading manufacturers, with their cost advantages from self-developed chips, may further squeeze the survival space of second-tier cloud service providers and strengthen their control over the computing power ecosystem. For small and medium-sized enterprises, Pan Helin analyzed, "The increase in computing power prices will significantly increase the cost of using AI for small and medium-sized enterprises and individual users." Currently, most small and medium-sized enterprises rely on purchasing computing power and storage resources in the cloud to complete model training and provide computing power support for AI applications. If AI can generate more value and create more profits, small and medium-sized enterprises are likely to choose to ignore the short-term cost increase and opt for an "AI+" strategy to improve operational efficiency and market competitiveness. Guo Liang summarized, "The high-quality development of the computing power industry will accelerate the shift from 'virtual to real'." High computing power costs will gradually erode the soil for "PPT startups." The industry's investment focus will shift from pure model research and development to commercialized scenarios that generate actual revenue and have a higher return on investment in computing power. "Computing Power Banks" and "Computing Power Supermarkets" will alleviate the burden for small and medium-sized enterprises. In response to the tight supply and demand for computing power, policy measures have accelerated breakthroughs. In April of this year, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued the "Notice on Carrying out Special Actions for Inclusive Computing Power Empowerment of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises," introducing two innovative models, "Computing Power Bank" and "Computing Power Supermarket," to directly address the pain points of computing power costs for small and medium-sized enterprises. Guo Liang stated, "The special action is a 'burden reduction' plan tailored for small and medium-sized enterprises to address the surge in AI computing power costs in 2026. The key lies in the effective implementation of these two innovative businesses." "Computing Power Bank" is similar to a financial bank model, which resourceizes, standardizes, and financializes scattered idle computing power resources, achieving inclusive supply through "lump-sum deposits and withdrawals" and cross-regional scheduling. Specifically, it involves four steps: First, resource aggregation (deposits), standardizing computing power of different brands and specifications into "standard computing power units," and connecting surplus computing power from research institutions, cloud vendors, and enterprises to the China Computing Power Platform, similar to absorbing deposits. Second, resource pooling (vault), using the platform to integrate scattered servers into a virtual resource pool, enabling cross-regional scheduling and balancing peak and off-peak loads, solving the problem of "some places being stuck and some places being idle." Third, on-demand allocation (loans), enterprises place orders as needed, like applying for loans. Small and medium-sized enterprises can obtain high-performance computing power at low costs through flexible packages such as "computing power coupons" or pay-as-you-go. Fourth, value settlement (clearing), establishing a metering and rebate mechanism, where providers receive revenue or future priority usage rights, users pay based on actual usage, and the government achieves precise subsidies through platform data. "A self-driving startup needs a large amount of computing power to process road test data, while a university laboratory's computing power is idle at night. Through the Computing Power Bank, the laboratory deposits its computing power to obtain future credits; the startup uses government-issued 'computing power coupons' to extract computing power at a low price, avoiding the peak prices of public clouds," Guo Liang explained with an example. The core of "Computing Power Supermarket" is the "commoditization" and "convenience" of computing power resources, allowing enterprises to obtain AI computing power like online shopping. This includes four key aspects: First, standardized resource listing, converting underlying hardware performance into standardized products, calculated by computing power specifications such as Token count, single-precision floating-point operations, and core-hour billing, eliminating technical barriers. Second, intelligent search and price comparison, based on the special zone for small and medium-sized enterprises on the China Computing Power Platform, enabling dynamic price comparison and computing power selection, automatically recommending low-cost, low-latency computing power packages, and solving problems such as information asymmetry. Third, out-of-the-box services, pre-installing model environments and development tools, allowing users to deploy mainstream large model images and datasets with one click, achieving "order and run," and shortening the development cycle. Fourth, inclusive policies and payment settlement, connecting with government subsidies, supporting direct settlement of "computing power coupons," and providing modes such as prepaid, postpaid, and annual/monthly packages. The platform undertakes QoS monitoring to ensure real performance. "If the Computing Power Bank is responsible for the underlying 'resource flow' and solves the problem of 'resource flow'; then the Computing Power Supermarket is responsible for the front-end 'user experience' and solves the problem of 'transaction threshold,' making computing power visible, affordable, and easy to use," Guo Liang believes. These two innovative businesses transform computing power from a high-threshold "capital-intensive asset" into an "on-demand information infrastructure" like water and electricity, which is crucial for small and medium-sized enterprises to break through in the 2026 computing power competition. The surge in Tokens is the "core engine" of the computing power price hike. "The root cause of the price increase is the demand-driven nature of artificial intelligence," Pan Helin believes. This includes both the computing power consumption brought about by AI training and the demand for inference computing power stimulated by the explosion of AI applications. Guo Liang analyzes that the price increase includes four factors: First, the "reverse" surge in hardware costs. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) storage and high-end chips are in an absolute seller's market, with storage prices doubling in the first quarter of 2026, leading to high hardware procurement and operation and maintenance costs. Second, the demand structure has shifted from training to inference. With the explosion of AI agents, the number of Token calls in the inference stage has surged. Inference is a continuous operational expenditure, and the electricity and bandwidth costs brought about by massive concurrency have exceeded the subsidy limits of cloud vendors. Third, the business model has shifted from "land grabbing" to "profitability." The early computing power price war has completed initial ecosystem binding, and under financial pressure, vendors must increase prices to cover expensive computing power depreciation. Fourth, the strategic scarcity of computing power resources. Global high-end computing power leasing capacity is in short supply, and electricity quotas are tight, leading to extreme supply-demand imbalance, leaving no room for price decreases. For more than two years, cloud vendors have continuously lowered prices with the logic of "burning money for market share," compressing Token costs to less than one yuan per million Tokens. However, currently, complex inference can lead to daily call costs of hundreds of yuan, and prices are continuously rising. The free public beta of large models has also ended simultaneously. "The collective price increase in the industry is an inevitable result of shifting from 'burning money to expand scale' to 'commercial sustainability'," Guo Liang stated. This marks the end of the era of cheap computing power and the entry into a stage of "value revaluation" oriented towards profit. The expansion of storage chip production capacity usually takes about 3 years. For small and medium-sized enterprises, Pan Helin analyzed, "The increase in computing power prices will significantly increase the cost of using AI for small and medium-sized enterprises and individual users." title_en: Six departments jointly issue document to promote e-commerce to serve the real economy
body_en: Report from this newspaper (Reporter Yuan Zan) Recently, six departments including the Ministry of Commerce, the Cyberspace Administration of China, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and the State Administration for Market Regulation jointly issued the "Guiding Opinions on Better Serving the Real Economy and Promoting High-Quality Development of E-commerce" (hereinafter referred to as the "Opinions"). The "Opinions" propose a series of practical measures focusing on empowering and increasing efficiency, innovation-driven development, high-level opening up, and creating a favorable ecosystem, aiming to promote e-commerce from "scale expansion" to "quality and efficiency improvement" and better serve the consolidation and growth of the real economy. Addressing the pain points of high costs and weak capabilities faced by small and medium-sized enterprises in digital transformation, the "Opinions" propose to deepen the implementation of a special action for digital empowerment of small and medium-sized enterprises, guide e-commerce enterprises to launch "small, fast, light, and precise" digital products and solutions, and open up data, channels, and technology resources to small and medium-sized enterprises and individual businesses, providing support for enterprise store location selection, new product development, and inventory management, helping small and medium-sized enterprises to operate with less burden. In the field of rural e-commerce, the "Opinions" deploy the implementation of a high-quality development project for rural e-commerce, promote models such as direct procurement by e-commerce and customized production, develop characteristic live streaming such as "village broadcasting" and "field broadcasting," improve the rural express logistics network, build "local good products" brands, and activate the consumption potential of counties. To better meet the people's demand for high-quality consumption, the "Opinions" propose to implement the "Quality E-commerce Cultivation Action," promote e-commerce platforms to optimize mechanisms such as traffic allocation and search ranking, increase the weight of indicators such as product quality and service reputation, and cultivate quality merchants and excellent brands. At the same time, e-commerce platforms are encouraged to jointly release lists such as "Gourmet Maps" and "Must-Eat and Must-Buy" with brand merchants, accelerate the online promotion of "time-honored brands" and other trendy domestic products, and build a contingent of famous Chinese consumer brands. In terms of technological innovation, the "Opinions" clarify the development of "Artificial Intelligence + E-commerce," guide e-commerce enterprises to strengthen research and development and application of technologies such as large AI models, optimize consumer experience, and reduce operating costs. At the same time, it emphasizes "technology for good," requiring the coordination of interests of all parties, optimization of algorithm rules, strengthening of judicial protection of technological achievements in the e-commerce field, exploration of rules such as evidence disclosure and obstruction of evidence, and appropriate reduction of the burden of proof for rights holders. Creating a fair and orderly e-commerce ecosystem. Regarding the key aspect of e-commerce regulation, the "Opinions" emphasize "creating a favorable ecosystem and promoting win-win development for all parties" with a large proportion of content. It specifically proposes to promote win-win development between e-commerce platforms and platform operators and laborers, urge platform operators that meet the conditions to register their business entities in accordance with the law, and improve intellectual property protection and regular communication mechanisms with laborers. Regarding platform fees, the "Opinions" propose to guide e-commerce platforms to standardize and optimize their charging behaviors towards platform operators, encourage reasonable fee reductions for newly settled small and micro enterprises and individual businesses, and promote e-commerce platforms to establish and improve complaint and relief mechanisms for the rights and interests of small and medium-sized merchants. In terms of strengthening normalized supervision, the "Opinions" propose to strengthen pre-regulation and guidance by comprehensively using compliance cases, risk warnings, and business guidelines, and to study and formulate guidelines for the compliant development of live e-commerce. The proportion of random inspections of online sales products will be increased, and the mechanism for quality supervision, random inspection, and punishment of online sales products will be improved. At the same time, the supervision and enforcement of monopolistic agreements and abuse of market dominant position in the e-commerce field will be strengthened, "involutionary" competition will be rectified, and a fair competition market order will be maintained. In terms of promoting high-level opening up, the "Opinions" focus on the development of cross-border e-commerce and the expansion of "Silk Road E-commerce." It proposes to promote the high-quality development of cross-border e-commerce comprehensive pilot zones, develop models such as "market procurement + cross-border e-commerce" and "China Railway Express + cross-border e-commerce," and vigorously support overseas warehouses for cross-border e-commerce. At the same time, it will continue to expand the "Silk Road E-commerce" circle of friends, cultivate a number of key cooperation cities, and tell the story of "Silk Road E-commerce." The "Opinions" also clarify the acceleration of institutional opening up, promote the selective expansion of "Silk Road E-commerce" cooperation pilot zones, form a batch of replicable and promotable institutional opening-up achievements in areas such as trade facilitation, international data services, and cross-border RMB settlement, and actively promote accession to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) and the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA). To ensure the effective implementation of various measures, the "Opinions" strengthen support from financial, data, and talent aspects. Financial institutions are encouraged to innovate credit products and services in conjunction with the financing needs of e-commerce enterprises, and support eligible e-commerce enterprises in issuing bonds and financing through listing at home and abroad. The mechanism for cross-border data flow will be improved, and cross-border e-commerce data resources will be integrated and shared among relevant departments. Higher education institutions and vocational schools are supported to deepen industry-education integration and vocational-general education integration, jointly cultivate talents with e-commerce enterprises, and carry out targeted and position-specific training.

title_en: Seven e-commerce platforms express sincere acceptance of the penalties from the State Administration for Market Regulation and are determined to implement food safety responsibilities.

title_en: A cake order leads to a huge fine
body_en: On April 17th, the State Administration for Market Regulation lawfully imposed a hefty fine of 3.597 billion yuan on seven e-commerce platforms, including Pinduoduo, Meituan, JD.com, Ele.me (Taobao Flash Purchase), Douyin, Taobao, and Tmall. Additionally, fines totaling 19.6874 million yuan were levied on the legal representatives and food safety directors of these seven platforms, severely punishing them for condoning "ghost takeout" practices. "Xinhua Viewpoint" reporters tracked the entire process, exposing the operational truth behind "ghost takeout" and examining the public welfare considerations behind the stringent regulatory crackdown. **Tearing Down the Curtain: A Cake Uncovers the "Ghost Takeout" Trap** A consumer complaint unexpectedly unearthed astonishing deceit within the cake delivery industry. In July 2025, the Haidian District Market Supervision Bureau in Beijing received a report alleging that a birthday cake purchased from the "Sweet Whisper Cake" store on a certain platform had fresh flowers directly inserted into it, raising suspicions of food safety issues. Upon receiving the report, law enforcement officers immediately launched an investigation. Browsing online, the store's presentation was exceptionally impressive: it claimed to have 378 chain stores, with over ten thousand orders per month, featuring exquisite real-life photos of cakes and neatly displayed food business permits. It appeared to be a legitimate and reliable brand store. However, after law enforcement officers verified over 20 stores in the Beijing area one by one, they discovered that none of the stores in Beijing had physical locations, and their business permit numbers were all forged. In August 2025, after an initial assessment of the case, the State Administration for Market Regulation decided to escalate the investigation. A task force of over 200 enforcement elites was assembled nationwide to conduct the first round of on-site inspections of e-commerce platforms. As the investigation deepened, the truth was gradually revealed. Law enforcement officers tracked the entire order flow and discovered that orders placed on platform stores were ultimately shipped from a dilapidated residential building. This brought the order transfer platforms to light. Taking a 6-inch high-end cream cake order, for which the consumer paid 252.3 yuan, as an example, after the e-commerce platform received the order, the "ghost store" listed it for sale on the "Zhuan Dan Bao" platform. Three receiving stores bid 100 yuan, 90 yuan, and 80 yuan, respectively, with the lowest bidder winning. In this process, the "ghost store" earned 121.9 yuan, and the e-commerce platform collected a service fee of 50.4 yuan. The store that actually made the cake accepted the order for 80 yuan, paid a 3.2 yuan service fee to Zhuan Dan Bao, and received 76.8 yuan after including self-arranged delivery costs. Reporters learned that the cost of a 6-inch cream cake made with good ingredients is approximately 60 yuan. Behind the bills, the e-commerce platforms and "ghost stores" reaped profits, while the operators who actually provided the cakes could only obtain meager profits. According to the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Food Safety for Online Catering Services," online catering service providers are prohibited from processing and producing food outside their processing and operation areas and are not allowed to entrust order processing to other food business operators. The investigated e-commerce platforms, despite knowing these regulations, signed data-sharing agreements with order transfer platforms, assisting in the transfer of orders by online stores and condoning the spread of "ghost takeout" practices. Shi Jianzhong, a professor at China University of Political Science and Law, believes that while order transfer itself is not illegal as a business model, its involvement with "ghost stores" turns it into a channel for evading food safety supervision. Following the leads, the task force discovered two major order transfer platforms, Chongqing Zhuan Dan Bao and Anhui Xunmeng, which cumulatively handled over 3.6 million illegally subcontracted cake orders. These involved seven e-commerce platforms: Pinduoduo, Meituan, JD.com, Ele.me (Taobao Flash Purchase), Douyin, Taobao, and Tmall, uncovering more than 67,000 "ghost stores." "This discovery is by no means a minor violation, but a new type of illegal model, a widespread chaos that is industrialized and scaled," stated Han Bing, director of the Fourth Inspection Division of the Enforcement Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation. Consumers are paying high prices for low-quality food, their right to know is being deprived, and the defense line for online catering safety is being riddled with holes by these 'ghosts'." **Undermining Supervision: Platform Negligence Creates Food Safety Hazards** Why could fake certificates and licenses be uploaded in bulk? Why was platform review perfunctory? As the investigation deepened, more hidden truths emerged: some leading platforms turned a blind eye to violations, condoning the proliferation of fake documents. The task force found that the operation of fake document syndicates was like an assembly line, with interconnected steps and division of labor. The upstream of the industry chain was responsible for obtaining the "materials"—the original copies of ID cards and business licenses required for online store registration. They either directly "photoshopped" real licenses by altering names and addresses or purchased realistic fake materials for thirty to forty yuan, including photos of individuals holding their ID cards, to pass the review. The intermediate technical processors were well-versed in platform rules and acted as "beauticians" for fake materials. They were aware of the key review points and loopholes. If materials were rejected, they would modify details according to the feedback until they were approved, earning 5 yuan per order. The downstream consisted of "guaranteed approval" runners who offered "one-stop" services, charging eighty to ninety yuan for registration, image uploading, and supervision of the review process. If a fake store was shut down, they could relist it for 30 yuan. Some individuals used them to register over 570 fake stores. The negligence and dereliction of duty by the investigated e-commerce platforms allowed fake certificates and licenses to pass through unimpeded. Intermediaries and platform reviewers colluded in secret, fostering a set of industry unwritten rules. "If fake documents were blocked by the system, the reviewer would inform the intermediary about 'incorrect seal color' or 'unfindable enterprise code.' The intermediary would then tell the fake document maker to make changes. This process of 'rejection, modification, and resubmission,' with insiders teaching outsiders, effectively turned fake into real," explained a member of the task force. Some platform staff argued, "If we were too strict with reviews, the stores would go to other platforms." Lou Sihan, an official from the Fourth Inspection Division of the Enforcement Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation, stated that some platforms, in their pursuit of market share, turned a blind eye to and condoned obviously fake documents and licenses. They even signed data-sharing agreements with order transfer platforms and opened interfaces to support one-click order transfers. The investigation process was not easy. Some platforms deliberately delayed or refused to cooperate under the pretext of "system upgrades" or "data confidentiality." Others provided fragmented or garbled data in an attempt to conceal the facts. Even more egregious, some resorted to outright violent resistance to the law—an enforcement officer on the Pinduoduo task force suffered a fractured left index finger and a sprained right ankle due to platform employees intentionally closing a door. Faced with massive data barriers and encrypted core information erected by the platforms, the task force studied platform algorithms and built data models to penetrate the technical blockade, gathering evidence of order flow, qualification filings, and order transfer transactions. **Thunderous Penalties: Guiding the Healthy Development of the Platform Economy** This case involved multiple platforms, a high amount of fines, and complex legal applications, presenting a new challenge in food safety supervision within the platform economy. To ensure accurate determination of facts, lawful procedures, and fair penalties, the State Administration for Market Regulation conducted thorough research, clarified legal applications, evidence standards, and penalty scales. After multiple rounds of deliberation and repeated discussions with legal experts and judicial personnel, a consensus was reached. The penalty decision issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation clearly stated that Pinduoduo, Meituan, JD.com, Ele.me (Taobao Flash Purchase), Douyin, Taobao, and Tmall were suspected of failing to fulfill their legal obligations for qualification review and did not take necessary measures against platform operators infringing upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests, thus violating the Food Safety Law, the E-commerce Law, and the Consumer Rights Protection Law. Order transfer platforms such as Zhuan Dan Bao and Anhui Xunmeng were suspected of failing to fulfill their legal obligations for qualification review, failing to obtain platform备案 (filing) according to law, and providing technical support for illegal order transfers. "Ghost stores" were suspected of illegal order transfers, using false credentials, and forging food business permits. Reporters learned that the regulatory authorities' penalties were imposed on a "one store, one penalty, cumulative calculation" basis, with each "ghost store" and each instance of review negligence being penalized individually. This ultimately resulted in the largest fine in the food safety sector since the revision of the Food Safety Law in 2015. "Platform qualification review is the first line of defense for food safety. If this line collapses, the entire regulatory system becomes ineffective. This 'one store, one penalty' approach is of milestone significance, forcing platforms to shift from 'formal review' to 'substantive review' and truly assume their primary responsibility," said Xue Jun, a professor at Peking University Law School. In Shi Jianzhong's view, this series of "ghost takeout" cases is a landmark case for regulatory authorities to strengthen online food safety supervision and standardize platform development, and it will provide a reference for the adjudication of similar cases in the future. Reporters learned that after the investigation was initiated, the State Administration for Market Regulation immediately ordered the e-commerce platforms to rectify the situation. Currently, all seven e-commerce platforms have removed the relevant "ghost stores" and ceased their catering order transfer cooperation with related order transfer platforms. From a 252.3 yuan cake order to the penalization of seven major platforms; from 378 forged documents to the elimination of over 67,000 "ghost stores"; from prudent research to establish judicial benchmarks to hefty fines deterring the industry—although the battle to investigate and handle the "ghost takeout" series of cases has concluded, its warnings and implications are worth deep consideration. The platform economy is a new engine for development in the digital age, and online catering is a basic necessity for people's daily lives. However, no matter how large the traffic or how broad the scale, the red line of food safety cannot be crossed. No matter how high the profits or how fast the expansion, legal obligations cannot be ignored, and the bottom line of public welfare cannot be disregarded. Only by adhering to integrity and responsibility, acting as a "gatekeeper," and guarding the "safety line" can consumer trust and support be earned, and can the platform economy achieve stable and long-term development amidst fierce market competition. (Xinhua News Agency, Beijing, April 17th. "Xinhua Viewpoint" reporters Han Jie, Dai Xiaohe, Zhao Yining, Wang Yueyang)

Three receiving stores bid 100 yuan, 90 yuan, and 80 yuan, respectively, with the lowest bidder winning the order. In this process, the "ghost store" earned 121.9 yuan, and the e-commerce platform collected a service fee of 50.4 yuan. The store that actually made the cake accepted the order for 80 yuan, paid a 3.2 yuan service fee to Zhuan Dan Bao, and received 76.8 yuan after deducting the self-provided delivery fee. Reporters learned that the cost of a 6-inch cream cake made with good ingredients is approximately 60 yuan. Behind the bill, the e-commerce platforms and "ghost stores" reaped profits, while the operators who actually provided the cakes could only obtain meager profits. According to the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Food Safety for Online Catering Services," online catering service providers are prohibited from preparing food outside their processing and operation areas and are not allowed to entrust order processing to other food business operators. The investigated e-commerce platforms, despite knowing these regulations, signed data-sharing agreements with order-transfer platforms, assisting in the transfer of orders by online stores and condoning the spread of "ghost takeout" behavior. Shi Jianzhong, a professor at China University of Political Science and Law, believes that as a business model, order transfer itself is not illegal. However, with the involvement of "ghost stores," it becomes a channel for evading food safety supervision. Following the leads, the task force discovered two major order-transfer platforms, Chongqing Zhuan Dan Bao and Anhui Xunmeng, which cumulatively handled over 3.6 million illegally subcontracted cake orders, involving seven e-commerce platforms: Pinduoduo, Meituan, JD.com, Ele.me (Taobao Flash Purchase), Douyin, Taobao, and Tmall. They uncovered more than 67,000 "ghost stores." "This discovery is by no means a minor violation, but a new type of illegal model, a widespread chaos that is industrialized and scaled," said Han Bing, director of the Fourth Inspection Division of the SAMR's Law Enforcement and Inspection Bureau. Consumers are paying high prices for low-quality food, their right to know is being deprived, and the food safety defense line for online catering is being riddled with holes by these 'ghosts'." **Undermining Supervision: Platform Negligence Creates Food Safety Hazards** Why could fake certificates and licenses be uploaded in batches? Why was platform review perfunctory? As the investigation deepened, more hidden truths gradually emerged: some leading platforms turned a blind eye to violations, allowing fake certificates to proliferate. The task force found that the operations of fake certificate syndicates were like an assembly line, with interconnected steps and division of labor. The upstream of the industry chain was responsible for obtaining "materials" – the identity cards, business licenses, and other base documents required for online store registration. They either directly "Photoshopped" real licenses by altering names and addresses or purchased realistic fake materials for thirty to forty yuan, including photos of individuals holding their ID cards, to "get by." The intermediate technical processors were well-versed in platform rules and acted as "beauticians" for fake materials. They understood the key points and loopholes in the review process. If materials were rejected, they would make modifications based on the feedback until they were approved, earning 5 yuan per order. The downstream consisted of "guaranteed approval" runners who offered "one-stop" services, charging eighty to ninety yuan to handle registration, image uploads, and review monitoring. If a fake store was shut down, they would charge 30 yuan to get it back online. Some individuals used them to register over 570 fake stores. The negligence and dereliction of duty by the investigated e-commerce platforms further allowed fake certificates and licenses to pass through "unhindered." Intermediaries and platform reviewers colluded in secret, fostering a set of industry unwritten rules. "If fake certificates were blocked by the system, the reviewer would inform the intermediary about 'incorrect seal color' or 'company code cannot be found.' The intermediary would then tell the fake certificate maker to make changes. This way, it was 'returned, modified, and resubmitted.' To ensure accurate classification, legal procedures, and fair penalties, the SAMR conducted careful research, clarified legal applications, evidence standards, and penalty scales. After multiple rounds of deliberation and repeated discussions with legal experts and judicial personnel, a consensus was reached. The penalty decision issued by the SAMR clearly stated that Pinduoduo, Meituan, JD.com, Ele.me (Taobao Flash Purchase), Douyin, Taobao, and Tmall were suspected of failing to fulfill their legal obligations for qualification review and did not take necessary measures against platform operators infringing upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests, thus violating the Food Safety Law, the E-commerce Law, and the Consumer Rights Protection Law. Order-transfer platforms such as Zhuan Dan Bao and Anhui Xunmeng were suspected of failing to fulfill their legal obligations for qualification review, failing to obtain platform备案 (filing) according to law, and providing technical support for illegal order transfers. "Ghost stores" were suspected of illegal order transfers, using false certificates and licenses, and forging food business permits. Reporters learned that the regulatory authorities' penalties were imposed on a "one store, one penalty, cumulative calculation" basis, with each "ghost store" and each instance of review negligence being penalized individually. This ultimately resulted in the largest fine in the food safety sector since the revision of the Food Safety Law in 2015. "Platform qualification review is the first line of defense for food safety. If this line collapses, the entire regulatory system will fail. This 'one store, one penalty' is of milestone significance, forcing platforms to shift from 'formal review' to 'substantive review' and truly bear their primary responsibility," said Xue Jun, a professor at Peking University Law School. In Shi Jianzhong's view, this series of "ghost takeout" cases is a landmark case for regulatory authorities to strengthen online food safety supervision and standardize platform development, and it will provide a reference for the judgment of similar cases in the future. Reporters learned that after the investigation was initiated, the SAMR immediately ordered the e-commerce platforms to rectify the situation. Currently, all seven e-commerce platforms have taken down the relevant "ghost stores" and ceased catering order transfer cooperation with related order-transfer platforms. From a single 252.3 yuan cake order to the fining of seven major platforms; from 378 forged certificates to the elimination of over 67,000 "ghost stores"; from careful research to establish judicial standards to hefty fines deterring the industry... Although the battle to investigate and crack down on the "ghost takeout" series of cases has concluded, the warnings and insights it brings are worth deep reflection. The platform economy is a new engine for development in the digital age, and online catering is a basic necessity for people's daily lives. However, no matter how large the traffic or how broad the scale, the red line of food safety cannot be crossed; no matter how high the profits or how fast the expansion, legal obligations cannot be ignored, and the bottom line of people's welfare cannot be abandoned. Only by adhering to integrity and responsibility, acting as a "gatekeeper," and guarding the "safety line" can we win the trust and support of consumers and achieve stable and long-term development in fierce market competition.

body_en: Foreign Ministry: Hopes relevant parties will responsibly abide by ceasefire agreements and provide necessary conditions for the normalization of passage through the Strait. On April 20, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jia Kun hosted a regular press conference. A reporter asked about the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Guo Jia Kun stated that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz is sensitive and complex, and we are concerned about the US forcibly intercepting relevant vessels. We hope that relevant parties will responsibly abide by ceasefire agreements, avoid escalating conflicts and tensions, and provide the necessary conditions for the normalization of passage through the Strait. National Energy Administration: Electricity consumption nationwide increased by 3.5% year-on-year in March, and 5.2% in the first quarter. The National Energy Administration released data on electricity consumption nationwide in March. In March, electricity consumption nationwide was 859.5 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 3.5%. By industry, electricity consumption in the primary industry was 11.3 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 6.7%. Electricity consumption in the secondary industry was 570.8 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 2.0%; of which, industrial electricity consumption was 566.1 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 2.3%, and electricity consumption in high-tech and equipment manufacturing was 105.4 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 5.6%. Electricity consumption in the tertiary industry was 160.1 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 7.7%; of which, electricity consumption in charging and swapping services and internet data services was 13 billion and 8 billion kilowatt-hours respectively, with growth rates of 51.3% and 40.1% respectively. Electricity consumption for urban and rural residents' lives was 117.2 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 5.2%. From January to March, total electricity consumption nationwide accumulated to 2,514.1 billion kilowatt-hours, a year-on-year increase of 5.2%. Hong Kong SFC Announces New Regulatory Framework Allowing Trading of Tokenized SFC-Authorized Investment Products in the Secondary Market. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of Hong Kong announced a new regulatory framework today (April 20) to promote the trial trading of tokenized SFC-authorized investment products (tokenized products) in the secondary market in Hong Kong, with the aim of promoting digital asset trading activities in the long run and supporting the further development of the ecosystem. The circular issued by the SFC contains new guidelines, the main purpose of which is to facilitate the secondary market trading of tokenized SFC-authorized open-ended funds on SFC-licensed virtual asset trading platforms, further expanding regulated trading services available to retail investors. However, the SFC will also consider arrangements for over-the-counter secondary market trading on a case-by-case basis. Hainan's Outbound Tax Refund Amount Increased by 8.5 Times in the First Quarter. Haikou Customs recently released statistical data showing that in the first quarter of this year, the customs processed 8,300 outbound tax refund applications, with an application amount of 23.394 million yuan and a tax refund amount of 2.908 million yuan, representing year-on-year increases of 16.8 times, 8.3 times, and 8.5 times, respectively. Since the beginning of this year, Haikou Customs has actively optimized its outbound tax refund supervision and services. Through policy promotion, simplification of verification processes, and the establishment of more service points, it has improved the efficiency of customs' outbound tax refund verification and further stimulated the inbound consumption market. A relevant负责人 from Haikou Customs stated that in the next step, Haikou Customs will continue to optimize the outbound tax refund customs supervision service model to inject new momentum into inbound tourism consumption in Hainan Free Trade Port. South Korea to Regulate E-cigarettes the Same as Cigarettes from April 24. From April 24, e-cigarettes in South Korea will be regulated the same as traditional cigarettes. In February, South Korea passed an amendment to the Tobacco Business Act, expanding the definition of tobacco to include all products made from tobacco or nicotine, effectively classifying liquid e-cigarettes as cigarettes. Before the amendment was passed, South Korean law did not classify e-cigarettes as tobacco products. Under the expanded definition, all nicotine products will be subject to the National Health Promotion Act. This law requires health warnings on packaging and imposes strict restrictions on advertising. The amendment also strengthens controls on vending machines, regulating their installation locations, distance requirements, and whether vendors hold retail licenses. For e-cigarette users, this amendment means they can no longer smoke e-cigarettes in non-smoking areas. Financial Institutions Guotou Baiyin LOF to be Suspended from Market Open to 10:30 AM on April 21. Guotou Ruibao Fund Management Co., Ltd. announced on April 20 that recently, the secondary market trading price of Guotou Ruibao Silver Futures Fund (LOF) Class A shares (on-exchange abbreviation: Guotou Baiyin LOF; trading code: 161226) managed by Guotou Ruibao Fund Management Co., Ltd. has significantly exceeded its net asset value, showing a substantial premium. This is to remind investors to pay attention to the risk of premium in the secondary market trading price. If investors blindly invest in fund shares with a high premium rate, they may face significant investment losses due to the subsequent decline in the secondary market price. To protect investors' interests, the fund will be suspended from market open to 10:30 AM on April 21, 2026, and will resume trading at 10:30 AM on April 21, 2026. Redemption business of the fund will continue as usual during the suspension period. If the premium rate of the fund's secondary market trading price does not effectively decrease on April 21, 2026, the fund reserves the right to take measures such as applying for intraday temporary suspension, extending the suspension period, and continuous suspension to alert the market to risks. The specific details will be subject to announcements at that time. Market Data A-share Closing: Shanghai Composite Index Rose 0.76%, Shenzhen Component Index Rose 0.55%. On April 20, the three major A-share indices showed mixed performance. As of the close, the Shanghai Composite Index rose 0.76%, the Shenzhen Component Index rose 0.55%, and the ChiNext Index fell 0.02%; the Beijing Stock Exchange 50 rose 1.12%. The turnover in the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets was approximately 2,578.77 billion yuan, an increase of about 153.186 billion yuan from the previous trading day. In the entire market, 3,424 stocks rose, 1,898 stocks fell, with 90 stocks hitting the daily limit and 17 stocks falling by the daily limit. In terms of sectors, aerospace, shipbuilding, Chengdu Aircraft Industry, defense and military industry, power grid equipment, and minor metals sectors and concepts led the gains; fentanyl, salt lake lithium extraction, non-ferrous metals (nickel), energy metals, biological products, and chemical pharmaceuticals sectors and concepts were among the biggest decliners. Margin Balance Increased by 2.169 Billion Yuan. As of April 17, the margin balance of the Shanghai Stock Exchange was 1,341.425 billion yuan, an increase of 619 million yuan from the previous trading day; the margin balance of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange was 1,301.422 billion yuan, an increase of 1.55 billion yuan from the previous trading day; the total margin balance of both markets was 2,642.847 billion yuan, an increase of 2.169 billion yuan from the previous trading day. Hong Kong Stock Market Closing: Hang Seng Index Rose 0.77%, Hang Seng Tech Index Rose 0.46%. On April 20, the Hong Kong stock market closed with the Hang Seng Index rising 0.77% and the Hang Seng Tech Index rising 0.46%. AI application stocks led the gains, with Qunhe Technology soaring over 101%, Zhipu rising over 9%, and Nobuyuki Kan rising over 7%. Company News iQIYI Responds to Controversy Over "Authorization from Hundreds of Artists for AI". On April 20, the topic "iQIYI has gone crazy" topped the hot search list on Weibo. iQIYI stated that over a hundred artists have agreed to join the artist pool of its professional film and television production platform, Nadou Pro, which has sparked heated discussion. @iQIYI responded by stating that joining the iQIYI Nadou Pro artist pool signifies the artists' willingness to engage in AI film and television projects. However, participation in specific projects or roles requires separate negotiation and authorization, which is consistent with the cooperation process for traditional live-action film and television projects. The integration of AI and film and television creation is still in the exploratory stage. In the future, while protecting the interests of artists, creators, and audiences, we will actively embrace technological changes and explore the future direction of this unknown field with industry partners. Wanda Film's Physical Stores Will Continue to Use the Name "Wanda Cinemas". On April 20, after Wanda Film officially changed its name to "Ruyi Film Entertainment Co., Ltd.", Chen Zhixi, Chairman and President of Ruyi Film, issued a letter to all employees. It is understood that Wanda Film's physical stores will continue to use the name "Wanda Cinemas," which will remain one of Ruyi Film's important cinema brands. New brands will be planned in the future based on market changes and user needs. Yonghui Superstores: Operating Revenue of Renovated Stores Increased by 16.57% in the First Quarter. On April 20, Yonghui Superstores stated at its first-quarter performance briefing that the large-scale store closures have ended, and the renovated stores have achieved revenue growth. In the first quarter of 2026, the operating revenue of renovated stores increased by 16.57% year-on-year. Purui Optoelectronics: Net Profit Increased by 512% in the First Quarter, and Sales Revenue from Core Key Customers in the Optical Communication Field Increased by 148% Year-on-Year. According to a report from the Kechuang Daily, Purui Optoelectronics (688337.SH) announced that in the first quarter of 2026, its operating revenue was 232 million yuan, a year-on-year increase of 38.00%; its net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company was 23.1503 million yuan, a year-on-year increase of 512.01%. During the reporting period, sales revenue from the company's key customers increased by 194.17% year-on-year. In the optical communication field, sales revenue from core key customers increased by 147.71% year-on-year, driving rapid growth in operating revenue for related product lines and becoming an important driver of the company's revenue growth. Alibaba's HappyHorse to Open for Testing on April 27. Alibaba ATH announced today that HappyHorse-1.0 will gradually open API testing through Alibaba Cloud's Baizhan platform starting April 27, with enterprise customers being the first to be invited for testing. Alibaba ATH revealed that Alibaba has been deeply involved in AI video generation for many years. The HappyHorse project is led by the ATH Innovation Business Unit and jointly developed by multiple teams including Alibaba Platform Technology, Tongyi Laboratory, and Taotian Technology. After the open testing at the end of April, HappyHorse-1.0 will be officially released for commercial use in May. Proofreading: Wang Jincheng

Under the expanded definition, all nicotine products will be subject to the National Health Promotion Act. This law requires health warnings on packaging and imposes strict restrictions on advertising. title_en: Lexical Reconstruction: The Commercial Ecosystem of the AI Era
body_en: The National Data Bureau recently officially designated the Chinese translation of "Token" as "词元" (cí yuán), clarifying its role as a value anchor in the intelligent era, serving as a "settlement unit" connecting technological supply with commercial demand. Discussions surrounding "词元" have remained highly popular in recent days. What are the essence and value of "词元"? What industrial impacts will the "词元 economy" it fosters bring? And what risks and challenges require high attention and systematic response? Exponential Growth in Call Volume "词元" is the smallest fundamental unit for large models to process information, with individual Chinese characters, words, and punctuation marks all considered "词元". "Large models face global languages, where Chinese, English, Arabic, code, mathematical formulas, and other content coexist," said Zhang Ting, Product Lead of Baidu Qianfan Platform. "词元" is equivalent to a universal "greatest common divisor," enabling models to process all languages and symbols in a unified manner, becoming the fundamental unit of measurement for artificial intelligence interaction. In daily use, "词元" consumption is ubiquitous. Asking an AI to write an 800-word essay, including prompts and complete output, consumes approximately 1,000 to 1,500 "词元"; asking an AI to analyze a 10-page contract might consume 5,000 to 10,000 "词元". In recent years, artificial intelligence has accelerated its integration into daily life, and many people have become accustomed to using AI for writing articles, searching for information, and translating. Currently, mainstream AI platforms offer free services to ordinary users, which generally meet their daily work and life needs. However, enterprise users and developers need to pay fees based on the number of "词元" calls or actual usage. Early this year, the AI agent tool "OpenClaw" quickly gained popularity, leading several domestic AI platforms to launch similar products, resulting in explosive growth in "词元" call volume. At a recent press conference held by the State Council Information Office, Liu Liehong, Director of the National Data Bureau, introduced that as of March this year, China's average daily "词元" call volume exceeded 140 trillion, an increase of more than 1,000 times from 100 billion at the beginning of 2024. Compared to 100 trillion at the end of 2025, it has grown by more than 40% in just three months. The leapfrog growth in "词元" call volume directly reflects that China's artificial intelligence industry has entered a period of rapid growth, with continuously deepening application scenarios and significantly enhanced industrial competitiveness. According to Bai Runxuan, an analyst at the AI and Big Data Research Center of CCID Consulting, the surge in "词元" call volume is mainly driven by three factors: first, significant improvements in model capabilities, such as the Seedance 2.0 video generation model from Doubao, which requires over 1 million "词元" to generate one minute of video; second, upgrades in application forms, shifting from simple Q&A to the era of intelligent agents, where long-context interactions involving task planning and tool invocation significantly increase "词元" consumption; and third, accelerated commercialization, with industries accelerating AI applications, driving exponential growth in "词元" call volume. The surge in "词元" call volume, coupled with factors like rising hardware costs, has also led cloud vendors such as Alibaba Cloud, Baidu Smart Cloud, and Tencent Cloud to recently raise prices for AI computing power and other products, with increases generally around 30%. "Market demand for computing power is strong, and prices naturally rise," said Pan Helin, a member of the Expert Committee on Information and Communication Economics of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. He believes that cloud vendors are enhancing their "词元" pricing capabilities by providing intelligent services, gradually moving away from reliance on free traffic acquisition models, and promoting the AI application into a more sustainable and commercialized new stage. Economic Value Gradually Emerging The popularization of AI intelligent agents allows more people to intuitively feel the economic value of "词元". If traditional internet was about traffic economy and attention economy, then the "词元 economy" of the AI era is a new model centered on productivity and billed by usage. "词元" consumption, unit output efficiency, and cost control capabilities are becoming key indicators for enterprises' digital transformation and refined operations. "Traffic is gradually becoming ineffective; '词元' is the core of the future," said Zhou Hongyi, founder of 360 Group. He believes that the traffic economy of the traditional internet is built on the scale effect of diminishing marginal costs: fiber optic capacity is nearly infinite, platforms transmit data packets, and the larger the user base, the lower the unit cost, with costs mainly related to duration and bandwidth occupation. However, in the AI era, the essence of AI is not data transportation but a deep coupling of computing power consumption, information processing, and "intellectual costs." "词元" is the core measurement unit for AI's intellectual and computing power consumption. The more consumed, the higher the marginal cost, and the business logic is completely changed. The shift of the large model industry from "traffic operation" to "词元 operation" represents a fundamental change in underlying business logic. "The 'hundred-model war' in the past two years focused on training computing power competition, mainly using AI for chatting and creation to verify model capabilities. Now, large models have entered the stage of industrial implementation, aiming to enter factories and offices to become true 'digital employees' that get work done," Zhou Hongyi said. He believes that the core scenario for large-scale consumption of computing power will be the comprehensive popularization of enterprise-level intelligent agents. Currently, "词元" call volume is mainly concentrated in sectors such as the internet, consumer electronics, finance, new retail, and business services, with application scenarios primarily involving unstructured information processing, education and teaching, content creation, search, and recommendation. Bai Runxuan believes that future software development, in-depth research, and personal intelligent assistants will become important growth points for "词元" calls. The "词元 economy" will reconstruct the path for releasing the value of data elements, reshape the commercial ecosystem of the AI industry, open up the connection channel between data elements and the real economy, and accelerate the intelligent upgrading of traditional industries such as manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, and finance. Coordinating Efficiency and Security Latest data from the global API aggregation platform OpenRouter shows that from April 6th to 12th, the total global AI large model call volume was 21 trillion Tokens. Among the top five global call volumes, three were Chinese AI large models, with Alibaba's Qwen3.6-Plus ranking first, with a weekly call volume of 1.66 trillion Tokens. Notably, China's AI large model weekly call volume has surpassed that of the United States for six consecutive weeks. "China's AI is truly being utilized. Call volume reflects the actual scale of use, not the number of model parameters or benchmark performance," said Zhou Hongyi. He stated that the core reason for global developers' preference for Chinese large models is that the gap in model capabilities between China and the US has narrowed to within three months, while Chinese models are priced at only one-tenth or even less than overseas leading models. Behind this low-cost advantage is the rapid maturity of the open-source ecosystem, which has formed a universal development pattern for Chinese large models, similar to the Android system. Currently, global AI competition has shifted from model parameter competition to application implementation capability competition. China has achieved leapfrog development in the AI field by leveraging its super-large market, complete power and computing infrastructure, and high cost-performance advantages. However, it must also be recognized that while computing power demand is experiencing explosive growth, supply has not fully kept pace, leading to a phased imbalance between supply and demand. "First, there is insufficient supply of high-end chips, with overseas high-end GPU production capacity being tight and delivery cycles extending. Second, data quality and standardization are insufficient, and the construction of high-quality datasets still needs to be strengthened," said Bai Runxuan. What is even more alarming is that "词元" transactions and AI service billing are all completed online, with deep binding of data, permissions, and financial links, leading to increased security risks. Qi Xiangdong, Chairman of Qi An Xin, believes that criminals can steal "词元" through vulnerability exploitation, terminal hijacking, malicious plugins, prompt injection, and other methods, thereby illegally accessing sensitive data, exceeding authorization to call AI services, fraudulently using billing amounts, and even carrying out identity forgery, network fraud, and other behaviors, triggering chain risks such as data leakage, loss of control over permissions, and financial losses. "For ordinary users, when using AI applications, do not input sensitive information such as ID numbers, bank accounts, home addresses, facial photos, or trade secrets. When using AI in a work context, real information should be concealed or blurred, and it is advisable to use locally deployed or securely certified enterprise-level AI services," Qi Xiangdong suggested. He also recommended establishing a tiered and classified management system for "词元" security risks and comprehensive security standards and specifications for the entire "词元" process, clearly defining the responsibilities of each party involved. As artificial intelligence accelerates its empowerment of various industries, industry insiders generally believe that the next step should focus on key areas such as high-quality data supply and standardization of "词元" measurement and pricing. Efforts should be made to accelerate the transformation of computing power into a convenient and accessible public basic resource like water and electricity. This approach, characterized by "regulating development through progress and progressing through regulation," will enable the "词元 economy" to truly become a vital force driving the in-depth implementation of the "Artificial Intelligence +" initiative and promoting the high-quality development of the intelligent economy.
