Dico Technology: Plans to issue shares to specific targets to raise no more than 3 billion yuan for the storage chip packaging and testing base project and other projects. Heliatai: Has confirmed business revenue of less than 10,000 yuan through external procurement and subleasing of computing power services. Sunhow Shares: Currently only a shareholder in Orbit Chenguang. Zijin Mining: Net profit in the first quarter increased by 97.50% year-on-year, with both volume and price of major metal products rising. Zhongfu Industrial: Net profit in the first quarter increased by 257% year-on-year, with increased sales of electrolytic aluminum and aluminum processing. title_en: ByteDance net profit falls 70%. Li Liang: Excluding accounting factors, actual profit margin has not significantly declined.
body_en: According to sources on April 20, ByteDance's overseas revenue in 2025 is expected to grow by nearly 50% year-on-year, with its revenue share exceeding 30% for the first time, reaching a record high. TikTok's e-commerce GMV growth is close to 70%. However, at the same time, due to significant increases in AI computing power procurement and infrastructure spending, as well as changes in preferred stock and option costs, the company's net profit for the full year is expected to decline by over 70% year-on-year. Nevertheless, Li Liang, Vice President of Douyin Group, revealed on Weibo that excluding changes in preferred stock and option costs, overall revenue and profit are still growing, and the business trends for TikTok e-commerce and emerging businesses are positive. In the tug-of-war between investment and return, and valuation and profit, this unlisted tech giant is reshaping its growth narrative with a bold AI gamble. ByteDance's overseas business delivered a better-than-expected performance in 2025. According to sources, ByteDance's overseas revenue in 2025 is expected to grow by nearly 50%, and the proportion of overseas revenue will increase from 25% in 2024 to over 30%, a record high. The core engine driving this growth is TikTok Shop, with its GMV growing by nearly 70% year-on-year in 2025. Public data shows that TikTok Shop has reached 400 million active consumers, with its annual GMV approaching $100 billion. Sales in the US market increased by 108%, and in the European market by over 100%. While maintaining its second position in Southeast Asia, new markets like Latin America and Japan are also growing rapidly. The Brazilian market saw a 25-fold increase in GMV in the first three months after its launch, and the Japanese market achieved a 20-fold increase in four months. Behind the strong growth in overseas revenue, TikTok's survival in the US market reached a critical turning point in early 2026. On January 22, 2026, TikTok officially announced the establishment of TikTok US Data Security Joint Venture LLC, successfully retaining its business in the US market. However, in stark contrast to the revenue side, profits have contracted. According to sources, ByteDance's net profit in 2025 is expected to decline by over 70% year-on-year, with a significant drop in net profit margin. The decline was mainly concentrated in the third and fourth quarters, directly caused by ByteDance's substantial increase in capital expenditure on AI computing power procurement, model research and development, and data center infrastructure during this period. On the afternoon of April 20, Li Liang posted on Weibo: "The report about ByteDance's net profit decreasing by 70% is based on International Financial Reporting Standards. In addition to increased investment in emerging businesses, there are also factors related to changes in preferred stock and option costs (which do not reflect operational substance). In reality, due to the slowdown in Douyin e-commerce growth and increased investment in emerging businesses, the operating profit margin slightly declined in the second half of the year, but not as significantly as reported." Sources revealed that ByteDance informed its shareholders that technology resource investment will further increase in 2026, and coupled with new factors such as the US data security joint venture, the company's net profit margin may continue to be under pressure in the short term. The substantial capital investment has already shown quantifiable progress in product development. According to Volcano Engine, as of March 2026, Doubao's large model daily token calls have exceeded 120 trillion, doubling in three months and increasing 1000 times since its launch in May 2024, ranking first in China and among the top three globally (behind OpenAI and Google). In Q1 2026, Doubao's monthly active users exceeded 200 million, making it the AI-native application with the largest user base in China. On the enterprise side, among Volcano Engine's external clients, the number of clients with cumulative token calls exceeding one trillion has reached 140. AI investment is reflected not only in computing power and products but also in talent incentive mechanisms. In October 2025, ByteDance piloted a long-term incentive plan for Doubao internally, establishing a virtual share system for Doubao-related large model businesses. This plan is currently being implemented in the Seed department. Unlike traditional cash rewards or company-wide option pools, Doubao shares, through the granting of virtual shares and a buyback mechanism similar to ByteDance options, allow key technical personnel to share in the value generated by business growth. At the business structure level, the penetration of AI is changing ByteDance's revenue composition. According to data previously disclosed by media and industry organizations, ByteDance's total domestic revenue in 2025 was approximately 901.2 billion RMB, a year-on-year increase of 28.3%. Breaking down the structure, advertising revenue was 420 billion RMB, accounting for 46.6% of revenue. E-commerce GMV exceeded 4 trillion RMB for the year, with e-commerce revenue accounting for about 45.5% of total revenue. Local lifestyle services GMV was about 71.2 billion RMB for the year, a year-on-year increase of 59%. In terms of user scale, Douyin's daily active users in China exceeded 850 million in 2025, and monthly active users surpassed 1 billion. In the global market, ByteDance's short-video products (including TikTok) combined have over 2 billion monthly active users, making it the first short-video platform globally to reach this user scale. Overseas business performance continued to strengthen, with TikTok's global advertising revenue in 2025 being approximately $33.1 billion, a year-on-year increase of 40.5%. ByteDance's overall overseas revenue share exceeded 30% for the first time in 2025. On April 15, 2026, ByteDance issued an internal email to launch a new round of option buybacks. The buyback price for current employees is $229.5 per share, and for former employees, it is $201.96 per share. In January of this year, the company's option price was adjusted to $226.07 per share. It is understood that ByteDance has established a regular semi-annual option buyback mechanism (April and October) since 2021. The buyback price for current employees was $126 per share in 2021, and it rose to $229.5 per share in April 2026, nearly doubling its internal valuation in four years. Almost simultaneously, ByteDance also launched the first buyback of Doubao shares. On April 16, the buyback price for Doubao shares was $13.08 per share, an increase of approximately 30.8% from its grant price of $10. Sources revealed that $13.08 per share is the latest pricing for Doubao shares, and employees who joined the company after March 1, 2026, and received Doubao share incentives will also be granted based on this price. Doubao shares adopt a phased vesting and tiered buyback mechanism: for general grant Doubao shares, 40% of vested shares can be repurchased in the first year after vesting, and the repurchase proportion increases by 12% for each subsequent year; for performance-based Doubao shares, 40% can also be repurchased in the first year, and the repurchase proportion increases by 15% for each subsequent year; shares from all batches can be repurchased once they reach one share. General grants primarily refer to Doubao shares granted upon joining and those issued with salary adjustments, while performance-based grants are awarded based on performance appraisal results. The difference in the repurchase increase rhythm between the two types corresponds to employee incentives in different scenarios. The continuous increase in the internal buyback price is consistent with the valuation in external equity transactions. In November 2025, Capital Today participated in a secondary share transfer of ByteDance at a valuation of $480 billion; in February 2026, General Atlantic sold a portion of its holdings, at which time ByteDance's valuation reached $550 billion. The divergence between valuation and profit reflects investors' pricing of revenue scale and AI growth trajectory, as well as the scarcity of unlisted equity in the secondary market. ByteDance's continued investment in talent also supports external confidence. In an all-hands meeting in early 2026, ByteDance CEO Liang Rubo set the annual keyword as "Climb to the Peak," emphasizing the need to increase talent density and enhance talent incentives, ensuring that compensation and incentives are leading in all global markets. Across the entire tech industry, the competition for cutting-edge technology talent has become fierce. Public information shows that since the beginning of 2026, leading companies such as Tencent, Alibaba, and Baidu have significantly expanded their AI job recruitment. Tencent has increased technical positions by 36%, AI-related positions at Alibaba account for over 60%, and AI positions in Baidu's campus recruitment account for over 90%, all focusing on core areas such as large models, multi-modal AI, and intelligent agents. Looking ahead to 2026, the race of "trading profit for the future" has just begun. In the tug-of-war between investment and return, and valuation and profit, this unlisted tech giant is reshaping its growth narrative with a bold AI gamble. ByteDance's overseas business delivered a better-than-expected performance in 2025. According to sources, ByteDance's overseas revenue in 2025 is expected to grow by nearly 50%, and the proportion of overseas revenue will increase from 25% in 2024 to over 30%, a record high. The core engine driving this growth is TikTok Shop, with its GMV growing by nearly 70% year-on-year in 2025. Public data shows that TikTok Shop has reached 400 million active consumers, with its annual GMV approaching $100 billion. Sales in the US market increased by 108%, and in the European market by over 100%. While maintaining its second position in Southeast Asia, new markets like Latin America and Japan are also growing rapidly. The Brazilian market saw a 25-fold increase in GMV in the first three months after its launch, and the Japanese market achieved a 20-fold increase in four months. Behind the strong growth in overseas revenue, TikTok's survival in the US market reached a critical turning point in early 2026. On January 22, 2026, TikTok officially announced the establishment of TikTok US Data Security Joint Venture LLC, successfully retaining its business in the US market. However, in stark contrast to the revenue side, profits have contracted. According to sources, ByteDance's net profit in 2025 is expected to decline by over 70% year-on-year, with a significant drop in net profit margin. The decline was mainly concentrated in the third and fourth quarters, directly caused by ByteDance's substantial increase in capital expenditure on AI computing power procurement, model research and development, and data center infrastructure during this period. On the afternoon of April 20, Li Liang posted on Weibo: "The report about ByteDance's net profit decreasing by 70% is based on International Financial Reporting Standards. In addition to increased investment in emerging businesses, there are also factors related to changes in preferred stock and option costs (which do not reflect operational substance). In reality, due to the slowdown in Douyin e-commerce growth and increased investment in emerging businesses, the operating profit margin slightly declined in the second half of the year, but not as significantly as reported." Sources revealed that ByteDance informed its shareholders that technology resource investment will further increase in 2026, and coupled with new factors such as the US data security joint venture, the company's net profit margin may continue to be under pressure in the short term. The substantial capital investment has already shown quantifiable progress in product development. According to Volcano Engine, as of March 2026, Doubao's large model daily token calls have exceeded 120 trillion, doubling in three months and increasing 1000 times since its launch in May 2024, ranking first in China and among the top three globally (behind OpenAI and Google). In Q1 2026, Doubao's monthly active users exceeded 200 million, making it the AI-native application with the largest user base in China. On the enterprise side, among Volcano Engine's external clients, the number of clients with cumulative token calls exceeding one trillion has reached 140. AI investment is reflected not only in computing power and products but also in talent incentive mechanisms. In October 2025, ByteDance piloted a long-term incentive plan for Doubao internally, establishing a virtual share system for Doubao-related large model businesses. This plan is currently being implemented in the Seed department. Unlike traditional cash rewards or company-wide option pools, Doubao shares, through the granting of virtual shares and a buyback mechanism similar to ByteDance options, allow key technical personnel to share in the value generated by business growth. At the business structure level, the penetration of AI is changing ByteDance's revenue composition. Breaking down the structure, advertising revenue was 420 billion RMB, accounting for 46.6% of revenue. E-commerce GMV exceeded 4 trillion RMB for the year, with e-commerce revenue accounting for about 45.5% of total revenue. Local lifestyle services GMV was about 71.2 billion RMB for the year, a year-on-year increase of 59%. In terms of user scale, Douyin's daily active users in China exceeded 850 million in 2025, and monthly active users surpassed 1 billion. In the global market, ByteDance's short-video products (including TikTok) combined have over 2 billion monthly active users, making it the first short-video platform globally to reach this user scale. The buyback price for current employees is $229.5 per share, and for former employees, it is $201.96 per share. In January of this year, the company's option price was adjusted to $226.07 per share. It is understood that ByteDance has established a regular semi-annual option buyback mechanism (April and October) since 2021. The buyback price for current employees was $126 per share in 2021, and it rose to $229.5 per share in April 2026, nearly doubling its internal valuation in four years. Almost simultaneously, ByteDance also launched the first buyback of Doubao shares. On April 16, the buyback price for Doubao shares was $13.08 per share, an increase of approximately 30.8% from its grant price of $10. Sources revealed that $13.08 per share is the latest pricing for Doubao shares, and employees who joined the company after March 1, 2026, and received Doubao share incentives will also be granted based on this price. Doubao shares adopt a phased vesting and tiered buyback mechanism: for general grant Doubao shares, 40% of vested shares can be repurchased in the first year after vesting, and the repurchase proportion increases by 12% for each subsequent year; for performance-based Doubao shares, 40% can also be repurchased in the first year, and the repurchase proportion increases by 15% for each subsequent year; shares from all batches can be repurchased once they reach one share. General grants primarily refer to Doubao shares granted upon joining and those issued with salary adjustments, while performance-based grants are awarded based on performance appraisal results. The difference in the repurchase increase rhythm between the two types corresponds to employee incentives in different scenarios. The continuous increase in the internal buyback price is consistent with the valuation in external equity transactions. In November 2025, Capital Today participated in a secondary share transfer of ByteDance at a valuation of $480 billion; in February 2026, General Atlantic sold a portion of its holdings, at which time ByteDance's valuation reached $550 billion. The divergence between valuation and profit reflects investors' pricing of revenue scale and AI growth trajectory, as well as the scarcity of unlisted equity in the secondary market. ByteDance's continued investment in talent also supports external confidence. In an all-hands meeting in early 2026, ByteDance CEO Liang Rubo set the annual keyword as "Climb to the Peak," emphasizing the need to increase talent density and enhance talent incentives, ensuring that compensation and incentives are leading in all global markets. Across the entire tech industry, the competition for cutting-edge technology talent has become fierce. Public information shows that since the beginning of 2026, leading companies such as Tencent, Alibaba, and Baidu have significantly expanded their AI job recruitment. Tencent has increased technical positions by 36%, AI-related positions at Alibaba account for over 60%, and AI positions in Baidu's campus recruitment account for over 90%, all focusing on core areas such as large models, multi-modal AI, and intelligent agents. Looking ahead to 2026, the race of "trading profit for the future" has just begun. title_en: What red lines are set by the new platform pricing plan?
body_en: Q: Recently, the "Rules on Pricing Behavior of Internet Platforms" jointly formulated by the National Development and Reform Commission, the State Administration for Market Regulation, and the Cyberspace Administration of China officially came into effect, with a validity period of 5 years. Which entities are subject to this systematic regulatory document? What red lines does it draw for the platform economy? A: This rule applies to the pricing behavior of platform operators and platform-based operators in their business activities, such as selling goods or providing services through internet platforms and other information networks within the territory of the People's Republic of China. Platform operators refer to legal persons or unincorporated organizations that provide platform services such as online business premises, transaction matching, and information release. Platform-based operators refer to operators who sell goods or provide services through platforms. Prohibition of "Big Data Price Discrimination" This document explicitly prohibits price discrimination behaviors such as "big data price discrimination" in the form of departmental regulations for the first time. Platform operators and platform-based operators shall not, without the knowledge of consumers, use data and algorithms, platform rules, and other means to set different prices or fee standards for the same goods or services under the same transaction conditions, based on information such as willingness to pay, ability to pay, consumption preferences, and consumption habits. Standardization of Price Promotion Activities Platform operators and platform-based operators conducting price promotion activities shall comply with the following provisions: 1. The promotion rules, activity period, scope of application, etc., shall be publicly displayed in a prominent position on the page. 2. The basis for discounts and price reductions shall be truthfully indicated. 3. When deducting prices through points, gift vouchers, exchange vouchers, cash vouchers, advance payments, etc., the specific calculation methods shall be indicated in a prominent manner. Prominent Reminder for Automatic Renewal For services that provide password-free payment, and bundled additional services or goods such as insurance, transportation services, other cooperative platform services, refund services, and delay compensation, platform operators and platform-based operators shall prominently display relevant options to consumers and provide convenient cancellation channels. When platform operators and platform-based operators charge fees through automatic renewal and automatic deduction, they shall remind and notify consumers in a prominent manner of the deduction time, amount, and cancellation channel before each deduction, and allow consumers to cancel automatic renewal and automatic deduction at any time. If the charging standard changes, consumers shall also be notified. (Reporter Gu Yang)

title_en: The first GEO group standard in the finance and economics field has been approved for establishment, and we are now seeking participating units nationwide.
body_en: The first GEO group standard in the finance sector has been approved for establishment and is now seeking participating units nationwide. As generative artificial intelligence deeply integrates into the dissemination of financial information, a group standard aimed at regulating Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) in the finance sector and preventing new risks such as "corpus poisoning" – the "Standard for Grading and Crediting Optimization of Financial Information Sources for Large AI Models" (hereinafter referred to as the "Standard") – officially passed its project approval review on April 16th. This marks the first GEO group standard in the finance sector nationwide. The Standard was initiated and is managed by the China Association for News Technology Workers. It is jointly developed by the Industrial Culture Development Center of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the China Economic Media Association, National Business Daily, CBNData Technology, and Sunshine Insurance Group, among other entities. At the standard development launch meeting held on April 16th, Tang Yuanqing, Director of the AIGC and Digital Intelligence Communication Special Committee of the China Association for News Technology Workers and a professor at the National Key Laboratory of Media Convergence and Communication at Communication University of China, explained the rationale behind the standard's establishment and its draft content. He stated that currently, generative artificial intelligence technology is accelerating its implementation and penetration, and the internet content ecosystem is undergoing a profound transformation from the "search era" to the "generative era." GEO has become a core variable determining information visibility and content dissemination efficiency in the AI era. However, issues such as "AI poisoning," large model "hallucinations," and the lack of unified standards for evaluating GEO effectiveness are prominent. The application of its technology and industry governance have become crucial for the healthy development of the AIGC industry. The reliability and professionalism of AI-generated content fundamentally depend on the quality and credibility of the underlying information sources. Financial information, with its high professionalism, strong timeliness, high sensitivity, and broad social impact, directly relates to market order, investment decisions, and financial stability, making the standardization of its sources particularly important. Therefore, establishing a group standard to clarify unified guidelines for grading and crediting information sources and to build a "source credibility defense line" for large AI models in financial applications is both necessary and urgent. The Standard will be developed in three core directions: First, definition, clarifying the scope of application, core definitions, and regulatory boundaries and applicable scenarios to avoid ambiguity in development and execution. Second, grading, establishing principles for a multi-dimensional grading system that combines institutional qualifications, content quality, and AI adaptability to classify financial information sources into multiple levels, adhering to principles of feasibility and operability, and conducting dynamic grading assessments in a transparent manner. Third, optimization, optimizing the process of crediting information sources by clarifying requirements for source compliance and quality, screening high-quality sources, and guiding information sources to improve their quality and upgrade, thereby ensuring the reliability of financial information generated by large models. The Standard's content will be continuously improved based on feedback from all parties to ensure it aligns with industry realities and is implementable. Starting immediately, the China Association for News Technology Workers will publicly solicit participating units for the joint development of this standard from all sectors of society. All types of market entities are sincerely invited to actively participate in the development, refinement, and subsequent implementation of the standard, working together to build a high-quality, reliable, and compliant financial information ecosystem.

title_en: How to deposit and withdraw from a "computing power bank"? How to buy and sell at a "computing power supermarket"? (with pictures)
body_en: Currently, artificial intelligence technology is iterating at an accelerated pace, leading to a surge in computing power demand. Experts predict that by 2030, global computing power demand will exceed current levels by more than 100 times. In the AI era, computing power is productivity. In recent years, China's computing power infrastructure has achieved remarkable development, ranking second globally in both total computing power and intelligent computing scale, with a gradually established tiered and optimized computing power supply system. However, while large enterprises and institutions are the first to benefit from the computing power dividend, a large number of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) still face the dilemma of "cannot afford or cannot use" high-end computing power in scenarios such as AI research and development, data analysis, and industrial simulation. The high cost of computing power and complex technical barriers have become one of the main bottlenecks for their innovation and development. To address this challenge, in April this year, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued a notice to launch a special action to empower SMEs with inclusive computing power. "Computing Power Bank" and "Computing Power Supermarket" are the core innovative businesses of this special action, directly targeting the pain point of high computing power costs for SMEs, which will effectively improve the inclusiveness and ease of use of computing power, and provide support and empowerment for SMEs. What is a "Computing Power Bank" and how is it deposited and withdrawn? "The 'Computing Power Bank' draws on the model of financial banks to resource, standardize, and financialize scattered idle computing power resources, and provide inclusive supply through 'lump-sum deposits from installments' and cross-regional scheduling," explained Guo Liang, Chief Engineer of the Cloud Computing and Digitalization Research Institute of the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT). How does the "Computing Power Bank" make idle computing power "come alive"? The first step is resource aggregation (deposit). Computing power resources of different brands and specifications are uniformly standardized into "standard computing power units." Similar to how financial banks accept deposits, surplus computing power from research institutions, cloud vendors, and various enterprises is connected to the China Computing Power Platform to achieve resource aggregation. The second step is resource pooling (vault). The platform integrates distributed servers into a virtual resource pool, balancing computing power usage peaks and troughs through cross-regional scheduling, solving the problem of "bottlenecks in some areas and idleness in others." The third step is on-demand allocation (loan). Enterprises that use computing power can place orders on demand, just like applying for a bank loan. SMEs can obtain high-performance computing power at low cost through flexible package models such as "computing power vouchers" for deductions and pay-as-you-go. The fourth step is value settlement (clearing). A measurement and rebate mechanism is established, where computing power providers receive revenue or future priority usage rights, users pay based on actual usage, and the government achieves precise subsidies for SMEs through platform data. "A self-driving startup needs a large amount of computing power to process road test data, while the computing power in a university laboratory is idle at night. Through the 'Computing Power Bank,' the laboratory deposits computing power to obtain future credits; the startup uses government-issued 'computing power vouchers' to extract computing power at a low price, avoiding the peak and high prices of public clouds," said Guo Liang, adding that this significantly lowers the threshold for SMEs to obtain and use computing power. How is a "Computing Power Supermarket" opened, and how are transactions conducted? The core of the "Computing Power Supermarket" is the "commoditization" and "convenience" of computing power resources, allowing enterprises to obtain AI computing power like online shopping, truly realizing "on-demand selection and immediate use." The reporter learned that the core operation of the "Computing Power Supermarket" involves four key links: First, standardized resource listing. Underlying hardware performance is transformed into standardized products, calculated by computing power specifications such as token count, single-precision floating-point operations, and core-hour billing, eliminating technical barriers. Second, intelligent search and price comparison. Relying on the SME zone of the China Computing Power Platform, dynamic price comparison and computing power selection are realized, and computing power packages with low costs and low latency are automatically recommended, solving problems such as information asymmetry. Third, out-of-the-box service. Pre-installed model environments and development tools allow SMEs to deploy mainstream large model images and datasets with one click, achieving "order and run," shortening the development cycle. Fourth, inclusive policies and payment settlement. It connects with government subsidies, supports direct settlement of "computing power vouchers," and provides payment models such as prepaid, postpaid, and annual/monthly packages. The platform is responsible for monitoring service quality to ensure real performance. How do "Computing Power Bank" and "Computing Power Supermarket" collaborate? "If the 'Computing Power Bank' is responsible for the underlying resource flow and solves the problem of resource flow, then the 'Computing Power Supermarket' is responsible for the front-end user experience and solves the problem of transaction barriers, making computing power visible, affordable, and easy to use," Guo Liang vividly explained the synergistic logic of the two. "Computing Power Bank" and "Computing Power Supermarket" collaborate based on different application scenarios: "Computing Power Bank" is responsible for the deposit and withdrawal of computing power, allocating idle resources through the "deposit and loan" mechanism; "Computing Power Supermarket" can not only "sell" computing power resources but also provide products such as models, data, and IT services, rapidly distributing resources to end-users through convenient transactions and flexible billing. Among them, the computing power scheduling platform, as the "resource pool" of the underlying technical infrastructure, has core functions such as heterogeneous computing power access, cross-domain scheduling, and metering and billing. Which pioneers have already laid out and implemented? Currently, "Computing Power Supermarket" has been piloted in multiple provinces and cities. The Shandong Artificial Intelligence Public Service Platform focuses on large models and AI applications, integrating computing power, model, and data services, and precisely matching supply and demand for key vertical scenarios, significantly lowering the threshold for industrial intelligence. The Shanghai Computing Power Trading Platform has launched an intelligent computing zone for education, standardizing and listing computing power resources. Educational institutions can select and deploy training environments with one click as needed, achieving one-stop empowerment from selection to application. The Ningxia (Zhongwei) Computing Power Monitoring and Scheduling Integrated Service Platform, through unified management and commoditized packaging of heterogeneous computing power, opens up cross-regional scheduling channels with high demand areas in the east, effectively supporting the collaborative implementation of "eastern models, western computing," and activating the value of western computing power. Practice has proven that "Computing Power Supermarket" is making computing power selection as convenient as online shopping and has become a key engine for promoting efficient matching of computing power supply and demand in various regions. In addition, Guo Liang introduced that the China Computing Power Platform has specially developed a "SME Inclusive Zone" to implement the "Computing Power for Enterprises" policy. The platform builds an integrated architecture of "computing power base + model services + application ecosystem" to provide pre-adapted operating environments and multi-source model invocation capabilities, effectively solving problems faced by enterprises in computing power acquisition and application, such as "scattered resources, complex connections, and high usage thresholds." The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has proposed that by the end of 2028, a comprehensive, low-cost, high-quality, vibrant, and talent-rich inclusive computing power service system will be basically established, covering no less than 10 categories among the 15 industries applicable to SME classification standards. Public services for SME computing power applications will be further strengthened, the threshold for SMEs to obtain and use computing power will be significantly lowered, and solid computing power support will be provided for promoting the specialized, refined, and innovative development of SMEs. As the special action deepens, the two innovative businesses, "Computing Power Bank" and "Computing Power Supermarket," will promote computing power from a high-threshold "capital-intensive asset" to a "pay-as-you-go information infrastructure" that is as convenient and accessible as water and electricity. This will become a key lever for SMEs to cope with challenges and achieve intelligent development in the computing power competition.

title_en: Head of the WTO Affairs Division of the Ministry of Commerce Interprets the Provisional Arrangement for the Implementation of the E-commerce Agreement Reached at the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference
body_en: On March 28, during the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14), 66 WTO members, including China, issued a declaration announcing the provisional implementation arrangements for the "E-commerce Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the "Agreement"), accelerating the implementation of the first set of global digital trade rules. A spokesperson from the WTO Affairs Department of the Ministry of Commerce provided an interpretation of the Agreement's provisional implementation arrangements. I. Background of the Agreement's Provisional Implementation Arrangements Digital trade has become a core engine of global economic growth, with an average annual growth rate far exceeding that of traditional goods trade, serving as a new driving force for the transformation and upgrading of global trade and the realization of inclusive development. In December 2024, after more than five years of negotiations, some WTO members, including China, the European Union, and Australia, confirmed the conclusion of the "E-commerce Agreement." Subsequently, in accordance with WTO rules, the participants of the Agreement, including China, have been committed to promoting consensus among all WTO members to incorporate the Agreement into the WTO rule framework and bring it into effect as soon as possible. The provisional implementation arrangements reached at MC14 are an important measure to promote the prior implementation of the Agreement before its formal incorporation into the WTO rule framework, marking the Agreement's entry into the entry into force procedure. Its goal is to allow participants to enjoy the benefits of the rules first, while continuously promoting the incorporation of the Agreement into the WTO rule framework. According to the provisional implementation arrangements, participants of the Agreement will initiate their domestic procedures for accepting the Agreement. Once the 45th participant submits its instrument of acceptance, the Agreement will enter into force for all acceding members. At the same time, the provisional implementation arrangements will automatically terminate once all WTO members reach consensus and agree to incorporate the Agreement into the WTO rule framework, and the Agreement will enter the formal implementation phase. II. Significance of the Agreement From the perspective of digital trade governance, the Agreement, as the first set of global digital trade rules, fills the gap in digital governance and leaves room for further negotiations on issues such as cross-border data flows and source code, creating a predictable digital trade framework for businesses, consumers, and other stakeholders. From a development perspective, the Agreement enhances the participation of developing members in digital trade through measures such as transitional periods, strengthened capacity building, and technical assistance, empowering small and medium-sized enterprises, women, and youth, and promoting inclusive trade development. From the perspective of the multilateral trading system, the Agreement and its provisional implementation arrangements demonstrate the WTO's ability to respond to the development needs of the digital age, and members' willingness to inject stability and certainty into the development of global digital trade through innovative approaches and joint actions, contributing to the deep reform of the WTO. III. Main Contents of the Agreement The Agreement consists of six major sections. (I) Empowering E-commerce. This section mainly includes provisions on electronic transaction frameworks, electronic authentication and electronic signatures, electronic contracts, electronic invoices, paperless trade, single window data exchange and electronic system interoperability, and electronic payments. It encourages members to establish legal frameworks that recognize the legality of electronic transactions and processes; clarifies that electronic signatures, electronic contracts, and other legal documents shall not be denied legal effect solely on the grounds that they are in electronic form; promotes the comprehensive electronic submission and recognition of documents for import, export, and transit goods to shorten customs clearance times; establishes electronic single windows to streamline import, export, and transit processes and improve trade efficiency; and regulates the supervision of the electronic payment sector to enhance regulatory transparency and facilitate cross-border trade. (II) Openness and E-commerce. This section mainly includes provisions on the duty-free treatment of electronic transmissions, open government data, and internet access and use for e-commerce. It stipulates that electronic transmissions between members shall be duty-free, with a review to be conducted five years later; promotes the public sharing of government data to enable small and medium-sized enterprises to develop innovative data products and services, enhancing their competitiveness and innovation capabilities; and clarifies the importance of internet access and use for e-commerce, allowing end-users to freely choose compliant terminal equipment and legally access internet services and applications. (III) Trust and E-commerce. This section mainly includes provisions on online consumer protection, regulation of unsolicited commercial electronic messages, personal data protection, and cybersecurity. It requires members to combat misleading and fraudulent commercial practices, improve channels for consumer redress, and enhance public awareness; requires members to control unsolicited commercial electronic messages, setting regulatory benchmarks through measures such as opt-out mechanisms and prior consent; establishes a legal framework for personal data protection and promotes the compatibility and interoperability of different regulatory systems; and stipulates that members should adopt a risk-oriented regulatory approach, strengthen international cooperation, and enhance cybersecurity capacity building. (IV) Transparency, Cooperation, and Development. This section mainly includes provisions on digital trade cooperation and development. It emphasizes the strong cross-border nature of digital trade and the need for members to establish cooperation frameworks to promote the exchange of regulatory experiences and the realization of digital trade transformation dividends; emphasizes the inclusivity of the Agreement, and that practical and comprehensive development support will be provided to developing members facing digital trade opportunities and challenges through transitional periods, needs assessments, capacity building, and technical assistance. (V) Telecommunications. This section mainly includes provisions on competitive safeguards related to basic telecommunications services, interconnection, and the public availability of licensing standards. It will upgrade existing WTO telecommunications rules to adapt to the development trends of digital technologies; requires the allocation of spectrum resources through market-oriented, public, transparent, and non-discriminatory means to ensure full market competition and enrich the choices of market players. (VI) Supplementary Provisions. This section mainly includes provisions on scope and exceptions, and mechanism arrangements. It clarifies that the Agreement excludes government procurement, government services, and government-held information; incorporates the general exceptions and security exceptions of the WTO's GATT 1994 and GATS, and adds exceptions for prudential regulation and personal data protection; establishes a regular review mechanism, and stipulates that future negotiations may be conducted on issues such as cross-border data flows, source code, and encrypted information and communication technology products. IV. Next Steps China will make all preparations for the provisional implementation of the Agreement, promote its early entry into force, and continuously expand the number of participants and acceding parties. China will fully implement the Agreement's commitment to inclusive development, strengthen rule exchanges, experience sharing, and practical cooperation with all members, and work together to build an open, inclusive, secure, and universally beneficial new pattern of global digital trade governance. China will also summarize the practical experience of Beijing in piloting the Agreement, continue to expand high-level opening-up in the digital field, help enterprises utilize the benefits of the rules, enhance the international competitiveness of the digital industry, and lay a solid foundation for the subsequent nationwide implementation of the Agreement.

title_en: AI Reconstructs the Data Foundation: How Can Domestic Databases Be User-Friendly, Durable, and Intelligent?
body_en: Databases, as the cornerstone of digital infrastructure, are key carriers for activating the value of data elements. However, truly achieving usability, durability, and intelligent use, and moving from a substitute space to value leadership, still faces severe challenges. Mei Hong, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a professor at Peking University, stated at the 2026 China Database Technology and Industry Conference on the 22nd that the long-term inadequacy of chip and basic software capabilities has led to a lack of core and soul in China's informatization development. The national "15th Five-Year Plan" clearly emphasizes improving the level of digital development and reiterates the need to enhance the production level of basic software. Databases, as important basic software, cannot be overemphasized in their strategic positioning. Mei Hong mentioned that if the information technology application innovation of the past decade solved the "bottleneck" survival problem, then from the "15th Five-Year Plan" onwards, we need to answer how to build independently developed digital infrastructure that is globally competitive in the digital age. AI Brings New Demands and Challenges Databases are an important component of basic software, and their level of independent innovation and industry maturity directly relates to the stability of the foundation and long-term development of Digital China. Yang Ju, vice president of the China Software Industry Association, stated that China's database industry has entered a critical stage of transitioning from following to parallel leadership. With deep collaboration among industry, academia, research, and users, a batch of high-quality domestic database products have been deeply applied in core industries such as finance, telecommunications, and healthcare, achieving a critical leap from peripheral support to core business hosting. Currently, the explosive growth of artificial intelligence is reshaping the technical architecture of databases from the bottom up. Feng Yucai, chairman of DM Data, stated that databases, as the core carriers for data storage, management, and application, are a key support for ensuring national data security and achieving information technology autonomy and control. Digital transformation trends such as cloud-native, distributed, and AI integration present many new demands and challenges for industry development. Song Yu, vice president of CCID Consulting, stated that the development of artificial intelligence technology, on the one hand, puts forward new demands for databases, including the widespread application of various data types such as text, images, videos, and audio, driving databases towards unified multimodal management. On the other hand, the training and inference of artificial intelligence rely on large-scale data, requiring databases to have massive storage and high concurrency processing capabilities. At the same time, intelligent applications have high requirements for real-time feedback, which also forces databases to improve their response capabilities. AI technology itself is also empowering databases, driving their evolution towards automatic tuning, intelligent operations, and self-adaptation. Under this logic, database products in the era of artificial intelligence exhibit three new development characteristics: integration, semanticization, and automation. Mei Hong stated that the rapid development of artificial intelligence is essentially "data-driven intelligence, computation realizes intelligence," and high-quality, secure data supply has become a key element. The high-quality development of the digital economy is inseparable from the full release of the value of data elements and efficient governance. These new scenarios and changes pose higher requirements for database technology. According to his analysis, the demands brought by artificial intelligence to databases are reflected in two aspects. First, how to effectively use artificial intelligence to empower database management, enabling systems to have self-production, self-optimization, and self-repair capabilities. Second, how data can better support artificial intelligence, not only storing structured data but also efficiently supporting data types such as vectors, graphs, and time series, preparing data for model training, and supporting retrieval-augmented generation for large models. Zhou Aoying, director of the Database Professional Committee of the China Computer Federation, also believes that the deep penetration of artificial intelligence is completely reshaping the technical boundaries and industry stickiness of databases. Meanwhile, industry development has entered deep water. After years of breakthroughs in information technology application innovation, domestic databases have basically achieved the phased goal of being usable. However, truly achieving usability, durability, and intelligent use still faces severe challenges. Core technologies still have gaps, the supply of high-end talent is still insufficient, the industry-academia-research transformation chain is still not smooth, the adaptation of extreme performance to complex scenarios still needs breakthroughs, and global competitiveness still needs to be improved. "These problems cannot be solved by a single enterprise or a single technology; they require deep and sustained collaboration among academia, industry, and application ends," Zhou Aoying said. "15th Five-Year Plan" Keywords: Integration and Leadership Mei Hong emphasized that the keywords for China's databases in the past decade were "breaking the ice" and "catching up." On the new journey of the "15th Five-Year Plan," the keywords should be "integration" and "leadership." It is necessary to integrate artificial intelligence to make infrastructure more intelligent, integrate industry scenarios to truly release the value of data elements, and integrate the industrial ecosystem to promote collaborative innovation among industry, academia, research, and users, leading technological directions, taking the lead in exploring entity-centric database data management, striving to seize the initiative, leading standard setting, and making China's voice heard in the global data governance system. As a national team in the cyberspace industry, Wang Guirong, deputy general manager of China Electronics Information Industry Group Co., Ltd., introduced that the group focuses on five major industries: integrated circuits, computing, networks, data, and high-tech electronics. It has formed an independent computing industry chain from Phytium CPU, Kylin operating system, DM database, and Great Wall servers to system applications, as well as an integrated circuit industry chain covering EDA design, manufacturing, materials, and supply chains. Wang Guirong stated that China Electronics adheres to open source and openness, does not create closed "all-in-one" solutions, and works with upstream and downstream partners to promote the industry's leap from "products are usable" to "ecosystems are easy to use." Feng Yucai introduced that as a leading domestic database enterprise under China Electronics, DM Data has achieved 100% independent research and development of its core source code. In the future, it will continue to deeply cultivate cutting-edge technologies such as the deep integration of AI and databases, cloud-native, distributed computing, and graph computing, forging independent, trustworthy, secure, efficient, and intelligent full-stack data capabilities; accelerating global layout, promoting Chinese database technology to the world, and building a world-class Chinese database brand. Yang Ju suggested adhering to innovation-driven development, tackling core technologies, focusing on areas such as database kernels, distributed architectures, AI-native integration, and data security, encouraging collaborative research and development between industry and academia, and participating in international and industry standard setting. At the same time, deepen ecological collaboration, break down enterprise barriers, jointly build open-source communities and technology alliances, and improve the full-stack adaptation system from chips to application software; strengthen industry-education integration and cultivate interdisciplinary talent. In addition, focus on value release, promote the large-scale implementation of database technology in key areas such as government affairs, finance, industry, healthcare, and transportation, and support enterprises in expanding into international markets.

title_en: Giants are vying to deploy payment Skill AI, the "positioning battle" has just begun.
body_en: In just over half a month, domestic payment giants have successively and intensively released a series of payment Skills or AI payment infrastructure products. Following the release of Alipay's first domestic "Payment Integration Skill" at the end of March, on April 20th, Alipay's Payment Integration Skill was simultaneously launched on leading AI tool platforms such as TRAE SOLO, Kouzi Programming, and Qoder. During this period, payment giants have been very active. WeChat Pay and Huawei HarmonyOS Pay have successively released Skill-related services. China UnionPay released the "Agentic Payment Open Protocol" (APOP). JD Technology launched ClawTip, an A2A (Agent-to-Agent) micro-payment infrastructure for the AI Agent ecosystem. Alipay, in conjunction with Qianwen App, Taobao Flash Purchase, Rokid, Damai, and Alibaba Cloud Baixian, released the ACT protocol (Agentic Commerce Trust Protocol). On the surface, this is a wave of intensive updates to technical tools: developers can add payment capabilities to applications with just a natural language command. However, upon closer examination, a battle for positioning regarding AI payment entry points, developer ecosystems, and industry standard-setting rights has quietly begun. While international players like Google and OpenAI are fiercely competing for the definition rights of global AI payment protocols, domestic payment institutions are "fighting their own battles" at the Skill level—WeChat relies on the Tencent ecosystem, Alipay is backed by the Alibaba ecosystem, Huawei has its own HarmonyOS system, and UnionPay is attempting to build a unified trust framework with APOP. Beneath the surface of excitement, the AI payment "positioning battle" has just begun, and the true endgame for domestic AI payment is far from here. Image source: Xinhua News Agency What are the Skills that major companies are rushing to release? In simple terms, a Skill is essentially an AI programming assistant toolkit that packages the complex API documentation, signature rules, callback verification logic, and other processes of payment institutions into a standardized component. Developers only need to describe their needs in natural language, and the AI can automatically generate payment-related code. For example, Alipay's "Payment Integration Skill" deeply encapsulates basic payment capabilities into standardized components. Through natural language interaction and automatic deployment, it allows "novice" developers without technical backgrounds to complete the entire process from product conception to commercial monetization without writing complex code. WeChat Pay, for instance, has released a comprehensive system for AI payment integration capabilities, which includes not only Skill packages but also two core modules: AI-friendly documentation and AI-friendly APIs. Data from WeChat Pay shows that over 70% of WeChat Pay merchant developers are using AI-assisted programming tools for integration development. According to analysts, the proactive deployment of AI payment integration capabilities by leading institutions is essentially a competition for merchant service entry points in AI scenarios, seizing the "gateway" for future commercial traffic. Wang Pengbo, a financial industry analyst at Broadcom Consulting, believes that the payment industry is at a critical juncture, transitioning from the mobile payment era to an era driven by agent ecosystems. The integration of payment and artificial intelligence has shifted from shallow functional integration to systematic adaptation for AI ecosystems. The nascent agent economy is giving rise to entirely new transaction demands and collaboration models. On this basis, leading institutions need to reduce integration costs through standardized, modular capabilities to seize AI payment entry points and developer ecosystems, consolidating their positions in the next generation of payment systems. Behind the excitement of Skills, a covert battle for underlying AI payment standards is fiercely unfolding globally. Looking back over the past six months, global tech giants have been fiercely competing for the definition rights of underlying AI payment protocols. In September 2025, OpenAI and Stripe launched the jointly developed and open-sourced Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP). In January 2026, Google launched the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). In February 2026, Stripe and Tempo launched the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP). In the field of AI agent payments, a protocol refers to a set of standardized rules, data formats, and communication mechanisms that govern the interaction between AI agents, merchants, payment service providers, and users. title_en: Notice of the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation on Printing and Distributing the "Action Plan for Service Trade Standardization (2026-2030)"
body_en: [Issuing Unit] Department of Trade in Services [Document Number] Shang Fu Mao Han [2026] No. 75 [Date of Issuance] April 17, 2026 Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Science and Technology, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Natural Resources, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Ministry of Transport, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Ministry of Culture and Tourism, People's Bank of China, State Administration for Market Regulation, General Administration of Sport, China National Intellectual Property Administration, National Copyright Administration, National Data Administration, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Departments of Commerce and Market Regulation of all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, cities specifically designated in the state plan, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps: To implement the decisions and arrangements of the Party Central Committee and the State Council, enhance the standardization level of trade in services, better leverage the fundamental, leading, and exemplary role of standards in industry development, accelerate the promotion of standardization in trade in services, and drive high-quality development and institutional opening-up of trade in services, the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation have jointly formulated the "Action Plan for Standardization of Trade in Services (2026-2030)" and reached a consensus with relevant departments. It is hereby issued, and you are requested to organize its implementation conscientiously in conjunction with your actual conditions. Ministry of Commerce State Administration for Market Regulation April 17, 2026 Action Plan for Standardization of Trade in Services (2026-2030) To thoroughly implement the relevant decisions and arrangements of the Party Central Committee and the State Council, implement the "National Standardization Development Outline" and the "Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Promoting High-Quality Development of Trade in Services with High-Level Opening-up," accelerate the promotion of standardization in trade in services, enhance the standardization level, promote high-quality development and institutional opening-up of trade in services, this Action Plan is formulated. I. Overall Requirements Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, fully implement the spirit of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and its plenary sessions, fully, accurately, and comprehensively implement the new development concept, serve the construction of a new development pattern, take promoting institutional opening-up of trade in services as the main thread, take the construction of a service trade standard system as a grasp, adhere to overall promotion, innovation-driven development, key breakthroughs, and open collaboration, cultivate the "China Services" brand, promote the alignment and compatibility of standards in the service trade field with international standards and rules, enhance the level of trade facilitation in services, and promote the high-quality development of trade in services. Within five years, the national capacity for standardization of trade in services will be enhanced, a number of technical institutions and leading groups for standardization of trade in services will be cultivated, a number of service trade standards in key areas will be formulated, and a number of international standards for trade in services will be led or participated in, and the level of standardization of trade in services will be significantly improved. By 2030, a standard system covering multiple fields and the entire chain of trade in services and adapted to the high-quality development needs of trade in services will be basically established, standard supply will be expanded, international influence will be enhanced, China's capacity to participate in international standardization governance of trade in services will be strengthened, and the role of standards in leading the high-quality development of trade in services, promoting institutional opening-up in the service sector, and supporting high-quality development will be further highlighted. II. Accelerate the Construction of a Standardization Work System for Trade in Services (I) Coordinate and promote standardization work in trade in services. Strengthen research on standard layout in the field of trade in services, guided by market demand, based on fundamental and general standards, key industries, international cooperation, and digitalization of trade in services, cultivate Chinese standard brands in key areas, increase standard promotion and implementation and international对接 cooperation, accelerate the formation of a standard system with a reasonable structure, prominent focus, international alignment, and conformity with China's stage of development and needs for trade in services, and gradually form a market-driven, government-guided, fully participatory, and open and shared work pattern. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation) (II) Optimize the structure of service trade standard supply. Promote the coordinated and complementary development of government-issued standards and market-driven standards in the field of trade in services. Based on the development of service industries and trade, strengthen the effective supply of national standards, focus on ensuring human health and life and property safety, national security, ecological and environmental safety, and meeting the basic needs of economic and social management, increase the intensity of mandatory standard formulation and revision, strengthen supervision of standard implementation, and improve the standardization of industry development. Encourage social organizations to formulate group standards that are urgently needed by the market and have international competitiveness according to market competition and innovation and development needs. Give full play to the role of leading enterprises, and encourage all types of enterprises, including private and foreign-funded enterprises, to strengthen innovation and formulate pioneering enterprise standards. Do a good job in the domestic translation of advanced and applicable international standards, promote the formulation and application of international standards in the field of trade in services, and enhance their global recognition and influence. While improving the domestic standard system, focus on strengthening the research and application of standards related to trade in services that are oriented towards the international market and support cross-border delivery. (Led by competent departments of commerce and market regulation) (III) Promote innovation in trade in services standards. Promote the close integration of standards with services, technologies, and application scenarios, strengthen the research and formulation of standards for new services and new technologies, and proactively carry out pre-standardization research on new trade formats and models, so as to effectively play the leading role of standards in the high-quality development of trade in services and enhance the guarantee capacity of services in key links and fields. Strengthen intellectual property protection during the standard formulation process. (Responsible departments of commerce, market regulation, intellectual property, and copyright according to their respective responsibilities) (IV) Strengthen the promotion and implementation of standards. Carry out publicity, guidance, and training through multiple channels and forms, widely disseminate the concepts, knowledge, and methods of standardization of trade in services, enhance the standardization awareness of various entities, and improve the capacity for standardization work. Open a special section on standardization work on the China Trade in Services Guide website to provide standard information and inquiry services. Timely release the dynamics of standardization work in trade in services, policy interpretations, etc., to improve work transparency and public participation. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce) (V) Strengthen supervision of standard implementation and promotion of experience. Accelerate the construction of a national standard implementation monitoring network, improve the information feedback mechanism for standard implementation, and solidly carry out the evaluation of standard implementation effects. Investigate and deal with violations of mandatory standards in the field of trade in services according to law to ensure the implementation of mandatory standards. Encourage the citation of national standards in laws, regulations, and policy documents in the service sector. Summarize the effectiveness of the implementation of the action plan in a timely manner, publicize practical cases and work experiences, and continuously promote the optimization and upgrading of trade in services standards. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation) III. Strengthen Standard Supply in Key Areas (VI) International travel services standards. Focus on accelerating the formulation of standards in areas such as tourism services and inbound consumption, improving service specifications, aligning service standards with international advanced standards, strengthening standard implementation and promotion, and promoting the establishment of a comprehensive standardization system covering travel service quality, safety, scenarios and applications, and guarantees and supervision. (Responsible departments of culture and tourism and commerce according to their respective responsibilities) (VII) International transportation services standards. Focus on taking the lead in formulating standards and building systems in areas such as digitalization of shipping trade, and accelerate the digital, green, and international development of international transportation services. (Responsible departments of transport and commerce according to their respective responsibilities) (VIII) Agricultural trade in services standards. Focus on strengthening research on standards for agricultural trade in services terminology classification, agricultural foreign technical service specifications, and cross-border outsourcing of agricultural material services, enhancing the international service capabilities and standardization level of agricultural service professional institutions, and providing technical support with "China Standards" for overseas agricultural development. (Responsible department of agriculture and rural affairs) (IX) Professional services standards. Increase the intensity of standard formulation in fields such as intellectual property, technology services, geographic information, human resources, language, consulting, inspection and testing, and creative design services, promote the coverage of relevant standards across the entire chain of domestic and foreign service provision in the industry, and enhance the international service capabilities of professional service institutions. Improve the standardization level of service outsourcing, focusing on promoting standardization construction in areas such as biomedical R&D outsourcing, information technology outsourcing integrated with manufacturing, and intellectual property protection for service outsourcing enterprises. (Responsible departments of education, industry and information technology, human resources and social security, natural resources, commerce, market regulation, intellectual property, and copyright according to their respective responsibilities) (X) Traditional and characteristic services standards. Promote the standardization construction of traditional and characteristic service trade such as culture, Chinese education, traditional Chinese medicine, Chinese cuisine, and martial arts, focusing on strengthening standard formulation in areas such as basic general standards, basic element standards, service provision standards, and safety and management standards, and enhance the international recognition and reputation of traditional and characteristic services. (Responsible departments of education, commerce, culture and tourism, sports, and traditional Chinese medicine according to their respective responsibilities) (XI) Digital trade standards. Focus on taking the lead in formulating standards and building systems in areas such as software and information services, data security and privacy protection in digital delivery trade, cross-border flow of data elements, and digital trade platform construction, explore standard scenarios for deep integration with new technologies such as artificial intelligence and virtual reality, carry out standardization practices in the field of service trade empowered by artificial intelligence, and accelerate the improvement of the institutional and market environment for digital trade development. (Responsible departments of cyberspace administration, development and reform, science and technology, industry and information technology, commerce, and data according to their respective responsibilities) (XII) Green trade in services standards. Focus on the green transformation of traditional service trade industries such as transportation and construction, as well as the standard needs for the development of trade in services with green attributes such as supply chains and finance, accelerate the formulation of basic common standards, promote the import and export and application of green technologies, and cultivate new competitive advantages in trade in services. (Responsible departments of housing and urban-rural development and transport according to their respective responsibilities) IV. Promote the Internationalization of Trade in Services Standards (XIII) Deepen international exchanges and cooperation. Relying on multilateral and bilateral cooperation mechanisms for trade in services, deepen standardization exchanges and cooperation with countries participating in the "Belt and Road" Initiative, BRICS countries, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and within the framework of free trade agreements, and promote the overseas application of Chinese standards. Support eligible regions in exploring the establishment of regional standard alignment and cooperation mechanisms with neighboring countries and regions. Strengthen dialogue and cooperation with international standardization organizations, and continuously improve the consistency between Chinese standards and international standards. Give full play to the role of major exhibition platforms such as the China International Import Expo, the China International Fair for Trade in Services, the Global Digital Trade Expo, and the China (Shanghai) International Technology Import Expo, organize relevant exhibitions and activities, promote Chinese standards, and promote international exchanges and mutual learning in standardization work. Enhance the international influence of relevant standardization forums or seminars, and build a platform for international exchanges in standardization. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation) (XIV) Actively participate in international standard formulation. Encourage domestic enterprises and institutions to participate in the activities of international standard organizations, industry international organizations, and various international professional standard organizations, contribute Chinese solutions, actively lead or participate in the formulation and revision of international standards for trade in services, especially emerging services and frontier technologies, and promote the transformation of China's advantageous trade in services standards into international standards. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation) (XV) Participate in the construction of international standard organizations. Support Chinese experts to actively participate in the construction of international standard organizations, and contribute more Chinese wisdom in key areas such as financial services, information technology services, travel services, and digital culture. Build a number of international standardization innovation teams in key areas. Support international standard organizations in holding relevant activities in China. Explore the promotion of the construction of international industrial standard organizations. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation, with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, etc., responsible according to their respective responsibilities) V. Consolidate the Foundation for Standardization Development (XVI) Strengthen research on basic theories and development frontiers. Encourage and support standardization service institutions, industry associations, universities, and research institutions to strengthen theoretical exploration and practical application research on standardization work in trade in services, focus on development trends such as digitalization and greening of trade in services, strengthen forward-looking research on standard needs for new models, new formats, new applications, and new service scenarios, as well as comparative research with international standards and trend research on international development dynamics. Establish an expert database for standardization work in trade in services to provide intellectual support for standardization work. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation) (XVII) Strengthen technical support for standardization institutions. Support national professional standardization technical committees in relevant fields of trade in services to carry out their work. Encourage the strengthening of professional standardization technical committees around frontier technologies and new trade formats and models in services, to provide technical support for enhancing standard supply in key areas of trade in services. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation) (XVIII) Strengthen the construction of a composite talent team. Build a multi-level talent training system. Encourage universities to offer courses related to standardization of trade in services, and focus on cultivating interdisciplinary talents in trade in services and standardization work. Improve the professional ability evaluation and incentive mechanisms for talents in standardization work, and strengthen the role of standard achievements in职称 evaluation. Increase the training and introduction of internationalized talents. Promote the carrying out of standardization training for trade in services in vocational education. (Responsible departments of education and human resources and social security according to their respective responsibilities) (XIX) Build platforms for pilot and experimental standardization work. Build demonstration projects for the research, development, and application of trade in services standards. Encourage and support national demonstration zones for innovation and development of trade in services, comprehensive pilot and demonstration provinces and cities for expanding opening-up of the service industry, national digital trade demonstration zones, and characteristic service export bases, etc., to make the promotion of standardization of trade in services an important task for innovation and development exploration, summarize experience in a timely manner, form replicable and promotable models, and accumulate experience for the establishment and improvement of a standardization work mechanism for trade in services nationwide. Encourage standardization service institutions to be located in relevant demonstration zones and bases to form a cluster development effect. (Led by the Ministry of Commerce) VI. Organization and Implementation Leverage the role of the State Council's standardization work coordination mechanism and the inter-ministerial joint meeting mechanism for the development of trade in services to coordinate and promote standardization work in trade in services. The Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAC) will take the lead, in conjunction with the competent industry authorities in various fields of trade in services, to determine phased key tasks, strengthen policy linkage, and formulate policy measures to support standardization work in trade in services according to actual needs. Relevant departments in various regions will carry out exploration of standardization work in trade in services in conjunction with their industrial and trade characteristics, and do a good job in the application, promotion, and implementation supervision of trade in services standards in their respective regions.

title_en: State Administration for Market Regulation: Strictly Crack Down on Illegal Internet Advertising Behaviors Strongly Reported by the Public
body_en: Reporters learned today (23rd) that the State Administration for Market Regulation has issued the "Notice on Deepening the Governance of the Internet Advertising Ecosystem" and the "Key Tasks for Rectifying the Order of the Internet Advertising Market," making comprehensive arrangements for deepening the governance of the internet advertising ecosystem and deciding to launch a six-month campaign to rectify the order of the internet advertising market. The "Notice on Deepening the Governance of the Internet Advertising Ecosystem" for the first time puts forward the concept of "internet advertising ecosystem governance" and deploys five aspects of governance tasks: improving the internet advertising regulatory system, consolidating the principal responsibilities of internet platform enterprises, strengthening advertising supervision in key areas and new business formats, enhancing monitoring technology and law enforcement capabilities, and strengthening advertising guidance and value leadership. The State Administration for Market Regulation has decided to take strengthening the rectification of the order of the internet advertising market as a breakthrough in promoting the governance of the internet advertising ecosystem. Through a six-month rectification campaign, it will severely crack down on illegal internet advertising behaviors that have aroused strong public concern in accordance with the law and effectively maintain the order of the internet advertising market. The State Administration for Market Regulation has issued the "Key Tasks for Rectifying the Order of the Internet Advertising Market," focusing on six aspects: strengthening the supervision of internet advertising orientation, strengthening the supervision of advertising activities in live-streaming e-commerce, strengthening the supervision of artificial intelligence-generated advertisements, increasing the regulation of internet pop-up advertisements, increasing the regulation of "matrix-style" internet advertising placement, and further consolidating the principal responsibilities of internet platforms. The tasks are detailed, focusing on prominent issues to exert precise efforts and fully maintain a good internet advertising market order. (CCTV Reporter Wang Jing)
